t: The metaphorical narrative of Marx's critique of false ideology and its inner logic
zh: 马克思虚假意识形态批判的隐喻叙事及其内在逻辑
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2025 no. 11
paras: Why does Marx's critique of false ideology rely so heavily on metaphor, and what does that reliance accomplish? Xue Yonglong argues that metaphor in Marx is neither decoration nor an aesthetic extra. It is a way of piercing appearances, and it runs through the critique from its theoretical premise to its mechanism and its historical outcome. Three metaphors, the "caricature", the "hat" and "Prometheus", form a linked and progressive critical system.

The article opens with the paradox that theorists distrust metaphor yet use it at decisive points, citing Althusser as an example. It then explains why Marx turned to metaphor: to overturn the apologetic discourse of speculative philosophy and bourgeois political economy, and to make capital's abstract domination perceptible. The author describes a movement in Marx's metaphors from "unveiling of cognition" to "construction of thought" to "summons to action". The three images are then analysed in turn, with reference to The Holy Family, The Poverty of Philosophy, Marx's doctoral dissertation and the Communist Manifesto. Derrida, Debord, Jameson and Hayden White are drawn in as commentators.

Xue reads the "caricature" as exposing the premise of false ideology: Bruno Bauer's self-consciousness philosophy exaggerates one side of Hegel and elevates spirit above reality, which turns real people into abstractions. The "hat" ("if an Englishman transforms men into hats, a German transforms hats into ideas") reveals the mechanism. People are first reduced to things, as Ricardo saw, and then things are raised into ideas, as Hegel did. The author presents this as reification and "abstract domination", in which domination by things is in fact domination of people by people. "Prometheus bound" points to the outcome: the proletariat is both sufferer and liberator, and its suffering must become universal and provoke it to rebellion. Xue adds that the three images move from surface description to essence and follow the dialectic of contradiction: its emergence, its development and its resolution.

Xue concludes that Marx's aim was not to abandon ideology or merely to judge whether an ideology is false. It was to expose the roots and operation of falsity and to show the necessity of escaping the "rule of ideas". The author holds that false ideology survives today in more hidden forms. These include Western scholars who beautify capitalism, consumerism that disguises "capital's needs" as "individual needs", and technological alienation and digital hegemony. Read the original if you study Marx's theory of ideology, his textual use of imagery, or the way Chinese scholars apply his critique to contemporary capitalism.
quoteEn: The three metaphors in the critique of false ideology, moving from theoretical essence to practical mechanism to historical destination, not only build a cognitive framework for false ideology but also form an interlocking, step-by-step critical system.
quoteZh: 虚假意识形态批判的三重隐喻，从理论本质到实践机制再到历史归宿，不仅共同构建起关于虚假意识形态的认知框架，而且形成了环环相扣、逐级递进的批判体系

t: The ecological narrative of Marxist productive-forces theory
zh: 马克思主义生产力理论的生态叙事
paras: Shen Guangming takes up the charge, made by some Western ecological scholars, that Marx's theory of productive forces contains anti-ecological elements. The article asks two questions: whether productive forces have an ecological character, and how ecological problems relate to productive-force development. Shen argues that, although Marx never used the word "ecology", his account of nature, of the contradiction between humans and nature, and of its resolution fits the core of ecology, and that this is concentrated in his productive-forces theory. Ecological crisis, on this reading, results from the anti-ecological form of capitalist productive forces.

The article is a textual and conceptual argument that moves from Marx's materialist view of nature and his concept of labour as metabolism (material exchange) between humans and nature to a typology of productive forces. It distinguishes labour productive forces, capitalist productive forces and green productive forces. It then turns to China, treating the Xi Jinping formulation that new quality productive forces are "in themselves green productive forces" as a major theoretical innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

Shen holds that labour productive forces are the power by which humans exchange matter, energy and information with nature, and so have an ecological character, while also having an economic character that can clash with it. Under capitalism, value valorisation drives production for production's sake, technology for technology's sake and consumption for consumption's sake, which Shen says breaks the metabolic relation. Green productive forces, by contrast, must respect ecosystem carrying capacity, ecological laws and humanity's free development. Shen holds that these conditions can be met only through public ownership of the means of production, which allows common control of metabolism and inheritance of capitalism's developed productive forces. Capitalist "green" policies and technologies, in this view, cannot escape the logic of capital.

Applying this to China, Shen proposes three tasks for cultivating new quality productive forces: a green transformation of the mode of production (adjusting economic and energy structures, building green industrial chains, extending this abroad through the Belt and Road Initiative and South–South cooperation), green innovation in science and technology, and a green revolution in lifestyles. Shen concludes that Marxist productive-forces theory is a resource for understanding and addressing ecological crisis, and that new quality productive forces are themselves green productive forces. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reply to Western ecological critiques of Marx and a theoretical account of how the green dimension of new quality productive forces is justified.
quoteEn: Developing green productive forces and responding to the current ecological crisis must be based on public ownership of the means of production.
quoteZh: 发展绿色生产力，应对当下生态危机，必须以生产资料公有制为基础。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation, high technology, high efficiency and high quality. It is used to guide the strategy of high-quality development.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for developing Marxism in line with Chinese conditions and contemporary circumstances, and the framing for new Party theory.
China's international infrastructure and cooperation initiative launched in 2013.

t: Engels's original contribution to the materialist foundations of dialectics
zh: 恩格斯对塑造辩证法的唯物主义根基的原创性贡献
paras: Marxist dialectics is usually said to have inverted Hegel's idealist dialectic, but how that inversion was achieved is seldom spelled out. Zhao Zhen argues that Engels carried out the decisive part of this work. By studying the dialectics of nature, Engels is said to have given Marxist dialectics its solid materialist base and, on that base, a general theory of dialectics that goes beyond Hegel.

The article begins with Hegel. It places his dialectic within modern philosophy's turn from ontology to epistemology. It then follows Engels's materialist reconstruction through natural science, the three laws of dialectics, the relation between natural and historical dialectics, and the dialectic of objective world and human thought. It also answers critics from Western Marxism, including Lukács, Alfred Schmidt and Norman Levine.

Zhao's central claim is that Hegel's dialectic was a dialectic of reason, not of the world. For Hegel, the question "how do we know the world" became "how is the world constructed", so worldview was reduced to a footnote of epistemology. Engels therefore could not simply swap concepts. He had to start from facts and, by inductive generalisation from physics, chemistry and biology, show that dialectics exists objectively. He drew the three laws from nature and history, which turned dialectics into a scientific theory, though Zhao notes he had not yet fully separated the unity of opposites from the negation of the negation. Against Lukács and others, Zhao contends that natural and historical dialectics are not two dialectics but one materialist dialectic in different fields. Nature acquires dialectical significance in its relation to humanity, so Engels never imposed dialectics on nature. Engels also divided dialectics into an objective and a subjective form, with thought required to master the first. Zhao says this division completed work Marx had left undone, since Marx used dialectics directly in political economy.

Zhao concludes that dialectics, for Engels, is not an eternal truth or a new metaphysics but an open scientific theory. It rests on natural science, is confirmed by its advances (Zhao cites relativity and quantum mechanics), and is enriched by them. Some of Engels's specific scientific points may be outdated, but scholars today should use materialist dialectics to address the philosophical problems of science in their own time. Read the original if you are interested in the Engels–Marx debate, in replies to Western Marxist critiques of the dialectics of nature, or in a Chinese reading of how Hegel's dialectic was turned materialist.
quoteEn: Natural dialectics and historical dialectics are not two dialectics; both belong to materialist dialectics and are its concrete manifestations in different fields.
quoteZh: 自然辩证法与历史辩证法并不是两种辩证法，它们都属于唯物主义辩证法，是唯物主义辩证法在不同领域的具体体现。

t: The meaning of cultural subjectivity from the perspective of historical materialism
zh: 唯物史观视域下文化主体性意涵阐析
paras: Guo Chao takes up the question "what is cultural subjectivity?", a concept Xi Jinping put forward when he said that any culture that is to stand firm and travel far must have its own subjectivity. The author notes that existing scholarship approaches it from philosophy, history, Chinese modernization and the Two Integrations, but rarely from historical materialism. The article argues that cultural subjectivity is an ideational superstructure rooted in material production, whose true bearer is the people, whose core is cultural leadership, and which develops through exchange with other cultures.

The article is organised around four relationships, each treated as a separate perspective. These are cultural subjectivity and economic subjectivity (material production), and cultural subjectivity and human subjectivity (the "real human being"). The other two are cultural subjectivity and cultural dominance (ideology), and cultural subjectivity and cultural inter-subjectivity (world history). In its closing summary the author says the four parts answer, in turn, where cultural subjectivity comes from, whose it is, what its essence is and how it develops.

Guo first argues that economic subjectivity, meaning a nation's autonomy over its economic path and resources, determines cultural subjectivity. Cultural subjectivity in turn acts back by setting direction, building consensus and supplying spiritual impetus, so historical materialism is not economic determinism. Second, because culture cannot itself be a subject, cultural subjectivity is in essence human subjectivity, ultimately that of the people under Party leadership. The author traces how the people built it across the revolutionary, socialist, reform-era and new-era periods. Third, the author names five components: cultural self-awareness, autonomy, dominance, innovation and transcendence. Of these, cultural dominance ("one dominant, many coexisting") is the core. Fourth, drawing on Marx's world-history theory, Guo argues that subjectivity and inter-subjectivity are mutually dependent. The author reads the Qing closed-door policy and Western "cultural hegemony" as two ways of severing the two.

Guo concludes that consolidating the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation requires strengthening its material base, including through new quality productive forces. It also requires upholding the Party's cultural leadership, advancing the "second integration" of Marxism with traditional culture, and embedding core socialist values. Externally, the author calls for equal treatment, mutual learning and shared benefit among civilizations, and for better international communication of Chinese culture. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Chinese theorists derive cultural subjectivity from historical materialism, and how they link it to Party leadership and cultural dominance.
quoteEn: Cultural subjectivity is the fundamental nature and essential characteristic of a culture's existence and development, as determined by the mode of material production.
quoteZh: 文化主体性是由物质生产方式决定的文化存在和发展的根本性质和本质特征

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to a nation's cultural independence, self-awareness and confidence in dealing with other cultures. The article tries to define it through historical materialism.
The official formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second).
A term introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced, technology-driven productive forces associated with high-quality development.
A twelve-word official set of values (such as prosperity, democracy, harmony, patriotism) promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Marx's critique of capitalist wages
zh: 马克思对资本主义工资问题的批判
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 3 March 2026
paras: Yuan Jiaxi asks how Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme exposes the nature of capitalist wages and, through it, the secret of capitalist exploitation. The short commentary argues that Marx's demolition of Lassalle's "iron law of wages" shows wages to be a historically specific form of the value or price of labour-power, not a natural law, and that only a transformation of production relations can end the exploitation they express.

The piece moves in two steps. It first reconstructs Lassalle's law and Marx's rejection of it as derived from Malthusian population theory. It then sets out Marx's account of the exploitative character and concealed form of wages, the link between the wage system and crisis, and the path beyond wage labour through the two stages of communism.

Yuan argues that Lassalle confused labour with labour-power. Wages, in Marx's phrase, are a disguised form of the value of labour-power, while labour creates surplus value that the capitalist appropriates unpaid. Wages are thus shaped by the balance of class forces, labour productivity and class struggle, and are not "iron" but elastic. The wage form hides the split between necessary and surplus labour time, and wages held to the value of labour-power leave consumption weak relative to accumulation, producing overproduction crises. Marx also found it illogical to demand abolition of the wage system "together with" the iron law, since abolishing wage labour would remove the law.

Yuan concludes that distribution depends on the mode of production. In the first stage of communism, with public ownership, distribution according to labour applies, and in the higher stage "from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs". The author holds that Marx's theory armed the German workers' party against error and still guides proletarian understanding of capitalism. Read the original if you want a brief, orthodox restatement of Marx's wage theory as developed in the Gotha critique.
quoteEn: Lassalle's mistaken understanding of the laws of wages essentially confuses the boundary between labour and labour-power.
quoteZh: 拉萨尔对工资规律的错误认知，本质上是混淆了劳动与劳动力的界限。

t: Marx's concrete paths for developing the materialist conception of history
zh: 马克思发展唯物史观的具体路径
paras: This short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (3 February 2026) asks how Marx developed the materialist conception of history after founding it. Peng and Yan argue that Marx never treated his theory dogmatically. In their account, while guiding the workers' movement and proletarian revolution he opened three concrete paths of development, showing a dialectical interaction between universal theory and particular practice.

The article takes the three paths in turn. The first is Marx's analysis of specific French political events in The Class Struggles in France, 1848 to 1850 and The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte. The second is his exposition of the laws of the capitalist mode of production in Capital. The third is his search for a way to cross the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism, drawing on the Asiatic mode of production and the Russian village commune.

On France, the authors argue that Marx read the 1848 revolution and Bonaparte's restoration through class struggle rooted in the economic base. The peasants' attachment to "Napoleonic ideas" is presented as evidence that ideology has relative independence and can act back on social being. In Capital, they say, Marx applied the theory to the production process and built the doctrine of surplus value, with absolute and relative surplus value as the capitalist's two methods. On Russia, they argue that Marx saw the commune as a fulcrum of social renewal. It could allow a skip over capitalism if social revolution shielded it from capitalist private property while it absorbed capitalism's positive achievements.

The authors conclude that each path made the materialist conception of history more concrete and richer. It gained content on revolutionary strategy, state power, ideology critique, proletarian emancipation and the diversity of social formations. Read the original if you want a concise, officially oriented overview of how Chinese scholars present Marx's own development of historical materialism.
quoteEn: Through a concrete analysis of the living historical event of the 1848 class struggle in France, Marx deepened and developed the materialist conception of history.
quoteZh: 马克思通过对1848年法国阶级斗争这一鲜活历史事件的具体化剖析，深化和发展了唯物史观。

t: Marx's critique of the "German modern problem"
zh: 马克思批判“德国式的现代问题”的理路
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 3 February 2026
paras: This short commentary from China Social Sciences Today asks how Marx, in his 1844 "Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right: Introduction", understood the "German modern problem". Liu Yong argues that Marx did not treat Germany's late-developer status as a lag to be closed by imitation. In Liu's reading, Germany's particularity ruled out repeating the French and British path of political emancipation and pointed instead to human emancipation, a new type of modernization with universal significance.

The article follows Marx's critique at three levels: the "anachronism" of the German system, its political-economic roots, and the state of German classes. It closes by suggesting the analysis still informs how latecomer countries' modernization is understood.

Liu contends that Germany in 1843 had missed the 1789 moment yet faced a capitalism whose contradictions were already visible in Britain and France. It therefore had to take on national unification, political emancipation and human emancipation together, rather than in sequence. For Liu, this makes Germany a prototype of resolving several tasks at once through theoretical critique and revolutionary practice. Marx's critique of the historical school of law and of the practical and theoretical political parties leads to the anatomy of civil society and to the materialist conception of history. Liu describes the German bourgeoisie as late, dependent on feudal power and compromising, and the Junker landlords as having turned into a harsh capitalist class. The proletariat, in this account, bears both a "civilizational" and a "barbaric" deficiency and is the only class able to turn philosophical critique into social revolution.

Liu concludes that Marx moved from German particularity through its political-economic roots and class analysis to a universal path: proletarian revolution as the fundamental solution to the problems of modernization. Liu presents this as a diagnosis of nineteenth-century Germany and as a lesson for latecomer countries facing "time-space compressed modernization". Read the original if you want a brief Chinese reading of the 1844 Introduction as a theory of late-developer modernization.
quoteEn: The essence of this problem is that Germany's particularity meant it could not retrace the French and British road of political modernization, but had to find a new road that goes beyond political emancipation and on to human emancipation.
quoteZh: 这个问题的本质是德国特殊性决定了德国不能重走法国、英国政治现代化老路，而是必须走出一条超越政治解放，进而实现人的解放的新路。

glossary.explanation: Marx's term in the 1844 Introduction and "On the Jewish Question" for emancipation from private property and alienated labour. He contrasts it with merely political emancipation, which leaves civil society's inequalities intact.
In Marx's early writings, the formal, legal emancipation achieved by bourgeois revolutions such as the French Revolution of 1789. In his view it leaves private property and class oppression in place.

A concept used in Chinese scholarship for latecomer modernization, in which stages that took centuries elsewhere are compressed into a short period. The author applies it to nineteenth-century Germany.

keywords: Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

t: The limits of "algorithmic time" from the standpoint of historical materialism
zh: 从唯物史观看“算法时间”的限度
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2026, asks how "human time" can regain its meaning and practical measure as AI accelerates social life. Sun Yan argues that "algorithmic time" is neutral only as an abstract technical structure. Once embedded in capitalist social relations, it becomes a force that dominates labour and time.

Drawing on Marx's analysis of technology and machinery, the article moves through three steps: the technical logic of algorithmic time, the limits of its neutrality, and the return to human time. It uses examples such as traffic scheduling, medical imaging, delivery riders timed by the second and algorithmically fragmented user attention. It also refers briefly to Habermas.

Sun identifies three features of algorithmic time: computability, efficiency and measurability. Sun holds that these carry no exploitation in themselves, but become institutionalised through three logics: acceleration, discipline, and quantification-cum-coercion. In this account, capital no longer only lengthens or intensifies labour. It controls the rhythm, structure and distribution of time, and hides this behind \"technical neutrality\". Practice then shrinks from purposeful activity to task execution, which Sun reads as the colonisation of the lifeworld by system logic.

Sun concludes that, in line with Marx's view of free time as the measure of human development, productivity gains should enlarge disposable time. Under socialism, the people-centred approach to development points to rebuilding this measure. Sun proposes embedding values in algorithms, treating time as a negotiable and guaranteed public resource, and protecting time for meaning and social interaction. The article states that the true value of new quality productive forces lies in widening people's time boundaries rather than in general acceleration. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist reading of AI, labour platforms and time politics.
quoteEn: The development of productive forces constitutes a real growth of social wealth only when it is converted into an expansion of free time.
quoteZh: 生产力的发展只有在转化为自由时间的扩展时，才真正构成社会财富的增长。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It refers to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, notably in digital technology and AI.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: An official formulation holding that development should aim at the well-being of the people. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 2010s.

t: Marx's thinking on the "shaping of the human being" and its implications
zh: 马克思关于“人的塑造”的思考及其启示
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 January 2026
paras: Li and Xie ask how Marx understood the "shaping of the human being" (a concept akin to cultivation or Bildung) and what it offers today. They argue that this theme forms a hidden thread running through Marx's economics, politics and philosophy, and that he moved it from ideas and culture into material labour and practice.

The newspaper article reads Marx chronologically: the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 on alienated labour, the Theses on Feuerbach, The German Ideology, Capital, and the late anthropological notebooks. It closes by linking the theme to Chinese modernization.

In the authors' account, Marx makes practice the ontological basis of human shaping, so that people remake their own cognition and abilities while transforming the world. Individuals form within social relations and the division of labour, and the bourgeoisie turns its interests into "eternal truths" through education, law and religion. Capital's logic disciplines workers into valorisation-serving subjects, yet crises can awaken a class "for itself". The late notebooks, the authors say, show non-alienated shaping in pre-class societies and treat colonial private property and "civilizing" law as destructive or legitimating exploitation.

The authors conclude that shaping becomes a two-way process in which individuals and the community form each other through material practice, aiming at free and all-round development. They propose that in Chinese modernization this logic appears as the "modernization of the human being", common prosperity and the all-round development of moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese overview of how Marx's texts are mapped onto human development and education policy.
quoteEn: In Marx's philosophy of labour and practice, the "shaping of the human being" is no longer pure ideological indoctrination or cultural transmission in the traditional sense, but is reconstructed as a process in which individuals and the community generate and shape each other in the material practice of transforming the world.
quoteZh: 在马克思的劳动—实践哲学中，“人的塑造”不再是传统意义上纯粹的观念灌输或文化传承，而是被深刻地重构为个体与共同体在改造世界的物质实践中双向生成、相互塑造的过程

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses common prosperity and the coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress.
An official goal of shared affluence for all, given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping. It is presented as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Reflecting on digital capitalism from the perspective of Marxist political economy
zh: 从马克思主义政治经济学视角反思数字资本主义
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 28 January 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how Marxist political economy can help assess digital capitalism, the form that emerged in the 21st century as capital fused with big data and artificial intelligence. Feng Wangzhou argues that digital capital shares capital's general nature, driven by the pursuit of surplus value, and therefore has a dual effect: a "civilising" effect that advances society and a "barbaric" effect of comprehensive exploitation and domination of people.

The article opens by citing Xi Jinping on understanding and guiding capital, then examines three areas in turn: social relations and human subjectivity, productive forces and contradictions, and digital interaction and real relationships. It closes with three proposals for managing digital capital.

Feng argues that digital platforms enrich social relations beyond region and kinship, yet under the logic of capital workers become data and relations become tradable assets, so that subjectivity is eroded. Productive forces advance through technological investment and the replacement of repetitive labour, but the article identifies contradictions between mass demand for data and oligopoly control of it, between socialised data production and capitalist control, and between technology's emancipatory potential and unlimited accumulation. Platforms become core means of production, and Feng describes a "data enclosure movement" in which platform owners act as "technology lords". Algorithms also filter and label interaction, and everyday exchanges become a direct source of surplus value as "digital commodity" relations.

Feng concludes that digital capitalism both sharpens capitalism's basic contradiction and nurtures the forces that negate it. The author calls for moving beyond technological determinism and returning digital capital to its instrumental role. Three measures are proposed: institutional regulation through basic data-factor rules and oversight of technology use; a people-centred orientation in which the logic of the people replaces the logic of capital; and a data production and ownership system suited to Chinese modernization that upholds digital justice. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese Marxist scholar frames digital capital's risks and its regulation in policy-oriented terms.
quoteEn: The development of digital capitalism both intensifies the basic contradiction of capitalism and breeds the forces and conditions that negate it.
quoteZh: 数字资本主义的发展既激化了资本主义的基本矛盾，也孕育了否定自身的力量和条件。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse stating that development should serve the people's interests and wellbeing.

glossary.literal: basic institutions for the data factor
glossary.explanation: Official policy term for the basic rules governing data as a factor of production, covering ownership, circulation, use and distribution.
A Marxist expression for capital's inherent drive to self-expand through surplus value, which shapes social life. Chinese writers often contrast it with the "logic of the people".

t: Engels's view of scientific socialism
zh: 恩格斯的科学社会主义观
paras: Bai Bingzhuo, writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2026, revisits Engels's reflections on scientific socialism, the part of Marxism where Engels is said to have played a key role. The article argues that Engels explained how socialism moved from utopia to science and from ideal to reality. Bai holds that these ideas still have strong explanatory and practical force.

The piece is organised in three parts: the real-world basis of the shift from utopian to scientific socialism, its theoretical cornerstone, and the path by which socialism becomes reality. It draws on Engels's assessment of Saint-Simon, Fourier and Owen, his prefaces and his accounts of historical materialism and surplus value.

Bai reports that Engels treated the three utopians as a direct source of scientific socialism but saw them as lacking a real basis. Only with the development of large-scale machine industry in the 1830s and 1840s did the contradiction between socialised production and private capitalist ownership, and the antagonism between proletariat and bourgeoisie, mature. The theoretical foundation, in Engels's view, is Marx's two great discoveries, historical materialism and the theory of surplus value. Scientific socialism is said to conform to objective law and to serve the working class's aims, and to emerge from German dialectics applied to English economic and French political relations.

Bai concludes that, for Engels, capitalism's achievements are relative to pre-capitalist systems and come with alienation, while recurring crises show its contradictions cannot be overcome within private ownership. The route forward is proletarian revolution led by a party, the overthrow of the bourgeois state, and public ownership of the means of production. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese overview of Engels's account of scientific socialism.
quoteEn: Engels pointed out that whether a theory is mature corresponds to whether capitalist production and class conditions are mature.
quoteZh: 恩格斯指出，理论成熟与否是同资本主义生产状况和阶级状况成熟与否相适应的

t: The practical dimension of Lenin's thought on building socialist culture
zh: 列宁社会主义文化建设思想的实践向度
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 20 January 2026
paras: This short commentary asks what socialist culture is and how to build it, according to Lenin. Yin and Liu argue that Lenin traced the proletariat's difficulties in economic management, consolidating power and social transformation to the cultural backwardness of the masses. In their account, he combined Marx and Engels's theory of proletarian culture with Russian conditions and so developed Marxism creatively.

The article organises Lenin's practice into three strands: holding leadership over cultural construction, forming new communist people, and critically absorbing humanity's cultural heritage. It draws on Lenin's struggles against Narodnik, Economist, Menshevik and Kautskyist currents, his disputes with Proletkult, and his proposals on education, electrification and voluntary labour.

On leadership, the authors say Lenin held that a backward society with entrenched small-producer habits requires the proletariat to lead culture. He therefore opposed Proletkult's claim of independence from the Party and called for sustained Marxist indoctrination, Party supervision of literature and publishing, and politically committed education. On new people, they report his stress on mass literacy, scientific and electrification education, political education that exposes the bourgeois claim of apolitical schooling, and labour education such as the Saturday volunteer work. On heritage, they present Lenin as rejecting both leftist nihilism and rightist conservatism: old culture and capitalist culture are to be selectively sublated and used, while a new socialist intelligentsia is trained alongside.

The authors conclude that these ideas form a systematic whole and show the truth and practical force of Lenin's thought. They offer no new case beyond summarising Lenin's measures. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language overview of how Lenin's cultural policy is currently presented in Chinese Marxist scholarship.
quoteEn: The core of culture is the cultivation of people.
quoteZh: 文化的核心是育人

glossary.explanation: A movement in early Soviet Russia, organised through the Proletarian Culture Organisations, that sought an independent, purely proletarian culture. Lenin criticised its separation from the Party and from earlier culture.

t: The intellectual-historical context of Marx's thought on justice
zh: 马克思正义思想的思想史语境
paras: Since the turn of the century, Chinese scholars have disputed whether Marx rejected justice as a normative category or pursued a higher form of it. Zhang argues that this apparent contradiction comes from neglecting the intellectual-historical context of Marx's thought. Returning to that context, the article contends, shows that his view of justice combines "realistic critique" with "ideal construction".

The short commentary first sets out these two aspects, drawing on the Critique of the Gotha Programme and the 1857–58 manuscripts. It then examines how Marx dialectically sublated two traditions of modern European political thought: Hobbesian realism and Spinozist rationalism. It ends by applying the approach to current debates.

Zhang reads Marx's attack on Lassallean "fair distribution" as a critique of bourgeois formal justice, which is tied to equivalent exchange and private property. Against this stands a "substantive justice" centred on the free and all-round development of the person, which the article links to the stage of "free individuality". Marx takes from Hobbes the point that justice depends on a given order, recast as "no particular mode of production, no particular justice", and historicises Hobbes's natural state. From Spinoza he takes positive freedom, and he gives it a practical route through changing the capitalist mode of production. The article therefore holds that Marx rejected the absolutising of bourgeois justice, not justice as such.

Zhang proposes that the same method suits new topics such as global justice and justice in the digital age. Analysis of platform labour, for example, should start from changes in the mode of production and not stop at fair wages, which the article says would repeat the Lassalleans' error. The author concludes that Marx's critical tradition and his goal of free individuality should both be kept. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language account of how Hobbes and Spinoza are used to settle the debate over Marx and justice.
quoteEn: The value of intellectual-history research lies in providing a \"historical coordinate system\", enabling scholars, once they grasp the sources of Marx's thought on justice, to move beyond the either-or dilemma of interpretation.
quoteZh: 思想史研究的价值在于提供“历史坐标系”，使学者在把握马克思正义思想源流的基础上超越非此即彼的解读困境。

t: The state apparatus as "the vital force of society itself"
zh: 作为“社会本身的生命力”的国家机器
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 14 January 2026
paras: This short commentary asks how the state apparatus changes its nature and function across history. Yu and Dai argue that the state is not eternal but a product of a particular historical stage. In their account it moves from being a \"force ruling over society\" in class society to becoming, under socialism, \"the vital force of society itself\".

The authors draw on Marx, Engels and Lenin in two parts. The first covers the state as a ruling force, with emphasis on the capitalist state. The second covers the transformation of the state apparatus under socialism, in the form of the dictatorship of the proletariat.

In the first part, Yu and Dai describe the army, police and courts as coercive organs serving the ruling class. They argue that capitalism pushes this alienation to its peak, adding ideological control through education and the media and a new economic role. They say this contradiction leads to proletarian revolution and to the need to smash the old state machine. In the second part, they identify three changes under socialism: the class character of the state, its organisational principles (recallable officials on the Paris Commune model, the Leninist \"semi-state\") and its focus, which shifts from class rule to social service. They state that this has been fully demonstrated in contemporary China, without giving evidence.

The authors conclude that the transformation is a move from \"political emancipation\" to \"human emancipation\". They define this as the gradual removal of the opposition between political state and civil society, and a progress toward an association of free individuals. They add that it requires material conditions, institutional improvement and a change in ideas. Read the original if you want a brief restatement of the classical Marxist theory of the state, as applied to the claim about the socialist state in China.
quoteEn: The essence of the socialist state lies in gradually transforming the state apparatus from a "force ruling over society" into "the vital force of society itself".
quoteZh: 社会主义国家的本质在于使国家机器从“统治社会的力量”逐步转化为“社会本身的生命力”

t: "Political philosophy" in the perspective of Marxist philosophy
zh: 马克思主义哲学视域中的“政治哲学”
paras: Did Marx have a political philosophy, or only a social philosophy? Long argues that, although Marx rejected abstract speculative systems, his philosophy can be read as a "political philosophy": a spiritual weapon of the proletariat in its struggle against political reality. The article seeks to identify the theoretical role and historical mission of this political philosophy.

This short piece in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (14 January 2026) draws mainly on Marx's early writings, including the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher period and the critique of Hegel's philosophy of right. It proceeds in three steps: scientific critique of political reality, the necessity of political philosophy's intervention, and its eventual "elimination".

Long's central move is that Marx grounded politics in civil society rather than in spirit or the state. The limits of political emancipation, such as the alienation of the political state and the opposition between "rights of man" and "rights of the citizen", spring from the crisis of civil society under private property. This makes political philosophy necessary, but it must go on to critique civil society itself. It supplies the proletariat with theoretical consciousness, while the proletariat supplies the material force. Once private property is abolished, the political philosophy loses its reason for being.

Long concludes that political philosophy is not Marx's "first philosophy", yet Marx did have one. Its "elimination" is the completion of its mission and the realisation of its highest value, not the end of human political wisdom. Read the original if you want a compact textual reading of the early Marx on political emancipation, civil society and the status of political philosophy.
quoteEn: A "political philosophy" moving towards "elimination" is by no means the end of human political wisdom, but the realisation of its highest value as the proletariat's spiritual weapon, and its glorious historical mission.
quoteZh: 走向“消灭”的“政治哲学”绝不是人类政治智慧的终结，而是其作为无产阶级的精神武器之最高价值的实现，也是其荣耀的历史使命。

t: Innovative development of the theory and methods of investigation and research
zh: 调查研究理论与方法的创新发展
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xi Jinping's statements on investigation and research (diaoyan) have advanced the theory and methods of this Party tradition. Wang Guowei presents them as answering what such research is, why it matters and how to do it well.

The article first sets out three theoretical contributions: the spiritual essence of investigation and research, its people-centred value, and its functional position drawn from Party history. It then turns to its practical value for current tasks and to three proposals for innovation: regular mechanisms, stronger capacity and new methods.

Wang reads investigation and research as a process of seeking truth and practical results, grounded in materialist dialectics and the principle of seeking truth from facts. Citing Xi, Wang equates it with following the mass line and with 'asking the people for advice', and calls it 'the foundation of planning and the way to success'. Wang says it is needed both to make sound decisions and to implement them, given a complex international and domestic environment.

Wang calls for institutionalised practice: leaders personally leading major research projects, grassroots contact points, and research woven into decision-making. Cadres should focus on pressing contradictions, gather comprehensive information and aim for results. Wang also urges using the internet and big data, following an 'online mass line', and cleaning up false online information. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present Xi's methodological guidance on investigation and research for cadres.
quoteEn: Investigation and research is both a scientific worldview and a scientific methodology; it is both a scientific mode of thinking and a scientific working principle and method.
quoteZh: 调查研究既是科学的世界观，又是科学的方法论；既是科学的思维方式，又是科学的工作原则、工作方法。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party method of fact-finding through fieldwork and analysis before making and implementing policy. It is associated with Mao Zedong's 'no investigation, no right to speak' and has been repeatedly stressed by Xi Jinping.
A Party principle of working 'from the masses, to the masses': gathering people's views, refining them into policy and returning them to practice. It was developed by Mao Zedong.
A principle of basing policy on actual conditions, treated in Party doctrine as the core of its ideological line. It is associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping.

t: The ideological superstructure: a key category for state governance under historical materialism
zh: 思想上层建筑：唯物史观下国家治理的关键范畴
paras: Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for state governance and social development to be better aligned with each other, Yang Hutao asks how the state governance system and the basic economic system actually interact within historical materialism. The article proposes the "ideological superstructure" as the missing analytical category linking the two. Yang argues that the shared ideas defining a political community are the key to the character and performance of state governance.

The article first reviews Marx's uses of "superstructure", especially in The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte and the 1859 Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy. From these it separates a political superstructure (legal and political institutions, army, courts) from an ideological one (political and legal thought, morals, beliefs, sentiments). It then discusses the role of the latter in state building and state capacity, draws on Chinese history, compares the United States and China, and ends with the Chinese case under the heading of putting the people first.

Yang's central move is to treat the ideological superstructure as the load-bearing frame beneath the visible political superstructure, comparable to informal institutions beneath formal ones. It rests on the basic economic system and fixes the source of legitimacy for political authority. The article reads China's four great historical transformations as changes in legitimacy ideas tied to productive forces, and criticises convergence and universal-values theories for ignoring differences in these ideas. Its sharpest distinction is between "sovereignty of the people", which answers whom power belongs to, and "putting the people first", which answers whom power serves. Yang contends that Western capital-led states hold only the first, and drift towards rentier and financial-capital dominance, while China unites both. Drawing on Michael Mann and others, Yang adds that the three dimensions of infrastructural capacity (penetration, extraction and negotiation) depend on shared knowledge supplied by the ideological superstructure.

Yang concludes that modernizing state governance means building core values systematically, not merely improving institutions. In the author's account, "putting the people first" is the soul of China's ideological superstructure and has been turned into policy goals such as self-reliance, poverty alleviation, common prosperity and Chinese modernization. The author presents this as a path of governance combining historical tradition with the needs of the present. Read the original if you study how Chinese scholars extend base–superstructure theory to state governance, or want to see a Marxist comparison of Chinese and Western legitimacy concepts.
quoteEn: The real difference lies not in whether one acknowledges that power is conferred by the people, that is, in how one answers the question of whom power belongs to, but in how one answers the question of whom power serves.
quoteZh: 真正的差别并不在于是否承认权力为人民所赋，亦即不在于如何回答权力“归属谁”的问题，而在于如何回答权力“服务谁”的问题。

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernization of the state governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal first set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) as part of deepening reform. It covers both the institutional system of governance and its performance.

The author's term for the ideas, values, beliefs and customs of a society, as distinct from the political superstructure of formal institutions. Yang derives it from Marx's wider uses of "superstructure".
A guiding principle of Party governance emphasised under Xi Jinping: development is for the people, relies on the people and its fruits are shared by the people.
A stated goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, stressed in recent years, aiming at prosperity shared by all rather than by a few.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.

t: Marx and Engels on building the political capacity of the proletarian party, and its contemporary value
zh: 马克思恩格斯无产阶级政党政治能力建设思想及其当代价值
paras: Ma Mingchong asks what Marx and Engels thought about building the political capacity of the proletarian party, and what that thinking offers the Communist Party of China today. The article argues that political capacity is the party's most fundamental and first-ranking capacity. Although Marx and Engels never coined a formal concept of it, Ma contends that their writings and practice amount to a coherent body of thought. Ma opens by linking this to the emphasis on political capacity placed by the Party leadership around Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The article has three parts. The first sets out the basic content of the thought: its aim of human emancipation, and its orientation towards political leadership, political judgement, political comprehension and political execution. Ma ties these four to the "political judgement, comprehension and execution" now stressed in Party documents. The second part derives principles from three relationships: capacity and power, capacity and authority, and capacity and Party consciousness. The third part draws five contemporary implications, supported by texts from Marx, Engels and Lenin.

Ma's central move is to read Marx and Engels's practical positions as components of political capacity. Examples are the Communist League's collective decision-making and annual congresses (leadership), Engels's shift to legal means in the 1870s and insistence on the party's independence (judgement), and political exposure and agitation, the party press and class struggle (execution). On the three relationships, Ma argues that capacity wins power, and that both rest on the principle of the people. Authority comes from capacity and is voluntarily accepted, and it is often embodied in leaders chosen for their ability. Capacity and consciousness advance together through self-criticism.

For the present, Ma calls for placing political capacity first in Party political building and for holding firmly to political direction, which Ma treats as the guarantee of the party's proletarian character. Ma also calls for strengthening collective leadership, political mobilisation around ideals and conviction, and struggle capacity to preserve unity. The decline of the Soviet Communist Party is offered as a cautionary case, and Ma links the task to the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar draws on Marx and Engels's texts to ground current Party-building doctrine.
quoteEn: The political capacity and the political power of the proletarian party stand in a relationship of unity of opposites.
quoteZh: 无产阶级政党政治能力和政治权力是对立统一的关系。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 20th Party Congress resolution (2022). It affirms Xi Jinping's status as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.zh: 政治判断力、政治领悟力、政治执行力
glossary.pinyin: zhèngzhì pànduànlì, zhèngzhì lǐngwùlì, zhèngzhì zhíxínglì
glossary.explanation: Three abilities that Party leaders have required of cadres since the 2019 education campaign. They cover assessing the political situation, grasping the leadership's intentions, and carrying out decisions.

t: The generative logic of data capital and its general and specific characteristics: an interpretation based on Marxist political economy
zh: 数据资本的生成逻辑及其资本一般性和特殊性——基于马克思主义政治经济学的阐释
paras: Wang Shuixing and Qiu Mengwen ask how data becomes capital and what distinguishes data capital from earlier forms. Starting from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) call to build national data infrastructure, they argue that data capital is a new form of capital that embodies and deepens capital's general features while having its own distinctive properties. They present a scientific view of data capital as necessary for regulating and guiding its healthy development.

The article has three main parts followed by a conclusion. The first traces the sequence "raw data – data resource – data commodity – data capital". The second draws on Marx's classic texts to define capital's general character and shows how data capital manifests it. The third sets out the general features of data (immateriality, ubiquity, dependence, diverse sources) and then four specific attributes of data capital.

The authors reconstruct the genesis of data capital as a process of capitalist appropriation. Platforms collect users' traces and take over ownership of the data, which the authors call a modern "data enclosure movement". Hired "data labourers" then process it into commodities and so create surplus value, and users' continued activity supplies fresh raw material for expanded accumulation. They summarise capital's general character as profit-seeking, motion and "subjection to things" (wuyixing), and argue that data capital intensifies each. It shows stronger profit-seeking, faster circulation because data is immaterial, and a harsher domination of people by reified relations. Living labour remains the only source of surplus value, and the authors describe "data colonies" built by multinational firms. The four specific attributes are sustainable usability, comprehensive reach over production, consumption, distribution and social life, value multiplication, and deeper, more concealed exploitation. The last includes algorithmic management, the "996" working pattern, gig work, and the extraction of value from users' unpaid activity and leisure time.

The authors conclude that data capital has both a "civilising" side, which advances productive forces, and a "barbaric" side, namely more hidden exploitation and sharper polarisation under digital capitalism. For China they call for upholding and improving the socialist market economy, accelerating independent innovation in digital technology, building an autonomous Chinese knowledge system for the digital society, and regulating data capital so that data is "taken from the people and used for the people", in service of common prosperity. Read the original if you want a Marxist political-economy account of data as capital, linked to Chinese policy on data governance and common prosperity.
quoteEn: Although data capital is an innovation in the form of capital, it has not changed the reification of people's relations by capital, nor the essence of the exploitation and squeezing of workers.
quoteZh: 数据资本虽然是对资本样态的创新，但并没有改变资本对人的关系的物化以及对劳动者剥削压榨的本质。

glossary.explanation: A long-term goal of Chinese socialism, stressed in Party policy since the 2010s, of shared affluence and narrower gaps in wealth and income.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and state guidance.
The authors' term for workers hired by platforms to clean, process and analyse data into commodities. They distinguish them from ordinary users, whose traces merely supply raw data.
The authors' own coinage for the third general feature of capital: material means of production take on a social power that dominates and enslaves wage workers.
A term for capitalism in the era of digital platforms and data. The authors hold that it remains capitalism, still resting on exploitation of living labour.

t: A historical-materialist interpretation of "major reforms must have a legal basis"
zh: “重大改革于法有据”的历史唯物主义阐释
paras: Yang Jun, writing in Guangming Daily in October 2025, asks how reform and the rule of law can be coordinated, and argues that Xi Jinping's proposition that major reforms must have a legal basis can be explained from the standpoint of historical materialism. Yang presents it as an original proposition within Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law and as the latest result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The commentary has three parts. It first sets out the context: Xi first stated the principle in November 2013 and it was repeated at later plenums, including the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It then gives the theoretical logic, and finally four practical steps for carrying the principle out.

Yang identifies a tension between reform, which breaks with existing arrangements, and law, which keeps order through fixed norms. Yang also notes that some reforms have been pushed forward at the cost of legality. The theoretical argument has three moves. Reform and law share a basic value, since law expresses the will determined by the people's common interests, citing The German Ideology. Law secures the socialist direction, predictability and long-term stability of reform. Law is historical, rooted in the mode of production, so existing law must guide reform where it still fits, and law reform becomes part of reform where it lags.

In practice, Yang calls for four steps: identify the legal basis in current law when a reform is planned; review whether conflicts with current law can be resolved by interpretation or require breaking with it; amend the law at the outset where conditions allow; and otherwise obtain formal legislative authorisation for pilot reforms, then codify proven experience. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how current Party legal theory links reform and legality, including the stages of legislative practice it proposes.
quoteEn: Major reform and the rule of law are deeply aligned in their fundamental values.
quoteZh: 重大改革与法治在根本价值上深度契合。

glossary.pinyin: zhòngdà gǎigé yú fǎ yǒu jù
glossary.en: major reforms must have a legal basis
glossary.literal: major reforms are grounded in law
glossary.explanation: A principle stated by Xi Jinping in 2013 that significant reforms should rest on legal authority. It is part of Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas on law and governance attributed to Xi Jinping, formally adopted as guidance for work on the legal system in 2020.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for developing Marxism in line with China's conditions and the current era.

t: On the new alienation of emotional labour in digital capitalism and its dissolution
zh: 论数字资本主义情感劳动新异化及其消解
paras: This article from World Socialism Studies (2025, no. 6) asks how emotional labour is newly alienated under digital capitalism and how that alienation might be dissolved. Ma Chao argues that digital technology has not changed the essence of alienated labour under capitalist relations of production, but has made it broader, deeper and better hidden than in the industrial era. The remedy, in Ma's view, lies ultimately in abolishing capitalist private ownership, with interim measures available now.

The article has four parts. It first distinguishes Hochschild's "emotional labour" from Hardt and Negri's "affective labour" and defines the digital form. It then describes four concrete manifestations, analyses three underlying logics, and finally proposes paths to dissolving the alienation. Examples come mainly from live-streaming, short video, fan labour and virtual companionship services.

Drawing on Marx's theory of productive labour, Ma holds that emotional labour is non-productive because it neither yields material commodities nor can be measured in socially necessary labour time. It is nonetheless commodified and drawn into capital's valorisation, for example by lengthening hours or intensifying work. Ma maps Marx's four forms of alienation onto algorithmic recommendation ("addictive emotional commodities"), traffic competition (staged personas), panoptic emotional surveillance ("unconscious spiritual colonisation") and covert platform discipline (three layers of exploitation, including free appropriation of user trace data). These are traced to a capital–technology logic (platform capitalisation), a capital–consumption logic (commodification of private feeling) and a capital–institution logic (private ownership of emotional commodities).

Ma concludes that the fundamental way out is to abolish capitalist private ownership and rebuild individual ownership on common possession of the means of production, while accepting that digital capitalism cannot be removed in the short term. Meanwhile Ma proposes three reconstructions: of the technology logic (transparent, ethically reviewed algorithms and non-profit digital infrastructure), of the consumption logic (public, non-commercial emotional services and education against consumerism), and of the institutional logic (tiered data rights and copyright for emotional data). Read the original if you want a Marxist-theoretical treatment of platform labour, live-streaming and data rights that applies Marx's alienation framework to emotional work and ends with policy proposals.
quoteEn: Although digital capitalism has driven changes in the form of emotional labour, it has not changed the essence of labour alienation under capitalist relations of production.
quoteZh: 数字资本主义尽管推动了情感劳动的形态变化，却没有改变资本主义生产关系下劳动异化的本质。

t: Marx and Engels's fourfold critique of Russian Narodism and its scientific method
zh: 马克思恩格斯对俄国民粹主义的四重批判及其科学方法
paras: How did Marx and Engels argue against the Russian Narodnik (populist) claim that Russia could bypass capitalism and move directly to socialism? Ji Mengling and Wang Yonggui argue that the critique had four parts, each aimed at a distinct Narodnik thesis and each using a distinct analytical method. In their reading, together these parts exposed the theoretical errors of Narodism and gave guidance on whether a 'non-capitalist path' was possible.

The article draws on Marx and Engels's direct polemics, including 'Refugee Literature' and 'On Social Relations in Russia', Marx's letter to the editorial board of Otechestvennye Zapiski, his correspondence with Vera Zasulich, and the 1882 Russian preface to the Communist Manifesto. It treats Herzen, Lavrov, Bakunin, Tkachev and Mikhailovsky as the Narodnik interlocutors. The four sections take up the 'superiority of the village commune', the 'revolutionary advantage of Russia', the 'peasantry as revolutionary subject' and the 'non-capitalist path utopia'.

On the commune, the authors say Marx and Engels used historical analysis to show that communal land ownership and the artel were forms suited to backward conditions, and that the Russian commune was being dissolved from within and by the 1861 emancipation. On revolutionary advantage, Engels used comparison to argue that socialist revolution presupposes both bourgeoisie and proletariat, and that the tsarist state served the nobility's interests. He therefore judged Tkachev's claim that Russia lacked these classes to be detached from reality. On the peasantry, class analysis showed their isolation and weakness, which made them unreliable as a leading revolutionary force. Finally, dialectical analysis rejected both a deterministic reading of Western capitalist development and the idea that Russia could leap ahead alone. Russia might cross the 'Caudine Forks' of capitalism only if a Russian revolution and a proletarian revolution in the West complemented each other.

The authors conclude that Marx and Engels's critique was long-running and thorough, continuing after Marx's death, when Engels still called for struggle against Narodists everywhere. They hold that this critique displays the scientific method of Marx and Engels in dealing with rival currents of thought. They also present it as a source of methodological guidance and experience for criticising erroneous social trends today. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist account of how Marx and Engels's analytical methods were applied to Russian Narodism, with close attention to the specific texts.
quoteEn: Marx and Engels's critique of Russian Narodism not only vividly displays the scientific method and distinctive wisdom with which they struggled against different currents of thought, but also offers methodological guidance and experience for our present-day work of criticising erroneous social trends.
quoteZh: 马克思恩格斯对俄国民粹主义的批判不仅生动展现了他们与不同社会思潮斗争的科学方法和独特智慧，也为我们当今的错误社会思潮批判工作提供了方法指导和经验借鉴。

t: Clarifying Marx's concept of productive forces: disputes, misreadings and corrections
zh: 马克思的生产力概念辨析：争议、误读与澄清
paras: Liu Wei and Huan Yingqi take up a long-running problem in Marxist theory: scholars still dispute and misread what Marx meant by "productive forces". The authors argue that this blurs the concept and weakens current work on new quality productive forces. Their thesis is that Marx's mature concept is single and coherent, and that it can be recovered by reading Capital, Volume I closely.

The article first sets out a method. Early texts such as the German Ideology and the letter to Annenkov, and Marx's unpublished manuscripts, are treated as secondary to Capital, Volume I, which Marx himself prepared for publication. Four sections follow: the content of the concept, the "factor productive forces" formulations, the claim that the concept has a double meaning, and the place of science and technology. Along the way the authors discuss Lefebvre, Bukharin, Stalin, Wang Xuewen and G. A. Cohen.

Liu and Huan define productive force as the overall power that arises when living labour, objectified labour and natural conditions combine. Marx's references to "new" productive forces created by cooperation or the division of labour are read as the surplus gained from organisation. Expressions such as "individual" or "machine" productive forces are said to follow the usage of Marx's day and not to introduce new concepts. Hence the authors reject proliferating labels such as "data productive forces". They also deny that Marx had separate philosophical and economic meanings, arguing that the difference lies in scope (the whole of society versus a given production process). On technology, they hold that it is not an extra factor and not a "permeating element". It is instead a specification of how the existing factors are combined and of their properties and quantities. Science, they argue, becomes a productive force only when applied through technology, and Marx's remarks on why eighteenth-century British capital could exploit scientific advances are cited in support.

For research on new quality productive forces, the authors call for avoiding the habit of loading every possible factor into the concept. They propose studying it through concrete labour processes at the levels of the firm, the industry and the industrial system. They also argue that treating all science as a productive force may have fed the "two skins" problem between scientific research and the economy. They conclude that science policy should focus on the application of science to industry. Read the original if you want a close, text-based argument about Marx's productive forces and its bearing on how Chinese scholars theorise new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: This article proposes that technology is not a factor of production but a specific determination of the factors of production; science in itself does not directly constitute a productive force, and becomes part of productive forces only when applied in technology.
quoteZh: 本文提出，技术不是生产要素，而是对生产要素的特殊规定；科学本身并不直接构成生产力，而必须应用于技术才成为生产力的内容。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by innovation and linked to high-quality development. Chinese scholars are currently working to give it theoretical grounding.
The authors' label for expressions that attribute productive force to a single factor, such as knowledge, land or data. They argue these are not separate concepts in Marx.

glossary.literal: scientific research and the economy as two separate skins
glossary.explanation: A common Chinese phrase for the disconnect between scientific research and economic practice, where research results are not applied in production.

t: How the young Marx's view of socialism sublated the thought of Moses Hess
zh: 青年马克思社会主义观对赫斯思想的扬弃
source: Contemporary World Socialism Issues (Dangdai shijie shehuizhuyi wenti), 2025 no. 2
paras: How did socialism move from an ethical ideal to a scientific theory? Liu and Wang take up this question by tracing the relation between the young Marx and Moses Hess, whom they call the "father of German socialism". They argue that Marx critically absorbed Hess's philosophical communism between 1841 and 1845 and then sublated it, replacing Hess's subjective-idealist, ethical socialism with a socialism grounded in historical materialism and political economy.

The article has four parts. It first describes the German context of the 1830s and 1840s: mass pauperization, the arrival of French socialist ideas, and the rival paths of Wilhelm Weitling and Hess. It then sets out Hess's three contributions: the "philosophy of action", the critique of communication and money as alienation, and the ideal of a free and then "organic" community. The third part shows how Marx took up Hess's ideas from the Rheinische Zeitung to the 1844 Manuscripts. The fourth part explains how Marx went beyond Hess.

The authors identify three points of departure. First, Hess confined his attention to the sphere of money and exchange and rejected capitalism from outside. Marx grasped the dialectic of civil society and of labour, distinguishing objectified from alienated labour and seeing capitalism as a historically necessary, transitory form. Second, Marx added private property as the link that moves the analysis from alienated communication to alienated labour. He later made production determine the forms of intercourse, which yields the productive forces–forms of intercourse framework of historical materialism. Third, Hess retreated to "loving union" and the abstract "human race", while Marx located the agent of communism in the proletariat and its revolutionary practice, which changes relations of production.

The authors conclude that the path from Hess to Marx shows socialism becoming a science. They present this as a rebuttal to current trends that reduce socialism to a value-based utopia or to social concern. They bring in Althusser's "break" but stress that scientific socialism does not reject subjective values. In their reading Marx's view of socialism is a unity of ethical value and scientific logic. Read the original if you study the young Marx, the Hess–Marx relationship or the sources of historical materialism, and want a Chinese scholarly account of the passage from Hess's ethical socialism to scientific socialism.
quoteEn: Marx's view of socialism is in essence a unity of ethical value and scientific logic.
quoteZh: 马克思的社会主义观本质上是伦理价值与科学逻辑的统一。

glossary.explanation: Hess's programme of turning speculative philosophy into a guide for revolutionary practice, centred on free, self-determining activity.
The term for the socialism of Marx and Engels, based on historical materialism and the critique of political economy, as opposed to utopian socialism.
Hess's term for a rational, organised and diverse human society in which labour and enjoyment are united and each person develops freely.

t: Reanalysing the relationship between Marx and Feuerbach in the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right
zh: 《黑格尔法哲学批判》中马克思与费尔巴哈思想关系再分析
paras: Did the young Marx, when writing his 1843 manuscript Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, still work inside Feuerbach's anthropological materialism? Chen Weici argues that Feuerbach's influence was real but limited, and that earlier scholarship has overstated it and so hidden Marx's own theoretical agency (主体性). The article, published in Theoretical Studies in 2025, contends that Marx's use of Feuerbachian vocabulary and method already served different aims.

The article opens by setting out the "Feuerbach factors" in the manuscript: the subject–predicate inversion method and a humanist stance, shown in Marx's emphasis on popular sovereignty, democracy and the abolition of the estates. It then rebuts Louis Althusser's reading, drawing on MEGA2 debates over the manuscript's dating, on Charles Barber, Z. Rosen, David McLellan, Rubel-era and Soviet editors, and on Rabin. The final part presents Marx's creative use of the inversion method and his concretisation of humanism.

Chen's main moves are three. First, against Althusser, Chen argues that the concept of a "problematic" is undefined and serves his thesis of a rupture, and that Marx gave borrowed terms such as alienation and species-being different meanings, emphasising sociality rather than natural attributes. Second, Chen holds that dating the manuscript by Feuerbach's influence is circular, and that Marx used the inversion method earlier in his notes on Epicurean philosophy and in his closeness to Bruno Bauer. The decisive spur to criticising Hegel, Chen says, was Marx's work on the Rheinische Zeitung, where problems such as the wood-theft debate forced him to confront private property and material interests. Third, Marx retained the negative side of Hegel's dialectic, insisting that civil society and the political state are separate extremes that cannot mediate each other. He also turned Feuerbach's abstract sensuous being into a critique of the state's internal institutions.

Chen concludes that Marx replaced Feuerbach's abstract "species-essence" with the real human being living in society, and extended this to a demand for popular legislative power based on universal suffrage and, ultimately, an association of free people. Neglecting this agency, the author says, feeds readings such as the "rupture thesis" and the "two Marxes", which break the continuity of Marx's thought. Read the original if you work on the young Marx, the dating debates around the 1843 manuscript, or the Chinese reception of Althusser's reading of Feuerbach.
quoteEn: With a realist and critical spirit, Marx went beyond Feuerbach's humanism and overcame its abstractness, taking the "real human being" living in society, rather than the abstract "species-essence", as his theoretical premise, and thereby brought out the agency of his theoretical construction.
quoteZh: 马克思以现实、批判的精神超越了费尔巴哈的人本主义，克服了其抽象性，将生活在社会中的“现实的人”作为理论前提，而非抽象的“类本质”,由此凸显了其理论建构的主体性。

glossary.literal: method of inverting subject and predicate
glossary.explanation: A critical procedure, associated with Feuerbach's critique of speculative philosophy, that treats what Hegel makes a predicate (such as thought) as dependent on its real subject (being). Marx used it against Hegel's philosophy of the state.
Here it denotes the independent, self-directed character of Marx's own theoretical construction, as opposed to its being derived from Feuerbach.
The view, associated with Althusser, that Marx's thought divides into an early humanist phase and a later scientific one separated by an epistemological break.

keywords: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

t: Marx's "inversion" of Hegel's dialectic seen through the development of historical materialism
zh: 从唯物史观发展脉络看马克思对黑格尔辩证法的“颠倒”
source: Journal of Xi'an Shiyou University (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 3
paras: Lu Tong and Gu Dongyue take up the question of what Marx actually did when he "inverted" Hegel's dialectic. They argue that the usual reading, which treats it as a switch from idealism to materialism or a transplanting of the dialectic onto a materialist foundation, is formalistic and misses Hegel's "rational kernel". In their account, historical materialism is a change of theoretical framework: from an "abstract philosophical dialectic" to a "concrete historical dialectic" grounded in people's real productive activity.

The article reads Marx's works in sequence to trace the inversion as a gradual process. It first reconstructs Hegel's "one–many–one" structure, in the Phenomenology of Spirit, the Logic and the overall system. It then follows Marx through the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology. A closing section draws out the implications.

The authors argue that for Hegel, estrangement and its sublation are both activities of consciousness, moving from an initial concept through opposed concepts to a higher one. Marx first reversed the starting point in the Critique, making civil society rather than the idea of the state the beginning. In the 1844 Manuscripts he turned Hegelian estrangement into estranged labour, whose structure the authors regard as identical, and relocated the negation of the negation into real life. They hold that this was still unfinished, since it rested on a humanist return to human essence. Marx completed the inversion in the Theses and The German Ideology. He recast the structure as "many–one–many", with practice as its form, and found the motive force of history in the development of people's needs for production and life. On this reading the negation of the negation becomes only a phenomenal regularity of history, not its logical premise.

The authors conclude that Marx inverted Hegel's dialectic in four respects: its starting point, its sphere, its structure and its driving force. The result is historical materialism, which unites the dialectic with human productive activity and makes it open rather than a closed circle. They also claim that once human needs become the premise of the dialectic, "the human being" steps out from behind thought. They add that this lays a theoretical foundation for proletarian liberation, the free and all-round development of the person and the "modernization of the human being". Read the original if you want a close, text-by-text account of how Marx's early works relate to Hegel's logic of "one" and "many".
quoteEn: Historical materialism is not a merely formal "inversion" of Hegel's dialectic but a transformation of its theoretical framework.
quoteZh: 历史唯物主义并非是对黑格尔辩证法形式上的“颠倒”,而是对其理论框架的转换

t: The Communist Manifesto's scientific construction of the Marxist discourse system and its significance
zh: 《共产党宣言》对马克思主义话语体系的科学构建及其意义
source: Socialist Studies (社会主义研究), 2025 no. 3
paras: Zhao Ende and Han Haitao ask how Marx and Engels built a Marxist discourse system in The Communist Manifesto, and what that example offers for building a Marxist discourse system suited to China and to the present.
