Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese university Party official presents the status of Marxism's basic principles and the guidelines for interpreting them.
quoteEn: The key reason Marxism is truth is that its basic principles are universal truths, not that every statement by Marx and Engels over a century ago fits contemporary reality.
quoteZh: 马克思主义之所以是真理，关键在于马克思主义基本原理是普遍真理，而不在于马克思、恩格斯在百余年前的所有论述皆与当代现实发展高度契合。

glossary.explanation: A formula associated with Xi Jinping: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is presented as the fundamental route to adapting Marxism in China.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of national development, promoted since the early 2020s as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: upholding what is correct while innovating
glossary.literal: guard the correct, create the new
glossary.explanation: A slogan in Party discourse meaning to keep to fundamental principles while innovating in theory and practice.

t: The theoretical features of Marx's idea of the emancipation of labour
zh: 马克思劳动解放思想的理论特质
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily (28 July 2025), Yan Guohong asks where Marx's idea of the emancipation of labour comes from and what its core content is. Yan argues that the idea is not an isolated innovation but a dialectical sublation of ancient Greek and Roman philosophy, German classical philosophy and classical political economy. At its centre, in Yan's account, is the link between labour and human liberation, aimed at the free and all-round development of the human being.

The short article has two parts. The first traces three sources: Aristotle and Cicero; Kant and Hegel; and William Petty, Adam Smith and David Ricardo. The second sets out the basic core of the idea around three questions: what labour is, how labour is emancipated, and by what path. A brief closing note ties the idea to the present.

Yan argues that each source gave Marx something specific. Aristotle's distinction between the labour of free people and the toil of slaves showed that labour has a social-historical character. Cicero's remarks on hired labour pointed to an early form of alienation. Kant supplied the principle that the human being is an end in itself, and Hegel the dialectical view of labour as both transforming nature and forming the self. Classical economists supplied the labour theory of value, which Marx developed into the theory of surplus value. In the core of the idea, Yan presents labour as the species-activity that distinguishes humans from animals. Under capitalism it becomes alienated, so that it affirms the worker's self no longer. Emancipation therefore requires abolishing the capitalist system and establishing socialism, and it also depends on highly developed productive forces that cut necessary labour and let labour become life's prime need.

Yan concludes that the idea retains contemporary value. Technology is reshaping forms of labour, and the sharing economy is reshaping the distribution of value. Yan states that the idea provides theoretical support and guidance for advancing Chinese modernization through high-quality development. Read the original if you want a compact survey, in the style of a Party-school commentary, of the intellectual lineage and main propositions of Marx's theory of labour emancipation.
quoteEn: The emancipation of labour rests on highly developed productive forces. Only when social productive forces are developed enough to create abundant material wealth that meets people's needs can labour change from a means of "making a living" into "life's prime want", and so return to its essence.
quoteZh: 劳动解放建立在高度发达的生产力之上，只有当社会生产力达到足够发达的水平，创造出丰富的物质财富以满足人们的需要时，劳动才能从“谋生”的手段转变为“生活的第一需要”，从而实现劳动的本质回归。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, developed in Party discourse especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official economic goal, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

t: Grasping the theoretical meaning of "measure" scientifically
zh: 科学把握“度”的理论内涵
paras: This newspaper commentary (Guangming Daily, 25 July 2025) asks what "measure" (du) means in Marxist philosophy and why it matters for practice. Zhang argues that measure is the link between quantitative and qualitative change. It is also a key yardstick for understanding how things develop, analysing social phenomena and guiding action. Zhang notes that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi Jinping has repeatedly stressed grasping measure, for instance in the art of struggle, in macroeconomic regulation and in resource use.

The piece has three parts. The first treats measure as the critical point between quantity and quality. The second links measure to the relation between truth and error. The third turns to how the Party and state should recognise, grasp and apply measure on the new journey. Zhang draws on Marx, Engels (including Dialectics of Nature) and Lenin (Philosophical Notebooks).

Zhang defines measure as the boundary beyond which accumulated quantitative change produces a qualitative leap. It marks the limit of a thing's old quality and the starting point of a new one, and it also serves as a gauge of stability and of stages of development. Citing Engels and Lenin, Zhang adds that truth holds only within certain conditions and limits. Going "one small step further" past them turns truth into error, so people must test and develop truth in practice, starting from reality.

Zhang calls for accurate recognition of measure, which means keeping to bottom-line thinking and using certainty to meet uncertainty. Zhang also calls for objective grasp of measure, and for scientific application of it that draws on the Party's sense of historical initiative. Examples include differentiated ecological management, risk early-warning in science and technology, and Chinese modernization. Zhang concludes that turning the philosophy of measure into institutional effectiveness supports high-quality development. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-affiliated scholars link dialectical categories to current policy language.
quoteEn: "Measure is the boundary point by which the accumulation of a thing's quantitative change is gauged."
quoteZh: “度”是衡量事物量变积累的边界点。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, set out by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official economic goal, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
A Hegelian-Marxist category for the unity of quality and quantity. It marks the range within which a thing keeps its quality, and quantitative change beyond it brings qualitative change.

glossary.literal: historical initiative / taking the initiative in history
glossary.explanation: A term in recent Party discourse for consciously grasping historical laws and seizing the initiative in development.

t: The self-identity crisis in accelerated capitalist society and its critique from political economy
zh: 加速资本主义社会的自我认同危机及其政治经济学批判
source: Journal of University of Science and Technology Beijing (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 4
paras: Wang Xiaoxia asks why individuals in what Hartmut Rosa calls accelerated capitalist society, above all in the digital age, suffer a crisis of self-identity. The article argues that the crisis grows out of capital's logic of acceleration. This logic changes how people interact and exist, and produces a loss of meaning, a loss of trust, existential anxiety and false identification. Wang offers a critique grounded in Marxist political economy and proposes ways of sublating the crisis.

The article has three parts. The first defines self-identity, drawing on Marx's view of the human essence as the ensemble of social relations, on Giddens and on Rosa, and then traces three causes of the crisis. The second sets out three manifestations and criticises each in turn: commodification, the expansion of digital platforms, and the totalising logic of acceleration. The third turns to practical paths, at the levels of the individual, platform regulation and the critique of capital itself.

For the causes, Wang points to the inversion produced by money fetishism, the collusion of capital and technology in exploiting emotion, and competition that makes emotional choices a legitimate principle of distribution. The manifestations are then examined. Commodification shapes false self-identity through consumerism and narcissism. Platforms create risks of lost trust through online violence, surveillance of privacy and fraud. Acceleration turns individuals into self-exploiting 'achievement subjects' whose lives feel uncontrollable. Wang reads these as continuations of Marx's critique of machinery and of the capitalist as the 'driving wheel' of a society in which wage labourers are 'driven wheels'.

Wang proposes that individuals strengthen critical reflection, adopt a rational view of consumption, resist blind involution and protect their privacy. The state should improve laws on digital platforms, regulate online communication, including real-name registration, and make platforms balance economic and social benefits. Wang adds that capital has a dual character, civilising and exploitative, and that the logic of capital can be transcended only by sublating capitalist relations of production through their own contradictions. Read the original if you are interested in how Rosa's theory of social acceleration is combined with Marxist political economy to analyse digital capitalism and subjectivity, and in the policy remedies Wang draws from it.
quoteEn: The commodification strategy of accelerated capitalist society shapes a false consciousness of self-identity.
quoteZh: 加速资本主义社会的商品化战略塑造了虚假自我认同意识。

glossary.explanation: Hartmut Rosa's characterisation of modern capitalism as driven by technological acceleration, social change and an increasing pace of life.
Marx's concept of how money conceals social relations of labour and makes them appear as natural properties of things.
The rendering of Aufhebung: overcoming something while retaining its valuable elements.
A popular term for intense, self-defeating competition in which rising effort yields no gain in return.

t: The logic and path of promoting all-round human development through new quality productive forces
zh: 以新质生产力推动人的全面发展的逻辑与路径
paras: Song Ziling and Qiu Gengtian ask how new quality productive forces can advance the all-round development of the human being. They note that existing scholarship has studied the concept's meaning, features and applications but has rarely linked it to human development. Their thesis is that new quality productive forces are a milestone form of productivity that supplies the material conditions for all-round development, provided that technological innovation is steered by talent and kept ethically in check.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the features of all-round development under Chinese modernization, drawing on Marx's multiple determinations of human essence: the all-round development of practical activity, the enrichment of social relations, and the improvement of overall quality. The second explains the logic through which new quality productive forces enable this development, in four respects. The third turns to practical paths centred on technological innovation, covering talent, the proper use of emerging technology and its ethical risks.

On the logic, the authors argue that new quality productive forces raise practical capacity by strengthening subjects' cognition, extending practice into non-material objects such as data and information, and increasing interaction between subject and object. They widen social interaction through digital media and reduce physical distance. They loosen the old division of labour through platform and gig work, cross-field technological integration and new industries such as unmanned factories. They also lengthen free time through efficiency gains, flexible work and the sharing economy. On the paths, the authors call for cultivating high-calibre talent while also developing ordinary workers, and for using technology "wisely". They analyse Industry 4.0 as an example of new quality productive forces, but also warn of its risks, including cities dominated by industry and the loss of personal data. In their account, these ethical risks stem from the excessive capitalisation of science and technology, which produces new forms of alienation.

The authors conclude that promoting all-round human development through new quality productive forces is an irreversible historical trend. They propose a talent-development mechanism, humane, ecological smart cities, and a division of responsibility among government, enterprises and individuals for privacy and data security. The aim is to turn the "misuse" of technology into its "proper use" so that its benefits reach all people. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese theorists tie the concept of new quality productive forces to Marx's theory of human development, including its treatment of free time, the division of labour and technological alienation.
quoteEn: The ethical risks of new quality productive forces are rooted in the excessive capitalisation of science and technology.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的伦理风险根源于科学技术的过度资本化。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24. It denotes advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading, with higher total factor productivity as its key marker.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: comprehensive development of the human being
glossary.explanation: A Marxist idea of the full development of human capacities, social relations and individuality. Chinese official discourse treats it as the ultimate goal of socialism and modernization.

t: Coordinating aggregate supply and aggregate demand to keep the national economic cycle unobstructed
zh: 统筹好总供给和总需求的关系，畅通国民经济循环
paras: Liu Wei and Fan Xin take up one of the "five musts" drawn from the Central Economic Work Conference of December 2024: the need to coordinate the relationship between aggregate supply and aggregate demand and keep the national economic cycle unobstructed. The authors argue that this principle is a basic problem of macroeconomic theory and the underlying logic of China's macroeconomic regulation. They also hold that it is the urgent requirement for countering the current shrinkage of both supply and demand.

The article has three parts. It first surveys how Western and Marxist economics have treated supply and demand: classical economics, the German historical school, Keynesianism and its offshoots, supply-side economics, national accounting, and Marx's theory of social capital reproduction. It then traces China's practice, from "comprehensive balance" under the planned economy to three phases of macro-regulation since reform and opening up. The last part diagnoses present conditions and sets out policy proposals.

The authors contend that classical economics stressed supply because supply shortage and free competition defined the industrial revolution, while Keynes's demand analysis answered the Great Depression. In Liu and Fan's reading, Marx's two-department reproduction model explains the institutional roots of capitalist crises and guides analysis of socialist reproduction. They divide China's regulation into demand management (1978–2012), supply-side structural reform as the main line (2012–2021), and, since the 20th Party Congress (2022), coordination of both ends. For the present, they cite persistently negative price indices, weakening consumption and investment, corporate difficulties, industrial restructuring, rising factor costs and external pressure from US and Western tariffs, monetary shifts and technology controls. They judge that demand contraction currently hits harder than supply contraction.

Liu and Fan call for expanding domestic demand and strengthening the domestic circulation, while continuing supply-side structural reform and pursuing high-quality supply that leads demand. They also propose four steps. The first is linking medium- and long-term strategic planning with annual targets. The second is coordinating fiscal, monetary and other policies through consistency assessment. The third is shifting to a "more proactive fiscal policy and moderately loose monetary policy". The fourth is deepening reform to build a high-standard socialist market economy, so that demand pulls supply and supply creates demand. Read the original if you want a systematic, official-aligned account of how Chinese economists place current macro policy within the history of supply-and-demand theory and of reform-era regulation.
quoteEn: Imbalance is the normal state; equilibrium is only a theoretical assumption.
quoteZh: 失衡是常态，均衡只是理论假设。

glossary.explanation: A policy line introduced by Xi Jinping in 2015. It aims to resolve structural problems such as overcapacity by improving the quality and efficiency of supply rather than only stimulating demand.

glossary.literal: comprehensive balance of the national economy
glossary.explanation: A planning concept of the planned-economy era that sought balance among materials, finance, credit and foreign exchange, with fiscal balance as its key.
An annual closed-door meeting of Party and state leaders, held in December, that sets economic priorities and policy tone for the coming year.

t: Critical strategy and methodology in the face of the production of abstract space
st: A reading of Lefebvre's The Production of Space
zh: 面对抽象空间生产的批判战略与方法论
zhSub: 列斐伏尔《空间的生产》解读
paras: Zhang Yibing reads the methodological discussion in Henri Lefebvre's The Production of Space, asking how a critical theory can confront an abstract space of capitalism whose relations of domination are invisible behind economic appearances. Zhang argues that Lefebvre responds with three linked proposals: a critical strategic hypothesis grounded in historical materialism, a regressive–progressive method of historical analysis, and the reconstruction of spatial codes. Zhang values these but repeatedly judges that Lefebvre cannot say how a spatial revolution would actually be carried out.

The article follows three sections. The first treats the historical-materialist premises of spatial critique, the second the regressive–progressive method and its Marxian origin, and the third the rebuilding of spatial codes and the political strategy for change. Zhang draws on Lefebvre's other works, including Critique of Everyday Life and The Survival of Capitalism, and on Marx's Grundrisse, Sartre, Foucault and Lenin.

In the first section, Zhang reports Lefebvre's claim that contemporary abstract space has become a technologically programmed, surveilled realm of social engineering. Lefebvre rejects idealist theories of discursive or Cartesian mental space, grounds spatial theory in the three material productions of The German Ideology, and holds that the production of space has replaced or overlain the production of things, allowing capitalism to survive. Zhang adds that Lefebvre fails to ask "whose technological utopia?" In the second section, Lefebvre takes Marx's idea that the anatomy of man is a key to the anatomy of the ape and applies it to space. Zhang explains that it also works synchronically: advanced capitalist space, such as the firms Microsoft and Apple, illuminates labour-intensive production elsewhere, and polluting industry is moved to poorer countries. In the third section, Zhang argues that recoding space through new language unifying public and private, inside and outside, work and non-work, will remain subjective unless the mode of production changes.

Zhang concludes that Lefebvre's strategic hypothesis is directionally right but vague. It rejects the Russian single-centre model, allows for revolutionary subjects drawn from the margins or from the developed working class, and accepts both violent and parliamentary paths. Zhang observes that it offers no workable plan for breaking Western capital's domination of world space. Read the original if you want a critical Chinese reading of Lefebvre's spatial methodology and its limits, set against Marx's historical method and unequal capitalist development.
quoteEn: If the production mechanism of capitalist abstract space is not genuinely changed and the mode of production thoroughly transformed, the discursive production and experience of space cannot be truly transformed.
quoteZh: 如果不能真正改变资本主义抽象空间的生产机制，彻底变革生产方式，空间话语生产及体验方式是不可能获得真正的变革的。

t: Progress and prospects in building the theoretical system of humanistic economics
zh: 人文经济学理论体系建构的进展和展望
paras: This literature review surveys the scholarship that followed Xi Jinping's 2023 call, made during the national "Two Sessions" while discussing the historic cities of Suzhou and Hangzhou, to study "humanistic economics" (renwen jingjixue). Wang and Duan ask where Chinese scholars have got to in building the field's theoretical system. They find a promising start but argue that most work still treats it as a branch of economics, when it needs to be understood as a theory of civilization.

The review is organised in five parts. It covers the field's basic features (object of study, disciplinary status, methods, nature), its theoretical content (the culture–economy relationship, theoretical foundations, significance), systematisation (historical genesis, discursive innovation, academic structure), and practical studies of humanistic-economy cities, Chinese modernization and new quality productive forces. A closing section assesses gaps and sets out directions.

On disciplinary status, the authors sort positions into three camps: economics (Luo Weidong, Bai Yongxiu), humanities and philosophy (Sun Ruru), and civilization studies (Fan Hao). They report scholars agreeing that historical materialism is the methodological base, but differing on specific methods. Many see the field as distinct from Western "humanistic" economics because it rests on a people-centred standpoint and on Marx's critique of political economy. Foundations are drawn from Marxism and from fine traditional Chinese culture, which one scholar, Ren Ping, says must be inherited as a whole rather than reduced to Confucian fragments. In practice, studies sort cities into types, examine Hangzhou, Suzhou and Nantong, and link humanistic economy to common prosperity, rural revitalisation and high-quality development.

Wang and Duan conclude that research remains tied to economics and cannot yet grasp the civilizational content of the "five-sphere" new civilizational order. They also note that some work narrows Chinese tradition to Confucianism, that case studies cluster in Suzhou, Hangzhou and developed eastern provinces, and that rural areas and corporate management get little attention. They call for work on basic categories, principles and methodology, and for linking humanistic economy to Chinese modernization, new quality productive forces and new production relations, with more attention to central and western regions. Read the original if you want a detailed map of who is arguing what in China's emerging humanistic economics debate, with many named scholars and positions.
quoteEn: It must be pointed out, however, that the discussion of the theoretical foundations of humanistic economics has mostly concentrated on its economic-thought foundations, while the theoretical foundations in politics, culture, society, ecological civilization and other directions and fields have yet to be explored.
quoteZh: 但需要指出的是，这里对人文经济学理论基础的讨论大多集中于人文经济学的经济思想基础，而政治、文化、社会、生态文明等多方向、多领域的理论基础尚未被发掘。

glossary.explanation: A proposition Xi Jinping put forward in 2023, asking scholars to study how culture and economy interact and reinforce each other in cities such as Suzhou and Hangzhou. Chinese scholars are now developing it into a theoretical field.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced, innovation-driven productive forces that depart from resource-heavy growth.
A official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, stressed in Party policy as a requirement of socialism.
The official policy goal of shifting from fast, extensive growth to growth that is innovative, coordinated, green and shared.

t: Understanding Xi Jinping's important discourse on the modernized industrial system
zh: 深刻理解习近平总书记关于现代化产业体系的重要论述
paras: Lin Muxi and Wang Cong set out to explain what Xi Jinping has said since the 18th Party Congress (2012) about building a modernized industrial system. They present it as a coherent body of ideas that guides high-quality development and the building of a modern socialist country. Their thesis is that the discourse is a scientific theoretical system, rooted in China's industrial history and responsive to present conditions.

The article moves through five parts. It traces the historical and practical background, from industrialisation under the Western blockade and the self-reliance line after 1949 to the shift of the industrial structure in the 2010s. It then discusses the significance of the discourse, its internal content (connotation, features, tasks), its practical requirements, and finally its value. The practical section covers the "five adherences", innovation-led development, and institutional reforms in areas such as services, infrastructure, supply-chain security and education, science and talent.

The authors argue that the modernized industrial system is a distinct step beyond earlier formulas such as the "modern industrial system" of the 17th Party Congress (2007). In their reading, it places industry within the overall plan for national modernization. They define its content as an integrated system of the real economy, technological innovation, modern finance and human resources, and as one that is complete, advanced and secure. They call for new quality productive forces, led by technological innovation, and for upgrading traditional industries rather than phasing them out. They contend that the real economy, especially manufacturing, must remain the foundation.

In the authors' account, the discourse sums up China's industrialisation experience and moves beyond mainstream Western theory, which treats a service share of 70 per cent or more as the mark of a modern economy and which they link to deindustrialisation. They also say it develops Marxist productive-force theory and offers developing countries a Chinese approach to modernization. They call for further systematic and theoretical study of the discourse. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese economists present the policy logic behind industrial upgrading, supply-chain security and technological self-reliance.
quoteEn: In proposing the building of a modernized industrial system, General Secretary Xi Jinping did not blindly copy Western theories of \"modern industrial structure\" or deliberately lower the share of industry in order to raise that of services.
quoteZh: 习近平总书记提出建设现代化产业体系，没有盲目照搬西方“现代产业结构”理论，不刻意降低工业比重而提高服务业比重

glossary.explanation: A term formally put forward at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as a task of national modernization. It stresses an industrial system that is complete, advanced and secure, built on the real economy.

A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, and by high efficiency and quality. It is closely tied to strategic emerging and future industries.
The official policy goal, stated since the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting from fast growth to growth based on quality, efficiency and innovation.

t: The ownership basis of new quality productive forces: an examination based on the theory of productive forces and relations of production
zh: 新质生产力的所有制基础：基于生产力和生产关系理论的考察
source: Reform and Strategy (Gaige yu Zhanlüe), 2025 no. 1
paras: The authors ask how China's ownership structure can help turn scientific and technological innovation into new quality productive forces. They argue that the leap from innovation to real productive forces is not spontaneous. It requires keeping to the Two Unwaverings while deepening reform, so that new relations of production fit the new productive forces. Their thesis is that public and non-public ownership complement and reinforce each other, and that this gives China an ownership advantage.

The article works within Marx's framework of productive forces and relations of production, with ownership of the means of production treated as the core of the latter. It has four sections. The first reviews Marx's account of productive forces, relations of production and ownership. The second defines the \"quality\" of new quality productive forces. The third traces how China's ownership structure and science policy developed from 1949 to the present. The fourth sets out how the two ownership forms should work together.

In the authors' reading, drawing on the Grundrisse and Capital, science and technology are both a productive force and a means of labour, and the core element of new quality productive forces. Innovation becomes real productive force only when it joins with enterprises and industrial innovation, so enterprise ownership forms the entity-level basis. The historical section argues that the single public-ownership structure of the Great Leap Forward and Cultural Revolution period concentrated science on military and heavy-industrial fields. It credits reform-era recognition of the primary stage of socialism, and of non-public ownership, with releasing innovation. The final section assigns distinct roles. Public ownership gives strategic direction, concentrates resources and supplies patient capital. Non-public ownership supplies flexibility and application scenarios, and the article cites figures for the private sector's contribution to taxes, GDP and innovation. Mixed-ownership reform is presented as a way to address \"bottleneck\" technologies.

The authors propose an analytical logic running from technological innovation to ownership to a leap in productive forces. They conclude that advance cannot rest on a single ownership form. Collective research capacity in the state sector and market sensitivity in the private sector should both be used, within an institutional environment that encourages cooperation, to build new relations of production and release an institutional dividend. Read the original if you want a political-economy account of how Chinese economists link ownership structure to new quality productive forces, with the historical narrative of science policy and the mixed-ownership argument.
quoteEn: The collective capacity of the state economy for tackling scientific and technological problems must be used, and so must the keener market awareness and customisation ability of the private economy.
quoteZh: 既要发挥国有经济的集体科技攻关能力，又要发挥民营经济的更为敏锐的市场意识和定制能力

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first put forward in 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and industrial upgrading, and it is tied to high-quality development.
The official formula of unswervingly consolidating and developing the public sector, and unswervingly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official judgement that China is still in an early, underdeveloped phase of socialism. It is used to justify a mixed economy and reform and opening up.
Policy of bringing private and other non-state capital into state-owned enterprises, and state capital into private firms, so that different ownership forms share one enterprise.

t: The core and distinctive features of the new round of scientific and technological revolution from the perspective of historical materialism
zh: 唯物史观视域下新一轮科技革命的核心与特质
source: Marxist Studies (马克思主义研究), 2025 no. 4
paras: Zhang Jianyun asks what lies at the centre of the current round of scientific and technological revolution and how it changes the mode of production. The article's answer is that the leading force is a "digital-intelligence technology system", formed by the convergence of information technologies, and that its core is artificial intelligence freeing mental labour on the basis of massive data. Zhang argues that this pushes digital cultural production to the fore, fuses cultural and material production, and runs against capitalist logic while fitting socialism.

The article has three parts. The first traces how older information technologies (computers, digitisation, AI, the internet, mobile communication) merged after 2000 with cloud computing, the Internet of Things, mobile internet and blockchain, and why data is the system's "concrete in thought". The second compares the machine system of the industrial revolution, which freed manual labour, with AI, which Zhang says frees mental labour. The third examines changes in the means of production, the form of labour and the organisation of cooperation, with reference to DeepSeek as a Chinese case.

Zhang draws on Marx's account of labour as first constructed in the head, to argue that mental labour is "ideal construction" that needs abundant information and strong processing capacity. Machine learning is described as simulating this process and assisting the human brain. Zhang insists that AI-generated output is not objectified human labour and cannot meet emotional needs or replace human labour. Data, as non-physical information, is said to be non-rival, easily copied and to gain value through sharing, so private ownership loses its traditional importance. Zhang claims that capital's drive to monopolise data, its centralised wage-labour model and Western decoupling policies obstruct these tendencies.

Zhang concludes that socialist public ownership, with its aim of common possession of the means of production, supports data sharing, small-scale distributed cultural production and deeper socialisation of labour. Zhang links this to Marx's "association of free men" working as "one social labour force" and to a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative. The article holds that socialism will reshape human civilisation in a fair and reasonable way. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reading of AI and data as forces of production, in which mental labour, data ownership and the socialist–capitalist contrast are central.
quoteEn: The value of data lies not in possession but in use.
quoteZh: 数据的价值不在于占有，而在于使用。

glossary.explanation: A term the article says the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) used to sum up the merged system of digital and AI-related technologies.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, introduced in the early 2010s, which calls for shared development and cooperation among states.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and economic links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: Theoretical questions on the "Second Integration" in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
st: A textual study based on Capital and its manuscripts
zh: 学习理解马克思主义中国化“第二个结合”的若干理论问题探析
zhSub: 基于《资本论》及其手稿的文本研究
source: Guide to Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 4
paras: Liu Shulin takes up several theoretical questions raised by the "Second Integration", the combination of Marxism's basic tenets with excellent traditional Chinese culture, which forms one half of the Two Integrations. The article argues that the proposition rests on a long evolution of Party thinking and on new archaeological and historical findings. In Liu's view, it must be applied through a dialectic of criticism and absorption, openness to other civilisations, and a view of tradition as a whole.

The article has five sections. It first traces the Two Integrations from Mao Zedong's 1938 report On the New Stage, through Ai Siqi's philosophical defence, the 1945 Party constitution and the 17th Party Congress (2007), to Xi Jinping's formulation in 2021 and 2023. It then sets out the conditions that made the Second Integration possible. The remaining sections treat the handling of criticism and absorption in cultural inheritance, the relation to other civilisations, and the need to approach traditional culture as a composite.

Liu first argues that the Chinese Civilization Origins Project and excavations at sites such as Erlitou show an independent origin, a "pluralistic yet unified" structure and an "endogenous dynamic" behind five thousand years of continuity. Second, drawing on the idea that the ideological superstructure has relative independence, Liu holds that the Party's attitude to tradition has been constant: in revolutionary periods the emphasis fell on criticising decadent elements, and in peaceful construction on absorbing excellent ones, with neither dropped. On this basis Liu defends the May Fourth attack on Confucianism and Lu Xun against a "re-criticism", and warns against reviving any single ancient school. Third, Liu argues that openness to foreign achievements goes together with rejecting "Western-centrism", "universal values" and Westernization, citing the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind. Tradition, Liu adds, is a composite of Daoist, Mohist, military, legalist and other strands, not Confucianism alone, and Liu reads Xunzi's long exclusion as the cost of narrow orthodoxy.

Liu concludes that the Second Integration calls for creative transformation and innovative development under Marxist guidance. It does not call for copying the past wholesale. Liu proposes drawing every progressive, popular and useful element from the whole of the tradition in service of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-theoretical account of how the Second Integration is justified historically, and of how criticism of tradition is reconciled with its revival.
quoteEn: In revolutionary periods the emphasis was on criticising and negating the decadent aspects of traditional culture; in periods of peaceful construction, it is on absorbing and drawing upon its excellent aspects.
quoteZh: 在革命时期，侧重对传统文化中的腐朽方面进行批判和否定；在和平建设时期，侧重对传统文化的优秀方面进行吸收和借鉴。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula, first stated in 2021, for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with excellent traditional Chinese culture (the second). The Party presents it as the key to adapting Marxism in China.
The combination of Marxism's basic principles with excellent traditional Chinese culture, stressed by Xi Jinping at the 2023 symposium on cultural inheritance and development.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme, launched in 2013. The article treats it as an example of active openness to other civilisations.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, the Party's official framework for global cooperation and civilisational exchange.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and global standing, often tied to the centenary targets of 2049.

t: The capitalist production logic of digital labour and the alienation of subjectivity
zh: 数字劳动的资本主义生产逻辑及其主体性异化
paras: What counts as digital labour, and how does capital extract value from it? Lu and Zhang argue that digital labour is in essence a form of capitalist exploitation, and that the surplus of digital platforms still comes from the living labour of waged technical workers rather than from the free online activity of users. The article also holds that this logic produces the alienation of workers' and people's subjectivity.

The article has three parts. It first reviews definitions of digital labour, from Dallas Smythe's audience commodity theory through Tiziana Terranova and Christian Fuchs, and criticises their breadth. It then analyses how digital platforms and algorithms arise, how platform capital valorises itself, and how algorithmic management consolidates capital's power. Finally it examines alienation at two levels: the digital worker and the human being as a social subject.

The authors' first move is conceptual. Drawing on Marx's account of labour and productive labour, they distinguish labour from mere activity: labour is purposive, productive and involves toil. Ordinary users' browsing and entertainment is therefore not labour, and the data it generates has no value until waged workers sort and process it. Digital labour is defined as purposive human activity that processes data using digital technology, covering software development and web design as well as gig work such as ride-hailing and food delivery. Second, they model platform capital circulation and argue that gig platforms also take monopoly profit through commission. Third, they describe alienation: de-skilling of workers, digital fetishism that conceals algorithms and reifies labour relations, an inversion of subject and object in a 'digital prison', and estrangement between people through information cocoons.

The authors conclude that criticism should target the defects of digital capitalism, not digital civilisation, so as to ease the social 'birth pangs' of digital capitalism and move towards digital socialism. They call for demystifying digital fetishism and restoring human beings as the subject of labour. For China they propose accelerating new quality productive forces, strengthening labour supervision of digital firms and protecting data engineers and gig workers. They also propose tougher anti-monopoly enforcement, in line with the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Read the original if you want a Marxist-political-economy argument that separates digital labour from online activity and links platform exploitation to alienation, written from within the Chinese policy context.
quoteEn: The essence of digital labour is labour, and its definition should focus more on 'labour'.
quoteZh: 数字劳动的本质是劳动，其概念界定更应聚焦在“劳动”上面。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, especially in digital and high-tech sectors.
The authors' term for a socialist alternative to digital capitalism, in which digital technology is freed from capital's monopoly and serves human development.
An extension of Marx's commodity fetishism: blind reverence for algorithms and digital terminals that, in the authors' view, masks the capitalists who control them.
Marx's term for labour actually being performed, as opposed to past labour embodied in machinery or data. The authors treat it as the sole source of platform value.

t: Promoting the development of new quality productive forces through the new-type whole-nation system
st: A political-economy perspective
zh: 以新型举国体制推动新质生产力发展
zhSub: 基于政治经济学视角
paras: Zheng Yangtao asks how China's new-type whole-nation system for tackling key core technologies can drive the development of new quality productive forces. Reading the question through political economy, Zheng argues that the system is a major theoretical innovation of Chinese political economy and an expression of the new relations of production that advanced productive forces require. The article is a research piece published in Jinyang Journal in 2025.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why strengthening the system matters, citing the achievements of the planned-economy-era whole-nation model, the pressure of Western technological hegemony, and the demands of innovation-driven high-quality development. The second analyses the internal mechanism linking the system to new quality productive forces. The third lists priority reform tasks. Zheng draws on Marx's remarks on the productivity of labour and cooperation, on Xi Jinping's statements, and on the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Examples include photovoltaics, State Grid and national big-science facilities.

The core argument is that the principle that relations of production must fit productive forces implies a new organisational form for allocating innovation resources. Zheng says this form works through three supports: an innovation ecosystem that speeds the conversion of results into output; efficient coordination of government and market, in which the government anticipates and guides rather than correcting afterwards; and enterprise-led innovation consortia, with leading firms linking universities, research institutes and small firms. Zheng illustrates the government role with a nationwide computing-power network that directs eastern demand to western data centres. The article treats the system as a way to move China from technology follower to leader.

Zheng proposes four tasks: improve the Party's centralised and unified leadership over science and technology work; build an integrated allocation mechanism joining the innovation, industrial, capital and talent chains; build an enterprise-centred innovation system, including support for state-owned, private and small specialised firms; and expand open international cooperation while balancing openness with security. The author presents these as a way to release reform dividends and speed new quality productive forces. Read the original if you want a political-economy account of how Chinese scholars link the new-type whole-nation system to productive-forces theory and to concrete institutional reform.
quoteEn: In other words, developing new quality productive forces means making breakthroughs on key core technologies, and changing the relations of production requires continually strengthening the new-type whole-nation system for tackling them.
quoteZh: 换言之，发展新质生产力就是要对关键核心技术的攻关与突破，新型生产关系变革就需要不断健全关键核心技术攻关新型举国体制。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese model for pooling state, market and social resources behind strategic science and technology goals. It updates the planned-economy-era 'whole-nation system' used for projects such as the 'two bombs, one satellite'.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It describes advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation rather than traditional growth paths.
An official goal that stresses efficiency, innovation and quality of growth over speed and scale.

t: The impact of artificial intelligence development on the labour market
st: An analysis from the perspective of political economy
zh: 人工智能发展对劳动力市场的影响
zhSub: 基于政治经济学视角的分析
source: Journal of Hubei University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 3
paras: Xu Zheng and Wu Xiaoliang ask what artificial intelligence (AI) will do to employment, and whether it can ease the contradiction between the productive forces and the relations of production. They note that existing research is mostly quantitative and concentrates on job numbers and job structure. The authors instead use Marxist political economy and focus on alienated labour. They argue that under capitalism AI deepens alienation and labour-market inequality. Under socialism, in their account, AI can serve the people and support free and all-round human development.

The article has four parts. It first reviews the dispute between a "creation" view, in which AI generates jobs, and a "deprivation" view, in which it displaces workers. It then restates Marx's account of technology and relative surplus population. Next it analyses AI-driven alienation. Finally it sets out the effects of AI under socialist conditions and a practical path, with recommendations for the state, firms and workers.

The authors read Marx's claims about machinery as a duality: machines expel workers while also creating work elsewhere. They add that rising organic composition of capital reduces demand for labour. They then extend Marx's alienation categories to AI. In their account, AI deepens the separation of manual and mental labour, human subjects, workers and their products, and workers and productive activity. Algorithmic management, data labour and platform monopoly are said to fragment labour relations and widen the gap between high-skill shortage and low-skill surplus. Under public ownership and a people-centred orientation, the authors hold, the same technology can reduce labour intensity, extend free time and lay material foundations for communism. They add that over the long run technological unemployment need not mean mass unemployment.

The authors propose four measures: upholding the socialist system and workers' status as主体 of production, with curbs on data monopolies; a national AI strategy and talent training; redistribution, retraining, unemployment insurance and public-benefit jobs, including higher taxes on high-skill earners; and a new, flexible division of labour that ends overwork ("involution"). They conclude that under socialism with Chinese characteristics AI can help bring the relations of production into line with the productive forces and contribute to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a Chinese political-economy argument that applies Marx's theory of alienation to AI and labour markets, with concrete policy proposals.
quoteEn: The application of AI has produced a large \"useless class\" and led to an \"economic singularity\" in which social mobility stagnates.
quoteZh: 人工智能的应用造就了大量“无用阶级”,导致出现社会流动停滞的“经济奇点”。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, describing a vision of shared global development and interdependence.
The official name for China's current political and economic system, combining Party leadership, public ownership as the mainstay and market mechanisms.
Marx's concept, from the 1844 manuscripts, of workers being estranged from their products, their activity, their species-being and other people under capitalism.

t: Promoting the integrated development of scientific and technological innovation and industrial innovation
zh: 推动科技创新和产业创新融合发展
paras: This commentary asks how scientific and technological innovation and industrial innovation can be fused so that China develops new quality productive forces and achieves high-quality development. Yang argues that the two are mutually reinforcing and that their deep integration is a core component of national competitiveness. Citing Xi Jinping, Yang presents the pairing as "the basic path" for developing new quality productive forces and for gaining strategic initiative in international technological competition.

The article has three parts. The first explains the relationship between the two kinds of innovation. The second considers how technological innovation can build a modernised industrial system. The third turns to strategic emerging industries and future industries, with separate treatments of artificial intelligence, life sciences, and new energy and new materials. It draws throughout on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference and speeches by Xi.

Yang's central claim is one of two-way traction. Technological innovation is the "booster" of industry: basic research is its source, core technologies are the key to turning results into products, and universities and research bodies supply talent, with the socialist system's ability to concentrate resources invoked as an advantage. Industrial innovation is the "main battlefield" that provides market demand, application scenarios and incentives, and so drives further technological iteration. On this basis Yang calls for technology to empower the real economy, upgrade traditional industries rather than abandon them, and raise the industrial base and modernise industrial chains, with firms as the main body of innovation.

For the new sectors, Yang proposes concrete priorities: mastering "root technologies", high-end chips, large models, computing power and datasets in AI; better research management and data sharing in life sciences and biomanufacturing; and market reform, price mechanisms and basic research in new energy and materials. Yang also urges making AI a focus of the 15th Five-Year Plan and expanding patient capital. Read the original if you want a Red Flag-style statement of how current policy links innovation, industrial upgrading and new quality productive forces, with sector-by-sector policy suggestions.
quoteEn: Scientific and technological innovation and industrial innovation pull each other forward in both directions, each drawing the other along.
quoteZh: 科技创新与产业创新双向拉动、互为牵引。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries rather than by traditional factor inputs.
The official goal for China's economy since the late 2010s, stressing efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
An official policy goal of building an industrial structure that is advanced, integrated and secure, combining the real economy with technology, finance and talent.
A policy category of industries such as new-generation information technology, biotechnology, new energy and new materials, designated as drivers of long-term economic growth.

t: Promoting deep integration of the real economy and the digital economy
zh: 促进实体经济和数字经济深度融合
paras: Taking its cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for a system to promote deep integration of the real economy and the digital economy, this commentary asks why such integration matters, where it is most likely to stall, and how policy should address this. Jia Lijun argues that integration is the key to sustaining China's economic development and industrial upgrading, given that China is the world's largest manufacturing country.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the practical significance of integration; the second identifies three critical "nodes" (technology, industry and enterprise); the third proposes measures for each node. It draws repeatedly on statements by Xi Jinping and is aimed at manufacturing in particular.

On significance, Jia presents integration as a strategic choice in the new round of technological and industrial change, the core driving force of new-type industrialization, an inherent requirement of new quality productive forces, and a path to national competitiveness and greater influence in global value chains. On the nodes, Jia contends that digital technology is a bundle of sub-technologies (artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data, the Internet of Things, blockchain), so that no single one transforms production and their integration and compatibility are what count. Industries differ in their processes and industrial systems, so digital transformation must be tailored to each. At enterprise level, large firms have made progress, while small and medium-sized manufacturers lack internal drive, innovation capacity and the funds for initial and continuing investment.

Jia's proposals follow the three nodes. For technology, build an innovation system led by enterprises, with state-owned enterprises heading industry–university–research consortia to overcome "chokepoint" bottlenecks, plus test zones, intellectual property protection and standards in smart manufacturing and data security. For industry, differentiated strategies for process and discrete manufacturing, collaboration along supply chains, and support for emerging industries. For enterprises, government-led transformation platforms offering one-stop services, new management models, and leading firms opening platforms to small and medium-sized firms. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-journal writing links the digital economy, new-type industrialization and manufacturing policy.)
quoteEn: Integration of the real and digital economies faces the problem of marked differences among industries in the course of digital transformation.
quoteZh: 实数融合面临着不同产业在数字化转型过程中存在显著差异的问题。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, such as digital technology and high-tech industries.
An official term for industrialization that integrates information technology with industry and stresses high-end, intelligent and green manufacturing.

glossary.zh: 实体经济和数字经济深度融合
glossary.pinyin: shítǐ jīngjì hé shùzì jīngjì shēndù rónghé
glossary.en: deep integration of the real economy and the digital economy
glossary.explanation: Official policy goal of applying digital technologies and data across production sectors, especially manufacturing. The article abbreviates it as "shi-shu ronghe" (实数融合).
Colloquial term for key technologies in which China depends on foreign suppliers, who could constrain its industries.

t: The Two Integrations: the necessary path for adapting the Marxist worldview and methodology to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: “两个结合”：马克思主义世界观、方法论中国化时代化的必由之路
source: Social Science Journal (Shehui kexue jikan), 2025 no. 3
paras: Tang Zhengdong asks how the Two Integrations (combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture) have adapted the Marxist worldview and methodology to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The article argues that each principle of dialectical and historical materialism now appears in a concrete, distinctively Chinese theoretical form. It presents this as the work of Xi Jinping and the Party leadership around him in the new era.

The article is organised in three parts. The first takes dialectical materialism: the material unity of the world, the movement of contradiction, the fundamental method of materialist dialectics, and the dialectic of cognition and practice. The second takes historical materialism: the movement of the basic contradictions of society, material production as the foundation of social life, and the people as makers of history. For each principle, Tang compares how Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping applied it. The third part examines how excellent traditional Chinese culture fits each principle.

Tang's central move is to say that the classical authors applied each principle to specific tasks, such as criticising idealism and capitalism or defending the New Economic Policy. They had no occasion to work out its concrete forms under socialist construction. The Party, in Tang's account, supplied these forms: "proceeding from reality" as a restatement of material unity, with reality understood as changing; "problems" as the form contradiction takes under socialism, where "crisis" was its form under capitalism; the wholeness and continuing development of the basic social contradictions; a correct and comprehensive use of the productive-forces criterion; and the combining of top-level design with "crossing the river by feeling the stones". The second move is cultural. Tang contends that ideas such as "change is the natural way of heaven and earth" and "unity of knowing and doing" resonate with Marxist principles. In Tang's view, this gave the Party a stronger cultural subjectivity and guarded against one-sided readings that British empiricism or German idealism, he says, produced in their traditions.

Tang concludes that the First Integration gives Marxism's adaptation a practical basis and the Second gives it a cultural basis, and that the two are dialectically unified. Together they have enriched the cultural life of Marxism's basic principles and given its worldview a clearer Chinese style, serving as the cultural form of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a detailed, principle-by-principle account of how Chinese Party theorists present the Two Integrations as a philosophical method, and how Xi Jinping's statements are placed in a line from Marx to Deng.
quoteEn: The Second Integration provides a cultural foundation for the sinicization of Marxism: it makes excellent traditional Chinese culture modern, and by enriching the cultural life of Marxism with that culture it makes Marxism Chinese.
quoteZh: “第二个结合”则为马克思主义中国化提供了文化基础，它不仅使中华优秀传统文化成为现代的，而且还通过用中华优秀传统文化充实马克思主义的文化生命而使马克思主义成为中国的。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressing that Marxism's basic tenets must be combined with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in Xi Jinping's 2021–2023 statements.
The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The principle that the development of productive forces is the basic measure of social progress. It was prominent in Deng-era arguments for reform.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Guiding young people with Marxist scientific theory
zh: 以马克思主义科学理论引领青年
paras: Han Xiping asks how the Party should guide China's young people at a time when the country is pursuing Chinese modernization. The article argues that Marxist scientific theory must lead and equip the young generation, so that youth can take up their part in building a modern socialist country and in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Han presents this as a long-standing strength of Marxist parties and as an urgent task of the present.

The piece, published in the Party journal Red Flag Manuscripts, has three parts. The first explains why theoretical guidance of youth is an advantage of Marxist parties. The second explains why the drive to build a modern socialist country in a full sense requires such guidance. The third sets out practical routes for carrying it out. Han draws on Marx, Lenin, Mao Zedong and many statements by Xi Jinping.

In the first part, Han contends that Marxist parties differ from bourgeois parties because they openly lead youth with scientific theory. In Han's account, bourgeois parties claim ideological freedom while quietly transmitting bourgeois values. Marxism, Han says, gives young people a firm political stance, scientific ways of thinking (historical, dialectical, systemic and innovative) and a noble character linked to national and popular causes. In the second part, Han describes youth as the main force in the national project up to mid-century. Han also says young people are exposed to varied social trends and to ideological infiltration by hostile forces, especially online, and so need the means to tell right from wrong. The third part proposes better ideological and political courses from primary school to university, including AI-assisted evaluation and "walking" classes of fieldwork. It calls for coordinated work among Party committees, schools, Party schools, the Communist Youth League and social organisations. It also urges fresh language on platforms such as Douyin, Xiaohongshu, Bilibili and Zhihu, and participatory formats such as "red murder-mystery" games on Party history.

Han concludes that the Party must keep guiding youth with Marxist theory and use Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to shape their ideals and character. Han presents this as a condition for young people to answer the call of the Party and the people. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-journal author links Marxist theory, youth work and ideological security, and which concrete measures in education and online media are proposed.
quoteEn: The process by which young people study and master Marxist scientific theory is the process of cultivating their own historical, dialectical, systemic and innovative thinking, and thereby mastering a scientific way of thinking.
quoteZh: 青年人学习掌握马克思主义科学理论的过程，就是培育自身历史思维、辩证思维、系统思维、创新思维，进而掌握科学思维方式的过程。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the main framework for national development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, with 2049 as the target date for a fully modern socialist country.
Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and political values.

t: Critical strategy and methodology facing the production of abstract space
st: A reading of Lefebvre's The Production of Space
zh: 面对抽象空间生产的批判战略与方法论
zhSub: 列斐伏尔《空间的生产》解读
paras: Zhang Yibing reads the methodological discussion in Henri Lefebvre's The Production of Space, asking how a critique can confront bourgeois abstract space, which produces invisible relations of domination behind an economic surface. Zhang argues that Lefebvre responds with three moves: a strategic hypothesis grounded in historical materialism, a regressive–progressive method of historical analysis, and a revolutionary reconstruction of spatial codes. Zhang praises these as Lefebvre's most concentrated methodological reflection, but repeatedly finds his account of how revolution could be realised thin.

The article has three sections. The first sets out the historical-materialist basis of spatial critique and Lefebvre's claim that production of space has replaced the production of things within space. The second treats the regressive–progressive method, which Lefebvre traces to Marx's Grundrisse remark that the anatomy of man is a key to the anatomy of the ape. The third turns to the reconstruction of spatial codes and to Lefebvre's political strategy. Zhang draws on Lefebvre's other works, including The Survival of Capitalism, and on Sartre, Foucault, Lenin and Walter Benjamin.

Zhang's central claim is that Lefebvre sees contemporary abstract space as a technologically programmed realm of surveillance and social engineering, and rejects idealist theories of discursive or Cartesian mental space, insisting that technical ordering is objective spatial practice. Lefebvre holds that capitalism has survived because productive forces now develop through the production of spatial relations. Zhang reads the regressive–progressive method as a spatialised temporal structure: developed capitalist space is the key to under-developed space within the same world, shown in uneven development and the export of polluting industry. Zhang adds criticisms: Lefebvre never asks "whose technological utopia?", underrates the critical theory he attacks, and misses that planners are themselves steered by capital.

On politics, Lefebvre rejects the Russian single-centre model of revolution and argues for plural subjects, including marginal groups and parts of the working class, and for varied forms, violent or quiet. His aim is differential space against the homogenising logic of abstract space. Zhang judges this dialectical in orientation but without any workable plan, and holds that changing spatial discourse is empty unless the mode of production changes. Read the original if you study Lefebvre, Western Marxist spatial theory, or Zhang Yibing's critical method of reading foreign Marxist texts.
quoteEn: If the production mechanism of capitalist abstract space is not genuinely changed and the mode of production radically transformed, the production of spatial discourse and the ways space is experienced cannot be truly transformed.
quoteZh: 如果不能真正改变资本主义抽象空间的生产机制，彻底变革生产方式，空间话语生产及体验方式是不可能获得真正的变革的。

t: The ownership basis of new quality productive forces: an examination based on the theory of productive forces and relations of production
zh: 新质生产力的所有制基础：基于生产力和生产关系理论的考察
source: Reform and Strategy (Gaige yu Zhanlüe), 2025 no. 1
paras: How can China turn scientific and technological innovation into new quality productive forces, and what kind of ownership structure supports that leap? Li, Chen and Hu argue that the leap is not automatic. In their account it requires deeper reform and new relations of production in which public and non-public ownership complement and reinforce each other, while the Party's principle of the "two unwaveringlys" is maintained.

The article starts from Marx's framework of productive forces and relations of production, in which ownership of the means of production is the core of the relations of production. It then defines new quality productive forces as advanced and real productive forces, with technological innovation as their core element. A historical section traces ownership and science policy from 1949 through the Mao-era single public-ownership structure to the reform period. The last part draws policy implications for public, private and mixed-ownership enterprises.

The authors propose an analytical logic running from technological innovation through ownership to a leap in productive forces. Drawing on Marx's Grundrisse, they treat science both as a productive force and as a means of labour. They argue that innovation becomes real productive force only when combined with enterprises and industrial innovation, so enterprise ownership forms the material basis. They credit public ownership with directing the replacement of old productive forces by new ones, through concentrated resources, strategic planning and "patient" capital. They credit the non-public sector with turning disruptive innovation into applications, citing figures such as over 60 per cent of GDP and over 70 per cent of technological innovation results. Mixed-ownership reform, they say, can bring the two together and help overcome "chokepoint" technologies.

The article concludes that China's ownership structure gives it an institutional advantage. State-owned firms contribute collective research capacity, and private firms contribute market sensitivity and flexibility. Each compensates for the other's weaknesses, and the authors call for an institutional environment that supports both. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese economists apply the productive forces and relations of production framework to the ownership question behind new quality productive forces, including a Party-historical account of science and ownership policy.
quoteEn: The collective capacity of the state-owned economy for scientific and technological breakthroughs must be brought into play, as must the private economy's keener market awareness and capacity for customisation.
quoteZh: 既要发挥国有经济的集体科技攻关能力，又要发挥民营经济的更为敏锐的市场意识和定制能力

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and industrial upgrading, and is tied to high-quality development.
The Party's formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector, and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A reform policy that brings state and private capital together in the same enterprises, mainly through investment in state-owned firms by non-state investors.

keywords: productive forces and relations of production

t: The core and distinctive features of the new round of scientific and technological revolution from the perspective of historical materialism
zh: 唯物史观视域下新一轮科技革命的核心与特质
paras: Zhang Jianyun asks what is the essence, core and distinguishing character of the current round of scientific and technological revolution, and answers from a historical-materialist standpoint. The article argues that a "digital-intelligent" technology system, formed by the convergence of older and newer information technologies, leads the revolution. Its core, in Zhang's reading, is that artificial intelligence, built on massive data, liberates mental labour, and this changes the mode of production.

The article has three parts. The first traces the fusion of twentieth-century technologies (computers, digitisation, AI, the internet, mobile communications) with twenty-first-century ones (cloud computing, mobile internet, blockchain, the Internet of Things) into what the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) called the "data-intelligence" system. The second draws on Marx's account of machinery and of labour to explain how AI relieves mental labour. The third examines three changes in production: the content of the means of production, the form of labour, and the organisation of cooperation. It contrasts how capitalism and socialism relate to each.

Zhang uses Marx's method of ascending from abstract determinations to the "concrete in thought" and names data as that concrete, around which all the technologies are organised. Machine learning, Zhang argues, simulates the brain's "ideal construction" of things, so AI aids mental labour much as the machine system freed manual labour. Zhang holds that AI output cannot replace human labour, because it lacks human emotion and so cannot be objectified in the way human labour is. Data is described as non-physical, easily copied, non-exclusive and gaining value when shared, which Zhang says undermines the importance of private ownership. Zhang contends that capital's logic of monopoly, mass wage-labour production and decoupling runs against these demands. Socialist public ownership, small-scale distributed cultural production and a community with a shared future for mankind are presented as compatible with them. DeepSeek is offered as an example.

Zhang concludes that digital-intelligent technology makes possible Marx's "one social labour force" and that socialism, by meeting the objective demands of the new productive forces, will reshape human civilisation in a fair and reasonable way. The article links these claims to new quality productive forces and the Belt and Road Initiative. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist theoretical account of AI, data and the digital economy, with attention to the contrast it draws between capitalist and socialist institutions.
quoteEn: The value of data lies not in possession but in use.
quoteZh: 数据的价值不在于占有，而在于使用。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, especially digital and intelligent technologies, and by high efficiency and quality.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of China's vision for international relations, stressing shared development and cooperation among states.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

A term used in the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to summarise the combined system of digital and intelligent technologies that the article calls the digital-intelligent technology system.

t: The positive-science character of historical materialism
zh: 唯物史观的实证科学性质
paras: Is historical materialism a positive (empirical) science? The authors identify three positions in Chinese scholarship: affirmation, flat denial, and a vague stance that neither affirms nor denies. They argue that only the first matches Marx's intention. In their view Marx called historical materialism a positive science explicitly on more than one occasion, and the claim is also built into its essential nature.

This short newspaper-style piece rests mainly on Marx's formulation in The German Ideology, that real, positive science begins where speculation ends, in front of real life. It reads that passage together with the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and the Theses on Feuerbach. It then takes four attributes in turn: actuality (xianshixing), practicality, critical character and popular character (renminxing, orientation to the people).

The central claim is that Marx's "positive science" is defined against Hegelian speculative philosophy, not simply modelled on natural science. The authors say it is a "positive science within positive science". It inherits the natural sciences' pursuit of truth but adds the four attributes. Actuality means that every principle derives from real history and the real individuals in it, with capitalist society as the main object of study. Practicality means that material production is the starting point and foundation, and the authors call it the most fundamental attribute. Criticism means opposing philosophies that, in the authors' account, supply theoretical justification for private property. Critique of old philosophy is a means, and the aim is a theoretical guide for working people to change the world. Popular character means that the masses create material and spiritual wealth and decide social change. The authors present this attribute as both the starting point and the destination of the theory.

The authors conclude that this positive-science character made philosophy a real science for the first time. They argue that philosophy must go beyond abstract logical deduction and beyond criticism that looks sharp but leaves private ownership untouched. It must instead pass the tests of reality, practice and the people. The piece is a compact restatement of an orthodox reading of Marx's method. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese Marxist scholars defend the scientific status of historical materialism against rival views.
quoteEn: The practicality of historical materialism is its most fundamental attribute and its cornerstone; the standpoint of practice is its primary and basic standpoint.
quoteZh: 唯物史观的实践性是唯物史观最根本的属性，是唯物史观的基石，实践的观点是唯物史观首要的和基本的观点。

t: From fetishism to data worship: Marx's critical theory in the digital age
zh: 从拜物教到数据崇拜：数字时代的马克思批判理论
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 11 July 2025
paras: Wang Qian asks how Marx's critique of fetishism, ideology and alienation can still explain a world in which data, algorithms and platforms increasingly mediate social life. The article argues that reification has not ended in the digital age but continues as "data worship", deepening capital's domination over people. In Wang's reading, the supposed neutrality of data, the personalised narratives of algorithms and the platforms' precise regulation of behaviour together form a new ideological structure of digital capitalism.

This short commentary, published in a Party-affiliated social science newspaper, is organised in three parts that follow three themes in Marx's critique. It moves from commodity reification to data reification, from false consciousness to algorithmic ideology, and from alienated labour to data alienation. Wang draws on Capital, The German Ideology and the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, and brings in Lukács on reification and Althusser on interpellation.

Wang's first move is that data, being immaterial, real-time and copyable, makes the value form more abstract and more concealed.
