Its mystery, like that of the commodity, lies in the unseen labour and practice it extracts, while value is increasingly measured by captured attention and predicted behaviour. Second, the article argues that algorithms take over the role of Althusserian interpellation: through personalised recommendation they shape what individuals can perceive, and feedback loops produce cognitive closure and "voluntary passivity". Third, data alienation blurs the line between labour and non-labour and between production and consumption, so that clicks, attention and emotion become sources of value, and individuals lose control over both their product and their understanding of their own existence.

Wang concludes that Marx's critical theory has a renewed task: to expose the social relations hidden behind data forms, to resist capital's total occupation of the subject, and to reaffirm human social essence and practical freedom. Wang calls for a view of the subject grounded in sociality, historicity and practice as the way to reopen a path to emancipation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese Marxist scholar adapts fetishism, ideology critique and alienation theory to the study of data and algorithms.
quoteEn: The shift from commodity reification to data reification is not a mere change of medium, but a deeper process by which capitalism restructures social relations.
quoteZh: 从商品物化到数据物化，不是一次单纯的媒介转换，而是资本主义对社会关系更深层次的重构过程。

t: Marx and Engels's critique of capitalist modern civilization and its implications
zh: 马克思恩格斯对资本主义现代文明的批判及启示
paras: Sun Xuan asks how the value core of capitalist modern civilization shapes that civilization and drives it into structural difficulty, and what Marx and Engels's critique offers for exploring other paths of civilization. The article argues that, because capitalism's value core is the supremacy of material interests and the maximisation of capital, it cannot realise the free and all-round development of the human being. Sun proposes a new path of human civilization that puts that development at its centre and embodies the values of a community.

The article opens by surveying Schumpeter, Gu Hongming, Rousseau and Weber on modern civilization. Sun finds that they mostly describe value deviation and dilemmas without showing systematically how the value core acts on civilization. The second part reads Marx and Engels through historical materialism across five dimensions: material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization. The third part turns each dimension into a constructive counterpart.

In Sun's account, Marx and Engels credit the bourgeoisie with enormous productive achievements, the overthrow of feudal authority and the opening of a world market. They also show that the same logic produces overproduction crises, a representative state that is a "illusory community" serving capital, and colonial subordination of the East to the West. Spiritual life is hollowed out by money fetishism, labour is alienated, and nature is plundered. Sun's alternative replaces the capitalist logic of "for capital, relying on labour, developing capital" with "for people, relying on people, developing people". Concretely, it calls for ownership and distribution that serve the majority, a "real community" of people's democracy, equal exchange among civilizations, and cultural production oriented to the people. It also calls for a division of labour that frees work from mechanical fragmentation, and for ecological development that reconciles using and protecting nature.

Sun concludes that capitalist modern civilization is being progressively "disenchanted" and shows a tendency to decay as the world becomes more multipolar. The lesson, in the author's view, is to move from a "thing-centred" to a "people-centred" civilizational standard. Material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization would then be developed within a community of all-round development and exchange. This is presented as a way to settle disputes over civilizational values and to ease civilizational conflict. Read the original if you want a systematic, five-part Chinese philosophical reading of Marx and Engels on capitalist civilization, and the normative alternative that Sun builds from it.
quoteEn: The free and all-round development of the human being must be made the aim of civilization, fully expressing the will and values of the community, so as to achieve people's all-round development and all-round social progress.
quoteZh: 必须把人的自由全面发展作为文明的旨趣，充分彰显共同体意志和共同体价值，进而实现人的全面发展和社会全面进步。

glossary.explanation: Marx's phrase in The German Ideology for the state and similar forms that present themselves as the common interest while serving a ruling class. Sun uses it for the bourgeois representative state and the capitalist world order.

glossary.en: free and all-round development of the human being
glossary.explanation: A Marxist ideal of the full development of individual capacities, treated as the goal of communist society. Chinese theoretical writing often uses it as the ultimate aim of socialist construction.
The Marxist theory that material production and social relations determine political and ideological life. Sun uses it as the method for judging civilizations.
Counterpart of the "illusory community" in Marx's thought, a community in which individuals develop together. Sun links it to people's democracy.
Marx's term for the way money and commodities appear to hold independent power over people, hiding social relations. Sun uses it to characterise the spiritual poverty of capitalist civilization.

t: The threefold limits of marginalism from the standpoint of historical materialism
st: Revisiting the first clash between marginalism and Capital
zh: 唯物史观视域中边际主义的三重限度
zhSub: 重新审视边际主义与《资本论》的第一次交锋
paras: In 1884 Philip Henry Wicksteed used William Stanley Jevons's marginal utility theory to attack Marx's labour theory of value in "Das Kapital: A Criticism". Gao notes that later critics, such as Rubin, Hilferding and Bukharin, mostly targeted later marginalists like Böhm-Bawerk, and that the few replies to Wicksteed were partial. The article argues that, judged by historical materialism, Wicksteed's critique fails in three dimensions: its form of thought, its methodology and its view of history. Gao takes this to confirm the scientific character of Marx's labour theory of value.

The article is organised in three sections matching these dimensions. The first deals with fetishistic thinking and the misplacement of the value form. The second deals with methodological individualism and the paradox of "abstract utility". The third deals with a non-historical outlook and a "clumsy" supply-and-demand theory. Gao draws on Capital, Marx's letters, Engels, Rubin, Lukács, Postone, Sohn-Rethel, Whitrow and others, and works through Wicksteed's examples of Robinson Crusoe and a commodity-free community.

Gao argues first that Wicksteed forgets the capitalist social form that gives concepts such as utility equilibrium their meaning. He projects the value form, along with a money-schema and clock-time calculation, onto societies without commodity exchange, and so treats relations between people as natural properties of things. Second, by defining value as "abstract utility", he subjectivises it and replaces Marx's real, socially situated individuals with abstract consumers. In Gao's reading this confuses value with use value, makes the explanation circular, and leaves money's role as measure of value unexplained, since money already presupposes value. Third, Gao holds that Wicksteed's theory reduces to supply and demand, takes technical change and the pursuit of surplus value as given, and ignores the M–C–M′ question of where surplus value arises, namely in the purchase of labour-power.

Gao concludes that Wicksteed, like classical and vulgar economists, treats exchange, money and value as eternal categories and so cannot grasp their historical origin. Gao attributes this to his position within a reified world, to the separation of exchange from thought, and to his bourgeois standpoint. For Gao, historical materialism is the "recollection of origins", and Marx's critique of political economy ties categories to the real historical movement of capitalism. Read the original if you want a detailed Marxist rebuttal of the earliest marginalist critique of Capital, grounded in value-form theory and the critique of fetishism.
quoteEn: Wicksteed's interpretation of value as "abstract utility" not only subjectivises value but also, in its method of argument, replaces Marx's "real human beings" with abstract individualism.
quoteZh: 威克斯蒂德将价值解释为“抽象效用”，不仅意味着将价值主观化，还意味着在论证方法上用抽象的个人主义取代马克思的“现实的人”。

glossary.explanation: Marx and Engels's theory of history, in which material production and social relations shape ideas and social forms. The article uses it as its analytical standpoint.

t: On a new model of exchange among human civilizations
zh: 论人类文明交往新模式
paras: Tang Aijun asks what view of civilizational interaction should guide a world marked by civilizational clashes and hegemony. The article argues that the Party's concept of 'exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations', put forward since the 18th Party Congress (2012), is a new model of civilizational interaction that goes beyond the Western-centric model. In Tang's account, it offers 'Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach' to handling relations between civilizations.

The article has three parts. The first draws on Marx's theory of world history, and on Fei Xiaotong, to trace the move from isolated 'each to its own beauty' civilizations to universal interaction driven by capital. The second criticises the Western-centric model through four elements: the singular concept of civilization, the hierarchy of civilizations, the 'civilizing mission' and the 'end of history' thesis. The third sets out the new model and the historical conditions Tang says make it possible.

Tang grants the Western-centric model a historical progressiveness: it spread productive forces and universal interaction. He nonetheless holds that it exported capital's contradictions, brought colonial disaster and licensed intervention as a main source of civilizational conflict. Against it he sets four principles. These are a plural view of civilizations, civilizational equality (equal in value, attitude and order, with 'partnerships of diverse civilizations'), mutual learning through open, reciprocal dialogue, and coexistence under the principle of 'harmony without uniformity'. Tang presents these as drawing on Marxist theories of interaction and on traditional Chinese culture, and as responding to multipolarity, shared global problems and the crisis of modernity.

Tang concludes that moving beyond Western-centrism is the main trend of civilizational development. He argues that the Party has built an 'exchange–mutual learning–coexistence' model, backed by mechanisms such as the Belt and Road Initiative and the Dialogue of Asian Civilizations. Tang adds that a community of diverse civilizations requires a deep change in cultural mentality. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist critique of Western civilizational discourse, from Guizot to Fukuyama, and the theoretical grounding of Beijing's civilizational-exchange rhetoric.
quoteEn: The ultimate goal of interaction among human civilizations is neither a single civilization ruling the world nor a clash of civilizations, but the coexistence and dialogue of civilizations.
quoteZh: 人类文明交往，最终目标不是单一文明一统天下，也不是文明冲突，而是文明的共存与对话。

glossary.en: exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations
glossary.explanation: A formula promoted by Xi Jinping and the Party leadership since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It calls for equal, open interaction among civilizations in which each learns from the others.
A Confucian principle, from the Analects, of living in harmony while keeping differences. The article presents it as the basis for a pluralist community of civilizations.
China's international cooperation initiative on infrastructure, trade and connectivity, launched in 2013. The article cites it as a mechanism for civilizational dialogue.

t: The epistemological foundations of Lenin's theory of imperialism
zh: 列宁“帝国主义论”的认识论基础
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 10 July 2025
paras: Hu Xiaokun asks what theory of knowledge underlay Lenin's analysis of imperialism and his judgement that socialist revolution could succeed first in a relatively backward country. The short article, published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper, argues that Lenin made practice the criterion of a materialist epistemology and held together subjective initiative and objective law. On this basis, Hu says, he analysed the international situation and Russia's social character, and laid the Marxist epistemological groundwork for breaking the single capitalist world system and founding the first socialist state.

The article begins with the early twentieth-century passage from free competition to monopoly capitalism and the division of the world among monopoly alliances. It then turns to the First World War, the collapse of the Second International and Russia's position as the weakest link in the imperialist chain. Hu draws on several Lenin texts: Materialism and Empirio-Criticism, the Philosophical Notebooks (on Hegel), Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism, and The Development of Capitalism in Russia.

Hu's central move is to read the dispute with the Second International's revisionists as a philosophical conflict. In Hu's account, they rested on relativism and distorted dialectics into scepticism and sophistry. They then favoured reformism and vulgar evolutionism, denied the imperialist character of the war and ignored the concrete conditions for revolution. Against them, Lenin defined dialectics as the study of contradiction within the essence of things, with transitions between opposites that are conditional, and marked by leaps and breaks in gradual development. Hu applies this to imperialism: free competition turns into its opposite, monopoly, sharpening contradictions at world scale, while the proletariat's struggle becomes international as production is increasingly socialised.

Hu then shows how Lenin applied this method to Russia. In this account, Lenin saw Russian capitalism as dependent on the landlord class at home and on European and American capital abroad. He judged that the 1861 land reform deepened the contradictions in the class structure. He therefore defined the revolution as a revolutionary-democratic dictatorship of the proletariat and peasantry, led by a vanguard party and linked to national-liberation movements. Hu concludes that an active materialist epistemology, stressing purposeful human activity within objective conditions, guided socialism's leap from theory to practice and from one country to several. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese philosophical reading of how Lenin's dialectics and theory of knowledge underpin his account of imperialism and the October Revolution.
quoteEn: Lenin made "the criterion of practice the foundation of materialist epistemology", firmly grasping the dialectical unity of subjective initiative and objective law.
quoteZh: 列宁将“实践标准作为唯物主义认识论的基础”，紧紧抓住了主观能动性与客观规律性的辩证统一问题

t: Lenin's thought on cultural leadership
zh: 列宁关于文化领导权的思想
paras: Yan Peiyu, in a short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (July 2025), presents Lenin's writing on cultural leadership (cultural hegemony) as a distinctive feature of his philosophy. Yan argues that, after Marx and Engels decoded the logic of capital, Lenin's task was to build and consolidate proletarian power in the age of imperialism, and that this led him to study cultural leadership.

The article reads Lenin's thought as inheriting the Marxist tradition of cultural critique and as having three layers. These are the Party spirit principle in cultural creation, firm Party control of cultural leadership in developing proletarian culture, and the construction of a socialist cultural subjectivity through state cultural leadership.

On the first layer, Yan traces Lenin's 1905 essay on Party literature and argues that he linked Party spirit to ample room for individual creativity and warned against formulaism. On the second, Yan describes Lenin's criticism of the Proletkult, which sought a "pure" culture independent of the Party. Lenin held that proletarian culture grows from the lawful development of all human knowledge, and Yan adds his "two cultures" theory of inherited culture. On the third, Yan points to raising the people's cultural level, avoiding rashness in cultural matters, and combating bureaucratism, symbolised by Oblomov.

Yan concludes that the common thread is a shift in Lenin's problematic from the logic of proletarian revolution to that of socialist construction, driven by twentieth-century world-historical change and Russia's transformation. This shift, in Yan's reading, turned Lenin from a revolutionary leader into an "architect" of socialism. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language overview of how Lenin's views on culture, the Party and the state are framed in current Chinese scholarship.
quoteEn: Looking across the three layers of Lenin's thought on cultural leadership, the main thread is his shift in problematic from the logic of proletarian revolution to the logic of socialist construction.
quoteZh: 综观列宁文化领导权思想的三个层次，主线是列宁从无产阶级革命逻辑到社会主义建设逻辑的问题域转换。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese rendering of cultural hegemony, the authority to direct a society's culture and ideology. Here it refers to the Party's and the state's role in guiding culture.
A principle that intellectual and cultural work should embody the stance and consciousness of the proletarian Party. The term draws on Lenin's writings on Party literature.
A Russian organisation founded around 1917 that sought a new proletarian culture independent of the Party and of older culture. Lenin criticised it.
The capacity of a society or people to be the autonomous agent of its own culture. Chinese scholarship uses it for building a distinctive socialist culture.

t: Lenin's hidden treasury of philosophical thought
st: Rereading the Philosophical Notebooks
zh: 列宁哲学思想的隐性宝库
zhSub: 重读《哲学笔记》
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 10 July 2025
paras: Liu Jun argues that Lenin's Philosophical Notebooks, often undervalued beside Materialism and Empirio-Criticism because they are reading notes and excerpts, are a 'hidden treasury' of his philosophy. Whereas the earlier book mainly set out the epistemology of dialectical materialism, the Notebooks, in Liu's view, cover materialist dialectics, the history of philosophy and philosophy of nature.

The commentary first reviews the text's composition and publication history, from the eight blue notebooks of 1914–15 written in Bern to the Soviet and Chinese editions. It then lists rival readings: the Soviet 'planned monograph' view of Kedrov, a practice-based dialectic reading, and Western 'Leninology' accounts that see a Hegelian turn or a break with Lenin's earlier thought. Liu holds that these positions rest on differing theoretical and ideological standpoints.

Liu locates the Notebooks' innovation in their overall design, a Leninist outline of a system of materialist dialectics. Lenin compared Hegel's Logic with the logic of Capital and held that dialectics, logic and epistemology are identical, with the unity of opposites as the core. His notes on natural science, Liu says, anticipated holistic and systemic approaches and criticised absolutising laws and simple causality. Liu also argues that the dialectic of the general and the particular gave a philosophical basis for backward countries such as Russia to reach socialism without passing through capitalist development.

Liu concludes that these methodological principles, originating with Marx and Engels, became a complete system in Lenin and carry theoretical and practical weight for Marxism and the socialist movement. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese academic overview of the Notebooks' editions, the debates about them and their significance for Leninist philosophy.
quoteEn: The theoretical innovation of the Philosophical Notebooks lies not in individual propositions or views but in their overall conception, which contains Lenin's blueprint for constructing a theoretical system of materialist dialectics.
quoteZh: 《哲学笔记》的理论创新不在于个别命题和观点，而在于其整体创意，其中包含着建构唯物辩证法理论体系的列宁构想。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist philosophical method that treats nature, society and thought as developing through contradiction and the unity of opposites. It is a core component of the dialectical materialism taught in Chinese Marxist philosophy.

t: Using sinicized Marxism to excavate and elucidate China's fine traditional culture
zh: 以中国化的马克思主义挖掘和阐发中华优秀传统文化
paras: Taking its cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for inheriting China's fine traditional culture as part of Chinese modernization, the article asks which theoretical tool is suited to excavating and elucidating that culture. Lin argues that the tool can be neither rationalised modern Western culture nor a conservative, self-enclosed Chinese culture, but only Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions. The article appeared in Philosophical Trends, 2025, no. 1.

The article has four sections. The first criticises the Western view of Chinese culture, using Hegel and Weber as main examples and Russell as a more appreciative counterpoint. The second examines the limits of reading Chinese culture only from within, focusing on Confucian "family-state isomorphism". The third makes the case for sinicized Marxism, drawing on Marx, Engels and Mao Zedong. The fourth sets out three methodological principles for the work.

Lin contends that Hegel and Weber judged China by Western political experience, especially the separation of civil society from the political state, and so found Chinese culture wanting. In Lin's reading this view overlooks the Daoist and Buddhist pull towards non-political life and the Confucian stress on self-cultivation. A purely internal approach, by contrast, risks conservatism. Lin notes that Confucianism worked as an ideology but that rulers practised "Confucian outside, Legalist inside", and that its real force lay in village and family life, which modernisation changes. Marxism, Lin argues, has critically reflected on Western rationalism and demands adaptation to concrete conditions, so it can treat Chinese culture as part of China's reality, with respect and dialectically, following Mao's call to discard feudal dross and absorb democratic essence.

On method, Lin proposes three requirements. First, respect and understand traditional culture. Second, treat "excavation and elucidation" as nurturing a living organism, not mining a resource, so that it supports creative transformation and innovative development. Third, engage in equal dialogue and keep self-reflection, avoiding a prophet-like stance, since the present is itself historically limited and judgments of what is "fine" may change. Lin warns against dogmatising Marxism or treating tradition as an outdated resource. Read the original if you want a Chinese philosophical account of why Marxism is presented as the proper framework for engaging traditional culture, including its readings of Hegel, Weber and Confucianism.
quoteEn: Practice has proved that this suitable theoretical tool is neither rationalised modern Western culture nor a conservative, tradition-bound Chinese culture, but can only be sinicized Marxism.
quoteZh: 实践证明，这一恰当的理论工具既不是理性化的现代西方文化，也不是那种因循守旧的中华文化，而只能是中国化的马克思主义。

glossary.explanation: Official Party concept of China's own path to modernisation, developed prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as combining material and cultural-ethical advancement.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula promoted by Xi Jinping for reworking traditional culture so that it fits contemporary society. It is the official guideline for handling China's cultural heritage.
Official term for the parts of traditional Chinese culture judged worth inheriting and developing, as distinct from outdated elements.

glossary.literal: family and state share one structure
glossary.explanation: A description of traditional Chinese political thought, especially Confucian, in which the state is seen as an enlarged family and the ruler as a household head.
A common scholarly phrase saying that imperial rulers professed Confucian ideals while governing by Legalist methods of law and interest.
Marxism applied and developed according to China's concrete conditions, a project associated with Mao Zedong and later Party theory.

t: The low-cost development path of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的低代价发展之路
paras: Qiu Gengtian argues that the large body of research on Chinese modernization lacks a perspective from the study of costs (daijiaxue, literally the study of 'prices paid' in development). Modernization everywhere carries costs, and a high-cost model would forfeit the historic missions assigned to Chinese modernization, including the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article's thesis is that Chinese modernization should follow a low-cost path, which requires the Party and society to cultivate a conscious 'cost awareness'.

The article has three parts. The first defines cost, classifies it, and reviews how Xi Jinping, Western writers (Rachel Carson, the Club of Rome's The Limits to Growth, E. O. Wilson, Stavrianos) and Chinese scholars have described the costs of modernization. The second traces Chinese modernization from the 1950s to the present as a process of overcoming costs. The third sets out what cost awareness involves and how costs should be regulated.

Qiu divides costs into cost-type, sacrifice-type and negative-consequence costs, and into 'necessary' and 'man-made' costs. In Qiu's account, modernization without cost cannot exist, so only high-cost and low-cost modernization are real options. Low-cost modernization means maximum development gain for minimum input, risk and harm. Qiu holds that modernization costs are unavoidable but controllable, and that progress and cost are interdependent, mutually constraining and mutually connected. Reducing costs raises 'modernization returns', so the best pattern is low cost, high development and high returns. Qiu presents the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as one of correcting earlier costs: Party discipline, extensive growth, ideological problems and ecological damage. Earlier mistakes such as the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution are counted as man-made costs.

Qiu calls for cost awareness that avoids both an idealised view of modernization and a pessimistic one. Costs should be actively reduced ('cut' necessary ones, 'eliminate' unnecessary ones) and kept within what people and ecosystems can bear. Four measures are proposed: public tolerance, the degree of modernization achieved, how widely benefits are shared (linked to common prosperity), and compensation for those who bear sacrifices. Read the original if you want a systematic, Party-School-style attempt to build a 'cost theory' of Chinese modernization, including its typology of costs and its account of how past errors are framed.
quoteEn: Taking a low-cost path of modernization should be the basic strategy of Chinese modernization, its basic direction of pursuit, and an important feature of it.
quoteZh: 走一条低代价的现代化之路，这应当是中国式现代化的基本方略，是中国式现代化追求的基本方向，也是中国式现代化的重要特色。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, set out systematically in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Deng Xiaoping had earlier used the phrase 'Chinese-style modernization'.
The author's term for a field that takes the costs paid for development as its object. It covers a theory of the existence of costs and a theory of managing them.
A goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, stressed in recent Party documents, in which all the people share in the fruits of development.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of restoring China to a leading position in the world, central to Party discourse since 2012.

t: The philosophical logic of constructing a discourse system of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色哲学社会科学话语体系建构的哲学逻辑
paras: Responding to the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to speed up building a discourse system of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics, Huang Hai asks what philosophical logic should govern its construction. The article argues that the task can be understood through four pairs of dialectical categories: the one and the many, criticism and construction, the general and the particular, and the ought and the is. Each pair, in Huang's account, corresponds to a distinct problem the discourse system must face.

The article opens by defining the discourse system as the outward expression of the theoretical and academic systems, built around Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It then devotes one section to each category pair, labelling them respectively the preconditional, strategic, generative and practical problems. Throughout, Huang uses discourse clusters such as Chinese modernization, a community with a shared future for mankind, shared values of all humanity and a new form of human civilization as running examples.

On the one and the many, Huang holds that the single guiding principle (the "dao") is Marxism and its Chinese innovations together with fine traditional Chinese culture, from which diverse signature concepts grow. On criticism and construction, the author argues that building Chinese discourse requires dismantling the epistemology of "Western centrism", for example the equation of modernization with Westernization, while constructing independently. Huang says the Chinese modernization narrative does both by contrasting itself with Western modernization. On the general and the particular, the discourse must be commensurable with general rules of discourse production and be "understood across cultures", yet carry distinctive Chinese concepts, so that its local character gives it wider significance. Huang contrasts the shared values of all humanity with what the article calls Western "universal values".

On the ought and the is, Huang treats "what to say" as the ideal content and "how to say it" as the practical expression. The author calls for unifying political, academic and popular discourse, so that the discourse has political height, theoretical depth and the warmth of everyday life. Huang concludes, citing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), that building Chinese discourse and narrative systems is urgent given what the article describes as Western dominance of international discourse power. The aim is to turn institutional strengths and governance effectiveness into discursive strengths. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese philosophy journal frames discourse-system building through dialectical categories and the current official vocabulary of discourse power.
quoteEn: The construction of a discourse system of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics is an interactive process of constructing within criticism and criticising within construction.
quoteZh: 中国特色哲学社会科学话语体系的建构，是一种在批判中建构、在建构中批判的互动过程

glossary.explanation: Official Party term for China's own path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s as the guiding idea of China's foreign policy and global governance proposals.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, associated with the Chinese Dream and a mid-century timeline.
Xi Jinping's formulation listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as values common to humankind. It is presented as an alternative to Western "universal values".

In Chinese academic and Party usage, the organised set of concepts, categories and expressions through which a theory or country presents itself. It is closely tied to the idea of "discourse power" (huàyǔquán) in international debate.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: Phrase used in Xi Jinping's 2021 speech marking the Party's centenary to describe the civilization created by Chinese modernization.

t: State-owned enterprises and the development of new quality productive forces: theoretical logic, practical difficulties and paths forward
zh: 国有企业发展新质生产力：理论逻辑、现实困境与路径选择
paras: Tang Jijun and Wang Xiaolei ask how state-owned enterprises (SOEs) should develop new quality productive forces, a topic they say existing research has treated mainly at the macro level and not systematically at the level of the firm. Their thesis is that SOEs have strong reasons and capacities to lead this process, but they face obstacles in original innovation, institutions and the layout of the state sector that must be removed through further deepening of reform.

The article has three parts. It first sets out the theoretical logic of SOE involvement from four angles: forming production relations suited to new quality productive forces, the missions assigned to SOEs, raising total factor productivity, and strengthening international competitiveness. It then identifies three practical difficulties, and finally proposes three paths, drawing on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and on Xi Jinping's remarks on new production relations.

On the theory, the authors argue that frontier technologies are too costly and uncertain for small firms and often for large private ones, so SOEs, with their capital strength, reform experience and policy support, should lead the change in production relations. They link the task to national security, high-level scientific self-reliance, the role of SOEs as 'chain leaders' of modern industrial systems and regional coordination. On the difficulties, they cite weak original innovation (inadequate basic research spending, weak incentives, closed innovation models), imperfect governance, error-tolerance, evaluation and investment mechanisms, and an unreasonable layout marked by unclear core business, over-broad diversification, thin presence in emerging fields and east–west imbalance.

The proposed paths are to make SOEs the 'source' of original technology through innovation consortia, higher R&D spending and better incentives; to embed Party leadership in modern corporate governance while building error-tolerance and mission-based evaluation; and to optimise the state-sector layout by focusing on core business, acting as chain leaders, investing in emerging and future industries, and promoting east–west cooperation. The authors also warn against narrowing or over-extending the concept of new quality productive forces. Read the original if you want a detailed, policy-oriented account of how Chinese economists see the SOE role in technological upgrading and the problems they identify in SOE governance and layout.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces and strengthening international competitiveness are inherently unified, and both are embedded in the process of comprehensively deepening SOE reform.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力与增强国际竞争力是内在统一的，共同内嵌于国有企业全面深化改革过程中。

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, described as high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality.
Firms owned by the central or local state, treated in Party doctrine as the material foundation of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A form of cooperative organisation led by leading enterprises together with universities and research institutes to tackle key technologies.

t: Empowering the development of new quality productive forces through state-owned enterprises: theoretical basis, historical experience and practical paths
zh: 以国有企业赋能新质生产力发展:理论基础、历史经验与实践路径
source: Journal of Hebei University of Economics and Business, 2025 no. 4
paras: Lin Pan asks how state-owned enterprises (SOEs) can drive the development of new quality productive forces, the Party's term for advanced productive forces defined by high technology, high efficiency and high quality. The article argues that SOEs, because the state owns or controls their capital, can follow political goals and take on strategic, non-routine tasks. In Lin's view they should therefore serve as the main force and the "source" and incubator of new quality productive forces. Lin contrasts this with earlier studies that stress private firms' innovative drive.

The article has three main parts. The first sets out the theoretical basis in Marx and Engels on state-run economic organisation, and in Lenin's and Stalin's Soviet practice of state enterprise. The second reviews the history of technology absorption and innovation in Chinese SOEs: the "156 projects" of the 1950s, the reform-era policy of "trading market access for technology", and the later shift to indigenous innovation. The third diagnoses current problems and proposes reforms at the macro, meso and micro levels.

Lin reads Marx and Engels as expecting the state eventually to take over the direction of production once productive forces outgrow joint-stock management. Lin treats the Soviet SOE system as a successful mechanism for concentrating resources and for technological innovation before the 1970s. For China, Lin cites the First Tractor Plant in Luoyang as a case of Soviet technology being localised. Lin lists three present weaknesses: the new-type whole-nation system is not fully used, industrial chains are poorly coordinated, and internal organisation is weak, including Party-building and business work running as "two skins" and shortages of skilled talent. Lin also admits monopoly and principal–agent problems. Because new quality productive forces call for new relations of production, the article proposes institutional innovation at three levels. At the macro level, it urges stronger legal and policy backing for industry–university–research cooperation, "patient capital" and "SOE+" innovation consortia. At the meso level, it wants SOEs to act as "chain leaders" in strategic emerging and future industries and to promote digitalisation and data circulation. At the micro level, it calls for integrating Party leadership with corporate governance, and for talent evaluation and income distribution that reward innovation.

Lin concludes that SOEs are both the backbone for cultivating new quality productive forces and the main arena where they take effect. Lin adds that leading does not mean doing all research in-house: SOEs should be innovation platforms that coordinate other actors. Lin calls for an "effective market" and a "capable government" to work together, backed by policy across basic research, funding, talent, finance and intellectual property. Read the original if you want a state-sector-centred account of new quality productive forces, with Soviet and Chinese historical cases and a detailed list of reform measures.
quoteEn: That SOEs act as the main force of new quality productive forces does not mean that all scientific and technological innovation is completed inside the enterprises.
quoteZh: 国有企业担当新质生产力的主力军，并不意味着科技创新都在企业内部完成。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It denotes advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new factor combinations and industrial upgrading, with higher total factor productivity as the main marker.
An approach that mobilises state, enterprises, universities and research institutes nationwide to tackle key technological problems, adapted to a socialist market economy.
A reform-era policy of giving foreign firms access to the Chinese market in exchange for technology transfer, often through joint ventures.
Key industrial construction projects of the 1950s built with Soviet and Eastern European assistance, which laid the base of China's heavy industry.
Long-term, stable funding that tolerates the long payback periods and high risk of innovation projects.

t: The basic contradictions of society and the driving forces of social development in the intelligent era
zh: 智能时代的社会基本矛盾与社会发展动力
source: Social Sciences in China (中国社会科学), 2025 no. 3
paras: Sun Weiping asks how historical materialism can explain the basic contradictions of a society being reshaped by artificial intelligence, and what those contradictions imply for social development. The article argues that intelligent productive forces are outgrowing capitalist relations of production inherited from the industrial age. In Sun's account, the resulting mismatch between productive forces and relations of production, and between the superstructure and the economic base, is a fetter on the intelligent society. Resolving it is presented as the fundamental driving force of development.

The article has four parts. It first distinguishes 'technological social formations' (fishing and hunting, agricultural, industrial, intelligent) from economic social formations, and describes intelligent productive forces and the intelligent society. It then examines how relations of production lag behind these forces, and how the superstructure lags behind the economic base in ideology, governance, ethics, law and culture. The last part sets out measures for change, and a short conclusion follows.

Sun's first move is to propose that communist society could be built on the foundation of the intelligent society. Data, algorithms and computing power are non-rivalrous and shareable, which Sun reads as favouring public ownership. Sun also points to demand-driven planning and the reduction of labour time as further links. The second move is a diagnosis of contradiction. Private ownership and the logic of capital restrict the development of intelligent productive forces through technological monopoly. Human–machine competition produces a 'new alienation'. Digital and intelligence divides produce technological unemployment and a 'useless class'. Algorithms are said to become an ideological machine, to obscure digital democracy and to risk 'machine-enforced governance'. Law and ethics also lag behind the claimed 'subject' status of intelligent robots. The third move is a programme of transformation. It would advance AI technology while keeping the principle that 'the human being is the end'. It calls for a new public ownership of digital means of production (through data shareholding, data remuneration and digital dividends) and open-source, publicly supervised algorithms. It also proposes distribution and a division of labour suited to this ownership, a decentralised participatory digital democracy, regulation of giant firms, and a tripartite system of rights and responsibilities for designers, algorithms and users.

Sun concludes that productive forces should keep developing, relations of production and the superstructure should be adjusted accordingly, and the basic contradictions should be turned into momentum for building the intelligent society and laying the ground for communism. Sun stresses that this is a long, complex undertaking. Even in socialist China, with public ownership established, industrial-era relations and superstructure still need deep adjustment, and the concrete form of new public ownership of digital resources remains to be explored. Read the original if you want a Marxist, historical-materialist framework for AI, including its proposals on digital public ownership and governance, as published in a leading Chinese journal.
quoteEn: Therefore, on entering the intelligent era, capitalist private ownership is becoming a 'fetter' that restricts and obstructs intelligent technology and intelligent productive forces from developing at their due speed and benefiting the peoples of the world.
quoteZh: 因此，迈入智能时代，资本主义私有制正在成为限制、阻碍智能科技和智能生产力以应有的高速度发展、造福世界人民的“桎梏”。

glossary.explanation: A way of periodising history by the technological level of the productive forces (fishing and hunting, agricultural, industrial, intelligent), set alongside the Marxist classification by ownership relations.

The author's term for a productive-force system using data, algorithms and computing power as means of production and AI systems and robots as tools. The author presents it as a form of 'new quality productive forces'.
The word used in the standard Chinese rendering of Marx's 1859 Preface, where relations of production turn from forms of development of the productive forces into their fetters.

t: Major theoretical innovations in the basic socialist economic system since the new era
zh: 新时代以来社会主义基本经济制度的重大理论创新
paras: Huang Kainan asks what theoretical innovations lie behind the way the basic socialist economic system has been extended since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article argues that the three-part system formulated by the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) rests on three theoretical "combinations", each of which reconciles positions that earlier theory treated as opposed. Huang presents these as major results of Xi Jinping's economic thought and as building blocks for an autonomous Chinese economics.

After an introduction reviewing existing research on the system's content, evolution and advantages, the article devotes one section to each combination. The first concerns a public-ownership-based ownership structure and the market economy. The second concerns the labour theory of value and the regulation and guidance of the healthy development of capital. The third concerns an efficient market and a capable government. A short conclusion lists directions for further work.

On ownership, Huang contends that both traditional Marxist economics (which sees no commodity economy under public ownership) and Western mainstream economics (which makes private property a precondition of markets) are overcome. In the primary stage of socialism, public ownership has a dual character, non-commodity and commodity, and markets need only clearly defined trading rights, not private ownership. The mechanisms are state-enterprise reform, rural collective property reform and the Two Unwaverings. On capital, Huang holds that only living labour creates value, but capital may share in distribution. Returns that compensate for risk, especially "residual risk" under Knightian uncertainty, are legitimate. Returns from monopoly control of working conditions are not, which Huang takes as grounds for antitrust action, a focus on the real economy and a financing structure matched to risk. On government and market, Huang argues that markets evolve and are partly built by government. Government's role extends to industrial policy and strategic planning. The two are said to combine in addressing scarce, idle, newly created and shared resources.

Huang concludes that socialist market economy, based mainly on public ownership, can avoid the disorder that private capital's pursuit of partial interests causes in capitalist market economies. It is also said to unify micro-level and macro-level efficiency. The article calls its own treatment preliminary. It proposes studying how the three innovations are logically connected and how a high-standard socialist market economy evolves. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Chinese economists theorise the compatibility of public ownership, the labour theory of value and market mechanisms.
quoteEn: A market economy based mainly on private ownership is a capitalist market economy; a market economy based mainly on public ownership is a socialist market economy.
quoteZh: 以私有制为主体的市场经济是资本主义市场经济，以公有制为主体的市场经济是社会主义市场经济。

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The core economic institutions of China's socialist system. Since 2019 they are defined as three elements: public ownership as the mainstay, distribution according to work as the mainstay, and the socialist market economy.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.

glossary.en: an efficient market and a capable government
glossary.literal: effective market and government that acts
glossary.explanation: A formula in Party documents, including the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020). It says the market should play the decisive role in allocating resources while government plays its role better.
The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, presented in official discourse as guiding China's economic work in the new era.
The official characterisation of China's present developmental stage, used to justify market mechanisms and multiple forms of ownership.

t: The role of data as a factor of production in economic growth at the stage of new quality productive forces
zh: 新质生产力阶段数据要素在经济增长中的作用
source: Journal of Documentation and Data (文献与数据学报), 2025 no. 1
paras: Zhang Xiaoxi asks how data, now treated as a fifth factor of production after land, labour, capital and technology, drives growth under new quality productive forces. The article argues that data reshapes traditional production modes and supplies a new source of growth, as the economy shifts from resource-driven to innovation-driven expansion.

The short article moves in four steps: the economic characteristics of data, the mechanisms through which data empowers growth, the main obstacles to its use, and policy recommendations. Its examples include manufacturing, agriculture, finance, medicine and retail, and the regional cases of Guizhou, Zhejiang and Shenzhen.

Zhang identifies three traits of data: marginal cost close to zero, non-rivalry and non-excludability, and network effects with increasing returns to scale. Because of these traits, Zhang holds, the use value of data far exceeds its ownership value, so returns should be distributed by use rather than ownership. Growth then works through higher productive efficiency, faster innovation, upgrading towards knowledge-intensive industries, and narrower regional gaps through an integrated national data market. The obstacles listed are data silos, privacy and security risks, an immature data market with weak pricing, and a shortage of skilled personnel.

Zhang recommends a unified national data market with trading and pricing rules, a dedicated data protection law and privacy-computing technologies, investment in 5G and Internet of Things infrastructure and a national big-data platform, new data-science programmes and vocational training, and digital-economy demonstration zones in central and western regions. Read the original if you want a brief policy-oriented overview of how Chinese economists link data to new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: These three characteristics make the use value of data far higher than its ownership value, so the distribution of returns to data is based more on use value than on ownership.
quoteZh: 上述三大特性使得数据要素的使用价值远高于其所有权价值，因此数据要素的收益分配更多是基于使用价值而非所有权。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries rather than resource-intensive growth.

t: Dual drivers, dual effects and dual-dimension institutions in developing new quality productive forces
zh: 发展新质生产力的双重驱动、双面效应与双维制度
source: Contemporary Economic Research (当代经济研究), 2025 no. 3
paras: Hu Lei takes up a gap in the growing literature on new quality productive forces: what drives their development, what effects they have, and what institutions should steer them. The article argues that their development is propelled by two forces, an internal technological one and an external institutional one. It also argues that it produces two-sided effects, creative and destructive, and therefore calls for a matching pair of institutional arrangements, one that encourages innovation and one that controls risk.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's 2023–2024 statements on new quality productive forces and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It then has three sections. The first sets out the technological and institutional logics of development. The second analyses creative and destructive effects. The third proposes technological and institutional innovation. Hu draws throughout on Marx's Capital and the Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, as well as on Schumpeter's notion of creative destruction.

On the drivers, Hu describes an internal chain of technological innovation, qualitative change in the factors of production, and industrial upgrading. An external chain runs from institutional reform to new relations of production to new quality productive forces, following the historical-materialist law that relations of production must fit the productive forces. On the effects, the creative side comprises new modes of production (data, platforms, digital capital), new industries and new jobs. The destructive side comprises investment bubbles, income polarisation by region, between capital and labour and among workers, and the displacement of jobs by machines. Hu also draws on Marx's account of machinery under capitalism to argue that China must prevent development from being trapped in the logic of capital valorisation.

Hu proposes a mechanism for "dual-dimension co-evolution" of institutions. To maximise creative effects, the article calls for a new-type whole-nation system, a high-standard market system, distribution according to factors and expanded consumption. To limit destructive effects, it calls for orderly replacement of old industries (establish the new before breaking the old), "patient capital" with curbs on disorderly capital expansion, an employment-first policy, and stronger protection of workers' rights. Hu concludes that technology and institutions must advance together so that development serves the people rather than capital. Read the original if you want a Marxist political-economy treatment of new quality productive forces that links Xi's formulations to classical texts and to concrete policy proposals on innovation, capital and employment.
quoteEn: In short, the external institutional logic of developing new quality productive forces is to adapt the relations of production to the internal requirements of the new productive forces: to remove those relations of production that obstruct and constrain them, and to establish new-type relations of production that suit and promote them.
quoteZh: 要言之，发展新质生产力的制度外驱逻辑是：对标新质生产力发展的内在要求，推进生产关系“适应性”发展，把阻碍和钳制新质生产力发展的生产关系“破除掉”,把适应和促进新质生产力发展的新型生产关系“立起来”。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by breakthrough technologies, new factors of production and industrial upgrading, rather than by input expansion.
Long-term capital that tolerates risk and delayed returns, promoted in Chinese policy to fund frontier technologies and emerging industries.
A policy model that pools state and market resources nationwide for major scientific and technological goals.

t: How patient capital empowers new quality productive forces: inner mechanism and paths of cultivation
zh: 耐心资本赋能新质生产力的内在机理与培育路径研究
source: Contemporary Economic Research (Dangdai jingji yanjiu), 2025 no. 4
paras: Li Zhe and Wang Chengyun take up the call at the Politburo meeting of April 2024 to "develop venture capital actively and expand patient capital" as a way of developing new quality productive forces in light of local conditions. They argue that patient capital is a concrete form of capital under the socialist market economy, that it develops Marxist capital theory, and that it can drive new quality productive forces through three channels, while facing real risks that call for coordinated cultivation.

The article has four main parts. It first defines patient capital and its attributes, then explains how it empowers new quality productive forces. It next identifies risks and challenges, and finally proposes cultivation paths for investment firms, government, policy and the market environment. A short conclusion follows. The authors draw on Marx's definition of capital as a social relation, on Lin Yifu and Wang Yan's definition, and on Western work on long-term private-equity investment.

The authors distinguish what patient capital shares with capital in general from what is specific to it. Like all capital, it is a factor of production that seeks valorisation, moves and accumulates. Its specific features are long investment horizons, counter-cyclical positioning, strategic orientation and relative safety. In the Chinese setting, they say, state capital is its main force, alongside long-term bank, insurance and social security funds. They argue that it empowers new quality productive forces by stabilising capital markets, acting as a "technological partner" that funds long-cycle research and the conversion of results into production, and supplying "financial impetus" to emerging and future industries, new-type workers and green development.

The risks they identify are a complex domestic and international situation, the conflict between short-termist investment concepts, models and appraisal systems and long-term innovation, and incomplete or unstable policies and an immature venture market. To address them, they call for longer performance-evaluation cycles (five years or more), fault-tolerance and incentive mechanisms, and a guiding government role in coordination, risk control and infrastructure. They also call for better tax policy, exit channels and regulation, and a market environment that protects intellectual property. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Chinese economists frame patient capital within Marxist political economy and the policy agenda for new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: As a \"friend of time\", patient capital has a long appraisal cycle and sticks to value investing. It can keep adding \"fuel\" to technological R&D, and even if setbacks occur in innovation it will not suddenly withdraw funds or leave a funding shortage.
quoteZh: 耐心资本作为“时间的朋友”，其考核周期较长、坚持价值投资，能够源源不断地为技术研发“添柴”“加油”，即使在技术创新过程中遭受挫折也不会出现紧急撤资、资金短缺等情况。

glossary.explanation: Capital invested for the long term, tolerant of short-term market pressure and high risk. The Politburo called in April 2024 for it to be expanded to support technological innovation.
A concept associated with Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, emerging and future industries, and green development.
The official description of China's economic system since the 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership playing a leading role.

t: Lefebvre's spatial dialectics in the context of the critique of political economy: a further examination
zh: 政治经济学批判语境下列斐伏尔的空间辩证法申论
source: Journal of Beijing Normal University (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 2
paras: Zhang and Zhao ask how Henri Lefebvre carried Marx's critique of political economy into the dimension of space, and what that move is worth today. They argue that Lefebvre inherited Marx's tradition and joined the critique of capital with the critique of space. In their account he extended Marx's labour–production dialectic of practice into a spatial dialectic. They also hold that this dialectic has real limits, chiefly its neglect of time.

The article has three parts. The first treats the production of space as the ground on which Lefebvre built his dialectic. It sets out his claim that earlier historical materialism had an 'absence of space', and traces the method of ascent from the abstract to the concrete from Hegel through Marx to Lefebvre. The second part reconstructs the 'three-dimensional' picture of abstraction, contradiction and difference. The third assesses the contemporary significance of the dialectic, its reception by Harvey, Foucault and Soja, and its shortcomings.

The core move is the authors' reading of Lefebvre's triad of spatial practice, representations of space and representational (symbolic) space. Under capitalism this triad is alienated into 'abstract space' ruled by exchange value, which the authors say Lefebvre links to a 'space fetishism' modelled on Marx's commodity fetishism. Space becomes one-dimensional, human relations to space and to one another are estranged, and space turns into an instrument of state power. Contradictions inside abstract space are said to generate a 'differential space', reached through a 'spatial revolution' by the urban proletariat allied with those on the margins. The authors stress that Lefebvre's third term is an independent element resting on difference, not a synthesis of the first two as in Hegel and Marx.

The authors credit Lefebvre with spatialising dialectics, enriching Marx's theories of alienation and reification, and pointing towards a just space. They then raise three criticisms. He elevates space over time, which in their view conflicts with Marx's emphasis on free time and with the unity of history and practice. His triad lacks an internal dialectical connection, so its ontological basis is left 'suspended'. His differential space is utopian and aesthetic, closer to the Western Marxist tradition of aesthetic redemption than to Marx's reliance on changes in the mode of production and social revolution. Read the original if you study Lefebvre, spatial theory or Western Marxism and want a Chinese Marxist assessment that tests his work against Marx's critique of political economy.
quoteEn: Time and space coexist within humanity's objectifying practice; history is nothing but the unfolding of people's practical activity in time and space, appearing as a twofold movement of the spatialisation of time and the temporalisation of space, and so changing humans themselves as they change the objective world.
quoteZh: 时间与空间共存于人类对象化的实践活动之中，历史不外是人们的实践活动在时间与空间中的展开，表现为时间空间化和空间时间化的双重化运动，进而在改变对象世界的过程中改变人自身。

t: The dialectical method and the wisdom of the mean in exploring the path of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化道路探索的辩证方法与中庸智慧
source: Renwen Zazhi (Journal of the Humanities), 2025 no. 3
paras: Zhang Shiwei and Zhu Yao ask how Chinese modernization came to take a path distinct from the Western and Soviet models. Taking the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its decision on deepening reform as a starting point, they argue that the key lies in a method: the Party's fusion of Marxist dialectics with the traditional Chinese wisdom of the mean (zhongyong), as part of the Two Integrations.

The article has four parts. The first treats the historical conditions and theoretical premises of Chinese modernization, tracing the global wave of modernization from Britain's industrial revolution, the Opium War as the turning point for China, and the late-Qing search by reformers and revolutionaries for Western models. The second examines how a dialectical self-awareness emerged from the later New Culture Movement, through Li Dazhao, Qu Qiubai, Li Da, Ai Siqi and Mao Zedong. The third analyses how the mean is applied in practice, and a short conclusion follows.

The authors argue that traditional zhongyong, born of feudal society, carried eclectic and metaphysical elements and a hierarchical outlook. In their account Marxist dialectics removed these limits and gave it a scientific content, while its stress on balance, the unity of opposites and moderation proved compatible with materialist dialectics. They then claim that this transformed 'grasping the two ends and using the mean' shaped three areas of practice. In choosing a road, it avoided copying either the Western or the Soviet model. In strategy, it balanced independence and self-reliance with opening up, avoiding extremes. In policy, it sought dynamic balance through common prosperity, the five-sphere overall plan, harmony between humans and nature, and non-alignment in foreign policy.

The authors conclude that the success of Chinese modernization is not accidental but the result of combining Marxist dialectics with the mean, which they describe as a mutual embedding of practical and speculative reason. They expect further development of the Two Integrations, especially the 'second integration', to bring methodological innovation and extend the strengths of this combination. Read the original if you study how Chinese scholars link Marxist dialectics with traditional philosophy to explain the distinctiveness of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: In handling the relationship between independence and self-reliance and opening up to the outside world, Chinese modernization displays the wisdom of the "mean".
quoteZh: 中国式现代化在处理独立自主和对外开放的问题上展现了“中庸”智慧。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Xi Jinping's formula of combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second).
A Confucian ideal of moderation and balance, avoiding extremes. The authors treat it as a practical method for handling opposing forces, summed up in 'grasping the two ends and using the mean'.
A Party goal of prosperity shared by all, stressed by Xi Jinping as a defining feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

t: On the distinctive worldview contained in Chinese modernization
zh: 论中国式现代化蕴含的独特世界观
paras: Tian Pengying takes up a statement by Xi Jinping in February 2023 that Chinese modernization contains a distinctive worldview, outlook on values, history, civilization, democracy and ecology. Tian argues that the worldview is the precondition for the others, so it must be understood first, including its theoretical basis, cultural sources and global horizon. The article sets out to explain, from a philosophical angle, what this worldview is, what it contributes theoretically and what its world-historical significance is.

The article is organised in five sections, each presenting a relationship through which Chinese modernization is said to view the modern world: China and the world; the general and the particular; matter and spirit; humanity and nature; and openness and independence. It draws on Marx's theory of world history, Lenin's and Mao Zedong's treatment of the dialectic of the general and the particular, and Marx's critique of capital. It also cites Xi Jinping's speeches throughout.

Tian's central move is to place Chinese modernization within a world-historical process. In this account the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is irreversible and converges with world socialism and global modernization. Tian describes three "basic plates" of the modern world: Chinese, Western and Global South modernization. Modernization has common features, namely a material and technological base, similar stages, similar drivers and kindred civilizational forms, but it also shows historical diversity, so "modernization is not a multiple-choice question with a single answer". Western modernization, in Tian's account, is driven by the logic of capital. It produces materialism, alienation and the exhaustion of nature, whereas Chinese modernization seeks coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress and harmony between humanity and nature. In foreign affairs Tian rejects the "Thucydides trap" as fatalism and argues for peaceful development, win-win cooperation and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind.

Tian concludes that Chinese modernization is not self-enclosed but in dialogue with the world. By handling these five relationships dialectically, it offers what Tian calls wisdom for humanity at a new crossroads of civilization and points towards a new form of human civilization. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Party theorists present the philosophical foundations of Chinese modernization, and how they set it against Western modernization.
quoteEn: The coordinated development of material and spiritual civilization is the right path in the human world; it resolves many problems of human social development and discards the capital-centred, materialism-bloated modernization of the West.
quoteZh: 物质文明和精神文明协调发展是人间正道，破解了人类社会发展的诸多难题，摒弃了西方以资本为中心的现代化、物质主义膨胀的现代化

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation for China's path of modernization, developed prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist and as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing common interests, cooperation and a more equitable global order.
A term for developing countries, used in Chinese official discourse to describe a bloc China presents itself as aligned with.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A Party formula claiming that Chinese modernization creates a civilizational pattern different from the Western one, with features such as common prosperity and harmony with nature.

t: The scientific concept of developing green productive forces and its realisation
zh: 发展绿色生产力的科学理念及其实现
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 3
paras: Zhang Yunfei asks how green productive forces, understood as the driving force of building a Beautiful China, should be conceived and developed. The article argues that green productive forces are the inner character and direction of new quality productive forces, and that they can be developed only if the new development philosophy is applied as an internally unified whole and if the basic contradictions of society are transformed together.

The article has three parts. The first explains why green productive forces are intrinsic to productive forces in general and to new quality productive forces in particular. The second takes the five elements of the new development philosophy (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) in turn and links each to green productive forces. The third applies the Marxist framework of the relations between productive forces, relations of production, economic base and superstructure.

Zhang's central move is to define productive forces as the real capacity to realise the metabolism between humans and nature, so that harmony between the two is built into the concept. On this basis, traditional productive forces appear as "black" or "brown", and new quality productive forces as "green" in their objects of labour (information, data, knowledge), means of labour (digital tools) and labourers (combining intelligent and ecological literacy). Zhang then calls for uniting digital with green technology and economy, and for coordinating urban–rural, regional, river-basin and maritime development. The article also calls for "green" opening up to the world, and for ecological products to be supplied fairly to meet people's need for a beautiful environment. Finally, Zhang argues for a new ecological paradigm in productive forces, relations of production built on ecological compensation, public ownership of primordial natural goods with no privatisation, and a state with stronger public governance. Zhang also argues for dropping the view of productive forces as the power to conquer nature.

Zhang concludes that green productive forces can become the sustainable fundamental driver and economic foundation of a Beautiful China if the new development philosophy guides them and the whole social structure changes accordingly. Zhang presents Xi Jinping's statements on the subject as the basic guide and calls for further deepening reform in line with the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese Marxist-ecological account of how new quality productive forces, ecological civilisation and the basic contradictions of society are linked in policy terms.
quoteEn: In sum, new quality productive forces are in essence green productive forces.
quoteZh: 总之，新质生产力本质上是绿色生产力。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new factor combinations and industrial upgrading.
An official goal of ecological civilisation, put forward by the Party in 2012, of building a country with a clean and healthy environment.
A guiding framework proclaimed in 2015 comprising innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
An official concept for a model of development that harmonises humans and nature, written into Party and state documents since the 2000s.

t: All-round human development: the essential requirement of Chinese modernization
zh: 人的全面发展：中国式现代化的本质要求
paras: Zhou Hang and Niu Xianfeng ask how Chinese modernization relates to Marx's idea of the all-round development of the human being. They argue that the all-round development of the person is the essential requirement and fundamental value of Chinese modernization, which they present as both an economic and social modernization and a path by which people's needs, free and conscious practice, free individuality and social relations are progressively enriched.

The article begins from Marx's statement that man appropriates his all-round essence in an all-round way, as a total man. The authors read this as three levels of essence: the species essence of free conscious activity, the social essence as the ensemble of social relations, and the individual essence as free individuality. From this they derive four yardsticks, which structure the article: human needs, labour practice, social relations and free individuality. Four sections apply them in turn to Chinese modernization, drawing on Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

On needs, the authors hold that material and spiritual needs must be met together, and that needs and production stimulate one another. They cite the primary stage of socialism, high-quality development, new quality productive forces and cultural policy as means to this end. On free and conscious practice, they contend that the basic economic system, the people's congress system and whole-process people's democracy secure the institutional conditions, while common prosperity and technological innovation supply the material base and free time that Marx saw as necessary. On free individuality, they use Marx's three stages (dependence on persons, dependence on things, free individuality). In their account, Chinese modernization removes dependence on persons, treats material things as a means to human ends rather than following the logic of capital, and encourages creativity through educational reform.

On social relations, the authors argue that public ownership as the main body, Party leadership, the political institutions and a shared sense of community for the Chinese nation prevent exploitation and class antagonism. They say these create harmonious relations among people, with nature and among ethnic groups. They conclude that the modernization of the human being is its essential requirement, and that Chinese modernization is the necessary path to all-round human development and comprehensive social progress. Read the original if you want to see how Party School scholars connect Marx's theory of human development to current official concepts of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The modernization of the human being is the essential requirement and the fundamental value of modernization.
quoteZh: 人的现代化是现代化的本质要求和根本价值所在。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a distinctively Chinese path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as differing from Western modernization in features such as large population, common prosperity and coordination of material and spiritual civilization.
An official term, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019, for the Chinese political system. It stresses people's participation at every stage of governance, not only in elections.
A socialist goal, revived under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all, to be reached through high-quality development and a fairer distribution of income.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation and high-tech, high-efficiency, high-quality sectors.
The official judgement, since 1981 and 1987, that China is at an early stage of socialism and will remain so for a long time, which justifies a focus on developing the productive forces.
The official development goal since 2017, favouring quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth alone.

t: Structural transformation of the qualitative forms of productive forces and its practical implications
st: An interpretation based on Capital and its manuscripts
zh: 生产力质态的结构性变革及其现实启示
zhSub: 基于《资本论》及其手稿的阐释
paras: Marking the 140th anniversary of the publication of Volume II of Capital, Ding Xiaoqin and Hou Wanyue reread Marx's theory of productive forces in Capital and its manuscripts to clarify what they call the 'qualitative form' (zhitai) of productive forces. They argue that Marx's analysis, in which transformations of this form underpin the rise of capitalism and the succession of social formations, provides the theoretical basis for understanding new quality productive forces. The authors present Xi Jinping's statements on the concept as a terminological and methodological innovation in Marxist productive-force theory.

The article has four parts. It first defines the structure of productive forces through three kinds of natural force. It then traces how a new qualitative form emerged under machine-based large-scale industry, moving from simple cooperation to manufacture to the machine system. Next it turns to Marx's remarks on how productive forces would develop in a future society. The last part draws implications for developing new quality productive forces in China.

The core argument distinguishes three natural forces and the productive forces that correspond to them: the labourer's own physical and mental capacities (individual productive force), the forces of nature applied through tools and machinery (social natural productive force), and the force of socially organised labour through cooperation and division of labour. The authors hold that the qualitative form of productive forces has three layers: substantive elements, science and technology, and modes of organisation. In their reading, the move from manufacture to machine industry marked a qualitative leap, because science and natural forces were incorporated into production, mental and manual labour separated, and the machine system became the material carrier of knowledge and a ruler over living labour. Under capitalism, they say, all three productive forces appear as capital's productive forces and can turn into destructive forces, including ecological ones.
