In a future society, they argue, machines would become the common property of associated workers, labour would become free labour, and surplus labour and free time would return to the producers.

The authors conclude that new quality productive forces mark a transitional stage between the qualitative leap of capitalist productive forces and the productive forces of a future society. They call for upgrading in three areas: comprehensive optimisation of substantive elements, with science and technology innovation in the lead and attention to social factors; a harmonious reconstruction of the relation between production and ecology, with green development as the foundation; and a qualitative leap in how production factors are combined, with public ownership, self-reliance in core technologies and international scientific cooperation. Read the original if you want a close reading of Capital, Volume II and the manuscripts used to ground the theory of new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: The proposal of the concept of 'new quality productive forces' precisely defines the transitional stage between the qualitative leap of capitalist productive forces and the formation of the qualitative form of productive forces in a future society.
quoteZh: 新质生产力”概念的提出，精确界定了资本主义生产力质态跃升与未来社会生产力质态形成之间的过渡阶段

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor combinations and industrial upgrading. It is presented as a core element of high-quality development.
The authors' term for the structural character of productive forces at a given stage, which they analyse through substantive elements, science and technology, and modes of organisation.

t: Marx's notebooks on religion in MEGA2 and their theoretical value
zh: MEGA2版中马克思的宗教笔记及其理论价值
paras: Marx's reading notebooks, collected in the fourth division of MEGA2 (the historical-critical edition of the Marx-Engels complete works), are described by Chen as the 'workshop and laboratory' of his thought. This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2025, asks what two little-studied notebooks of 1840–1842 reveal about the young Marx. Chen argues that they are Marx's only two religion-themed notebooks and that together they record his intellectual 'awakening' before historical materialism.

The article first introduces the Berlin Notebooks (1840–1841), excerpts from Aristotle, Leibniz, Hume and Spinoza, and the Bonn Notebooks (1842), excerpts on art and the history of religion, including works by Rumohr, Creuzer, de Brosses and Benjamin Constant. It then clarifies what 'religiosity' means, sketches Marx's religious upbringing and Young Hegelian circle, and explains the political pressure of the Prussian state after 1840. It closes by locating the notebooks within Marx's development.

Chen's central claim is that the notebooks served a double critique. Marx regarded Feuerbach's The Essence of Christianity (1841) as having settled the purely Christian question, yet the political and philosophical problems tied to religion remained. He faced the official philosophy of Schelling and the Young Hegelians, above all Bruno Bauer, whose work Chen calls theology in another form. Chen reads the Berlin Notebooks as a philosophical approach to religion, drawing on thinkers with a rudimentary materialism. The Bonn Notebooks, with their material on fetishism and natural religion, take an anthropological and sociological approach.

Chen concludes that the notebooks show Marx already moving against idealism, a move Chen describes as 'leaving Germany' and a 'French turn'. The Aristotle excerpts signal a reaction against the German theoretical tradition, while the French works on fetishism and religion point towards French materialism and socialist and communist ideas. Chen stresses that this stage was still far from the maturity marked by The German Ideology. Read the original if you want a brief orientation to the Berlin and Bonn Notebooks and to how a Chinese scholar places them in the young Marx's development.
quoteEn: The Berlin Notebooks and the Bonn Notebooks are proof that the young Marx used the theory of religion to explore philosophical and political possibilities.
quoteZh: 《柏林笔记》和《波恩笔记》是青年马克思通过宗教理论探寻哲学和政治上的可能性的证明。

t: The contemporary development of materialist dialectics
zh: 唯物辩证法的时代发展
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in June 2025, asks what Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times has added to materialist dialectics. Zhang Tao argues that this body of thought has made a systematic contribution, rooted in China's practice of revolution, construction, reform and governance, and that the contribution falls into five areas.

The article is organised around five paired formulations, each presented as an original contribution on one dimension of dialectics: problem-oriented practical dialectics, contradiction-transformation process dialectics, strategy-centred systems dialectics, people-first subject dialectics, and historical-initiative historical dialectics. Each is defined against a rejected alternative.

Zhang contrasts problem orientation with rationalism detached from practice and with utilitarian pragmatism, and names three kinds of key problems: those that are widespread, those that are paradoxical, and those that are newly emerging. Process dialectics, covering reform, bottom-line thinking, innovation and harmony, is set against either-or thinking. Systems dialectics, built on strategic significance, planning and realisation, is set against short-sighted and one-dimensional metaphysics. Putting the people first is set against atomistic individualism and defines the people as a subject led by the proletariat and its vanguard party. Historical initiative is set against a mechanical materialism that waits for laws to realise themselves.

Zhang concludes that this body of thought has given materialist dialectics a distinctive form in China and shows the Chinese Communists' theoretical thinking and dialectical wisdom. Zhang calls for Marxist theorists to keep exploring these contributions, and says that historical initiative should help turn a capital-first world order into a people-first one. Read the original if you want a compact outline of how current Chinese scholarship frames the Chinese-context contribution to dialectics.
quoteEn: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times has given Marxist materialist dialectics a distinctive form of expression in China, embodying the theoretical thinking and dialectical wisdom with which Chinese Communists understand and transform the world.
quoteZh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义使马克思主义唯物辩证法在中国获得了独特的表现形式，体现了中国共产党人认识世界和改造世界的理论思维水平和辩证智慧。

glossary.zh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义
glossary.en: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's ongoing project of fitting Marxism to Chinese conditions and to contemporary developments. It is often rendered in short as the 'sinicisation and contemporisation' of Marxism.
A slogan in Party ideology stating that the people's interests take highest priority. The article treats it as the basis of a 'subject dialectics'.

keywords: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context

t: Capital's critique and transcendence of Hegel's dialectic
zh: 《资本论》对黑格尔辩证法的批判与超越
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 24 June 2025
paras: Sun Lin takes up the Hegelian element in the dialectic of Capital, which the author treats as an unavoidable problem for research on the materialist conception of history. The article asks how the dialectic of Capital relates to Hegel's "nous" and "logos", and in what way it goes beyond them. Sun's thesis is that Marx actively sublated Hegel's speculative dialectic, grounding it in real social-historical "metabolism" (material exchange), so that the dialectic becomes a materialist one rooted in real essential human powers.

The piece is a short essay in three parts. The first reads the development of the commodity through the image of the embryo, drawing on Engels's description of Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit as an "embryology of spirit". The second examines Marx's remark that in the chapter on value he "coquetted" with Hegel's characteristic modes of expression, set against the Logic's sequence of being, essence and concept. The third treats metabolism as the manifestation of force and as a "dialectic of force".

In Sun's reading, the simple value form is an embryonic form that matures through changes of form into money and then capital. Metabolism has two senses: change in the material's form and exchange between use-value and exchange-value. Sun argues that Marx moves Hegel's inverted, supersensible world from speculation to the social-historical level, where the interactive relation turns into an exchange relation and a fetishistic society emerges. Hegel's force, which Sun equates with free will, becomes in Marx the unfolding of capital's drive for self-valorisation, the real ground behind the conversion of forces. Capital is thus the only thing that realises free will in ideas, yet in reality it is caught in contradiction and repeated crisis, and its "spectral objectivity" depends on the metabolism continuing.

Sun concludes that breaking the blockade of objectified labour requires a dialectic with real reflective power and will. Its ground is the essential powers of sensuous human beings in sensuous activity, which restore use-value and make the dialectic one of continual self-reflection and self-revolution. The author adds that this carries foundational significance for further liberating and developing social productive forces and raising social vitality today. Read the original if you study the Hegel–Marx relationship in Capital, especially the theory of metabolism and the form of value, and can read dense philosophical Chinese.
quoteEn: Marx holds that metabolism, or labour objectified into time, is value.
quoteZh: 马克思认为物质变换或劳动对象化为时间就是价值。

t: Exploring paths of education to empower the training of young Marxists
zh: 探索育人路径 赋能青年马克思主义者培养
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2025, describes how the Guangdong Provincial Party School trains young Marxists. Ruan Yuchun presents this work as part of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and as a way to pass the Party's cause on to the next generation. The author's thesis is that Party schools should combine theoretical education with practical education.

The piece is organised in two parts. The first covers paths of theoretical education: course development and a reading culture. The second covers paths of practical education: themed activities, social surveys and new practical formats. All examples come from the school's own programmes.

On theory, Ruan reports that the school uses case-based, seminar-style, simulation and on-site teaching, and holds collective lesson-preparation meetings across departments. It also works with the Central Party School, other Party schools, universities and research institutes. It promotes reading of the original works of Marxism, Chinese classics and Western classics through reading months and shared-reading events, so as to address trainees' "knowledge anxiety". On practice, the school runs salons and Party-day activities linked to Greater Bay Area quality branding and urban-rural integration. It sends survey teams to Dongguan, Zhaoqing, Qingyuan, Heyuan and Jiangmen. It has also set up a "Yue-Jing Cai" micro-salon with trainees from Beijing, which produces survey reports and policy advice.

Ruan concludes that these methods help trainees strengthen their theoretical grounding, hold to principle on questions of path, direction and stance, and improve their political judgement, understanding and execution. The aim is to turn the Party's innovative theory into a "golden key" for solving development problems. Read the original if you want a concrete, officially framed example of how a provincial Party school describes its youth training methods.
quoteEn: Together, they turn the Party's innovative theory into a "golden key" for solving development problems.
quoteZh: 共同将党的创新理论转化为破解发展难题的“金钥匙”。

glossary.explanation: Institutions run by Party committees at each level to train cadres and Party members in Party theory, policy and discipline. The Central Party School is the national flagship.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to contemporary developments.
A national development strategy integrating nine cities in Guangdong with Hong Kong and Macao economically.
A Guangdong provincial programme, launched in 2023, to promote county, town and village development. The article links it to urban-rural integration.

t: How Marxism understands "human essence"
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“人的本质”
paras: Liang takes the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to put the people first as a starting point and asks how Marxism arrives at a true account of the human essence. The commentary argues that, for Marxism, humans are real subjects engaged in material production within concrete social relations. On this view the essence of the human is both socially determined and historically formed, in contrast to abstract theories of human nature.

The piece is a short newspaper commentary in three parts: practice as the basis for grasping the real human essence, the class character of humans within historical development, and the free and all-round development of the person as the value goal. It draws on Marx's Theses on Feuerbach, The German Ideology, the 1844 Manuscripts and the Communist Manifesto. It ends with the Chinese Communist Party's record and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Liang contends that Feuerbach's "species essence", Enlightenment "natural rights" and ancient Chinese debates on whether human nature is good or evil all construct an abstract human being detached from social relations. Marx instead locates the essence in practice and in production, so it changes with modes of production, from dependence on kin communities, through personal dependence, to the "dependence on things" of capitalism. In class society, Liang argues, no supra-class human essence exists, and the social attributes of people appear first as class attributes.

Liang concludes that communism is the social form in which the human essence is regained on the basis of developed productive forces, and that the Party's policies from "serving the people" to reform and opening up and common prosperity pursue this aim. The piece presents Chinese modernization as centred on human development and calls for adherence to the principle of putting the people first. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-press commentary links Marx's theory of human essence to current policy language.
quoteEn: In class society there is no supra-class, universally uniform "human essence"; the social attributes of people appear first of all as their class attributes.
quoteZh: 在阶级社会里，不存在超阶级的、普遍同一的“人的本质”，人的社会属性首先表现为其阶级属性。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A policy goal of shared wealth for all, emphasised in Party discourse as a feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: The "-isms" disputes in economics and their social-philosophical foundations
zh: 经济学的“主义”之争及其社会哲学基础
paras: Why do disputes between economic schools persist even though every school builds mathematical models and cites econometric evidence? Zhu Fuqiang argues that each school rests on a social philosophy, above all a view of how individual and collective interests relate. In this account, models and statistics have become rhetoric that supports prior convictions, so the "-isms" disputes cannot be settled by claims to scientific method.

The article first sets out four social-philosophical outlooks in Western thought: the optimistic (natural harmony), the pragmatic (harmony achieved by human effort), the fatalist (innate conflict) and the radical (conflict rooted in ownership). It links each to thinkers and schools, from Smith, Bentham, Malthus and Marx to Keynes, Veblen and Pareto. It then explains how the first three outlooks merged into a mainstream, and compares how Marxist and neoclassical economics treat exploitation. It closes with the roots of the dispute and ways to ease it.

Zhu contends that from the late nineteenth century, and decisively in the 1970s and 1980s, classical liberalism, conservatism and Keynesian pragmatism converged into neoclassical liberalism. Neoclassical economics was thereby turned from Marshall's gradualist, evolutionary version into a doctrine of laissez-faire. The present contest is therefore between this mainstream and Marxist economics, in the shorthand of "preserving Marx" versus "non-Marx". The author says the two branches each capture one dimension of exploitation: Marxism stresses concentrated private, money power in production, while neoclassical thought attends to public power and to unequal exchange. Both are said to share a naturalist "affirmative rationality", which pushes policy to swing between extremes.

Zhu concludes that all schools carry ideology and none is simply progressive or backward, because their social philosophies are incommensurable. The author calls for recognising each school's one-sidedness and seeking complementarity, so that economic theory can integrate and develop. This is also meant to help readers avoid being misled by mainstream textbooks. The author also judges neoclassical liberalism to be closer to business studies than to an economics of enriching nation and people. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's typology of economic schools by social philosophy and an account of why Marxist and mainstream economics clash.
quoteEn: The cause behind the "-isms" disputes in economics is precisely the difference in the social philosophies on which the various schools are grounded.
quoteZh: 经济学界的“主义”之争，背后因由正是各流派所根基于的社会哲学观的差异。

t: Marx's writings on the East and Chinese modernization
zh: 马克思的东方社会论述与中国式现代化
paras: Wang Xiaozhang asks what Marx's scattered writings on China and Eastern societies contribute to the theoretical self-awareness expressed in the concept of Chinese modernization. The article argues that Marx's account explains why Chinese modernization is both necessary and desirable: Western-style modernization is "impossible" for China because of its traditional social structure and its position in the world order, and "undesirable" because of its capitalist form.

The article first sets out Marx's general view of history, the three stages from personal dependence through material dependence to free individuality, and the tension between historical progress and moral cost. It then turns to Marx's journalism on the Opium Wars and the Taiping movement, his remarks on the "Asiatic mode of production", and his 1848 free-trade speech. Wang also draws on dependency theory, Qin Hui's contrast between "small-community" and "large-community" societies, and Immanuel Wallerstein's distinction between technological and emancipatory modernity.

Wang argues that Marx separates modernization from its "narrow bourgeois form". Old China's dissolution under British guns was brutal and hypocritical, yet in Marx's view it was inevitable once large-scale industry created world history. On the Asiatic mode, Wang reads Marx as holding that land belongs to a despotic centre above self-sufficient village communities, which blocked exchange and kept the economy static. From this Wang concludes that China had to reform the centralised state first, and that the state must be a stronger, development-oriented actor, not a weaker one. Because China began modernizing from a subordinate position, the "underdeveloped" condition of dependency theory, Wang holds that Western colonial routes cannot be copied.

Wang concludes that the features of Chinese modernization, including common prosperity, the coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development, strip away the bourgeois form and return to Marx's goal of human emancipation. In this reading, Chinese modernization is not merely a particular case set against a universal one, but a socialist alternative to the Western-style type. It could open the way for what Wallerstein calls emancipatory modernity and enrich Marxism in turn. Read the original if you want a Marxist-theoretical justification of Chinese modernization built on Marx's Eastern-society texts, and on how Marx's views on state, land and world order are used in that argument.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is not only possible but also desirable.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化，不仅仅是可能的，而且是可欲的。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernity, set against Western-style modernization. It is stated to include common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.
A long-standing socialist goal of shared affluence, stressed in recent Party policy as a defining feature of Chinese modernization.
A term Marx used for a pre-capitalist Eastern social form with no private landownership, in which a despotic centre stands above village communities. Its meaning has been long debated among scholars.

t: The theoretical path of Marx's ecological thought and ecological revolution
st: An examination based on the relations-of-production paradigm
zh: 马克思生态思想的理论路径与生态革命
zhSub: 基于生产关系范式的考察
paras: Many Western scholars hold that Marx's thought lacks an ecological dimension, or that he ended up in a pro-technology 'Prometheanism'. Xu Hengbing and Xu Di dispute this. They argue that Marx's analysis of the human–nature relationship underwent a paradigm shift, from a single subject–object paradigm to a paradigm of relations of production. In their reading, this shift gives lasting guidance for analysing ecological problems and for building socialist ecological civilization.

The article has three parts. The first traces Marx's path from the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, through the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology, to Wage Labour and Capital, the 1857 Introduction and Capital. The second examines the roots of ecological problems under capitalist relations of production. It also criticises rival explanations from Leiss, Agger, Giddens and others, and draws on Moishe Postone and David Pepper. The third discusses how changing relations of production leads to ecological revolution, and briefly turns to China's own experience.

The authors argue that the 1844 Manuscripts remained within an abstract subject–object scheme and ended in circular reasoning about alienation. They claim that from The German Ideology onward Marx placed the human–nature relationship on the basis of human–human relations in production. On this basis, under capital nature becomes a pure instrument of self-valorisation, and capital's boundless pursuit of surplus value drives ecological damage such as the loss of soil fertility. The authors therefore reject Leiss's idea that a mindset of 'controlling nature' is the root cause, and Agger's emphasis on high consumption. In their view both are secondary effects of the relations of production. Marx's target is also a specific form of capitalist labour, not human mastery of nature as such, which answers the charges of Prometheanism and anthropocentrism.

The authors conclude that Marx's ecological programme is a thoroughgoing revolution aimed at overthrowing capitalist relations of production. They hold that ecological problems are at root social problems. Socialism does not automatically bring harmony with nature, they add, but lays the foundation for it. They state that China's ecological problems since reform and opening up stem from an unreasonable mode of development and mistaken ideas, not from the socialist system. They see the Party's drive for high-quality development and ecological education since the new era as addressing the key issue. Read the original if you want a Marxist-theoretical rebuttal of the 'anti-ecological Marx' thesis, set against Western ecological Marxism and linked to Chinese ecological civilization discourse.
quoteEn: Ecological problems are in essence social problems; only by thoroughly eradicating the social-institutional roots from which they arise can a truly rational relationship between humanity and nature be established.
quoteZh: 生态问题本质上是社会问题，只有彻底铲除其由以产生的社会制度根源，方可建立起真正合理的人与自然的关系。

glossary.explanation: An official concept, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.
An official Chinese policy goal of integrating environmental protection into economic, political and social development. It became a national strategy in the Party's 2012 congress documents.

t: A century of debate on the relationship between Marxism and traditional Chinese culture
st: A review and outlook of the scholarship
zh: 马克思主义与中国传统文化关系的百年论争
zhSub: 学术史的回顾与展望
paras: Zhang and Wang review a hundred years of Chinese scholarship on how Marxism relates to traditional Chinese culture. They begin from Xi Jinping's call at the centenary of the Communist Party (2021) to integrate Marxism both with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional culture. The authors argue that the question, which they link to 'which road China takes' and to ideological security, has never been settled, and that the scholarship falls into four schools of thought.

The article covers the period from Marxism's arrival in China (dated to 1899) to the present. It traces four positions in turn: the 'heterogeneous conflict' theory, the 'limited symbiosis' theory, the 'absorption and fusion' theory and the 'two-dimensional development' theory. It names representative figures for each, among them Chen Duxiu and Li Dazhao, Liang Shuming and Mou Zongsan, Mao Zedong, Feng Youlan, Fang Keli and Jiang Hui. It also cites foreign commentators such as Joseph Levenson, Max Weber and Joseph Needham.

On the authors' reading, the first school treats the two as mutually exclusive orthodoxies, whether in the form of Marxists who reject Confucianism or Confucians, including the mainland New Confucians Jiang Qing and Kang Xiaoguang, who want to replace Marxism. The second admits traditional culture only as a resource that Marxism may critically draw on. The third, which the authors call the current mainstream, seeks mutual absorption under Marxist guidance. The fourth treats the two as relatively independent, with Marxism as the 'soul' and traditional culture as the 'root', each developing in its own field. The authors judge the first school's 'Confucianising China' project to be utopian. They fault the third and fourth for not explaining the mechanisms of integration or the division of functions in practice.

The authors observe that research stays mostly at the level of what ought to be, with little on practical policy. They propose four directions: advancing the Two Integrations within Chinese modernization, building a more tolerant and dialogic atmosphere, making ideological security a basic aim of promoting traditional culture, and designing institutions and policies for both. They also insist that the two systems differ in essence and cannot replace one another. Read the original if you want a detailed map of Chinese-language scholarship on Marxism and Confucian tradition, and a view of how mainland scholars frame the issue today.
quoteEn: One must not be confined to affirmative thinking that endlessly exaggerates the consistency between the two, while ignoring their essential differences and irreplaceability.
quoteZh: 不能囿于肯定性思维无限夸大二者之间的一致性，忽视二者本质的差异性与不可取代性。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The 'second' integration, with traditional culture, was stressed from 2021–2023.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, as set out by Xi Jinping since 2021–2022.
The official concern that the Party's Marxist guiding ideology keep its leading position against rival ideas, including historical nihilism and cultural conservatism.

t: The historical-materialist road to "universal world history"
zh: 通向“普遍的世界历史”的唯物史观之路
paras: Wu Hongzheng asks what Marx meant by "universal world history" (universal history), a concept first formulated by Kant and then filled with different content by Hegel. The article argues that for Marx the concept refers to the unified world-historical whole, communism, that emerges once "universal intercourse" has sublated the particular interests of single nation-states and overcome civilisational barriers. Wu presents this reading as a theoretical support for the new categories of 21st-century Marxist world-history theory in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article has three parts. The first compares how Kant, Hegel and Marx pursued the concept: Kant through a contractual "league of nations" and perpetual peace, Hegel through the theodicy of Absolute Spirit moving from the Oriental to the Germanic world, and Marx through historical materialism. The second part sets out Marx's critique of idealist versions, drawing mainly on The German Ideology. The third part states the principles of universal world history under three headings: a "universal class", highly developed productive forces, and the breaking of "domination–subordination" relations of production.

Wu argues that Kant's scheme never started from real human beings and Hegel offered only a "thought in the form of universality" that gave no real freedom. Following Marx, Wu holds that the true ruler of world history is not nature's hidden plan or Absolute Spirit but the relations of production built on capitalist private property, whose expansion began with commercial capital and manufacture. Wu applies Marx's critique of false communities and ideology to the present. In this reading, "universal values" are the modern form of an abstract universality that masks the pursuit of national interest through zero-sum thinking, unilateralism and de-globalisation.

Wu concludes that Marx's road runs through the proletariat as the "universal class" and through productive forces developed enough to create universal intercourse. It also requires overcoming the domination–subordination structure, such as the city–country opposition and the opposition between developed and late-developing nations. Wu proposes that building a community with a shared future for mankind is the 21st-century Marxist content of "universal world history". Nations that sublate narrow interests on the basis of common values of all humanity could partly escape capital's logic and move towards communism. Read the original if you want a close textual account of Marx's critique of Kant and Hegel on world history, and of how a Chinese theorist links it to current world-history concepts.
quoteEn: Under capitalist private property, people are subject less to the "abstract rule of ideas" than to the "abstract rule of capital".
quoteZh: 在资本主义私有制下，与其说是人们受到“观念的抽象统治”，毋宁说是人们受到“资本的抽象统治”。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for cooperative, win-win international relations.
A formulation Xi Jinping put forward in 2015, listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. It is presented as an alternative to Western "universal values".

Marx and Engels's term in The German Ideology for the worldwide web of exchange and relations created by large-scale industry and the world market. The article treats it as the real basis of world history.
A term for values such as freedom, democracy and human rights, regarded as valid for all societies. Chinese official and academic discourse often criticises it as Western ideology.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Deconstructive practice, methodological path and significance of cultural materialism
st: Centred on Raymond Williams's The Country and the City
zh: 文化唯物主义的解构实践、方法论路径及意义
zhSub: 以雷蒙·威廉斯《乡村与城市》为中心
paras: Feng Hao and Shao Hong ask how Raymond Williams's cultural materialism, usually discussed at the level of theory, works as a method in practice. They argue that The Country and the City (1973) is a key worked example of the theory. In their reading it shows cultural materialism deconstructing the pastoral tradition and, in doing so, supplies a methodological path that deepens Marxist literary criticism.

The article first sets out the theory's origins. Williams presents it in Marxism and Literature as a critique of the orthodox base–superstructure model. It then identifies three links between the theory and the book: the book as an instance of the theory, a shared revolt against orthodox Marxism and Cambridge's official English culture, and a shared stress on historical analysis. Next it examines the book's deconstructive practice through language, structure of feeling and perspective. A final section draws out the method's theoretical and practical significance.

The authors argue that Williams moves from literature as 'reflection' of reality to literature as 'representation' and as a form of production. In their account, the green language of pastoral verse removes labour, poverty and exploitation, and the poems conceal the agrarian capitalism behind the country estate. Different structures of feeling, from pastoral innocence to the city in Blake and Wordsworth to social mobility in Hardy, mediate between local experience and dominant narratives. The progression 'perspective–form–social relations' ties a writer's vantage point, as in Ben Jonson's patron's house, to a social order. The authors read Williams's method as uniting theoretical, textual and historical analysis, and they reject Terry Eagleton's charge that cultural materialism abandons historical materialism. In their view Williams questions one-way, exclusive economic determination without denying the importance of economic practice.

The authors conclude that cultural materialism makes the base a dynamic historical process. It adds sensitivity to concrete experience in Marxist literary criticism, and it shifts criticism from aesthetic to social value while widening literary history. They suggest that future work should move towards local experience and lived practice, and should reread the theory against new literary and artistic forms. Read the original if you study Raymond Williams, Marxist literary theory or cultural studies and want a detailed case-based account of how cultural materialism operates as method.
quoteEn: The idea that 'literature is a social process of production' involves deconstructing central narratives, scrutinising literary writing and supplementing the wholeness of literary history, moving from the text towards a far wider world beyond it.
quoteZh: “文学是一种社会生产过程”的观念涉及对中心叙事的解构、对文学书写的审视、对文学历史整体性的补充，从文本出发指向文本之外更为广阔的天地。

t: Marx's thought on the city in the perspective of social reproduction and its contemporary development
zh: 马克思社会再生产视域中的城市思想及其当代发展
paras: Western urban Marxists such as Henri Lefebvre, David Harvey and Manuel Castells are often said to have made the city a Marxist theme. In their view, Marx and Engels treated it only as a site of production. Lin Mi disputes this. The article argues that in Marx and Engels the city expresses definite social relations, is an inner mechanism of a given mode of production, and externalises the contradictions of those relations. It therefore has to be studied from the standpoint of social reproduction as a totality.

The article has three parts. The first treats the city as a historical totality, tracing it from ancient society through medieval society to modern capitalism. The second treats the city as a social totality, in which capitalist social relations are continually reproduced. The third turns to Lefebvre, Harvey, Castells and Neil Smith, and asks how they developed Marx's approach. Lin also uses Peter Saunders's three methodological types (Durkheimian, Weberian, dialectical) and Lukács's critique of reification.

Lin's central move is methodological. Empiricist and Weberian approaches are called formal-rational "external reflection", which defines the city by population or size and turns it into a fixed natural entity. Marx's "ascent from the abstract to the concrete" instead traces how the city arises historically, as city and countryside move from an "undifferentiated unity" to opposition and then to the "urbanisation of the countryside". Lin then argues that the capitalist city reproduces capital relations economically, through urbanisation as a way of absorbing surplus capital. It does so politically and ideologically as well, through an unequal urban–rural order of morality, law and ideas of freedom and equality. This order hides the contradiction between capital and labour and amounts to what Lefebvre and Harvey call the fetishism of space. In Lin's reading, the Western urban Marxists show that capital now reproduces its relations through the production of space itself. Examples are urban planning and gentrification across the Fordist and post-Fordist stages, Castells's "collective consumption", and Harvey's "urban lifestyle". The city is also the setting in which the proletariat grows and may achieve liberation, so that the right to the city and spatial justice become issues.

Lin concludes that Marx's critique of political economy is an open system that must keep moving towards historical specificity, and that the city is one concrete expression of this. Lin suggests that this line of inquiry could underpin a Chinese autonomous knowledge system on the modernization of urban–rural relations, and could ground the study of urban questions in the context of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you are interested in how a Chinese Marxist scholar reconstructs Marx's urban thought from the method of the critique of political economy and reads Lefebvre, Harvey and Castells as extensions of it.
quoteEn: The city is precisely the dialectical unity of the premise and the result of the continual production and reproduction of capitalist relations of production.
quoteZh: 城市正是资本主义生产关系不断生产与再生产的前提和结果的辩证统一体。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept of China's own path of modernization, prominent in official discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article invokes it as the context for later urban research.

glossary.en: ascent from the abstract to the concrete
glossary.explanation: Marx's method of presentation in the Grundrisse and Capital, which builds up from simple abstract categories to a concrete totality in thought. Lin uses it to reconstruct how the city develops historically.
A slogan promoted in recent years for building Chinese social-science theory with its own concepts and frameworks rather than relying on Western ones.

t: A new interpretation of Marx's dialectics in the algorithmic society
zh: 马克思辩证法在算法社会的新诠释
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 11 June 2025
paras: Qin Zehua asks how Marx's dialectics can be reactivated to read the algorithmic society. The article argues that this is no simple transplant of theory but an epistemological revolution that looks past the surface of digital alienation to the relations of production. In Qin's account, dialectics must pierce the ideological illusion of technological neutrality and expose the antagonistic logic inside algorithmic society.

The short essay has three parts. It first restates the method of the "concrete totality" and argues that it remains valid in the digital age. It then describes a "leap" in how contradictions move, in form, content and space. Finally it shows how dialectics can "solve" the contradictions of the digital age, drawing on Capital, the Theses on Feuerbach, Theories of Surplus Value and The Poverty of Philosophy, with a reference to David Harvey's "spatial fix".

Qin's central move is to carry Marx's categories into the digital sphere. The dual nature of the commodity becomes a duality of data: data is a product of human interaction and so should be a "digital commons", yet under capital it becomes exclusive "digital private property". This split is said to generate a new class antagonism between an "algorithmic bourgeoisie" and a "digital proletariat". Alienation is described as threefold: in products, in the labour process and in species-being. Clicks and likes are treated as "micro-labour", through which dead labour, in the form of data, exploits living labour and blurs the line between productive and unproductive labour. Spatially, cloud infrastructure is said to bring developing countries into a "data colonial" system that reproduces the centre–periphery structure.

Qin concludes that the aim is not to reject algorithms but to free them from the logic of capital. The article points to data-commons arrangements, experiments in algorithmic democracy, blockchain-based data rights, open-source communities and transnational digital labour solidarity as practical forms of dialectics. It calls for a threefold synthesis: revolutionary restructuring of production relations, institutional practice of technological democratization, and the emancipatory return of human subjectivity. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese Marxist scholars apply the concrete totality and Marx's theory of alienation to data, platforms and digital labour.
quoteEn: The real revolution of the digital age lies not in negating algorithmic technology, but in using the epistemological revolution of dialectics to liberate it from the logic of capital.
quoteZh: 数字时代的真正革命，不在于否定算法技术，而在于通过辩证法的认识论革命，将其从资本逻辑中解放出来。

t: From classical theories of imperialism to new theories of imperialism: concepts and paradigms
st: On foreign left-wing scholars' "return to historical materialism"
zh: 从经典帝国主义论到新帝国主义论：概念与范式
zhSub: 兼论国外左翼学者“重返历史唯物主义”
source: Journal of Hubei University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2025 no. 3
paras: Qin Shiya takes up a debate among foreign left-wing scholars since the early twenty-first century: how the classical theory of imperialism (Hilferding, Luxemburg, Bukharin, Lenin) relates to the new theory of imperialism (Harvey, Wood, Callinicos). The article sorts the positions into a "continuity" view (Callinicos), a "rupture" view (Harvey) and a "transcendence" view (Panitch and Gindin). Qin argues that the disagreements come down to two questions, what imperialism is and how it should be studied, and that all sides end up by "returning to historical materialism".

The article has five parts. It first examines imperialism as a specific policy in Hobson, Hilferding, Luxemburg and Kautsky. It then follows the move to imperialism as a historical stage in Bukharin and Lenin, and describes how Harvey and Callinicos periodise a new stage after 1970 or 1991. It next compares economic–political paradigms, then turns to the theoretical reconstruction that the "return" involves, and ends with a conclusion.

Qin's central move is to reject the charge, made by the "transcendence" camp, that classical theory is economically reductionist and ahistorical. In Qin's reading, classical theorists historicised imperialism as a stage of capitalism. Luxemburg treated accumulation as a mix of economic exchange and political violence, and Bukharin set capital's expansion against the limits of the nation-state. Lenin's definition was economic but, Qin argues, covered political manifestations as well. The new theorists use dual frameworks: Harvey's capitalist and territorial logics of power, Callinicos's economic and geopolitical competition, and Wood's economic and extra-economic power. Robinson, a transnational-state theorist, criticises such dualism. Qin traces the dispute to differing understandings of the economic base and of the state, and notes Engels's 1890 letter to Conrad Schmidt on the state's reaction on the economy.

Qin concludes that these paths share one aim, the innovative development of historical materialism in the context of globalisation. The article says this requires a new theory of the capitalist state, which Harvey also calls for, and a re-conceptualisation of accumulation such as Harvey's "accumulation by dispossession", which Qin notes critics find too broad. Qin presents continuity and innovation together as supplying an indispensable framework for judging contemporary capitalism. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's map of the Callinicos–Harvey–Panitch–Gindin–Robinson debate and its roots in the classical theorists.
quoteEn: Foreign left-wing scholars' discussion of the new imperialism in essence constitutes a contemporary development of historical materialism in the context of globalisation.
quoteZh: 国外左翼学者对新帝国主义的探讨本质上构成了全球化语境下历史唯物主义的当代发展。

t: Critique of communicative capitalism and the emancipation of the subject
zh: 交往资本主义批判与主体解放
paras: Hu Jiandong takes up the "critique of communicative capitalism" raised by Western left scholars such as Jodi Dean. The short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in June 2025, argues that technological change has not ended alienation. In Hu's account, capital now invades everyday communication, and emancipation requires abolishing private ownership of technological means of production, not simply developing technology.

The piece first traces the historical emergence of communicative capitalism, linking the expansion of communication to successive forms of civilisation and to the fourth technological revolution of big data, cloud computing, 5G and artificial intelligence. It then analyses how this stage exploits people, and closes by setting out a social order based on technology sharing and universal communication, drawing on Marx.

Hu holds that communicative capitalism results from the interaction of \"capital becoming technological\" and \"technology becoming capital\". Its core logic remains exploitation and expansion, but the target shifts from factory labour to the social relations at the centre of the commodity. Every browsing, following or forwarding act produces data that is appropriated without payment, and capital also controls the supply of information in order to profit from unequal attention. Hu cites Dean's claim that the imbalance between information supply and demand for attention is the system's basic contradiction.

Hu concludes that private ownership still fetters new technologies, whose potential for governance, education and health is used only selectively and often destructively. Technology alone does not liberate, and revolutionary theory and struggle are needed. Hu calls for removing private ownership of technological means of production and for full technology sharing, so as to approach the universal intercourse Marx envisaged. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist reading of Jodi Dean's concept and its link to Marx's theory of intercourse.
quoteEn: At the stage of communicative capitalism, the key direction of subject emancipation lies not in technological development itself but in eliminating, at the institutional level, private ownership of technological means of production, and on the basis of full technology sharing, promoting the universal intercourse Marx envisaged.
quoteZh: 在交往资本主义阶段，主体解放的重点方向并非在于技术发展本身，而在于从制度层面消除技术生产资料的私人占有，以技术的全面共享为基础，推动实现马克思所设想的普遍交往状态。

t: Historical materialism as a transcendence of Feuerbach's philosophy
st: An inquiry into foundational questions in the discipline of the history of Marxism's development
zh: 历史唯物主义是对费尔巴哈哲学的超越
zhSub: 马克思主义发展史学科基础问题探究
paras: Heng Lin asks how historical materialism emerged in the specific conditions of nineteenth-century Germany, and what part Feuerbach's philosophy played in that process. The article argues that Feuerbach's anthropological materialism was an indispensable transitional link and a direct theoretical precondition. Marx and Engels, in this account, criticised and surpassed it by placing practice and social-economic relations at the centre of their thinking.

The article has five parts. It first sets out the German background: industrialisation in the Ruhr and Saxony, the crisis of 1847, feudal political fragmentation, and the intellectual currents of Hegelianism, the Young Hegelians and utopian socialism. It then traces Marx's and Engels's changing relationship to Feuerbach, from enthusiasm to rupture. Two textual comparisons follow: the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 against Feuerbach, and the Theses on Feuerbach against the Feuerbach chapter of The German Ideology. A conclusion draws the threads together.

Heng's central claim is that Marx took three things from Feuerbach: the primacy of matter, the idea of religious alienation, and a focus on the human being. Marx then transformed each of them. In the 1844 Manuscripts, alienation is carried from religion into wages, profit and rent, so that it is explained through political economy. The Theses of 1845 are read as the decisive break. They criticise old materialism for grasping reality only as an object of contemplation and not as practice, and they define the human essence as the ensemble of social relations. The Feuerbach chapter then develops the full system: social being determines social consciousness, and the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production drives social change. Heng treats the Theses as a qualitative leap that still lacked a developed theory, and the Feuerbach chapter as a mature one.

Heng concludes that historical materialism arose from several interacting factors. These were German classical philosophy, including the rational kernel of Hegel's dialectic; Feuerbach's materialism; the contradictions of German capitalism; and Marx's and Engels's own theoretical and practical work. The author presents the result as critical inheritance, not wholesale rejection, and cites Xi Jinping on practice and on Marxism as a guide to action. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly account of the Marx–Feuerbach relationship, traced through the 1844 Manuscripts, the Theses and The German Ideology.
quoteEn: Marx and Engels critically inherited the basic core of Feuerbach's materialism while overcoming its contemplative and incomplete character. They carried materialism through into the field of social history and founded historical materialism, raising understanding of social history to a new height.
quoteZh: 马克思和恩格斯批判地继承了费尔巴哈唯物主义的基本内核，同时克服了其直观性和不彻底性，将唯物主义贯彻到社会历史领域，创立了历史唯物主义，使人们对社会历史的认识达到了一个新的高度。

t: Nature, labour and capital in Capital and its manuscripts: a deductive reading
st: With a note on the practical wisdom of the ecological outlook of Chinese modernization
zh: 《资本论》及其手稿中的自然、劳动与资本关系演绎
zhSub: 兼论中国式现代化生态观的实践智慧
paras: Wang and Gao ask how Marx's Capital and its manuscripts treat the relationship among nature, labour and capital, and what that treatment means for ecological thinking today. They argue that Marx presents history as a dynamic interplay of the three, moving from fundamental opposition under capitalism towards coordinated unity under socialism. In their view, this unity is both historically necessary and the value orientation of the ecological outlook of Chinese modernization.

The article first sets out the three concepts: nature as the "prior" foundation, labour as the mediating activity, and capital as a social force. It then follows three stages: separation turning into combination, unity turning into opposition, and enslavement giving way to transcendence. A final section turns to the ecological outlook of Chinese modernization and draws three practical implications. The authors rely mainly on close reading of Marx's texts, including the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, supplemented by references to Xi Jinping's statements.

The central analysis holds that capital's drive to self-valorisation, which the authors describe as its "effect principle" and "valorisation law", intensifies the exploitation of labour and the impoverishment of nature. Nature "costs capital nothing", and technology serves as capital's ally in dominating both workers and the natural world. The authors then read Marx as locating capital's limits in itself, in natural boundaries and in workers' bodily limits. On this reading, crises, proletarian association and the negation of private property lead to free labour and the "revival" of nature.

Turning to the present, the authors argue that Chinese modernization, defined as modernization in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony, rests on three points. These are treating humans and nature as a community of life, developing socialist ecological labour with ecological aims, workers and tools, and using institutional strengths to steer capital. Because capital still operates in the primary stage of socialism, the authors call for regulating it through Party leadership, the basic economic system, the rule of law and administrative oversight, so that it serves ecological construction. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reading of Capital's ecological content and its link to current Chinese environmental policy discourse.
quoteEn: The coordinated unity of nature, labour and capital in socialist society is historically inevitable; it is the value aspiration of the ecological outlook of Chinese modernization and the guide for building a modernization in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony.
quoteZh: 社会主义社会自然、劳动与资本关系的协调统一是历史发展的必然，是中国式现代化生态观的价值诉求，也是人与自然和谐共生现代化的建设遵循。

glossary.explanation: A Party-state concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), describing China's own path of modernization as distinct from the Western model.

glossary.zh: 人与自然和谐共生的现代化
glossary.pinyin: rén yǔ zìrán héxié gòngshēng de xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernization in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony
glossary.explanation: One of the stated features of Chinese modernization, which stresses ecological protection alongside economic development.
The official thesis that China is still at an early stage of socialism. It is used to justify a mixed ownership system and a market economy.
A term the authors use for labour oriented towards a benign material exchange between humans and nature, as opposed to alienated labour under capital.

t: The philosophical logic of constructing a discourse system of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色哲学社会科学话语体系建构的哲学逻辑
paras: Following the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to accelerate the building of disciplinary, academic and discourse systems of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics, Huang asks what philosophical logic should govern the construction of the discourse system. The article argues that four paired categories (the one and the many, critique and construction, the general and the particular, the ought and the actual) frame the basic problems, and that Marxist guidance and Chinese practice together make the resulting discourse autonomous.

Huang opens by defining the discourse system as the outward expression of the theoretical and academic systems. It is built around the question of what kind of socialism with Chinese characteristics to uphold and develop in the new era, and it has already produced discourses such as Chinese modernization, the shared values of all mankind, a community with a shared future for mankind and a new form of human civilization. Four sections then treat each pair as a distinct problem: a precondition, a strategy, a question of generation and a practical question.

On the first two pairs, Huang holds that the "one" is the guiding "Dao", meaning Marxism and its Sinicized theories plus fine traditional Chinese culture, while the "many" is the cluster of distinctive concepts and expressions. Critique and construction must be unified. Huang says the "modernization equals Westernization" frame reflects Western-centrism and treats Western discourse as "local knowledge" rather than universal truth. On the third pair, the discourse must be commensurable with others, so as to avoid "talking to itself", while keeping its own core categories. Huang presents the shared values of all mankind as an example of generality, and the Western "universal values" discourse as a counter-example. On the fourth pair, the "ought" is what to say and the "actual" is how to say it. Huang asks for political, academic and popular discourse to be fused, with theoretical depth and rich practice as the foundation.

Huang concludes that the Chinese discourse system must rest on thoroughgoing theory and on the practice of Chinese modernization. Citing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Huang stresses the need to build Chinese discourse and narrative and to raise the effectiveness of international communication, given what the article describes as Western dominance of global discourse power. The aim is to turn institutional strengths and governance effectiveness into discursive strength. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese philosopher uses dialectical categories to justify and structure official discourse-building, and how Chinese modernization serves as the main case.
quoteEn: The discourse system of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics must have political height, theoretical depth and the warmth of popular life.
quoteZh: 中国特色哲学社会科学话语体系既要有政治的高度，也要有理论的厚度，还要有大众生活的温度。

glossary.explanation: Official concept that presents China's path of modernization as distinct from Western models. It is central to Party theory since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance.
Official formulation naming peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as common values. It is presented as an alternative to Western "universal values".

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: Official phrase for the civilizational outcome claimed for Chinese modernization, used by Xi Jinping in 2021.

The organised set of concepts, categories and expressions through which a body of theory is articulated and communicated. In Chinese academic policy it is linked to "discourse power" in international debate.
A classical Chinese term for the underlying principle or way. Here it refers to the ideas and guiding theory behind discourse.

t: High-quality development as a major innovation in the categories of Marxist political economy
zh: 高质量发展是马克思主义政治经济学范畴的重大创新
paras: Qiu Haiping argues that high-quality development is an original and signature concept of Xi Jinping's economic thought and a major innovation in the categories of Marxist political economy. The commentary, first published in the People's Daily in June 2025, holds that the concept both applies and extends the Marxist tradition. Qiu presents it as the "hard truth" of the new era and the first task of building a modern socialist country.

The piece sets out four ways in which the concept develops Marxist political economy. These are the theory of stages of economic development, the thinking on the quality of economic development, the thinking on the mode of development, and the theory of productive forces. For each, Qiu first recalls what Marx, Engels and Lenin said, drawing on Capital and the Critique of the Gotha Programme. Qiu then sets out Xi Jinping's statements from 2012 to 2024.

On stages, Qiu traces Xi's successive judgements from the "three-phase superposition" and the "new normal" to the 2017 claim that China had moved from high-speed growth to a stage of high-quality development. Qiu says all of these point to high-quality development. On quality, Qiu holds that Xi's definition, which covers meeting people's needs for a better life and embodying the new development philosophy, goes beyond a GDP-centred accounting system. On the mode of development, Qiu links Marx's distinction between extensive and intensive reproduction to Xi's 2017 criteria for supply, demand, input-output, distribution and macroeconomic circulation. On productive forces, Qiu argues that new quality productive forces carry forward high-quality development and give productive forces a distinction of "qualitative forms" that Marx never made.

Qiu concludes that Xi's expositions on high-quality development are scientific theory that has been borne out in practice. Qiu cites growing innovation capacity and the upgrading of traditional industries since the new era began. Qiu calls for continued study of Xi Jinping economic thought and for treating high-quality development as the priority, so as to offer "the greatest certainty" to an uncertain world. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary presents Xi Jinping's economic concepts as continuous with, and innovations upon, classical Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: The concept of new quality productive forces for the first time gives productive forces an explicit division into qualitative forms and a theoretical definition, promotes a "revolution in terminology", and achieves a major innovation in the Marxist theory of productive forces.
quoteZh: 新质生产力概念第一次对生产力进行了明确的质态划分和理论规定，推动“术语的革命”，实现了对马克思主义生产力理论的重大创新。

glossary.explanation: An official economic goal that Xi Jinping set out in 2017, when he said China's economy was moving from rapid growth to a stage of quality-focused growth. It stresses innovation, coordination, green growth, openness and sharing instead of speed alone.

A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023–24. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, and it is closely tied to the policy of high-quality development.
The official framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015. It serves as the official yardstick for judging the quality of development.
Xi Jinping's 2014 term for China's economy shifting from high-speed to medium-high-speed growth and to structural upgrading.
The official name for the body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, which forms part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

t: New quality productive forces empowering Chinese modernization: a literature review and outlook
zh: 新质生产力赋能中国式现代化：文献述评与展望
source: Journal of Xi'an University of Finance and Economics, first published online 31 March 2025
paras: This literature review surveys Chinese scholarship on how new quality productive forces "empower" Chinese modernization. Written after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), it treats the concept as a strong driver of Chinese modernization and high-quality development. Kang and Zhang aim to consolidate recent findings and identify where further research is possible.

The review is organised around four questions: the analytical frameworks scholars use, the operating mechanisms of empowerment, the proposed implementation paths, and an overall assessment with an outlook. Frameworks are grouped by their basis: Marx's thought on modernization, the theory and practice of Chinese modernization, and the theory of new quality productive forces itself. The mechanisms section distinguishes theoretical from empirical methods. It then sorts substantive claims into three schools: industry empowerment, factor empowerment and civilisation empowerment. The paths section covers principles, institutional guarantees and practical routes.

The authors report that scholars largely work from historical materialism: qualitative change in productive forces transforms relations of production and drives modernization. In their account, the literature has not yet specified concrete empowerment mechanisms, and it tends to neglect relations of production. They illustrate this with driverless vehicles, where the issue is not only job displacement but a restructuring of production relations. They add that frameworks should include national institutional factors, namely a dual path of institutional advantage developing productive forces and productive-force growth prompting institutional reform. Education, they argue, is the decisive link, since people are both the goal and the active force.

Kang and Zhang conclude that the literature has begun to build a research paradigm for a Chinese autonomous economics knowledge system, has formed a basic analytical framework, and is moving from theory towards empirical indicators for measuring effects. They propose two directions: situating Chinese modernization and new quality productive forces in the world history of modernization, with comparison to Western modernization and a return to Marx's analysis; and studying the distinctive mechanisms through which Chinese modernization fosters new productive forces, including comparison with other countries' modernization models. Read the original if you want a map of the 2024–25 Chinese debate, with the scholars and frameworks named, and a view of the gaps the authors identify.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are, after all, productive forces; to define their distinctive advantages, one must return to Marx's analysis of capitalist modernization and the mechanisms that generate modern productive forces.
quoteZh: 新质生产力终究是生产力，如何界定其独特优势，还需回到马克思对资本主义现代化与现代生产力产生机制的分析上

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It denotes advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of factors and industrial upgrading, with higher total factor productivity as its core marker.

The official term for China's path of modernization, emphasised since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization, with features such as a huge population and common prosperity.
The official economic goal that replaces a focus on high-speed growth with quality, innovation and efficiency. It has been a central theme since 2017.

keywords: productive forces and relations of production

t: Promoting the development of new quality productive forces through high-standard opening up
zh: 以高水平开放推动新质生产力发展
source: Journal of Northeastern University (Social Science Edition), 2025 no. 2
paras: Huang Qunhui asks how high-standard opening up can drive the development of new quality productive forces, a concept Xi Jinping first put forward in September 2023. The author argues that new quality productive forces, as an advanced form of productive forces in line with the new development philosophy, must also accord with the principle of open development. Expanding high-standard opening up, in Huang's view, creates a favourable international environment for them.

The article has three parts. The first reads productive forces as a system with three dimensions: elements, structure and function. The second uses statistics and a composite index to identify weak points in China's development of new quality productive forces. The third sets out three priority areas for using opening up to advance them.

Huang holds that the core marker of new quality productive forces is a large rise in total factor productivity. On the elements side, the author cites shortfalls in high-level talent, basic research spending (6.65% of R&D in 2023) and computing infrastructure, noting that chip imports were 72% of the global total in 2022. On structure, a six-dimension index of the modernized industrial system gave China 0.54 in 2019, behind the United States, Japan and Germany. Completeness is China's strength, while advancement, openness and security are weaker. On function, total factor productivity growth has hovered around 1% since the 2008 crisis, and Huang links its earlier surges to the gains from reform and opening up.

Huang proposes three priorities. The first is a world-class international business environment, including a "tech immigration" scheme for foreign talent, new markets for technology factors, and alignment with high-standard trade rules such as CPTPP and DEPA. The second is to build the modernized industrial system through open cooperation in global industrial and supply chains, easing foreign investment access and encouraging foreign R&D centres in China. The third is to make free trade zones platforms for testing high-standard rules, such as cross-border data flows, and to use Hainan, the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area, Hong Kong and Macao as demonstration sites. Huang presents these steps as a way to raise total factor productivity and support the goal of basically achieving modernization by 2035. Read the original if you want an economist's policy-oriented account linking new quality productive forces to institutional opening up, with the index and productivity figures it cites.
quoteEn: Overall, looking at the industrial system that carries new quality productive forces, advancement, openness and security are our weak points, while completeness is our greatest strength.
quoteZh: 总体上从新质生产力承载的产业体系看，先进性、开放性和安全性是我们的短板，完整性是我们的最大优势。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in September 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and higher total factor productivity. It is now central to official economic policy discourse.
The official framework, set out in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development. It guides Chinese economic policy.
Opening that goes beyond tariffs and market access to align domestic rules, regulations and standards with high-standard international ones.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: The materialist dialectics in further deepening reform comprehensively: an exploration
zh: 进一步全面深化改革的唯物辩证法意蕴探赜
paras: This article asks how the Chinese Communist Party has drawn on materialist dialectics in the policy of further deepening reform comprehensively. Jia Limin argues that the Party's grasp of three laws of dialectics (the transformation of quantity into quality, the unity of opposites, and the negation of the negation) has let it fix the historical position, the concrete tasks and the overall goal of this round of reform. The author presents this as a creative application of Marxist method that can help improve the quality and efficiency of reform in the new era.

The article has three main sections, one for each law. The first treats reform and opening up as a process in which gradual change and qualitative leaps interweave, and places further deepening within it. The second applies the law of the unity of opposites to identify the starting point, the focal point and the key point of reform. The third uses the negation of the negation to set out the role, the path and the forward-moving character of the reform. Jia draws on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong's "On Contradiction" and Xi Jinping's statements, and refers to the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and that of the 20th (2024).

Jia's central moves assign each stage of reform a dialectical position. Comprehensive deepening of reform after 2013 is read as a qualitative leap, in its starting problems, its process and its results. Further deepening is then read as a new quantitative phase built on that leap, with greater breadth, depth and effectiveness. For the unity of opposites, the author names the starting point as the contradiction between the overall goal of reform and the reality of reform, citing formalism and weak coordination among departments. The key point is the principal contradiction between productive forces and relations of production. Reform should therefore focus on liberating and developing the productive forces, with economic reform in the lead, while combining the "two-point" and "emphasis" approaches. Finally, further deepening is treated as the stage of negation of the negation. It sublates earlier reform by keeping its positive elements, for example by moving from the "six focuses" of 2013 to the "seven focuses" of 2024, and adds new ones.

Jia concludes that further deepening is a higher-level reform that is dynamic and continuing, not a stopping point, and that it will advance with irresistible momentum. Reform should uphold the Party's leadership and other major principles, link itself to Chinese modernization, combine emancipating the mind with seeking truth from facts, and show a fighting spirit and historical initiative. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese academic maps the Party's reform agenda onto the three laws of dialectics.
quoteEn: The principal contradiction faced in the process of further deepening reform comprehensively is how to keep adjusting the relations of production so as to further liberate and develop the productive forces.
quoteZh: 进一步全面深化改革过程中所面对的主要矛盾就是如何持续调整生产关系以进一步解放和发展生产力。

glossary.explanation: The reform agenda adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in July 2024. It builds on the comprehensively deepening reform launched in 2013 and sets a timetable of targets, with a main goal of perfecting socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernizing national governance.
The official Party concept of China's own path of modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A slogan dating from the late 1970s urging Party members to break free of rigid dogma. It is usually paired with seeking truth from facts.

glossary.literal: theory of two points and theory of key points
glossary.explanation: A principle from Mao's "On Contradiction": consider both sides of a contradiction while giving priority to its principal aspect.

t: An analysis of "historical initiative" from the perspective of Marxism
zh: 马克思主义视阈下“历史主动”问题探析
paras: Mei Lan asks what "historical initiative" (lishi zhudong) means in Marxism and why it matters. Earlier studies, the author says, drew on Marx and Engels's judgements of the proletariat and discussed the present-day significance of the "spirit of historical initiative" from the standpoint of the socialist movement, but could not explain how the problem arises or what it means philosophically. Mei argues that historical initiative is not mere subjective agency. It is a practice-based process of making history, and the concept of practice reveals its essence.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs the problem's "logic of formation" from Marx's concept of practice, especially the Theses on Feuerbach. The second examines the concrete grounds on which Marx and Engels judged historical initiative, drawing on the Communist Manifesto's critique of utopian socialism and Marx's assessment of the Paris Commune. The third derives three general forms of historical initiative from their reflections on proletarian revolution.

In Mei's reading, practice is the activity of changing the world, so history is made by people and becomes "their own" only when they act to change it. Initiative therefore means "going to practise", not waiting for history to unfold. Because the changed world is a social formation, the standard for judging initiative is concrete. Marx and Engels faulted the utopian socialists for the "absence of action", since they gave the proletariat no distinctive political movement. They praised the Commune for smashing the old state machine. Mei restricts the bearer of initiative to the working class, whereas the petty bourgeoisie, in the article's account, lacks autonomy. The three general forms are: stimulating initiative by creating material, class and ideological conditions; exercising it through organised, political direct action and class struggle; and keeping it through flexible strategy, illustrated by Marx's analysis of the failure of the 1848 revolution in France and by the long-term nature of socialist construction after seizing power.

Mei concludes that elucidating historical initiative frees Marxism from historical determinism and makes people the subject and creator of history. The author adds that this deepens the understanding of the relation between initiative and practice. In the "new era" and on the "new journey", Mei calls for a more conscious strengthening of the spirit of historical initiative, and of the determination, courage and perseverance to change the world, in order to advance socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a close philosophical reading of how Marx and Engels's texts on practice, the Commune and revolutionary strategy can be organised into a theory of historical initiative.
quoteEn: "Historical initiative" is nothing other than making history the history of its creators, giving history a certain quality of being "one's own".
quoteZh: 所谓“历史主动”无非就是要让历史变为创造者的历史，使历史获得某种“属己性”。

glossary.explanation: A term in Party theory for the active, self-conscious role of practical agents in shaping historical development. It features prominently in recent Party documents and in scholarship that traces it back to Marx and Engels.
A core category of Marxist philosophy in China, understood following Marx's Theses on Feuerbach as sensuous human activity that changes the world.
The overall structure of a society defined by its mode of production, such as feudal or capitalist society. Changes of social formation are treated as the content of historical development.
The official name for China's current path and system, used since the 1980s.

t: Lukács's Ontology of Social Being as a misplaced reading of Marx
zh: 卢卡奇《关于社会存在的本体论》对马克思的错位阅读
paras: Yang Haifeng examines Georg Lukács's late work The Ontology of Social Being, which rebuilds Marx's philosophy on the basis of labour. Yang argues that this reconstruction rests on a "misplaced reading" (cuowei yuedu) of Marx, and that earlier discussions of Lukács have not identified the problem. The misplacement is said to be twofold: logical, because it explains Marx through a Hegelian ontology of labour, and textual, because it reads Capital through the Grundrisse.

The article opens by noting three shifts from History and Class Consciousness: Lukács accepts the priority of nature, criticises Hegel's subject–object identity, and replaces practice with labour as the ontological basis. Yang concentrates on the third. The first section reconsiders Marx's development from The German Ideology to Capital, set against the humanist (Fromm), Althusserian, Soviet-textbook and Chinese-textbook views. The second section sets out Lukács's labour ontology, and the third compares the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, the Grundrisse and Capital. It also counts Lukács's citations in the second volume of the Ontology.

Yang's central claim is that the shared consensus on the continuity of Marx's thought after 1845 is mistaken.
