In Yang's account, Marx moved from a "production logic", concerned with satisfying needs and close to classical political economy, to a "capital logic", in which the drive for surplus value governs material production and turns needs into carriers of insatiable desire. Lukács's labour ontology, with its unity of teleology and causality, its "second nature" and its account of freedom, extends the production logic. Yang traces it to Hegel's treatment of labour and to the 1844 and 1857–58 manuscripts. Yang adds that the Grundrisse already holds both logics, and that Marx there warns that capital cannot be understood from material production or from objectification and alienation. According to Yang, Lukács cites Capital about 81 times but follows the Grundrisse's labour-ontological line. Yang also criticises Postone and Arthur for explaining capital through value, since Marx held that value is determined by capital.

Yang concludes that Lukács reconstructed Marx creatively but missed the major shift from The German Ideology to Capital, and so could not resolve the difficulties of labour ontology. Yang says the same limit affects Christine Gould's reading and, in part, Postone's. Properly understanding Lukács and other Western scholars therefore requires re-reading Marx, in order to gain a theoretical reference point. Read the original if you study Lukács, Western Marxism or the relation between the Grundrisse and Capital, and want a Chinese scholar's argument about labour ontology versus capital logic.
quoteEn: Marx's use of the logic of capital to govern the logic of production was the fundamental inversion of traditional philosophy and classical political economy.
quoteZh: 马克思以资本逻辑来统摄生产逻辑，才是对传统哲学与古典经济学的根本性颠倒

glossary.explanation: Yang's term for Lukács's reading of Marx, which he says puts Marx's concepts and texts in the wrong logical and textual place.
The view that labour is the foundational category of human social being. Lukács adopts it in his late work, and Yang traces it to Hegel and the 1844 and 1857–58 manuscripts.

Yang's name for an anthropological logic in which production serves the satisfaction of human needs. He says it is shared with classical political economy and with the viewpoint of The German Ideology.
The logic in which production is subordinated to value valorisation and the pursuit of surplus value. Yang says it is the basis of Capital and marks a break from production logic.

t: A deep understanding of the theoretical meaning and innovative contribution of building a new development pattern
zh: 深刻理解构建新发展格局的理论内涵与创新贡献
paras: Zhang Yan and Wang Chen write in the People's Daily in 2025 about the "new development pattern" that Xi Jinping first proposed in 2020. This pattern takes the domestic circulation as the mainstay, with domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other. The authors describe it as an original, signature concept of Xi Jinping's economic thought. They argue that it unites strategy, theory and practice, and that it innovatively develops Marxist political economy.

The piece first sets out the strategic, theoretical and practical sides of the concept. It then reads the concept through four areas of Marxist political economy: the laws of economic circulation, the world market, social reproduction, and the contradictions of capitalist economic operation. Each section pairs Marx or Engels, or a statement by Xi, with the authors' account of how the new pattern extends that framework. The authors also contrast the new pattern with what they call the limits of Western economics.

On circulation, the authors say the pattern adds to the production–distribution–exchange–consumption cycle. It asks for supply to adapt to demand, for fairer distribution, and for a wider exchange sphere that includes the unified national market, logistics and finance. On the world market, they present it as an open dual circulation, not a closed one, and cite rising outward direct investment and high-level opening. They also name the Belt and Road Initiative. On reproduction, they stress scientific and technological self-reliance, new production factors such as data, and a modern industrial system. On capitalism, they say it distinguishes capital from capitalism: capital's drive for profit must be regulated, while its role as a production factor is used under the socialist market economy. They also call for balancing opening with security.

The authors conclude that the pattern rests on Marxist worldview and methodology and reveals the objective path from economic power to economic strength. They call for understanding it in terms of historical necessity, long-term development and the whole of modernization, and for relying on the nation's own strength. The text links this to planning for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Read the original if you want an example of how official Chinese commentary ties a current economic policy concept to Marx's theories of circulation, the world market and reproduction.
quoteEn: Building the new development pattern has further enriched and extended the content and scope of each link in the Marxist political economy framework for analysing economic circulation.
quoteZh: 构建新发展格局进一步丰富拓展了马克思主义政治经济学关于经济循环分析框架中各环节的内涵外延

glossary.explanation: An economic strategy announced by Xi Jinping in 2020. It makes the domestic circulation the mainstay while domestic and international circulations reinforce each other.
The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping. It is presented officially as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
China's infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013, linking China with countries in Eurasia, Africa and elsewhere.
The official name for China's economic system, which combines market mechanisms with public ownership and Party leadership. It was adopted as a goal in 1992.

t: Value theory, crisis theory and the contemporary world from a Marxist perspective
st: An interview with the British Marxist economist Michael Roberts
zh: 马克思主义视角下的价值理论、危机理论与当代世界
zhSub: 访英国马克思主义经济学家迈克尔·罗伯茨
paras: This is an interview, conducted by Qin Shiya for World Socialism Studies (2025, no. 4), with the British Marxist economist Michael Roberts (born 1946), author of The Great Recession and The Long Depression and a long-time blogger on the world economy. Asked what is central to Marxism, Roberts names class struggle as the driver of history and the law of value, under which capitalism is a system of production for the profit of owners of the means of production. From this he derives his main thesis: crises are inherent to capitalism and stem from a falling rate of profit, so they cannot be cured by reform.

The interview has four parts: Marxist value and crisis theory; financialization; digital capitalism and 'technofeudalism'; and Trump and economic imperialism. Along the way Roberts discusses Engels's editing of Capital, volume 3, cryptocurrencies, artificial intelligence, the North–South gap, public debt and prospects for the global economy. He closes by describing his blog, aimed at activists rather than academics, and a forthcoming sequel to The Long Depression.

Roberts argues that the tendency of the profit rate to fall (Capital, vol. 3, chs 13–15) is Marx's core crisis theory, and rejects underconsumptionist and overproduction accounts as secondary to profitability. He dismisses Michael Heinrich's claim that Engels distorted Marx's text as 'nonsense'. He holds that Keynes, Minsky and monopoly-capital theorists all wrongly suggest capitalism can be stabilised. In his view financialization has not turned capitalism into a money-making system detached from exploitation, because most profit still comes from workers' production. Likewise, big-tech firms are for him thoroughly capitalist, so he rejects 'technofeudalism'. He also rejects 'multitude' as a replacement for the proletariat, treating mental labour as value-creating.

Roberts expects another recession before the end of the decade, possibly triggered by corporate debt and 'zombie' firms, and describes the post-2009 period as a long depression. He argues China has avoided capitalist crises through its large state sector and planning, and should expand both. He predicts Trump's tariffs and tax cuts will raise tensions and inequality, and calls for developing countries to cooperate under governments representing labour and common ownership. Read the original if you want a Western Marxist's profit-rate view of crisis, finance, AI and US–China rivalry, presented to a Chinese Marxist readership.
quoteEn: The only way to end crises is to replace capitalism with a planned economy under common ownership, that is, to eliminate the capitalists.
quoteZh: 结束危机的唯一方法是用共有制(common ownership)下的计划经济取代资本主义，即消除资本家。

t: The revolutionary character of Marx's thought
st: An analysis based on the Theses on Feuerbach
zh: 马克思思想的革命性特质
zhSub: 基于《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》的分析
paras: Li Yang asks what the Theses on Feuerbach reveal about the revolutionary character of Marx's thought. Engels called the Theses the first document containing the germ of a new world outlook. Li argues that this short text concentrates Marx's revolutionary quality, both as a philosophical revolution and as a philosophy of revolution.

The commentary has two parts. The first traces revolutionary character through Marx's life and work: his critique of reality, his theoretical critique, and his practical activity. The second turns to the Theses themselves, covering their view of human essence, their new conception of practice and the new materialism.

Li holds that Marx's critique was not moral indignation but a thorough theoretical critique grounded in the laws of social development. It led from the criticism of Hegel and of Feuerbach to political economy and scientific socialism. In the Theses, Li reads human essence as the ensemble of social relations. Practice becomes the core category, overcoming the opposition of subject and object and of individual and society. Li stresses that this is not a new practice-based ontology or metaphysics. Practice points concretely to revolution: changing circumstances and self-change coincide only as revolutionary practice, and the truth of thinking is a practical question. This active theory of reflection gives communism a revolutionary philosophical basis.

Li concludes that we still live in the historical era Marxism identified, so the Theses' revolutionary quality remains the spiritual essence of the age. Citing Xi Jinping, Li calls on contemporary Marxists to let the Party's self-reform lead social revolution, and to combine Marxism with present conditions. Read the original if you want a short, Party-aligned introduction to how Chinese scholars currently read the Theses on Feuerbach.
quoteEn: The Theses are a concentrated expression of the revolutionary character of Marx's thought.
quoteZh: 《提纲》是马克思思想革命性特质的集中体现。

glossary.explanation: A term prominent under Xi Jinping for the Communist Party's continuous efforts to correct itself and maintain discipline. The article presents it as leading social revolution.

t: Re-examining Marx's social theory and its contemporary relevance
zh: 重审马克思社会理论及其当代性
paras: Lü Jingmei takes up Marx's proposition of the "self-criticism of bourgeois society", from the Introduction to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, as a way to reread Marx's social theory and show why it still matters. The article argues that this reading does not replace other interpretations but enriches the description and understanding of bourgeois society. It treats Marx's social theory as an anatomy of bourgeois society as a whole, as well as an account of real individuals and their reified condition.

This is a short commentary published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2025, and it is a stage result of a National Social Science Fund project on Marx and Engels's idea of social self-criticism. It first sets out how Marx conceives bourgeois society, then compares two routes to understanding it, and finally turns to three kinds of contemporary "power" in Marx's theory: to explain, to criticise and to shape social reality.

Lü argues that Marx treats bourgeois society as a constantly moving "real subject", composed by individuals yet structurally determining them. Two routes lead into this society. The political-economy route takes the relation of capital and labour as its axis, and the social-political-philosophy route takes the relation of individual and society. Lü proposes refining the latter into individual, society and state, inserting a middle level of economic society, which they call Weberian ideal types. This gives the abstract contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, and the antagonism between bourgeoisie and proletariat, more concrete bearers. In Lü's view it also balances structure and agency, so the two routes complement each other.

On contemporary relevance, Lü argues that Marx's method can explain changes such as immaterial labour, globalisation, financialisation and digital technology, if they are seen as expressions of society's self-movement. It can also criticise a capitalism that has learned self-repair through the reproduction of social relations, a point Lü draws from Althusser and Lefebvre. Lü adds that Marxism informs feminist, ecological and anti-colonial movements, and that China should keep reflecting on social-relations reproduction and human emancipation. Read the original if you want a compact, theory-oriented statement of how Chinese scholars link Marx's social theory to contemporary capitalism and to China.
quoteEn: Marx's social theory is not a finished, closed system to be taken out and used to cut social reality to fit; it aims at the universal emancipation of humanity and actively intervenes in human social life.
quoteZh: 马克思社会理论不是业已完成的封闭理论体系，可以拿出来随意剪裁社会现实，而是以普遍的人的解放为鹄的，主动介入和积极干预人类社会生活。

t: Building and applying the knowledge system of the Marxist theory discipline
zh: 马克思主义理论学科知识体系的构建和应用
paras: Twenty years after Marxist theory was established as a first-level discipline (at the end of 2005), Zhang Leisheng argues that its high-quality development now depends on constructing and applying its own knowledge system. The commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2025, treats this as part of the wider task of building an autonomous Chinese knowledge system in philosophy and the social sciences with Chinese characteristics.

The piece has two parts. The first deals with construction: the discipline's leading position among the Chinese social sciences, why it needs its own knowledge system, and what that system consists of. The second deals with application, moving from the knowledge system to the course system, the textbook system and the teaching system in graduate education.

On construction, Zhang holds that two decades of debate about the discipline's connotation, structure, research objects and personnel training show that, to differ from Marxist philosophy, Marxist political economy and scientific socialism, it must study Marxism as a whole. In Zhang's account, the knowledge system is the condensed expression of three further systems. The disciplinary system has three elements: object, features and research directions. The academic system is the body of theory that reveals the object's essence and laws. The discourse system is its form of expression and must combine scholarly and ideological character. On application, Zhang argues that the knowledge system determines the modular master's and doctoral curricula, which in turn determine the textbook system. Textbooks then have to be turned into a teaching system that students can understand and enjoy.

Zhang concludes that existing textbook types cannot meet the needs of training high-quality talent. The commentary calls for stronger textbook construction with Chinese characteristics, style and manner. It also calls for digital and audiovisual materials and a teaching resource base at both first- and second-level discipline scope, containing basic materials, documents, guiding questions and theoretical discussion. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a leading Chinese Marxist theorist links discipline-building to curriculum, textbooks and teaching in Marxist theory education.
quoteEn: Building the teaching system must not only reflect the requirements of the discipline's knowledge system, but, more importantly, reflect the requirement that students can take it in, concentrating on imparting knowledge in a way that students like to hear and can understand.
quoteZh: 教学体系的构建不仅要体现学科的知识体系要求，更重要的是要体现学生能够接受学科知识体系的要求，着重于面向学生传授知识使他们爱听并能听懂。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论一级学科
glossary.explanation: In China's university classification, a first-level discipline is a major academic field containing several second-level disciplines. Marxist theory was added as one at the end of 2005, alongside Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism, which became second-level disciplines within it or related fields.

In current Chinese policy discourse, the 'autonomous knowledge system' is the goal of building Chinese-developed theories and concepts. The author treats it as the combined expression of the disciplinary, academic and discourse systems.

keywords: philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics

t: The historical dimension in the Theses on Feuerbach
zh: 《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》中的历史维度
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 22 May 2025
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary, Lin Qing asks whether and how a historical dimension appears in Marx's Theses on Feuerbach (1845), a text whose wording centres on materialism and 'practice'. Lin argues that the Theses complete a socio-historical turn in materialism. Marx takes over Feuerbach's materialist 'inversion' of Hegel but restores the social and historical dimension that Feuerbach discarded. The result, in Lin's account, is the new materialism, or historical materialism.

The article moves through three steps. It first shows how the socio-historical dimension comes to the fore in the Theses' account of being and of knowledge. It then turns to Marx's critique of the idea of an 'end of history'. Finally it considers what the historical dimension means for Marx's philosophical revolution, drawing on The German Ideology.

Lin reads Thesis 1 as showing that contemplation and the purely objective view of the object are both unhistorical, since history appears only in the relation between subject and object. Theses 3 and 6 then make human social being the unity of changing circumstances and self-change, 'the ensemble of the social relations'. On knowledge (Thesis 2), Lin holds that Marx places cognition within historical change and requires a critique of ideology before the real object can be known. On Thesis 9, Lin argues that contemplating civil society is not enough, because Hegel in effect treats it as the end of history. Marx's standpoint is 'human society or social humanity', which calls for transforming civil society through revolutionary practice.

Lin concludes that Marx turns philosophical questions into socio-historical ones. Traditional philosophy, especially Hegel's, put society and history inside the framework of philosophy, whereas Marx puts philosophy inside the framework of society and history. In Lin's view the Theses mark the start of this philosophical revolution. Read the original if you want a concise reading of the Theses on Feuerbach as the starting point of historical materialism's socio-historical turn.
quoteEn: Traditional philosophy, especially Hegel's, puts the social and historical dimensions inside the framework of 'philosophy', whereas Marx puts 'philosophy' inside the framework of society and history, and thereby completes a philosophical revolution against traditional philosophy.
quoteZh: 传统的哲学，尤其是黑格尔的哲学，是将社会、历史维度装进“哲学”的框架中，而马克思则将“哲学”装进社会和历史的框架中，从而完成了对传统哲学的哲学革命。

t: The dialectics of practice and the spirit of historical initiative
zh: 实践辩证法与历史主动精神
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2025, rereads Marx's Theses on Feuerbach as the founding document of Marxist philosophy. Wang Yicheng argues that Marx's concept of practice, understood as the dialectical unity of subject and object, supplies the philosophical basis for what is now called the spirit of historical initiative (历史主动精神).

The article has three parts. It first treats the Theses as a paradigm revolution centred on practice, then asks how changing the world is possible, and finally draws out a contemporary reading. Wang follows the concept of practice from the Theses through The German Ideology and the Communist Manifesto to Capital.

Wang says Marx surpassed Feuerbach and sublated Hegel. Feuerbach's inversion of subject and predicate, in this reading, left sensuous objects abstract and intuitive, while Hegel grasped the activity of practice only as the self-development of absolute spirit. Marx kept Hegel's dialectical principle of activity and rooted it in material production. Wang rejects two misreadings of practice: as pure subjectivity detached from objective conditions, and as an objective process without a subject. Practice is both conditioned by existing historical circumstances and able to transform its objects. The laws of history, like the economic laws analysed in Capital, exist within people's own activity.

Wang concludes that the spirit of historical initiative needs two things together. It must rest on a scientific grasp of objective laws, to avoid voluntarism, and it must reject mechanical determinism and fatalism. Wang presents changing the world as the historical mission of the proletariat, and the joining of Marxism with the workers' movement as the realisation of that task. Read the original if you want a brief, Party-school-style account of how the Theses on Feuerbach is linked to the current slogan of historical initiative.
quoteEn: The manifestation of historical laws is not the spontaneous result of a process without a subject; it is deeply rooted in human practice and requires the consciousness and initiative of the historical subject.
quoteZh: 历史规律的呈现不是无主体的自发结果，它深深根植于人类的实践活动，并需要历史主体的自觉与主动。

glossary.explanation: A phrase prominent in recent Party discourse, stressing that Party and people should act consciously and proactively in making history while following objective laws.

t: The new-materialist implications of practice
zh: 实践的新唯物主义意蕴
paras: Ma Junhai returns to Marx's Theses on Feuerbach, which the article calls the manifesto of Marx's new materialism. The question is what new materialism is and how it goes beyond both old materialism and idealism. Ma's answer is that Marx makes practice a way of thinking and a theoretical principle, which at once criticises and creatively synthesises the two earlier positions. The article presents this return to the source as a way of disclosing the 'secret' of Marx's philosophical revolution, not as idle repetition.

The short piece, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2025, has three parts. The first traces how the concept of practice changed from Aristotle through Kant, Fichte and Hegel. The second examines the metaphysical thinking of old materialism, represented by Feuerbach, and of idealism, represented by Hegel. The third sets out how new materialism changes the mode of thinking.

Ma argues that grasping new materialism depends on understanding practice as a mode of thinking. Treating practice vulgarly pulls new materialism back into natural thinking, and treating it as absolute returns it to metaphysics. Marx, on this account, absorbed the purposiveness, freedom, creativity and mediation found in earlier thinkers, but extended practice to economic and all other real activity and made it humanity's originary way of being. Idealism, in Ma's reading, develops the active side abstractly and reaches only a concreteness of thought. Old materialism offers mere static intuition of the sensuous world and lacks the dimensions of history and activity. Both, Ma says, rest on the principle of identity. New materialism restores the primacy of the object while understanding the sensuous world as the product of human negating, creative activity, and so as 'the history of industry'.

Ma concludes that new materialism has a revolutionary character and an orientation towards the future. It goes beyond merely verbal intellectual activity, reshapes people's values and calls them to revolutionary practice. Humanity, Ma holds, can leave consciousness behind through practice and change the world. Read the original if you want a compact, textbook-style account of how Chinese scholars read the Theses on Feuerbach through the idea of practice as a way of thinking.
quoteEn: New materialism holds that through practice humanity can step out of inner consciousness and change the world.
quoteZh: 新唯物主义主张人类经由实践可以走出内在的意识而改变世界。

t: Guiding young people with Marxist scientific theory
zh: 以马克思主义科学理论引领青年
paras: Han Xiping asks how Marxist scientific theory should be used to guide young people as China builds a modernised socialist country. Writing in the Party journal Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, Han argues that such guidance is a distinctive strength of Marxist parties, is required by the task of Chinese modernization, and needs new practical methods.

The commentary has three parts. The first explains why theoretical guidance of youth is an advantage of Marxist parties. The second links it to the current stage of building a modern socialist country. The third sets out practical routes: ideological and political courses, institutional arrangements, and new forms of discourse.

In the first part, Han contrasts Marxist parties with bourgeois parties. In Han's account, bourgeois parties proclaim freedom of thought yet covertly convey bourgeois values, whereas Marxist parties openly arm youth with a scientific worldview and method. Han says this theory gives young people a firm political position, scientific modes of thinking (historical, dialectical, systemic and innovative) and lofty character. In the second part, Han presents young people as the main force in national rejuvenation who face ideological infiltration online from what the article calls hostile forces and from Western capitalist ideology. They therefore need Marxism to tell right from wrong and to reconcile personal aims with the national cause.

Han's practical proposals begin with integrated ideological and political courses from primary school to university. These would use artificial intelligence and big data for feedback, and "walking" courses based on fieldwork and volunteering. Han also calls for Party committees, schools, Party schools, the Communist Youth League and social organisations to share responsibility under Party leadership. Finally, Han proposes a new-media matrix on platforms such as Douyin, Xiaohongshu, Bilibili and Zhihu, regulation of traffic-driven algorithms to counter "information cocoons", and participatory formats such as Party-history "murder mystery" role-play games. Han concludes that the Party must keep arming youth with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want to see how a university Party official sets out the ideological, institutional and media methods of youth work in the Chinese modernization era.
quoteEn: The process by which young people study and master Marxist scientific theory is the process of cultivating their own historical, dialectical, systemic and innovative thinking, and so of mastering a scientific way of thinking.
quoteZh: 青年人学习掌握马克思主义科学理论的过程，就是培育自身历史思维、辩证思维、系统思维、创新思维，进而掌握科学思维方式的过程。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's path of national development, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernisation.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and official values. They are treated as central to the task of fostering virtue and cultivating people.
The Party's mass organisation for young people, which works under Party leadership to mobilise and educate youth.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, with a target date of mid-century.

t: Promoting the innovative development of contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy
zh: 推动当代中国马克思主义政治经济学创新发展
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (13 May 2025), Li Zheng takes Volume I of Selected Economic Writings of Xi Jinping as the occasion for asking how contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy is being advanced. Li argues that Xi Jinping's economic thought turns practical experience into a systematic economic doctrine. The article presents it as both the latest result of the Party's innovative theory and a Chinese contribution to Marxist political economy.

The commentary is organised under four headings. It covers adherence to Marxism's guiding role, the Two Integrations, guidance for building an autonomous Chinese knowledge system, and the guidance this thought offers for economic practice at home and in other developing countries.

Li first claims that Xi's thought keeps Marxism's basic stance and method: a people-centred position, dialectical and historical materialism, and the basic principles of political economy. Examples include the dominant place of public ownership alongside the Two Unwaverings, and the idea of data as a factor of production that earns income. Li then argues that the thought combines Marxism with China's realities and with traditional culture. Innovation as the first driving force and new quality productive forces draw on Marx's productivity theory. The notion of "harmony between humanity and nature" and the vision of a community with a shared future for mankind draw on traditional ideas. Li adds that concepts such as high-quality development, the new development philosophy and Chinese modernization, together with the "six musts" and "five balances", form the core of an autonomous Chinese economics.

Li concludes that the thought is a fundamental guide for Chinese modernization, including high-quality development, the market's decisive role alongside a better-performing government, and resilient industrial and supply chains. Li also contends it offers lessons to the Global South on people-centred development, high-quality growth and balancing development with security. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese economists frame Xi Jinping's economic thought as Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping's economic thought is a result and exemplar of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture.
quoteZh: 习近平经济思想是把马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际相结合、同中华优秀传统文化相结合的成果和典范。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating the public sector and unwaveringly supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A concept promoted since 2023 to describe innovation-driven, technology-intensive productive forces seen as the basis of high-quality development.
The official goal of shifting China's economy from rapid growth towards quality, efficiency and innovation.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of international cooperation and shared development.
A term for developing countries, which Chinese official discourse uses to describe China's partners.

t: Accelerating the construction of an independent knowledge system for the discipline of Marxist theory
zh: 加快构建马克思主义理论学科自主知识体系
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao, 2025, no. 8) in the 20th anniversary year of the first-level discipline of Marxist theory, Liu Jianjun asks what it means to build an "independent knowledge system" (zizhu zhishi tixi) for that discipline. Taking up the goal set by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Liu argues that the task must be understood carefully and carried out through the discipline's six second-level sub-fields.

Liu first defines the terms. "Independent" means rooted in China rather than copied from the West; "knowledge system" means turning practical experience into general knowledge that is logically systematic rather than scattered. The article then sets out the discipline's origin in 2005 and its scope, and goes through the six sub-fields in turn: basic principles of Marxism, history of Marxism's development, the adaptation of Marxism to China, foreign Marxism, ideological and political education, and basic problems in modern Chinese history.

The central distinction in Liu's argument is between Marxism as guiding ideology and Marxism as an academic discipline. Liu holds that the two operate at different levels and should not be conflated, and that Marx and Engels hold the "intellectual property" of Marxism itself, so one cannot call Marxism as such a Chinese independent knowledge system. What China can build independently is the discipline's knowledge system. For basic principles, Liu stresses upholding the principles ("keeping to the right path") over innovation. Liu distinguishes the principles from their textbook systematisation, a task Liu assigns to Chinese Party members and scholars, who must move beyond the system originally imported from the Soviet Union. For foreign Marxism, Liu proposes absorbing its critiques of capitalism while criticising its "misreadings and reconstructions" of Marxism from a Marxist standpoint.

Liu concludes that each sub-field needs its own knowledge system. Liu calls for a narrative of Marxism's development in China and for work on classic texts and editions. Liu also proposes more study of the theoretical results of adapting Marxism to China, and turning Party experience in ideological education into systematic knowledge. Liu further wants a scientific answer to why history and the people chose Marxism, the Communist Party and socialism. Read the original if you want to see how a Renmin University professor defines the scope of the Marxist theory discipline and its six sub-fields in official terms.
quoteEn: Guiding ideology and a disciplinary system are not matters at the same level; if they are conflated, the status of Marxism as the guiding ideology may be lowered.
quoteZh: 指导思想与学科体系不是一个层次的事情，如果混为一谈就可能降低马克思主义指导思想的身份。

glossary.explanation: A goal set by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) of building Chinese philosophy and social science on China's own practice rather than on Western models.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论一级学科
glossary.explanation: A discipline category established in China in 2005 under the law major group, with six second-level sub-fields. It underpins research and the teaching of ideological and political courses in schools.
The Party-state's system of education in political ideology and values, taught in schools, the army, workplaces and communities. It is also an academic sub-field.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Pushing Marxist political economy to a new stage
zh: 将马克思主义政治经济学推向新境界
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary on the first volume of Selected Economic Works of Xi Jinping (published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today, May 2025), Li Qiankun presents the volume as the authoritative text of Xi Jinping's economic thought. Li argues that this thought inherits the philosophical methodology and basic standpoint of Marxist political economy and, from the standpoint of a new historical era, carries that discipline to a new stage.

The piece is organised in three steps. It first traces the origins of Marxist political economy, from classical political economy to Marx and Engels's critique. It then sets out what Xi's economic thought preserves (the article's "upholding the fundamentals"). Finally it lists the innovations Li credits to it.

In Li's account, Marx and Engels's critique of classical political economy helped produce historical materialism, which in turn allowed them to treat economic categories as expressions of social relations rather than relations among things. Li holds that Xi's thought keeps four inheritances: the people-centred standpoint, the historical-materialist method, centralised and unified Party leadership over economic work, and a global outlook. Li then names the innovations: judgments that the world is undergoing great changes unseen in a century and that China has moved to high-quality development; the new development philosophy and the new development pattern; the upholding and improvement of the basic socialist economic system, including the Two Unwaverings; and a deeper understanding of capital's characteristics and laws, especially finance.

Li concludes that these elements make Xi's economic thought both continuous with Marx and Engels and a response to present conditions. Li notes that Engels described a broad political economy as still "to be created", and presents Xi's thought as the latest theoretical answer to that task in socialist construction. Li claims that the institutional measures offer a Chinese approach to economic-system innovation for the world. Read the original if you want a short, official-line overview of how Chinese scholars link Xi Jinping's economic thought to the Marxist political-economic tradition.
quoteEn: Development is for the people; this is the fundamental standpoint of Marxist political economy.
quoteZh: 发展为了人民，这是马克思主义政治经济学的根本立场。

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping and promoted by the Party as the guide for economic work since the 2010s. It covers development philosophy, the economic system, and Party leadership of the economy.
A framework announced in 2015 that calls for innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development. It is the Party's guiding principle for economic policy.
An official goal that shifts emphasis from rapid growth to quality, efficiency and people's sense of gain.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
An economic strategy announced in 2020 that makes the domestic cycle the mainstay while domestic and international cycles reinforce each other.

t: Opening up a new realm for Marxist political economy
zh: 开拓马克思主义政治经济学新境界
paras: This short commentary in China Social Sciences Today (7 May 2025) reads the first volume of Selected Economic Writings of Xi Jinping as a new body of theory for political economy with Chinese characteristics. The volume collects Xi's main writings on economic construction from November 2012 to December 2024. Ding Renzhong argues that it reflects the Party Central Committee's reflection on, and theoretical summary of, economic practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012). In Ding's view it shows the core content and distinctive qualities of Xi Jinping's economic thought.

The article is organised around four qualities: Party spirit (dangxing), people-centredness, epoch-making relevance (shidaixing) and innovation. Each section pairs statements by Xi with Ding's own reasoning. The last section places the volume in a lineage from Mao Zedong's economic ideas, through the post-1978 reform period, to the present.

On Party spirit, Ding argues that strengthening Party leadership of economic work expresses three advantages: the political system, the economic management system and the continuity of policy. On people-centredness, Ding says it follows from the Party's purpose, from historical materialism and from the nature of socialism, and links it to common prosperity. On the epoch-making quality, Ding names three tasks: deepening reform, expanding opening up and advancing scientific and technological innovation. Ding cites the 22 pilot free trade zones and the Hainan free trade port, membership of regional trade agreements, the Belt and Road Initiative, and the innovation-driven development strategy.

On innovation, Ding lists theoretical results of contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy. They include the theory of the essence of socialism, the basic economic system of the primary stage of socialism, the new development philosophy, the socialist market economy, the economic "new normal" and the three rights in rural land contracting. Ding endorses Xi's statement that these were not addressed by the Marxist classics and open up a new realm for Marxist political economy. Ding expects further theoretical results under Xi Jinping's economic thought, and a contribution to an autonomous Chinese system of economic knowledge. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned overview of how Chinese economists frame Xi's economic writings and their place in Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: Strengthening the Party's leadership over economic work is an expression of the advantages of China's political system.
quoteZh: 加强党对经济工作的领导，是我国政治制度优势的体现。

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping and presented in official discourse as part of Xi Jinping Thought and as guidance for economic work since 2012.
A goal of shared affluence for all, presented officially as an essential requirement of socialism and given new emphasis under Xi Jinping.
The official framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, set out in 2015.
An official thesis that China is at an early, long-lasting stage of socialism, which is used to justify its basic economic system and policies.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
An official term for China's shift from high-speed to medium-high-speed growth and structural upgrading, in use since about 2014.

keywords: Selected Economic Writings of Xi Jinping

t: The political and revolutionary character of Marx and Engels's thought and its contemporary relevance
st: An interview with Professor Terrell Carver of the University of Bristol
zh: 马克思恩格斯思想的政治性、革命性及其当代启示
zhSub: 访英国布里斯托大学特里尔卡弗教授
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2025 no. 4
paras: This is an interview, conducted by Liu Zixu of the Institute of Marxism, CASS, with Terrell Carver, a Marx and Engels scholar at the University of Bristol. It asks how the intellectual relationship between Marx and Engels should be understood and what their work offers today. Carver's main answer is that both men saw themselves as political activists from youth, and that later readers have anachronistically recast their subversive journalism and pamphlets as philosophy or economics.

The conversation moves through four areas: the Marx–Engels partnership, including the 'young' and 'later' Engels; the question 'which Marx?'; Marx's contributions on profit, historical materialism and the base and superstructure; and Marx in historical context, covering colonialism, national liberation, Eurocentrism, gender and the prospects for human emancipation. It closes with Carver's view of what Marx, Engels and Marxism research should do next.

Carver rejects the binaries commentators impose, such as young/mature Marx, break/continuity, and philosophy/economics, as projections that make biographical drama. In his reading, Marx's writing from the outset responded to changing political circumstances, readerships and censorship rather than reflecting a closed theoretical journey. He adds that Engels presented 'a Marx' for political purposes after 1883, and he describes his own approach as post-structuralist: meaning is constructed by readers, so there are 'many Marxes'. On economics, he reads Marx as locating profit in production, in the special surplus-producing property of human labour, and the opening theoretical chapters of Capital as a prelude to a political critique. He therefore regards claims that capital is neutral and creates value as vulgar economics that blunts class struggle.

Carver judges that Marx remains the most comprehensive analyst and critic of capitalism and that Marxism has been a progressive force for emancipation. He calls 'Eurocentrism' a poorly framed charge, and he sees the present as a bind in which identity-based and national struggles are weakly linked to anti-capitalism. He urges researchers to drop worn-out framing concepts and to give less priority to theory over practice, to canonical books over journalism and letters, and to MEGA's separation of 'economic' works. Read the original if you want a Western specialist's anti-anachronistic account of Marx and Engels as political actors, as presented to a Chinese Marxist readership.
quoteEn: My most important generalisation is that, from their youth, both saw themselves as political activists in some sense.
quoteZh: 我最重要的概括是，从年轻时起，他们都将自己视为某种意义上的政治活动家。

glossary.explanation: Marx's term for economic thought that describes surface appearances and justifies capitalism instead of analysing its inner relations. Carver applies it to claims that capital is neutral and creates value.

Marx's metaphor relating the economic structure of society to its legal, political and ideological forms. Carver notes it appears in full only once in Marx's writings and was later over-read as determinism.
The theory that material production and its social relations shape history, law, politics and ideas. Carver notes that Marx never used the term, which Engels and later Marxists popularised.

t: Key issues in a century of philological study of The German Ideology
zh: 《德意志意识形态》百年文献学焦点问题探析
source: China Social Sciences Net / Chinese Social Sciences Today, 23 April 2025
paras: The German Ideology, written by Marx and Engels in 1845–47 and never published in their lifetime, is widely regarded as the work marking the birth of the materialist conception of history. Zhao Yulan reviews a century of philological work on the manuscript, which has produced more than ten editions, and identifies three questions that have dominated scholarly attention: how the text should be presented, what form of writing it represents, and which chapter is its core. In each case Zhao defends the established view against the position taken in the latest historical-critical edition.

The short article first traces the editions: Riazanov's 1924 and 1926 publications of the "Feuerbach" chapter, the complete MEGA1 text of 1932, the new Feuerbach editions after Barna's 1962 discovery in Amsterdam, and the MEGA2 pre-edition (2004) and full volume (2017). It also notes a 2018 chronological edition by Hubmann and Pagel and a 2019 online Feuerbach edition produced by Chinese and Japanese scholars. It then takes the three disputed questions in turn.

On presentation, Zhao sets out the shift from logical ordering (Riazanov, MEGA1, the 1960s editions) to Taubert's chronological ordering in 2004, and then the MEGA2 editors' rejection of it in 2017, which Zhao calls a "negation of the negation". On form, Zhao argues that the MEGA2 "quarterly journal" thesis, first proposed by Galina Golovina in 1980, explains only the project's origin. After the break with the Westphalian backers in 1846, Zhao says, Marx and Engels withdrew other contributors' texts, and Marx's 1860 letter refers to "a work" in two volumes, so the text remains a work. On the core chapter, Zhao rejects the MEGA2 editors' preference for the "Saint Max" chapter, because its bulk comes largely from line-by-line quotation of Stirner. Pages 1–29 of the Feuerbach manuscript, Zhao adds, were written first and do not derive from it.

Zhao concludes that the "Feuerbach" chapter keeps its unique status, and that the choice of ordering depends on whether the manuscripts are treated as unfinished texts or as parts of a work. The article closes by saying that thorough philological study can deepen understanding of the text and support independent Chinese research on Marxist texts, contributing to an autonomous system of knowledge in Chinese philosophy and social sciences. Read the original if you want a compact overview of the editorial history of The German Ideology and a Chinese scholar's response to the MEGA2 editors' positions.
quoteEn: In the final analysis, The German Ideology is a work by Marx and Engels.
quoteZh: 《德意志意识形态》归根结底是马克思恩格斯的一部著作。

glossary.explanation: A slogan of recent Chinese policy on philosophy and social sciences, calling for scholarship built on China's own concepts and research traditions rather than on Western frameworks. The article links it to independent Chinese study of Marxist texts.
Marx and Engels's theory that material production and social relations shape history. Chinese scholarship treats The German Ideology as the work where it was first systematically set out.

t: Accurately understanding the basic tenets of Marxism in the "Two Integrations"
zh: 准确理解“两个结合”中的马克思主义基本原理
paras: Tao Wenzhao takes up a term that, in his view, is neglected in current discussion of the Two Integrations: "the basic tenets of Marxism" (Marxist basic principles), which holds the leading position in the formula. The Two Integrations join Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. Tao argues that grasping the formula correctly first requires grasping this term correctly. This short commentary appeared in Beijing Daily in April 2025.

The article has four parts. It traces how the wording has changed in Party usage; it distinguishes broad and narrow senses of "Marxism"; it explains why "basic tenets" replaced "universal truth"; and it indicates what the basic tenets contain. Tao draws on the Selected Works of Mao Zedong, later volumes of Mao's writings, and statements by Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

On wording, Tao reports that before 1949 the Party spoke almost entirely of "universal truth", and that "basic tenets" became the prevailing usage only after reform and opening up. Tao treats the older and current phrasings as substantively identical, but sees the current one as more precise. On scope, Tao reasons that because the other terms in the formula already carry "China", Marxism there must mean classical Marxism from outside China. Yet Tao adds that later "integrations" should reasonably take in the existing results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, Mao Zedong Thought above all. The phrase "basic tenets" also screens out scattered individual judgements, dogmatic readings and tacked-on erroneous views, which Tao says helps prevent copying texts mechanically.

Tao says the tenets consist first of a worldview and methodology, namely the stance, viewpoint and method that Xi Jinping calls the living soul of Marxism, including seeking truth from facts. Tao also lists major propositions from philosophy (the material world; productive forces and relations of production; base and superstructure), political economy (labour as the source of value; surplus value) and scientific socialism (the historical tendency towards socialism and the free and all-round development of each person). The author stresses that no such list is exhaustive or fixed, and that the tenets should be viewed developmentally. Read the original if you want a compact account of how Party terminology around the Two Integrations has evolved and how a Chinese Marxist scholar defines the term "basic tenets".
quoteEn: If Marxism already included the "Chinese" element, it would make no sense to integrate it once more with China's realities.
quoteZh: 如果包括了“中国”的马克思主义，却再去同“中国”的实际结合就显得不通了。

glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in official discourse in 2021–2023.
The standard Party term for the core, lasting propositions of Marxism, distinguished from particular judgements made by the classics in specific circumstances.
The Party's official designation for Mao Zedong's theories, regarded as the first major result of adapting Marxism to China.
A principle associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, held in official discourse to be the essence of the Marxist stance and method.

t: Re-examining Marx's materialist conception of history: an investigation based on The German Ideology
zh: 重审马克思的唯物史观：基于《德意志意识形态》的考察
source: Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2025 no. 2
paras: Is the materialist conception of history that Marx and Engels developed in The German Ideology a genuine historical science, or does it fall back into an ideology of productivism? Ma Canlin takes up this question, prompted by critics such as Jean Baudrillard, who argued that Marx's analytical tools were themselves a sophisticated ideological illusion of capital. Writing from the standpoint of the history of ideas, including Marx's own development, Ma argues that the text founds a real science of history and that its difference from productivism can be shown.

The article has three main parts plus a conclusion. The first part treats the materialist conception of history as a practical materialism and distinguishes Marx from Feuerbach. The second part addresses the charge of productivism, drawing on Baudrillard, Hannah Arendt, Max Weber, Antonio Negri and Herbert Marcuse. The third part asks what the object of historical materialism is. Ma draws on Marx's Capital, the 1857–58 manuscripts, Engels's late letters and the readings of Lukács and Althusser.

Ma makes three moves. First, the "inversion" of thought and being does not separate Marx from Feuerbach. For Marx, matter is the product of human sensuous activity (praxis), and nature is historicised nature. Ma warns, however, against reading this as a subjectivist philosophy of practice, because practice always unfolds under inherited conditions, so the text holds subject and object together dialectically. Second, answering the critics, Ma says Marx distinguishes three senses of freedom: non-interference, non-domination, and the realm of freedom beyond necessary labour. Marx also holds that this last realm can flourish only on the basis of the realm of necessity, so material production is not the opposite of freedom. Third, the object of historical materialism is not the economy but a social whole of economic, political and ideological elements. Ma calls this whole structured and uneven rather than Hegelian and expressive, and says political economy is a branch of the science that studies the economy as part of that whole.

Ma concludes that The German Ideology rebuilt the meaning of matter on the basis of practice and sketched the structure of the social whole, even though it first gave an impression of economic determinism. That challenged the legitimacy of the philosophy of history and announced a genuine positive science of history. The theoretical revolution was neither instant nor smooth, Ma says, and it involved a long process of reversals and struggle. Read the original if you work on Marx's early texts, the debates over productivism and economic determinism, or how Western critics of Marx are answered from within the Chinese Marxist tradition.
quoteEn: The true object of the materialist conception of history is in fact not the economy but the social whole; yet this is not a homogeneous whole but an uneven one with a complex structure.
quoteZh: 唯物史观的真正对象事实上并非经济，而是社会整体，但是这并不是一个同质性的整体，而是一个有着复杂结构的不平衡的整体。

glossary.explanation: The standard Chinese term for Marx and Engels's theory of history, also called historical materialism. Chinese scholarship often treats The German Ideology as its birthplace.
A reading of Marx's "new materialism" that stresses practice (praxis) and human subjectivity, in contrast to Feuerbach's contemplative "old" materialism.

t: The historical-materialist content of innovation phenomena, innovation practice and innovative thinking
zh: 创新现象、创新实践和创新思维的历史唯物主义内涵
paras: Bao Dawei asks what innovation means when it is understood through historical materialism, covering both material production and social institutions. The article argues that human civilization is driven forward by innovation practice, marked off in stages by innovation phenomena, and guided by effective innovative thinking. Bao holds that the concept of innovation must be grasped from a "big history" standpoint and according to the general laws of social development.

The article is organised in three parts. The first treats innovation as a phenomenon and its distinctly human character. It sets out three levels: the development of productive forces, the adjustment of relations of production, and the dynamic between economic base and superstructure. The second analyses the "object-structure" of innovation practice, covering subject, intermediary and object. The third examines innovative thinking as the forerunner of practice. Bao draws on Marx, Engels, Lenin and Xi Jinping, and contrasts historical materialism with rationalism, mechanical materialism and constructivism.

Bao argues that innovation is a human activity that depends on human cognition and carries human intentions. It is nonetheless objective, because motives and conditions are shaped by history and by contradictions between subject and object. Innovation practice has a structure: a self-sublating subject, intermediaries such as labour tools and ideology, and ever-renewed objects. Innovative thinking is described as a "rehearsal" in thought of the negation of the negation, and Bao says it is effective when objective and systematic. Under class society and capitalism, Bao claims, it suffers a double deficiency, because particular interests limit objectivity and the division of labour and the culture industry limit systematic vision.

Bao concludes that the double deficiency can be overcome at two levels. Micro-level ideological critique through Marxism, both dialectical and historical materialism, frees thinking from old concepts. At the macro level, social conditions must no longer be dominated by particular interests. The people, and within them the proletariat led by Marxist parties, are presented as the creators and testers of innovation. Bao points to the institutional strengths of socialism with Chinese characteristics, such as concentrating resources on major undertakings, long-term strategic planning and an innovation-driven ecosystem. Read the original if you want a systematic Marxist-philosophical account of innovation, with extensive use of the classics, as it appears in current Chinese theoretical writing.
quoteEn: The essential content of innovation phenomena is the process of recognising new problems, solving new problems, and discovering new problems again.
quoteZh: 创新现象的本质内涵就是认识新问题、解决新问题、再发现新问题的过程

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's political and economic system since reform and opening up, presented by the Party as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.

t: Extending Marx's theory of world money
st: With a discussion of strategic choices for the current internationalisation of the renminbi
zh: 马克思世界货币理论的再拓展
zhSub: 兼论当前人民币国际化的战略选择
paras: Liu Haoyan starts from the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to advance renminbi internationalisation in an orderly way. The article argues that this task cannot rest on inherited Western theory and needs Marx's theory of world money. Marx mainly analysed metallic money, and later Marxists did not build a full doctrine for the age of sovereign credit money. Liu proposes to extend Marx's insights on money, credit, social power and international relations into such a doctrine, and to use it to guide China's currency strategy.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Marx's scattered remarks on world money (its origin, form, functions and contradictions) and reviews later left-wing scholars such as Lapavitsas, de Brunhoff, Duncan Foley, Samir Amin, David Harvey and Michael Hudson. The second sets out how world money is generated under sovereign credit money, and what it does to issuing and using countries. The third assesses the renminbi's position, its obstacles and recommended policies.

Liu's central claim is that a 'dual power structure' of economic and political power determines which currency becomes world money. The economic factors are trade scale, financial markets, transaction costs, monetary credit and the power to settle scarce commodities. The political ones are political stability, international institutions, strategic alliances and military strength. World money works in two directions: issuers gain policy independence, seigniorage and financial leverage over others, but also face a stronger currency, industrial hollowing-out, the Triffin dilemma and financial risk. Liu cites the pound and Germany and Japan after 1945 to show why users may hesitate to challenge the incumbent currency.

On this basis Liu identifies obstacles for the renminbi: the quality of trade, immature financial markets, late cross-border infrastructure, the exchange-rate dilemma, geopolitical pressure, imbalance in international financial bodies and security risks. Liu calls for a steady, gradual approach with four elements: high-quality development and technological upgrading, a bond-market-centred financial system, digital legal tender and fintech, and tools to defend monetary sovereignty alongside reform of international monetary institutions. Liu warns against internationalisation for its own sake. Read the original if you want a Marxist political-economy framework for currency competition and renminbi strategy, with detailed data and policy proposals.
quoteEn: One must not form the notion of pursuing internationalisation for the sake of internationalisation.
quoteZh: 不能形成为了国际化而国际化的观念。

glossary.explanation: The policy of increasing the use of China's currency in cross-border trade, finance and reserves. It began in 2009 and was restated at the 20th Party Congress as something to be advanced in an orderly way.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, that shifts emphasis from growth speed to quality, innovation and efficiency.
The author's own analytical term for the combination of economic and political power that decides which sovereign currency becomes world money.

t: The essence–appearance method of penetrating insight: the fundamental method of Marx's critique of political economy
zh: 本质－现象透视法：马克思政治经济学批判的根本方法
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2025 no. 3
paras: Which method is basic to Marx's critique of political economy? Liu Zhihong argues that it is neither the ascent from the abstract to the concrete nor any other familiar procedure, but what Liu calls the essence–appearance method of penetrating insight (本质－现象透视法). Liu holds that this method has been widely known but never adequately recognised or developed, and that recent scholarship has treated the ascent from the abstract to the concrete as the main method of Capital without discussing it. The article was published in Studies on Marxism, 2025, no. 3.

The article has three parts. The first re-reads the ascent from the abstract to the concrete, using the 1857 Introduction, as a movement from essence to appearance. The second sets out the content and logic of the essence–appearance method in five steps: the distinction between essence and appearance, essence producing illusory appearances, appearances posing as essence, penetrating appearances to grasp essence, and criticising appearances on the basis of essence. The third shows the method at work in Capital and its manuscripts, including the analysis of interest-bearing capital and the theories of surplus value, and explains why it is fundamental.

Liu's central claim is that the 'abstract' at the starting point is the decisive essence, above all value, and that the ascent to the concrete is the dialectical concretisation of that essence into ever more complex appearances. In Liu's account, Marx stresses that capitalism necessarily generates a system of inverted appearances, whose core is the illusion that capitalism is rational and eternal. Only by seeing through these appearances, and then criticising them from the standpoint of essence, can the historical and transitory character of capitalism be shown. Liu argues that this method governs the use of the ascent from the abstract to the concrete and also of typical analysis and scientific abstraction. It is fundamental because it serves Marx's overall aim of criticising and surpassing capitalism, his overall problem of why capitalism must give way to communism, and the critical and revolutionary substance of materialist dialectics. Without it, Liu contends, the ascent could slide into vulgar economics.

Liu concludes that Hegel's dialectic is concretised directly as the ascent from the abstract to the concrete, whereas Marx's dialectic is concretised first as the essence–appearance method and only then as the ascent. Liu adds that criticism of illusions must move from ideas to practice, because only changing the capitalist mode of production removes their basis. Liu uses the image of a tree: the ascent is a 'branch', and the essence–appearance method is the 'root'. Read the original if you work on Marx's methodology, the philosophy of Capital, or current Chinese debates on the dialectical structure of the critique of political economy.
quoteEn: The essence–appearance method of penetrating insight is the fundamental method of Marx's critique of political economy.
quoteZh: 本质－现象透视法是马克思政治经济学批判的根本方法。

glossary.explanation: The author's own term for a method of seeing through appearances, especially illusory ones, to grasp essence, and then criticising appearances on that basis. The author presents it as the root method of Capital.

glossary.pinyin: cóng chōuxiàng shàngshēng dào jùtǐ fǎ
glossary.en: ascent from the abstract to the concrete
glossary.explanation: The method Marx describes in the 1857 Introduction to the Grundrisse, in which thought starts from simple, abstract determinations and reconstructs the concrete as a rich totality. It is often treated as the main method of Capital.
The dialectical method of Marxism, which the author treats as Marx's overall method, whose substance is critique and revolution.
Marx's project of criticising both capitalist society and the economic theory that reflects it. It is the subtitle of Capital and the title of his 1859 work.

t: Marx's historical consciousness and class consciousness in examining the transformation of money into capital
zh: 马克思考察货币转化为资本的历史意识与阶级意识
source: Studies on the Theoretical Discipline of Marxism (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2025 no. 3
paras: Liu Jingdong asks how Marx's account of the transformation of money into capital, and of labour-power becoming a commodity, supports a reading of the birth of capital and the world history of capital. The article argues that Marx's analysis rests on an organic unity of historical consciousness and class consciousness, which together let him do two things: criticise capital and criticise bourgeois political economy.

The article draws mainly on Volume I of Capital (Part Two, "The Transformation of Money into Capital") and on Volume II's chapter on the circuit of money capital. It also refers to Marx's 1857–58 and 1861–63 manuscripts. It is organised in three parts: money becoming capital as the precondition for the shift from traditional to modern modes of production; the emergence of capital and the free worker as the secret of capital's birth and world history; and the social conditions of the money-capital circuit and the new class relations. A short conclusion follows.

Liu first contrasts simple circulation C–M–C, aimed at use-value and consumption, with the circulation of capital M–C–M′, aimed at self-expanding value. For Liu, this contrast marks two different social-economic epochs, and the capitalist appears as personified capital driven by surplus value. Liu then follows Marx through the contradiction in the general formula of capital. Surplus value cannot arise from circulation, whether exchange is equivalent or not, yet it cannot arise outside it, and Marx resolves this through labour-power as a commodity. Labour-power can be a commodity only once workers are free in the double sense and the separation of producers from the means of production has occurred through primitive accumulation. Liu holds that this condition "contains a whole world history". In Volume II, Liu argues, Marx revisits the point to show that the formula M–C…P…C′–M′ presupposes a wage-labouring class on a social scale, and that the wage form conceals exploitation behind formal equality, which bourgeois economists treat in ahistorical terms.

Liu concludes that Marx's unity of historical and class consciousness exposes the claimed freedom and equality of exchange as a veil. Behind it, in Liu's reading, lie capital's exploitation, domination and enslavement of labour, which is why Marx calls capitalist commodity production an "epoch-making" mode of exploitation. The article also presents the combination of labourers and means of production as Marx's criterion for distinguishing economic epochs. Read the original if you want a close, text-based reading of Capital Volumes I and II on the origin of capital, and an example of how Chinese Marxist scholars frame Marx's historical method and class analysis.
quoteEn: Marx's theory of capital is the backbone of his theory of society and history; without understanding the conscious historical consciousness and critical class consciousness of his critique of capital, one cannot truly grasp the inner secret and basic features of his social-historical theory.
quoteZh: 马克思的资本理论是其社会历史理论的主干部分，不理解马克思资本批判的自觉的历史意识和批判的阶级意识，就不可能真正地把握其社会历史理论的内在秘密和基本特征。

t: Activating China's fine traditional culture with Marxism: objectives, principles and approaches
zh: 马克思主义激活中华优秀传统文化：目标、原则与进路
paras: Yan Lianfu and Yang Jinfu ask how Marxism can "activate" the fine elements of China's traditional culture, and to what end. Taking up Xi Jinping's 2023 and 2024 remarks on the high degree of fit between Marxism and fine traditional culture, they argue that activation should drive the creative transformation and innovative development of that culture. The new culture formed through the Second Integration, they say, would become the cultural form of Chinese modernization and support the building of a strong socialist cultural nation.

After a literature review that finds existing work strong on feasibility, methods and significance but weak on systematic planning and long-term mechanisms, the article is organised in three parts. It sets out four objectives, seven principles and seven concrete approaches. The approaches each pair a traditional idea with a Marxist counterpart, such as "harmony between heaven and humanity" with the Marxist ecological view.

The four objectives rest on a set of pairings. Marxism's advanced character is said to activate the tradition's values and adaptability. Its worldwide character is said to activate the national character and universal value of Chinese culture. Its critical and revolutionary spirit is said to reshape the tradition's harmonious core, which the authors link to the Party's self-reform. Its developmental outlook is said to activate the tradition's capacity for adaptation. The seven principles are named guidance, excavation, endowing with new meaning, infusion, interpenetration, fusion and climbing. The authors present them as a two-way process in which Marxism becomes Chinese and traditional culture becomes modern, with the combination a "chemical reaction" rather than a mere assemblage. The seven approaches link traditional ideas to ecological civilisation, a community with a shared future for mankind, people-centred livelihood policy, moral construction, high-quality development, the unity of knowing and doing, and individual striving.

The authors conclude that the work is a historic mission for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They call for deeper research on the mechanisms of integration and wider application in the economy, politics, society, culture and ecology. They also call for cultural products with Chinese characteristics and for training people versed in both Marxist theory and traditional culture. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Party theorists frame the Second Integration in terms of goals, principles and policy areas.
quoteEn: This integration is not a simple addition, but is rooted in the unity of the two at the level of their spiritual essence.
quoteZh: 这种融入并非简单叠加，而是根源于二者在精神本质层面的统一性

glossary.explanation: The Party's formulation of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023. It is the second part of the Two Integrations, alongside combining Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The official term for the parts of China's inherited culture regarded as worth preserving and developing. It implies selection among traditional elements rather than endorsement of all of them.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化和创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for how traditional culture should be treated: reworked and given new forms and meanings suited to contemporary society.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernisation, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations, stressing common interests and cooperation among states.
The Party's term for its own continuing internal correction and discipline, presented as a way to keep its character as a Marxist party.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The necessity and the ought of green development after escaping the "Malthusian trap"
zh: 超越“马尔萨斯陷阱”之后绿色发展的必然与应然
paras: Lu Feng asks which direction human civilisation should take now that modern development has escaped the "Malthusian trap". The article argues that the "black development" of early modernity, which was built on fossil fuels, pollution and the conquest of nature, was historically necessary but is unsustainable. Lu contends that civilisation must turn to green development, meaning ecological civilisation, if it is to avoid destruction.

The article has three sections. The first reinterprets Deng Xiaoping's dictum "development is the absolute principle" through the economic historians Gregory Clark and Oded Galor, and treats China's reform-era growth as an escape from the trap. The second characterises "black development" and the early modern worldview behind it, then sets out the scientific and philosophical challenges to that worldview. The third describes green development and what it requires of production, distribution, consumption and innovation.

Lu argues that before 1800 the living standards of labouring people were no better than those of other animals, and that rapid innovation in modernization lifted them above that level. The early modern ideology, he says, rested on a physicalist view of nature, a dogmatic rationalism that held nature to be fully knowable and conquerable, and a human-centred value theory. Drawing on Prigogine, cosmology and complexity science, Lu proposes a creative, "vitalist" view of nature and a humble rationalism, and concludes that nature cannot be conquered. He then argues that the economy is a subsystem of the biosphere. On this basis he holds that the "trickle-down" pattern of distribution is not sustainable, because material wealth has ecological limits and rich-led consumerism cannot be generalised. He proposes progressive taxation within democratic and legal frameworks, a circular economy, renewable energy and green consumption, all driven by green innovation in technology, ideas and institutions.

Lu concludes that civilisation can keep developing without limit through innovation, but only if it abandons the conquest of nature. He adds that this conquering drive is tied to war between humans and war against nature. He cites China's "dual carbon" commitments (peak emissions before 2030, carbon neutrality before 2060) and its stress on respecting nature as signs that Chinese civilisation is turning green. Read the original if you want a philosophical argument from a Chinese ecological-civilisation scholar that links economic history, critiques of anthropocentrism and distributional justice to green development.
quoteEn: The fundamental way to ease this tension is the building of an ecological civilisation, that is, the path of green development.
quoteZh: 缓解张力的根本道路就是生态文明建设，即绿色发展之路。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese official concept, promoted since the 2000s and written into Party documents and the Constitution, that treats environmental protection as the basis of a new stage of civilisation.
A line attributed to Deng Xiaoping during the reform era, used to stress that economic growth takes priority in solving China's problems.

t: Marx's critique of Hegel's philosophy of right
zh: 马克思对黑格尔的法哲学批判
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 15 April 2025
paras: Cheng Guangyun asks how Marx's early critique of Hegel's philosophy of right should be understood, and what it settled. The article argues that Marx still worked inside Hegel's speculative philosophy, yet used it to expose a contradiction between Hegel's political doctrine and his own logic. In doing so, Cheng contends, Marx took the decisive step away from Hegel by founding popular sovereignty on the labouring, propertyless estate.

The article is a compact reading of Marx's Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, built around Hegel's three political powers: the monarchy, the executive and the legislature. Cheng first sets out Hegel's method, in which the philosophy of right is the visible front stage and the Logic is the hidden back-stage programme. The text then takes each power in turn, setting Hegel's account against Marx's objections, and closes with the question of who can represent the universal interest of the state.

Cheng's central claim is that Hegel repeatedly breaks his own logic when it conflicts with the Prussian political reality he wants to defend. Examples include making the monarch the subject of the state rather than its predicate, placing the executive between crown and legislature, and reducing the legislature to an advisory body. Cheng reports that Marx reversed Hegel's inversion: the monarch depends on the people, and sovereignty belongs to the people. Marx also called Hegel's bureaucracy 'state formalism' that treats the state as private property, and he rejected the estates as private interests posing as universal ones. Against this, Marx demanded direct democracy, a single chamber and universal, unrestricted elections. Cheng adds that Marx's argument remained entangled in speculative concepts and bore the mark of Feuerbach and the Young Hegelians.

Cheng concludes that Marx and Hegel shared one problem, namely who represents the universal and public interest of the state. Hegel answered with the monarch, bureaucracy and estates.
