In the author's account, they drive innovation, raise efficiency and quality, spread from emerging sectors to traditional ones, and serve digitalisation, high-end upgrading and low-carbon development. They also supply data as a new factor, which the author says supports a unified national market and digital trade. On the problem side, Chen names global economic volatility, technological change, shifting consumer demand and the rise of new business forms. The article also cites insufficient R&D spending, foreign technology blockades and intellectual property barriers, and a gap between universities, research and industry. It notes that traditional industries account for over 80 per cent of manufacturing and face problems of efficiency, quality, pollution and energy use. Chen cites examples such as AI use in coal mining and a building-materials firm said to have raised labour productivity by over 50 per cent.

Chen proposes stronger innovation-driven policy and R&D funding, support for basic research and talent training, and closer cooperation among industry, universities and research institutes. Further proposals are international scientific cooperation, stronger intellectual property protection, and world-class advanced manufacturing clusters. For industry, the author calls for high-end, intelligent and green upgrading, including strict environmental accountability for officials and tax and loan incentives for firms. Read the original if you want an overview of how a Chinese economics article links new quality productive forces to real-economy policy, with its list of problems and proposed measures.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces, as advanced productive forces, have industry as their carrier: through high technology they empower innovative development of the real economy, through high efficiency its development efficiency, and through high quality its development quality, helping the national economy grow steadily.
quoteZh: 新质生产力作为先进生产力，载体是产业，其以高科技赋能实体经济创新发展、以高效能赋能实体经济发展效率、以高质量赋能实体经济发展品质，助力国民经济稳固增长。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and digital and green transformation, rather than by traditional factor inputs.
An official goal since the late 2010s that shifts emphasis from growth speed to quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
The part of the economy that produces goods and services, such as manufacturing, as distinct from finance and speculative activity.

glossary.en: cooperation among industry, universities and research institutes
glossary.explanation: A standard policy phrase for linking firms, universities and research bodies so that research results can be turned into products.

t: Capitalism and the grand narrative of early modern world history
zh: 资本主义与近代早期世界史宏大叙事
paras: Yu Jinyao asks why capitalism, once the organising concept of modern world history, has largely disappeared from accounts of the early modern period. Yu argues that this marginalisation is a mistake. Capitalism, in the article's view, is a basic fact of the past five centuries, and dropping the concept leaves historians without an effective tool for analysis and critique.

The article has four main parts. It first traces the decline of capitalism as a historical category, blaming postmodern attacks on grand narratives and anti-Eurocentric global history. It examines the California School, taking in Gunder Frank, Kenneth Pomeranz, R. Bin Wong and Li Bozhong. It then sets out seven elements of Marx's concept of the capitalist mode of production and discusses capitalism's creative and destructive sides. Finally, it applies these to early modern debates.

Yu reads Marx as defining capitalism by wage labour, commodity production in which labour-power itself is a commodity, ceaseless accumulation, and a world market, with the capitalist era beginning in the sixteenth century. On this basis Yu argues that commercial growth alone does not produce capitalism. Applying "Smithian growth" to Ming–Qing Jiangnan, Yu says, treats a largely domestic commodity economy as equivalent to Europe's world-market-based commercial capitalism, when Jiangnan stayed at the stage of capitalist sprouts. Coal and colonies, the article contends, mattered in Britain only because capitalism had developed there, which is why Spain and Portugal gained less from their empires. Yu adds that "interaction" cannot explain colonial plunder or ecological damage, which the concept of capitalism and Marx's primitive accumulation can.

Yu concludes that any divergence between East and West happened early, when capitalism grew in Europe while elsewhere it remained in sprout form. Yu presents this as a matter of fact, not Eurocentrism, and says that Frank's call to abandon the concept only courts attention. The article proposes capitalism as the framework for a new grand narrative of early modern world history, built on Marx's theory of the capitalist mode of production. Read the original if you want a Marxist historian's critique of the California School and of "Smithian growth" in Chinese debates on Jiangnan and the Great Divergence.
quoteEn: Historical research needs the concept of capitalism; it is our analytical and critical tool for studying history.
quoteZh: 历史研究需要资本主义概念，这是我们进行历史研究的分析和批判工具。

glossary.explanation: A group of mainly US-based historians, including Pomeranz, Wong and Frank, who challenge Eurocentric accounts by stressing the similarities between early modern Europe and Asia.
The debate over why Europe, and especially Britain, industrialised and pulled ahead of China and other regions. The term comes from Pomeranz's 2000 book.
Economic growth driven by the division of labour, trade and market expansion, without major technological change. Some historians use it for both early modern Europe and Jiangnan.
Marx's term for the violent separation of producers from the means of production, through enclosures, colonial plunder and similar processes. It created the preconditions for capitalist production.
An overarching account that gives a society's or the world's history a single framework. Postmodern thought has criticised such accounts.

t: Engels's influence on Marx's turn to political economy: a textual study based on Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy
zh: 恩格斯对马克思转向政治经济学研究的影响——基于《国民经济学批判大纲》的文本考察
source: Journal of Anyang Institute of Technology, 2025 no. 1
paras: How far did Engels's early essay, Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy (1843–44), shape Marx's move into political economy? Guo Jinlong argues that the essay was the first work of Engels's economic studies and an opening piece of Marxist critique of political economy, and that Engels was both a forerunner and a guide for Marx. The article nonetheless concludes that the influence was real but external: it was not the internal, decisive factor in Marx's turn.

The article examines the Outlines against Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, which acknowledged the essay as an original and rich work. It is organised under four kinds of influence: orientation (the path of analysing real social problems economically), method, specific theses, and the communist goal. Guo draws on Engels's biography from Bremen through Berlin to Manchester, on Marx's Rheinische Zeitung and Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher years, and on commentators such as Terrell Carver, David McLellan, Cornu and Ilyichev.

Guo's central claims are as follows. On orientation, Engels had reached the economic critique of society before Marx, but Marx was already pushed towards it by his Rheinische Zeitung encounters with material interests and by his critique of Hegel's philosophy of right, which located the anatomy of civil society in political economy. Guo therefore rejects McLellan's view that Engels redirected Marx's attention. On method, Engels's historical, materialist and dialectical analysis of the basic categories of political economy, ending in the abolition of private property, surpassed Proudhon, Hess and the economists. Marx's Manuscripts, still governed by a humanist logic of alienation, took over Engels's starting point in private property and his category-based analysis of wages, profit and rent. Guo lists six shared theses, including the premise of private property, labour as free activity, wages at subsistence level, concentration of capital, and communism as reconciliation.

On the communist goal, Guo holds that what drew Marx to the Outlines was its economic argument for communism, which matched his own aim of human emancipation. Guo concludes that grasping the Outlines' influence in this limited and balanced way is key to understanding the link between Marx's and Engels's early economic thought. Read the original if you study the formation of Marx's political economy, the Marx–Engels intellectual relationship, or the 1844 Manuscripts, and want a close textual comparison that disputes the idea of Engels as the decisive influence.
quoteEn: For Marx's turn to political economy, the Outlines exerted only a certain external influence; it was not an internal, decisive factor.
quoteZh: 《大纲》对马克思转向政治经济学研究而言，只是一定的外在的影响，并不是内在的决定性的因素。
keywords: Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy

t: Three dimensions of upholding harmony between humanity and nature
zh: 坚持人与自然和谐共生的三重维度
paras: Huan Qingzhi examines "upholding harmony between humanity and nature", which the article calls the theoretical cornerstone of Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilization. The author argues that it answers, at the level of Marxist ecological philosophy, why China builds an ecological civilization, what kind it builds, and how. The thesis is that the principle has three connected dimensions: a material-ontological premise, a philosophical-ethical outlook, and a national development strategy.

The article follows these dimensions in turn. The first is the premise that "humanity and nature are a community of life". The second is the ethic of respecting, adapting to and protecting nature. The third is the strategic choice to build a Chinese modernization in which humanity and nature live in harmony. Huan draws on Engels's Dialectics of Nature, Marx's account of labour as metabolism with nature, Xi Jinping's speeches, and Party congress documents. Examples include the Saihanba forest farm, the national parks system, functional zoning and Yellow River policy.

In the first part, Huan holds that nature is the material origin of human life. Even digital labour depends on natural inputs, and the relation between humanity and nature is the most basic social relation, interacting with relations between people. The author contrasts capitalist and socialist institutional frameworks as giving modernization different ecological outcomes. In the second part, "respecting" nature means obeying ecological laws, "adapting" means adjusting to nature's rhythms (for example through land-use zoning, ecological red lines and climate adaptation), and "protecting" nature means integrated care of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts.

In the third part, Huan treats harmony with nature as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization. The author says it responds to the people's demand for a better life, offers an alternative to the Western model, and suits a large developing country that cannot copy Western consumption patterns. Material and ecological civilization must advance together, since neither can exist without the other. Huan notes that the foundations of improvement remain fragile and endorses the "five major relationships" Xi set out at the 2023 national ecological conference. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars derive the ecological civilization doctrine from Marxist texts and policy practice.
quoteEn: It must always be clear that, in contemporary society, there can be no ecological civilization detached from the economic base that material civilization provides, and likewise no healthy and sustainable material civilization that defies the principles of ecological civilization.
quoteZh: 必须始终明确，当代社会中不可能存在脱离物质文明所提供的经济基础的生态文明，同样也不会有悖逆生态文明准则的健康持续的物质文明。

glossary.explanation: Ecological civilization (shēngtài wénmíng) is a Chinese policy concept that places environmental protection alongside economic, political, cultural and social development. It became part of the Party's overall plan at the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The official name for the Party's model of development, stressing features such as a huge population, common prosperity, and harmony between humanity and nature. It was formally elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 人与自然是生命共同体
glossary.pinyin: rén yǔ zìrán shì shēngmìng gòngtóngtǐ
glossary.literal: humanity and nature are a life community
glossary.explanation: A formulation in Xi Jinping's ecological thought holding that humans and nature form an interdependent whole, so harming nature ultimately harms people.
Boundaries drawn around ecologically important or fragile areas within which development is restricted or prohibited. They form part of China's land-space planning.
A national land-use strategy that divides territory into optimized, prioritized, restricted and prohibited development zones according to ecological and economic function.

t: On the new quality mode of production
zh: 论新质生产方式
source: Contemporary Economic Research (当代经济研究), 2025 no. 1
paras: Lu Baolin and Xie Hui take up a gap in the literature on new quality productive forces. In their view, existing studies tend either to reduce the concept to technological progress or to treat it in isolation as a matter of changing production relations. The authors argue that, in Marxist political economy, the mode of production is the missing link between productive forces and relations of production. Whether productive forces have undergone a qualitative change, they contend, depends on whether the associated mode of production has changed fundamentally, so cultivating new quality productive forces requires remaking the basic form of the mode of production.

The article has four parts. It first clarifies, from Marx's texts, what the mode of production means and how it relates to productive forces and relations of production. It then traces the capitalist mode of production from simple cooperation through manufacture to large-scale machine industry. Next it analyses how breakthrough changes in the mode of production come about under capitalism. Finally it discusses how China, in the new stage of development, can move from a traditional mode of production to a new quality one.

Lu and Xie define the mode of production as a unity of a material substance (how labourers and means of labour combine) and a social form that carries the relations of production. They read Marx's account of machine industry as showing mutual shaping: capital relations drive the mode of production, which in turn produces a leap in productive forces. They draw five mechanisms from Capital: changes in the means of labour as the foundation; the chase for extra surplus value as the driving force; competition as the means of diffusion; state intervention, such as factory legislation, as a catalyst; and deepening specialisation spreading the new mode across the whole system. They apply this to China's large-scale, standardised, export-oriented mode, which they say rested on cheap factors, open supply chains and rising overseas demand, supports that have weakened since 2008.

For the transition, the authors propose five measures: iterating and upgrading the means of labour through a new system for mobilising national resources; embedding Party leadership in corporate governance; being guided by the new development philosophy; developing mixed-ownership economy; and building a high-standard socialist market economy. In a closing note they describe great-power competition as at bottom a competition between modes of production. They argue that only an original, high-quality material mode of production, under the basic socialist economic system, can let China catch up with developed countries. Read the original if you want a Marxist, production-mode reading of new quality productive forces that stays close to Capital and ends in concrete policy proposals.
quoteEn: Whether productive forces have undergone a qualitative change is judged by whether the mode of production associated with them has undergone a fundamental transformation.
quoteZh: 判定生产力是否发生质变就看与其相联系的生产方式是否发生了根本性变革。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation. It has since become a prominent theme in Chinese economic policy and scholarship.
The official guiding framework for development announced in 2015, centred on innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.

An economic arrangement in which state, collective and private capital hold cross-shares in the same enterprises. The Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) described it as an important way of realising the basic economic system.

glossary.en: a new system for mobilising national resources
glossary.explanation: An official formula for concentrating state, market and social resources on major science and technology goals, building on the earlier 'whole-nation system'.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The official term for China's system of public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse forms of ownership, distribution according to work as the mainstay alongside other methods, and the socialist market economy.

t: The philosophical foundations of the theory of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化理论的哲学根基
paras: Feng Yanli asks what lies beneath the theory of Chinese modernization, beyond surface-level exposition of its positions. The article argues that the "six outlooks" embedded in Chinese modernization (worldview, values, view of history, view of civilization, view of democracy and view of ecology) form the theory's philosophical foundation. Feng takes as the starting point Xi Jinping's remark after the 20th Party Congress (2022) that the theory is a major theoretical innovation and the latest major achievement of scientific socialism.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the philosophical foundation matters: it deepens research into the regularities of China's distinctive path, and it widens the practical scope of the theory by handling the relations between tradition and modernity, part and whole, and present and long-term development. The second part defines the foundation's core meaning through three principles ("the people first", independence and self-reliance, and "having the world in mind") and then describes each of the six outlooks in turn. The third part examines how the six outlooks cohere.

Feng's central claim is that the foundation is an organic whole with a vertical and a horizontal structure. Vertically, the worldview, grounded in dialectical and historical materialism, plays the leading role and determines the other five outlooks; Feng supports this with Marxist claims that history, civilization and democracy are rooted in practice and the people's role. Horizontally, the six outlooks interact at the same level, which Feng illustrates through the mutual shaping of the view of history and the view of civilization, while each keeps its own emphasis. Feng contrasts each outlook with Western counterparts, presenting the Chinese ones as surpassing zero-sum thinking, capital-centred values, the "clash of civilizations" and an approach to development that neglects the environment.

Feng concludes that the six outlooks together constitute the theory's philosophical foundation and develop dynamically as practice resolves real contradictions. Understanding them is said to give theoretical guidance for advancing Chinese modernization and to offer "Chinese wisdom" for world modernization. Read the original if you want a systematic account, in official Party-theory terms, of how Chinese scholars derive the "six outlooks" from Marxist philosophy and relate them to one another.
quoteEn: As a leading force, the worldview of Chinese modernization runs through the whole process of its theory and practice, and determines and governs the development of the other five outlooks.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化的世界观作为引领性力量，贯穿于中国式现代化理论与实践的全过程，决定并支配着其他五观的发展。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of national development, given prominence at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.

The article's term for the worldview, values, view of history, view of civilization, view of democracy and view of ecology that it says Chinese modernization embodies. It draws on Xi Jinping's phrasing about the "unique worldview, values, view of history…" of Chinese modernization.
A principle stressed in Party documents under Xi Jinping, holding that the Party's work should rest on and serve the people.

t: The innovative development of the Marxist theory of ownership in the age of the digital economy
zh: 数字经济时代马克思主义所有制理论的创新发展
paras: Bao Weijie asks in what sense the Marxist theory of ownership can be developed further under the digital economy. The article argues that the theory should be read as an organic whole rather than as a question about the title to means of production alone. On that reading, it both changes and stays the same in the digital age. Its classical core remains fully applicable to the critique of digital capitalism, and Bao also proposes new research agendas.

The article first sets out three theoretical questions: whether to take a structural or an element-based view, which principle to start from, and what practical purpose the research serves. It then divides the argument into the "change" of ownership theory and its "constancy", examined through historical materialism. A final section reviews the literature on the digital economy and on ownership theory. It closes with three directions for further work.

On "change", Bao uses three core propositions: who owns the means of production, how labourers are combined with them, and how products are distributed and appropriated. Data now appears as a new, non-material means of production with several possible owners (platforms, the public). Platform work, such as ride-hailing, produces a "semi-combined state" in which workers own part of the means of production. Data revenue is being recalculated. On "constancy", Bao holds that capital's employment of wage labour is unchanged, and that digital productive forces are social labour's productive forces, not "platform capital's" productive forces. Platforms gain "original" and "derived" data ownership, extract rents and lobby against antitrust rules, and Bao cites a 2020 US House Judiciary Committee report on Google and Facebook. In Bao's reading this confirms the limits of labour's liberation under digital capitalism.

Bao proposes three research directions. The first is the impact of the digital economy on traditional ownership relations, including platform capital as a new type of owner and the subjectivity and rights of digital workers. The second is the applicability of ownership theory to building socialist ownership, to anti-monopoly work and to preventing the disorderly expansion of capital, with attention to public capital combined with digital technology and to whether "social ownership" might be realised. The third is data ownership, including data rights confirmation, tiered public, enterprise and individual rights, and the ownership of AI-generated products. Bao ties this work to the aim that all the people share the dividends of the digital economy. Read the original if you want a Chinese political-economy account of platform capitalism and data ownership, with a map of the domestic literature.
quoteEn: From \"original data ownership\" to \"derived data ownership\" and then to the \"data ecosystem\" and \"data monopoly\", the economic base of digital capitalism has been constructed.
quoteZh: 从“原始数据所有权”到“衍生数据所有权”再到“数据生态”“数据垄断”，数字资本主义的经济基础被建构起来了

glossary.explanation: A Marxist notion of ownership of the means of production by society as a whole, which the author asks whether the digital economy might make achievable.
Official phrase, used from around 2020–21, for curbing monopolistic and unregulated growth of large private capital, especially in platform companies.

t: Treating reification within the dialectical relation between spirit and body
zh: 在精神与肉体的辩证关系中对待物化
paras: Since Lukács introduced the critique of reification, the authors observe, Western Marxism has often criticised capitalism for the reification it produces rather than for its internal contradictions. Huang and Wang argue that most thinkers have not found the right way of dealing with reification. They propose a materialist-dialectical approach: reification is to be both acknowledged as rationally necessary to a degree and continually resisted.

The article has four sections. It first argues that Lukács's theory is idealist in nature, then traces the roots of reification to the opposition of spirit and body. It next compares three ways of overcoming the subject–object dichotomy: Hegelian idealism (Lukács), Heidegger's phenomenology, and Marx's dialectical materialism. A final section considers the theoretical and social significance of reification, drawing on Adorno and Horkheimer, Honneth, Kant and Baudrillard.

The authors contend that Lukács shifted Marx's analysis from the economic base to ideology and took over Hegel's notion of totality, so that the 'reified totality' repeats the Hegelian claim of a society governed by spirit. Following Adorno and Horkheimer, they trace reification to a civilisational necessity: to survive, humans must master external nature and also their own bodily nature. This divides spirit from body and subject from object. Heidegger tries to leap over the opposition and so negates civilisation, while Lukács's proletarian subject-object, even if it took control, would still run a rationalised system. For the authors, Marx's subject is a living, self-contradictory person, and the incalculable use-value of commodities is the non-identical element that resists reification.

The authors conclude that reification cannot be abolished, because human survival requires it, but that it can be resisted by reviving suppressed passion and reconciling it with spirit. They hold that the problem of modern capitalist civilisation is that reification is unconditionally treated as rational. Under commodity fetishism and in Baudrillard's 'hyperreality', true and false needs become hard to tell apart, and excessive competition between states and individuals becomes self-harming. They call for a Marxist materialist dialectic that avoids both Lukács's idealism and Heidegger's contemplation of Being. Read the original if you want a Chinese philosophical reading of Lukács, Heidegger and Marx on reification, with particular attention to the body–spirit relation.
quoteEn: We must therefore exercise the role of the subject at all times, see through the 'illusions' of everyday life, and not be taken in by them.
quoteZh: 因此，我们必须时刻发挥主体的作用，认清生活中的“幻相”，不被其迷惑。

glossary.explanation: Lukács's term for the process by which social relations under capitalism take on the appearance of thing-like, rationally calculable objects. It is a central theme of Western Marxism.
The tradition of Marxist thought associated with Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci and the Frankfurt School, which emphasises culture, consciousness and philosophy.
Marx's term for the way relations between people appear as relations between things, so that social products seem to have natural, independent power.

t: Accelerating the formation of distribution relations suited to the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 加快形成与新质生产力发展相适应的分配关系
paras: Xu Ji and Liu Xueliang take up Xi Jinping's call to build new relations of production suited to new quality productive forces, and ask what distribution relations that would require. Their thesis is that distribution relations and new quality productive forces can reinforce each other, but only if the distributional risks of the new round of scientific-technological revolution and industrial transformation are managed. The article, published in Caijing Zhiku in 2024, treats distribution as a core component of the relations of production.

The article first sets out the two-way interaction. Fair incentives for talent, knowledge and technology are said to support new quality productive forces, while these forces create conditions for reforming distribution and for common prosperity. It then reviews Chinese and international literature on four channels of disruption: employment structure, income polarisation and skills, labour–capital conflict and equality of opportunity, and falling labour income share with unbalanced development. It next identifies four potential paths by which new quality productive forces could improve distribution, and closes with policy proposals.

On the risks, the authors draw on studies of automation. These include estimates of jobs at high risk of replacement, from Frey and Osborne's 47% for the United States to more moderate task-based estimates of 6–12%. They also cite research on the polarisation of middle-skill workers, platform-based flexible employment, algorithmic discrimination, and capital-biased technical change and "superstar" firms. The authors then argue the effect is not necessarily negative. In their account, a people-centred employment ecology, new rules for factors such as knowledge, technology and data to share in distribution, a high-standard market system that curbs monopoly, and innovation-driven integration of town and country and of regions (for example the "East Data, West Computing" project) can narrow gaps.

The authors conclude that suitable distribution relations should centre on rewarding innovation and respecting labour, knowledge, talent and creativity. They propose better protection for workers in new forms of employment, incentives that reward innovation and tolerate failure, technology-enabled targeted poverty relief and public services, and digital social governance. The governance measures include algorithm audits, "precision taxation" and a data-income scheme that favours data creators in primary distribution and uses data taxes in redistribution. Read the original if you want a literature-rich account of how Chinese economists link new quality productive forces, technological unemployment and common prosperity.
quoteEn: Distribution relations suited to the development of new quality productive forces should have the incentivising of innovation as their core feature, and respect for labour, knowledge, talent and creativity as their basic content.
quoteZh: 与新质生产力发展相适应的分配关系要以激励创新为核心特征，以尊重劳动、尊重知识、尊重人才、尊重创造为基本内涵

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovative combinations of labour, means of labour and objects of labour. It is closely tied to high-quality development.
A long-standing socialist goal, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all rather than a few. It is described officially as covering both material and cultural life.

t: On the humanistic-economy attribute of Chinese modernization
zh: 论中国式现代化的人文经济属性
paras: Luo Weidong asks what most basically defines Chinese modernization as distinct from the Western model. The article argues that its fundamental attribute is its people-centred character, and that in economic terms this means a "humanistic economy" (renwen jingji), an economy that takes the human being as its starting point, purpose and standard. Luo holds that, in this sense, the humanistic economy coincides with a socialist economy and can only be realised under socialism.

The article first traces the move from the "four modernizations" to Chinese modernization, as formulated at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It then reflects on capitalist modernization and sets out three senses of "humanistic economy": a cultural economy, an economy attentive to workers' human traits, and a human-centred economy. It surveys intellectual sources from Confucian thought, Aristotle and Aquinas through Sismondi and the utopian socialists to Marx's 1844 Manuscripts, the Communist Manifesto and Capital. It closes with institutional practice, including Zhejiang province, and a research agenda.

Luo contends that capitalist modernization is driven by the logic of capital and profit maximisation, which inverts means and ends and produces polarisation, ecological damage and conflict. The first two senses of humanistic economy still treat people as instruments of wealth creation. Sismondi is credited as a founder of humanistic economics but lacked a scientific method, while Marx's critique of political economy gave it a scientific form. Under Chinese modernization, Luo describes the humanistic economy as seven things: a people's economy, an economy of common prosperity, a market economy, a moral economy, a cultural economy, an aesthetic economy and a green economy.

Luo concludes that the humanistic economy is the basic attribute of Chinese modernization and that Chinese modernization, so defined, is modernization as it should be. Luo judges that conceptual innovation is largely done but theoretical work lags behind. The article proposes research on reconciling capital's profit-seeking with humanistic goals, on common prosperity and high-quality growth, on the threat AI poses to employment and human character, on the place of human modernization, and on building an autonomous Chinese economics. Read the original if you want a Chinese economist's account of how humanistic economics is linked to Marx, Confucianism and Party policy, and of its proposed research agenda.
quoteEn: In short, the humanistic-economy attribute is the basic attribute of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 要而言之，人文经济属性就是中国式现代化的基本属性。

glossary.explanation: A formulation put forward in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), presenting China's path as socialist modernization led by the Party. It is described as having common features of modernization alongside Chinese characteristics.

A concept the author develops, rather than a fixed official term. It is read here as an economy in which human beings, their culture and their wellbeing are the starting point and purpose of economic activity.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, described in official discourse as an essential feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
The goal of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence and science and technology. It was set out in the 1950s and 1960s and reaffirmed after reform and opening up.

t: Postone and Adorno: two materialist orientations of dialectics
zh: 普殊同与阿多诺对辩证法的两重唯物主义定向
paras: Moishe Postone argued in Time, Labor, and Social Domination that Marx's mature concept of labour is not Hegel's alienation of a conscious subject but a historically specific form of labour under capitalism. Lu Kaihua reads this as continuing Lukács's aim of giving Hegelian dialectics a materialist turn, echoing Lukács's 1967 self-criticism that History and Class Consciousness was 'more Hegelian than Hegel'. The article's thesis is that Postone's 'positive' dialectic of capital and Adorno's negative dialectics are not truly opposed. Lu proposes an 'alliance' between them.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Postone's critical inheritance from Lukács, covering his account of capital as a quasi-independent social subject-substance, the historical development from manufacture to machine industry, and where he departs from Lukács. The second argues that Postone's criticism of Adorno, as a pessimistic heir of Lukács trapped in the philosophy of consciousness, is too simple. The third sets Adorno's Negative Dialectics beside Lukács's 1967 preface and draws on Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit and Logic, Fichte and secondary commentators.

In Lu's reading, Postone locates materiality in the social effects of the value form, not in the class consciousness of the proletariat. His 'treadmill' dialectic holds that productivity gains raise material wealth but not value created per unit of time, which forces ever-greater productivity and produces ecological and social crises. Lu argues that Postone's ideal-typical analysis leaves out concrete labour, social organisation and ideology, as Postone himself admits. Adorno's primacy of the object, Lu argues, already treats value as a 'quasi-independent' entity and traces domination historically.

Lu concludes that Postone's capital dialectic gives critical theory a useful account of structural contradiction, but it risks a Fichte-like conceptual compulsion by turning capital into an 'absolute self'. Adorno's negative dialectics, Lu argues, warns against this risk and against the closure of Lukács's totality. Lu paraphrases Kant: without positive dialectics, negative dialectics becomes empty, and without negation, positive dialectics goes blind. Read the original if you work on Postone, Lukács or the Frankfurt School and want a Chinese-language case for reconciling value-form theory with Adorno.
quoteEn: Without positive dialectics, negative dialectics falls into emptiness; without elements of negativity, positive dialectics is bound to fall into blindness.
quoteZh: 若无肯定的辩证法，否定辩证法则会陷入空洞；若无否定性要素，肯定的辩证法必将陷入盲目。

t: Theoretical sources and features of the heterogeneity dimension in New Historicist criticism
zh: 新历史主义批评异质性维度的理论渊源及其特征探析
paras: This article asks where the concept of 'heterogeneity' in New Historicism comes from and what features it gives the school. Cheng and Fan argue that, unlike traditional historicism, which pairs the 'universal' with the 'particular' or 'different', New Historicism prefers 'heterogeneity'. They trace this mainly to Michel Foucault and Michel de Certeau, whose shared influence they say produces a distinctive 'heterology' in New Historicist practice.

The article is organised in three parts followed by a conclusion. It examines in turn a heterogeneous view of history, a heterogeneous view of power and discourse, and a constructivist method centred on the 'Other'. Its main New Historicist figures are Stephen Greenblatt, Louis Montrose, Hayden White and Catherine Gallagher. It also draws on commentators such as Jürgen Pieters, Ian Buchanan and Frank Ankersmit.

The authors make three main moves. First, Foucault's discontinuity and Certeau's idea of history as writing about the Other move New Historicism from a singular History to plural 'small histories'. White's tropology replaces deductive logic with figurative logic, and Greenblatt's wish to 'speak with the dead' is read as a Certeauvian struggle against death. Second, New Historicism takes up Foucault's analysis of power and subjectivity, for instance in Greenblatt's self-fashioning and Gallagher's work on marginal women writers. It also takes up Certeau's strategy–tactics opposition, which Montrose uses to ask how subjects keep some autonomy. Third, the authors argue that Certeau's 'New World' writing and Foucault's marginal anecdotes together shape the school's characteristic methods, namely thick description, anecdotalism and interdisciplinarity.

The authors conclude that heterogeneity runs through New Historicist theory and practice, which they call a literary-critical version of postmodern historiography. They credit it with directing attention to marginal materials and plural histories, and with promoting practice-orientation and cross-disciplinary work, which they say is useful for building Chinese literary theory. They also warn of risks: attention to particulars may become an escape from theory, and uncritical copying in China may end in 'theory-less homogenisation'. They add, following Tao Dongfeng, that China's 'new liberal arts' should aim to advance modernity, not return to the medieval. Read the original if you study New Historicism, Foucault and Certeau's reception in literary criticism, or debates over how Chinese literary theory should use Western critical schools.
quoteEn: The concept of heterogeneity runs through the theory and practice of New Historicism.
quoteZh: 异质性概念贯穿于新历史主义的理论和实践。

t: Marx and Engels on the global time lag in capitalist development
zh: 马克思恩格斯论资本主义发展的全球时差
paras: Xu Changfu takes up a neglected part of historical materialism, its geographical dimension, and asks how Marx and Engels understood the uneven timing of capitalist development between countries. The article argues that the two thinkers held a systematic view of a global 'time lag' (shicha) in capitalism's development. Xu says they never set this out in a dedicated text, so the article reconstructs it from their writings and links the scattered arguments together. It was published in Marxism and Reality in 2024.

The article has three main parts. The first follows Engels from 1842 to his last years: his first judgement that England lagged behind the Continent, his reversal by 1844, and his later comparison of England with France, Germany and the United States. The second turns to Marx, in three stages: the 1843 introduction to the critique of Hegel's philosophy of right, the 1848 writings on the English, French and Prussian revolutions, and the preface to Capital, Volume I (1867). The third part draws these together into a map of the world and a short conclusion.

Xu argues that Engels worked by observation, while Marx built a theory. In Xu's reading, Marx moved from lags between elements of one society (German philosophy ahead of German politics), to lags between whole societies (the 1648 and 1789 revolutions, and Prussia's March revolution as 'more than half a century' behind), to an economic essence: England as the classic site of the capitalist mode of production, showing other countries 'the image of their own future'. From these texts Xu derives six descending 'gradients', from England down to India and China. They fall into three tiers of lag, measured in decades, centuries and millennia respectively.

Xu concludes that Marx and Engels stressed capitalism's global reach and world-historical significance, while still noting differences between countries. On Xu's reading, the guiding principle is that communist revolution has its objective material conditions only once the first three gradients have made the whole world capitalist. Russia's possible leap over capitalism's 'Caudine Forks' and the collapse of China's traditional economy after the 1894–95 war are treated as external triggers for European proletarian revolution. Read the original if you want a close, text-based reconstruction of the geographical and temporal logic in Marx's and Engels's view of uneven capitalist development.
quoteEn: Marx and Engels held a systematic view of the global time lag in capitalist development, and these views make up the concrete content of the geographical dimension of historical materialism.
quoteZh: 马克思恩格斯对于资本主义发展的全球时差有着系统的看法，这些看法构成了唯物史观地理维度的具体内容

glossary.explanation: The Marxist theory of history, which explains social change through material production and class relations. Chinese scholarship often treats it as the foundation of Marxist theory.
The article's term for the gap in years or centuries between countries in reaching a given stage of capitalist development. It is Xu's own synthesis, not a phrase Marx or Engels used.

A metaphor Marx used in his late writings on Russia, asking whether a country could reach socialism without passing through the humiliations of the capitalist stage. It refers to a Roman military defeat in 321 BC.

t: Methodological shifts in the young Marx's exploration of the philosophy of law
zh: 青年马克思法哲学探索中的方法论转换
source: Observation and Thinking (Guancha yu sikao), 2025 no. 1
paras: Why did the young Marx, who began with legal commentary, end up addressing questions of law through the critique of political economy rather than through law itself? Sun Meitang takes up this familiar trajectory, from the Rheinische Zeitung to the critique of Hegel's philosophy of law to political economy. Sun argues that the popular explanation, that Marx met the problem of material interests and moved from the 'copy' to the 'original', is not wrong but oversimplified, and overlooks a change of dialectical method.

The article follows Marx's path in four stages. It first treats the Rheinische Zeitung commentaries on press censorship and the wood-theft law, then the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, then the reasons for the turn to political economy, and finally how Marx's practical dialectic works out legal questions in economic analysis. Sun also places the shift in its wider setting: the rise of capitalism in Western Europe, Marx's reading in history, economics and politics, and his contacts with Engels.

Sun's central claim is that Marx's dialectic passed through three forms. In the Rheinische Zeitung period it was an 'understanding' dialectic (zhixing bianzhengfa) that measured actual Prussian law against an ideal law that 'ought to be', with traces of Hegel. In the critique of Hegel it became a negative dialectic that turned Hegel's conceptual method against him: civil society and the family are the basis of the state, not the reverse, and democracy is the genuine unity of universal and particular. Because law and state arise from material life, they cannot be understood from themselves, so Marx moved to a historical, practical dialectic. Sun, drawing on Althusser, reads Marx's 'inversion' of Hegel as a change in the structure of dialectic, not a mere reversal of its content.

Sun concludes that Marx converted legitimacy from a question of legal doctrine into one of historical process and human emancipation, so that justice, equality and legality are results of developing productive forces and not moral postulates. Every historical legal form is both legitimate and illegitimate, and even socialist distribution according to work retains traces of 'bourgeois right'. Sun adds that Marx's context cannot simply be transplanted onto the rule of law under socialism with Chinese characteristics, but that its essence, emancipation and social transformation over speculation, can guide it. Read the original if you want a close account of how Marx's methods in the philosophy of law developed from the Rheinische Zeitung to political economy.
quoteEn: In the end the question of law is the question of human emancipation, and emancipation cannot be achieved by deducing categories of the philosophy of law but only through the practical dialectic of social revolutionary movement.
quoteZh: 法的问题终究是人的解放，而人的解放不是用法哲学范畴演绎能解决的，而是通过社会革命运动的实践辩证法来进行的。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's current line of socialist development, associated with reform and opening up. The article mentions it in connection with the rule of law.
In Sun's usage, a dialectic that grasps contradictions only as fixed opposites, here between the ideal and the actual. Sun draws it from Hegel's description of the 'understanding' (Verstand).
Here the Hegelian method in which each category is negated and passes into a more concrete one. Sun says Marx followed this method in his critique of Hegel while inverting its idealist basis.

Sun's term for Marx's mature method, which analyses the contradictory movement of real social practice, chiefly production, instead of movement from concept to concept. Sun treats it as equivalent to the historical dialectic.

t: Three perspectives on the spatial critique theory of foreign Marxism
zh: 国外马克思主义空间批判理论的三重视域
paras: Wang Yuchen and Gao Xiaoxi ask how spatial critique, a major strand of left theory since the late twentieth century, developed across different currents of Marxism outside China, and what it gained and lost. They argue that it appears in classical Western Marxism, neo-Marxism and post-Marxism, with shared features but divergent stances on modernity versus postmodernity. Their verdict is that it enriches the critique of capital but ends in a radical retreat from class politics.

The article takes three thinkers as representatives of the three traditions. Henri Lefebvre stands for classical Western Marxism, David Harvey for neo-Marxism, and Edward Soja for post-Marxism and the Los Angeles school. The authors read each through his theory of space, then draw wider comparisons with Foucault, Deleuze, Massey, Negri and world-systems theorists.

On Lefebvre, the authors say that his humanist totality, reached through the production of space, the dialectic of space and the right to the city, replaces class emancipation with individual freedom and differences. Harvey, in their account, turns Lefebvre's meta-philosophy into a historical-geographical materialism: accumulation by dispossession, "creative destruction" of cities and uneven geographical development explain how capital displaces its crises. His process dialectic and "dialectical utopianism of space and time" are credited with keeping a class standpoint. Soja is portrayed as the weakest case. His thirdspace and spatial justice rest on a loosely defined idea of production relations and on marginal narratives, and so, the authors say, cannot reach private ownership as the root of injustice. For the authors, all three recast the contradiction between labour and capital as oppositions such as totality/fragment, global/local and centre/periphery.

The authors conclude that spatial critique reflects the weakness of foreign Marxism in forming a collective subject. It exchanges class narrative for marginal positions and micro-politics, and amplifies the utopianism they see as inherent in foreign Marxism. They still credit it with prompting a clarification of space within historical materialism and with widening the empirical perspective on capital. They single out Harvey as the most valuable, although they judge that he also wavers on the priority of time and space and does not escape postmodernism. Read the original if you want a critical Chinese assessment of Lefebvre, Harvey and Soja that places spatial theory within debates over Western Marxism, post-Marxism and the fate of class politics.
quoteEn: Strictly speaking, it is a radical retreat that replaces class narrative with marginal positions and usurps total emancipation with micro-politics, continuing and amplifying the utopian character inherent in foreign Marxism.
quoteZh: 在确切的意义上，它是以边缘立场取代阶级叙事、以微观政治僭越总体解放的激进退守，延续并放大了国外马克思主义所固有的乌托邦性质。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic field covering Marxist currents outside China, including Western Marxism, neo-Marxism and post-Marxism. The term is broader than "Western Marxism".

The tradition of Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School and similar thinkers. Chinese scholarship usually sees it as stressing philosophical critique over the economic analysis of Soviet Marxism.
A current associated with Laclau and Mouffe that rejects essentialism and the primacy of class. It stresses discourse and the linking of heterogeneous subjects.
David Harvey's term for capital's expansion into new spaces and resources, in a manner similar to Marx's primitive accumulation, to absorb surplus capital and labour.
Edward Soja's concept holding that justice and injustice are produced in and through geography. It was developed against universalist theories of justice such as Rawls's.

t: The ecological implications of developing new quality productive forces
zh: 论发展新质生产力的生态意蕴
paras: Li Yongsheng and Xu Xialin take up Xi Jinping's statement that new quality productive forces are "themselves green productive forces" and ask what ecological meaning the concept carries. They argue that new quality productive forces are inherently ecological. In their reading, the shift from "natural productive forces" to "social productive forces" and then to new quality productive forces marks a deeper Party understanding of how economic and ecological construction relate.

The article opens with Xi's remarks from September 2023 to mid-2024 that link the concept to green development. It then has three parts: the ecological connotation of new quality productive forces, the ecological thinking needed to develop them, and their ecological orientation. The first part covers the optimised combination of productive elements, digital and green technology, harmony between humanity and nature as a value goal, and an ecological innovation system. The later parts draw on Marx, Engels, Xi Jinping Thought on Civilization and ecology, and economic theory such as the environmental Kuznets curve.

The authors' central move is to read productive forces, following Marx, as a metabolic relation between humans and nature. On this basis they say new quality productive forces overcome the opposition between economy and environment. They reason that protecting the environment is protecting productive forces. They recommend three modes of thought: materialist dialectics, green development and ecosystem thinking. Ecosystem thinking is to be applied through innovative allocation of elements for protection, technological breakthroughs for pollution control, and deep industrial upgrading for restoration. The orientation is then set out under three headings. The first is respecting natural law, including the "mountains, waters, forests, farmlands, lakes, grasslands, deserts and ice" as a community of life and global ecological governance. The second is coordinating green technology innovation, upgrading the three productive elements, and fostering strategic emerging and future industries. The third is meeting people's ecological and living needs through platform, low-carbon circular and smart-industry economies.

The authors conclude that high-quality development is the primary task of building a modern socialist country and that developing new quality productive forces means developing green productive forces. They present the concept as a "balance beam" between ecological construction and economic growth. In their view, grasping its ecological implications helps connect Xi Jinping's economic thought with his thought on ecological civilization and advances Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how Party-affiliated scholars tie new quality productive forces to Marxist ecological ideas and to ecological civilization policy.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces break the dualistic opposition between economy and environment; they follow both the laws governing the development of productive forces and the laws of nature.
quoteZh: 新质生产力打破经济与环境的二元对立关系，它既遵循生产力发展规律，又遵循自然规律

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in September 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, high efficiency and high quality, and is now central to official economic discourse.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.

t: New quality productive forces: a major innovation and development of the Marxist theory of productive forces
zh: 新质生产力：马克思主义生产力理论的重大创新与发展
paras: Lu Guoqi and Chen Xinjian ask how the concept of new quality productive forces, first put forward by Xi Jinping during an inspection tour of Heilongjiang in September 2023, relates to the Marxist theory of productive forces. They argue that it is a scientific, complete and systematic theoretical system and a major innovation and development of that theory, offering guidance for high-quality development and Chinese modernization. The authors define it as a leap in labourers, means of labour, objects of labour and their optimal combination, marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality.

The article was published in Theoretical Exploration (2024, no. 6). After a short introduction it is organised into six sections. Each pairs one element of the Xi-era formulation with a strand of Marxist theory that it is said to develop: quality–quantity unity, the composition of productive forces, productive-force progress, the ecological theory of productive forces, the dialectic of productive forces and relations of production, and the methodology of productive-force development. Each section opens with Marx and Engels, drawing mainly on Capital, and then turns to Xi's remarks and the policies they imply.

The central move is to show continuity and innovation together. Marx held that new productive forces cannot rest on quantitative expansion alone, and the authors read “high quality” (zhiyou) as the contemporary form of this quality–quantity unity. Marx treated science as a “spiritual productive force” that shortens labour time, and in the authors' reading this becomes technological innovation as the core driver, with digital means of labour and data as a new object of labour. Marx's critique of the “productive force of capital” becomes the claim that new quality productive forces are by nature green productive forces, uniting social and natural productive forces. On the relations of production, the authors draw on the unity and struggle of opposites to call for new relations of production through deepened reform, including market-based reform of factor allocation, a new whole-nation system and closer coordination of education, talent and technology. Their methodological formula is to establish the new before breaking the old, adapt to local conditions, and give classified guidance.

The authors conclude that new quality productive forces extend Marxism in the Chinese context and the needs of the times, and they attach concrete proposals to each section. These include upgrading traditional industries and fostering emerging and future industries, strengthening basic research and work on core technologies, and promoting a green transition in development. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars link this concept to Marx's texts and to specific industrial, technological and reform policies.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are a major innovation and development of the Marxist theory of productive forces.
quoteZh: 新质生产力是马克思主义生产力理论的重大创新与发展

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first put forward in September 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation and marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality.
An official goal of the Chinese economy, stressed since the late 2010s, which prioritises quality, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources in a coordinated way to achieve major scientific and technological breakthroughs.

t: Bringing into play the leading role of state-owned enterprises in China's digital economy
st: Based on an understanding of the characteristics of digital capital
zh: 发挥国有企业在我国数字经济发展中的引领作用
zhSub: 基于对数字资本特性的认识
paras: Liu asks how digital capital can be regulated and guided so that China's digital economy develops in a high-quality way. The article argues that state-owned enterprises (SOEs) must play the leading role, as the "lead goose" with private firms as the "main force". Liu bases this claim on both the nature of digital capital and China's practical experience, and presents it as integral to a Chinese-style path of digital modernization under a socialist market economy.

The article opens by separating the general and the specific features of digital capital. It then builds its case in three steps: SOEs as the "ballast" of the digital economy (security, guiding capital, shared benefits); SOEs as the "lead goose" in innovation, industrial chains and international competition; and four policy recommendations. Liu draws on Marx's Grundrisse and Capital, Xi Jinping's remarks and Chinese data and cases, and compares these with the United States and Europe.

In Liu's account, digital capital shares the general traits of capital: profit-seeking, mobility and a dual character. It also has three specific traits. It has pan-accumulation, drawing unpaid user labour and data beyond the wage relationship. It has super-expansiveness, through winner-takes-all dynamics and cross-sector spread. It is composite, combining productive, commercial and financial functions in whole ecosystems. From this Liu argues that private capital alone tends to diverge from national goals, for example by favouring platforms over basic technology, which the author links to "choke-point" problems. SOEs can resist transnational digital monopolies, take on high-risk basic research and infrastructure, narrow income and regional gaps, and anchor domestic innovation systems. They can also help to fill, strengthen and extend industrial chains, and help private firms "go global" and compete for international standards.

Liu proposes four measures: using Party building to speed SOE digital transformation and key-technology breakthroughs; using capital operation to drive innovation; building a "state and private advance together" model of division of labour with private firms; and drawing on international innovation resources and talent. The author concludes that SOEs under Party leadership are a major advantage of socialist China over Western capitalist states. Liu holds that they secure the socialist character of the digital economy. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist political-economy case for state-owned enterprises in the digital sector, with specific examples such as TD-SCDMA and China Mobile's orders to Huawei.
quoteEn: State-owned enterprises are the \"lead geese\" and private enterprises the \"main force\"; this is integral to taking the Chinese path of digital-economy modernization under a socialist market economy.
quoteZh: 国有企业是“领头雁”，民营企业是“主力军”，这是社会主义市场经济条件下走中国式数字经济现代化道路的应有之义

glossary.explanation: A form of capital specific to the digital age, such as platforms, algorithms and data. Liu treats it as sharing the general traits of capital while having its own distinct features.
Enterprises owned by the state, which carry public-ownership capital in China's economy. Liu presents them as both commercial organisations and public-sector actors.
The official description of China's economic system since the 1990s. It combines market mechanisms with a predominantly public-ownership base and state guidance.

glossary.literal: to be throttled by the neck
glossary.explanation: A common expression for China's dependence on foreign supply of key technologies such as high-end chips and operating systems.

t: On the ontological character of Marx's method of critique of political economy: the category of labour as an example
zh: 论马克思政治经济学批判方法的存在论属性——以劳动范畴为例
paras: Xia Ying asks what Marx's "method of political economy" in the 1857 Introduction to the Grundrisse actually is. The article argues that it should not be read as a general methodology or epistemology of capitalist society. In Xia's reading, the passage mostly describes the path of classical political economy and of Kant and Hegel. Marx's own critique instead performs an "ontological deduction" of economic categories, one that probes the real conditions and limits of those categories.

The article has three parts. The first separates Marx's description of classical political economy's "two paths" (from the concrete whole to abstract determinations, and back up to the concrete) from Marx's own advance. It reads the "scientifically correct method" through Kant's theory of knowledge and Hegel's idealism. The second part sets out how Marx moves beyond this standpoint, using the Introduction's remarks on the thinking head, the real subject and the "dual tension" between categories and historical reality. The third part tests the approach on the category of labour, tracing it through monetarism, mercantilism, physiocracy and Adam Smith.

Xia's central claim is that Marx changes the core problem. Classical economists, Kant and Hegel all aim to secure the "purity" of category deduction within thought. Marx instead posits a real subject, society or material life, that stays independent of the head and always has to be presupposed. Categories therefore take their content from the historically specific social reality and not from speculative dialectic. Xia stresses that this yields a break between history and logic, not their unity. Using the German terms Allgemein and überhaupt, Xia argues that Marx replaces Hegel's triad of universal, particular and individual with a standoff between the "general" and the "determinate". On this reading, "labour in general" is "practically true" only in developed capitalism, where labour has become indifferent to its particular kinds.

Xia concludes that Marx offers no free-standing methodology; the method is "presented" in the course of a historical exposition and is not stated as a separate doctrine. The ontological, materialist character of the critique, Xia argues, lets Marx use classical categories to expose the limits of capital's logic, for example through crisis and surplus value. This also supplies the starting point for his later study of capital. Read the original if you work on the Grundrisse Introduction, on Marx's relation to Kant and Hegel, or on the philosophical status of economic categories, and want a close German-term reading of the labour category.
quoteEn: In Marx's philosophy there is no methodology that can be abstracted from specific social reality, so there is no need to understand his critique of political economy from an epistemological perspective.
quoteZh: 在马克思的哲学中并不存在一种可被抽离出特定的社会现实之外的方法论，因此也无需从认识论的视角来理解马克思的政治经济批判。

t: Marx and Engels's theory of the relations of production and its sinicization
zh: 马克思恩格斯生产关系理论及其中国化的发展
paras: Tian Keqin asks how Marx and Engels's theory of the relations of production has been carried forward in China, and what it implies for present reform. Published in 2024 after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee, the article argues that the Chinese Communist Party has applied the theory's basic standpoint and method to Chinese conditions. In Tian's account, this has been done in revolution, construction and reform, and has produced specific forms of socialist production relations suited to China's level of productive forces.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the theory's content: the general law linking relations of production to productive forces, the essence and structure of production relations, and their forms. The second traces the Chinese development in three periods: socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The third draws lessons for today, centred on new quality productive forces, new production relations suited to them, and further comprehensively deepening reform.

On the classical theory, Tian stresses that productive forces generally play the determining role, while relations of production can react back on them. Tian holds that a one-way reading, either "productive forces only" or "production relations only", distorts historical materialism. On the Chinese side, Tian describes a sequence: new-democratic relations of production and the socialist transformation; Mao Zedong's exploration of the contradictions of socialist society and of commodity production; and the shift under reform from single public ownership to a basic economic system. That system combines public ownership as the mainstay with several ownership forms, distribution according to work alongside other methods, and a socialist market economy. For the new era, Tian cites the stress on letting the market play the decisive role in allocating resources while the government plays its role better, and the dual-circulation development pattern.

Tian concludes that continuing to adapt the theory to Chinese conditions is both a requirement of Marxism's development and the route to liberating productive forces. The author calls for new production relations that fit new quality productive forces, and for deeper reform guided by the "six adherences" of the Third Plenum, including Party leadership and a people-centred approach. Tian presents the socialist system's advantage as its ability to adjust production relations to advanced productive forces. Read the original if you want a Party-theoretical account of how Chinese scholars link the classical theory of production relations to the policy line of the 2024 Third Plenum.
quoteEn: The basic socialist economic system, as the concentrated embodiment of the relations of production and economic base of the primary stage of socialism, is the key point of leverage for modernising the national governance system and capacity.
quoteZh: 社会主义基本经济制度作为社会主义初级阶段生产关系、经济基础的集中体现，是实现国家治理体系和治理能力现代化的关键着力点

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24. It stresses innovation-driven, high-technology and high-efficiency productive forces as the engine of high-quality development.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official term for China's economic system, adopted in the early 1990s. It combines market allocation of resources with public ownership as the mainstay and state macro-regulation.
The policy of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world, begun at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.

t: Cultivating and expanding patient capital to advance new quality productive forces
zh: 培育和壮大耐心资本 推动新质生产力发展
paras: Hong Yinxing and Jiang Jichuang ask how China can grow "patient capital", a term that entered official documents in 2024, so that it supports new quality productive forces. They argue that technological breakthroughs of the kind these forces need involve heavy investment, long cycles and high risk. In their view short-term capital cannot meet these conditions, and patient capital is therefore an important support and driver of the new forces.

The article opens with the April 2024 Politburo meeting and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for developing patient capital. It then reviews the sparse literature, which it describes as mostly theoretical or empirical studies of listed firms, and says this literature has not examined the concept's content or mechanisms. The authors define patient capital, explain how it promotes new quality productive forces, examine three forms (technology credit, venture capital and the stock market), and end with five policy recommendations.

The authors define patient capital as strategic, socially responsible, proactive, rational and scarce risk capital that takes part in the management of the firms it funds. Not all long-term capital qualifies, since they require strategic vision and active involvement. They propose a broad scope covering bank credit, venture capital, primary-market equity, bonds, industrial funds and government guidance funds, but limited to the real economy rather than virtual economy. Citing Marx on the costly equipment needed to exploit science, they argue that innovation needs both funding and risk-sharing, and cite the steam engine, canals and railways, and Silicon Valley as historical examples. On technology credit, they note that such loans were 1.01% (small and medium technology firms) and 5.63% (high-tech firms) of total loans at the end of 2023. They propose larger supply, lower rates, longer terms and stricter screening against loans diverted to property. For venture capital and stocks, they stress longer fund lives and tighter entry and delisting rules.

The policy proposals are to develop venture capital and the stock market together; to build multi-level capital markets; and to make state capital the main "ballast" of patient capital through reformed evaluation, incentives and fault-tolerance. They also propose bringing in international patient capital, which they say invests earlier, and building a supporting system of legislation, coordinated fiscal and monetary policy, and differentiated conduct regulation. Capital that stays long in loss-making state enterprises is, they say, not patient capital but "helpless" or "problem" capital that must be restructured. Read the original if you want a Chinese economists' policy framework linking finance, state capital and new quality productive forces, with figures on technology lending and venture investment stages.
quoteEn: Patient capital can meet the new requirements of large investment, long cycles and high risk, and is an important support and driving force for developing new quality productive forces.
quoteZh: 耐心资本能适应大投入、长周期、高风险的新要求，是发展新质生产力的重要支撑和推动力。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of factors and industrial upgrading.
Long-term investment capital that does not seek quick returns and can bear high risk. The term entered Chinese official documents in 2024.

glossary.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Èrshí Jiè Sān Zhōng Quánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The July 2024 plenary meeting of the Party's Central Committee, which adopted a decision on deepening reform comprehensively.
State-capitalised investment funds meant to draw in private capital to priority sectors such as technology.

t: The fundamental guidance for further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 进一步全面深化改革的根本遵循
paras: This article, published in Qiushi's sister Party journal Qianxian (Frontline) in early 2025, asks what should guide the next stage of reform in China. Li and Zhang argue that the new ideas, viewpoints and judgements on comprehensively deepening reform put forward since the 18th Party Congress (2012) by the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core answer why and how reform must be deepened in the new era. In their account, these ideas supply the fundamental guidance for further comprehensively deepening reform.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the practical basis: reform has entered a stage of tackling hard problems, and the authors trace the sequence of plenums from the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The second presents the theoretical guidance, centred on the "six adherences" set out in 2024. The third turns to implementation through "three greater emphases".

For the authors, the practical record shows reform moving from local experiments to systematic integration. They cite 72 meetings of the central reform commission or leading group over 11 years, more than 600 reform documents and over 3,000 reform plans. The "six adherences" are the Party's overall leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, institution-building as the main thread, law-based governance in every field, and a systems approach. The authors present these as a summary of experience since reform and opening up and as a guide to the rule-governed nature of reform. On method, they call for greater emphasis on systematic integration, on key priorities (with economic reform as the lead) and on practical results, pursued with a "nail-driving spirit".

Li and Zhang conclude that further deepening reform requires studying and applying Xi's ideas on the subject, mastering these methods and building broad consensus. They state that the aim is to mobilise every positive factor for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The text is an authoritative-style exposition of current Party doctrine rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a compact, official-register account of how Chinese Party theorists link the 2024 reform decision to Xi Jinping's earlier statements on reform principles and method.
quoteEn: Reform and the rule of law are like the two wings of a bird or the two wheels of a cart.
quoteZh: 改革与法治如鸟之两翼、车之两轮。

glossary.explanation: The principles for further deepening reform set out at the 2024 plenum: Party leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, institution-building, law-based governance and a systems approach.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, usually tied to the mid-twenty-first century.

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.literal: keeping to the correct path and innovating
glossary.explanation: A formula calling for fidelity to core political principles alongside innovation in practice.

t: The impact of artificial intelligence on the economy and society
zh: 人工智能对经济社会的影响
paras: Zhu Xufeng asks how artificial intelligence (AI), as a fusion of modern information technology with the socio-economic system, is changing production, daily life and governance, and what risks come with it. The article argues that AI empowers industries and restructures the economy, but also deepens social differentiation and creates ethical and governance problems. These, Zhu holds, call for agile governance and international cooperation. Published in Qiushi's sister journal Qianxian in early 2025, it frames the topic as important for building a strong science and technology nation, for new quality productive forces and high-quality development, and for Chinese modernization.

The article has four parts. It first outlines AI technology and industry: three levels of intelligence (perceptual, cognitive, creative), three layers of the industrial chain (foundation, technology, application), and China's position, including the world's largest industrial robot market. It then examines how AI empowers sectors and adjusts industrial structure, then how it reshapes social structure, and finally the ethical and governance challenges and responses. Zhu cites figures such as a projected 7 per cent boost to global GDP over ten years from generative AI and International Federation of Robotics data on robot stock.

Zhu argues that AI is upgrading industry, services, smart cities, energy and information technology, while redistributing value between capital and labour. The article lists four distributional changes: polarisation of returns to capital and labour, a wider income gap between high-skilled and ordinary workers, polarisation of profits between large intelligent firms and ordinary firms, and a deeper intelligence divide between core and peripheral countries, producing a technology-driven globalisation. In society, routine jobs are automated and demand for high-skilled workers rises, unequal educational resources entrench inequality, and personalised information feeds create filter bubbles that polarise politics. On governance, Zhu points to algorithmic bias, privacy and data security, and lagging, fragmented global rules.

Zhu notes responses such as the EU's 2018 ethics guidelines, UNESCO's 2019 recommendation and China's 2019 governance principles for responsible AI. The article calls for data-protection laws, stronger state supervision, agile governance with rapid response and continuous adjustment, and international standard-setting, and it urges individuals to keep learning new skills. Zhu concludes that coordinated development of technology and governance could bring a more intelligent, efficient, fair and inclusive era.
