The first draws on Engels's remark about the industrial revolution in England, the political revolution in France and the philosophical revolution in Germany to identify three preconditions: the modern individual, the modern state and the modern material mode of production. The next sections treat the human subject as the force of modernization, free and all-round development as its value goal, and the critique of capitalist modernity as its way of thinking. The last turns to the communist future and the "association of free individuals".

Zhou's central move is to read Marx and Engels as both affirming and criticising capitalist modernity. Capitalism, in this account, advanced productive forces and opened the world-historical stage, yet subordinated human development to the valorisation of capital and produced alienation, crises and a "fictitious community". Zhou holds that Marx and Engels therefore rejected any single formula for modernization. They pointed to diverse paths shaped by history, culture and geography, and to a socialist "new modernity" that supersedes capital's logic. Zhou also cites Engels's "parallelogram of forces" as a theory of how individual wills combine into historical force, and stresses the unity of material and intellectual production.

Zhou concludes that Chinese modernization is the contemporary practice of this thought. In the article's account, it is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party, combining an effective market with an active government and a people-centred approach, and so has substantively surpassed Western modernization and its claims to "universal values". The author calls for building a community with a shared future for mankind and for advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's systematic account of how Marx and Engels's texts are mobilised to ground Chinese modernization theoretically.
quoteEn: Marx and Engels identified "modernization" as the necessary manifestation and necessary result of the "modern", one reflected above all in the mode of production.
quoteZh: 马克思恩格斯把“现代化”认定为“现代”的必然呈现和必然结果，并且集中反映在生产方式上。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path of modernization, described as led by the Party and socialist in character.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping, presented as a vision of interdependent and cooperative international relations.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, central to official discourse since the 2010s.

t: Accelerating the development of new quality productive forces and steadily advancing high-quality economic development
zh: 加快发展新质生产力 扎实推进经济高质量发展
paras: Taking its cue from the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform to advance Chinese modernization, this article asks how the new development philosophy, high-quality development and new quality productive forces fit together. Zhang argues that they form one system. The new development philosophy supplies the guiding principles, high-quality development is the first task of socialist modernization and the test of whether the philosophy is being carried out, and new quality productive forces are the intermediate link that connects the two.

The article has three parts. The first sets out how to understand and apply the five elements of the new development philosophy (innovation, coordination, green, open and shared development), stressing a problem-oriented and systemic approach. The second discusses how to coordinate the philosophy with high-quality development, covering institutional design, regional coordination, the real economy, the division of tasks between central and local governments, and performance evaluation. The third turns to new quality productive forces, drawing on Marx's writings on productive forces and the labour process, and on Xi Jinping's statements.

Zhang's central move is to read each element of the philosophy broadly: innovation as integrated innovation rather than technology alone, green development as a re-engineering of social production rather than environmental protection, and shared development as a step towards common prosperity rather than distribution alone. High-quality development is then presented as a shift from speed and scale to quality and efficiency, and as the standard by which the philosophy is judged. The author cites dependence on imported chips, lithography machines and machine tools as evidence of the need to innovate. New quality productive forces are described as both a new state of productive forces and an ongoing process. Zhang places them within a modernized economic system and argues that they need new relations of production.

Zhang concludes that high-quality development has to rest on deeper reform. Specific proposals include removing institutional obstacles to technological innovation, allowing room for failure, turning research results into industry, and funding future industries. Traditional industries should be upgraded, not abandoned, and policy should vary by region. Zhang also calls for a performance evaluation that adds ecological, livelihood and social indicators and rewards innovation rather than growth alone. The article ties all of this to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how the new development philosophy, high-quality development and new quality productive forces are linked, and how it draws on Marx's concept of productive forces.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces is by no means the business of any one person, department or region, but the shared responsibility of the whole of society.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力，绝不是哪一个人、哪一个部门、哪一个地区的事情，而是全社会的共同责任。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new combinations of production factors and industrial upgrading.
The official goal of shifting the economy from speed and scale to quality, efficiency and sustainability. It has been presented as the first task of building a modern socialist country.
The five-part guiding principle of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, set out by the Party leadership in 2015.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis in Party policy since 2021.
A concept from the 19th Party Congress (2017). It combines a modern industrial system with a high-level socialist market economy.

t: Reflecting on the premises of paradigm construction in Chinese Marxist philosophy
st: From the perspective of the "self-justification of a philosophical paradigm"
zh: 中国马克思主义哲学范式建设的前提意识之思
zhSub: “哲学范式自我证成”的视角
paras: Cao Dianshun asks what premises must be examined before Chinese Marxist philosophy can build a distinctive research paradigm of its own. Treating paradigm construction as the process by which the paradigm justifies itself, Cao argues that four "premise-reflections" come first: on the theoretical premise, on problem-consciousness, on theoretical grounds, and on academic discourse. The thesis is that paradigm construction must unite "practicality" and "academic character", and must leave behind a stage of "apprentice scholarship".

The article opens by placing paradigm construction as a third stage of research, after studies of Marxist philosophy paradigms and of Chinese Marxist philosophy paradigms. Its four sections follow the four premise-reflections in turn. Each is built around paired concepts, such as practicality and academic character, "realistic concern" and "genuine philosophy", and "theoretical practicality" and "apprentice academic character". The text draws on Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong, Gadamer and Xi Jinping's formulations about philosophy and social science.

Cao first holds that practicality supplies the method, starting point and test of paradigm construction, while academic character supplies its standards and guiding principle, so the two are internally unified. Second, Cao diagnoses an earlier phase of "apprentice academic character" in Chinese Marxist philosophy. Examples include textbook-paradigm work shaped by limited sources and Soviet influence, and readings that explain Marx through Hegel, Kant or Heidegger. In Cao's view this imitation and dogmatism limits originality and delays the arrival of paradigm construction. Third, Cao proposes a new discourse. "Realistic practicality" is set against idealist "rational practicality" and dogmatic "theoretical practicality", and "scientific academic character" against "abstract rational" and "apprentice" scholarship. Cao treats these two as complementary features of a paradigm guided by historical materialism.

Cao concludes that Chinese Marxist philosophy should stress the particular logic of historical materialism, since Marx already set out its general logic. It should keep reflecting on social practice and keep up original theoretical research. Cao presents this as a mission set by social development and as a way to serve Chinese modernization theoretically and practically. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese philosopher sets out the conceptual preconditions for an autonomous Chinese Marxist philosophical paradigm and criticises earlier Chinese scholarship.
quoteEn: The organic fusion of "realistic practicality" and "scientific academic character" in paradigm construction is not only a historical mission assigned by social development but also the academic discourse of paradigm construction itself.
quoteZh: 范式建设中“现实实践性”和“科学学术性”的有机融合,不仅是社会发展赋予的历史使命,也是范式建设本身的学术性话语。

glossary.explanation: Official Party concept for China's own path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article treats it as the practical task that Chinese Marxist philosophy should serve.
The author's term for a proposed stage of research that builds a distinctive paradigm of Chinese Marxist philosophy, following earlier studies of Marxist and Chinese Marxist paradigms.
The author's label for a phase of scholarship that largely imitated Soviet or Western philosophy without original contribution.
The author's term for practice grounded in real individuals and material life, set against idealist and dogmatic conceptions of practice.
The Marxist theory of history that explains social development through material production and social relations. The article treats it as the guiding logic of the proposed paradigm.

t: Marx's conception of revolution and its significance for the new era
zh: 马克思革命观及其新时代意蕴
paras: Gao Junhua takes up Hannah Arendt's claim that Marx, despite being the greatest theorist of revolution, almost wholly neglected the revolutionaries' true aim, the founding of freedom. Gao treats this as a representative misreading: it denies the idea of freedom in Marx and so his theory of revolution, and it pits the mature Marx against the young one. The article argues that political and social revolution are closely linked in Marx, and that freedom is central to his conception of revolution. On that basis it explains in what sense China in the new era speaks of continuing revolution.

The article has four parts. The first sets out the scientific content of Marx's conception of revolution, drawing on On the Jewish Question, the 1844 articles against Arnold Ruge and the Communist Manifesto, and on Hal Draper's study of Marx's revolutionary theory. The second examines the value orientation of that conception, namely political and social freedom, and answers Arendt. The third takes up the revolutionary subject, the proletariat. The fourth applies the framework to China since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Gao's central move is that bourgeois political revolution delivered only formal freedom, because the state was separated from civil society and private ownership remained. Social revolution is therefore needed: developing the productive forces, replacing private ownership of the means of production with public ownership, and supplying the basis for political revolution. Against Arendt, Gao holds that she mistakes Marx's concern with abolishing alienated labour for neglect of freedom, and that the mature Marx kept the ideal of free individuality. Gao also argues that the proletariat moves from a class in itself to a class for itself through revolutionary practice, uniting ideas with reality and the particular with the universal.

Gao reads the new era through this lens. The Party's self-reform is presented as political revolution, and common prosperity as the core content of social revolution. Gao calls the formula of leading a great social revolution through a great self-reform (the 'two great revolutions') a theoretical innovation that develops Marx's theory. Common prosperity rests on developing the productive forces, keeping public ownership dominant while supporting the non-public sector, and creating conditions for free time and all-round human development. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic defence of Marx's theory of revolution against Arendt, or an example of how it is tied to the Party's self-reform and common prosperity today.
quoteEn: The revolutionary spirit in Marx's conception of revolution is not the abstract freedom of liberalism but real freedom within society.
quoteZh: 马克思革命观中的革命精神不是自由主义抽象的自由，而是社会中的真实自由。

glossary.explanation: A term stressed in Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012) for the Communist Party's continuing effort to correct its own problems and maintain its vitality. Official English translations render it as self-reform.
An official goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, stressing prosperity shared by all rather than a few. It has been promoted heavily in Party policy since the 2010s.

t: How Marxism understands "productive forces"
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“生产力”
paras: This short commentary in Study Times asks what Marxism means by "productive forces" and how the concept develops over time. Zhao argues that Marx defines productive forces as humanity's capacity to transform and use nature, and that the Communist Party of China has deepened this understanding through successive stages of liberating and developing them.

The article first sets out Marx's and Engels's definition, drawing mainly on The German Ideology and Capital. It then covers the social role of productive forces and traces the Party's treatment of the concept from Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping through the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping.

Zhao presents productive forces as both a natural and a social relation, with objective and historical features. The author holds that Marx's three elements (labourers, means of labour and objects of labour) go beyond Western theory's capital, labour and land. In Zhao's account, productive forces are the basic driving force of social contradictions and the final determinant of historical development, in line with historical materialism. The article then reads new quality productive forces as an innovation within this tradition, describing new demands on workers, technology-driven means of labour and emerging industries as objects of labour.

Zhao concludes that, guided by Marx's theory, the Party has proceeded from the fundamental interests of the people and kept deepening Marxist understanding of productive forces. The article presents new quality productive forces as important for self-reliance in science and technology, high-quality development and Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned overview of how Party writers link Marx's concept of productive forces to current policy.
quoteEn: Productive forces arise from humanity's practical relationship with nature; they are a composite force formed as people actively transform nature.
quoteZh: 生产力源自人类与自然的实践性关系，是人类在能动地改造自然的过程中形成的综合性力量

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological innovation, such as digital technology and artificial intelligence, and by emerging and future industries.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth stressing quality, innovation and efficiency.
A guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao's leadership in the 2000s, stressing comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the interests of the overwhelming majority.

t: How does Marxism understand "heroes"?
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“英雄”
paras: This short commentary from the Study Times asks how Marxism understands the "hero". Li Junshi argues that the Marxist view of the masses as makers of history does not deny the achievements of heroic figures. In Li's account, the Marxist conception rests on a dialectical grasp of the relation between the people and outstanding individuals.

The piece first looks at how Marx and Engels use the word "hero", then at the basic principles of historical materialism behind that usage. It then turns to Lenin and Plekhanov on the role of the individual. It ends with the heroic culture of the Communist Party of China.

Li distinguishes two usages in Marx and Engels. In The Civil War in France, praise for the Communards' "heroism" (Heldenmut) is praise for courage and willingness to sacrifice. In The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, Engels uses "heroic age" neutrally for a stage of Greek social development. Li argues that Marxism opposes the "heroic" view of history because it severs heroes from the masses and attributes their deeds to personal talent alone. Outstanding individuals can have great influence, in Li's reading, but only by drawing on the wisdom and strength of the people. Li cites Lenin and Plekhanov for the point that social conditions set the scope of individual influence.

Li concludes that Chinese Communist heroic culture joins this historical-materialist outlook with the traditional Chinese esteem for moral character. Li gives Liu Hulan and Zhang Side as ordinary people who became model heroes, and cites Xi Jinping's remark that the new era is one that makes heroes. Read the original if you want a brief, official-register account of how Party theory reconciles the people-centred view of history with the celebration of heroes.
quoteEn: The Marxist understanding of the hero is built on a dialectical grasp of the relationship between the people's masses and heroic figures.
quoteZh: 马克思主义对英雄的理解建立在对人民群众与英雄人物关系的辩证把握之上

t: How does Marxism understand "happiness"?
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“幸福”
paras: Prompted by Xi Jinping's remark that the people's happy life is "earned through work" and by the 20th Party Congress (2022) report on improving people's wellbeing, this short commentary from Study Times asks how Marxism understands happiness. Jin and Zhang answer that Marxism sees happiness as a unity of three pairs: subjective pursuit and objective creation, material abundance and spiritual richness, and individual development and social progress.

The authors first contrast Marx with earlier sensualist and rationalist views of happiness. They then take each of the three unities in turn and name the corresponding outlook: a practice-based, a comprehensive and a people's view of happiness. The final section applies these to the tasks set out by the 20th Party Congress.

Jin and Zhang argue that Marx starts from the \"real person\", who has needs and aims but acts under inherited conditions. Practice joins subjective pursuit to objective creation, so happiness is built up through creative activity. Material abundance is a basic condition, but in the authors' reading Marx held that capital fetishism and alienated labour turn people into slaves of money and produce unhappiness. Happiness therefore requires both material and spiritual fullness. Finally, because human essence is the ensemble of social relations, personal happiness cannot be separated from that of the people. The authors cite Marx's youthful essay on choosing a profession and his answer \"struggle\" when asked what happiness is, and they point to communism as the point where individual and social development coincide.

The authors conclude that Chinese modernization should rest on these three views. They call for a spirit of struggle and innovation, for material conditions together with advanced socialist culture, and for fulfilling the people's aspiration for a better life through common prosperity. They add that China's modernization will bring benefits to the wider world. Read the original if you want a concise, Party-press statement of how Marx's idea of happiness is linked to current policy language.
quoteEn: Material poverty is not happiness, and spiritual emptiness is not happiness either.
quoteZh: 物质贫乏不是幸福，精神空虚也不是幸福。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as combining material and spiritual civilization and aiming at common prosperity.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, stressed in Party policy under Xi Jinping.

t: How Marxism understands "true philosophy"
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“真正的哲学”
paras: Writing in Study Times, Xu Hengbing and Zhang Xiaoxu ask how Marxism understands "true philosophy". They argue that Marx, while founding dialectical and historical materialism through a sustained critique of older philosophy, especially German philosophy, repeatedly set out what a true philosophy is, and that his view can be read along three dimensions.

The short commentary draws on Marx's early editorial on the Kölnische Zeitung, the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology, with a supporting reference to Engels. It then turns to the present, linking the discussion to the Party's current theoretical work.

The authors say that, first, a true philosophy belongs to its time: it responds to the era's "pressing questions" and, by grasping the general laws of social development, becomes real knowledge rather than empty speculation. For Marx and Engels these questions were where capitalism and human history were heading and how human emancipation could be achieved. Second, a true philosophy is a philosophy of the people. It serves the great majority rather than the ruling class, and Marx's starting point of "real individuals" and his goal of a "community of free individuals" express its commitment to universal emancipation. Third, it is tied to practice: it aims not only to interpret the world but to change it, and becomes a material force only when it grips the masses.

The authors conclude that Marxist philosophy lasts because it opens a path to truth, not because it exhausts truth. They state that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has used this worldview and methodology to form the "six musts", part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They urge readers to study these in continuity with Marxist theory. Read the original if you want a concise, Party-press account of Marx's conception of philosophy and how it is linked to current official theory.
quoteEn: A "true philosophy" is not merely a philosophy that interprets the world, but above all one that changes it.
quoteZh: “真正的哲学”不仅仅是解释世界的哲学，更是改变世界的哲学

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six principles presented as the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought, covering the people-centred approach, self-confidence and self-reliance, and related themes. They were set out in official documents of the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: How does Marxism understand "cooperation"?
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“协作”
paras: This short commentary in Study Times asks how Marxism understands "cooperation" (xiezuo), which Marx defines as many people working together according to plan in the same or in connected production processes. Zhang argues that cooperation creates a collective productive force greater than the sum of individual labours, and that Marx's theory still guides practice today.

The article first traces cooperation through history: the Great Wall and the pyramids, integrated manufactures, and factory production under large-scale machine industry. It then sets out why cooperation raises productivity and discusses management in capitalist cooperation.

Zhang explains the productivity gain through three features drawn from Marx and Engels. Cooperation has identity, shortening necessary labour time through joint action. It has systemic character, extending or concentrating the space of work and saving costs. It has a social character, stimulating competition and allowing complementary roles. Zhang adds that large-scale cooperation needs direction, like an orchestra conductor, but that capitalist management is dual: it organises social labour and also serves the valorisation of capital. Because capitalists pay for independent labour-power rather than cooperative labour-power, the extra productive force costs them nothing, which Zhang reads as deepening exploitation.

Zhang concludes that, as socialised production deepens, cooperation matters more, and calls for better cooperation between sectors, organisations and countries. For the development of new quality productive forces, Zhang proposes deeper integration of industries, of the digital and real economies, and of industry, universities and research, under the Party's leadership. Read the original if you want a brief, Party-press account of Marx's theory of cooperation and its link to current policy language.
quoteEn: Cooperation creates productive force and a level of productivity that individual labour cannot achieve; that is, the whole functions more than the sum of its parts, making it possible to concentrate efforts on major undertakings.
quoteZh: 协作创造了生产力，创造出单个劳动所无法实现的生产率，也就是整体功能大于局部功能之和，实现了集中力量办大事。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, digital technology and industrial upgrading.

t: How Marxism understands the "conception of history"
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“历史观”
paras: Zhang Hong's short commentary asks what the Marxist conception of history is. The author argues that it is a practical materialist view of history, starting from "real human beings" and objective laws of history. In Zhang's account, it surpasses humanist conceptions of history and shifts inquiry from "how is the world possible" to "how is human emancipation possible".

The article first traces how Marx's view took shape, from the Rheinische Zeitung and the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher through the 1844 manuscripts, The Holy Family and the Theses on Feuerbach. It then follows the view to The German Ideology, which Zhang says marks the formation of historical materialism, and on to the Communist Manifesto, the Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy and Capital. It then sets out five features of the conception.

The five features are as follows. Its premise is real, living individuals. Its cornerstone is practice. Its basic theory is the relation of social being to social consciousness, with the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production as the motor of history. Its subject is the people, who make history under inherited conditions. Its direction is towards communism, a free association of individuals in which, Zhang says, capitalism is ultimately replaced by socialism and communism.

Zhang concludes that this is the "only scientific conception of history". The author calls for opposing historical nihilism, drawing on a "grand view of history" to understand a century of Party history, and strengthening the discipline, academic and discourse systems of research on national, Party and military history. Zhang also urges tighter guidance of propaganda and media to protect the dominance of historical materialism in ideology. Read the original if you want a compact, officially oriented outline of the Marxist conception of history and its link to the campaign against historical nihilism.
quoteEn: History cannot be chosen at will.
quoteZh: 历史不能任意选择。

glossary.explanation: In Party discourse, a label for interpretations that question or negate the official account of Chinese revolutionary and Party history. The article treats it as a main ideological threat.
A term in Party discourse, popularised under Xi Jinping, for viewing history in broad, long-term and global perspective.
The Marxist theory that material production and social relations determine the course of history.

t: How Marxism understands "belief"
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“信仰”
paras: Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that faith in Marxism is the political soul of Communists, Yao Chong asks what Marxism itself means by "belief" (xinyang). The commentary, published in Study Times, argues that belief in Marxism is the internalisation of a scientific theory in people's inner world. Yao holds that this internalisation must begin with Marx's own conception of belief.

The piece first traces how Marx rebuilt the concept through value critiques of earlier beliefs: religion and Hegelian philosophy, bourgeois political ideals, and the fetishism of commodities, money and capital. It then turns to why humans need belief and what separates Marx's version from blind worship of existing powers. It closes by linking belief to the communist ideal of human freedom and liberation.

Yao contends that Marx exposed religion and speculative philosophy as ideological tools of ruling classes. He also exposed bourgeois ideals of right, freedom and democracy as protecting a minority, and showed how fetishism leaves workers ruled by their own creations. Real freedom, in this reading, requires changing social relations and modes of production. Marxist belief is therefore tied to practice: scientific truth is internalised as a guide to action and tested in social practice. Yao says it joins ultimate concern with practical concern. Communism is presented as a "real movement" rather than an abstract ideal, and human liberation as an open possibility, not a predetermined outcome.

Yao concludes that grasping Marx's view of belief allows Party members and cadres to build communist belief. The author presents this as a source of spiritual strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization, amid what is called great changes unseen in a century. Read the original if you want a short Party-press account of how Marx's critique of religion and fetishism is used to ground communist belief.
quoteEn: Belief, as the way people identify with and grasp the world, has two dimensions: ultimate concern and practical concern.
quoteZh: 信仰作为人对世界的认同和掌握方式有其终极关怀与现实关切两重维度

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream and the aim of national strength by mid-century.

t: Marx's epistemology of time
zh: 马克思的时间认识论
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 2024
paras: This short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (2024) asks how Marx understood time and why that understanding matters for his ethical thought. Yu Shugui argues that Marx opened a third path between Newton's absolute time and Kant's subjective time. On this path time is placed within the dialectical unity of subject and object, which Yu presents as both scientific and as pointing to the ethical character of time.

The article moves through three themes. It first sets Marx against Newton, Kant, Hegel and Feuerbach, then discusses free time as a central concept in Marx's analysis of capitalism, and finally treats time as the measure of human life. It closes with a brief remark on the acceleration of modern society and intelligent machines.

Yu's core claim is that time is the 'positive existence' of human beings. Following Engels' proposition that labour created humanity, Yu concludes that social labour creates time: nature offers only the motion of matter, and people build time out of its rhythms, with the 'year' as a public rhythm. Newton, in this reading, mistook natural rhythms for time itself, while Kant swung to the other extreme. Marx sublated both by treating time as a product of social practice. Yu then reads free time as leisure time, as time of rights (escape from capital's claim on the worker's surplus labour time) and, essentially, as ethical time. Full free time is attainable only after capitalism and private ownership are overthrown, when labour becomes life's prime need.

Yu distinguishes natural, social and logical (abstract) time, and argues that human beings still have biological limits, the 'biological clock'. As time units shrink to milliseconds and nanoseconds, human rhythms fall behind the pace of an intelligent society. The 'tyranny of time' that Marx criticised under capitalism is therefore turning into one dominated by intelligent machines. Yu suggests that Marx offers valuable methodological guidance for addressing this, but does not develop concrete proposals. Read the original if you want a brief, accessible Chinese reading of Marx's views on time, free time and labour as a starting point for a Marxist ethics of time.
quoteEn: Marx sublated the two different absolute conceptions of time held by Newton and Kant, grasping the essence of time from human social practice and seeing it as a product of that practice, thereby raising human understanding of time to a scientific level.
quoteZh: 马克思扬弃了牛顿与康德两种不同的绝对时间观，而是从人的社会实践中把握时间的本质，将时间看成社会实践的产物，从而使人类对时间的认识达到了科学的层面。

glossary.explanation: The standard Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: a concept or form is overcome while its valid elements are retained in a higher one.
In Marx, time at people's disposal beyond necessary labour, used for development, education, social life and culture. The article treats it as the basis of a Marxist ethics of time.
A phrase the article uses for domination of human life by the time demands of capital, which it extends to the pace set by intelligent machines.

t: The two dimensions of Marx's thought on democracy and their practical embodiment
zh: 马克思民主思想的二维向度及实践体现
paras: Liu Lin asks how Marx's thought on democracy can be understood as a complete system, and answers that it has two complementary dimensions. The first is a 'substantive' dimension, concerning the philosophical grounds and inner value of democracy as rule by the majority. The second is an 'authenticity' dimension, concerning how that majority rule is realised in practice. The author argues that Xi Jinping's whole-process people's democracy fuses the two.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs the substantive dimension through democracy's essence (a state system), its ontological basis (people's democracy) and its true aim (human emancipation), drawing mainly on Marx's Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right and The Civil War in France. The second sets out the authenticity dimension as a critique of bourgeois democracy, a summary of the Paris Commune, and a set of general principles for realisation. The third applies the framework to contemporary China at three levels: the state, the people and society.

Liu argues that for Marx the state is not independent of its economic base, so the extent of democracy depends on economic liberation. Political emancipation remains formal and partial, and only human emancipation goes further. On this basis the author reads Marx as demystifying representative government, universal suffrage and the separation of powers as forms that mask class rule. From the Commune the author draws four lessons: economic emancipation of labour, breaking the old state machine, self-government by the people, and public servants who can be recalled. Realisation requires the unity of new democracy with new dictatorship, of Communist Party leadership with the proletariat as the main force, and of institutional procedure with popular supervision.

In the final section Liu presents whole-process people's democracy as a creative application of these principles. It must suit Chinese modernization and the primary stage of socialism. It must widen participation beyond elections and build people's political capacity. It must also advance in step with the 'five-sphere integrated plan' under the unity of Party leadership, people's mastery of the country and law-based governance. Liu adds that this institutional system needs continued refinement in the face of globalisation and informatisation. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reading of Marx's democratic theory that links it to current Party doctrine on whole-process people's democracy.
quoteEn: Marxist thought on people's democracy also requires that the participants in democracy be broadened and deepened.
quoteZh: 马克思主义人民民主思想还要求对民主参与的主体进行拓展和深化。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019 and written into Party documents. Official accounts say it covers the full chain of democratic procedures, including consultation, decision-making, management and supervision, and not only elections.

The official name for China's path to modernity, set out prominently in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is said to combine features common to all modernizations with Chinese characteristics.
An official judgement, formalised in 1987, that China is still in an early phase of socialism. It is used to justify a development path adapted to national conditions.
The official overall layout for development, which coordinates economic, political, cultural, social and ecological progress.

t: On the microfoundations of Marxist macroeconomics
zh: 论马克思主义宏观经济学的微观基础
paras: Wang Zhongbao asks whether efficiency at the level of the firm is consistent with efficiency at the level of the whole economy, a question the author treats as basic to both Western economics and Marxist political economy. Wang argues that Western economics cannot ground macroeconomic analysis in microeconomic analysis, because under private ownership the two kinds of efficiency come apart. Marxist political economy, in this reading, can explain why and so builds macroeconomics on a microeconomic base.

The article has three parts. The first contrasts privately owned and publicly owned firms, using a reductio argument and citing Thomas Piketty, Joseph Stiglitz and David Harvey on inequality and weak demand. The second analyses sustainable macroeconomic development through ownership, income distribution, market regulation and government intervention. The third proposes a new framework for Marxist economics, listing the topics that microeconomics and macroeconomics would each cover.

Wang's central claim is that ownership of the means of production determines distribution, and distribution determines whether total supply and total demand can match. Under private ownership, a firm raises its profit rate by squeezing wages and shifting costs onto workers, nature and society. Wang argues that competition and capital accumulation then polarise wealth and income, producing insufficient effective demand and recurring crises. Wang holds that Keynesian policy, neoliberalism, progressive taxation and welfare measures only soften or delay this outcome. Under public ownership with distribution according to labour, the owners of capital and of labour-power are the same people. Wang says this removes the antagonism between profit and wages and keeps income gaps small, so that micro-level and macro-level efficiency coincide.

Wang calls for replacing the textbook split between a capitalist part and a socialist part with a unified "modern Marxist economics" centred on the producing firm. The aim is a shift from the "needs of revolution" to the "needs of development", to serve the socialist market economy. Its shared core would be the labour theory of value, ownership theory and the theory of distribution between capital and labour. Wang adds that where private ownership exists within a socialist market economy, it should be guided and regulated, and the public sector should keep its absolute and relative advantage. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese Marxist argument linking ownership, distribution and demand to a proposed restructuring of Marxist economics textbooks.
quoteEn: The construction of the theoretical system of modern Marxist economics must achieve a creative transformation from the "needs of revolution" to the "needs of development".
quoteZh: 现代马克思主义经济学理论体系的构建必须实现从“革命需要”到“发展需要”的创造性转换。

glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system since the 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership as the mainstay and state macro-control.

The principle, taken from Marx's account of the first phase of communist society, that income is allocated according to the quantity and quality of labour contributed. Chinese texts treat it as the main distribution principle under socialist public ownership.
Ownership of the means of production by the whole people or by collectives, which the Chinese constitution defines as the mainstay of the socialist economic system.

t: A community with a shared future for mankind from the perspective of Marxist humanistic theory
zh: 马克思主义人学视域下的人类命运共同体
source: China Theory Network (中国理论网), posted 2024-12-17
paras: Lü Hongxia and Li Luming ask how the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind can be understood through Marxist theory of the human being (renxue). Their thesis is that the idea rests on Marx's concepts of the human as a "species being", of human essence, and of human emancipation. They present it as a contemporary interpretation of Marx's "philosophy of the species" and as a Chinese answer to the problems facing a closely connected world.

The article opens with the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's commitment to building such a community, and then proceeds in three sections. The first treats the idea as a contemporary reading of Marx's species philosophy. The second argues that the human mode of practical existence supplies the idea's practical principles. The third links it to Marx's theory of human liberation. Throughout, the authors cite Marx, the Communist Manifesto and Xi Jinping.

The authors draw on Marx's three social forms (dependence on persons, independence based on dependence on things, and free individuality) to argue that today's world remains in the second. In their account, capital is the material root of division and conflict, and it produces a "thing-centred way of thinking" that loses sight of human species essence. They hold that a shift to "species thinking" is needed, and that the community idea follows this logic. Citing Chinese initiatives in economic, political, ecological and nuclear-security fields, and a series of "community" concepts, they say China acts on the human capacity for practice and sociality. They also argue that bourgeois political emancipation left "illusory communities" intact, whereas this idea develops Marx's theory of human liberation in a Chinese form.

The authors conclude that building the community is a necessary stage on the road to human emancipation. In their view, guided by the common values of all humanity, it is a new exploration of the path of liberation and will go beyond "illusory communities" bound by interests. They describe it as a practice of great significance for turning the communist ideal into reality. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese Party-affiliated scholars root Xi-era foreign-policy language in Marx's humanistic and emancipation theory.
quoteEn: The shift from "thing-centred thinking" to "species thinking" is a necessary requirement for human society to evolve toward a higher social formation and thereby realise the free and all-round development of the human being.
quoteZh: 由“物的思维”向“类思维”的转变，是人类社会向更高级的社会形态演进从而实现人的自由全面发展的必然要求。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013. It calls for common security, development and shared values among states, and is presented in official discourse as China's contribution to global governance.

glossary.en: Marxist theory of the human being (renxue)
glossary.explanation: A field of Chinese Marxist philosophy that studies the nature, existence and development of the human being, often drawing on Marx's early writings.
A formula introduced by Xi Jinping in 2015 listing peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom as values shared across civilizations.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind
Marxist theory of the human being

t: Grasping the dialectics of Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military
zh: 深刻领悟习近平强军思想的辩证法
source: China Social Sciences Network (中国社会科学网), 2024
paras: This article asks what dialectical method underlies Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military and argues that it forms a contemporary Chinese Marxist outlook and methodology on military affairs. Li Honglang contends that the thought rests on Marxist military dialectics, draws on traditional Chinese military culture and grows out of practice in building a strong military in the new era. In Li's account it deepens the Party's understanding of the laws of army-building and opens a new stage in the development of Marxist military thought.

The article is organised around five "adherences" attributed to Xi: political guidance, stopping war through the use of force, active initiative, overall coordination, and the courage to fight and win. Each is paired with a dialectical unity: combat-power building and political work; preparing for war and being able to win; bottom-line thinking and proactive progress; breakthroughs at key points and all-round advance; and material conditions and fighting spirit. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi, then explains the mutual reinforcement of the two sides and links it to current conditions.

Li's central claim is that each pair interacts and promotes the other. Politics directs the military and political work is itself a form of spiritual combat power, so the Party's absolute leadership is the soul of the army; Li ties this to the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds and rejects calls to depoliticise or "nationalise" the armed forces. Readiness for war is said to deter war, so the military must train for real combat amid an uncertain world, while bottom-line thinking must be combined with innovation and reform. Drawing on materialist dialectics, Li says material conditions come first but fighting spirit can offset material shortfalls, citing the Korean War formula of "less steel, more spirit" and Xi's remark that now there is more steel, there must be even more spirit.

Li concludes that the five pairings should be pursued together to achieve the goal of a world-class military and to defend national sovereignty, security and development interests. The article calls for coordinated work on political army-building, reform, science and technology, talent and rule by law, and for cultivating the fighting spirit of the armed forces. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned exposition of how Chinese military-theory writing frames Xi's strong-military thought in dialectical terms.
quoteEn: This profoundly elucidates the dialectical relationship of mutual interaction and mutual promotion between material conditions and fighting spirit.
quoteZh: 这深刻阐明了物质条件与战斗精神的相互作用、相互促进辩证关系。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's ideas on national defence and army-building, formalised in the 2010s and 2020s as part of Xi Jinping Thought, centred on Party leadership over the armed forces and a combat-ready, world-class military.
A mode of strategic thinking promoted by Xi Jinping that stresses anticipating worst-case risks and setting limits that must not be crossed.

The principle of building the armed forces first and foremost on political loyalty to the Party, one of five strategies in Xi's strong-military approach alongside reform, science and technology, talent and rule by law.

t: Rethinking the totality of Marx's concept of "history"
zh: 重新理解马克思“历史”概念的总体性特征
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 2024
paras: Wu Meng asks how the totality of Marx's concept of "history" should be understood. The author argues that the influential reading by Georg Lukács, which ties totality to a Hegelian dialectic of part and whole, is internally inconsistent. In Wu's alternative account, totality in Marx is a historical feature tied to the capitalist mode of production, not an all-encompassing whole that contains and determines its parts.

The short article, published in the China Social Sciences Today, has three parts. It first sets out Lukács's exposition in History and Class Consciousness. It then identifies three weaknesses in that exposition. It ends by proposing a different reading of Marx's dialectic and of totality in his critique of political economy.

Wu summarises Lukács as treating Marx's method as a dialectic of part and totality and of subject and object. Phenomena such as commodity relations and reification appear as parts, and the proletariat grasps the social totality through class consciousness. Wu objects on three grounds. First, grafting Hegel's part–whole dialectic onto Marx's analysis of capitalism is logically unsound: Hegel's concept-dialectic works because the Absolute Idea unites particularity and totality, whereas the social structure is not a particular phenomenon alongside commodity or capital relations. Second, reading Marx's ascent from the abstract to the concrete as an ascent from part to whole leaves the "mediating" concepts vague. It also cannot explain why Marx's analysis of relations between things is always combined with analysis of relations between people. Third, Lukács turns Marx's historically specific concept into an abstract logic applicable to any epoch.

Wu holds that the root error is equating Marx's dialectic with Hegel's. For Marx, totality is the precondition of the historical movement of capitalist objects, namely the capitalist mode of production. It is a functional whole that cannot be objectified, the "complicity" of human and material factors, and it appears as the way phenomena are given. Wu concludes that Marx starts from historical "universality", not from "objectivity", and so avoids abstracting his concept of history. On this reading, Marx's critique of political economy asks about the historical preconditions of the universality that classical economists took to be eternal. Read the original if you want a compact, critical re-reading of Lukács on totality and the Hegel–Marx relation in the philosophy of history.
quoteEn: Rather, this totality-dimension of history manifests itself precisely as the "mode of givenness" of phenomena.
quoteZh: 毋宁说，历史的这种总体性维度正是作为诸现象的“给出方式”而展现自身的

t: The three-dimensional historical foundations of historical materialism
zh: 历史唯物主义的三维历史底蕴
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), posted 2024-12-17
paras: This short commentary asks what makes historical materialism a "total" conception of history rather than a mere method of historiography. Jin argues that Marx and Engels inherited and transcended the totalizing tradition of "general philosophy of history" represented by Hegel. By "returning the content of history to history", grounding it in the productive practice of "real individuals", they produced a scientific answer to the question of history in general. Jin contends that this total view rests on three dimensions.

The article is organised around three paired relations: natural history and human history (the dimension of content), past and future (time), and national history and world history (space). Each section draws on Marx and Engels, chiefly The German Ideology, Engels's account of nature's evolution, the late writings on Russia and the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism, and a brief citation of E. H. Carr. Jin describes the pieces as forming a single, unified, diverse and open whole.

On the first dimension, Jin argues that natural and human history are structurally parallel both externally (both display diverse, mutually conditioned forms) and internally (both are governed by laws grounded in the material exchange between humans and nature). Under capitalism, Jin says, human history seems to move blindly like natural history, and this is the "alienation" that must be overcome through the active practice of historical subjects. On the second, the author holds that historical materialism links "interpretation–critique–prediction" through a "practical reflection" that works backwards from developed forms, and ties history's direction to the real movement of communism and the contradictions between productive forces and relations of production. On the third, Jin reads Marx and Engels as moving beyond a Eurocentric view of history: the diversity of national paths, including Russia's, does not negate the laws of world history, since everything depends on concrete historical conditions.

Jin concludes that this practice-based "grand view of history" is an important intellectual resource for the Communist Party of China in governing the country. It is said to fit the theme of the Party's century of history and to help Marxism guide Chinese modernization and the building of a new form of human civilization. The author also links it to adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a compact, textbook-style statement of how contemporary Chinese scholars present the historical, temporal and spatial structure of historical materialism.
quoteEn: In the dimension of historical time, historical materialism is a future-oriented philosophy: it grasps the laws of history as a whole in social practice and assesses historical trends through scientific method, uniting scientific rigour with foresight.
quoteZh: 历史唯物主义在历史时间维度上是面向未来的哲学，既在社会实践中实现对历史规律的总体性把握，又通过科学的方法研判历史发展的趋势，是科学性与预见性的统一。

glossary.explanation: Official Party concept for China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to contemporary circumstances.
A phrase used in Party discourse for viewing events within long-term and broad historical trends. Here the author derives it from the total conception of history in historical materialism.
Marx's metaphor, used in his late writings on Russia, for the possibility of a country reaching socialism without passing through the full capitalist stage.

t: From quantitative accumulation to qualitative leap: the generative logic of "new quality productive forces"
zh: 量变到质变：“新质生产力”的生成性逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Network (cssn.cn), posted on marxism.cass.cn, 17 December 2024
paras: Taking as its starting point Xi Jinping's remarks in Heilongjiang in September 2023, this short commentary asks how the concept of new quality productive forces came about. Sun and Ma define the term as a new type of productive force that differs from traditional ones, is led by scientific and technological innovation, breaks with traditional growth paths and meets the requirements of high-quality development. They argue that the concept has a "generative logic" that can be read through the dialectic of quantitative accumulation and qualitative leap.

The article is organised in three parts: the feasibility of the concept (quantitative accumulation), its inevitability (qualitative leap) and its reality (the unity of gradual change and leaps). It begins with the Marxist three-element account of productive forces and traces Party thinking on them from Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping through Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao to Xi Jinping. It then draws on statistics on education, agricultural mechanisation and industrial output.

In the authors' account, reform and opening up expanded all three elements of productive forces: labour, means of labour and objects of labour. They cite figures such as 99 million graduates from higher education since 1978, a higher-education system with more than 44.3 million students, and China ranking first in 220 of more than 500 major industrial products. The authors present the successive industrial revolutions and the current digital and information revolution as the source of a qualitative leap, with innovation as the key to moving from "quantity" to "quality". They treat the new development philosophy and the 20th Party Congress (2022) emphasis on technological self-reliance as the policy conditions for this shift.

The authors conclude that developing new quality productive forces requires three things. These are growth of the real economy, with technology converted into actual productive capacity; a leading role for innovation, which means fostering strategic emerging and future industries such as quantum information, gene technology and hydrogen energy; and the upgrading of traditional industries, which they say make up over 80 per cent of manufacturing, through deep integration of digital technology and the real economy. They claim the concept enriches and develops the Marxist theory of productive forces. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars link the Party's productive-forces tradition to the new quality productive forces concept using the quantity–quality dialectic.
quoteEn: The "new" in new quality productive forces lies in renewing traditional industries and giving them fresh vitality.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的“新”在于对传统产业的推陈出新，使之重新焕发新活力。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023. It refers to productive forces driven by technological innovation rather than by resource inputs, and it has become central to official economic discourse.
An official goal, stressed since the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting from high-speed growth to growth based on efficiency, innovation and better structure.
The five principles of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, first set out at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2015.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: Grasping the inner unity of the dialectical view of contradiction and the systems concept
zh: 深刻领悟矛盾观与系统观念的内在统一性
source: China Social Sciences Network (中国社会科学网), 2024
paras: This short article, published in December 2024, asks how the Marxist view of contradiction and the systems concept (系统观念) relate. The authors argue that the two are not different ideas but possess an inner unity. They hold that the dialectical view of contradiction stresses the unity of opposites in the world, while the systems concept, which they trace to natural philosophy, stresses wholeness, structure, levels, openness and self-organisation.

The article builds its case in two parts. The first examines the systematicity of contradiction and the contradictoriness of systems, drawing on Mao Zedong's writings and on Xi Jinping's statements about the systems concept. The second traces how each concept has been inherited and developed, from Marx, Engels and Lenin through Mao's On Contradiction to Xi Jinping in the new era. The authors also cite some scholarly literature in support.

The central move is a two-way relation. Contradiction is systemic: following Mao, a large entity contains many interlinked contradictions, among which one principal contradiction plays the leading role, so the authors read Mao's principal-contradiction thesis as a foundational and original contribution to the systems concept. Systems are contradictory: Xi's formulation requires attention to principal and secondary contradictions and combines the "two-point" and "focal" approaches, which the authors read as showing the systems concept to be dialectical. The authors add that the systems concept is the unity of a worldview and a methodology.

On inheritance, the authors say Marx, Engels, Lenin and Mao held rich systemic ideas but never named the systems concept. They credit Xi Jinping with first stating it explicitly and building it into a theoretical system. They interpret its worldview as three unified levels: an ecological-civilisation systems concept for the human–nature contradiction, a community-with-a-shared-future systems concept for human society, and a people-centred systems concept for the principal social contradiction of the new era. The authors caution against clinging to textbook versions of contradiction or copying natural-philosophy systems thinking. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars tie Xi Jinping's systems concept to Mao's theory of contradiction and to the new-era principal contradiction.
quoteEn: In our view, the contradictoriness of systems in essence deepens our understanding of the unity of opposites in the interaction of a system's constituent elements, and likewise our understanding of the imbalance in their mutual relations.
quoteZh: 我们认为，系统的矛盾性实质上是深化了对系统结构中诸构成要素相互作用的对立统一性认识，同时也深化了对系统结构中诸构成要素相互关系的不平衡性认识。

glossary.explanation: A way of thinking that treats things as interconnected wholes with structure and levels. Xi Jinping has made it a methodological principle in Party theory, and Chinese scholars present it as part of Marxist dialectics.

A concept developed in Mao Zedong's On Contradiction: among many contradictions in a process, one plays the leading, decisive role. Party documents also use it to define the central problem of each historical stage.

glossary.pinyin: liǎng diǎn lùn yǔ zhòngdiǎn lùn
glossary.explanation: A methodological pair in Chinese Marxist discourse: consider both aspects of a contradiction (two-point) while concentrating on the key aspect (focal). Xi Jinping calls for their unity.
A 1937 philosophical essay by Mao Zedong on dialectical materialism. It is treated in China as a core text of Mao's thought on universality and particularity of contradiction.

t: Deepening understanding of the theoretical innovation in upholding a systems approach
zh: 深化认识坚持系统观念的理论创新
paras: Responding to Xi Jinping's call to study the foundational theoretical results contained in the Party's new concepts and judgements, Leng Shuqing examines the injunction to uphold a systems approach (系统观念), one of the "six musts" of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article argues that this principle amounts to a basic and original theoretical innovation across all three component parts of Marxism, and that it is a major marker of the Thought's systematic and theoretical character.

The article has three sections. The first traces the inheritance and innovation of the Marxist view of contradiction and its methodology, from Marx through Mao Zedong to Xi. The second extends the claim to Marxist political economy and scientific socialism. The third presents the systems approach as a major principled theoretical achievement of Xi Jinping Thought and as a paradigm innovation in Marxist philosophy.

Leng's central move is to argue that, although Marx, Engels, Lenin and Mao's accounts of contradiction already carry systems-related meaning (Mao's analysis of layered contradictions and of socialist society as a system of relations, for example), only Xi explicitly urges viewing and resolving social contradictions from a systems standpoint and abstracts the systems approach into a worldview and methodology. Leng proposes the concept of a "contradiction-systems view" and treats the principal contradiction of the new era as the logical starting point of both Xi Thought and the systems approach. On this basis the author reads the new development philosophy and the turn in political economy towards "becoming strong" as expressions of systems thinking, and sees the systems approach as renewing the socialist theory of the principal contradiction. A further claim is that the approach fuses Marxist dialectics with systems science, producing categories such as systems thinking, bottom-line thinking and holistic advancement.

Leng concludes that the contradiction-systems view is a major result of Xi Jinping Thought, which is described as contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. It is said to provide the worldview and methodology for building a disciplinary, academic and discourse system with Chinese characteristics. The author calls for deeper study of Xi's statements on the systems approach. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar of the systems approach places this concept within the Party's official theoretical framework and within the Marxist tradition of the doctrine of contradiction.
quoteEn: Upholding the systems approach is in fact the systems outlook for scientifically grasping and effectively resolving the principal contradiction of the new era.
quoteZh: 坚持系统观念实际上即是科学把握与有效化解新时代社会主要矛盾的系统观念

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
One of the "six musts" of Xi Jinping Thought. It calls for seeing things as interconnected wholes and balancing the overall and the partial, the short and long term, and so on.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Official summary of the worldview, methodology and standpoint of Xi Jinping Thought: put the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, uphold fundamental principles and break new ground, a problem-oriented approach, a systems approach, and a worldwide perspective.

glossary.en: principal contradiction of the new era
glossary.literal: main social contradiction of the new era
glossary.explanation: The Party's 19th Congress (2017) formulation: the contradiction between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
The set of five concepts (innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development) put forward in 2015 to guide economic and social development.

t: Does the "production" of artificial intelligence create value?
zh: 人工智能的“生产”创造价值吗
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), posted 2024-12-17
paras: Li Yaogeng asks whether artificial intelligence (AI) can create value, and what this means for Marx's labour theory of value. The commentary argues that the theory still supplies the basic framework for understanding labour's role in value creation, even as AI challenges traditional assumptions.

The piece sorts AI into three types, weak, strong and super AI, and considers how each intervenes in production, labour and social relations. It also notes legal, political and ethical questions raised by each type.

Li holds that weak AI, found in automated production lines and smart tools, is an extension of human labour and a new instrument of production. It raises efficiency but leaves labour as the core of value creation and workers as its subject. Strong AI, which Li treats as hypothetical, could think, learn and innovate, and might prompt a reassessment of labour's contribution. Li still sees it as working toward human-set goals under human leadership. Super AI, by contrast, is imagined as surpassing human intelligence and acting beyond human control. In Li's account it could take over resource allocation, upend existing relations of production and leave humans as passive recipients rather than subjects, challenging Marx's ideal of free and all-round human development.

Li concludes that Marx's labour theory of value remains an important basis for understanding labour change in the AI era, but must be explored anew in changed conditions. The author calls for balancing technological progress with social interests and for vigilance about the risks of super AI. Read the original if you want a brief, schematic Marxist classification of AI types and their implications for labour and value.
quoteEn: Although weak AI raises efficiency in production, it has not fundamentally changed how labour value is generated; labour remains the core of value creation, and workers remain its subject.
quoteZh: 弱人工智能虽然在生产中提高了效率，但并未根本改变劳动价值的生成方式，劳动仍然是价值创造的核心，劳动者仍然是创造价值的主体。

glossary.explanation: Marx's theory that the value of commodities derives from socially necessary human labour. Chinese Marxist writers treat it as a basic principle of political economy.
In Marxist theory, the social relations people enter into in producing goods, including ownership of the means of production and the distribution of resources.

t: The labour theory of value in the age of artificial intelligence
zh: 人工智能时代的劳动价值论
source: China Social Sciences Net, China Social Sciences Today
paras: Does the spread of unmanned factories and the rise of general artificial intelligence make Marx's labour theory of value obsolete? Qin Zizhong, writing in a newspaper commentary, rejects the claim that the core thesis that labour is the only source of value has been broken. In Qin's view, this reading both misunderstands Marx and lacks a careful look at how AI is developing.

The piece first uses Marx's dual character of commodities and labour, and his category of the collective worker, to explain unmanned production. It then turns to new questions for the theory: the dominance of mental and digital labour, Sakaiya Taichi's knowledge-value theory, and the redefinition of the working day. Finally it separates two stages of AI, before and after a threshold of autonomous consciousness.

Qin argues that AI has moved from automated machines needing on-site workers, through remote control over the internet, to a stage where programmers, data engineers and internet users together form an integrated collective worker. Below the threshold, AI is a tool and its work extends human labour, so humans still create the value. Because leisure is also digitised, Qin proposes a working day with a third segment, leisure labour time, whose value is ignored or partly appropriated free by data and platform companies. Above the threshold, an autonomous AI subject would become another source of value, which would challenge Marx's thesis.

Qin sees two possible responses: abandoning the thesis, which Qin says is not necessarily Marxist, or reading labour as performed by multiple subjects, including AI, which Qin calls Marxist or compatible with Marxism. The author calls for inheriting and developing the theory under new historical conditions rather than accepting it dogmatically. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist argument on how digital labour and possible AI subjects bear on the labour theory of value.
quoteEn: What creates value is not the labour of artificial intelligence but human labour.
quoteZh: 创造价值的不是人工智能的劳动，而是人类的劳动。

glossary.explanation: Marx's category (Gesamtarbeiter) for the combined body of workers whose varied functions together produce a commodity, so that an individual need not manipulate the object directly to count as a productive labourer.

t: The generalisation of artificial intelligence and new questions for the labour theory of value
zh: 人工智能的通用化与劳动价值论的新论题
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), December 2024
paras: Tu Liangchuan asks what the generalisation of artificial intelligence (AI) means for the Marxist labour theory of value. Writing in a Chinese social science newspaper in late 2024, the author starts from Xi Jinping's remark that AI is a major driver of the new round of technological and industrial revolution. Tu argues that general-purpose AI has moved from replacing labour with machines to replacing the labour subject itself, and that this raises new questions about value, ownership of output and the distribution of wealth. The article's answer is that general AI does not negate labour as the source of value, but that it forces a rethinking of how value, ownership and wealth are organised.

The piece is built in three sections. The first treats generalisation as a 'replacement technology' that changes how labour creates value. The second considers AI's 'human-like labour' and the problem of establishing ownership (确权) of social products. The third examines AI as a 'quasi-subject' and the question of who enjoys the wealth it produces. Tu lists social problems the author associates with general AI, including 'unmanned factories', a 'useless class', digitised forms of labour and a new alienation.

Tu's central claim is that general AI is an accumulation of past human labour and technical knowledge, not a new source of value. Its human-like labour carries use-value into products and may increase use-value, but it does not originate purposes or develop genuinely new use-values. For this reason AI cannot be the subject that holds rights over products, and owning AI is not a sufficient ground for claiming them, because only labourers who realise real innovation are the basis of innovative use-value. As a 'quasi-subject', AI makes means of labour into autonomous machines and removes workers from production. In Tu's reading, 'technological unemployment' and the 'useless class' stem from the capitalist logic of valorisation and of fixed capital displacing people, not from any inevitability of technology.

Tu concludes that AI, as an objectified product of human essential powers, should return to humanity and become 'common wealth' under socialism. Only in this way, the author holds, can its development be economically just, politically reasonable and serving of free human development. Read the original if you want a short example of how a Chinese Marxist philosopher defends the labour theory of value against claims that AI creates value or deserves ownership.
quoteEn: AI cannot be the subject of rights over products, because only labourers who achieve genuine innovation are the ontological basis and the socio-economic principle of innovative use-value.
quoteZh: 人工智能不能作为确权的主体，因为只有实现真正创新的劳动者才是创新性使用价值的存在论根据和社会经济原则。

glossary.explanation: The term means establishing or confirming legal and economic rights over a thing. The article uses it for the question of who holds rights over products made with AI. The summary renders it as 'ownership'.
The Marxist theory that the value of commodities derives from socially necessary human labour. The article tests it against general AI.

t: New orientations in Western critiques of philanthrocapitalism and a theoretical assessment
zh: 西方慈善资本主义批判的新取向及理论评析
paras: Tao examines philanthrocapitalism, the idea first formulated in The Economist in 2006 that private philanthropy should operate like profit-seeking capital markets. Since the 2008 financial crisis it has been promoted as a remedy for capitalism's social ills. The article argues that Western left-wing scholars have criticised it comprehensively but remain limited by their class standpoint, and that a Marxist view of charity is needed to grasp its contradictions.

The article has three parts. The first traces the economic and social background: the rise of a new generation of wealthy elites in the information-technology era, the spread of neoliberal values into charity, and doubts about traditional charity under the welfare state. The second surveys critiques by Western left-wing and critical scholars, including Slavoj Žižek, Robert Reich, Linsey McGoey and Wilson Japhy. The third assesses those critiques from a Marxist standpoint.

Tao groups the newer critiques into three lines. They attack market-oriented commercialisation of charity as wasteful and exclusionary of citizens. They argue that philanthropic capital deepens inequality between people and sustains a 'colonial–dependency' order globally. And they hold that the logic of capital is opposed to the charitable ideal, citing tax avoidance through foundations and the claim that donors give back only a fraction of what they accumulate. Tao then identifies four weaknesses in these critiques. They stay with exchange and distribution rather than tracing charitable funds back to surplus value produced by labour. They hold the consequences to account without reaching private ownership of the means of production. They weaken the class character of charity through pluralist class views. And they neglect socialist public welfare and offer no workable proposals for citizens' philanthropy.

Tao concludes that Western left scholarship is reactive, slow to respond and tends to demolish without building, with a markedly academic style. Tao calls for research to rest on the labour theory of value, the ownership of the means of production and Marxist class analysis. It should also take up the philanthropic role of working people and Marx and Engels's ideas about socialist public welfare. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist assessment of Western left critiques of billionaire philanthropy, with many references to English-language scholarship.
quoteEn: Western left-wing scholars must ground their research and critique at the level of ownership of the means of production, and see through to the fundamental internal contradictions of capitalist private ownership.
quoteZh: 西方左翼学者必须将研究与批判落脚到生产资料所有制层面，从根本上透视资本主义私有制的内在矛盾。

glossary.explanation: A term popularised by The Economist in 2006 and by Bishop and Green's book. It refers to wealthy donors applying business and investment methods to philanthropy.

t: Digital socialism: problem field and theoretical lineages
zh: 数字社会主义：问题域与理论流脉
paras: Pan Na asks how "digital socialism" arose as a concept, how Western left scholars took it over, and what Marxists should make of it. The article argues that the term began as a Silicon Valley ideological device and was later reclaimed by the Western left as a proposed alternative to capitalism.
