In Pan's assessment, this left version is valuable as a constructive and cross-disciplinary body of work, but remains a twenty-first-century utopian socialism that cannot replace capitalism. It was published in Open Times in 2024.

The article first traces the term from Kevin Kelly's 2009 Wired essay "The New Socialism" to his later "protopia" narrative and the 2016 "techlash". It then follows the left debate over "technofeudalism", involving Kotkin, Varoufakis, Durand, Dean, Morozov, Ström and Brenner. The central part sets out three left routes: reviving the socialist calculation debate (Morozov, Benanav, Rief on Polanyi); returning to Marx's "fragment on machines" (Virno, Peters, Fuchs, Fischli, Muldoon); and "blockchain socialism", which either redesigns cryptocurrency or tries to abolish money. Pan then assesses their value, limits and lessons.

Pan reads Kelly's "socialism without a state" as an anti-statist cover for tech oligarchs' interests, and finds the left models marked by the same neglect of the state. In Pan's view they omit the question of establishing proletarian state power, citing Lenin on the dictatorship of the proletariat. They also ignore Marx's "two never's" (the conditions for a new social formation must mature within the old), because they rely on digital technology alone and are designed for single countries or regions. Pan sees the Fuchs-style approach as continuing Italian autonomist readings of the "fragment on machines" and as sliding into an "ethicist politics of the subject". Pan nonetheless credits the left with linking critique to construction, theory to practice, and with drawing on many disciplines.

Pan concludes that Western left digital socialism cannot transform capitalism and is confined to marginal social experiments. Pan still draws three lessons for non-Western countries: it supports the search for a new form of human civilisation, it offers meso- and micro-level ideas on technology and governance for China's digital construction, and it gives an internal view of capitalism's digital crisis. Pan calls for China to build an autonomous body of knowledge on how digital technology and scientific socialism can empower each other. Read the original if you want a detailed, Chinese Marxist map of the Western left's digital-socialism debates and their reception in China.
quoteEn: The construction paths for digital socialism proposed by the Western left overreach the historical stage in how they understand and seek to transform the capitalist social formation they live in, and lack theoretical thoroughness and scientific method.
quoteZh: 西方左翼提出的数字社会主义建构路径，对其所处的资本主义社会形态的认识和改造超越了历史阶段，缺乏理论的彻底性和方法的科学性。

glossary.en: a new form of human civilisation
glossary.explanation: A Party formulation, associated with Chinese modernization, for a civilisational path presented as an alternative to the Western model.

Marx's 1859 Preface claim that no social formation perishes before its productive forces are fully developed, and that new relations of production never appear before their material conditions mature.
The classical Marxist-Leninist term for working-class state power during the transition from capitalism to communism.

t: Re-examining the idea of "labour ownership" in the context of the critique of political economy
zh: 重审政治经济学批判语境中的“劳动所有权”观念
source: Studies on the Discipline of Marxist Theory, 2024 no. 9
paras: Sun Liang takes up Locke's proposition that labour grounds property, which the article calls "labour ownership", and asks how Marx's critique of political economy dismantles it. The thesis is that Marx separates two meanings of the idea: the identity of labour and ownership, and labour appearing as negated ownership. This distinction, the author argues, takes Marx beyond both Lockean liberal political philosophy and the classical political economy of Adam Smith.

The article is built in four parts, drawing on Marx's 1861–63 manuscripts, the Grundrisse and Capital. It starts with the Physiocrats and Smith and the contradiction between two determinations of exchange-value. It then turns to the way ownership becomes the appropriation of others' labour, and to the critique of fetishism as Marx's method. A short conclusion follows. Rubin and Locke are the main secondary points of reference.

Sun reads Smith's wavering between the two determinations of value as an intuition of the contradiction that appears once labour and capital exchange. Smith could not resolve it, the author says, because he took the worker to sell labour rather than labour-power and did not grasp the historicity of the capitalist mode of production. For Marx, once labour-power is a commodity its owner no longer controls its use. Equivalent exchange in the market is then only a form, and the real process is the appropriation of unpaid labour. Sun holds that apologists confuse two kinds of private property, one resting on the producer's own labour and one on exploiting others'. They also conflate abstract and concrete labour and so blur social and natural relations. The author treats this as fetishism, which naturalises a historical social form, and cites Marx's account of primitive accumulation as a refutation.

Sun concludes that Marx's critique keeps categories and reality in contradiction, whereas political economists close the gap and make categories into defences of the existing order. The author claims that showing how labour ownership turns into its opposite under capitalism undermines the foundations of classical political economy and Western political philosophy. The article also presents this as a way into Marx's political philosophy and its contemporary value. Read the original if you want a close, text-based account of how Marx's critique of political economy engages Locke's and Smith's theories of property.
quoteEn: "Labour ownership" is a "juridical relation" founded on the capitalist mode of production, the juridical relation of capital's appropriation of labour, so the social form of labour is the basis for understanding it.
quoteZh: “劳动所有权”是在资本主义生产方式基础之上的“法权关系”，是资本对劳动占有的法权关系，故而，劳动的社会形式是理解这个法权关系的基础。

glossary.explanation: The Lockean idea that a person's labour, mixed with natural things, makes them that person's property. The article treats it as a category that Marx's critique shows turning into its opposite under capitalism.
Marx's project, with Capital as its main work, of criticising the categories of classical political economy and exposing the social relations they conceal.
Marx's term for the way social relations among people appear as properties of things such as commodities and money. The article uses it as a method for criticising labour ownership.

t: Does artificial intelligence challenge the labour theory of value?
zh: 人工智能挑战了劳动价值论吗
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), December 2024
paras: Zhou Jiaxin takes up a question that has followed recent advances in artificial intelligence: whether Marx's labour theory of value still holds when machines appear to replace people and when scholars speak of "immaterial labour" and "digital labour". The author's answer is that AI poses no challenge to the theory. In the digital economy, Zhou argues, the theory is not outdated but remains the scientific tool for analysing the social and historical effects of AI.

This short commentary, published in a Chinese social science newspaper, has two parts. The first clarifies what the labour theory of value is, and the second applies it to labour under AI. Zhou notes that Marx himself hardly used the term. It took shape in the later nineteenth century, after the marginal revolution, in opposition to utility theories of value. Zhou also separates Marx's theory from Ricardo's and from Western economics, citing Samuelson as an example.

Zhou's central claim is that the theory has to be read through historical materialism and the dual character of labour, not as the bare claim that labour creates value. In this reading, value is a historically specific proportion of exchange determined by the mode of production, and commodity relations express relations of production. Applied to AI, this yields three points. AI is essentially a complex and efficient machine, so questions about it become questions about changes in the mode of material production. Labels such as "immaterial labour" and "digital labour" should be treated with caution, because coding, designing machines and using AI are all labour, differing in socially necessary labour time. The relation between mental and manual labour, "productive consumption" and "play labour", and the data-annotation and hardware labour behind AI should be analysed through concrete social and economic relations. Zhou treats strong AI and machine consciousness as closer to science fiction. Control by data and algorithms is, in Zhou's view, a new version of the "abstract forces dominating people" that Marx already analysed. The problem of machines replacing workers dates from the Industrial Revolution and cannot be solved by Luddite machine-breaking.

Zhou concludes that AI is not a "myth" but a machine system, and that Marx's theory grasps real modes of production and social formations rather than starting from anthropological premises or abstract concepts. Instead of dwelling on replacement and control, Zhou urges more active exploration of how to develop the digital economy and form new quality productive forces, where Marxist political economy will show its theoretical appeal. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese Marxist rebuttal of the claim that AI and digital labour undermine the labour theory of value.
quoteEn: Artificial intelligence is not a "myth" but a complex, systematic and efficient tool, or a system of machines.
quoteZh: 人工智能不是一个“神话”，而是一个复杂、系统、高效的工具，或者说一种机器体系。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, such as digital technology and AI.

The theory that the value of commodities is determined by the socially necessary labour time needed to produce them. Chinese Marxist economics treats Marx's version as the foundation of his theory of surplus value.
The Marxist theory that material production and its social relations determine historical development. The author uses it as the basis for reading the labour theory of value.

t: The innovative development of the Marxist theory of productive forces in contemporary China
zh: 马克思主义生产力理论在当代中国的创新发展
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2024, Zhang Yu asks how the Marxist theory of productive forces has been developed in contemporary China. The article argues that Xi Jinping's discourse on productive forces, and above all his concept of new quality productive forces, has raised the Party's understanding of the laws of productive-force development to a new level. Zhang presents it as an original theoretical result of contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy and a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece is a theoretical commentary organised in nine thematic sections. Each pairs classical positions from Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping with Xi's statements and a closing judgement on what the statements add. The topics are the productive-force criterion of social progress, the socialist purpose of development, the elements of productive forces, the technological and industrial revolution, scientific and technological innovation, ecology, industrial innovation, reform of production relations, and the advanced character of new quality productive forces.

Zhang's central claim is that each element of Xi's discourse develops a corresponding Marxist principle. Productive forces remain the decisive standard of social development, and their aim is to meet the people's growing needs for a better life, in contrast to capitalist monopoly of their fruits. New quality productive forces are defined as a leap in workers, means of labour, objects of labour and their optimal combination, with data counted as a new factor of production. Scientific and technological innovation is described as their core element, and ecological protection is said to be protection of productive forces, so that they are inherently green productive forces.

Zhang adds that technological innovation must be integrated with industrial innovation, supported by a complete industrial system and a very large market. He also argues that continued reform must make production relations fit new productive forces, drawing on socialism's institutional strengths such as the new type of whole-nation system. The article concludes that new quality productive forces are essentially advanced productive forces, characterised by the new technological revolution and by informatisation, digitalisation and intelligence. In Zhang's account they form the material and technological basis of Chinese modernization and high-quality development. Read the original if you want a concise official-line overview of how Party theorists link Xi's new quality productive forces to the classical Marxist theory of productive forces.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are in essence advanced productive forces.
quoteZh: 新质生产力本质是先进生产力。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023–24 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and higher productivity, especially digital and green technologies. It became a central theme of Chinese economic policy discourse.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.
An official economic goal since 2017, stressing innovation, efficiency, green growth and better living standards over speed alone.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary developments.

glossary.en: the new type of whole-nation system
glossary.explanation: The official term for mobilising state, market and social resources nationally to achieve major scientific and technological breakthroughs.

t: On the actualisation of historical materialism
zh: 论历史唯物主义的现实化
paras: Zhou Luping asks how historical materialism acquires its vitality as a practical philosophy for changing the old world. The article, a short piece in Guangming Daily (28 October 2024), argues that this "actualisation" (xianshihua) runs through the whole of Marx and Engels's thought and should be grasped as a whole. Historical materialism, in Zhou's account, goes beyond the rational constraints of idealist philosophy by engaging with and criticising the capitalist world.

The article is organised around three dimensions of actualisation: philosophical transformation, political reflection and economic critique. Zhou draws on texts from the mid-1840s, including the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology, then on Marx and Engels's political writings on France, Germany and the United States. The article closes with Capital and its manuscripts. It also contrasts Marx with Proudhon as a thinker whose critique of capital stayed ethical.

On the philosophical side, Zhou argues that the 1845 philosophical revolution dismantled speculative metaphysics and put practice and sensuous activity in its place. It also shifted the study of history to productive forces and forms of intercourse, property forms and the history of industry and commerce, which points towards communist emancipation. On the political side, Zhou reads works such as The Class Struggles in France and The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte as showing that bourgeois revolutions were driven by material interests, that class struggle was the bourgeoisie's means of establishing rule, and that political movements remained subordinate to the movement of capital. On the economic side, Zhou contends that Capital turns historical materialism into a theoretical weapon against capitalism's internal contradictions, undermines the claim that private property is rational, and points to the free and all-round development of the human being.

Zhou concludes that Marx set himself apart from other thinkers by continually externalising his ideas, so that historical materialism criticises the modern world in practical terms. In this reading, philosophical change, political reflection and economic critique together lead to the real destination of human emancipation. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language statement of how a Guangming Daily author frames historical materialism as a unified, practice-oriented critique of capital.
quoteEn: The actualisation of historical materialism consists in criticising the modern world in actual terms through philosophical transformation, political reflection and economic critique, ultimately pointing to the real destination of human emancipation.
quoteZh: 历史唯物主义的现实化是以哲学变革、政治反思与经济批判等方式，对现代世界加以现实化批判，最终指向人类解放之现实化归宿。

t: The theoretical value of the "small bundle" manuscripts in the "Feuerbach" chapter of The German Ideology
zh: 《德意志意识形态》“费尔巴哈”章 小束手稿的理论价值
paras: This short article, first published in Guangming Daily on 28 October 2024, asks what theoretical weight should be given to the "small bundle" manuscripts of the "Feuerbach" chapter of The German Ideology. Wang Guoqin and Wang Daiyue argue that these manuscripts, though unfinished and repeatedly revised, were written later than the rest of the chapter and therefore show Marx and Engels's thinking at a more mature point. They claim the manuscripts bring out the subjective dimension of historical materialism, develop its "realistic" spirit, and help settle philological disputes over the text.

The authors begin with the structure of the chapter in the new historical-critical edition (MEGA2, vol. I/5, 2017). It contains the "large bundle" of paginated main manuscripts and a "small bundle", a term the authors attribute to the Japanese scholar Hiromatsu Wataru. The small bundle comprises three chapter openings and two fragments, which the editors date to roughly May–July 1846. The authors then take three themes in turn: the subjective dimension, the realistic spirit of historical materialism, and the philological controversies.

The central claim is that earlier scholarship read historical materialism mainly through its objective side, namely productive forces, forms of intercourse and civil society. The small bundle adds the concept of "real individuals". The authors say Marx and Engels, unlike Feuerbach, separate humans from animals by material production rather than by consciousness, and distinguish individuals from one another by the material conditions of production they inherit. On this reading, productive forces are the objectified powers of real individuals, so without them neither productive forces nor relations of production exist. The authors add that the fragments use "definite" five times and trace the development of ownership forms, which they take to show that historical materialism starts from empirical reality and not from abstract dogma. They cite Marx's resistance to universalising his account of capitalism's origins and his cautious reply to Vera Zasulich as examples.

On the philological questions, the authors argue that the sequence of the three chapter openings shows Marx and Engels's thought clarifying. The "real individual" appears in the second opening, which they read as a response to Stirner. The deletion of a passage naming Feuerbach as the main target in the third opening suggests, in their view, that Feuerbach lost his central place as the object of critique. They conclude that the small bundle summarises the results of work on the text and deepens its account of historical materialism. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-language account of how MEGA2's dating of these manuscripts is used to argue for a subject-centred reading of historical materialism.
quoteEn: The small bundle contains not only a more mature statement of the abstract principles of historical materialism, but also a first realisation of historical materialism in concrete terms.
quoteZh: 小束手稿不仅存在着对唯物史观抽象原理更加成熟的表述，而且初步实现了唯物史观的现实化。

t: Better balancing, promoting and unifying efficiency and fairness
zh: 更好实现效率与公平相兼顾、相促进、相统一
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 25 October 2024, takes up the relationship between efficiency and fairness (equity). Chen Dongfang argues that, in order to deepen reform comprehensively and advance Chinese modernization, the two must be handled so that they are balanced, mutually reinforcing and unified, which in turn raises the balance, coordination and inclusiveness of development.

The piece begins from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and a statement by Xi Jinping that Chinese modernization must create higher efficiency than capitalism while also safeguarding social fairness more effectively. It then proceeds through three headed sections: institutional reform, high-quality development, and common prosperity.

Chen reads the three terms "balancing", "promoting" and "unifying" as follows: neither economic growth nor fairness may be sacrificed to the other; fairness rests on efficiency while efficiency takes fairness as its purpose and driving force; and the two must be organically combined. High-quality development is presented as the material base, since it joins "making the cake bigger" with "dividing it well", through higher total factor productivity and a more equal distribution of income. Common prosperity is the route to seeking the best balance point, through better public services, a larger share of labour income, employment and social security measures, and coordinated primary, secondary and tertiary distribution, alongside innovation, anti-monopoly measures and the orderly development of capital.

Chen concludes that efficiency is the material precondition of fairness and fairness is the guarantee of efficiency. The author calls for balanced handling of both so that the fruits of modernization reach all people more fairly, which the article describes as a distinctive strength of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party commentary in late 2024 interprets Xi Jinping's formula on efficiency and fairness and links it to reform policy.
quoteEn: Efficiency is the material precondition of fairness, and fairness is a strong guarantee of efficiency; the two promote and complement each other.
quoteZh: 效率是公平的物质前提，公平是效率的有力保障，两者相互促进、相辅相成。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's model of modernization, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western paths.
An official economic goal, stressed since 2017, that favours quality, efficiency and innovation over raw growth in output.
A long-standing socialist goal that the Party has given greater weight since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing narrower gaps in income and public services.

t: Further deepening reform comprehensively must follow the "six adherences" principles
zh: 全面深化改革必须遵循“六个坚持”重大原则
paras: This commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today on 29 October 2024, interprets the six principles set out by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) for further deepening reform comprehensively. Hong and Zhang argue that the "six adherences" are both a scientific summary of experience since reform and opening up, especially in the new era, and a major result of the Party's deepening grasp of the laws governing reform. In their view, the principles strengthen the scientific character, foresight, initiative and creativity of reform and help it advance steadily over the long term.

The article is organised as a sequence of short sections, one for each principle: the Party's overall leadership; a people-centred approach; upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground; institution-building as the main thread; law-based governance in all respects; and a systems perspective. Each section restates the principle, mostly in the language of Party documents, and draws on statements by Xi Jinping.

On leadership, the authors state that Party leadership is the defining feature and greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the fundamental guarantee of reform. They tie this to the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and link it to the direction of Chinese modernization. On the people-centred principle, they say the people are the starting point and value aim of reform, which must serve fairness, justice and common prosperity. On institutions, they hold that institutional advantage is a country's greatest advantage, and that reform should strengthen fundamental, basic and important institutions so that "Chinese institutions" produce better "Chinese governance". They also argue that reform and the rule of law must be unified: major reforms should have a legal basis, and proven reform experience should be turned into law. On the systems perspective, they say reform has reached a stage in which piecemeal adjustment will not work, and they name five relationships to balance: economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and development and security.

The authors conclude that the six principles together give guidance for pushing reform forward in a stable and lasting way. They treat the principles as interlocking: fundamentals such as Party leadership, Marxism and the socialist path must not waver, while reform proceeds boldly elsewhere. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars present the Third Plenum's guiding principles for reform and how they link them to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Reform has meaning only when it is carried out for the people; it has momentum only when it relies on the people.
quoteZh: 为了人民而改革，改革才有意义；依靠人民而改革，改革才有动力。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A formula from the Party's 2021 historical resolution, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
A Party goal of shared wealth for all the people, emphasised in recent years as a feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.literal: keeping to what is correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: An official formula calling for adherence to core political principles alongside innovation in practice.

glossary.literal: comprehensively governing the country according to law
glossary.explanation: A Party policy adopted in 2014 that stresses the rule of law as a means of governance under Party leadership.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: Using the systems perspective to keep further comprehensively deepening reform steady and far-reaching
zh: 以系统观念推动进一步全面深化改革行稳致远
paras: Shuang Chuanxue's commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 25 October 2024, takes up one of the six major principles for further comprehensively deepening reform set out by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): adhering to a systems perspective. Shuang argues that reform has entered deep waters, and that the more complex the situation, the more reform must be made systematic, integrated and coordinated.

The article has four parts. It first sets out the meaning of the systems perspective, then explains why further reform urgently needs it. It next lists five pairs of relationships that must be handled correctly, and closes with practical ways to strengthen conscious application of the principle.

In the first part, Shuang presents the systems perspective as an enrichment of the Marxist view of systems, grounded in materialist dialectics. Shuang also reads it as a lesson from the Party's long experience, from the New Democratic Revolution through socialist construction to reform and opening up, and as a basic thought and work method for the new journey. The case for urgency rests on three points: the general goal of improving the socialist system and modernizing national governance, the large list of risks and difficulties still to be resolved, and the growing interdependence of reforms across fields. The five relationships are economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and development and security. Shuang treats each as a dialectical unity in which the two sides condition one another and neither should be set against the other.

Shuang calls for stronger theoretical study of dialectical materialism, against mechanistic and dogmatic thinking. Shuang also calls for forward-looking thinking, planning for the whole, strategic layout and integrated advancement in practice. The systems perspective should run through the whole reform process, from policy formulation through implementation to evaluation and adjustment of results. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party theorists present the systems perspective as a methodological principle of the current reform agenda.
quoteEn: Adhering to a systems perspective is both a worldview and a methodology; it is the "bridge" and "boat" for solving problems, and has a distinct practical character.
quoteZh: 坚持系统观念既是世界观又是方法论，是解决问题的“桥”和“船”，具有鲜明的实践品格。

glossary.explanation: A way of thinking that treats things as interconnected wholes and requires overall planning and coordination. Party documents describe it as part of the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought and as one of the principles of further deepening reform.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de Èrshí Jiè Sān Zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A plenary meeting of the Central Committee held in July 2024. It adopted a decision on further comprehensively deepening reform.

t: A high-standard socialist market economy as an important guarantee for Chinese modernization
zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制是中国式现代化的重要保障
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2024, Hu Xiaopeng takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its call to build a "high-standard socialist market economy" by 2035. The article argues that this economic system is an important guarantee for Chinese modernization. In Hu's account it also develops and deepens the Party's theory of the market economy.

The commentary has three parts. The first places the concept in the Party's changing understanding of the market economy, from the post-1978 position that planning and market are both economic means to the 19th Central Committee's Fourth Plenum, which listed the socialist market economy among the basic economic systems. The second treats the government–market relationship as the core problem. The third ties the project to high-quality development as the first task of building a modern socialist country.

Hu's central claim is that "high standard" is a criterion both for how well the market works and for whether the system fits the basic socialist economic system. Citing Xi Jinping, Hu holds that the market's "invisible hand" cannot solve long-term underinvestment in basic research or negative externalities such as environmental damage. A high-standard system therefore asks more of the government's "visible hand", which should keep markets fair and orderly, be "lively but not chaotic", and be "free to flourish yet firmly managed". Hu adds that the system must be built on the rule of law, since the socialist market economy is "essentially a law-based economy".

For high-quality development, Hu proposes institution-building as the main thread. This includes the Two Unwaverings, a unified national market, better property rights, market access, exit and social credit systems, and further reform of state-owned enterprises. It also covers a better environment for private firms, high-level self-reliance in science and technology, and institutional opening-up that aligns with international high-standard trade rules and promotes a new development pattern of dual circulation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party theorists link the Third Plenum's market-economy goals to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Building a high-standard socialist market economy must revolve around the core question of handling the relationship between government and market.
quoteZh: 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制，必须围绕处理好政府和市场关系这个核心问题

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
Official term, prominent since 2017, for a growth model stressing quality, innovation and efficiency over speed alone. It is described as the first task of building a modern socialist country.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The system adopted in the 1990s that combines market allocation of resources with public ownership as the main body and Party-state guidance.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōng quánhuì
glossary.en: the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024)
glossary.explanation: The July 2024 meeting of the Central Committee that adopted a decision on further deepening reform comprehensively to advance Chinese modernization.

t: On building a high-standard socialist market economy
zh: 论构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制
paras: Li Yiping's commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 29 October 2024, takes up the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to "build a high-standard socialist market economy". Li argues that the meaning of "high-standard" can only be grasped by understanding how the socialist market economy developed and what its essential features are.

The piece has three parts. It first traces the history: Deng Xiaoping's affirmation that socialism and markets can be combined, the 14th Party Congress (1992) goal of letting the market play a basic role in resource allocation under state macro-control, and the Third Plenum of the 14th Central Committee's decision that made this concrete. It then defines a high-standard system, and finally lists four priorities drawn from the 2024 plenum.

In Li's account, such a system allocates resources more effectively. This requires improving the price mechanism so that prices reflect scarcity, and improving competition, which Li says drives innovation and the elimination of backward producers. It also requires a correct relationship between government and market: the government's "visible hand" must obey market laws, so that markets are both "lively" and "well regulated", with scientific, standardised oversight to prevent market failure.

Li names four tasks: protecting market entities through the Two Unwaverings, building a unified national market, improving basic market institutions (property rights, information disclosure, market access, bankruptcy and exit, credit systems), and forming a higher-level government–market relationship in which the market plays the decisive role. Read the original if you want a short, official-line outline of how the 2024 plenum's market-economy agenda is explained to a general Chinese readership.
quoteEn: The better coordinated the relationship between government and market, the more it is possible to be both "lively" and "well controlled".
quoteZh: 政府与市场的关系越协调，就越能实现既“放得活”又“管得住”。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula committing to unwaveringly consolidate and develop the public sector and unwaveringly encourage, support and guide the non-public sector.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The economic system adopted formally at the 14th Party Congress in 1992, combining market allocation of resources with public ownership and state macro-control.

t: Paths to building an autonomous knowledge system of Chinese humanistic economics
zh: 中国人文经济学自主知识体系的建构路径
paras: Han Xiping asks how China's theorists should build an autonomous knowledge system of "Chinese humanistic economics", a field prompted by Xi Jinping's remark that economies often thrive where culture is highly developed. The article, first published in Guangming Daily in October 2024, argues that this is an important responsibility for theorists in the new era. Its thesis is that culture and the economy are tightly linked, and that a theory grounded in Chinese culture and practice should make this link explicit.

The piece is a short commentary organised around five tasks. They are to clarify the people-centred purpose of economic development, to uncover cultural elements in growth, to summarise classic cases of humanistic support for the economy, to strengthen the economic force of Chinese culture, and to show the cultural function within the mode of production. Han draws on Marx, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping's remarks from his time in Zhejiang, on the history of economic thought, and on examples from several regions.

Han first sketches a history of economics. In this account it began as part of moral philosophy, narrowed into mathematical formalism and instrumental rationality after the marginal revolution, and is now returning to concern with human beings. Marxist economics, Han says, redirected the field towards relations between people, and the Party's aim of meeting the people's need for a better life requires a theory that reflects this. Han then treats culture as a production factor that shapes motivation, market behaviour and innovation, which matters for cultivating new quality productive forces. Regional cases are offered as raw material for theory: ice-and-snow culture in the northeast, Wu-Yue culture in Jiangsu and Zhejiang, Confucian culture in Shandong, and film and television that draw on classical literature. Han argues for moving from practice to experience to theory, and for drawing on history, philosophy and sociology. Han also cites traditional ethics of righteousness and benefit, and values such as good faith and respect for contracts, which are said to lower transaction costs and stabilise expectations.

Han concludes that humanistic economics would reveal the cultural factors behind China's development. It would also show how cultural advantages can support high-quality development and the building of a modern socialist country. Building the field means combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's realities and its fine traditional culture, and producing an economic theory with wide international influence. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Chinese economists are being encouraged to link culture, Marxist political economy and development theory.
quoteEn: Such experience should be raised into systematic theoretical expression, forming a path of construction from Chinese practice to Chinese experience and then to Chinese theory.
quoteZh: 要将此类经验上升为系统的理论表达，形成从中国实践到中国经验再到中国理论的建构路径。

glossary.explanation: A field proposed in Chinese discussion after Xi Jinping suggested in 2023 that the relationship between culture and economic prosperity be studied. It examines how cultural and human factors shape economic development.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by innovation, technology and new industries.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, that shifts emphasis from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and sustainability of development.
A slogan from Xi Jinping's calls to build Chinese philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics, rooted in China's own experience rather than Western theories.

t: Setting reform goals and tasks in step with the times to provide institutional guarantees for Chinese modernization
zh: 与时俱进确定改革目标任务 为中国式现代化提供制度保障
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 30 October 2024, Jiang Xiaojuan interprets the Decision on further deepening reform comprehensively to advance Chinese modernization, adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The article asks how the Decision's goals and tasks update earlier reform agendas. Jiang argues that the Decision continues two epoch-making plenums while adding new requirements, and that it supplies the institutional guarantees Chinese modernization needs.

The piece has two parts. The first traces the shift from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) through later "third plenums" to that of the 18th Central Committee (2013). The second examines the Decision's guiding principle of making three pairs of relations "better suited to each other" and illustrates it with specific reform measures.

Jiang's central claim is that the early reform era aimed chiefly at liberating and developing the productive forces, through steps from household contracting to a socialist market economy. Since 2013, the aim has also been to improve socialist institutions and modernize the system and capacity of national governance. The Decision's three pairings are relations of production and productive forces, the superstructure and the economic base, and national governance and social development. The last is a new formulation. On the first two, Jiang says reform must "break" and "build" together. Examples include equal and long-term protection of property rights across ownership types, better market exit mechanisms such as bankruptcy rules, and institutional rules on taxation and local investment promotion. The pairing of governance and social development responds to a different problem. Jiang argues that modernization raises social vitality and instability together, as rising education and migration lift expectations. The remedy is to balance vitality with order. The Decision's measures include equal access to public services for migrants and sealing records of minor offences.

Jiang concludes that the Decision contains major theoretical innovations. They rest on an accurate reading of the historical stage, of the relation between Chinese modernization's distinctive features and the general laws of modernization, and of new opportunities and challenges. Jiang calls it another landmark document in the history of reform and opening up. Full implementation, the author says, will give Chinese modernization strong momentum and solid institutional guarantees. Read the original if you want an official-line scholarly account of how the 2024 Decision is positioned against earlier reform plenums and why its governance language matters.
quoteEn: Promoting the better alignment of national governance and social development is an important new formulation in the Decision, reflecting the Party's deep understanding of the new problems and challenges that arise in the course of economic development and social progress.
quoteZh: 推动“国家治理和社会发展更好相适应”是《决定》中的一个重要新提法，体现了我们党对经济发展和社会进步过程中产生新问题新挑战的深刻认识和把握。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of a modernization path with Chinese characteristics, developed in Party discourse especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The theme of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It extends the comprehensively deepening reform programme launched in 2013.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernize the system and capacity of national governance
glossary.literal: modernization of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal introduced at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It refers to improving institutions and the ability to run them.

t: The critique of fetishism in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
zh: 《1844年经济学哲学手稿》中的拜物教批判思想
paras: Cheng Gang asks how Marx understood fetishism in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and where this stands between his earlier and later treatments. The article, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2024, argues that the Manuscripts' notion differs from the 1842 'idol fetishism' of the Cologne Gazette articles, a natural-religion idea. It also differs from the systematic fetishism of Capital, which Cheng presents as a social ontology of objective forms. Cheng places the 1844 notion between the two: it draws on religious and philosophical critique and opens the way to the critique of political economy.

Cheng's central claim is that fetishism appears to be a mystical power attributed to material wealth under private property but is in substance a separation of subjectivity from objectivity. The article is organised in three parts. The first treats the political-economic dimension, the worship of private property in classical political economy. The second treats the philosophical dimension, the alienation of 'self-consciousness' in Hegel. The third sets out sensuous practice as the route to overcoming fetishism.

On political economy, Cheng reads Marx as saying that Adam Smith and the Enlightenment economists, though they called the mercantilists 'fetishists', were fetishists themselves. The earlier school worshipped the product of labour as an object, while Smith's school made labour, and so the human being, the pure subjective essence of private property. In Cheng's reading, this wholly negates human objectivity and sets up a non-objective entity, so the growth of the world of things stands in direct proportion to the devaluation of the human world. In Hegel, Cheng argues, 'man' is equated with self-consciousness, so subjectivity detached from objectivity becomes an abstract 'subject' and objectivity becomes mere 'thingness'. Cheng calls Marx's critique of 'absolute knowledge' a philosophical form of fetishism critique.

Cheng concludes that for Marx fetishism is a historical product of practice and a 'temporary necessity' that will be superseded. Human senses are historically formed, depend on their objects and are created only by sensuous, objective labour. Practice, which Cheng ties to Marx's 'objective activity', unites subjectivity and objectivity and leads to a return of the human being to himself. Marx's aim, Cheng says, is to expose the roots of fetishism in private property and in thought, negate private property and enable all-round human self-emancipation. Read the original if you want a compact account of how the 1844 Manuscripts link fetishism critique to alienated labour, Hegel and the later critique of political economy.
quoteEn: The aim of Marx's twofold critique of fetishism in the Manuscripts is not to solve the theoretical riddle of fetishism or to analyse its essence, but to expose its roots in private property and in thought, and to negate private property.
quoteZh: 马克思在《手稿》中对拜物教进行双重批判的目的不在于解答有关拜物教的理论之谜，也不在于分析拜物教的本质，而在于揭露拜物教产生的私有制根源和思想根源，否定私有制，

t: Creating history: a social-mechanism perspective
zh: 历史创造：一个社会机制的视角
paras: The Marxist principle that the people are the creators of history is usually stated as a conclusion about who makes history. Wang argues that, under present conditions, it needs a further analytical tool: the category of "mechanisms of creating history", drawn from the analysis of social mechanisms. The article contends that this lens explains how the people's historical activity proceeds. On this view it is neither arbitrary nor chaotic, and it keeps its direction, continuity and stability.

The article identifies six mechanisms in the process of creating history: practice, interests, orientation toward the good, organization, combined force and mutual learning among civilizations. Each section defines one mechanism and grounds it in passages from Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. The sections also draw on examples from Chinese revolutionary history and on references to Western scholarship. The article closes by arranging the six into a single system.

The author gives each mechanism a distinct function. Practice answers the question of means and is the basic mechanism. The interest mechanism supplies motive force, both for "maintaining" creation in ordinary production and for "transformative" creation in revolution and reform. The mechanism of orientation toward the good sets direction. It requires that conformity to law and conformity to purpose be united, and it favours common interest over polarisation, citing Why Nations Fail on inclusive institutions. Organization and combined force are linked as cause and result: mobilised masses must form a force with shared consensus and interests, which Wang reads through Engels's parallelogram of forces. The author claims that this force can be undermined by what the article calls Western "colour revolution" tactics. Mutual learning rests on the nation-state as the unit of creation and on the shift toward world history.

Wang concludes that practice is the foundational mechanism, interests the core, orientation toward the good the regulator, and the other three "technical" mechanisms that sustain history-making. Together they form a unity that can move historical creation from the spontaneous to the conscious and from high cost to low. The methodological implications are listed: concrete hard work, attention to the people's immediate interests, the mass line, the united front, and openness to other civilizations. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese statement of how Party theory reads "the people as creators of history" through a mechanism-based framework, with its textual sources.
quoteEn: The mechanisms of creating history form a system, a unity of six elements.
quoteZh: 创造历史的机制是一个系统，是六位一体的统一。

glossary.explanation: The author's own category, which applies social-mechanism analysis to the Marxist thesis that the people make history. It names the internal structure and modes of operation of the people's historical activity.
A Chinese Communist Party method of work developed under Mao Zedong. It stresses gathering the views of ordinary people, acting on them and relying on them to carry out policy.
The Party's long-standing strategy of building broad alliances with non-Party groups and social strata to pursue shared goals. The article presents it as a key historical lesson of the Party.
A term used in official Chinese discourse for popular movements against governments, which it attributes to Western subversion. The article describes them in this way.

t: The critique of Hegel and of political economy in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
zh: 《1844年经济学哲学手稿》对黑格尔与政治经济学的批判
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 11 July 2024
paras: Dai Shengpeng asks how Marx's critique of political economy in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 (the Manuscripts) stands in relation to Hegel's earlier philosophical critique and reworking of the same discipline. The article argues that Marx's critique extends and deepens Hegel's logic of critique but reverses its purpose. Hegel reworked political economy to ground his theory of the state, whereas Marx criticised it to ground a new worldview and communism.

The piece first reconstructs Hegel's treatment of political economy, then explains why Marx turned to a direct critique of it, and finally reads the Manuscripts as a double critique of political economy and of Hegelian philosophy. It closes by noting differences among the Manuscripts' notebooks I, II and III, and by pointing forward to The German Ideology.

Dai sets out two lines of logic. For Hegel it runs: need, ownership, activity and labour, division of labour, wealth, estates, state. For Marx in the Manuscripts it runs: need, labour, division of labour, private property, class, state, communism. In Hegel's account, political economy seeks the reason at work in things, and starting from reality means starting from necessity, which he equates with freedom. Ownership is the outward form of the free will, property is freedom's first existence, and value and money give property its quantitative determination. Estates arising from diversified needs become a basis of the state. Dai holds that Hegel thus brought political economy into the perspective of human species-essence, which opened a new dimension for Marx. In Dai's reading, however, Hegel criticised from heaven rather than from the human world, so he could not explain civil society or help real human emancipation. Dai also links Marx's motives to the difficulty he met in 1842–43 in commenting on material interests and to his early misjudgements of communism.

Dai concludes that in the Manuscripts communism, not the state, sublates private property and civil society. Notebooks I and II still use Hegelian terms, so Marx there remains in some sense a young Marx still within the Young Hegelian orbit. Notebook III begins a systematic critique of Hegel's dialectic and philosophy, and the two critiques together produced the new worldview and new materialism of The German Ideology. Read the original if you want a concise account, in a Chinese scholarly perspective, of how Hegel's reworking of political economy relates to the Manuscripts' critique.
quoteEn: If Hegel's philosophical critique and construction of political economy laid the theoretical groundwork for his theory of the state, then Marx's philosophical critique and construction of political economy or national economics in the Manuscripts laid the groundwork for his new worldview and for communism.
quoteZh: 如果说黑格尔对政治经济学的哲学批判与建构是为其国家学说做理论铺垫与立论基础的话，那么马克思在《手稿》中对政治经济学或国民经济学的哲学批判与建构，则是为其新世界观与共产主义做理论铺垫与立论基础的。

t: Deng Xiaoping's financial thought: theoretical contributions to the path of financial development with Chinese characteristics and its practical implications
zh: 邓小平金融思想对中国特色金融发展之路的理论贡献及现实启示
source: Observation and Thinking (Guancha yu sikao), 2024 no. 9
paras: Li Bin asks what Deng Xiaoping's views on finance contributed to what official discourse now calls the path of financial development with Chinese characteristics. The article, published in 2024 after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee and the Central Financial Work Conference of October 2023, argues that Deng's financial thought is an integral part of Deng Xiaoping Theory. In Li's account it supplied the theoretical basis for China's financial reform and anticipates central themes in Xi Jinping's statements on financial work.

The article opens with a short review of existing scholarship, grouped into three strands: the formation and stages of Deng's financial thought, its core content, and its practical influence. Li notes that the literature has paid little attention to how Deng developed Marxist financial theory. The body then has two main parts, on the pioneering significance of Deng's thought and on its specific theoretical contributions, followed by a section on its present-day value.

Li identifies three features of Deng's thought: applying Marxist principles to Chinese conditions, requiring finance to serve economic construction and the people's interests, and pursuing reform in a spirit of innovation marked by political, holistic and open characteristics. The article then draws out three contributions. The first is the idea that finance is "the core of the modern economy", which Li reads as defining the function of finance and its link to fiscal policy. The second is the call to "run banks truly as banks", which Li credits with moving China from a highly centralised, People's Bank-dominated system towards a modern financial system through the reforms from 1979 and the 1993 programme. The third is Deng's stress on macroeconomic regulation, price stability, controlling inflation and guarding against financial risk, which Li says enriched the theory of financial governance.

Li concludes that studying Deng's thought helps explain the lineage of Xi Jinping's statements on financial work. Four implications follow: grasping the political and people-oriented nature of finance, including the Party Central Committee's centralised leadership; having finance serve the real economy and preventing speculation and disorderly capital expansion; deepening financial reform to build a financial powerhouse; and strengthening macroeconomic regulation and risk prevention to avoid systemic financial risk. Read the original if you want to see how Deng's remarks on banking, money and inflation are assembled into a genealogy for current Party financial policy.
quoteEn: As an important component of Deng Xiaoping Theory, Deng Xiaoping's financial thought not only provided a theoretical basis for China's financial reform but also made a theoretical contribution to the path of financial development with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 邓小平金融思想作为邓小平理论的重要组成部分，不仅为中国金融体制改革提供了理论依据，而且对中国特色金融发展之路作出了理论贡献。

glossary.zh: 中国特色金融发展之路
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó tèsè jīnróng fāzhǎn zhī lù
glossary.en: the path of financial development with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: A formulation set out by Xi Jinping at the Central Financial Work Conference in October 2023. It describes a financial model stressing Party leadership, serving the real economy and risk prevention.
The body of ideas associated with Deng Xiaoping on reform and opening up and socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is written into the Party's guiding ideology.
A high-level Party meeting on financial policy. The one held in October 2023 introduced the aim of building a financial powerhouse.
An official goal, stressed since the Central Financial Work Conference of 2023, of building China into a country with strong, internationally competitive financial institutions and markets.
The part of the economy that produces goods and services, as opposed to financial speculation. Official policy says finance must serve it.

t: Western civilisation as seen through Western economics
zh: 从西方经济学看西方文明
source: Journal of Ningxia University (Social Sciences Edition), 2024 no. 3
paras: Yu Bin takes up a description of Western economics in China's official guide to postgraduate disciplines: a field that aims at efficient resource allocation under scarcity and studies market-economy theory and policy. Yu argues that the field is seriously flawed. In this reading it does not scientifically reflect the laws of capitalism, as Marx's economics does, but turns capitalists' vulgar notions into academic doctrine. For that reason, Yu holds, it reveals the one-sided traits of the mainstream ideology and of Western civilisation.

The article is organised in four parts, each reading a feature of Western economics as a trait of Western civilisation: its research goals, its content (individual agents, firms, fluctuations, growth, incentives, government policy), its schools, and its methods. Yu draws on Marx, Engels, Coase, Pigou, Pareto, Keynes, Samuelson and Zhang Wuchang, and on Xi Jinping's remarks on supply-side economics. Each section attaches a label to Western civilisation, among them absurdity, capital-centredness, plunder, deception of the people, self-contradiction and fabrication.

In Yu's account, scarcity theory exists to discredit the labour theory of value, and 'efficient allocation' means giving resources, and rights such as the right to pollute, to large capital. Marginal utility theory, with its claim that utilities cannot be compared between persons, is presented as a device for blocking redistribution from rich to poor. The article says the 'rational economic man', the production function, growth models and incentive design all ignore commerce, finance and exploitation. Yu attributes the field's many schools to rival interest groups, such as industrial versus financial capital, rather than to scientific disagreement. On method, Yu separates legitimate mathematical analysis, citing Marx's reproduction schemes, from what the author calls the 'Pythagorean complex' and formalism. Examples include utility functions, the Keynesian multiplier and methodological individualism, which Yu likens to Marx's 'sack of potatoes'.

Yu concludes that the proliferation of schools shows confusion, not scholarly prosperity, and that Marxist political economy is the only true economic science. Yu calls for critical study of Western economics in light of political economy and historical materialism, and rejects both direct borrowing and the 'Sinicisation' of Western economics. Chinese economics should instead be a product of Xi Jinping's economic thought and the Two Integrations. Yu also urges that individualism not be taught to Chinese graduate students. Read the original if you want to see an uncompromising Marxist critique of Western economics and of how it is taught in Chinese universities.
quoteEn: The large number of schools in Western economics does not signify academic prosperity; on the contrary, it indicates the disorientation of its scholarship.
quoteZh: 西方经济学流派众多，并不意味着学术的繁荣，反而代表其学术的迷惘

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory, associated with Xi Jinping, for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, presented officially as part of Xi Jinping Thought and as the guide to China's economic work.

t: On money as a special general commodity
zh: 论货币是特殊的一般商品
paras: Is money a "special commodity" or a "general commodity"? Yu Bin takes up this long-running dispute in Chinese Marxist economics and argues that it is badly framed. Competing definitions (money as a special commodity serving as general equivalent, as a general commodity serving as general equivalent, or simply as a commodity serving as general equivalent) all differ from the definition Marx himself gave. Yu's own answer is that money is a "special general commodity".

The article, published in Guangxi Social Sciences in 2024, opens with an overview and then reviews three camps in turn: the "general commodity" view, the "special commodity" view, and the compromise view that money is both. It closes with a section setting out Yu's own position and several peculiarities of gold as money. Yu engages many unnamed scholars' arguments, tests them against passages of Capital and the Grundrisse, and uses historical cases such as Tang-dynasty silk, Xue Muqiao's commodity-reserve paper currency in the liberated areas, and cigarettes in US prisons.

Yu argues that in Marx's usage only the other commodities are "special" relative to money, which is their general equivalent, so the qualifier "of all other commodities" must accompany "general equivalent". Money is also not "fixed" in the role but holds it exclusively. Against the special-commodity camp, Yu holds that gold's suitability rests less on its physical properties than on the relative stability of the socially necessary labour time needed to produce it; aluminium and silk are offered as counter-examples. The view that money is more special than general, Yu says, falls into the illusion Marx described, that a commodity seems to be money because the others express their value in it. Marx's remark that money is both general and special arose in discussing speculative price rises, when supply and demand outweigh the law of value. Yu takes Marx's actual definition (the commodity that serves as measure of value and, directly or through representatives, as means of circulation) to qualify a commodity by social function alone, which makes money a general commodity.

Yu concludes that the most accurate formulation is: money is a special general commodity, or a general commodity holding a social monopoly, though even this is not a definition. Textbooks that do not start from Marx's own definition, Yu says, need to be rewritten. Yu lists further peculiarities of gold: the rivalry of gold and silver standards, the effect of plunder on its value, shifts in its labour time, its uselessness elsewhere, its role as a reserve, and its easy conversion between forms. Read the original if you work on Marx's theory of money, or want to see how Chinese scholars argue over Capital's wording and its application to gold and paper currency.
quoteEn: Therefore only the special equivalents of money, that is, all other commodities, are special commodities; money is not.
quoteZh: 所以，只是货币的特殊等价物，只是其他一切商品，才是特殊商品，货币不是。

t: On the transmission mechanism from productive forces to way of life and its implications
zh: 论生产力—生活方式的传导机制及其启示
source: Observation and Thinking (Guancha yu sikao), 2024 no. 2
paras: Yu Bin takes up a passage in Capital in which Marx endorses a factory inspectors' report linking machine inventions to changes in the workers' way of life. From it Yu derives a chain of transmission: productive forces, mode of production, relations of production, social relations, way of life. Yu argues that this chain is the core of historical materialism, and that Marxist scholarship has attended mainly to its first three links while neglecting social relations and, above all, the way of life of the people.

The article, published in 2024, has four sections. The first defends 'productive-forces determinism' against critics: Tang Changli, advocates of economic determinism, Engels's 'resultant of forces' reading of history, and Althusser's overdetermination. The second argues that the mode of production is a mediating link rather than, as Stalin held, the unity of productive forces and relations, and takes issue with Guo Guanqing's classification. The third distinguishes relations of production from social relations. The fourth turns to the people's way of life and to common prosperity.

Yu's central move is to read 'determination' as ultimate and dialectical rather than one-to-one: the same productive forces may correspond to different relations of production, and each link also reacts back on the one before. On this basis Yu reads the Russian and Chinese revolutions as consistent with the theory, and says that disregarding the theory led to the earlier belief that communism could be reached quickly at a low level of productive forces. Yu then argues that social relations contain relations of production and have them as their core. Transforming social relations suits revolutionary periods, whereas in construction the task is to reproduce socialist relations of production. Yu attributes the Soviet collapse to neglect of this task and the limits of the Mao-era approach to excessive focus on social relations outside production.

Yu concludes that public ownership must remain the mainstay of the economy so that socialist production relations can sustain the people's social relations. Citing Marx's accounts of working hours, child labour and the workers' living conditions, Yu argues that social relations shape way of life, and that a better way of life in turn raises workers' quality and frees productive forces. Yu calls for better working conditions, shorter working days and enforcement of labour law as part of common prosperity, and for balanced attention to every link in the chain in pursuing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist's systematic defence of productive-forces determinism and of the distinction between relations of production and social relations.
quoteEn: Therefore, the mode of production is not the unity of productive forces and relations of production, but the transmission medium between them.
quoteZh: 因此，生产方式不是生产力和生产关系的统一，而是生产力和生产关系的传导中介。

glossary.explanation: The view that productive forces ultimately determine relations of production and, through them, wider social change. In Chinese debates it is often defended against charges of mechanical or one-factor determinism.
Here the way productive forces are used (for example cooperation or manufacture). Yu treats it as an intermediate link, not as the unity of productive forces and relations of production.
The wider set of relations among people, including political, ideological and cultural ones. Yu holds that relations of production form their core but are not identical with them.
The conditions and pattern of people's daily life, such as working time, housing and family life. Yu treats it as the last link in the chain and as a measure of socialism.
A goal of socialism in Chinese official discourse, stressing prosperity shared by all rather than by a minority.
The official term, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path of modernization.

t: Telling China's story well requires following historical materialism
zh: 讲好中国故事需要遵循唯物史观
source: Marxist Cultural Studies (马克思主义文化研究), 2024 no. 1
paras: Taking up the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to build China's own discourse and narrative system and present a credible, lovable and respectable image of China, Yu Bin asks why telling China's story to foreigners is so hard and how it can be done. The article argues that historical materialism, and especially the principle that social being determines consciousness, both explains the difficulty and points to the solutions.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the difficulties, drawing on Zhuangzi's image of the summer insect that cannot talk of ice, on the Communist Manifesto's 'world literature', and on Engels's letters. The second sets out why the task is possible, citing Marx, Engels and Lenin. The third gives four groups of practical recommendations. Yu also criticises other authors' views, such as the claim that historical anecdotes or 'empathetic communication' will carry China's story abroad.

Yu argues that foreign audiences live in a different social being, so they cannot readily grasp Chinese consciousness. In class-divided societies, Yu adds, no story pleases everyone, and Western media are hostile to socialism. Yu holds that the story can still be told in several ways. One is to reach audiences with similar social conditions, such as ordinary people in developing and developed countries who want a better life. Another is to present China's new form of human civilization as a preview of other countries' future, as Marx did with England in Capital. A third is to use China's weight as a customer, the import expo and new media, which Yu says weaken Western narrative control. Yu also says Chinese stories told as exotic 'national allegories', or films such as Dying to Survive that expose shortcomings, do not present a respectable image.

Yu's proposals are: openly acknowledge China's strengths, for instance by classing China as a 'high developing country' and promoting its digital life; abandon the policy of hiding one's capabilities and be more assertive, including by exporting books and films about China's anti-hegemonic past; tell the story of the new era and of the Two Integrations; and explain socialism's difference from capitalism. Yu also proposes teaching Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to foreign students in China and creating language exams based on Chinese discourse. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar applies historical materialism to international communication, along with its concrete policy suggestions.
quoteEn: Telling China's story well means getting people in other countries to understand the Chinese consciousness expressed in it, so it amounts to telling the summer insect a good story about ice.
quoteZh: 讲好中国故事就是让世界上其他国家的人理解中国故事中所表现的中国意识，从而讲好中国故事其实就相当于要给夏虫讲好冰的故事。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Chinese Communist Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The formula of combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.literal: hide one's brightness and nourish obscurity
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy maxim associated with Deng Xiaoping, advising a low profile and avoiding open displays of strength.
An official phrase describing the path of Chinese modernization as a new type of civilization, distinct from Western models.

t: Understanding the value implications of building a community with a shared future for mankind
zh: 深刻理解构建人类命运共同体的价值意蕴
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 18 July 2024
paras: This commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in July 2024, asks what values lie behind the idea of building a community with a shared future for mankind. Zhang Xiaobo and Qin Hui present the idea as an important part of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought and as one of the essential requirements of Chinese modernization. They argue that it should be understood as a scientific theoretical system whose values can move from recognition to consensus, and from vision to reality.

The authors analyse the concept along five dimensions: its value subject, value basis, value criterion, value goal and value realisation. Each dimension is set against a contrasting position, either an abstract, Western-centred or conflict-oriented one. The authors draw on Marx's concept of the real human being, on Xi's 2015 United Nations speech on common values, on the Global Civilization Initiative of 2023, and on traditional Chinese ideals of harmony.

Zhang and Qin contend that the subject of the community is the real, concrete "humanity" facing a turbulent world and a strained system of global governance, not an abstract humanity. Its value basis is the "common values of all humanity" (peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom), which the authors distinguish from the "universal values" that they say the United States and other Western states use to pursue hegemony. Its criterion is the equality and mutual learning of civilizations, in contrast to theories of civilizational superiority or clash, which they describe as grounded in prejudice. Its goal is the ideal of "each appreciating its own beauty and that of others, and the world in harmony", which they say does not mean replacing one system or civilization with another.

In the authors' account, realisation of these values lies in a modernization that follows the path of peaceful development, which they say differs from a Western model built on capital, aggression and colonial plunder. They claim that China has not started a war since 1949 and has written peaceful development into its constitution and Party charter. The authors conclude that China will join other countries in a world modernization of mutual benefit and common prosperity. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Chinese commentary presents the philosophical and civilizational grounding of this concept.
quoteEn: The value subject of building a community with a shared future for mankind is concrete, real "humanity", not a vague and abstract concept of "humanity".
quoteZh: 构建人类命运共同体的价值主体是具体的、现实的“人类”，而非笼统的、抽象的“人类”概念。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2012–13. It calls for countries to cooperate on shared global challenges and is presented as a goal of Chinese diplomacy.
The official name for China's path of development, presented by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western modernization.
A formulation Xi Jinping first used at the UN in 2015, listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. Official texts contrast it with Western "universal values".
A proposal announced by Xi Jinping in March 2023. It calls for respect for the diversity of civilizations, shared values, cultural exchange and mutual learning.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The theoretical significance and practical requirements of being both "lively" and "well-regulated"
st: Letting the market "come alive" while keeping it "under control"
zh: 既“放得活”又“管得住”的理论意义和实践要求
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 29 August 2024
paras: The Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) called for a high-standard socialist market economy that is both "fang de huo" (loosened enough to be lively) and "guan de zhu" (regulated enough to be controlled). This commentary by Lü Wei and Liu Xinqi takes up the formulation as a new way of framing the relationship between government and market. The authors argue that handling "loosening" and "managing" together expresses both the socialist character and the market-economy content of the system, and that it serves as an important safeguard for Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised in three parts: deepening theoretical understanding, summarising regular patterns, and identifying practical directions. The first part places the formulation within the theory of the socialist market economy and the history of economic thought. The second links it to pairs of values: vitality and order, development and security. The third sets out concrete reform tasks.

Lü and Liu define "loosening" as the government's "subtraction": reducing direct resource allocation, intervention and approvals to release market vitality. "Managing" is the government's "addition": correcting market failure, improving public services and safeguarding fairness and stability. They argue that the debate over "small" versus "big" government should give way to the criterion of an "effective" government, one that is a service-oriented government and a government under the rule of law. In their account China, unlike Western developed countries that let markets expand freely, relies on national planning, policy commitments and macro-regulation, and this explains its steady growth. They also tie the formulation to the development of new quality productive forces, which they say require new relations of production and a larger market role.

On practice, the authors name three levels. The precondition is clarifying responsibilities under the Two Unwaverings, through state-enterprise reform, credit evaluation systems and support for private firms. The foundation is fair competition: removing market-access barriers, antitrust enforcement, equal property protection and financing support for small and medium-sized enterprises. The key is smooth circulation: market-determined factor prices, a unified national market, and an integrated domestic-demand system of investment and consumption. Read the original if you want a concise official-line academic gloss on how the "loosen and manage" formula is being turned into Third Plenum reform priorities.
quoteEn: Handling the relationship between "loosening" and "managing" well can both use reform to bring the market's efficiency into play and use coordination to raise the effectiveness of governance.
quoteZh: 处理好“放”和“管”的关系，既能以改革发挥市场之效率，又能以协调提升治理之效力。

glossary.pinyin: fàng de huó, guǎn de zhù
glossary.en: "fang de huo" (loosened enough to be lively) and "guan de zhu" (regulated enough to be controlled)
glossary.literal: loosened so as to be lively, managed so as to be held in check
glossary.explanation: A formulation in the Third Plenum (2024) decision on government–market relations: reduce state interference so markets thrive, while retaining effective regulation and oversight.
