The official term for China's development path under Communist Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western modernization models.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading.
The official policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official name for China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and state macro-regulation.

t: On the complexity of the world modernization movement
zh: 论世界现代化运动的复杂性
paras: Dai Mucai asks why modernization, as a world historical process, is so complex, and what follows for how Chinese modernization should be understood. The article argues that modernization is both universal and particular: no single model or standard exists, and the complexity of the process also makes modernization theory complex. Against this background, Dai presents Chinese modernization as a path without precedent in the history of the world modernization movement.

The article has six sections. It begins with the bloody origins of modernization, then examines the contested meanings of "modern", "modernity" and "modernization". It goes on to the complexity of the historical process, using Kondratiev's long-wave theory, and to the diversity of models, drawing on Cyril Black's comparative typology of more than 170 countries. It then discusses the difficulty of evaluating modernization, including the criticisms it has drawn, and ends with Chinese modernization compared with the wider movement.

Dai makes three central moves. First, citing Marx on primitive accumulation, colonialism and the slave trade, the author characterises Western-style modernization as a "path of evil" built on invasion, plunder, colonization, enslavement and war, and contrasts it with a "path of good" of openness, mutual benefit, peace and cooperation. Second, Dai argues that even Western modernization varied (the Anglo-Saxon, Rhine, Nordic and East Asian models), so modernization cannot be equated with "Westernization"; the claim that Western theories present their own model as universal is called a case of taking the part for the whole. Third, modernization is both fact and value, and capitalist modernization has been criticised by utopian socialism, Marxism, Western Marxism, Western thinkers themselves and dependency theory.

Dai holds that Chinese modernization shares the common features of world modernization but also rests on Chinese conditions, on 5,000 years of civilization and on the Two Integrations. Dai calls for a theoretical system open to existing modernization theories, able to speak to Western theory and to claim international discourse power. In closing, the author says the "next volume" of Chinese modernization, towards 2035 and the mid-century goal, will bring both crises and opportunities. Dai calls for Party leadership, reform and opening up, and a spirit of struggle. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist account of modernization theory that links Kondratiev, Cyril Black and dependency theory to the case for Chinese modernization as a non-Western path.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a path of socialist modernization opened up by persisting in \"taking our own road\", and it has no precedent in the history of the world modernization movement.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是坚持“走自己的路”而开创出来的一条社会主义现代化发展之路，在世界现代化运动史上没有先例。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of socialist modernization under Communist Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as sharing common features with other countries while reflecting China's own conditions.
The formula of integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is used to describe how the Party developed its theory and path.
The capacity to set the terms and concepts in international debate. Chinese official and academic writing uses it to argue for China's own concepts and theories to be heard.

t: The conceptual logic of "the critique of capital"
st: The core meaning of the "doctrine of the concept" in Marx's political economy
zh: “资本批判”的概念逻辑
zhSub: 马克思政治经济学“概念论”的核心要义
source: Contemporary Economic Research (Dangdai jingji yanjiu), 2024 no. 7
paras: Liu Daoyi asks how the concepts of Marx's political economy are built and how they move, and argues that the "conceptual logic" of Capital is the methodological model for any later critique of capital. In Liu's reading, the capitalist economic system is a system of contradictions, so the concepts that define it must form an organised group centred on one core concept. The movement of the concepts, Liu argues, mirrors the real "movement of contradictions", which turns Hegel's dialectic from standing on its head to standing on its feet.

The article first traces the idea of "concept-movement" to Hegel's speculative logic and then to Marx's materialist inversion of it. It next sets out four basic forms of conceptual movement in Capital and its manuscripts: critique of old concepts, definition of new ones, reworking of concepts, and transformation between concrete and abstract. It then follows the genesis of this logic through the 1844 Manuscripts, the 1857–58 and 1861–63 manuscripts, and the three volumes of Capital.

Liu's central claim is that Marx moved "from the concrete to the abstract and back up to the concrete" through three theoretical cycles over some twenty years. The core concept first defined was "alienated labour" in the 1844 Manuscripts. Marx then replaced it with "surplus value", first in the 1857–58 manuscripts and then in the 1861–63 manuscripts, before fully defining it in Volume I. Liu stresses that abstract and concrete are relative: commodity is abstract relative to money, and surplus value is abstract relative to profit but concrete relative to value. From surplus value Marx derives relative surplus value, wages and accumulation (Volume I), capital circulation and reproduction (Volume II), and profit, average profit, production price, commercial profit, interest and rent (Volume III). Liu reads the closing part on revenues and their sources as the counterpart of Hegel's "absolute idea", aimed at vulgar economics and its "trinity formula".

Liu concludes that this systematic argument built on surplus value rejects the "factor theory" and other apologetics for capitalism. It also differs from Hegel's harmonious final picture of absolute spirit. According to the author, the conceptual doctrine remains necessary for critical study of today's global capitalism and for thinking about "human emancipation", since it drives practical change and a scientific vision of a good life. Read the original if you study the methodology of Capital, Marx's relation to Hegel's Logic, or how Marx's core concept shifted from alienated labour to surplus value.
quoteEn: The general principle of the \"conceptual logic\" of Capital is the form of \"transformation\" that goes \"from the concrete to the abstract and then rises from the abstract to the concrete\".
quoteZh: 《资本论》“概念逻辑”的总原则是“从具体到抽象再由抽象上升到具体”的“转化”形态

t: Marx's theory of civilization and building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 马克思的文明理论与建设中华民族现代文明
source: Social Sciences in China (Zhongguo shehui kexue), 2024 no. 7
paras: Duan Yan asks what theoretical basis Marx's writings on civilization provide for the new cultural mission of building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation, a task Xi Jinping set out in 2023. The article argues that Marx's theory supplies the foundation and that the Chinese project develops it further. It does so by combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture, which the article calls the Two Integrations.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Marx's theory under three headings: civilization as the unity of social formation and state form; the free and all-round development of each person as the goal of civilization; and world history as the driving force of modern civilization. The second part presents the modern civilization of the Chinese nation as an innovative development of that theory. The third sets out five practical paths for building it.

In Duan's reading, Marx treats civilization as a historical category: material and spiritual progress develop together, and the state is its "summary". Marx also criticises capitalist civilization, which opened world history yet combined progress with barbarism, and he looks to a successor civilization that abolishes private ownership. Duan argues that the Chinese civilization fits this pattern in three ways. It is socialist in both social and state form, coordinating five civilizations (material, political, spiritual, social and ecological). It takes a people-centred orientation, linked to traditional minben (people-as-foundation) thought and to common prosperity. It stresses openness, mutual learning and a community with a shared future for mankind, which Duan says goes beyond the "clash of civilizations" and Western-centrism.

Duan proposes five paths: advance Chinese modernization while taking China's own road; draw selectively on the achievements of other civilizations, with Chinese needs as the principle; promote the flourishing of socialist culture under core socialist values; carry out the creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture, with heritage protection; and spread Chinese civilization abroad through a community with a shared future for mankind. The article presents these as contributions to human progress and as a new form of human civilization. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar ties Marx's remarks on civilization, the state and world history to current Party cultural policy.
quoteEn: The degree of civilizational development is intrinsically consistent with the degree to which human emancipation is realised.
quoteZh: 文明的发展程度与人的解放的实现程度具有内在一致性。

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023 as part of a new cultural mission. Official discourse presents it as a civilization that combines socialism, Chinese tradition and modernity.
The Party formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.

A Party goal of prosperity shared by all the people, with narrowing of regional, urban–rural and income gaps. The 20th Party Congress (2022) called it an essential requirement of Chinese modernization.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, presented as an alternative to confrontation and hegemony.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

keywords: modern civilization of the Chinese nation

t: Marx's twofold critique of modern science and technology and its inheritance and development
zh: 马克思对现代科学技术的双重批判及其继承发展
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2024 no. 3
paras: Li Le examines Marx's speech of 14 April 1856 at the fourth anniversary dinner of the Chartist People's Paper, a short text the author says has received little scholarly attention. The article argues that two metaphors in the speech, modern science and technology as a "most dangerous revolutionary" and as a "shrewd spirit", ground a twofold critique: one of the facts of science and technology under capitalism, and one of the attitudes different parties take towards it. Li presents this as a basis for understanding Xi Jinping's statements on science and technology in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first reads the "revolutionary" metaphor against Blanqui, Barbès and Raspail, and then sets out how science and technology work as a new social force and stand opposed to modern poverty. The second turns to the "spirit" metaphor, surveying how petty-bourgeois democrats such as Kinkel, Christian Socialists, Tories and David Urquhart's circle responded, and then Marx's view of the proletariat as the "new men". The third moves to the present and discusses Xi Jinping's remarks on science and technology.

In Li's reading of the first metaphor, science and technology advance the productive forces, create revolutionary pressure and reshape the social structure. Under capitalist relations, however, they become a tool of capital: nature is conquered for profit, science is separated from workers, and machinery lengthens and intensifies labour, deskills workers and subordinates their life rhythm to the machine. Li stresses that the cause of poverty is the capitalist relations of production that distort technology, not technology itself. On the second metaphor, Li holds that only workers can master this force, through a social revolution that is comprehensive, broad in scope and historical, ending wage labour and the monopoly over technology.

In the final part Li presents Xi Jinping's discourse as continuing this tradition. It treats science and technology as the primary productive force and as a foundation for Chinese modernization. Li also describes an original idea of "initiative" in science and technology, which includes judging trends, self-confidence in innovation and strategic initiative. Li lists socialist requirements: meeting people's needs, self-reliance in core technologies, a new whole-nation system to regulate capital's logic, and opposing the politicization of technology. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese doctoral researcher links a little-studied Marx speech to current Party science and technology policy.
quoteEn: What causes modern poverty and social decay is not the development of science and technology itself, but the distorting control that capitalist relations of production exert over it.
quoteZh: 造成现代贫困和社会衰颓的不是科学技术本身的发展，而是资本主义生产关系对科学技术的扭曲控制。

glossary.explanation: The official concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of a distinctively Chinese path to modernization, contrasted with Western models.
An official term for mobilising state, market and research institutions in a coordinated way to achieve major scientific and technological breakthroughs.

t: Marx's investigation of the essence of the state through the interplay of history and political economy, and its implications
zh: 马克思在历史与政治经济学交互视域中对国家本质的考察及其启示
source: Contemporary Chinese Marxism Studies (Dangdai Zhongguo Makesizhuyi Yanjiu), 2023 no. 4
paras: What is the state, and by what route did Marx determine its essence? Wang Guang argues that Marx's approach differs from both empirical political science and normative political philosophy. In Wang's account, Marx combined two perspectives: he went into real history to trace how states develop and change, and he went beyond the political sphere into political economy to define the state's content. Wang holds that this research path, and not only Marx's conclusions, is what present-day scholars should study.

The article follows Marx's thought in four steps. It begins with the Kreuznach Notebooks of 1843 and the break with Hegel's "rational state". It then traces the state's essence through the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, The Holy Family, The German Ideology and the Communist Manifesto. Next it turns to The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte, The Civil War in France and Engels's remarks on the Paris Commune and the United States. It ends with a discussion of how Marx's political philosophy should be defined today.

Wang's central claim is that the Kreuznach excerpts on French, English and German history taught Marx to see property relations behind political rule, so that he reversed Hegel's order of explanation. After 1844 he tied the state to production, and in The German Ideology the modern state appears as the form that matches modern private property and serves the bourgeoisie's common interests. Wang reads the Commune as the practical answer: the working class cannot simply take over the ready-made state machine but must smash it, and the Commune returns to society the powers a "parasitic excrescence" had taken from it. In the final section Wang argues that applying Western political philosophy's standards to Marx concentrates attention on justice, equality and freedom, and neglects the state, class and revolution. Wang proposes a "broad-spectrum" Marxist political philosophy, with wider topics and a normativity grounded in scientific necessity, in which what ought to be rests on what is and what must be.

Wang concludes that Marx's political philosophy differs in kind from that of Plato, Hobbes, Rawls and others, because it derives values from the laws of history and not from reason or moral principle. The article calls for widening the themes of Marx's political philosophy and for rebuilding its normativity along these lines. Wang presents this as part of building China's own independent knowledge system. Read the original if you are interested in how Chinese Marxist philosophers define Marx's political philosophy against Western political philosophy, or in a close reading of Marx's early texts on the state.
quoteEn: Marx did not advocate an "ought" detached from reality (the "is") and from historical law (the "must").
quoteZh: 马克思并不主张那种脱离现实（“实然”）与历史规律（“必然”）的“应然”。

glossary.explanation: A slogan in Chinese official discourse of recent years that calls for building Chinese scholarship with its own concepts and standards rather than relying on Western frameworks.

t: Principle-level achievements of the Party's theoretical innovation in the perspective of scientific socialism
zh: 科学社会主义视阈中党的理论创新的原理性成果
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2024 no. 6
paras: Wang Conglong takes up a task that Xi Jinping set in June 2023: to clarify the "principle-level theoretical achievements" (yuanlixing lilun chengguo) within the Party's innovative theory and to show how they connect. The article argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party has put forward a series of original achievements of this kind, which in Wang's account have opened a new realm for scientific socialism in contemporary China.

The article has three parts. The first defines principle-level achievements as major judgements that are foundational in origin, in supporting function and in essential character, and explains why proposing them is required to uphold and develop scientific socialism. The second sets out nine such achievements, each paired with a question the classics left open. The third assesses what they accomplish for scientific socialism.

Wang argues that the classical writers stated only the most general principles, whose application must change with historical conditions, so new principle-level achievements are needed both to keep to the classics and to renew them. The nine achievements are: Party leadership as the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics; the general task of socialist modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation; a people-centred stance; the new development philosophy; modernizing national governance; humanity and nature as a community of life; the Party's self-reform as the "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and fall; a community with a shared future for mankind; and Chinese modernization. Wang reads these as meeting four kinds of question: foundational, core, guarantee-related and forward-looking.

Wang concludes that these achievements strengthen the theoretical roots of scientific socialism in China and show it in a new form. They also set a new height for its twenty-first-century development and open a new prospect for it in the contemporary world, including long-term coexistence between socialist states and the capitalist world. Wang calls Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era the scientific socialism of contemporary China. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-theoretical account of how the Xi-era formulations are presented as extending scientific socialism.
quoteEn: Proposing principle-level theoretical achievements is the only way to drive the formation and development of scientific socialism, and also a basic law that must be followed in upholding and developing it.
quoteZh: 提出原理性理论成果是推动科学社会主义形成和发展的必由之路，也是坚持和发展科学社会主义必须遵循的基本规律。

glossary.explanation: Major judgements within a theoretical system that are foundational, essential and an origin for other claims. Xi Jinping called for research on them in 2023 as part of systematizing the Party's theory.
The socialist doctrine founded by Marx and Engels on historical materialism, as distinct from utopian socialism. Chinese Party theory treats it as the core of Marxism that is continually developed.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
The official principles of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
The Party's term for its own continuous self-correction and discipline, presented as its answer to how a ruling party avoids decline.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations and global governance, promoted since 2012–13.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The place and role of "needs" in the framework of historical materialism
zh: “需要”在历史唯物主义框架中的地位及其作用
paras: Wang Wei asks where "needs" belong within historical materialism. Chinese scholarship since the 1980s has mostly treated need as a basic category of historical materialism, often comparing its weight with that of the productive forces. Wang argues that need is better understood as a mechanism than as a fixed category. On this view, need is not the driving force of history but the content determination of social production and social life, and it is rooted in both nature and society.

The article has four sections. The first lists the problems with classing need only as a historical-materialist category. The second sets out how need determines the content of the framework. The third examines its formal determination and its limits. The fourth turns to the theory of the principal social contradiction in China, which Wang presents as a development of Marx's theory of needs. Wang draws on Marx and Engels throughout, including the 1844 Manuscripts, The German Ideology, Capital and Engels's essay on the role of labour in the transition from ape to man.

Wang's central claim is that need belongs to the dialectics of nature as well as to historical materialism. Natural needs form the biological precondition of society, so need cannot simply be ranked against the productive forces. In content, need defines who the historical subject is, what practice is carried out and how, the unity of natural history and human history, and the ideological forms of class society. Its form is tied to subjectivity and has limits. Needs can become distorted under exploitative relations of production, and they are constrained by natural and social conditions and by cultural tradition. Morality and law can discipline them only within limits set by the relations of production, and the development of the productive forces ultimately drives them. Need therefore does not replace the productive forces' decisive role.

In the final section Wang reads the Party's formulations of the principal contradiction as putting need at the centre of socialist development. These are the 1981 formulation (growing material and cultural needs against backward production) and the 19th Party Congress (2017) formulation (needs for a better life against unbalanced and inadequate development). Wang presents this as a creative advance on Marx's theory, linked to Chinese modernization, common prosperity and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a philosophical treatment of need in Marxist theory that ends in a Party-line account of the principal contradiction.
quoteEn: Need is not the driving force of social development but the content determination of social production and social life.
quoteZh: 需要并不是社会发展的动力，而是社会生产和社会生活的内容规定。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Party theory for the central contradiction at a given stage, used to set development priorities. The 1981 resolution and the 19th Party Congress (2017) each gave a formulation.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, stressed in Party documents especially since the 2020s.
An official goal of shared wealth for all, in the Party's usage tied to socialism and to narrowing regional and urban–rural gaps.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance.

t: A historical-materialist critique of the capitalization of games
zh: 唯物史观对游戏资本化的批判
paras: Liu Yuzhou takes up the question of how games should be studied and criticised in the age of digital capitalism. The article, a short commentary first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, argues that the cultural-sociological tradition of Huizinga and Schiller, and even the Situationists' romantic view of play, treat games as a cultural phenomenon and so miss the capitalist relations of production behind them. Liu likewise rejects explanations of internet addiction that blame games themselves, and calls for a turn from cultural sociology to a critique of the capitalization of games.

The piece has two parts. The first uses historical materialism to trace how game capitalization arose, dividing the modern history of games into four overlapping eras: the stand-alone era, the rent era, the consumption era and the present era of game capitalism. The second turns to political economy and names three categories of critique: the absorption of social capital, the invisible exploitation carried out through artificial intelligence, and the reproduction of bourgeois ideology.

In Liu's account, each era brings the player into a closer relation with capital. Stand-alone games such as the FC console resemble simple commodity circulation, ending once money changes hands. In the rent era, players buy time cards, which Liu likens to Marx's ground rent, with the player acting as both tenant farmer and labourer. In the consumption era, nominally free games rest on what Liu calls an illusion, because makers manufacture false needs that players then pay to meet. Liu holds that capital is thereby absorbing the sphere of reproduction into production. Liu then argues that game events harvest players' social networks through sharing and vote-gathering, that AI-controlled opponents covertly gather data which can be monetised, and that game worlds such as Minecraft teach players to think only within bourgeois limits.

Liu concludes that game capitalization is a historically and practically real concept, and that the game world is not purely virtual, since it derives from reality and acts back on it. Games are becoming a way of life for young people, Liu writes, and it is mistaken to say that games themselves cause addiction; the problem should be understood at the deeper level of capital's logic of self-expansion. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese Marxist scholars apply Marx's concepts, such as simple commodity circulation and ground rent, to video games and digital capitalism.
quoteEn: In fact, the game world is not a purely virtual world; to a large extent it derives from reality, and people's various activities within it in turn act upon the real world.
quoteZh: 事实上，游戏世界并非纯粹虚拟的世界，在很大程度上它来源于现实，并且，人们在游戏世界当中的各种活动还会作用于现实世界。

glossary.explanation: Marx and Engels' method of explaining social development through material production and relations of production. Chinese texts use the term for the Marxist theory of history.
The author's term for the process by which capital turns games, once a leisure activity, into a means of self-expansion and surplus extraction.
The author's name for the present stage in which game production and play are fully integrated into capitalist relations of production.
A term for contemporary capitalism in which digital platforms, data and algorithms are central to accumulation.

t: The self and the subject in the perspective of the materialist conception of history
zh: 唯物史观视域中的自我与主体
paras: Sun Lin takes up a problem that idealist philosophy could never settle: how the self and the subject can be internally consistent. The article, a newspaper-length piece in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (August 2024), argues that only Marx, through the materialist conception of history, unified the two on real ground, both historically and logically.

The text first traces the idealist path to this unity through four thinkers: Descartes, Kant, Fichte and Hegel. It then turns to Marx's critique, which Sun presents as inseparable from his critique of the modernity of capital. The article ends with the materialist account of the real subject's self-activity.

In Sun's reading, each idealist step achieves only a partial or illusory unity. Descartes resolves the mind–body problem by appeal to a spiritual substance, which splits self from subject. Kant separates self-consciousness from free will, placing them at the poles of theory and practice. Fichte unites them through the self's action but cannot explain concrete, varied reality. Hegel gives the unity a social and historical form through the externalisation and retrieval of self-consciousness, but makes it "absolute", which for Sun turns the unity into illusion.

Sun's central move is to argue that Hegel's logic of objectification mirrors the logic of capital under private ownership, which externalises itself to capture profit and surplus value and then returns to itself as expanded capital. Hegel's consistency of self and subject is therefore, in this account, a false unity grounded in fetishism, in which relations between people become relations between things. The materialist conception of history instead raises the speculative subject to a real subject whose self-activity achieves a historically conditioned consistency. Sun calls for overcoming fetishism by raising productive forces and labour capacity, and moving towards a society of the free and all-round development of every individual. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese Marxist reading of the Descartes–Kant–Fichte–Hegel sequence on selfhood and subjectivity, and its link to the critique of capital.
quoteEn: The materialist conception of history raises the speculative subject to a real subject that always floats beyond appearance, and through its own objectifying activity, that is, the real subject's self-activity, it achieves a historically conditioned internal consistency of subject and self.
quoteZh: 唯物史观把思辨的主体提升为始终浮现在表象之外的实在主体，通过自身的对象化活动也就是实在主体的自我活动，实现主体与自我有历史条件的内在一致性。

glossary.explanation: Marx and Engels' theory that material production and social relations shape historical development. Chinese texts use it as the standard term for historical materialism.
Marx's term for the way social relations between people appear as relations between things, especially under commodity and capital relations.
The process by which a subject expresses itself in an external object or activity. The article applies it to both Hegel's self-consciousness and the movement of capital.

t: Cultivating the real-economy soil for Chinese modernization
zh: 厚植中国式现代化的实体经济沃土
paras: Xia Jiechang asks why the real economy matters for Chinese modernization and how it should be strengthened. Writing in the Economic Daily in October 2024, Xia argues that a strong real economy is the material and technological foundation of Chinese modernization and of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Xia holds that the sector must be made solid, strong and excellent, and that this is the basis for high-quality development.

The piece is built in three parts. It first sets out the real economy's position, drawing on Xi Jinping's statements from 2020 to 2023, the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the Third Plenum decision of 2024. It then applies the new development philosophy (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) to the real economy. It ends with four practical areas of work: modern agriculture, new industrialization, a new services system, and institutional support.

Xia's core move is to treat each element of the new development philosophy as a feature of high-quality real-economy development. Innovation is the first driving force, resting on technology, institutional reform and talent. Coordination means the real economy and the virtual economy exist side by side, but the virtual economy must serve the real one, and manufacturing, agriculture and producer services must advance together. Green growth is an inherent requirement, openness is the necessary path, and sharing is the fundamental aim, tied to employment and common prosperity. In the policy section, Xia calls for a broad view of agriculture, better rural infrastructure and digital agriculture. Xia also calls for stronger indigenous innovation and supply-chain resilience, and deeper integration of the real and digital economies. Further proposals are to merge manufacturing and services and to integrate urban and rural development.

Xia concludes that finance should serve the real economy, with tighter supervision of funds circulating idly or drifting away from the real economy. Fiscal policy should become more forceful and efficient to support the real–digital integration, and industrial policy should mainly give direction. Xia notes that the real economy is evolving into a "new real economy" fused with digital technology, and that a matching fiscal framework remains a new research question. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how official economic discourse in late 2024 links the real economy, the new development philosophy and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: China's economy was built on the real economy, and it must rely on the real economy to move into the future.
quoteZh: 我国经济是靠实体经济起家的，也要靠实体经济走向未来。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's path to modernization under Communist Party leadership. It is described as having features such as a huge population, common prosperity and harmony between humans and nature.
The part of the economy that produces goods and services, mainly manufacturing, agriculture and some producer services. It is contrasted with the virtual (financial) economy.
A framework put forward under Xi Jinping that stresses innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth driven by innovation, efficiency and sustainability.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal, linked to the second centenary goal of building a modern socialist country by 2049.
A policy concept stressing industrialization that is digital, networked, intelligent and green, and integrated with information technology.

t: Grasping the rich connotations of the new form of human civilization
zh: 深刻把握人类文明新形态的丰富内涵
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 22 October 2024
paras: Ma Min takes up Xi Jinping's claim that Chinese modernization has created a "new form of human civilization" and asks in what sense it is new. The article argues that the two concepts are internally linked: Chinese modernization supplies the path and method, while the new civilizational form is its direction, goal and essential requirement. In Ma's account, the novelty lies in a socialist civilization that transcends Western capitalist modernity while drawing on Chinese tradition.

The commentary has three parts. It first places the concept in the history of the idea of "civilization" and the current decline of Western civilization. It then sets out four ways in which the new form is said to surpass capitalist modern civilization. Finally it treats the form's Chinese cultural roots and its world significance.

Ma argues that industrial civilization arose with Western capitalism and has a dual character: historically progressive against agrarian society, yet marked by exploitation through wage labour, extreme individualism and colonial expansion. Modernization, in this view, is not the same as Westernization, and the author sees an "East rising, West declining" pattern in the present world. Socialist civilization is said to surpass the West in four relationships: balanced material and spiritual progress, replacing "capital-centred" with "people-centred" development, harmony between humans and nature, and peaceful coexistence rather than power politics. Ma also traces its Chinese character to ideas such as renewal, "the people as the foundation of the state", "all under heaven is shared", unity of heaven and humanity, and harmony among nations, and presents it as the outcome of the Two Integrations and of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

Ma concludes that this civilization is both Chinese and global, offering a "Chinese approach" and "Chinese wisdom" that reflect common human values. The author concedes that its creation is a long process with many practical and theoretical problems still unresolved, and calls for exploration that is rooted in China while looking to the world. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the official concept of a new form of human civilization is tied to Chinese modernization, a critique of Western capitalist modernity and appeals to traditional Chinese thought.
quoteEn: The \"newness\" of the new form of human civilization emerges in comparison with capitalist civilization, develops in the competition between the socialist and capitalist social systems, and is continually summed up and distilled in the practice of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 人类文明新形态之“新”，是在与资本主义文明的比较中呈现出来的；是在社会主义与资本主义两种社会制度的竞争中发展起来的；是在中国式现代化实践中不断总结、提炼出来的。

glossary.explanation: Official Party concept of a modernization path with Chinese characteristics, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as an alternative to Western modernization.
Official phrase for the civilization said to be created by Chinese modernization, used by Xi Jinping since around 2021. It is presented as a socialist alternative to Western modernity.
Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions and contemporary circumstances.

t: An important innovation in the Marxist theory of productive forces
zh: 马克思主义生产力理论的重要创新
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily in June 2024, asks what the concept of new quality productive forces adds to Marxist theory. Ji Zhengju argues that Xi Jinping's call to develop new quality productive forces answers the question of what kind of productive forces the new era needs and how to develop them. In Ji's reading, it is a major theoretical result of Xi Jinping's economic thought and gives the Marxist theory of productive forces new content.

The article is organised around five aspects of the Marxist theory of productive forces: its driving force, its principles, its process, its purpose and its laws of development. For each, Ji sets a classical Marxist proposition beside the corresponding feature of new quality productive forces.

On the driving force, Ji notes that Marx and Engels stressed the revolutionary role of science and technology, while new quality productive forces are marked by innovation and superior quality, treating science and technology as the primary productive force and innovation as the primary driver. On the process, they are defined by a leap (yuesheng) in labourers, means of labour, objects of labour and their combination, which Ji says stresses qualitative change more than "development" does. On the laws of development, Ji holds that productive forces determine relations of production. New quality productive forces therefore require new relations of production, deeper economic and science-and-technology reforms, and the removal of institutional bottlenecks.

Ji concludes that each of these points enriches Marxism, and that high-quality development meets the people's growing need for a better life, which Ji presents as a new application of the Marxist view that production serves human free and all-round development. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the official case that new quality productive forces develop Marxist theory.
quoteEn: The proposal of new quality productive forces is another major theoretical achievement of Xi Jinping's economic thought, and it injects new content into the Marxist theory of productive forces.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的提出是习近平经济思想的又一重大理论成果，为马克思主义生产力理论注入了新的内涵。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023–24 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, with high technology, high efficiency and high quality. It is now central to official economic policy discourse.
An official goal since the 19th Party Congress (2017) that stresses quality, efficiency and meeting people's needs over growth in scale alone.
The official name for the economic component of Xi Jinping Thought, which the Party presents as guiding China's economic work in the new era.

t: Guiding high-quality development with a new theory of productive forces
zh: 以新的生产力理论指导高质量发展
paras: This short newspaper commentary, originally published in Economic Daily, argues that developing new quality productive forces is an inherent requirement of, and a key lever for, high-quality development. Han draws on Xi Jinping's statements that high-quality development needs guidance from a new theory of productive forces, and presents these remarks as an innovative development of the Marxist theory of productive forces.

The piece first links productive forces to Chinese modernization and the 20th Party Congress (2022) report. It then shows how new quality productive forces fit the requirements of high-quality development, and closes with three practical areas: scientific and technological innovation, deepening reform and opening up, and talent.

Han starts from the Marxist claim that productive forces are the most active and revolutionary factor and the ultimate determining force in social development. In Han's account, high-quality development is development that embodies the new development philosophy, and new quality productive forces match it in three ways. They are innovation-led, high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality; they raise total factor productivity and spread digital technology, which supports common prosperity; and they are inherently green and low-carbon. Drawing on historical materialism, Han adds that relations of production must adapt to productive forces, so deeper reform is needed to remove obstacles and form new relations of production suited to them.

Han calls for faster breakthroughs in core technologies, especially original and disruptive innovation, applied through China's huge market and complete industrial system. Han also urges higher-level opening up and better mechanisms for cultivating talent, including a climate that encourages innovation and tolerates failure. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary ties new quality productive forces to Marxist theory and to high-quality development.
quoteEn: To develop new quality productive forces, we must stimulate internal drivers through comprehensively deepening reform, especially of the economic and science-and-technology systems, clear the bottlenecks that constrain them, and form new relations of production suited to them.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力，必须通过全面深化改革激发内生动力，尤其是通过深化经济体制和科技体制等方面的改革，着力打通束缚新质生产力发展的堵点卡点，形成与新质生产力发展相适应的新型生产关系。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping from 2023, describing innovation-led productive forces marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality. It is presented as a development of Marxist productive-force theory.
The official goal, since the late 2010s, of shifting the economy from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and sustainability.
Five principles set out in 2015: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
The official name for China's path to modernization, emphasised since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A goal of prosperity shared by all people, presented in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism.

t: Letting economic structural reform play its leading role
zh: 发挥经济体制改革牵引作用
paras: Writing in Qiushi (2024, no. 18), Han Wenxiu interprets the decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. Han argues that the decision's emphasis on letting economic structural reform play a leading role (牵引作用) is of major significance, and that deepening economic reform remains the focus of comprehensive reform. The piece is an official commentary on the document rather than an independent research article.

The article has three parts. The first explains why economic reform should lead. The second, the longest, goes through the decision's main economic tasks under eight headings: a high-standard socialist market economy, high-quality development, comprehensive innovation, macroeconomic governance, urban-rural integration, high-level opening up, livelihoods, and ecological civilization. The third part sets out how these tasks are to be carried out.

Han gives three reasons for economic reform's leading role. It accords with the Marxist principles that the productive forces determine the relations of production and the economic base determines the superstructure, so that economic reform affects the pace of reform elsewhere. It is the basic experience of reform and opening up, from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee onward, centred on the relationship between government and market. And it is required by high-quality development: Han cites per capita GDP rising from 156 US dollars to 12,700 in 2023 against a middle-developed-country average above 20,000, and says China remains a developing country facing unbalanced and inadequate development. The listed tasks include the Two Unwaverings, a unified national market, new quality productive forces, fiscal and tax reform, institutional opening up, and a distribution structure with a large middle.

On implementation, Han calls for strengthening Party leadership, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and for assigning clear responsibility for each reform task. Han also calls for stronger supervision, respect for local and popular initiative, and a firm stand against formalism and bureaucratism, with reforms judged by results and public satisfaction. The article closes by urging unity around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, so that reform can drive high-quality development and Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an authoritative official reading of the Third Plenum's economic reform agenda and its stated rationale.
quoteEn: The essence of reform is to adjust and optimise the relations of production and the superstructure according to the needs of developing the productive forces, thereby liberating and developing social productive forces and stimulating and strengthening social vitality.
quoteZh: 改革的本质，就是根据生产力发展的需要，调整和优化生产关系及上层建筑，从而解放和发展社会生产力，激发和增强社会活力。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation in emerging and future industries.
A Party formula, adopted in 2021, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The official goal of shifting from high-speed growth to growth stressing quality, efficiency and innovation. It was put forward at the 19th Party Congress (2017).

t: Grasping the "Second Integration" through systematization and theoretical grounding
zh: 以体系化学理化为着力点深刻把握“第二个结合”
paras: This commentary, first published in People's Daily in October 2024, asks how to study Xi Jinping Thought on Culture in depth. Wang Weiguang argues that a key route is to grasp the "Second Integration" (combining Marxism's basic tenets with excellent traditional Chinese culture) in a systematic, theory-based way. In Wang's account, this means handling three relationships correctly: preserving fundamental principles and innovating, the "soul" and "root" lines of culture, and "substance" and "application".

The piece opens by presenting Xi Jinping's cultural thought as a complete theoretical system that has developed Marxist cultural theory. It then has three main sections. The first explains why the Second Integration is the necessary path for socialist culture with Chinese characteristics. The second and third take up the relationships above, and a closing section links theory and practice through "substance" and "application".

Wang gives three reasons for the Second Integration's importance. It enriches Marxist cultural theory, it is required for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and it is inherent in the flourishing of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics. On method, Wang treats "preserving fundamental principles" as the precondition and innovation as the driving force. Marxism must remain the guiding ideology and the Party must keep its cultural leadership, while traditional ideas are reactivated and given contemporary meaning. Wang's second move uses Xi's image of the Marxist "soul line" and the traditional-culture "root line", which must not be abandoned. Marxism is the standard for separating the essence of tradition from its dross, and Wang says this is how the Second Integration resolves the dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western, and consolidates the Chinese nation's cultural subjectivity. Wang's third move reads Xi's thought as unifying epistemology (what the Second Integration is) with methodology (how to carry it out).

Wang concludes that advancing the Second Integration requires following Xi Jinping Thought on Culture and uniting study with thought, application and practice. This is meant to deepen the integration of Marxism and traditional culture and open a new phase of work on propaganda, ideology and culture. The piece is a statement of the official interpretation, useful for seeing how the Party's cultural-theory line is framed. Read the original if you want a concise authoritative statement of how the Second Integration is theorised within Xi Jinping's cultural thought.
quoteEn: Preserving fundamental principles is the precondition; innovation is the driving force.
quoteZh: 守正是前提，创新是动力。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with excellent traditional Chinese culture. It is the second of the Two Integrations, the first being the combination of Marxism with China's concrete realities.

The body of Xi Jinping's views on culture, ideology and propaganda work, formally put forward in October 2023 and presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.literal: the sinification and modernization of Marxism
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the present era.
A term in recent Party discourse for a nation's self-awareness and independence in culture. Here it means the Chinese nation's firm cultural self, rooted in its own history and tradition.

glossary.literal: upholding what is right and innovating
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for keeping to core principles and direction while innovating in ideas and methods.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: The fourfold meaning of Marx and Engels's thought on civilization
st: With implications for developing a new form of human civilization
zh: 马克思恩格斯文明思想的四重意蕴
zhSub: 兼论对发展人类文明新形态的当代启示
source: Teaching and Research at Renmin University (人大教学与研究), 13 September 2024
paras: Huang Wenyan and Song Youwen ask what Marx and Engels's thought on civilization contains and what it offers for understanding the "new form of human civilization" that Xi Jinping put forward in his speech marking the Party's centenary (2021). They argue that the thought has four layers, which they label practice–civilization, history–civilization, dialectics–civilization and revolution–civilization. These layers build on one another. The authors claim that the thought goes beyond earlier Western theories of civilization and is the theoretical root of the Chinese Communist Party's creation of a new form of human civilization.

The article has an introduction, four main sections and a short conclusion. Each section sets out one layer of Marx and Engels's thought. Each then draws practical lessons for China's current efforts to develop the new form of human civilization. The history section sets Marx and Engels against Toynbee, Jaspers and Huntington.

In the first two layers, the authors read civilization through historical materialism. Civilization arises from the material production practice of real individuals and has practical and social attributes, with the people as its main agent. Marx and Engels divide civilization forms by economic social formation, from slave-society to feudal, capitalist and communist civilization. In the authors' view, Toynbee, Jaspers and Huntington describe features of civilizations but miss their decisive cause. The third layer treats capitalist civilization as dual, both progressive and barbaric. It then sketches communist civilization, built on social ownership, planned production, distribution according to need, the withering away of the state and free and all-round individual development. The fourth layer holds that the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production makes revolution the basic means of change, and that the proletarian party is the organising force.

The authors conclude that the new form of human civilization sublates capitalist modern civilization and unites national and world character. In practice they call for the Two Unwaverings, guidance and regulation of capital so that it serves civilization, continued Party leadership and comprehensive deepening of reform. They also call for the new development philosophy, high-quality development and a people-centred stance. They add that this civilization draws on the ancient Chinese ideal of harmony among nations and can offer other countries a path to diverse modernities. Read the original if you want a systematic example of how Chinese theorists derive the concept of a new form of human civilization from Marx and Engels's texts.
quoteEn: Marx and Engels divided civilization forms on the basis of economic social formations. In doing so they fundamentally identified the essential driving force, inner laws and trajectory of civilization's development, and fixed the basic coordinates for grasping civilization forms today.
quoteZh: 马克思恩格斯基于经济的社会形态划分文明形态,从根本上发现了文明发展的本质动力、内在规律和演进轨迹,还为当前把握文明形态确定了根本坐标。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in his speech at the Party's centenary in 2021. Official discourse uses it for the civilization it says China's modernization path is creating.
The official line of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official guideline, set out in 2015, that development should be innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared.
The official aim of the economy since the late 2010s: growth that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability, not only speed or scale.

t: Several issues in the study of China's fine traditional culture that call for deeper reflection
zh: 中华优秀传统文化研究中需再深化思考的若干问题
paras: Since Xi Jinping put forward the Two Integrations, Chinese scholarship on "fine traditional Chinese culture" has grown rapidly, but Mei Rongzheng notes that disagreements remain. The article offers the author's own views on three of them, for discussion with colleagues. Mei's thesis is that the concept must be defined precisely, that old culture must be sifted into dross and essence before it is used, and that Marxist scientific abstraction is the proper route to its creative transformation and innovative development.

The article has three parts. The first sets out five "is" and "is not" propositions about the concept. The second defends full use of ancient culture against scholars who take a negative view, drawing on Lenin, Mao Zedong and Xi. The third turns to method and to the Marxist way of moving from the concrete to the abstract and back again, illustrated with Capital, Mao's reinterpretations of classical phrases and Xi's concepts.

Mei argues first that the fine tradition is not the same as all of ancient culture. It is a narrower, integrative, historical set of elements marked by scientific, democratic, revolutionary and popular qualities. Mei rejects both historical nihilism and reactionary revivalism, including calls to "Confucianise" China or the Party. Second, citing Mao, Mei holds that essence and dross often cannot be cleanly separated, so they must be judged by the people's standpoint and the test of practice. Mei lists six distinctions Mao drew, for example between feudal-era culture and feudalism, and between a thinker's ideas and later accretions. Third, Mei rejects the view that fine tradition needs no transformation, since simply grafting non-Marxist material onto Marxism would produce eclecticism. Concepts such as Confucian benevolence should be stripped of their feudal basis and then filled with the content of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

Mei concludes that these steps, which the article calls scientific abstraction, give a method for combining Marxism with fine traditional culture and for turning old concepts into those of a modern Chinese civilization. Mei adds that applying the method to traditional culture is a new field with many open problems and must not be oversimplified. Read the original if you want to see how a Marxist scholar tries to justify and discipline the Second Integration, with Mao's methods of analysis and Marx's method of abstraction as the guide.
quoteEn: Simply grafting the non-Marxist onto the Marxist can only produce eclecticism, not Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 非马克思主义和马克思主义的简单嫁接只能出折中主义，不能出中国化时代化的马克思主义。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second, put forward in 2021–2023).
The official term for those elements of China's past culture judged worth inheriting. The article defines it as narrower than "ancient Chinese culture".
Short for 创造性转化、创新性发展, Xi Jinping's formula for reworking traditional culture so that it serves present needs.
In official Chinese discourse, a label for tendencies seen as wrongly denying or discrediting the Chinese revolution, socialism or China's history and culture.
The official name of China's path and system since reform and opening up. The article treats it as the ultimate criterion for what in tradition is worth drawing on.

t: Scientifically grasping the methods of comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 科学把握全面深化改革方式方法
paras: Song Jianxiao's commentary, first published in Economic Daily in July 2024, asks how the drive to comprehensively deepen reform should be carried out. It starts from Xi Jinping's remarks at a symposium with entrepreneurs and experts in Jinan in May 2024. There Xi said that deepening reform must centre on Chinese modernization, highlight key points, hold to the right value orientation and attend to method. Song's answer is that reform should rest on three methods: upholding fundamental principles while innovating, stressing systems integration, and ensuring implementation.

The piece is organised under three headings that correspond to these methods. The first covers "keeping to the right path and innovating" and links it to Xi's description of this approach as an important way of thinking for the Party's governance in the new era. The second treats systems integration as both a feature and a methodology of reform since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third deals with making reform measures take effect on the ground. Each section ends in three or four concrete requirements.

On the first method, Song argues that keeping to the right path and innovating form a dialectical unity of change and constancy, continuity and development, principle and creativity. Holding to the right path means upholding the Party's leadership, Marxism, socialism with Chinese characteristics and whole-process people's democracy. Innovation means breaking institutional obstacles and escaping path dependence. On the second, Song calls for top-level design that keeps policy orientations consistent and links overall planning with local conditions. Reforms in the market economy, high-quality development and new quality productive forces should be coordinated as a "combination of punches". On the third, Song says reform is hard to implement as well as important, and calls for a "nail-driving spirit", clear priorities, and results that people feel. Reform should be pursued with urgency and also with attention to timing, degree and effect, doing what is within capacity and persevering over the long term.

Song concludes that grasping these methods lets reform keep its direction and momentum, with coordination across fields and measures that deliver. Reform is presented as a complex systemic undertaking that needs steady effort and no slackening. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary frames the methodology of reform in the Xi era, in terms of the Party's leadership, dialectics and implementation.
quoteEn: Further comprehensively deepening reform is not a single reform in one field or one aspect, but comprehensive and systematic reform and improvement.
quoteZh: 进一步全面深化改革，不是某个领域某个方面的单项改革，而是全面的系统的改革和改进。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path to modernization. Party texts present it as the central theme of the national task.

glossary.en: keeping to the right path and innovating
glossary.literal: uphold what is correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A phrase in Xi Jinping's discourse that pairs fidelity to fundamental principles with creative development. Officially it is described as a method of thought for governance.
The official term for China's democratic model, put forward by Xi Jinping. It stresses popular participation at every stage of political and policy processes, not just in elections.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 that refers to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries. It is linked to the goal of high-quality development.
An official economic goal that prioritises quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth alone.
The Party's official name for its current path and system, combining Marxist principles with China's conditions since reform and opening up.

t: Adhering to reform and innovation to promote the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 坚持改革创新推动新质生产力发展
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 17 July 2024, treats the development of new quality productive forces as both a development task and a reform task. Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that developing them requires deepening reform comprehensively and forming new types of relations of production suited to them, Ding argues that bottlenecks must be cleared so that these forces supply steady new momentum for high-quality development.

The article is organised in three parts. The first concerns deepening reform to release innovative vitality in science and technology. The second concerns building a modern industrial system. The third concerns shaping new relations of production through economic reform and reform of the education, science and technology, and talent systems.

On innovation, Ding holds that it is the defining feature of new quality productive forces and covers technology, business models, management and institutions. The author sees weak original innovation, dependence on foreign key technologies and low conversion of results, and calls for a improved new-type whole-nation system, with centralised Party leadership of science and technology work, and for reform of science management, funding and evaluation, together with greater openness in international cooperation. On industry, Ding calls for making industries more intelligent, greener and more integrated, through supply-side structural reform, digital infrastructure, market-based green policy tools and closer linkage among sectors, regions and firms of different sizes. On relations of production, the author applies the principle that productive forces determine relations of production, and proposes a high-standard socialist market economy, a unified national market, and the Two Unwaverings.

Ding concludes that talent is the primary resource and that innovation-driven development is in essence talent-driven. The author proposes integrating education, science and technology, and talent strategies, cultivating innovative talent independently, and reforming evaluation and incentive systems to give value to knowledge, technology and data as production factors. Read the original if you want a compact example of how an official Chinese economic newspaper links new quality productive forces to reform of science policy, industrial upgrading and market institutions.
quoteEn: Accelerating the development of new quality productive forces is both a question of development and a question of reform.
quoteZh: 加快发展新质生产力，既是发展命题，也是改革命题。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, characterised in official usage as high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality.
The official goal for China's economy since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

glossary.literal: new-type system of the whole nation
glossary.explanation: An official term for mobilising state, Party, market and research resources nationally to achieve major scientific and technological goals, such as key core technologies.
The official policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
An economic policy line introduced in 2015 aimed at improving the structure of supply, cutting excess capacity and raising the quality of the industrial system.

t: Promoting further comprehensively deepening reform in the spirit of self-reform
zh: 以自我革命精神推动进一步全面深化改革
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2024, Gao Liwei takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its blueprint for further comprehensively deepening reform. The commentary argues that the Party must keep leading social revolution through its own self-reform, and that this spirit is the precondition for carrying reform through and for supplying Chinese modernization with momentum and institutional guarantees.

The piece has three parts. It first presents courage in self-reform as the Party's defining character and greatest strength. It then explains why further deepening reform requires thoroughgoing self-reform. Finally it sets out four practical directions: leadership capacity, Party rules and supervision, the political and organisational functions of Party organisations, and conduct and anti-corruption work.

Gao grounds the first claim in Marx and Engels and in Mao Zedong. On this reading, the proletarian revolution is distinctive because it constantly criticises itself, and self-criticism is a form of dialectical negation. Because the Party, in the author's account, has no interests apart from those of the great majority, it can accept supervision by the people and escape the "historical cycle of rise and fall". Gao then argues that reform has entered deep waters, with unprecedented breadth, sharpness and complexity. Emancipating the mind, which the author calls the fundamental driver of reform, is impossible without turning the blade inward.

Gao calls for improving the Party's leadership methods, strengthening Party regulations, combining self-supervision with supervision by the people, and persisting with the Central Committee's eight-point regulation. The author also calls for tackling formalism, bureaucratism and new or hidden forms of corruption, so that the strategic plans for reform become real strength. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links the Party's self-reform to the current reform agenda.
quoteEn: Whether there is a strong spirit of self-reform, whether the Party has the hardy quality of self-purification, and whether it can persist in continual self-reform bear on the success or failure of comprehensively deepening reform and on the success of the cause of the Party and the people.
quoteZh: 有没有强烈的自我革命精神，具不具备自我净化的过硬特质，能不能坚持不断自我革命，事关全面深化改革的成败得失，事关党和人民事业成功与否。

glossary.explanation: A term stressing that the Party must critique, purify and renew itself. It has been emphasised in Party discourse under Xi Jinping.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
The theme of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (July 2024), which adopted a decision on reform measures through 2029.
Rules adopted by the Party leadership in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The idea of recurring dynastic rise and decline, which the Party says it can escape through self-reform and supervision by the people.

t: Comprehensively deepening economic structural reform in the new era
zh: 全面深化新时代经济体制改革
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2024, Zhao Xiaolei takes up the July 2024 Decision of the Party's Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. The article asks what the goal of a "high-standard socialist market economy" means and why economic reform is to lead the wider reform agenda. Zhao argues that the goal is the latest stage of a consistent line whose purpose is to liberate and develop the productive forces.

The piece is a short commentary in four parts. It first traces how the reform goal has matured from the 14th Party Congress (1992) to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It then sets out a Marxist theory of productive forces against Western growth theory. It next reviews how successive Party meetings tied reform to productive forces, and it ends by discussing reform together with opening up.

Zhao's central move is theoretical. Western classical and neoclassical economics, including endogenous growth theory, treat production as resource allocation and technological progress, measured through factor productivity. Marxist political economy, in Zhao's account, adds that production is a social process. Productive forces therefore have a social as well as a material and technical attribute, and developing them means adjusting relations of production, not merely increasing output. On this basis Zhao reads the reform record, from 1978 through the Scientific Outlook on Development to the new development philosophy, as one thread. The change in the principal contradiction in the new era shifts the emphasis to balanced, higher-quality growth. Here Zhao presents high-quality development and new quality productive forces as the theory and form of advanced productive forces suited to a high-standard market economy.

Zhao concludes that reform must proceed together with opening up. Drawing on the logic of exchange, specialisation and international trade, Zhao says a market economy is by nature open. The article calls for steady institutional opening in rules, regulations, management and standards. It also calls for a role in reforming global economic governance and for opening that supports the real economy. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account of how Chinese economists link the 2024 reform decision to Marxist productive-forces theory and the Party's reform chronology.
quoteEn: Developing the productive forces is not merely a quantitative increase in material production; relations of production must also be adjusted to suit the development of the productive forces.
quoteZh: 发展生产力不单单是物质生产的量的增长，还要对生产关系进行调整以适应生产力发展。

glossary.zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.pinyin: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
glossary.explanation: A reform goal set at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the Third Plenum (2024), which aims to build it fully by 2035. It is the successor to the earlier aims of establishing and then improving the socialist market economy.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation and a shift towards higher-quality growth.
An official development goal that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed. It is tied to the new development philosophy.
Xi Jinping's formula of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, introduced in 2015.
The guiding concept of the Hu Jintao era, adopted at the 17th Party Congress (2007). It stresses coordinated and sustainable development.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models.

t: Adhering to a people-centred approach in comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 坚持以人民为中心推进全面深化改革
paras: Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), this commentary asks what it means to keep a people-centred orientation while comprehensively deepening reform. An argues that such an orientation is the fundamental driving force of Chinese modernization as it advances the building of a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In the article's account, the people-centred approach shapes the problem focus, strategic layout and value standards of reform and opening up.

Published in the China Social Sciences Today in October 2024, the piece is built around four themes. It covers the liberation and development of new quality productive forces, the people's principal role and creative initiative, the pooling of the broadest public wisdom and strength, and the promotion of the people's well-being as the highest criterion of reform results. It draws repeatedly on Xi Jinping's remarks and the Plenum's conclusions.

An's first move rests on the Marxist view that the fundamental task of socialism is to liberate and develop the productive forces. The author traces reform from building a market economy to deepening market mechanisms to innovation-driven development, and says that removing obstacles to new quality productive forces is now a key breakthrough point for improving living standards. The second move holds that reform is in essence a readjustment of existing interests and institutions, so it needs the people's creativity. The author says experience from the people's practice should be generalised from single 'points' of breakthrough to wider 'surfaces', and that reform has entered a stage of 'tackling tough problems' and holistic design. Reform therefore spans the economic, political, social, cultural and ecological fields and calls for systematic integration, ideological emancipation and the Two Integrations.

For An, popular satisfaction is the test of reform. The author contrasts the present approach with the early strategy of letting some people and regions get rich first, and says reform now aims at common prosperity. An calls for concrete measures on income distribution, education, employment, social security, elderly and child care, healthcare, housing and environmental governance, so that people's sense of gain, happiness and security keeps growing. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link the Third Plenum's reform agenda to people-centred and productive-forces arguments.
quoteEn: Comprehensively deepening reform is not confined to the single field of the economy, but involves comprehensive deepening of institutions and mechanisms in the economic, political, social, cultural and ecological fields.
quoteZh: 全面深化改革并不是局限于经济这一单一领域的改革，而是涉及经济、政治、社会、文化和生态领域体制机制的全面深化改革。

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A term Xi Jinping introduced in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation. It is used to guide economic policy and reform.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, stressed in recent Party policy as a requirement of socialism.
The Party's formula for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of national revitalisation, tied to the Chinese Dream and to modernization by mid-century.

t: Improving the institutions and mechanisms for developing new quality productive forces in light of local conditions
zh: 健全因地制宜发展新质生产力体制机制
