paras: This commentary by Liu Quanhong and Liu Fang, first published in Economic Daily on 15 October 2024, takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee's call (2024) to improve the institutions and mechanisms for developing new quality productive forces in light of local conditions. The authors argue that this task is not only a question of development but also one of reform. In their account, deepening reform must produce production relations that fit the new productive forces.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why developing new quality productive forces is a reform issue, taking in turn technological innovation, the allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading. The second sets out the methodology of "adapting measures to local conditions" (yīn dì zhì yí). The third lists systemic reforms in science and technology, traditional industries, emerging industries, future industries and factor allocation.

Liu and Liu rest the argument on the Marxist premise that productive forces determine production relations. They say that new quality productive forces arise from technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and deep industrial transformation, and that each of these is held back by institutional obstacles, such as weak basic research, mismatched factors and a hostile external environment. On local conditions, the authors warn against three errors: rushing in en masse, hurrying for quick results, and favouring the new while abandoning the old. They say some localities chase hot sectors such as AI and hydrogen without regard to their own endowments. This, they argue, produces homogenised industrial plans, "involutionary" investment-attraction policies and fiscal strain. They hold that traditional and emerging industries support each other, and that traditional industries should be upgraded rather than discarded.

The authors propose strengthening the new whole-nation system for science and technology, and building interdisciplinary research centres. They also propose standards and exit channels for inefficient, high-emission capacity, and clearing out improper investment-attraction policies. For future industries they propose mechanisms for commercialising results, application scenarios and flexible regulation. They further call for a unified national market, "patient capital", better talent systems and income distribution that reflects the market value of knowledge, technology and data. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the policy agenda that official commentary linked to the 2024 Plenum's reform decisions on new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces is both a question of development and a question of reform.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力，既是发展命题，也是改革命题

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces led by technological innovation and characterised by high technology, high efficiency and high quality.

glossary.literal: act according to the land, make suitable arrangements
glossary.explanation: An old Chinese idiom, cited here from the Eastern Han text Wu Yue Chunqiu, meaning to devise solutions suited to the actual circumstances of each place. The article treats it as a methodology for regional development.
A mode of organising science and technology in which the state mobilises resources across institutions to reach major strategic goals, adapted to the market economy.
Long-term investment that tolerates slow returns, promoted in official documents as suited to early-stage, hard-technology enterprises.

t: Accelerating the building of a high-standard socialist market economy
zh: 加快构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2024, Guan Xueling interprets the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (July 2024) on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. The article asks what it means to build a high-standard socialist market economy and how this should be done. Guan argues that such a system is an important safeguard of Chinese modernization and that it rests on three tasks: implementing the Two Unwaverings, building a unified national market, and improving institutions for high-standard opening up.

The commentary opens with the historical sequence from reform and opening up in 1978 to the 18th Party Congress's call for comprehensive deepening of reform in 2013. It then traces how the Party's formulation developed: "establishing" a socialist market economy at the 14th Congress, "improving" it at the 16th, and "building a high-standard" one at the 20th. Three thematic sections follow, on business entities, the national market and opening up.

Guan presents the socialist market economy as a major innovation grounded in Chinese practice and as the most effective route to Chinese modernization. In this reading, the move from the market's "basic" to its "decisive" role in allocating resources shows the historical logic of the system. On enterprises, the author argues that both public and non-public sectors are essential. State-owned enterprises should deepen reform, strengthen their core functions and lead in breaking through technological bottlenecks. Private firms, which Guan says face real difficulties, need reassurance through the Two Unwaverings.

On the national market, Guan says commodity and service markets are fairly well integrated, but factor and resource markets lag. The author proposes four steps, including a better institutional framework, removal of barriers to factor flows, and fuller use of idle resources. These would serve new quality productive forces. On opening up, Guan describes a shift to institutional opening, meaning alignment of "behind-the-border" rules, with free trade pilot zones and the Belt and Road Initiative as its vehicles, and calls for high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of the 2024 Plenum's market-economy agenda and the figures it cites.
quoteEn: A high-standard socialist market economy is an important safeguard of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制是中国式现代化的重要保障

glossary.zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.pinyin: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
glossary.explanation: A formulation stressed at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the Third Plenum (2024) for upgrading the existing socialist market economy. It combines the market's decisive role in resource allocation with a stronger role for government and the primacy of public ownership.

The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector. It is used in Party documents to define the relationship between state-owned and private business.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
Opening up that centres on aligning rules, regulations, management and standards with international norms, rather than only on cross-border flows of goods and factors.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Handling well the relationship between government and market, the core issue
zh: 处理好政府和市场关系这个核心问题
paras: Writing in the Economic Daily after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Zhou Wen argues that handling the relationship between government and market is the core issue of economic reform. The article presents the Plenum's Decision as the latest theoretical advance on this question and as part of Xi Jinping's economic thought. Zhou's answer is that a "high-level socialist market economy" requires the market to play the decisive role in allocating resources while the government plays its role better.

The commentary has four parts. It first treats the government–market relationship as a worldwide problem in economics and traces the Party's evolving formulations from 1984 to 2013. It then links the issue to Chinese modernization, sets out three priorities for building the high-level market system, and finally applies the argument to new quality productive forces and the new-type whole-nation system.

Zhou rejects the Western economic view of government and market as opposites, and says that applying that framework in China leads to wrong policy choices. Citing Xi Jinping, the article holds that the two are organically unified and neither may replace the other. "Better" government, in Zhou's account, does not mean more government: it means handling what markets cannot or do not handle well, without overstepping or neglecting duties. The three priorities are a fairer and more dynamic market environment (a unified national market, fair competition, market-determined factor prices), a more complete and mature system with the government–market relationship as its "ox's nose", and systematic, coordinated reform within the basic socialist economic system.

On new quality productive forces, Zhou contends that scholars wrongly assume innovation comes only from markets. In Zhou's reading, the history of industrial and information revolutions shows governments leading technological change. The government should fund and coordinate high-risk basic and key technologies, while markets and private firms turn results into products. The new-type whole-nation system is presented as combining both, using national laboratories, research institutions, universities and leading firms. Zhou concludes that China has offered its own answer to a global problem. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how the 2024 reform Decision frames the government–market relationship and its link to technology policy.
quoteEn: Letting the government play its role better does not mean letting it play a bigger role. It means that, on the premise of fully letting the market play the decisive role in resource allocation, the government manages well what the market cannot manage or manages poorly, without misplacement, overstepping or absence.
quoteZh: 更好发挥政府作用，不是要更多发挥政府作用，而是要在充分发挥市场在资源配置中的决定性作用的前提下，管好那些市场管不了或管不好的事情，做到不错位、不越位、不缺位

glossary.zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.pinyin: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
glossary.explanation: A goal put forward by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in 2024 for improving China's market-economy system by 2035. It stresses a unified national market, fair competition and better macroeconomic governance.
The official term for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation, high technology and high efficiency.
An official term for mobilising state and market resources together toward major scientific and technological goals. It adapts the earlier state-led "whole-nation" approach to a market economy.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The system of public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse ownership forms, distribution according to work as the main mode alongside others, and the socialist market economy. It was formalised in 2019.

t: Deepening the understanding of the laws governing good economic work
zh: 深化做好经济工作的规律性认识
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in March 2024, He Zili takes up the "five musts" put forward at the 2023 Central Economic Work Conference. He argues that they uphold fundamental principles while innovating, add to Xi Jinping's economic thought, and deepen the Party's understanding of the laws that govern economic work in the new era. In He's view, grasping their content matters both theoretically and practically for advancing Chinese modernization through high-quality development.

This short commentary takes the five musts in turn, each under its own heading. They are: pursuing high-quality development as the "hard truth" of the new era; deepening supply-side structural reform while expanding effective demand; relying on reform and opening up to strengthen internal momentum; achieving a positive interaction between high-quality development and high-level security; and treating the advancement of Chinese modernization as the greatest political task.

On high-quality development, He says it reflects the need to shift from extensive expansion to intensive growth driven by innovation, and to meet a changed principal contradiction, in which people's aspirations have moved from "having enough" to "having better". It must be guided by the new development philosophy. On supply and demand, He holds that the main constraint is now structural, so large-scale stimulus is no longer adequate. The author points to China's very large market and complete industrial system as the basis for a new development pattern centred on the domestic cycle. On the last must, He lists six relationships to handle, including top-level design and practical exploration, strategy and tactics, fundamental principles and innovation, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and self-reliance and opening up.

He concludes that reform and opening up is the key to the success of Chinese modernization, and that development and security are like two wheels of a cart or two wings of a bird. He calls for an economic focus on high-quality development so that the blueprint of Chinese modernization is realised step by step. Read the original if you want a compact, official-line exposition of the 2023 Central Economic Work Conference's "five musts" and how Chinese economists frame them.
quoteEn: Development and security are like the two wheels of a cart or the two wings of a bird; a marked weakness in either will affect the process of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 发展和安全，犹如车之两轮、鸟之两翼，任何一方面有明显短板，都会影响中华民族伟大复兴进程。

glossary.explanation: A set of five principles on economic work set out at the Central Economic Work Conference in December 2023, summarising the Party's understanding of how to conduct economic work in the new era.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, described as having distinctive features such as a huge population and common prosperity.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, that shifts emphasis from the speed of growth to its quality, efficiency and innovation-driven character.
A set of five principles (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) put forward by the Party in 2015 to guide development.
A policy line introduced around 2015 that aims to improve the structure and quality of supply, for instance by cutting excess capacity, rather than relying mainly on demand stimulus.

t: Focusing on directional, overall and strategic issues to further deepen reform comprehensively
zh: 聚焦方向性全局性战略性问题进一步全面深化改革
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 30 September 2024, interprets the document adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. The authors take up Xi Jinping's summary of how the document is organised, the "five emphases". They argue that these must be properly understood so that reform keeps to directional, overall and strategic issues and that its different parts work together efficiently.

The article is a short interpretive piece with an introduction and five numbered sections, one for each emphasis. The emphases are the leading role of economic reform, building mechanisms that support comprehensive innovation, comprehensive reform, coordinating development and security, and strengthening Party leadership over reform. Each section gives a rationale, refers to experience since reform and opening up began, and sets out tasks for the coming five years, with the 2035 goal of basically realising socialist modernization as the anchor.

On the economy, the authors invoke the Marxist contradiction between productive forces and relations of production. They hold that the economic system underlies all other systems, so economic reform can pull other reforms along. They tie this to the primary stage of socialism, which they call China's greatest national condition, and to the need to handle the government–market relationship and build a high-standard socialist market economy. On innovation, they argue that education, science and technology, and talent reinforce one another and should be reformed together. Comprehensive reform, they say, must be planned within the five-sphere overall plan and the Four Comprehensives, with attention to short and long-term goals and to local and overall interests.

On security, the authors present development and security as mutually supporting and call for a new security architecture to protect the new development pattern. On leadership, they treat Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee of reform and divide it into political, ideological and organisational leadership. Political leadership is anchored in the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee. Ideological leadership rests on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Organisational leadership means better implementation mechanisms and cadre system reform. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the Third Plenum's reform agenda is framed and justified in Party media.
quoteEn: The economic system is the bridge and foundation of all the social systems, and deepening economic reform is the focal point of further comprehensive reform.
quoteZh: 经济体制是社会各种体制的桥梁和基础，深化经济体制改革是进一步全面深化改革的重点所在。

glossary.explanation: The official formula, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path to a modern socialist country.
The official view that China remains in an early, long-lasting phase of socialism, used to justify the focus on economic development and a market economy.
A strategic framework put forward by Xi Jinping: building a modern socialist country, deepening reform, governing the country by law, and exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance.
The official scheme of integrated economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
An official strategy that takes the domestic economic cycle as the mainstay while allowing domestic and international cycles to reinforce each other.

t: Steadily advancing all the people towards common prosperity
zh: 推动全体人民稳步迈向共同富裕
paras: Writing after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Jiang Yongmu asks how common prosperity can be advanced further through deepening reform. The commentary, first published in the Economic Daily, argues that common prosperity for all the people is the essential feature of Chinese modernization and a goal that can only be reached by pressing ahead with reform and opening up. It presents Xi Jinping's statements on the subject as the guide for action.

The piece has three parts. The first treats Chinese modernization as a modernization of common prosperity, tracing the goal from the "Great Harmony" ideal of the Book of Rites through the Party's successive historical periods. The second links reform and opening up to common prosperity, using figures on poverty and regional and income gaps. The third sets out four priority tasks: improving people's quality of life, income distribution and employment, social security, and basic public services.

Jiang contrasts Western modernization, described as capital-centred and marked by polarisation, materialism and external expansion, with Chinese modernization, which is said to be people-centred and therefore to go beyond it. The author argues that reform opening-up lifted the rural poor, citing a 1978 rural poverty rate of 97.5% and the 2020 elimination of absolute poverty among 98.99 million people. Jiang also names remaining obstacles, citing 2023 figures: an urban–rural income ratio of 2.39, an eastern share of 52.1% of national output, and a gap of 85,840 yuan between the top and bottom income quintiles. In Jiang's account, deeper reform must both "make the cake bigger", through a high-standard socialist market economy and innovation, and "divide it well", through support for agriculture, coordinated regional development and better income distribution. The author presents the "six musts" of the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the worldview and method for this task.

Jiang concludes that common prosperity is a long, arduous and complex historical process that demands historical patience. The author calls for coordinated primary, secondary and tertiary distribution, high-quality employment, a multi-tiered social security system, and public services that are both more balanced and more accessible. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-aligned economic commentary links common prosperity, reform and the Third Plenum agenda.
quoteEn: Common prosperity for all the people is the essential feature of Chinese modernization and the marked sign that distinguishes it from Western modernization.
quoteZh: 全体人民共同富裕是中国式现代化的本质特征，是中国式现代化区别于西方现代化的显著标志。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal of shared wealth, given new prominence under Xi Jinping. It is presented as a way of reducing the gaps between urban and rural areas, regions and income groups.

The official name for China's development path, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is distinguished from Western modernization by features such as a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de Èrshí Jiè Sān Zhōng Quánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The July 2024 meeting of the Party's Central Committee that adopted a decision on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978. It introduced market-oriented reforms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six principles in the 20th Party Congress report (2022): put the people first, be confident and independent, uphold fundamental principles while innovating, be problem-oriented, apply systems thinking, and have a global vision.

t: Building a high-standard socialist market economy that is "lively yet well regulated"
zh: 构建“放得活、管得住”的高水平社会主义市场经济体制
paras: Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which set the task of building a high-standard socialist market economy, Han Baojiang asks what it means for that system to be both "放得活" and "管得住" (roughly, free enough to be lively and regulated enough to stay in order). The article, a commentary first published in Guangming Daily on 3 October 2024, argues that this pairing is the inherent requirement of such a system and calls for further reform of the relevant institutions.

The piece has three parts. It first traces how Party thinking on plan and market developed, from Deng Xiaoping's 1979 remarks and Chen Yun's "bird and cage" image through the 12th, 13th and 14th Party Congresses to the 18th Central Committee's Third Plenum (2013). It then sets out institutional tasks under each half of the formula. Finally it turns to the micro-level ownership base, meaning public and non-public enterprises.

Han's central move is to equate "放得活" with letting the market play the decisive role in resource allocation, and "管得住" with improving government's role through macroeconomic governance. For the first, the author lists respect for the principle of material interest, better basic market institutions (property rights, fair competition, market access, bankruptcy and credit systems) and a sound factor-market system. For the second, Han lists a national strategic planning and policy-coordination system, fiscal and tax reform, and financial reform. Han also argues that consolidating the public sector supports "管得住" while encouraging the non-public sector supports "放得活". The two are presented as complementary, not opposed, and mixed-ownership economy is promoted to link them. Han leans heavily on quotations from Xi Jinping, Deng Xiaoping and Marx.

Han concludes that a high-standard system must combine an "efficient market" with an "effective government" and keep the word "socialist" in view throughout. Proposals include the Two Unwaverings, a law to promote the private economy, opening competitive infrastructure fields to private firms, reform of state-owned capital and enterprises, and easing private-sector financing. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party theory frames the government–market relationship and the reform agenda of the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: To be "lively", we must unwaveringly encourage, support and guide the development of the non-public sector of the economy.
quoteZh: 要“放得活”，就必须毫不动摇鼓励、支持、引导非公有制经济发展。

glossary.pinyin: fàng de huó, guǎn de zhù
glossary.literal: loosen so it is lively, control so it is held
glossary.explanation: A formula from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) for balancing market vitality with effective state regulation. The article treats it as an inherent requirement of a high-standard socialist market economy.
The official policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system, adopted at the 14th Party Congress (1992). It combines market allocation of resources with public ownership as the main body and Party leadership.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A Central Committee meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a decision on further deepening reform comprehensively. It set the task of building a high-standard socialist market economy.

t: Further deepening reform comprehensively must uphold a systems perspective
zh: 进一步全面深化改革必须坚持系统观念
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 24 September 2024, takes up one of the "six adherences" set out in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): that further deepening reform comprehensively must uphold a systems perspective. Feng Jikang argues that reform is a complex systemic undertaking. The systems perspective, which the author calls an important category of Marxist epistemology and methodology, should make reform more systematic, integrated and coordinated.

The article is organised around five major relationships that the author says must be handled with this perspective: economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and development and security. Each receives one paragraph, with a short statement of why the two sides depend on one another and what is required in practice.

Feng's central move is to treat each pair as mutually conditioning rather than opposed. Economic development is the basis of social development, and social investment in education and talent feeds back into growth. On government and market, the author calls for an effective market combined with a capable government, with the market playing the decisive role in resource allocation while the government remedies market failure. Efficiency and fairness are to be pursued together under Chinese modernization, described as modernization for the common prosperity of all. Vitality and order, and development and security, are likewise presented as reinforcing each other, with high-quality development and high-level security serving as the pairing.

Feng concludes that handling these relationships through a systems perspective will give reform a stable, orderly and dynamic social setting. The text is a brief, programmatic exposition of official policy language. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party commentary frames the Third Plenum's methodology for reform.
quoteEn: Handling the relationship between vitality and order is a difficult problem in the historical process of modernization.
quoteZh: 处理好活力和秩序的关系，是现代化历史进程中的一道难题。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's development path, stressing common prosperity, coordinated material and cultural progress and peaceful development. It has been elaborated prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official goal of shared wealth for all people, presented as an essential requirement of socialism and central to current policy.
The official term for a growth model that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed, promoted since about 2017.
The theme of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (July 2024), which adopted a decision on a new round of reform measures.

t: Upholding and improving the basic socialist economic system to promote high-quality economic development
zh: 坚持和完善社会主义基本经济制度 推动经济高质量发展
paras: Taking its cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Sun Libing argues that high-quality development depends on unwaveringly upholding and improving the basic socialist economic system. That system is public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse ownership forms, distribution according to work alongside other modes of distribution, and the socialist market economy. Sun presents it as showing the superiority of socialism while suiting the primary stage of socialism.

The article is a Party-theory commentary in four parts. It first traces how the economic system evolved from the 1950s to the present, citing successive Party congresses from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee onwards. It then takes ownership, distribution and the market economy in turn, each tied to the aim of high-quality development and common prosperity.

Sun first reads the system's development as continuous self-improvement of socialism: the Party moved from a planned economy on a public base to a market system, adding the Two Unwaverings and, in 2019, a three-dimensional formulation covering ownership, distribution and economic operation. On ownership, Sun calls for deepening state-asset and state-enterprise reform, concentrating state capital in security, public-service and emerging strategic sectors, and supporting private firms through a fairer business environment, financing and digital transformation. On distribution, citing Marx that the structure of distribution is determined by the structure of production, Sun argues that public-led ownership requires distribution according to work as the mainstay, with factor-based distribution (including data) alongside it, and coordinated primary, secondary and third distribution.

On the market, Sun treats the goal of a high-level socialist market economy by 2035 as a new stage of reform. Sun calls for a decisive role for the market and a better-functioning government, a unified national market, and basic market institutions such as property-rights protection, market access, fair competition and social credit. Sun concludes that all this is needed to advance Chinese modernization and common prosperity. Read the original if you want a concise official-style summary of how Party discourse links ownership, distribution and market reform to high-quality development after the 2024 plenum.
quoteEn: To promote high-quality economic development, we must unwaveringly consolidate and develop the public sector of the economy.
quoteZh: 推动经济高质量发展，必须毫不动摇巩固和发展公有制经济。

glossary.explanation: The policy formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector. It was first put forward at the 16th Party Congress (2002).
The official characterisation of China's present historical stage, used to justify mixed ownership and market mechanisms within a socialist system.
The official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to development emphasising quality, innovation and efficiency.
A Party goal of prosperity shared by all members of society, presented as a defining requirement of socialism.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The socialist principle that workers are rewarded by the quantity and quality of their labour. Here it is the mainstay of distribution alongside factor-based modes.

t: Anchoring on high technology, high efficiency and high quality in developing new quality productive forces
zh: 锚定高技术高效能高质量发展新质生产力
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily in September 2024, takes up the demand in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to develop productive forces marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality. Fang argues that building the material and technological base of Chinese modernization requires grasping these three features, accelerating new quality productive forces and forming production relations suited to them.
The piece has three sections, one for each feature, followed by a section on institutional reform. Each section pairs a historical or conceptual point with figures on China's recent performance.

On high technology, Fang holds that every leap in productive forces has rested on original, disruptive technologies, and that AI, the Internet of Things, biotechnology, advanced manufacturing and new energy now form a green, intelligent and ubiquitous wave of technological revolution. The author cites R&D spending above 3.3 trillion yuan in 2023, an intensity of 2.64%. On high efficiency, Fang defines new quality productive forces through the improved combination of labourers, means of labour and objects of labour, with data as a key new factor. Labour productivity per worker is said to have risen from 72,817 to 161,615 yuan between 2012 and 2023. On high quality, Fang argues that digital technology, as a general-purpose technology, upgrades traditional industries and that new quality productive forces are inherently green.

Fang concludes that new production relations must be formed through deeper reform. The author proposes mechanisms to support original and disruptive innovation, a better system for turning research into products, and institutions that help traditional industries upgrade digitally, greenly and through services. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official economic commentary links new quality productive forces to technology, productivity data and reform priorities.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are in themselves green productive forces, marked by environmental friendliness and low-carbon, green features.
quoteZh: 新质生产力本身就是绿色生产力，具有环境友好、绿色低碳的特征。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, a central theme of Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Theoretical achievements on new quality productive forces highlight an original contribution
zh: 新质生产力理论成果彰显原创性贡献
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in September 2024, Qiu Haiping asks what is original in Xi Jinping's discussion of new quality productive forces, which Xi has set out since 2023. Qiu argues that the concept is a new "revolution in terminology" within Xi Jinping's economic thought. In Qiu's account, it is the first explicit attempt to characterise productive forces by their qualitative state, and it develops Marxist political economy and historical materialism.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first treats the concept as a terminological innovation and sets out the practical sources of the idea. The second places the concept within Xi Jinping's economic thought as a whole and summarises Xi's statements on it. The third turns to the Marxist category of productive forces and says what the new concept adds. It opens with the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), whose decision calls for mechanisms to develop new quality productive forces according to local conditions.

Qiu begins from Engels's remark that every new insight in a science brings a revolution in its terminology. Xi's economic thought has innovated either by redefining existing terms or by coining new ones, such as the new development philosophy, high-quality development and the new development pattern. New quality productive forces, Qiu says, follow this path. Qiu traces their rationale to the new stage of development, the new development philosophy, the new development pattern, high-quality development and Chinese modernization. Qiu then reviews Marx's treatment of productive forces: the human and material elements, labour productivity, and the relation between productive forces and relations of production. Qiu argues that the classics speak of new productive forces and revolutions in them but never define or classify productive forces by qualitative state. The new category does so, defined by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and deep industrial upgrading. Its core marker is a marked rise in total factor productivity.

Qiu concludes that the concept lets historical materialism describe the productive forces of different social formations more precisely, and so deepens understanding of the laws of historical development. Qiu also stresses the call to build new relations of production suited to the new forces, through deeper reform and opening up. Qiu adds that local conditions should guide development, and that a rush into bubbles or a single template should be avoided. Read the original if you want an official-line theoretical account of why new quality productive forces are presented as an original contribution to Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: The major theoretical contribution of the category of new quality productive forces lies first in giving productive forces an explicit qualitative definition and classification, thereby revealing more clearly the laws of quantitative and qualitative change in productive forces and elevating the theoretical understanding of the category.
quoteZh: 新质生产力范畴的重大理论贡献，首先体现在对生产力进行了明确的质态规定和划分，从而更加清晰地揭示了生产力的量变质变规律，升华了对生产力范畴的理论认知。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading, and it is linked to the goal of high-quality development.

The official body of economic theory attributed to Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers themes such as Party leadership of economic work, the new development philosophy and high-quality development.
The official term for a shift from speed and scale towards efficiency, quality and innovation in economic growth.
Five principles set out in 2015: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
A strategy that takes the domestic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other.

The official name for China's path of modernization. It is described as featuring a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.

t: The innovative development of the Marxist theory of productive forces in contemporary China
zh: 马克思主义生产力理论在当代中国的创新发展
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2024, Zhang Yu asks how the Marxist theory of productive forces has been developed in contemporary China. The article argues that Xi Jinping's discussions of productive forces, and above all his proposal to develop new quality productive forces, raise the Party's understanding of how productive forces develop to a new level. Zhang describes this as an original theoretical result of contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy and a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece is organised as a sequence of themes. Each takes a classical Marxist proposition, traces how Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping handled it, and then sets out Xi's statements on the same point. The themes are: productive forces as the standard of social progress; the purpose of socialist production; the elements of productive forces; the scientific and industrial revolutions; scientific and technological innovation; ecology; industrial innovation; and reform of the relations of production.

Zhang's core move is to present each of Xi's statements as a creative development of historical materialism. Technological innovation is called the core element of new quality productive forces. Data is treated as a new factor of production. Protecting the ecological environment is described as protecting productive forces, and new quality productive forces are said to be green productive forces by nature. Zhang also argues that the relations of production must be reformed to fit new productive forces, and that the socialist system combined with the market economy has distinct advantages in liberating and developing them. The article closes by defining new quality productive forces as advanced productive forces and gives four reasons. They arise from the new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial change. They are the advanced productive forces of the information, digital and intelligent era. They raise the quality of workers, means of labour, objects of labour and their combination. They are the material and technological basis of Chinese modernization and high-quality development.

Zhang concludes that the theory of new quality productive forces deepens understanding of the decisive role of productive forces, the essence of socialism, the elements of productive forces, their driving force and their relationship to the relations of production. The purpose of development, in this account, remains meeting the people's growing needs for a better life. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned account of how Chinese theorists link Marx, Mao, Deng and Xi on productive forces and justify the concept of new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: The essence of new quality productive forces is advanced productive forces.
quoteZh: 新质生产力本质是先进生产力。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24. It refers to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and the upgrading of labour, means of labour and objects of labour.
The official name for a growth model that stresses innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed. It became a central economic goal after the 19th Party Congress (2017).
The Party's official term for its own path to modernization, set out in detail at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

t: The two dimensions of Marx's thought on democracy and their practical embodiment
zh: 马克思民主思想的二维向度及实践体现
paras: Liu Lin asks how Marx's thinking on democracy can be organised into a coherent system and what it means for democratic practice in China today. The article proposes two dimensions: a substantive dimension, concerned with the philosophical grounds and inner value of democracy, and an authenticity (or reality) dimension, concerned with how rule by the majority is actually realised. Liu argues that the two complement each other and that whole-process people's democracy joins them in contemporary China.

Part one reconstructs the substantive dimension through three headings: the essence of democracy as the form of the state, its ontological basis in the people, and its authentic aim in human emancipation. This draws on Marx's Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, On the Jewish Question and The Civil War in France. Part two treats the authenticity dimension as a demystification of bourgeois democracy and a distillation of proletarian practice, followed by Marx's general principles for realisation. Part three applies the framework to China at the level of the state, the people and society.

The central move is that Marx locates democracy in the economic base and in the people's self-determination, not in abstract liberty and equality. On this basis Liu reads his critique of representative government, universal suffrage and the separation of powers as showing that they leave exploitation intact. From the Paris Commune, Liu draws four lessons: economic emancipation as the precondition, breaking the old state machine, self-government by the people, and public servants who can be recalled. For realisation Liu identifies three pairings: new democracy with new dictatorship, Communist Party leadership with the proletariat as the active force, and institutional procedure with popular supervision.

Liu concludes that whole-process people's democracy fuses the substantive and authentic dimensions and is a new creation of Marx's thought in China. In the article's account, it must fit Chinese modernization and the primary stage of socialism, broaden and strengthen popular participation, and advance through the five-sphere integrated plan. It must also keep the three-way unity of Party leadership, the people as masters of the country and law-based governance. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language case for reading Marx's democratic thought as grounding the official concept of whole-process people's democracy.
quoteEn: The realisation of the authenticity of Marx's thought on democracy is not a concrete, dogmatic scheme but the construction of general principles of democracy.
quoteZh: 马克思民主思想的真实性实现不是具体的教条的方案而是民主一般原则的构建。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019 to describe China's democracy as covering the whole chain of elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight. Official sources contrast it with democracy limited to periodic voting.

The official term for China's own path of modernization, set out prominently in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as sharing features common to all countries while reflecting China's national conditions.

The official assessment, dating from the 1980s, that China is still in an early phase of socialism with relatively underdeveloped productive forces. It is used to justify China's particular institutions and development path.

The official overall layout for building socialism with Chinese characteristics, covering the economic, political, cultural, social and ecological spheres. It was formalised at the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The revolutionary government of Paris in 1871, which Marx analysed in The Civil War in France as a form of working-class self-government. It is a key reference point in Marxist theories of the state and democracy.

t: Main historical lessons of modernization since the founding of the People's Republic
zh: 新中国成立以来现代化建设的主要历史经验
paras: Writing in 2024, on the 75th anniversary of the People's Republic, Yang Deshan and Guo Wei ask what lessons can be drawn from the Communist Party's record of modernization. They argue that the Party's success rests on continually summing up experience, and that the record yields three main lessons: one political, one ideological and one methodological. They present this as relevant to studying Xi Jinping's statements on Chinese modernization, to implementing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), and to building a Chinese-style body of knowledge on modernization.

The article is organised around these three lessons. The first concerns political direction. The second traces how the Party's understanding and strategic targets changed across four stages: building an industrial base, the "Four Modernizations", "modernization of the Chinese type" under reform and opening up, and Chinese modernization since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third examines two pairs of relationships: upholding fundamental principles versus innovation and reform, and self-reliance versus cooperation and opening up.

On the political side, the authors argue that Party leadership, the socialist road and a people-centred approach were treated as the premise of modernization from the New Democratic period onward, and that the three form an organic unity. On the ideological side, they hold that the Party adjusted its goals as it learned more about modernization and about China's conditions, citing the shift from the "Four Modernizations" to the three-step strategy, a moderately prosperous society, and the two-step plan to 2035 and mid-century. On method, they claim that economic reform (from the planned commodity economy to a socialist market economy) and the strengthening of Party leadership show dialectical handling of continuity and change. Self-reliance is described as the inner basis, with opening up, including WTO entry in 2001, as an external condition turned into internal momentum.

The authors conclude that the Party has consistently kept its original mission while innovating, and has combined independence with openness, neither overrating nor underrating itself, and that this has kept modernization on course. They stress that China remains in the primary stage of socialism and the world's largest developing country. Read the original if you want a Party-centred periodisation of China's modernization strategy, from the Four Modernizations to Chinese modernization, and how Chinese scholars derive official lessons from it.
quoteEn: Within political direction and principles, upholding Party leadership is the essential requirement and fundamental guarantee of following the socialist road and putting the people first.
quoteZh: 在政治方向和政治原则的组成中，坚持党的领导是坚持走社会主义道路和以人民为中心的本质要求和根本保证

glossary.explanation: The official concept, elaborated under Xi Jinping and prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of a modernization path said to be distinct from Western models. It is presented as combining Party leadership, socialism and a people-centred approach.
The goal of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence and science and technology, announced by Zhou Enlai in 1964 and revived after 1978 as a core reform-era objective.

An official judgement, formalised in the 1980s, that China is at an early stage of socialism with underdeveloped productive forces. It underpins the Party's basic line and long-term development policy.
A goal introduced by Deng Xiaoping in 1979 and later developed into the target of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, declared achieved in 2021.

t: Achievements and lessons of economic development in New China
zh: 新中国经济发展的成就与启示
paras: Marking the 75th anniversary of the People's Republic in 2024, Wu Li reviews the country's economic record and asks what it shows. The article argues that the 75 years of economic development and institutional change demonstrate the distinctive strengths of Communist Party leadership and of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics. In Wu's account, China moved from a backward agrarian country to an advanced industrial one despite scarce per capita resources and fierce international competition.

The piece is a historical overview organised around three periods that Wu presents as continuous: the era of socialist revolution and construction, the era of reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Each section pairs a policy logic with statistics, such as reservoirs and irrigated land up to 1978, GDP rankings from 1978 to 2010, and GDP, social insurance and infrastructure figures for 2012–2023. A closing section lists current problems and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Wu's central claim is that each period's strategy fitted its conditions. Heavy-industry priority, planning and socialist transformation secured high accumulation at low income, and produced a complete industrial system and defence capacity. Reform introduced a socialist market economy in which the market and the government work as a "dual-wheel drive", and growth averaged nearly 10% a year from 1978 to 2012. After 2012 Wu describes the "three overlapping periods" of slower growth, structural adjustment and digesting earlier stimulus, which called for a shift to high-quality development. Wu names four continuing advantages: Party leadership, the government–market combination, the size of the economy, and abundant human capital.

Wu acknowledges that unbalanced and inadequate development persists. The listed problems include an incomplete market system, weak innovation, dependence on foreign core technologies, and gaps in urban–rural development and income distribution. The article concludes that deepening reform, centred on a high-standard socialist market economy, will carry the country towards the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned narrative of China's economic history in three periods, with the statistics it cites, as an example of how Chinese scholarship presents this record.
quoteEn: This policy of a government–market \"dual-wheel drive\", with domestic and foreign resources and markets considered together, provided an important guarantee for China's world-renowned economic miracle.
quoteZh: 这种政府与市场“双轮驱动”、国内国外资源与市场统筹兼顾的方针政策，为中国创造举世瞩目的经济发展奇迹提供了重要保障。

glossary.explanation: An official goal, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting from fast, extensive growth to growth driven by innovation, efficiency and better structure.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official name for China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market allocation of resources with public ownership and state guidance.
The policy begun at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, which introduced market mechanisms and opened the economy to foreign trade and investment.
The Party's official designation of its own path of socialism, adapted to Chinese conditions since the reform era.
An official description, used from about 2013, of the simultaneous slowdown in growth, structural adjustment pains and digestion of earlier stimulus policies.

t: The innovative development of the Marxist theory of productive forces in contemporary China
zh: 马克思主义生产力理论在当代中国的创新发展
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in October 2024, this article asks how the Marxist theory of productive forces has been developed in contemporary China. Zhang Yu argues that Xi Jinping's series of statements on productive forces, culminating in the concept of new quality productive forces, raises the Party's understanding of the laws of productive-force development to a new level. Zhang presents it as an original theoretical achievement of contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy and a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece is organised as a sequence of themes. Each opens with Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong or Deng Xiaoping and then sets out Xi's corresponding formulations. The themes are: productive forces as the fundamental criterion of social development; the purpose of production as meeting people's needs; the components of productive forces; the new round of technological and industrial revolution; scientific and technological innovation; ecology; industrial innovation; reform of production relations; and the nature of new quality productive forces.

Zhang's core move is to show continuity and extension. Marx's elements of the labour process (labourers, means of labour, objects of labour) are said to underpin Xi's definition of new quality productive forces as a leap in these elements and their optimised combination. Data is treated as a new production factor. Marx's view that science is a productive force becomes the claim that technological innovation is the core element. His view of metabolism between humans and nature becomes the idea that protecting the environment is protecting productive forces, so that new quality productive forces are "green productive forces". Zhang also holds that socialist institutions, combining the market economy with the socialist system, must be reformed so that production relations fit new productive forces.

Zhang concludes that new quality productive forces are in essence advanced productive forces. They are described through four features: they arise from the new technological and industrial revolution, they belong to the information, digital and intelligent era, they involve a leap in factors and their combination (platform economy is one example), and they are the material and technological basis of Chinese modernization and high-quality development. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party theorists link Xi Jinping's economic thought to the Marxist classics on productive forces.
quoteEn: The key to understanding and grasping new quality productive forces lies in understanding and grasping their advanced character.
quoteZh: 认识和把握新质生产力，关键在于认识和把握新质生产力的先进性。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023–24 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and higher-quality factors of production. Official texts present it as the basis of high-quality development.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party from the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official economic goal, stressed since about 2017, that puts quality, innovation and sustainability ahead of speed of growth.

t: Marx's thesis of "revolutionary practice" as an answer to the relation between environment and human beings
zh: 马克思“革命的实践”论断对环境与人关系的回答
paras: Liu Tongfang revisits the third of Marx's Theses on Feuerbach, which holds that the coincidence of the changing of circumstances and of human activity or self-change can only be conceived and rationally understood as revolutionary practice. Liu argues that three basic questions remain disputed: what "environment" refers to, how changed activity relates to self-change, and why the relation can "only" be understood as revolutionary practice. Answering them, in Liu's view, shows how Marx's new materialism of "practice" surpasses all earlier materialism and leads towards the communist movement.

The article is organised around these three questions and returns to the intellectual-historical context of the Theses. It draws on Marx's engagement with eighteenth-century French materialism (especially Helvétius) in The Holy Family, on the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, The German Ideology, the Grundrisse and Capital, and on Hegel's master–slave dialectic. It also compares Marx's original wording with Engels's edited version, which dropped "self-change".

On the first question, Liu rejects both the view that "environment" means social environment and the view that it means natural plus social environment. Liu holds that it means the "human environment": social environment together with humanised nature, excluding nature-in-itself. On the second, Liu proposes reading the relation through a "practice–education" logic derived from Marx's critical inheritance of Hegel's "labour–formation" idea. In Liu's account, changed activity is the practical precondition and aim of self-change, while awakened self-consciousness drives conscious revolutionary action, giving the proletariat a double subjectivity. On the third, Liu argues that only relational practice, dialectically uniting the human environment and humans, overcomes the subject–object dualism of mechanical and French materialism. This yields the historicity, mediating character and revolutionary character of the new materialism.

Liu concludes that understanding the human environment and humans as revolutionary practice is the only way to escape the utopian trap of earlier materialisms and open the revolutionary possibility of the communist movement. The Theses, Liu notes, remain a philosophical outline that does not yet grasp the concrete forms of capitalist production relations. Even so, Liu sees in them the unity of social, natural and human history that underlies historical materialism. Read the original if you work on the early Marx, the Theses on Feuerbach or the concept of practice, and want a detailed Chinese reading of the Marx–Engels textual difference and the Hegelian background.
quoteEn: Marx's "environment" does not refer merely to the social environment, but is the "human environment" that contains both the social environment and the humanised natural environment.
quoteZh: 马克思的“环境”并非仅仅指涉社会环境，而是包含社会环境和人化自然环境的“人的环境”

glossary.explanation: Liu's own term for the "environment" in Marx's thesis: social environment plus humanised nature, as distinct from nature-in-itself.
A concept from Marx's 1844 Manuscripts for nature shaped by human labour and imbued with human essential powers, as opposed to nature existing independently of humans.
Liu's interpretive formula: practice itself educates the agent, awakening self-consciousness, which in turn guides further action.
The Chinese rendering of Hegel's idea (Bildung through work) in the master–slave dialectic, that the labouring slave gains independent consciousness by shaping things.
In Chinese Marxist scholarship, the term for the materialism of practice that Marx first outlined in the Theses on Feuerbach, as opposed to earlier "old" materialism.

t: A pioneer of contemporary Chinese Marxist philosophy
st: A study of Chen Xianda's philosophical thought
zh: 当代中国马克思主义哲学研究的开拓者
zhSub: 陈先达哲学思想研究
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 18 October 2024, a week after the death of Chen Xianda (1930–2024), this tribute and appraisal by Hao Lixin presents Chen as a pioneer of contemporary Chinese Marxist philosophy. Hao describes Chen, an honorary first-grade professor at Renmin University of China, as a philosopher and educator who held that "philosophers are not spectators of society". The piece argues that his work combined historical depth, problem-oriented engagement with reality and a popular style.

The article is organised under four headings. It first covers Chen's insistence on the practical and critical character of philosophy. It then turns to his history-of-thought research, including the first systematic Chinese study of Marx and Engels's intellectual development, a study of Marx's early thought, and the monograph Towards the Depths of History. The third section deals with his "problem-oriented" work on traditional Chinese culture and cultural confidence. The last discusses his philosophical essays written for general readers.

Hao highlights three moves. First, in method, Chen held that history and logic must be studied together, that Marxism must be seen as an integrated whole, and that the sources of historical materialism are multiple and not purely philosophical. In Hao's account, this approach guards against dogmatism and rebuts attempts to set a "young Marx" against mature Marxism, and Chen also defended historical materialism against historical nihilism. Second, Chen argued that adapting Marxism to China means solving China's problems. He proposed that Marxism and traditional culture be seen as two aspects of one process, using the phrase "an old country with a new mission" (旧邦新命) and the idea of creative transformation. Third, Chen wrote plain-language essays, such as the "walking towards" image for active reflection theory, and treated Marxist teaching as a matter of belief as well as a profession.

Hao concludes that Chen carried forward the practical and critical spirit of Marxist philosophy and set an example for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times and for making it accessible to the public. The text is a commemorative appraisal, not a critical assessment. Read the original if you want an overview of Chen Xianda's major works and methodological ideas, or a sense of how Chinese Marxist philosophers present a leading figure of their field after his death.
quoteEn: Philosophy must never become a useless art of dragon-slaying; it should be the art of Cook Ding carving an ox.
quoteZh: 哲学绝不应变为不能用的屠龙之术，而应该是庖丁解牛的解牛术。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing process of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the contemporary era. Chen Xianda is presented as a contributor to it.

glossary.en: an old country with a new mission
glossary.explanation: A phrase from the Classic of Poetry. Chen used it to say that socialist China is a new social formation that continues an ancient country and its culture.
Official term for confidence in China's traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. It is one of the Four-sphere Confidence along with confidence in the path, theory and system.

In official Chinese usage, a label for views that deny or distort the Party's history and the historical necessity of socialism. Chen is said to have criticised it from the standpoint of historical materialism.

t: How does Marxism understand "education"?
zh: 马克思主义如何理解“教育”
paras: Published in Study Times in October 2024, this short commentary asks how Marxism understands and approaches education. Gong Keju answers by drawing on Marx and Engels, arguing that proletarian education has defined tasks, methodological requirements and a political character, and that its essence is the all-round development of the human being.

The piece moves through three perspectives. It begins with the demands that large-scale socialised production places on the training of labour. It then turns to the three dimensions of educational method that arise from practice as a relationship between subject and object. Finally it considers education historically, in terms of its political character and its essential purpose.

Gong, building on Capital, identifies three tasks: changing "general human nature", imparting skills in a particular branch of labour, and producing developed and specialised labour-power together with firm ideals and fighting spirit. The three methodological dimensions are that educators must themselves be educated, that learners should stress self-improvement and self-education, and that the Communist Party must lead the education of workers. Gong adds that, citing Engels, education must be free of bourgeois influence and serve proletarian interests. Citing Marx, Gong holds that only proletarian education unites raising social production with the all-round development of people.

Gong closes by describing education as a cornerstone of national rejuvenation. Xi Jinping's statements on education since the 18th Party Congress (2012) are presented as continuing and developing Marxist educational thought. They are said to answer the questions of whom to train, how to train them and for whom. Read the original if you want a brief Party-press overview of how Marx and Engels's remarks on education are being marshalled for current policy.
quoteEn: The essence of proletarian education lies in raising the labour skills of the proletariat through the transformation of the communist mode of social production.
quoteZh: 无产阶级教育的本质就在于要从共产主义社会生产方式的变革中提高无产阶级的劳动技能

t: The logical path of common prosperity from the perspective of systems thinking
zh: 系统观念视阈下共同富裕的逻辑进路
paras: Zhu Fengming and Wang Ziyu ask how common prosperity, which they describe as a complex, long-term systemic undertaking, can be understood and advanced through systems thinking. They note that systems thinking was raised to the level of a principle at the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020) and listed among the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era at the 20th Party Congress (2022). Their thesis is that common prosperity can be driven forward only if its inner laws are grasped through this approach.

The article has three parts, which the authors call the logical starting point, the logical support and the logical destination. The first defines systems thinking and its four features: foresight, a global view, strategic character and wholeness. The second reviews what the Party has done since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under each feature, citing figures on the Gini coefficient, regional GDP shares, poverty alleviation, social insurance, charitable trusts, culture and trade. The third turns to remaining problems and proposals.

The authors argue that, since 2012, the Party has applied each feature in turn. For foresight, they cite the shared-development concept, the Zhejiang demonstration zone and the three staged targets for 2025, 2035 and the mid-century. For the global view, they cite the poverty-alleviation campaign, the treatment of common prosperity as integral to Chinese modernization, and regional coordination. For strategy, they cite its definition as a major political question bearing on the Party's governance base and the coordinated arrangement of primary, secondary and tertiary distribution. For wholeness, they cite the unity of efficiency and fairness, of material and cultural wealth, and of internal and external factors. They admit that the gap between urban and rural incomes remains large and that the Gini coefficient is still above 0.40.

To carry systems thinking through the whole process, the authors call for a broad historical perspective and a global outlook, citing Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. They also call for balanced planning that gives priority to top-level design, high-quality development, rural revitalisation and prosperity achieved through hard work, while avoiding welfarism. Finally, they propose efficient coordination: macro-level policy coherence, and the pairing of an effective market with a capable government, urban–rural integration, state and private sectors, domestic and international circulation, and material and cultural progress. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how systems thinking is used to frame common prosperity policy, with the statistics the authors cite.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is a vast and complex systemic undertaking and a long-term goal, and it is above all a task of our times and an urgent one: meeting the people's need for a better life.
quoteZh: 共同富裕是一项复杂庞大的系统工程，也是一个长远目标，更是满足人民美好生活需要的时代课题和紧迫任务。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new policy prominence under Xi Jinping, notably after 2021. Official texts present it as a staged objective with targets for 2025, 2035 and the mid-century.

A way of thinking that treats things as interconnected wholes and calls for comprehensive, forward-looking planning. Official documents have set it out as a principle since 2020 and as part of the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought.
The official term for China's path to modernization, used prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as including common prosperity for all the people as one of its features.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

t: A critique of historical nihilism from the perspective of the "big historical view"
zh: 大历史观视阈中历史虚无主义批判
paras: Gao Bingliang asks how the "big historical view" (da lishiguan), which Xi Jinping has stressed repeatedly since the 18th Party Congress (2012), can be used to criticise historical nihilism. The article argues that this view is a Marxist historical outlook that grasps history across long time spans, in its connections and in its inseparable objective conditions and subjective creativity. On this basis, Gao holds that historical nihilism is an idealist trend that rejects Marxism's guiding role, the historical necessity of China's turn to socialism and the leadership of the Communist Party of China.

The article is organised in three parts. The first identifies the idealist essence of historical nihilism, surveying its Western forms from god-centred myth, through reason- and will-centred philosophy (Plato, Hegel, Schopenhauer, Nietzsche), to postmodern historiography, and tracing Marxist struggles against it from Marx to Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and the period since 2012. The second examines its value standpoint. The third treats opposition to it as a political struggle, drawing on the Soviet collapse, the "Arab Spring" and current policy measures.

Gao's core argument is that historical materialism is the decisive weapon: it returns attention to real life and the study of productive forces and relations, it relies on full and accurate historical materials, and it treats the Party's own errors by acknowledging, analysing and correcting them. Gao then argues that nihilism stands against the people, denying their role as historical subject, serving the logic of capital through commodified and falsified history, and weakening class consciousness and aspirations for a better life, including through online entertainment. Politically, Gao claims it assisted Western "peaceful evolution" in the USSR and Eastern Europe, citing Xi's account of the Soviet collapse, and that it attacks Marxism, promotes a "Western-centric" model of modernization and magnifies the Party's setbacks.

Gao concludes that the struggle is in essence one against Westernisation, division, infiltration and subversion, and must be won through a comprehensive effort. The proposals are: strengthen Party leadership over ideological work, guide and manage media and monitor online opinion, and use legal means. The article lists the 2016 Party guidelines, the 2018 Heroes and Martyrs Protection Law and the 2020 Criminal Law amendment. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how current Party-ideological writing links the big historical view to the campaign against historical nihilism and to the policy and legal instruments used in it.
quoteEn: Historical nihilism does not fail to "study" history but "studies" it idealistically; it does not lack a value standpoint but stands against the people.
quoteZh: 历史虚无主义并非不“研究”历史，而是唯心地“研究”历史；并非不持价值立场，而是站在背离人民的立场

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has promoted since the 18th Party Congress, urging officials to analyse events within the long course of history, the tide of the times and global developments. Chinese writers present it as a Marxist historical outlook.

In official Chinese discourse, a label for views that negate the Party's history, its leaders or the historical necessity of China's socialist path. Here it is also applied to Western idealist and postmodern historiography.
The Marxist theory that material production and social relations shape history, and that the people are its decisive force.
A term in Chinese Party discourse for alleged Western strategies of undermining socialist states through ideological and cultural infiltration rather than force.

t: Chinese modernization as a wholly new form of human civilization
zh: 中国式现代化是全新的人类文明形态
source: Journal of the University of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, 2024 no. 3
paras: Tian Pengying and Zhang Xiaopeng take up Xi Jinping's description of Chinese modernization as "a wholly new form of human civilization". They treat it as an evaluative proposition about civilizational value and ask what lies behind it. Their answer is that Chinese modernization combines several civilizational sources in a new synthesis, differs from Western modernization, and points to the future of human civilization.

The article is organised in three parts. The first examines how Chinese modernization came to be, as an integrated creation. The second compares it with Western modernization. The third considers its orientation towards the future. The authors draw on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, and on Aristotle, Hegel and Fukuyama.

In the first part, the authors argue that Chinese modernization is an integration of three elements: a "本我" (original self) in fine traditional Chinese culture, a "真我" (true self) in the advanced essence of scientific socialism, and a "自我" (self) formed by dialectically learning from the "other", chiefly the West. They hold that this is guided by the Two Integrations. In the second part they argue that the formula "modernization equals Westernization" mystifies capitalist modernization, which is only a particular form of "modernization in general". Western modernization has a dialectical character, but its negative side recurs: polarisation, materialism, ecological conflict and violent expansion. Against this, the authors set the five features of Chinese modernization named at the 20th Party Congress (2022): a huge population, common prosperity, coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development. The authors present these as socialist in essence. In the third part they argue that Chinese modernization is historically isomorphic with the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and guides it, setting targets for 2035 and the mid-century.

The authors conclude that Chinese modernization has absorbed Chinese, socialist and other civilizational achievements, overcome the "civilizational barriers" set by Western modernization, and opened up a new picture of civilization. They add that this does not aim to replace "modernization equals Westernization" with "modernization equals Sinicization". In their account it shows that the human future has many possibilities and will be created by all humanity together. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist journal grounds the claim of a new form of human civilization in classical-Marxist and Chinese cultural sources, and in a comparison with the West.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is not a "Chinese copy" of the Western model of modernization. It is a new path of socialist modernization with Chinese characteristics, created by stepping outside the whole sequence of Western capitalist modernization and starting afresh.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化不是西方现代化模式的“中国复写”，而是跳出西方资本主义现代化的整体序列、另起炉灶创造出来的体现中国特色的社会主义现代化新道路

glossary.explanation: The official Party formula for China's development path, elaborated especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist modernization with five stated Chinese features.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as an essential requirement of socialism and a feature of Chinese modernization.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
