glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, to restore China to a position of strength and prosperity, with targets set for 2035 and the mid-century.

t: Why does ideology "have no history"?
st: The key problem in going beyond German idealism and the historical-materialist solution
zh: 意识形态何以“没有历史”？
zhSub: 超越德国观念论的关键问题与历史唯物主义的解决路径
source: Studies on the Discipline of Marxist Theory
paras: Li Chengwang asks how Marx and Engels were able to say, in The German Ideology, that morality, religion, metaphysics and other ideology have 'no history, no development'. The article argues that explaining this claim was the central task in surpassing German idealism and in establishing historical materialism. Li notes that research on the positive exposition of historical materialism is mature, whereas work on this particular problem remains comparatively thin.

The article has three parts. The first traces Western philosophy's 'two-world' substance thinking from ancient Greece through medieval Christianity to Vico, Voltaire, Kant, Hegel and the Young Hegelians (Bruno Bauer, Feuerbach, Stirner). The second reconstructs the mechanism of material production in The German Ideology. The third follows Marx and Engels in showing historically how law, the state, religion, philosophy and morality depend on social relations, drawing on Engels's Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy.

Li contends that German idealism, despite internal differences, turns human history into a history of thought in which ideas, concepts or self-consciousness govern reality. Marx and Engels, in Li's account, begin instead from the empirical premise of producing the means of life and analyse production in five dimensions: the means of subsistence, new needs, human reproduction, the production of social relations, and the production of consciousness. Consciousness is therefore determined by production and the division of labour. Li then argues that Marx and Engels show, case by case, that ruling ideas express ruling material relations, that religious change follows economic needs, that Kantian and Feuerbachian ethics reflect bourgeois conditions, and that law and the state follow forms of ownership. Ideology thus has no independent history of its own.

Li concludes that ideology is an inverted and illusory reflection of reality which cannot resolve real contradictions, and that its content changes with relations of production. Human history is a history of production and labour, and freedom is to be achieved through changing ownership and through communist revolution rather than through a revolution in ideas. Li presents this as the reason that historical materialism ends the idea that thought governs history. Read the original if you want a close reading of The German Ideology and Engels's Feuerbach essay as a systematic critique of German idealism.
quoteEn: Ideology having "no history" mainly means that ideology has no independent history of its own.
quoteZh: 意识形态“没有历史”，主要是指意识形态并没有属于自己的独立的历史。

t: The dialectical connections among the outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization
zh: 中华文明突出特性的辩证关联
paras: Liu Zhihong takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, which identified five outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness) and also discussed how they relate. The article, a commentary in Guangming Daily (2 October 2024), argues that each characteristic has its own irreplaceable value and that the five are organically linked. Liu holds that understanding their mutual reinforcement helps in grasping the overall nature of Chinese civilization and the scientific requirements of the Two Integrations.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the significance of each characteristic in turn, drawing heavily on Xi's formulations. The second shows how each characteristic supports every other. The third singles out several pairings that Liu treats as the key mechanisms of mutual reinforcement.

Liu assigns each characteristic a distinct role. Continuity is the precondition, since without it the other four would have no ground. Innovation supplies inexhaustible force. Unity is the "main axis". Inclusiveness is the safeguard, and peacefulness is both a common result and a common guarantee of the others. On the key interactions, the author argues that unity and continuity are two sides of one thing, so that Chinese civilization has a continuous unity and a unified continuity. Inclusiveness and peacefulness are said to condition each other, and inclusiveness and innovation to generate each other. Unity and continuity are presented as conditions for inclusiveness, which in turn strengthens them. Liu adds that continuity is not stagnation but a historical process of progress supported by innovation.

Liu concludes that the five characteristics form a dialectical unity that drives the development of Chinese civilization. The article follows the official line and offers no critique. It restates and systematises Xi's account instead. Read the original if you want a concise exposition of how current Party-aligned scholarship reads the relations among the five characteristics, as part of the discourse on the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: Unity and continuity are internally consistent, two sides of one whole.
quoteZh: 统一性与连续性内在一致、一体两面。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities (the first integration) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second). The second integration is often stressed in discussions of cultural inheritance.
Xi Jinping's term, used in his 2023 speech on cultural inheritance and development, for the five features of Chinese civilization: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness.

glossary.en: symposium on cultural inheritance and development
glossary.explanation: A meeting held in Beijing in June 2023 at which Xi Jinping gave a speech on culture, including the five outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization.

t: Further comprehensively deepening reform must adhere to a people-centred approach
zh: 进一步全面深化改革必须坚持以人民为中心
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2024, Huang Rongsheng takes up one of the principles set out in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further comprehensively deepening reform: adhering to a people-centred approach. Huang argues that this principle expresses the Party's founding mission, the meaning of the phrase "Chinese modernization puts people's wellbeing first", and the value orientation of the new round of reform.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first traces the people-centred stance to Marxism's understanding of the people. The second links it to Chinese modernization and presents statistics on living standards. The third treats the people as the driving force of reform.

Huang first argues that the people-centred approach inherits and develops the Marxist view that the masses make history. It cites Marx, Engels and Lenin, and then Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. In this account the people's standpoint distinguishes Marxist parties from others, and the Party's growth from a small group into a major governing party results from adherence to it. Huang then contrasts Chinese modernization with what the article calls capital-centred Western modernization. As evidence of delivery, the article cites rising per capita disposable income (39,200 yuan in 2023), basic pension coverage above 1 billion people, basic medical insurance above 1.3 billion, and a public sense of security of 98.2%. Finally, Huang holds that more than four decades of reform show the people to be its fundamental driving force, citing poverty alleviation and the building of a moderately prosperous society.

Huang concludes that reform must be carried out for the people and relying on them, with improving living standards as a key goal. The author calls for the Party's mass line to be followed in the new era, for top-level design to be combined with seeking the people's views, and for popular initiative to be mobilised. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's official discourse links Marxist people-centred theory to the justification of current reform.
quoteEn: The people are the wellspring of reform's momentum; as the self-improvement and development of the socialist system, reform must rely closely on the people, fully respect their principal status and bring the masses' pioneering spirit into play.
quoteZh: 人民是改革的动力源泉，改革作为社会主义制度的自我完善和发展，必须紧紧依靠人民，充分尊重人民主体地位，发挥群众首创精神。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of a Party-led path of socialist modernization with Chinese characteristics. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A guiding principle of Xi Jinping-era Party theory. It holds that development and reform should be carried out for the people and by relying on them.
The Party's traditional working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of going among the masses, gathering their views and returning them as policy.

t: Further deepening reform comprehensively demonstrates historical initiative
zh: 进一步全面深化改革彰显历史主动
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 8 August 2024, interprets the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. Wei Zhiqi argues that the decision shows the Party's "historical initiative" (lishi zhudong) in improving socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernizing national governance.

The author opens by presenting reform and opening up as the key to Chinese modernization and credits it for the achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The commentary then reads the Plenum through four themes, each framed by the word "historical": resolve, position, responsibility and confidence.

On resolve, Wei cites Xi Jinping's insistence that Party leadership, Marxism, the socialist path and the people's democratic dictatorship cannot be shaken, and argues that this firmness lets the Party resist erroneous currents. On position, the author holds that China has moved from high-speed growth to high-quality development, with problems such as weak innovation, regional and income gaps, and that institution-building now carries greater weight. On responsibility, Wei describes reform as the self-improvement of the socialist system, with the Third Plenums of 2013 and 2024 forming a continuous logic that increasingly stresses systemic and coordinated reform.

On confidence, Wei contends that opening up is a defining mark of Chinese modernization, that globalization remains the long-term trend, and that China should oppose deglobalization and protectionism. The author concludes that further reform will offer the world more opportunities and contribute to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official press framed the 2024 Plenum's reform agenda.
quoteEn: Turning the blueprint of Chinese modernization into reality depends fundamentally on further deepening reform comprehensively and continually improving institutions and mechanisms in all areas.
quoteZh: 把中国式现代化蓝图变为现实，根本在于进一步全面深化改革，不断完善各方面体制机制。

glossary.literal: historical initiative / taking the initiative in history
glossary.explanation: A phrase in Party discourse for consciously grasping historical trends and acting on them rather than reacting to events. It is used widely in official texts of the Xi Jinping era.
The official concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The Party's official name for its system and path since the reform era, combining Marxism with China's conditions.
An official goal that replaces a focus on speed of growth with emphasis on innovation, balance, sustainability and efficiency.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of shared interests among nations, used to frame China's approach to global governance.

t: Deepening reform along the track of the rule of law
zh: 坚持在法治轨道上深化改革
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in August 2024, Zhai Guoqiang takes up the Decision adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which makes law-based governance a major principle of further deepening reform. Zhai's thesis is that reform and the rule of law must be unified, like two wings of a bird, and that the rule of law is both a component and a safeguard of Chinese modernization.

The commentary has three sections. The first reviews how comprehensive law-based governance has taken shape since reform and opening up and under Xi Jinping. The second argues for the guiding, regulating and safeguarding role of law. The third sets out how to advance reform under law and improve law through reform.

Zhai's core argument draws on comparison. In the author's account, every country that has modernized successfully has handled the problem of rule by law versus rule by individuals, while states that fell into development "traps" largely suffered from weak rule of law. On the reform–law relationship, Zhai holds that major reforms need a legal basis, but existing law must not become an excuse for delay. Mature experience should be quickly written into law, pilot reforms should be authorised by statutory procedure, and outdated provisions should be amended or repealed. Zhai names the building of a socialist rule-of-law system with Chinese characteristics as the overall lever.

Zhai concludes that reform must uphold the unity of Party leadership, the people as masters of the country and law-based governance. The author also calls for implementing the Constitution and for fair enforcement, so that society stays both dynamic and orderly. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how the 2024 Plenum links legal reform to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Reform and the rule of law are like the two wings of a bird or the two wheels of a cart.
quoteZh: 改革和法治如鸟之两翼、车之两轮。

glossary.explanation: Official Party concept of a modernization path with distinct Chinese features, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.literal: comprehensively governing the country according to law
glossary.explanation: Official policy, part of the "Four Comprehensives" strategy, of running the country by law under Party leadership.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义法治体系
glossary.en: socialist rule-of-law system with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The official overall framework for law-based governance. It covers legal norms, implementation, supervision, safeguards and Party regulations.

t: Relationships to handle well in safeguarding and improving people's livelihood through development
zh: 在发展中保障和改善民生需处理好若干关系
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 19 September 2024, this commentary by Lin Nan and Wang Liexuan takes up the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The Decision describes safeguarding and improving people's livelihood through development as a major task of Chinese modernization, to be pursued by doing one's best while acting within one's means. The authors argue that carrying out this task requires handling several paired relationships correctly.

The article takes six pairs in turn: top-level design and practical exploration; government leadership and multiple forces; economic development and improving livelihood; the present and the long term; overall advancement and breakthroughs in key areas; and doing one's best and acting within one's means. Each section sets out the two sides as complementary and then gives examples, mostly from social security, charity, employment, population policy, health reform and elderly care.

Lin and Wang treat each pair as a dialectical unity rather than a choice. On the economy, they hold that growth is the material basis of better livelihood, and that livelihood work in turn drives high-quality development and opens new growth points. They cite figures: per capita disposable income rising from 16,510 yuan in 2012 to 39,218 yuan in 2023, basic pension coverage of nearly 1.1 billion people, and centralised drug procurement savings of about 300 billion yuan. On the last pair, they present doing one's best as the Party and government's responsibility, and acting within one's means as the requirement to base welfare on sustainable economic and fiscal capacity, so as to avoid a "high-welfare trap".

The authors conclude that grasping these relationships, which they describe as a method of thinking and working stressed by Xi Jinping, will let policy combine firm direction with local initiative, state action with social participation, and urgent needs with lasting institutions. They say this will gradually bring about common prosperity for all. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary translates the Third Plenum's livelihood language into working principles, with the statistics it uses.
quoteEn: Doing one's best and acting within one's means are a dialectical unity within development; together they test the degree and level of high-quality development and ensure that common prosperity for all the people is gradually achieved.
quoteZh: 尽力而为和量力而行，两者辩证统一于发展之中，共同检验着高质量发展的程度和水平，确保逐步实现全体人民共同富裕。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, which the leadership has promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, that shifts emphasis from the speed of growth to its quality, including innovation, efficiency and the sharing of benefits.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, which the leadership has emphasised in recent years as a feature of socialism.
The official term for centrally planned, overall design of reforms and strategy, usually set against local experimentation.

t: Grasping the strategic priorities for advancing Chinese modernization
zh: 深刻把握推进中国式现代化的战略重点
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 20 September 2024, reads the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. Wu and Zhao argue that the decision's "seven focuses" together cover the strategic priorities of Chinese modernization. In their account, deepening reform in the new journey depends on grasping these priorities, ordering reform measures sensibly and carrying out the tasks effectively.

The article takes the seven focuses in turn, giving each a short paragraph. They are: a high-standard socialist market economy; whole-process people's democracy; a socialist cultural powerhouse; a higher quality of life for the people; a beautiful China; a higher-level safe China; and better Party leadership and long-term governing capacity. Each section opens by placing the priority within Chinese modernization, cites Xi Jinping, summarises developments since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and ends with what is required in the new journey.

The core of the argument is that each priority is both a component and a condition of Chinese modernization. The authors describe the socialist market economy as a creative combination of Marxist principles with practice, which can liberate and develop the productive forces and supply the material basis. Whole-process people's democracy is presented as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization, and the pursuit of common prosperity and a better life as its value goal. Ecological civilization, security and culture are treated as supporting foundations and spiritual underpinning. Party leadership, which the authors call the "most essential feature" of socialism with Chinese characteristics, is named the fundamental guarantee, and they link it to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform.

Wu and Zhao conclude that only by deepening reform along these seven lines can the goals of building a strong country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation be realised. Throughout, they treat the achievements since 2012 as proof that the chosen path works. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style overview of how the Third Plenum's reform decision was framed for a general readership in 2024.
quoteEn: The Party's level of leadership and its capacity for long-term governance directly determine the success or failure of our cause.
quoteZh: 党的领导水平和长期执政能力直接决定着我们事业的兴衰成败。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official concept of China's own path to modernization, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official term, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, for China's democratic model. It stresses popular participation at every stage of governance, not only at elections.
A Party goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping. It is linked to narrowing income and regional gaps.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's discipline and anti-corruption drive since 2012. It covers ideological, organisational and disciplinary measures.

An official term for the Party's continuing efforts to correct itself and maintain its governing capacity. Under Xi Jinping it is presented as the Party's answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal, tied to the Chinese Dream. It is set for the middle of the twenty-first century.

t: The construction logic of a high-standard socialist market economy
zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制的建构逻辑
paras: Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called a high-standard socialist market economy an important safeguard of Chinese modernization, Wang Shengsheng asks how such a system should be constructed. Writing in Guangming Daily on 24 September 2024, Wang argues that it bears on the whole of high-quality development and must be grasped through systems thinking. In this reading, its practical core is the dialectical unity of productive forces and relations of production, economic base and superstructure, and social development and state governance.

The article is organised into four sections, each naming a requirement for building the system: upholding the Party's overall leadership; letting an effective market play its role; letting a capable government play its role; and building the system on a rule-of-law footing. Each section ends in concrete reform measures drawn from the Plenum's language, such as a unified national market, property-rights protection and institutional opening up.

Wang's core claim is that the word "socialist" must be stressed first. Party leadership of economic work, in this account, secures the socialist direction of reform, mobilises the people and combines social mobilisation with organisational capacity, which Wang presents as a unity of democracy and centralism. An effective market depends on responsive price, supply-and-demand and competition mechanisms, on better division of labour and productivity through new quality productive forces, and on the Two Unwaverings, which Wang says free up market actors. A capable government is required because the law of value works spontaneously and the market cannot by itself settle accumulation and consumption, urban and rural areas, or regional layout. Wang gives government a role in organising major scientific projects, coordinating macroeconomic policy and building a new open economy with secure supply chains.

Wang concludes that the system should be built in step with legal construction, with major reforms grounded in law and reform results codified. Constitutional authority, equal legal protection for all forms of ownership, competition and anti-monopoly rules, a Financial Law and alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules are the measures proposed. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how official commentary after the 2024 Third Plenum links Party leadership, market, government and law in one framework.
quoteEn: In building a high-standard socialist market economy, the first thing is to stress the qualifier "socialist".
quoteZh: 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制，首先要突出“社会主义”这个定语。

glossary.zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.pinyin: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
glossary.explanation: A formulation from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) for the next stage of developing China's market-based economic system under Party leadership and public ownership as the mainstay.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models, and a central slogan since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 that stresses technology-led, innovation-driven productive forces such as digital and advanced manufacturing sectors.
The official goal of economic growth that emphasises quality, innovation and efficiency over speed alone, prominent since 2017.
A term in Chinese economic discourse for a government that actively intervenes through planning, regulation and public investment, usually paired with an "effective market".

t: Upholding a systems approach to further deepen reform comprehensively
zh: 坚持系统观念进一步全面深化改革
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 13 August 2024, takes up how reform should be advanced after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Ji and Wang argue that the systems approach (xitong guannian) is both a valuable lesson of comprehensively deepening reform in the new era and a major principle that further reform must follow.

The piece has three parts. It first traces the systems approach through successive Party leaderships, from Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping. It then discusses five major relationships that reform must handle: economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and development and security. It closes with three practical requirements for putting the approach into effect.

On the first part, the authors present the systems approach as a methodological summary of reform practice since reform and opening up. They cite Deng's view of reform as comprehensive, Jiang Zemin's twelve major relationships and Hu Jintao's "ten combinations", and argue that under Xi Jinping reform moved from local experiments and breakthroughs to systems integration. On the second, they hold that each pair of relationships is mutually reinforcing rather than opposed. Examples include the government and the market working as "two hands", fairness not meaning egalitarianism ("first make the cake bigger"), and high-quality development and high-level security supporting each other.

The authors call for stronger systems integration, with the Party exercising overall leadership, top-level design and coordination, and breakthroughs at key points driving the whole. They call for overall advancement, in which local and overall interests, root causes and symptoms, and gradual and breakthrough measures are combined. They also call for more coordinated reforms across fields from the market economy and whole-process people's democracy to ecological civilisation and national defence, backed by strong coordination mechanisms and supervision to ensure implementation. Read the original if you want a concise official-style statement of how the systems approach is meant to guide the reform agenda adopted in 2024.
quoteEn: Upholding the systems approach is both a valuable lesson from comprehensively deepening reform in the new era and a major principle that must be followed in further deepening reform comprehensively.
quoteZh: 坚持系统观念，既是新时代全面深化改革的一条宝贵经验，也是进一步全面深化改革必须贯彻的一个重大原则。

glossary.explanation: A method of thinking stressed by Xi Jinping that asks officials to treat policy areas as interconnected wholes, balancing global and local, short and long term, and main and secondary contradictions.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The official term, used since 2019, for China's democratic model, which the Party describes as covering every stage of decision-making and not only elections.

t: Exploring paths to accelerate the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 探索加快发展新质生产力的路径
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily in July 2024, asks how new quality productive forces can be developed faster. Yu argues that Xi Jinping's statements on the subject carry major theoretical and practical significance. The article holds that deepening understanding of them and finding concrete paths will support high-quality development and bring strategic initiative in international competition.

The piece is organised around four paths: developing new quality productive forces according to local conditions, strengthening science and technology innovation, deepening institutional reform, and building a large pool of high-calibre talent. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi and then sets out policy recommendations.

On local conditions, Yu calls for adherence to the Party's overall leadership and for each region to build on its own resources, avoiding blind imitation. On innovation, the author points to bottlenecks in core technologies and supply chains and to trade frictions created by some Western countries. Yu urges stronger basic research, upgrading of traditional industries and deeper integration of the digital and real economies. On reform, the author argues that production relations must suit the productive forces, and proposes a unified national market, an effective market working with an effective government, and wider opening up.

On talent, Yu proposes expanded vocational education, more open recruitment and less burdensome evaluation for researchers. The article concludes that these four steps together would create conditions for new quality productive forces and strengthen the drivers of high-quality development. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary translates Xi's remarks on new quality productive forces into a policy checklist.
quoteEn: Only by comprehensively deepening reform, continuously driving change in the mode, drivers and quality of development, and further removing institutional obstacles so that new production relations take shape, can more favourable conditions and broader space be created for the development of new quality productive forces.
quoteZh: 只有通过全面深化改革，不断推动发展方式、发展动力、发展质量变革，进一步破除体制机制障碍，形成新型生产关系，才能为新质生产力的发展创造更加有利的条件、开辟更加广阔的空间。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than traditional resource-heavy growth.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth emphasising efficiency, innovation and sustainability, prominent since 2017.

t: Developing new quality productive forces requires winning five innovation campaigns
zh: 发展新质生产力亟待打好五大创新战役
paras: Fan Jida asks how China should organise innovation in order to develop new quality productive forces, which the article defines as an advanced form of productive forces led by innovation, marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality, and consistent with the new development philosophy. Fan argues that, in light of a new round of technological revolution and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), the task should be pursued through five distinct "campaigns". The piece appeared in Red Flag Manuscript (Hongqi Wengao) in 2024 and cites Xi Jinping's statement that high-quality development requires such productive forces.

The article is organised as five sections, each framed as a campaign: a decisive battle on key core technologies, a protracted war on basic research, a contest for innovative talent, a breakout battle for enterprises in competition, and a positional battle for regional innovation. Each section combines a diagnosis of current weaknesses with policy proposals, and cites the Third Plenum's wording. Fan draws on figures for research spending and on historical examples of Britain and Germany to support the case.

On technology, Fan says many key technologies remain controlled by others and calls for strengthening national laboratories, the Chinese Academies of Sciences and Engineering, and research universities. The new-type whole-nation system, Fan stresses, is not government control of everything, a substitute for private-sector innovation, or a return to the planned economy. On basic research, Fan cites 2023 spending of 2,212 billion yuan, only 6.65 per cent of R&D funding, and argues that many bottleneck problems stem from weak foundational theory. Fan proposes steadier funding, more autonomy for scientists and new evaluation methods. On talent, enterprises and regions, Fan calls for reform of education, support for young scientists, immigration arrangements for high-tech talent, and enterprise R&D reserves and patient capital. Fan also proposes innovation centres in Beijing, Shanghai and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area, and upgrading traditional industries rather than abandoning them.

Fan concludes that these five campaigns together form the path to developing new quality productive forces, and that matching production relations, meaning institutional and management reform, must accompany technological effort. The text also stresses openness, arguing that regions should use international innovation resources rather than pursue self-isolation. Read the original if you want a Party-journal statement of how the Third Plenum's innovation agenda is translated into specific policy priorities on science funding, talent, enterprises and regional development.
quoteEn: This \"whole-nation system\" is by no means the government taking charge of everything, nor a substitute for private enterprises' innovation, still less a return to the management system of the planned-economy period.
quoteZh: 这一“举国体制”绝不是政府包揽一切，不是对民营企业创新的替代，更不是回到计划经济时期的管理体制

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation rather than traditional growth paths.
A set of five principles (innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development) introduced by the Party leadership in 2015 to guide economic policy.
An official policy goal since 2017 that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over the speed of growth.
An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources in a coordinated way to achieve major scientific and technological goals.
A common expression for technologies on which China depends on foreign suppliers and which can be restricted by others.

t: New quality productive forces inject momentum into high-quality development
zh: 新质生产力为高质量发展注入动能
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 23 July 2024, takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its call to treat high-quality development as the primary task of building a modern socialist country. Yuan Lei argues that new quality productive forces are an inherent requirement of high-quality development and a key lever for it. The author presents the concept as Xi Jinping's theoretical summary of productive-force development in the new era, drawing on the basic principles of Marxist political economy.

The article is organised in three parts. The first explains why developing new quality productive forces follows from the new development stage, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern. The second sets out four "dividends" through which they are said to raise total factor productivity. The third lists four routes to high-level scientific and technological self-reliance.

Yuan's central claim is that new quality productive forces raise total factor productivity, which the author calls the key to improving both the quality and the quantity of growth. The four dividends are technological (new products and higher efficiency, with traditional industries said to make up over 80% of manufacturing), structural (innovative allocation of production factors as the old shift from agriculture to manufacturing slows), green (the author cites energy use per unit of GDP at about 1.5 times the world average, and an output target of 11 trillion yuan for green industries by 2025) and reform-related. The reform dividend is tied to changes in the relations of production: reform of the economic system, the science and technology system, factor markets and income distribution. Yuan also argues that these forces can ease regional imbalances, cut resource costs, support opening up and help domestic and international circulation.

Yuan proposes four tasks: let scientific and technological innovation lead, especially in basic research; push industrial upgrading through strategic emerging and future industries; accelerate the green transformation of development; and build institutions that let each region develop new quality productive forces according to local conditions. The author presents these as the way to secure a material and technological base for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official economic commentary links new quality productive forces to total factor productivity and institutional reform.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces is an inherent requirement of, and an important focal point for, promoting high-quality development.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力是推动高质量发展的内在要求和重要着力点。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading. It is presented as a new stage in adapting Marxist political economy to China.
The official goal, stressed since 2017, of moving from fast growth to growth that is efficient, innovative, green and balanced.
The Party's guiding approach of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, introduced in 2015.
The official name for China's path to becoming a modern socialist country, a core concept since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An economic measure of output growth not accounted for by increases in labour and capital inputs, often used as a proxy for technology and efficiency.
A strategy, proposed in 2020, that centres on domestic circulation of the economy while keeping international circulation as a complement.

t: The theoretical connotations and practical requirements of new quality productive forces
zh: 新质生产力的理论内涵和实践要求
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in July 2024, asks what new quality productive forces are and how they should be developed. Xu Jianwei and Li Ziwen present Xi Jinping's statements on the subject as an innovation and development of the Marxist theory of productive forces. They argue that the theoretical meaning of the concept must be combined with concrete practical requirements.

The article first sets out the content of the concept, then turns to six practical requirements. It treats the new development philosophy, scientific and technological innovation, the optimal recombination of production factors, the modern industrial system, total factor productivity and deepened reform as the guiding principle, driver, substance, carrier, marker and safeguard of the new productive forces.

On the theory, the authors define new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productive forces in line with the new development philosophy. Their basic content is a leap in workers, means of labour, objects of labour and their optimal combination, and they form an organic whole. Technological innovation is the core factor, the modern industrial system is the carrier, and a large rise in total factor productivity is the core marker. Supply-chain resilience and lower emissions are further measures. On practice, the authors distinguish two kinds of innovation: broadly penetrating technological revolutions and vertically disruptive technological changes. They say weak traditional industries reflect insufficient innovation, and they call for innovation to be applied to upgrading traditional industries, nurturing emerging ones and planning future ones.

The authors conclude that relations of production must suit the development of productive forces, so further comprehensive deepening of reform is needed to build new-type production relations. They call for reforms in science, education and talent systems, factor markets, opening up and income distribution. Read the original if you want a concise official-style summary of how the new quality productive forces concept was framed in Chinese policy discussion in mid-2024.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are an advanced form of productive forces in which innovation plays the leading role; by spreading new technologies they greatly raise total factor productivity and open up broader room for gains in returns.
quoteZh: 新质生产力是创新起主导作用的先进生产力质态，通过推广应用新技术大幅提高全要素生产率，带来更加广阔的效益增长空间。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping from 2023, describing advanced productive forces driven by innovation rather than by heavy input of resources and low-cost labour. It is presented in official discourse as a development of Marxist productive-forces theory.
A set of five principles announced in 2015: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. Official texts treat it as guiding China's economic policy.
An official term for an industrial structure described as complete, advanced and secure, combining upgraded traditional industries with emerging and future industries.
An economic measure of the overall efficiency with which inputs are turned into output, reflecting technology, factor allocation and institutional factors.

t: Making better use of market mechanisms and creating a fairer, more dynamic market environment
zh: 更好发挥市场机制作用 创造更加公平、更有活力的市场环境
paras: Writing in Qiushi (2024, no. 17), Luo Wen interprets the market-related sections of the Decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. The article takes up the core question of the government–market relationship and argues that market regulators must raise their comprehensive supervisory capacity so that the market is both free enough ("放得活", "let go effectively") and well enough governed ("管得住", "kept under control"). In Luo's account, this serves to optimise resource allocation, remedy market failure and release innovation.

The piece is a policy commentary organised in six parts, each linking a passage of the Decision to the tasks of market supervision. They cover basic market-economy institutions, the healthy development of business entities, fair competition policy, market order, public-safety baselines, and the modernization of comprehensive market supervision. Each part first explains why the Decision's provision matters, then lists concrete measures for the regulatory authorities.

Luo's central claim is that vitality and order are organically unified, which the article equates with a better combination of an efficient market and a capable government. On one side, it calls for protecting property rights, market access, credit systems and equal treatment of all forms of ownership under the Two Unwaverings, while curbing local protectionism, market fragmentation, monopoly and unfair competition. On the other, it holds that price violations, counterfeits and false advertising distort incentives, and that food, drug and industrial safety are expressions of market failure that the state must address.

For supervision itself, Luo proposes tools including graded credit regulation, unified information systems, "smart supervision" and standardised administrative discretion. The article calls for strengthening legal, credit-based and smart supervision to fit a super-large market, and presents this as support for modernising national governance. Specific measures include a mandatory exit system for business entities, trade-secret protection, a review system for fair competition, regulation of platform firms and stronger consumer-rights enforcement. Read the original if you want a detailed, official-line account of how China's market regulators translate the Third Plenum Decision into concrete supervisory tasks.
quoteEn: The organic unity of vitality and order is in essence a better combination of an efficient market and a capable government.
quoteZh: 活力和秩序的有机统一，实质上就是有效市场和有为政府的更好结合。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula calling for unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector. It underpins official policy on the mixed-ownership economy.
The official name for the Party's development path and goal, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models of modernization.

glossary.en: an efficient market and a capable government
glossary.explanation: A formula for the government–market relationship in which the market plays the decisive role in allocating resources while the government acts to correct failures and maintain order.
An official umbrella term for enterprises, individual businesses and other registered market participants.

t: The contemporary expression of building an independent knowledge system of Chinese philosophy and social sciences
zh: 构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系的时代表达
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2024, Lü Xinbin takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which named the building of an independent knowledge system of Chinese philosophy and social sciences as a strategic task. Lü argues that, if reform is to power this task, it must rest on three underlying logics: a fundamental direction, a fundamental attitude and a fundamental path.

The commentary is organised under three headings: "holding to the soul and the roots" (direction), "firm confidence and consciousness" (attitude), and "adhering to innovation and creation" (path). Each section draws on Xi Jinping's statements and on the 20th Party Congress (2022) and Third Plenum documents. Lü also gives examples from the Hebei Academy of Social Sciences, which Lü presents as putting each principle into practice through research projects and reform programmes.

On direction, Lü holds that the "soul" is Marxism, now embodied in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and Xi Jinping's thought on culture, and the "roots" are fine traditional Chinese culture. The two are joined in the Two Integrations and in the practice of Chinese modernization. On attitude, Lü calls for cultural subjectivity, intellectual independence and a sense of mission, and says China is creating a new form of human civilisation that goes beyond Western capitalist and traditional socialist civilisations, in which Chinese social science should play a foundational and leading role. On path, Lü stresses innovation in theory, practice, institutions and culture, plus creative transformation and innovative development of tradition. Lü argues that no ready-made textbook exists for China's social transformation, so new concepts and categories must be drawn from Chinese practice.

Lü concludes that direction settles the question of the banner of reform, attitude the question of resolve, and path the question of substance, and that together they will bring a new era of flourishing for the independent knowledge system. Lü expects theory to interpret Chinese practice and practice to enrich theory, and envisions a more systematic, scholarly Chinese social science. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official commentary after the Third Plenum frames the task of building an independent knowledge system, including local academy examples from Hebei.
quoteEn: We must distil new theories with scholarly rigour from the practice of China's reform and development, summarise new practices that reveal regularities, and strive to put forward civilisational models distinctive in Chinese standpoint, Chinese wisdom and Chinese values.
quoteZh: 必须从我国改革发展的实践中提炼出有学理性的新理论，概括出有规律性的新实践，着力提出独具中国立场、中国智慧、中国价值的文明样本。

glossary.explanation: A slogan from Xi Jinping's speeches, notably 2022, for Chinese-originated disciplines, academic concepts and discourse not dependent on Western frameworks. The Third Plenum (2024) listed it among reform tasks.
Xi Jinping's formulation that Marxism is the "soul" and fine traditional Chinese culture the "roots" of theoretical innovation.
Official formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in 2021–23.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought, formally put forward in 2023, covering ideological and cultural work and the "new cultural mission".
A term stressed by Xi Jinping from 2023, meaning that Chinese culture should maintain its own standpoint and identity while drawing on other civilisations.

t: Building a high-standard socialist market economy
zh: 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制
paras: Guo Chunli takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) formulation that a high-standard socialist market economy is an important guarantee for Chinese modernization. This newspaper commentary argues that the system should be built by improving four things: high-quality business entities, a high-standard market system, high-efficiency basic institutions of the market economy, and a high-efficiency governance system. Guo presents this as a way to supply strong momentum and institutional support for Chinese modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why the system is needed and what it means, tracing the socialist market economy from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee through the 14th Party Congress and the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee to the 2024 plenum. The second lists four ways in which the system underpins Chinese modernization. The third sets out four practical tasks.

In Guo's account, the core of the system is the "decisive role" of the market in allocating resources together with a better-performing government, producing what the article calls an effective market and a capable government in organic unity. The author reads the reform record as a deepening Party understanding of market laws and a search for an economic system suited to the productive forces, including new quality productive forces. The four guarantees are: meeting the goals for 2035 and the mid-century target, mainly by raising total factor productivity; applying the new development philosophy fully; building a new development pattern through a national unified market and domestic–international dual circulation; and promoting high-quality development.

Guo's four tasks are to uphold the Two Unwaverings, including a law to promote the private economy, to build a unified national market, to improve basic market institutions (property rights, market access, bankruptcy, social credit), and to improve macroeconomic governance. The last covers policy coordination, fiscal, tax and financial reform, and regional coordination. The piece is an official-line statement of how the plenum's market-economy agenda is to be understood and implemented. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative-style overview of the policy priorities and rationale for the "high-standard socialist market economy" after the 2024 plenum.
quoteEn: The core of building a high-standard socialist market economy is to give full play to the decisive role of the market in resource allocation while better playing the role of the government.
quoteZh: 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制，核心是充分发挥市场在资源配置中的决定性作用，更好发挥政府作用

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A concept promoted since 2023 that stresses technology-driven, innovation-led productive forces as a basis for high-quality development.
The Party's guiding framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, introduced in 2015.
The official goal of shifting from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and innovation, described as the first task of building a modern socialist country.
A policy aim to remove local protection and market segmentation so that goods and factors of production move freely across China.

t: Finding the right path to accelerate the cultivation and development of new quality productive forces
zh: 找准路径加快培育发展新质生产力
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 29 August 2024, asks how China can speed up the cultivation of new quality productive forces. Deng Quheng argues that the path runs through three tasks: deep industrial transformation and upgrading, innovative allocation of production factors, and deeper reform of institutions and mechanisms. The piece takes its direction from the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which it quotes at the outset.

The article is organised under three headings that match these tasks. The first deals with industrial structure, the balance between traditional, emerging and future industries, and coordination among regions. The second covers technology, talent and finance as the main factors to be allocated. The third turns to markets, income distribution, and the joint development of education, science and technology, and talent.

Deng holds that upgrading industry raises labour productivity and total factor productivity and helps China gain the initiative in a restructuring of global industrial chains. Traditional industries, which the author says make up over 80% of manufacturing, should become carriers of new quality productive forces, while strategic emerging and future industries receive support for core technology breakthroughs. On factors, Deng calls for pooling scientific resources through the new whole-nation system, turning the demographic dividend into a talent dividend, and steering finance, including patient capital, towards early-stage and hard-technology projects. Citing the principle that production relations must suit the productive forces, the author proposes building new production relations by improving factor markets, relying on state-owned enterprises and private firms, and reforming income distribution.

Deng concludes that reform must clear the blockages that hold back new quality productive forces and let advanced innovation factors gather around them. Education, science and technology, and talent cultivation are to be advanced together. Read the original if you want a concise policy-oriented overview of how a Chinese economist links the Third Plenum's reform agenda to new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Productive forces determine production relations, and production relations must be suited to the development of the productive forces.
quoteZh: 生产力决定生产关系，生产关系需与生产力发展相适应。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading. It is presented as a basis for high-quality development.
An official term for mobilising national resources, combining state coordination with market mechanisms, to achieve major scientific and technological goals.
Long-term investment capital that tolerates slow returns and high risk, promoted in official policy to fund technological innovation.

t: Upholding a systems approach in developing new quality productive forces
zh: 坚持系统观念发展新质生产力
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily in September 2024, asks how new quality productive forces should be developed. Yang and Ge argue that this is a systemic undertaking touching every area of economic and social life, and that it requires a systems approach. They tie the argument to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for sound institutions for developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions.

The authors first define new quality productive forces and analyse them from the standpoint of systems theory. They then set out two methodological principles, and close with three practical measures: basic research, talent and the modern industrial system.

In the authors' account, new quality productive forces are a complex system of elements, structure and function. The elements are new types of workers, objects of labour, instruments of labour and infrastructure; the structure is a modern industrial system led by emerging and future industries; the function is to raise total factor productivity and meet people's needs for a better life. They stress that these forces are a qualitative leap driven by innovation, not a marginal improvement on traditional productive forces. Two principles follow: proceed from local realities, since no uniform template exists, and advance as a whole while achieving breakthroughs at key points. The authors add that emerging industries and the digital, green and integrated upgrading of traditional industries should reinforce each other.

Yang and Ge call for sustained investment in basic research and organised research, a strategy of strengthening the country through talent, with fewer barriers to mobility and a reformed evaluation system, and a modern industrial system with secure, self-controlled industrial and supply chains. They name quantum information, brain-inspired intelligence, gene technology and brain–computer interfaces as targets for breakthroughs. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official systems-based reading of new quality productive forces and its policy priorities.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are not a partial optimisation or simple improvement of traditional productive forces, but a qualitative leap realised from the quantitative change that innovation sets off: productive forces of higher quality, higher efficiency and greater advancement.
quoteZh: 新质生产力不是传统生产力的局部优化与简单提升，而是创新激发的量变实现了质的跃迁，是更高质量、更高效率、更先进的生产力。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of factors and industrial upgrading. It is linked to high-quality development.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōng quánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A plenary meeting of the Chinese Communist Party's Central Committee held in July 2024. It adopted a decision on further deepening reform.
A method stressing that problems be viewed as interconnected wholes, with overall planning and coordination. It is presented in Party documents as a basic principle of governance.
An official term for an industrial structure combining advanced manufacturing, emerging and future industries and upgraded traditional sectors, with secure supply chains.

t: Paying attention to strengthening the Party's leadership over reform
zh: 注重加强党对改革的领导
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 22 August 2024, reads the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. Cao Wenze argues that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of further comprehensive deepening of reform, and that it must run through every aspect and stage of reform.

The piece is organised in four short sections. It deals in turn with the Party's vanguard character as the reason for leading reform, the full leadership of the Party as an experience and principle of reform since 1978, the building of a stronger Marxist party, and the Party's self-reform as the guide of broader social revolution.

Cao begins from the Communist Manifesto, taking Marx and Engels's account of communists as the most resolute, driving section of the movement to mean that a Marxist party is inherently reform-minded. The author then argues that reform has reached its "deepest part of the deep waters", where deep institutional problems rather than local ones are at stake. In this setting, Cao holds, the Party must uphold the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds so that reform avoids both a rigid closed path and a path of abandoning socialism. Cao also presents Party leadership and Party building as advancing together: reform requires full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and better leadership is itself an internal requirement of reform.

Cao concludes that the Party should strengthen centralised, unified leadership and the mechanisms for implementing Central Committee decisions, and should pursue the Party's self-reform through ideological, organisational, conduct and discipline building and anti-corruption work. The stated aim is to complete the Decision's reform tasks by 2029, the 80th anniversary of the People's Republic. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary justifies Party leadership of reform after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's overall leadership is a valuable experience of reform and opening up, especially of comprehensively deepening reform in the new era, and also an important principle that further comprehensive deepening of reform must follow.
quoteZh: 坚持党的全面领导，是改革开放以来特别是新时代全面深化改革的宝贵经验，也是进一步全面深化改革必须贯彻的重要原则。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan from the Xi Jinping era for strict Party discipline, ideological education and anti-corruption work within the Party.
The Party's official term for its own continuing self-purification, self-improvement and renewal through internal discipline and institutional reform.
The official concept of China's path to modernization under Party leadership, set out prominently in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

t: Deepening reform to provide momentum for developing new quality productive forces
zh: 深化改革为发展新质生产力提供动力
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 28 August 2024, Zhang Wanming argues that speeding up new quality productive forces is a question of reform as much as of development. Taking the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) as its starting point, the commentary holds that further comprehensively deepening reform is needed to build production relations better suited to these forces and to raise total factor productivity.

The piece moves in three steps. It first sets out what developing new quality productive forces requires, then explains why reform must continue in three areas, and finally lists the institutional mechanisms to be improved. Zhang follows the Plenum's wording closely and presents the argument as an application of the Party's line.

Zhang defines new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productive forces produced by revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and deep industrial transformation and upgrading. Three requirements follow: innovation as the primary driving force, a modern industrial system as the main lever, and efficient allocation of production factors as the foothold. Zhang then argues that reform is itself innovation, with technological and institutional innovation compared to a bird's two wings. Reform is said to be needed to release innovative vitality, to deepen industrial upgrading through supply-side structural reform, and to correct the misallocation of factors, including barriers to urban–rural exchange. Four sets of measures are proposed: reform of the science and technology system, reform of market-based allocation of factors (property protection, market access, fair competition, a unified national market, the Two Unwaverings), reform of talent development, and wider high-level opening up, including institutional opening up.

Zhang concludes that new quality productive forces should be pursued through comprehensive reform of the economic, scientific, educational, talent and financial systems, and by improving mechanisms suited to local conditions. The commentary treats reform and opening up as the means of releasing productive potential. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how reform is linked to new quality productive forces in the policy discussion after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Innovation is not only technological innovation but also institutional innovation.
quoteZh: 创新不仅是技术创新，也是制度创新。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new factor allocation and industrial upgrading, in place of resource-intensive growth.
The official formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
An economic measure of output growth not accounted for by increases in labour and capital inputs. Official texts use it as an indicator of efficiency and quality of growth.
A policy approach launched around 2015 that aims to cut ineffective and low-end supply and expand effective and mid-to-high-end supply.
The policy of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground to keep reform steady and far-reaching
zh: 坚持守正创新推动改革行稳致远
paras: This commentary in Economic Daily takes up one of the major principles of the decision adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): "upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground" (守正创新). Zhang argues that this principle is the essential requirement of reform and a methodology for further deepening reform comprehensively, which demands both strategic resolve and sound methods.

The piece has three parts. It first presents the principle as a lesson from the Party's century of struggle and from reform and opening up. It then sets out what "upholding fundamental principles" requires, and finally what "breaking new ground" requires.

On the first side, Zhang argues that reform must keep to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, rejecting both a rigid, closed path and a path of changing banners. The author lists five anchors: the Four Cardinal Principles, Chinese modernization as the theme, the overall goal of improving the socialist system and modernizing national governance, and the socialist market economy. On the second side, Zhang calls for courage in emancipating the mind, a problem-oriented approach aimed at deep-seated institutional obstacles, and innovation in theory, practice, institutions and culture.

Zhang concludes that fundamental principles secure the direction and prevent "subversive errors", while innovation lets reform keep pace with the times. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style account of how the Third Plenum's reform principle is explained to a Chinese economic readership.
quoteEn: Only by upholding fundamental principles can reform avoid losing its direction and committing subversive errors; only by innovating can it discern what the times demand, keep pace with them and adapt to circumstances, so that reform always stays at the forefront and leads the era.
quoteZh: 只有坚持守正才能不迷失改革前进的方向、不犯颠覆性错误；坚持创新才能辨明时势发展的要求，做到与时俱进、相机而变，使改革始终勇立潮头、引领时代。

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse for holding to the correct political path and basic principles while innovating in theory, practice and institutions. The Third Plenum (2024) listed it among the principles of further deepening reform.
The official name for the Party's model of national development, presented as distinct from Western modernization. It is the central theme of the Third Plenum's reform decision.
Principles set out by Deng Xiaoping in 1979: the socialist path, the people's democratic dictatorship, the leadership of the Communist Party, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.
The official description of China's economic system, which combines public ownership as the mainstay with market allocation of resources.

t: Methodological features of further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 进一步全面深化改革的方法论特征
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in September 2024, interprets the methodology behind the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. The Decision calls for "paying more attention" to three things: systems integration, key priorities and practical results. Liu argues that these three emphases summarise the methodology of the reform effort so far and are the distinctive methodological features of the next stage. In Liu's view, only a scientific method can keep reform clear in direction and steady in progress, so that it supplies momentum and institutional guarantees for Chinese modernization.

The article is organised in three sections, one for each "paying more attention". Each section gives a philosophical grounding, an assessment of the reform record since the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), and a set of requirements for the new stage. It is a short official-style commentary rather than a research study, and it relies on Party documents and the vocabulary of materialist dialectics.

On systems integration, Liu grounds the principle in the dialectical view of universal connection: society is an organic system whose elements constrain and affect one another. Reform has moved from laying foundations to comprehensive advance and now to integration and coordination. Because structural contradictions have sharpened, Liu holds, single-item or piecemeal reform no longer suffices. Reform must be made more systematic, integrated and coordinated, with economic reform leading and the Party's leadership as the coordinating core. On key priorities, Liu invokes the unity of the "two-point" and "key-point" approaches, meaning attention to principal versus secondary contradictions. Priorities include the government–market relationship, high-quality development, macroeconomic governance, urban–rural integration and high-level opening up, together with livelihood problems such as housing, employment and healthcare. On practical results, Liu stresses implementation: a plan means little unless it takes effect. The author calls for a "nail-driving spirit", a correct view of performance, avoidance of formalism and vanity projects, and better mechanisms for follow-up, supervision and evaluation.

Liu concludes that Chinese modernization advances through reform and opening up, and that the Party must grasp these methodological features and turn the strategic plans of the Decision into driving force for modernization. The text offers a compact guide to how official commentary frames the method of the current reform agenda. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese Party-affiliated writers link materialist dialectics to the policy method of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee.
quoteEn: Reform needs to advance as a whole, but effort must not be spread evenly; it should focus on the key issues that affect the whole, and use breakthroughs on priorities to drive overall development.
quoteZh: 改革需要整体推进，但不能平均用力，要聚焦牵一发而动全身的关键问题，以重点突破带动全局发展。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the central task of national rejuvenation.
A reform principle stressing that measures across fields should be linked, coordinated and mutually reinforcing rather than pursued in isolation.
A phrase associated with Xi Jinping, meaning persistence in carrying a task through step by step until it is actually implemented.
The official economic goal, stated since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth emphasising quality, innovation and efficiency.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in China in 1978.

glossary.literal: theory of two points and theory of key points
glossary.explanation: A formulation from Mao Zedong's dialectics: consider both aspects of a contradiction, while identifying the principal contradiction and its main aspect.

t: Grasping the rich connotations and practical requirements of new quality productive forces
zh: 把握新质生产力的丰富内涵和实践要求
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 6 September 2024, asks how new quality productive forces should be understood and developed in light of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Zhong and Wang argue that Xi Jinping's statements on the subject are an innovative development of Marxist productive-force theory and that developing new quality productive forces is an inherent requirement of high-quality development.

The article follows the Plenum Decision's wording and takes up three tasks in turn: driving revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovatively allocating factors of production, and deeply transforming and upgrading industry. A closing section sets out why the development matters and what institutional steps follow.

On technology, the authors hold that scientific and technological innovation is the core element, producing new industries, models and drivers of growth, and they call for original and disruptive innovation and breakthroughs in key core technologies. On factors of production, they say the "newness" lies in new qualities of labourers, means of labour and objects of labour, and in their optimised recombination, which raises total factor productivity. On industry, they note that traditional industries make up over 80 per cent of manufacturing and should be upgraded with digital-intelligence and green technologies rather than phased out as "low-end"; strategic emerging and future industries are described as the main arena.

The authors present new quality productive forces as a major strategic measure for advancing Chinese modernization and as a way for China to shift from "follower" to "leader" in science and industry. They add that suitable relations of production require deep, systematic reform, including stronger institutional supply for new fields, higher standards, and financial support such as venture capital and "patient capital". Read the original if you want a concise, official-style outline of the policy components that the Party attaches to new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Industry is the carrier of productive forces.
quoteZh: 产业是生产力的载体。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–2024 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading. It is presented as a Chinese development of Marxist productive-force theory.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth based on efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
The official name for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de Èrshí Jiè Sān Zhōng Quánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A Central Committee meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a Decision on further deepening reform comprehensively.

t: Keeping institution-building as the main thread
zh: 始终突出制度建设这条主线
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 22 August 2024, explains why the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) made "adhering to institution-building as the main thread" an important principle of further comprehensively deepening reform. Tao Wenzhao argues that the Party has consistently kept institution-building at the centre of reform, and that this can be understood along three dimensions: goal orientation, historical process and problem awareness.

The piece draws on Xi Jinping's explanation of the Plenum's Decision and on earlier Party documents. It moves from the overall goal of reform, through the history of institution-building since reform and opening up, to the priorities set out in the Decision.

On goals, Tao notes that the overall aim is to improve and develop the socialist system with Chinese characteristics and modernise national governance, now with the word "continue" added to the 18th Central Committee's formulation. In Tao's reading, this signals continuity and stages in the same effort. On history, Tao traces a path from Deng Xiaoping's remark on a more mature and fixed system, through the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), to a stage that demands more systematic and coordinated design. On problems, Tao says existing institutions must be improved while new ones are created. The Decision's "seven focuses" and more than 300 measures, Tao argues, all run through institution-building.

Tao concludes that more deliberate attention to institutions will give Chinese modernization strong momentum and institutional guarantees, turning institutional advantages into governance effectiveness. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of why institution-building is presented as the organising principle of the 2024 reform agenda.
quoteEn: When institutions are stable, the country is stable; when institutions are strong, the country is strong.
quoteZh: 制度稳则国家稳，制度强则国家强。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernisation, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The theme of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (July 2024), continuing the reform agenda launched in 2013.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernisation of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal set at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) to make China's institutions and their operation more effective and systematic.

t: Summing up and elevating the Party's successful experience in leading reform and opening up
zh: 党领导改革开放成功经验的总结升华
