An official slogan, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over pure growth rates.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, promoted since 2012–2013, which stresses shared interests and cooperation among countries.
A Party goal put forward in the early to mid-2000s under Hu Jintao, aimed at easing social tensions and inequalities.

keywords: philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics

t: The theory of new quality productive forces and the construction of China's independent knowledge system
zh: 新质生产力理论与中国自主知识体系建构
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, Wei Chuanguang takes the theory of new quality productive forces as a model case of how China's independent knowledge system is being built. The article holds that the theory, associated with Xi Jinping, is an exemplar of an independent Chinese economics and offers methodological guidance for the wider project.

The piece starts from Xi's 17 May 2016 speech on philosophy and social sciences and his April 2022 call at Renmin University to build an independent Chinese knowledge system. It then works through the theory under three headings: coining a distinctive Chinese term, keeping a problem orientation, and innovating theory in response to new practice.

Wei argues first that new quality productive forces is a distinctive Chinese term which recasts the Marxist category of productive forces for the present era. In Wei's account, it stresses disruptive technological breakthroughs, innovation-driven development and the innovative allocation of production factors, and it is easily understood abroad. Second, the theory answers problems that "foreign theories" cannot, such as the shift to high-quality development, the digital economy and carbon peaking and neutrality. Third, it keeps the Marxist productive forces–relations of production framework while giving more weight to original, disruptive innovation. Wei links this to progress in chips, deep-sea and deep-space technology.

Wei concludes that the theory raises the originality and competitiveness of China's knowledge system and widens the influence of Chinese discourse. Wei also presents it as an example of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Wei urges scholars to work on major problems of national importance in order to take part in building the system. Read the original if you want a short, official-line example of how Chinese scholars link the theory of new quality productive forces to the call for independent knowledge production.
quoteEn: The theory of new quality productive forces is an independent theoretical innovation, advanced to address and study the "Chinese problems" that arise amid broad and profound social change and grand, distinctive practical innovation.
quoteZh: 新质生产力理论是应对和研究广泛而深刻的社会变革、宏大而独特的实践创新中出现的“中国问题”而推进的自主理论创新。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first used in September 2023 in Heilongjiang. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, and is tied to the policy of high-quality development.
An official goal, in use since around 2017, of shifting from fast growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and sustainability.
A call by Xi Jinping in 2022 for Chinese scholarship to build its own concepts and theories from China's own experience, rather than relying on Western ones.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and to the present era, and for developing it further in that process.

t: Engels's late-life guidance of the British workers' movement in practice
zh: 恩格斯晚年指导英国工人运动的实践历程
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, asks how Engels, in his last years and without leading any organisation, shaped the British workers' movement. Liu Jian argues that he became an intellectual and practical mentor to the international workers' movement. In Britain he guided it in two ways: through the New Unionism and through the founding of an independent working-class party.

The article opens by noting Britain's place as the home of utopian socialism and the birthplace of scientific socialism. It says that after Chartism the British working class lost its revolutionary edge and trade unionism took hold. Liu then takes two cases in turn: the New Unionism of the late 1880s, and Engels's advice on party-building, including the Independent Labour Party founded in 1893.

Liu contends that Engels criticised trade unionism for settling for "a fair day's wage for a fair day's work" and for creating a labour aristocracy. In his 1881 articles for the Labour Standard, Engels pointed to wage labour itself as the root problem, called for workers' ownership of the means of labour and urged workers to organise and send their own representatives to parliament. Marxist-influenced leaders such as Tom Mann and John Burns led the movement, and the 1889 London dock strike was its climax. On party-building, Liu says Engels urged a break with dependence on the Liberal Party. The later reformist turn of the Independent Labour Party is presented as proof that a workers' party cannot succeed without scientific socialism as its theory.

Liu concludes that Engels's indirect guidance, through letters, articles and advice to leaders such as Mahon and Hardie, marked each stage of British party-building. Liu holds that his work was inseparable from Marx's and that he deserves the title of outstanding scholar and teacher of the modern proletariat. Read the original if you want a brief overview of Engels's practical influence on late nineteenth-century British labour politics.
quoteEn: The development of the Independent Labour Party proved that, without accepting scientific socialism as its theoretical basis, establishing a working-class party cannot succeed.
quoteZh: 独立工党的发展证明了如果不接受科学社会主义作为理论基础，建立工人阶级政党是不会成功的。

t: The logic of Engels's research on scientific socialism
zh: 恩格斯科学社会主义研究的学理逻辑
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 18 August 2024
paras: This short commentary asks how Engels studied scientific socialism and what his methods mean for research today. Zhang argues that Engels upheld Marxism's basic method while building more specific methodological principles suited to scientific socialism's object and content, thereby carrying Marxism a step further.

The article distinguishes two levels in Engels's work. One concerns scientific socialism as theory, including its content, relations and place within the whole of Marxism. The other concerns socialism as a practical movement and institutional form, including general laws, basic principles and paths of development. It closes with proposals for research on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

On theory, Zhang reports that Engels treated dialectics, epistemology and logic as identical, called for analysis based on full command of concrete material, and warned against quoting out of context and against dogmatism. On practice, Engels is said to have made historical materialism the methodological base, mediated by materialist dialectics, to show how capitalist private ownership cannot accommodate the productive forces and moves towards self-negation. Zhang adds that Engels kept class analysis central to the end of his life, calling violent seizure of political power the "only door to the new society". Engels also stressed researchers' diligence and a sound scholarly attitude.

Zhang draws five tasks for research on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They are to start from the changed principal contradiction in Chinese society, to keep a people-centred position, and to study the logical starting point of Sinicized Marxism through dialectics, epistemology and logic. They also include drawing out its methodology and keeping a rigorous, truth-seeking attitude. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese statement of how Engels's methodological writings are being tied to current Party-theory research.
quoteEn: Class analysis, especially taking class struggle as a main thread for observing class society, was a basic methodological principle to which Engels consistently adhered.
quoteZh: 阶级分析法尤其是以阶级斗争作为观察阶级社会的一条主要线索，是恩格斯始终坚持的基本方法论原则。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for combining Marxist theory with Chinese realities and contemporary conditions. The article uses the shorter form 'Sinicized Marxism'.

t: Engels's critique of erroneous currents of thought
zh: 恩格斯对错误思潮的批判
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 18 August 2024
paras: This short commentary starts from the claim that the history of Marxism is also a history of struggle against erroneous theories. Zhang and Zhou argue that Engels was not only a founder and developer of Marxism but also its loyal defender. In their account, he criticised harmful currents in the workers' movement without mercy, and these critiques helped Marxist theory mature.

The article takes four targets in turn: Proudhonism (together with Grün's \"true socialism\"), Bakuninism, Dühringism and dogmatism in late nineteenth-century Germany. Each section links Engels's critique to a stage in the consolidation of Marxism, from the First International to the Hague Congress of 1872 and the later defence of historical materialism.

Zhang and Zhou report that Engels rejected Proudhon's reformism and his scheme of buying up France with workers' savings, which they say showed the necessity of violent revolution. Against Bakunin, Engels held that abolishing capital, not the state, must come first, and that telling workers to abandon politics pushes them towards priests or bourgeois republicans. Against Dühring, he set out Marxism's three components: philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. Against dogmatists who reduced Marx to economic determinism, he held that the economy decides only \"in the last instance\" and that ideology has relative independence.

The authors conclude that Engels, who played \"second fiddle\" while Marx lived, took up Marx's unfinished work after his death. They hold that tracing his critiques helps consolidate Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, and they call this the best way to commemorate him. Read the original if you want a brief, Party-oriented overview of Engels's polemics and how they are presented today.
quoteEn: Systematically reviewing Engels's critique of non-Marxist currents of thought matters for consolidating Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, and it is also the best way for us to commemorate the great revolutionary teacher Engels.
quoteZh: 系统梳理恩格斯对非马克思主义思潮的批判，对巩固马克思主义在意识形态领域的指导地位具有重要意义，也是我们对伟大革命导师恩格斯的最好纪念。

t: A scientific understanding of Engels's view of authority
zh: 科学理解与把握恩格斯权威观
paras: Li Houdong asks what Engels's writings on authority offer for upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee in the present period. The commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2024, argues that Engels's view of authority gives direct theoretical grounds for upholding that authority as China moves to build a modern socialist country in all respects.

The piece draws mainly on Engels's Anti-Dühring and On Authority, and links them to the 14th Five-Year Plan and the 2035 long-range objectives. It is organised in three parts: why Central Committee authority is the basic guarantee of modernization, why the leader's core status is the key, and why institutional and rule-of-law authority is the foundation.

Li reads Engels as treating authority as an objective necessity that accompanies social development, citing his examples of cotton mills and railways and his critique of anarchist rejection of all authority. In Li's account, Engels's stress on a core and leader means that upholding Central Committee authority includes upholding the core position of the leader, here identified as Xi Jinping. Li adds that authority now carries non-coercive meanings such as democracy, consultation and participation, and must combine political, institutional and rule-of-law authority.

Li concludes that Party organisations should put political development first, unite around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, and turn the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds into political commitment. Li also calls for improving the legal system centred on the Constitution, so that rule-of-law authority is embedded in political authority. Read the original if you want a short example of how Engels's On Authority is used in current Party-building discourse.
quoteEn: The authority of the leading core is the main vehicle and form of expression of a party's inherent authority.
quoteZh: 领导核心的权威是政党内生权威的主要载体和表现形式。

glossary.explanation: A formulation, associated with Xi Jinping, calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

A Party requirement, formulated in 2018, to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
A Party formulation calling for political awareness, awareness of the big picture, of the leadership core, and of keeping in alignment with the Central Committee.

t: Three important documents in "Engels on China" and their theoretical value
zh: “恩格斯论中国”的三篇重要文献及其理论价值
paras: Wang Donghong, in a short commentary first published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2024, asks what Engels actually wrote about China. The author notes that existing compilations of Marx and Engels on China are selections rather than complete collections, yet research relies heavily on them. Wang counts at least 80 works by Engels touching on China between 1839 and 1894 and presents three texts absent from the 2015 edition of Marx and Engels on China and, the author says, not yet studied.

The article takes the texts in turn: the 1839 journalistic piece Letters from the Wuppertal, with related early writings on religion; the dictionary entry Burma (1858), written for The New American Cyclopaedia; and the 1892 translation-and-commentary A Newly Discovered Case of Group Marriage.

Wang argues that the first group shows Engels's interest in China from the age of eighteen, earlier than the 1845 speech usually cited, with Chinese writing and religion serving as markers of a distinct civilisation. The Burma entry, in the author's reading, gives detailed information on China–Burma geography, trade and cultural differences, and reflects Engels's careful, scientific method despite the entry's brevity; Wang cites his letters to Marx complaining about the labour it cost. The 1892 text uses the expression "China-ised" in an anthropological sense, which Wang suggests may offer a pointer for tracing the concept of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

Wang concludes that these texts enrich the study of Engels's life, his ideas and his relationship with Marx, and that the groundwork of "Marx and Engels on China" requires a full inventory of sources. Read the original if you work on Marx and Engels's writings on China, source compilation, or the genealogy of the term "Sinicisation" in Marxism.
quoteEn: To carry out foundational and innovative research on "Marx and Engels on China", one should first clarify the inventory of the documents.
quoteZh: 开展对“马恩论中国”的基础性与创新性研究，应厘清文献“家底”。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions. The article links the older term "Sinicisation" to Engels's 1892 usage.

t: On Engels's "three greats"
zh: 论恩格斯的“三个伟大”
paras: Marking the 200th anniversary of Engels's birth, this newspaper commentary (China Social Sciences Today, 18 August 2024) proposes three headings for understanding him: a great life, a great character and great contributions. Wang Yonghe argues that together they show why Engels deserves to be remembered, studied and revered alongside Marx.

The piece is organised under those three headings. It first sketches Engels's life from his birth in 1820 to his death in London in 1895. It then turns to his friendship with Marx, and finally lists his theoretical contributions, drawing throughout on Lenin's assessments and on a few other commentators.

On life, Wang stresses that Engels came from a bourgeois family yet took the revolutionary road, and that his work in Manchester led to The Condition of the Working Class in England (1845). On character, Wang points to the 40-year friendship, his financial support for Marx and his remark that he played "second violin". The contributions are set out in five points. Engels co-founded Marxism with Marx. He edited volumes two and three of Capital after Marx's death. He systematised Marxism, including the dialectics of nature and the name "scientific socialism". He made pioneering contributions in philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. He also defended Marxism against dogmatic readings and economic determinism.

Wang concludes that Engels's lifelong struggle for proletarian and human emancipation, his selfless help to Marx and his modesty are all worth remembering and learning from. Read the original if you want a brief, officially oriented overview of how Chinese commentary frames Engels's life and legacy for his bicentenary.
quoteEn: Engels's life was a life of exploring and founding scientific theory for the emancipation of the proletariat and humanity, a life of unceasing struggle to transform the old world and build a new one, and a life devoted entirely to seeking and defending truth.
quoteZh: 恩格斯的一生，是为无产阶级和人类解放探索创立科学理论的一生，是为改造旧世界建立新世界战斗不止的一生，是为追求真理捍卫真理奉献所有的一生。
keywords: Condition of the Working Class in England

t: Rethinking the Marxist view of progress
zh: 重新认识马克思主义进步观
paras: Zhao Song, in a short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (11 May 2024), takes up Western readings that label Marx a "progressivist". The author argues that the Marxist view of progress is neither an eschatological theory of the "end of history" nor a linear theory of progress. Both readings, Zhao holds, misread it by ignoring that it is built on real human beings.

The piece first sets out the two Western claims: Francis Fukuyama's view that Marx, like Hegel, posited a final goal of history, and the reading of Sean Sayers and others that Marx's account is a linear sequence of ever higher stages. It then answers each in turn, drawing on Marx's own texts and on Fredric Jameson.

On the end of history, Zhao concedes that images such as the "association of free individuals" and the "realm of freedom" suggest a goal. The author denies that this amounts to historical teleology: for Marx, history has no preset purpose, and the only purposes are those of acting human beings. Communism therefore opens a new history rather than closing history, a point Zhao supports with Jameson's formulation of the end of "prehistory". On linearity, Zhao argues that Marx's late study of "Eastern society" and his reply to Mikhailovsky rejected a universal path for all nations, and that Marxism sees history as spiral. Linear progress also implies a supra-historical subject such as spirit or self-consciousness, which Marx criticised in Hegel. In Zhao's reading, history moves through the contradiction between the productive forces and the relations of production, driven by human practice, which unites diversity with general laws.

Zhao concludes that equating Marxism with the "end of history" or linear progress betrays its human-centred approach. A correct understanding, the author says, must start from the irreplaceable position of real people in historical progress. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language rebuttal of Fukuyama-style and linear readings of Marx's theory of progress.
quoteEn: On the basis of human practical activity, the Marxist view of progress dialectically unites the diversity of historical development with its universal laws, and so correctly depicts the process of historical progress, which differs in essence from the linear view of progress.
quoteZh: 马克思主义进步观在人类实践活动的基础上，辩证统一了人类历史发展的多样性与普遍规律，从而正确地描绘出人类历史进步的过程，这与线性进步观有着本质区别。

t: The dual logic of Marx's theory of social progress
zh: 马克思社会进步理论的双重逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 11 May 2024
paras: This short commentary asks how Marx's theory of social progress differs from the Enlightenment philosophy of history from which it emerged. Zhang argues that the theory rests on a dual logic. The first is the 'material relations of life' as the source of historical motion. The second is the understanding of social progress as a 'natural history'. Both are said to be unified in human material production, that is, practice.

The article first sets Marx against Kant and Hegel. Zhang says that for them history is the movement of an a priori consciousness, whether a hidden plan of nature or the self-realisation of 'absolute spirit'. It then turns to the shared premises that Marx kept: the idea of progress, humanity's capacity to advance society by perfecting itself, and the defence of human subjectivity through humanism. Finally it examines Marx's remark in Capital that the development of the economic formation of society is a natural-historical process.

In Zhang's reading, Marx replaces 'reason' with 'practice' as the measure of history. Enlightenment thinkers, the author says, leave history split between empirical reality and transcendental reason and turn it into a footnote to reason. Marx instead locates a constant element in the material relations of life, the totality of production relations that form an economic structure. The contradictory movement of productive forces and relations of production is what makes a science of history possible and drives progress. The 'natural history' logic then has two sides. Society shares the materiality of nature, so its laws operate independently of human will. Humans also transform nature into a 'humanised nature', treating nature as an 'inorganic body' and society as an 'organic body' in which lawfulness and purposiveness coincide. Human initiative can therefore speed progress, even to the point of a 'Caudine Forks'-style leap, but it cannot create matter itself.

Zhang concludes that Marx's theory forms a rigorously logical system. It moves historical study from philosophy of history to a science of history and gives the fullest account of the laws of social progress. Progress is presented as the 'deduction' of the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, unfolding in empirical time and space. Read the original if you want a concise, introductory statement of how Chinese scholarship distinguishes Marx's historical materialism from Kantian and Hegelian philosophy of history.
quoteEn: For Marx, social progress is a tortuous process that must pass through various complex factors.
quoteZh: 在马克思这里，社会进步是一个需要经历各种复杂因素的曲折过程
keywords: productive forces and relations of production

t: The value orientation of further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 进一步全面深化改革的价值取向
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Chen Jinlong asks what value orientation should guide the further comprehensive deepening of reform. The answer is that a people-centred approach, which the author calls the Party's value stance, governs the policy-making, planning and practice of reform and so has an overarching significance for it. Chen reads the Plenum's Decision on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization as applying this principle throughout.

The commentary is organised in three parts, each tied to the Decision and to statements by Xi Jinping. The first deals with respecting the principal position of the people and their creativity. The second deals with planning and advancing reform from the standpoint of the people's interests. The third deals with the people's judgement as the final test of reform results. A short conclusion draws these together.

In the first part, Chen presents the people as the main force of reform: their support is needed because reform now touches deep-seated contradictions and entrenched interests. The Decision's reference to "the people's new expectations" among the "three confrontations" is read as a sign that reform responds to popular demands. The second part argues that the people's interests are concrete, and that the Decision picks entry points in distribution, employment, social security, healthcare and public services. Chen adds that Chinese modernization, which the author describes as the greatest interest of all the people, is the ultimate aim of reform. The third part says reform should be judged by how far people's interests are met, and that the people are the most authoritative evaluators. Their assessment, Chen contends, marks a starting point for the next stage of reform.

Chen concludes that a people-centred orientation helps secure the direction of reform, mobilise support, build consensus and gather strength for Chinese modernization. The author adds that putting this orientation into practice depends on upholding the Party's overall leadership throughout the whole process of reform, so that the Party remains its strong leadership core. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how the 2024 reform Decision is framed in terms of the people-centred principle.
quoteEn: The people's interests are not empty or abstract, but concrete and real.
quoteZh: 人民利益不是空泛、抽象的，而是具体、现实的。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization. It stresses a huge population, common prosperity and material and cultural-ethical advancement, among other features.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Xi Jinping-era Party discourse. It holds that development and reform should rest on, serve and be judged by the people.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōng quánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A Party meeting held in July 2024 that adopted the Decision on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization.
The principle that the Communist Party leads all fields of work and all stages of policy implementation.

t: How to tell the story of Chinese modernization well in the digital age
zh: 数字时代如何讲好中国式现代化故事
paras: Zhang Honglu, in a short commentary for Guangming Daily (3 September 2024), asks how digital technology can be used to tell the story of Chinese modernization to international audiences. Starting from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its call to rebuild the international communication landscape, the author argues that telling this story well shapes China's national image, raises its international discourse power and strengthens the influence of Chinese culture.

The piece holds that big data, cloud computing and artificial intelligence have transformed the media ecosystem, and that communication is becoming mobile, social and visual. It then sets out four practical directions: new narrative methods, a communication matrix, differentiated targeting of audiences, and better feedback mechanisms.

Zhang calls for stepping outside Western narrative frameworks and using Chinese discourse and Chinese narratives, with interactive, visual, multimodal and AI-generated storytelling, including short web dramas. The author proposes a matrix of many voices, among them foreign bloggers, experts and virtual "digital humans", together with integrated all-media channels. Big-data audience profiles and algorithmic distribution would tailor content to different groups. Real-time monitoring, a communication-power index and sentiment analysis would measure effects and adjust strategy.

Zhang concludes that digital tools can make the story more attractive, more coordinated, more approachable and more widely spread, and so raise the effectiveness of international communication. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary translates the Third Plenum's external-communication goals into concrete digital-media practices.
quoteEn: We need to make great efforts to step proactively outside the Western narrative framework and tell the story of Chinese modernization well with Chinese discourse and Chinese narratives.
quoteZh: 我们需要下大力气主动跳出西方叙事框架，用中国话语和中国叙事讲好中国式现代化故事。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted by the Communist Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The official term for China's external messaging and media outreach to foreign audiences, aimed at improving its image and discourse power abroad.
An official concept of integrating traditional and new media across all channels and formats into one communication system.

t: Three important dimensions of building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 建设中华民族现代文明的三个重要维度
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2024, takes up Xi Jinping's call to build a "modern civilization of the Chinese nation", presented as part of the new cultural mission set out at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development. Chu and Cui argue that the task is an inherent requirement of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and of Chinese modernization, and that it rests on three dimensions.

The piece opens by situating the concept in Xi Jinping's cultural thought and then proceeds in three numbered sections. Each section takes one dimension: the Two Integrations, the practice of Chinese modernization, and mutual learning among civilizations. Each is developed with extensive quotation from Xi Jinping and from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

In the first dimension, the authors hold that the Marxist "soul" and the "root" of fine traditional Chinese culture must both be kept. They describe the first integration, with China's concrete realities, as aimed at solving practical problems, and the second, with traditional culture, as aimed at cultural fusion and strengthening the subjectivity of Chinese culture. The two form an organic whole. In the second dimension, they argue that the new civilization must draw on and serve Chinese modernization: it must rely on the practice led by the people, whom the authors call its creators, and in turn supply spiritual support, national identity and what they term discursive advantage. In the third, they stress openness and inclusiveness, rejecting "clash of civilizations" and civilizational superiority, and call for cultural confidence and active outreach through telling China's story well.

The authors conclude that building this civilization requires combining Marxism with China's realities and culture, grounding itself in practice, and deepening exchange with other civilizations, so as to give people spiritual richness alongside material wealth. They also present it as a contribution of Chinese wisdom and solutions to human civilizational progress. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the official line links the Two Integrations, Chinese modernization and civilizational exchange in the project of a modern Chinese civilization.
quoteEn: Building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation is an inevitable requirement for advancing Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 建设中华民族现代文明，是推进中国式现代化的必然要求

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 as part of a new cultural mission, alongside promoting cultural prosperity and building a strong cultural nation. It is presented as a civilization combining Chinese tradition, Marxism and modernity.
Official formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to Party theory in 2021–2023.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models. It was elaborated especially from the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term national goal in Party discourse, associated with the Chinese Dream and with restoring China's strength and standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
The official stance of confidence in China's own cultural traditions, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, promoted by Xi Jinping as a basis for the Four-sphere Confidence.

The body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture and ideology, formally presented in October 2023 as an important component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

t: Advancing human civilisation through exchanges and mutual learning
zh: 在交流互鉴中推动人类文明进步
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 5 February 2024, takes as its starting point Xi Jinping's congratulatory letter to the World Chinese Studies Conference (Shanghai Forum). Wang Bo reads the letter's three claims as a guide for understanding history and reality, China and the world: trace history to understand the present world, follow cultural roots to recognise present-day China, and practise mutual learning among civilisations to achieve common progress.

The piece is organised in three sections, one for each claim. The first deals with the dialectic of history and reality, the second with China's cultural foundations and how to cultivate them, and the third with the attitude toward other civilisations and its practical implications.

In the first section, Wang argues that the unity of logic and history is the methodological basis of Marxist philosophy, citing Marx and Engels's use of world-historical material. Against the backdrop of what the article calls great changes unseen in a century, it calls for historical thinking in assessing the world economy, international politics and ecological protection. The second section holds that the continuity of Chinese civilisation means China can only be understood through its history. It treats fine traditional Chinese culture as a basis for building a modern Chinese civilisation, and proposes family, school and social education to transmit it. The third section claims that the inclusiveness and peacefulness of Chinese civilisation mean China pursues exchange without cultural hegemony and does not impose its values or political system on others. Wang adds that civilisations should seek "harmony in diversity", not copy one another's development paths, and treat each other as co-agents of progress.

Wang concludes that, given what the article describes as growing deficits in peace, development, security and governance, correct handling of civilisational differences is a precondition for international cooperation. Mutual learning, in this view, helps turn the Global Civilization Initiative from an idea into action. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese official commentary links Xi Jinping's statements on civilisation to Marxist historical method and cultural policy.
quoteEn: Different civilisations can progress together through exchanges and mutual learning, which helps turn the Global Civilization Initiative from an idea into concrete action.
quoteZh: 不同文明能够在交流互鉴中共同进步，有利于推动全球文明倡议从思想理念成为实际行动。

glossary.explanation: A proposal put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 that promotes respect for the diversity of civilisations, common human values, cultural heritage and international cultural exchange.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse since around 2017–2018 to describe a period of shifting global power, technology and governance.

glossary.literal: modern civilisation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A term used in Chinese official discourse, notably by Xi Jinping in 2023, for a new form of civilisation said to be built on fine traditional culture, Marxism and contemporary practice.

t: Understanding Mao Zedong's idea of seeking truth from facts from multiple dimensions
zh: 多维度认识毛泽东同志的实事求是思想
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 28 February 2024, asks how Mao Zedong's idea of "seeking truth from facts" (shishi qiushi) can be understood and put to use today. Peng treats it as the fundamental viewpoint of Marxism and as the Party's basic ideological, working and leadership method. The article argues that Mao and the Chinese communists distilled Marxist world outlook and methodology into this phrase in Chinese idiom, drawing on revolutionary practice. Examining it from several angles, Peng says, helps the Party use it as an effective intellectual weapon.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's remark at the symposium marking the 130th anniversary of Mao's birth (2023). Xi named seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence as the three basic aspects of the "living soul" of Mao Zedong Thought. Peng then takes five "views" in turn: the mass view of history, the view of the subject, the view of contradiction, the view of development and the systems view. Each section cites episodes from Mao's career and ends with a requirement for carrying out the Party's ideological line now.

Peng's core move is to read each phase of Mao's revolutionary practice as an application of a Marxist principle. Mao's stress on serving the people grounds the mass view of history. His investigation reports, such as the Hunan peasant report and the Xunwu and Xingguo surveys, and his maxim "no investigation, no right to speak", illustrate the view of contradiction. His shifting united-front policies across the revolutionary stages illustrate the view of development. On the view of the subject, Peng points to Mao's critique of Wang Ming's dogmatism and his rural-encirclement road, which rested on China's own conditions. For the systems view, Peng cites On Protracted War and the planning of the three great campaigns of the civil war.

Peng concludes that each view carries a present-day demand. These are to put the people first, to be self-confident and self-reliant while avoiding both rigid closure and uncritical copying of foreign models, and to stay problem-oriented. They also include upholding fundamental Marxist principles while innovating and breaking with dogmatism and empiricism, and planning forward-looking, holistic work. The author ties this to Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact example of how current Party commentary organises Mao's methodology into themes for contemporary governance.
quoteEn: Doing investigation and research well is the precondition for upholding seeking truth from facts.
quoteZh: 做好调查研究是坚持实事求是的前提条件

glossary.explanation: A classical Chinese phrase that Mao Zedong adopted in the 1930s and 1940s to describe the Party's ideological line of basing policy on actual conditions. It was revived as a central slogan after 1978.
A method of leadership associated with Mao, summed up as "from the masses, to the masses": gathering the people's views, systematising them into policy, and testing them in practice.
The official term for China's path of development, set out by Xi Jinping and the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, stressed since 2012, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: A systematic grasp of the rich connotations of the modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 系统把握中华民族现代文明的丰富内涵
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 1 April 2024, asks how to understand the modern civilization of the Chinese nation, the new task of building which has been set out by Xi Jinping. Wang Guang argues that it is the modern form of Chinese civilization and the new form of human civilization created by Chinese modernization. In Wang's account it must be grasped through dialectical thinking.

The article is organised around three pairs of relations: the blending of tradition and modernity, the unity of critique and construction, and the meeting of national character and worldwide significance. Each section draws mainly on statements by Xi Jinping, with additional citations from Marx and Engels on colonialism and civilization.

On tradition, Wang holds that modernity does not mean abandoning the past: a modernity that discards tradition lacks a foundation. The author cites the five salient features of Chinese civilization and presents Marxism as the soul of the new civilization, with the blending achieved through the Two Integrations, above all integrating Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. On critique, Wang describes Western capitalist civilization as built on slavery, colonialism, plunder and war behind a façade of civilization, while Chinese modernization is said to reject this logic of capital and put the people first. On the global dimension, Wang rejects civilizational superiority and calls for exchange and mutual learning among civilizations.

Wang concludes that the modern civilization of the Chinese nation expresses cultural agency and cultural confidence, and that it belongs to the world as well as to China. The author presents it as embodying the ideal of harmony among all nations and a world of great harmony, and as confirming that the path chosen by socialist China is correct. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames this concept for a general readership.
quoteEn: A modernity that discards tradition lacks a solid foundation; a tradition that rejects modernity has no bright future.
quoteZh: 丢弃传统的现代，缺乏厚重的依托；拒绝现代的传统，没有光明的未来。

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for the task of building a modern form of Chinese civilization alongside Chinese modernization. Official texts present it as combining Chinese tradition, Marxism and openness to the world.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
Official formula for integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second, added in 2021–2023).
A term in Xi Jinping's recent cultural discourse for the Chinese nation's self-awareness and independence in developing its own culture.
Official phrase describing Chinese modernization as creating a new type of civilization that is said to differ from the Western capitalist model.

keywords: modern civilization of the Chinese nation

t: Several theoretical issues that need attention in developing new quality productive forces
zh: 发展新质生产力需要重视的几个理论问题
paras: Following Xi Jinping's remarks of 31 January 2024 that high-quality development needs a new theory of productive forces, Zeng Zheng asks which macro-level theoretical questions must be understood when developing new quality productive forces. The article, a commentary first carried in Guangming Daily on 2 April 2024, argues that beyond micro-level questions of technology, industry and markets, the topic needs to be seen through historical laws, technological trends and the adaptation of relations of production.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first examines the historical conditions and practical basis for new quality productive forces. The second deals with the gradual and repetitive character of innovation and with competition between technological routes. The third addresses the mutual adaptation of productive forces and relations of production.

On the first point, Zeng holds that scientific revolutions lead to industrial revolutions only under suitable economic conditions and social systems, citing a gap of about a century in the first industrial revolution. The author describes a fourth industrial revolution under way, with major countries launching national strategies, and lists China's advantages (talent, market scale, a full industrial chain, and numerical-control and digital R&D tool rates of 55.3% and 74.7%) alongside shortfalls in top talent, factor-market rules and digitalisation. On the second, Zeng uses breech-loading guns and electric vehicles to show that technologies advance in spirals, and contrasts national routes in new energy vehicles, artificial intelligence and 'green power plus computing power'. On the third, Zeng says new productive forces produce new relations such as the sharing economy and platform organisations, but also constraints such as data monopolies and widening income gaps.

Zeng proposes using the new whole-nation system to pick technological tracks and concentrate on core technologies, letting the market play the decisive role in allocating resources while avoiding duplicated construction across localities, and expanding international cooperation to avoid standards gaps. In the sphere of production relations, the author calls for promoting the digital economy and strengthening regulation together, preventing digital capital and platform data monopolies from over-appropriating surplus labour. Read the original if you want a short, official-line example of how Chinese commentators connect new quality productive forces to the classical thesis on productive forces and relations of production.
quoteEn: The development of new quality productive forces determines the emergence of new relations of production, and these relations in turn act back on new quality productive forces; factors that do not suit their further development should be adjusted quickly so as to promote their sustainable development.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的发展决定了新型生产关系的出现，这种关系又反作用于新质生产力的发展，对于其中不适应新质生产力进一步发展的因素要尽快调整，以促进新质生产力的可持续发展。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023–24 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, presented as supporting high-quality development.
The official goal of the Chinese economy since the late 2010s, emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources nationally to achieve key scientific and technological breakthroughs.

t: Accelerating the construction of Chinese discourse and Chinese narrative systems
zh: 加快构建中国话语和中国叙事体系
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 1 March 2024, Tang Aijun asks how China can build a discourse and narrative system that matches its comprehensive national strength and international standing. Tang argues that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation must be accompanied by cultural revival and greater appeal of its discourse. On this view, building Chinese discourse and narrative reflects the Party's strategy of raising national cultural soft power and occupying the international moral high ground. It requires new concepts, categories and formulations that connect China with the world.

The piece is a short commentary guided by Xi Jinping's thought on culture and organised in three parts. The first concerns holding to a Chinese cultural standpoint and rejecting the abstract opposition between tradition and modernity. The second concerns breaking Western discourse hegemony while establishing a Chinese discourse system, above all on modernization. The third concerns combining a firm Chinese standpoint with a global outlook, through agenda-setting, signature concepts and national image.

Tang contends that treating tradition as backward and modernity as progress leads to the view that modernization requires negating tradition. Rejecting this opens the way to drawing on China's fine traditional culture, whose spiritual markers should be distilled with three qualities: distinctiveness, contemporary relevance and universal significance. Tang then argues that Chinese scholarship has long been in an apprenticeship to Western theory, and that Western narratives equate modernization with Westernization and cast China as a backward 'other'. Success in practice does not turn automatically into success in discourse, so Tang calls for a Chinese modernization discourse and a plural narrative of modernization. This would present Chinese modernization as sharing common features of modernization while offering a new option for developing countries. Tang also holds that China should move from 'China's story' to 'the world's story'. Concepts such as a community with a shared future for mankind, the Belt and Road Initiative and the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives are cited as examples that have gained international recognition.

Tang concludes that China should set global agendas on governance, development, security and civilisational exchange. It should also present its views on peace, development, global governance, the correct approach to justice and interests, and civilisation. Tang says this would build an image of China as credible, lovable and respectable: a peace builder, a contributor to development and a reliable friend of developing countries. Read the original if you want a concise statement, from within the official discourse, of how Chinese commentators link cultural confidence, critique of Western narratives and international communication.
quoteEn: In building Chinese discourse and a Chinese narrative system, one urgent intellectual task is to break free of Western theory, Western discourse and Western narrative, and to put forward a genuine "self-assertion".
quoteZh: 构建中国话语和中国叙事体系，一项紧迫的思想任务就是摆脱西方理论、西方话语、西方叙事，提出真正的“自我主张”。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, popularised since 2012, of restoring China's national strength, prosperity and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, calling for shared interests and joint global governance.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
The body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture and ideology, formally presented as a distinct component of Party theory in 2023.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The significance of the "Second Integration" seen through the meaning of emancipating the mind
zh: 从思想解放的内涵看“第二个结合”的重大意义
paras: This commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in June 2024, takes up Xi Jinping's description of the "Second Integration" (combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture) as "another emancipation of the mind". Yang Hongyuan argues that, by clarifying what emancipating the mind involves, one can see why the Second Integration matters and why it creates better conditions for resolving the long-running dispute over "ancient and modern, Chinese and Western".

Yang builds the article around three elements that, in the author's account, make up emancipating the mind: being guided by correct theory, criticising dogmatism and subjective prejudice, and studying new circumstances to solve new problems. Each element is used as a lens on the Second Integration. The text draws on Deng Xiaoping's definition of the term, on Xi's remarks, and on the Party's earlier episodes of ideological renewal, from the Yan'an rectification to the debate on the criterion of truth.

On the first element, Yang reads the Chinese word "tong" (with) in the formulation as showing that Marxism keeps the leading, guiding position, and holds that only Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times can ensure the right direction. The second element carries the most polemical weight. Yang rejects views that the Second Integration is already contained in the First, or that it elevates traditional culture too much. Yang also rejects the claim that traditional culture has replaced Marxism as the core of modern Chinese civilisation, and cultural revivalism that would "Confucianise" or "Daoify" Marxism. In Yang's reading, the move from the First to the Second Integration is a shift from spontaneous to self-aware grasp of the relation between Marxism and tradition. It also links Chinese civilisation with the socialist path and fully emancipates the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation.

On the third element, Yang says the Second Integration answers the central task of building a modern socialist country and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. It gives the Chinese path deeper historical roots and offers developing countries a model, according to the author. Yang calls for continuing to develop traditional culture, localising foreign culture, and producing achievements that join past and present, China and the West. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party theorists frame the Second Integration against both dogmatist and traditionalist readings.
quoteEn: The move from the "First Integration" to the "Second Integration" is not only a grasp of the relationship between the basic principles of Marxism and China's fine traditional culture, achieving a fundamental advance from the "in-itself" and "spontaneous" to the "for-itself" and "self-aware";
quoteZh: 从“第一个结合”到“第二个结合”，不仅是对马克思主义基本原理与中华优秀传统文化之间关系的把握，实现了由“自在”“自发”到“自为”“自觉”的根本性进步；

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture, put forward in 2021–2023. It is paired with the First Integration, which combines Marxism with China's concrete realities.
A Party slogan for breaking free of rigid thinking in order to deal with new conditions, closely associated with Deng Xiaoping and the late-1970s reform period.

glossary.en: dispute over "ancient and modern, Chinese and Western"
glossary.literal: the contest of ancient and modern, China and the West
glossary.explanation: A long-standing debate since the late Qing about how China should relate its inherited culture to modernity and to Western learning.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, associated especially with Xi Jinping's leadership.

t: Advancing Chinese modernization through building a country strong in quality
zh: 以质量强国建设推进中国式现代化
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 3 April 2024, asks how the drive to build China into a country strong in quality (质量强国) can advance Chinese modernization. Liu takes the Outline for Building a Country Strong in Quality, issued by the Central Committee and State Council in February 2023, as the basic guide. The author argues that quality-focused development lays the foundation for Chinese modernization, and that five practical paths are needed to deliver it.

The article has three parts. The first explains why quality building underpins Chinese modernization. The second describes the new situation and tasks, setting China's advantages against domestic and international challenges. The third sets out five practical paths: innovation and new quality productive forces, modernized quality governance, regionally coordinated quality development, quality improvements that benefit the people, and a green, low-carbon orientation.

Liu's core claim is that quality is both a livelihood issue and a development issue, so high-quality development, which the author calls an essential requirement of Chinese modernization, depends on it. The author sees China's advantages in the socialist market economy and an ultra-large market, whose varied demand encourages quality innovation. The challenges listed include population ageing, a supply system that lags behind consumer demand, uneven regional quality, an industrial chain still in the middle and low end of the international division of labour, and the tight timetable for carbon peaking and carbon neutrality. The paths respond to these: basic research "from 0 to 1" and the commercialization of results "from 1 to N"; stronger laws, digital supervision and shared governance by firms, industry, society and government; joint regional brands; quality grading in food, medicine, elderly care and education; and unified green product standards and carbon-reduction measurement.

Liu concludes that quality building should run through every stage of Chinese modernization, and that these five measures, planned together, can turn quality gains into material strength, better livelihoods and harmony between humans and nature. The piece is a policy-oriented commentary in official language rather than a scholarly study. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-state discourse links quality policy, high-quality development and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Quality is both a livelihood issue and a development issue; it bears on the people's immediate interests and on the overall picture of economic and social development.
quoteZh: 质量问题既是民生问题又是发展问题，关系人民群众切身利益，关乎经济社会发展全局。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A national goal of raising product, service and engineering quality and industrial competitiveness. It was elaborated in the 2023 Outline for Building a Country Strong in Quality.
The official development goal since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over raw growth rates.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries.
China's declared climate goals: carbon emissions to peak before 2030 and net-zero to be reached by 2060. Often abbreviated as the "dual carbon" goals.

t: Grasping the true meaning of the "common values of all humanity"
zh: 深刻把握“全人类共同价值”的思想真谛
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2024, Xu Yanling takes up the concept of the "common values of all humanity", which the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) linked to building a community with a shared future for mankind. Xu presents the concept as a Chinese proposal, and as an original contribution of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, offered in response to what the article calls changes unseen in a century. The thesis is that one should understand what the values are, why they should be promoted and how.

The commentary is organised in three parts, each tied to a formula of \"knowing\": knowing the meaning, knowing the reasoning, and putting it into practice. The first part defines the six values named by Xi: peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom. The second gives three reasons for promoting them. The third sets out three routes for doing so.

In the first part, Xu groups the six values into three pairs: peace and development as a common cause, fairness and justice as a common ideal, and democracy and freedom as a common pursuit. Xu reads fairness as equality among states large and small, and justice as upholding the UN-centred international system together with a \"correct view of justice and interests\". Democracy has no single model: the article holds that only democracy suited to a country's conditions is real and effective, and it extends the term to the democratisation of international relations. The second part argues that the values accord with the trend of world history, answer the \"deficits\" in peace, development, security and governance, and give a value foundation for the community with a shared future for mankind.

On how to promote the values, Xu calls for three things. The first is deeper theoretical elaboration, including a systematic theory covering their background, content, features, discourse and paths. The second is better international communication: unobstructed economic globalisation, use of the Belt and Road Initiative, and coordinated mainstream media, scholarly and popular channels, with audiences segmented. The third is reform of global governance: opposing unilateralism, protectionism and hegemonism, and raising the representation of emerging and developing countries. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Chinese commentary defines and justifies this concept and what practical steps it proposes.
quoteEn: There is no single, universally applicable democracy; only democracy suited to a country's own national conditions is real, workable and effective democracy.
quoteZh: 没有定于一尊、放之四海而皆准的民主，适合本国国情的民主，才是真实的、管用的、有效的民主。

glossary.explanation: A formulation promoted by Xi Jinping since 2015, listing peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom as values said to be shared across civilisations. Official texts present it as an alternative to the idea of "universal values" defined by the West.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's guiding concept for China's foreign policy and global governance proposals, in use since around 2012–2013.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
The management of transnational problems and international rules through institutions such as the UN. Chinese official discourse calls for reforming it to give developing countries more voice.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Understanding and grasping the theme of further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 深刻理解和把握进一步全面深化改革的主题
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 August 2024
paras: Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), this commentary asks why further deepening reform comprehensively must be organised around Chinese modernization. Wang takes the Plenum's Decision as the starting point. The article argues that this theme is a successful experience and strategic choice of the Party's leadership of reform and opening up, and that it rests on historical, theoretical, practical, developmental and reform logics.

The piece is built in three numbered steps. It first sets out what modernization is and how it has unfolded worldwide. It then traces how Chinese modernization has advanced through reform and opening up, from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Finally it lists seven areas on which further reform should focus.

Wang defines modernization as a historical process in which advances in productive forces transform modes of production and ways of life. The author identifies three waves, the steam, electrical and information-technology revolutions. Countries that became developed, in this account, built relations of production suited to the productive forces of their time, while others stagnated or fell into the "middle-income trap", and developing countries that simply copied the Western model failed. From this Wang concludes that technological and industrial revolution is the basic driver of modernization, and that institutional and cultural renewal secures it. China's own record is presented as proof that reform and opening up is the means by which modernization advances. The seven focal areas are a high-standard socialist market economy, whole-process people's democracy, a strong socialist culture, better living standards, a beautiful China, a higher-level safe China, and the Party's leadership and capacity to govern over the long term.

Wang concludes that opening a new chapter of Chinese modernization still depends on reform. It must proceed from China's conditions while following the general laws of modernization, so that relations of production and productive forces, and the superstructure and the economic base, fit each other better. The author compares Chinese modernization to a ship, with reform and innovation as the engine, rule of law and social security as stabilisers, and Party leadership as the anchor. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the Plenum's reform agenda is linked to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: If Chinese modernization is likened to a ship forging ahead through wind and waves, then reform, opening up and innovation are its engine, the rule of law and social security are its stabilisers, and Party leadership is its anchor.
quoteZh: 如果把中国式现代化比作一艘正在乘风破浪、奋力前行的航船，那么，改革开放和创新就是发动机，法治和社会保障就是稳定器，党的领导就是“定海神针”。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched at the end of 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The official term for China's democratic model, which the Party presents as covering every stage of political life, not only elections.
A concept from development economics describing countries whose growth stalls after reaching middle-income level.

t: Opening a new path of emancipating the mind through the "Two Integrations"
zh: 以“两个结合”开辟思想解放的新路径
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today on 20 August 2024, asks how ideological emancipation can support the decision to "further deepen reform comprehensively" taken at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Wang Zhiwei argues that the Two Integrations, the Party's theoretical innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, supply the guiding thought for this emancipation and give it a scientific, non-arbitrary direction.

The article opens by presenting thought as the precursor of action and of social change, citing Marx on the "lightning of thought" and Xi Jinping on advanced values and emancipated thinking as sources of social vitality. It then sets out three tasks: showing that the Two Integrations are the ideological precursor of deeper reform, deepening understanding of reform through the first integration, and strengthening intellectual initiative through the second.

Wang holds that the Two Integrations give reform a scientific worldview and methodology, loosen the hold of traditional habits of thought, and root reform in cultural confidence. Through the first integration, Marxism combined with China's concrete reality, Wang draws on Engels's view that socialist society is one of constant change to argue that reform is necessary and long-term, "always in progress and never completed". Drawing on Marx's account of the basic contradiction of society and Engels's account of the interaction of base and superstructure, Wang also argues that reform is arduous and complex. Through the second integration, Marxism combined with fine traditional Chinese culture, the author sees culture as an internal force that builds intellectual initiative. Wang cites sayings such as "when things reach an extreme they change" and "benefit the people by what benefits them" as ideas that support reform and its people-centred governance.

Wang concludes that the second integration "opens up space for innovation" and secures cultural confidence, which the author links to the Plenum's goal of building a strong socialist culture. The article calls for consolidating cultural subjectivity and strengthening the inheritance and renewal of culture, so that the right path, scientific theory, effective institutions and advanced culture develop together as a spiritual support for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-affiliated scholars link the Two Integrations to the reform agenda set at the 2024 Third Plenum.
quoteEn: The second integration stresses the relationship between theoretical innovation and culture, and focuses on culture's internal driving role in social development.
quoteZh: “第二个结合”强调的是理论创新与文化关系问题，关注的是文化对社会发展的内在推动作用。

glossary.explanation: Formula associated with Xi Jinping: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first integration) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second). It is presented as the core method of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official phrase for the Party's project of developing Marxism in line with Chinese conditions and contemporary developments. The phrase "of our times" was added in the 2020s.
The theme of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (July 2024), which set out a reform programme to 2029 and beyond.
Official term for the Party's path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
Official term for confidence in China's own cultural traditions and socialist culture. It is part of the Four-sphere Confidence.

t: Chinese modernization will open broad prospects through reform and opening up
st: Understanding the major significance of the Third Plenum of the 20th Party Central Committee
zh: 中国式现代化必将在改革开放中开辟广阔前景
zhSub: 深入领会党的二十届三中全会的重大意义
paras: Writing after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Li Yi offers a study-and-interpretation commentary on why the plenum matters. The article argues that advancing Chinese modernization requires further comprehensively deepening reform, and that such reform must in turn be focused on Chinese modernization; the two are presented as closely linked and internally unified. The plenum's Decision is described as the continuation of the reform agenda begun at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and as a new chapter for the new era.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first treats further reform as a practical necessity for realising the blueprint of the 20th Party Congress (2022), looking at domestic problems, the international environment and the need for unity. The second presents the Decision as an act of historical initiative to improve socialist institutions and modernize state governance. The third reviews the achievements since 2012 and sets out the Decision's tasks as a mobilisation order and a roadmap.

Li's core reasoning is that reform is the means by which the Party has repeatedly overcome obstacles, and that it remains so. Domestically, the author lists uneven and inadequate development, an incomplete market system, a large but not strong industrial base, dependence on foreign core technologies, and urban–rural and income gaps. Internationally, Li points to accelerating global change and escalating external pressure, requiring institutions that can prevent and defuse risks. Institution-building is treated as a dynamic process that must stay on the socialism with Chinese characteristics path, avoiding both a closed, rigid road and one that changes banners. Li then outlines priority areas: economic reform led by the Two Unwaverings, the market economy and new quality productive forces; integrated reform of education, science and talent; democracy, law, culture, livelihood and ecology; the balance of development and security; and Party leadership over reform.

Li concludes that the Decision's more than 300 measures should be carried out so as to complete its reform tasks by 2029 and to build a high-standard socialist market economy and basically realise modernization by 2035. The author expresses confidence that Chinese modernization will produce new and greater achievements. The text works as an authoritative-line exposition of the plenum's priorities, with strong emphasis on Party leadership. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned overview of how the Third Plenum's Decision was framed and justified in Party-theoretical media in 2024.
quoteEn: Advancing Chinese modernization requires further comprehensively deepening reform, and further comprehensively deepening reform must focus on Chinese modernization; the two are closely linked and internally unified.
quoteZh: 推进中国式现代化必须进一步全面深化改革，进一步全面深化改革必须聚焦中国式现代化，二者紧密联系、内在统一。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernity, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.pinyin: jìn yí bù quánmiàn shēnhuà gǎigé
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the reform programme adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in 2024. It builds on the 'comprehensively deepening reform' agenda launched in 2013.
The official principle of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, characterised as high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality.

t: Understanding the scientific meaning and practical requirements of "We Must Put the People First"
zh: 深刻理解“必须坚持人民至上”的科学内涵和实践要求
paras: Wang Ming and Qing Yulin write in response to Xi Jinping's article "We Must Put the People First", published in Qiushi on 1 April 2024. The commentary, which first appeared in China Social Sciences Today on 25 June 2024, argues that the principle expresses the Party's unchanged ideals, nature, purpose and founding mission. The authors hold that understanding it matters for reading the "two overall situations" and for sustaining strategic resolve in advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first identifies the Marxist philosophical content of the principle. The second sets out the political logic of the Communist Party's long-term governance. The third lists four practical requirements for building a modern socialist country through Chinese modernization.

On philosophy, the authors find three dialectical unities in the principle. These are subject and object (the people as both the driving force of history and the beneficiary of development), theory and practice, and the historical and the contemporary. For the third, they trace the idea from Mao Zedong's "serve the people", through Deng Xiaoping's mass line, Jiang Zemin's Three Represents and Hu Jintao's Scientific Outlook on Development, to Xi's formulations. On political logic, they argue that the principle reflects a grasp of three kinds of law: the laws of social development, the traditional Chinese idea of the people as the root of the state, and the laws of socialist modernization. In their account, the Party combines the Marxist view of the people with this traditional thought, and its policies win broad support because they improve livelihoods and share results fairly.

The four practical requirements are these: Party members and officials should firmly hold to a political stance rooted in the people and accept their supervision; whole-process people's democracy should be developed; popular wisdom and energy should be gathered through united struggle, including developing new quality productive forces and high-quality development to achieve common prosperity; and the people should be treated as the examiners of the Party's work. On the last point, the authors cite Xi's view that the Party's performance can be judged only by the people, and they call for officials to treat the people's concerns as questions they must answer. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-affiliated scholars present the people-first principle as continuous with earlier leaders' theory and with Chinese tradition.
quoteEn: "Putting the people first" means respecting the people's position as the subject of history and uniting the struggle for lofty ideals with the pursuit of benefits for the broadest masses of the people.
quoteZh: “必须坚持人民至上”就是尊重人民历史主体地位，把为崇高理想奋斗与为最广大人民谋利益统一起来

glossary.en: We Must Put the People First
glossary.explanation: The title of an article by Xi Jinping in Qiushi (1 April 2024). It restates the Party's claim that the people's interests rank above all else, and is listed as one of the principles to be upheld in the new era.
The official term for China's development path, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
An official concept of Xi Jinping's era. It holds that democracy covers every stage of governance (election, consultation, decision-making, management and supervision), not only voting.
A concept promoted from 2023–24 that stresses innovation-driven, technology-intensive growth as the basis of high-quality development.
An official goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics: prosperity shared by all, rather than by a few, and narrowing of gaps in income and development.
Jiang Zemin's theory introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority of the people.
Hu Jintao's guiding concept from the early 2000s, centred on people-oriented, comprehensive and sustainable development.

t: Improving institutions and mechanisms for developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions
zh: 健全因地制宜发展新质生产力体制机制
paras: Taking up the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to improve the institutions and mechanisms for developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions, Yin argues that deepening reform must produce relations of production better suited to these forces. The commentary, published in the Guangming Daily, presents this as the way to secure high-quality development.

The piece has two parts. The first explains why local adaptation is required, drawing on basic Marxist political economy. The second sets out three areas where institutions and mechanisms need strengthening: comprehensive innovation, the allocation of production factors, and the modern industrial system.

Yin reasons that new quality productive forces arise from technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of factors and industrial upgrading. Regions differ in innovation capacity, resource endowment and industrial base, so their paths must differ rather than follow one model.
