Because relations of production tend to lag behind productive forces, the author says the state can adjust them, across production, exchange, distribution and consumption, in line with a high-standard socialist market economy.

Yin calls for a new-type whole-nation system for innovation, reform of talent evaluation and of industry–university–research cooperation, and reform of the allocation of land, labour, capital, technology and data. The market should play the decisive role while government guides factors towards promising fields and supervises factor markets. Regions should build up the new before dismantling the old, upgrade traditional industries, guide emerging industries away from bubbles and invest in future industries. Read the original if you want a concise official-style account of how local adaptation is linked to the Marxist theory of productive forces and relations of production.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions is the result of the dialectical movement of productive forces and relations of production.
quoteZh: 因地制宜发展新质生产力，是生产力与生产关系辩证运动规律的作用结果。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading, in place of reliance on traditional growth models.
An official goal since 2017 that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation in economic growth rather than speed or scale alone.
An official term for mobilising state and societal resources in a coordinated way to achieve major scientific and technological goals, combining government planning with market mechanisms.
An official term for an industrial structure that combines upgraded traditional industries, emerging strategic industries and future industries.

t: Understanding the philosophical grounds of the people-centred approach
zh: 深刻领会以人民为中心的哲学理据
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, Lu Yanqin takes up the principle of putting the people first, listed among the six principles of the Third Plenum decision on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. The author argues that it needs to be understood philosophically, as a value stance. In Lu's account it answers the basic Marxist question of "for whom and relying on whom".

The short piece is organised around three logics: the generation of a value relationship, the manifestation of the value subject, and the verification of values in practice. It draws on the history of the philosophical concepts of subject and object, and on Marx's three historical stages of human development.

Lu holds that the people-centred approach treats people as both end and means, with development aimed at people and achieved through them, so that purpose-value and instrumental value are unified. Using Marx's stages (dependence on persons, dependence on things, free individuality), Lu says people become true subjects only in social relations, and that capitalism alienates and reifies them. Socialism, in this reading, supplies the material base and institutions for the all-round development of individuals. In practice, Lu points to the people's creativity in culture and to an ecological ethic expressed in phrases such as "protecting nature is protecting humanity".

Lu concludes that the approach corrects both the neglect of people and the neglect of things, escapes the logic of capital, and runs through high-quality development and Chinese modernization. Studying it is said to deepen understanding of the essence of socialism and to surpass the "reified" and "abstract" person of Western civilization. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-theory writing grounds the people-centred principle in Marxist value theory.
quoteEn: Putting the people first means integrating people into a unified whole of value: development aims at human development and is achieved by relying on people. The two cannot be separated or merged, but blend into, promote and generate each other.
quoteZh: 以人民为中心就是将人融入价值统一体中，以人的发展为目的、发展依靠人来实现的价值意蕴，不能将二者拆分或合一，二者互融互促、相互生成。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official economic goal since about 2017. It stresses quality, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Xi Jinping-era Party theory. It holds that development should be for the people, rely on the people and have its fruits shared by the people.

t: Accelerating the building of a high-standard socialist market economy
zh: 加快构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 23 August 2024, asks why a high-standard socialist market economy matters and how to build it. Li Yuju argues that, as the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) put it, such a system is an important guarantee of Chinese modernization, and that its construction must be accelerated.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's statement that markets deciding resource allocation is the general law of a market economy. It then traces reform from the 14th Party Congress (1992) to the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), reviews achievements since 2013, and sets out remaining problems and tasks.

Li credits the 2013 formula that the market should play the decisive role in allocating resources, with a better-functioning government, with guiding later reform. Since then, the author says, reforms have improved basic market institutions, implemented the new development philosophy, strengthened macroeconomic governance and institutionalised security in areas such as food and energy. Li then notes that an incomplete market system, underdeveloped markets and an unsettled government–market relationship still constrain high-quality development.

Li concludes that the 2035 target of fully establishing the system requires markets that are both lively and well regulated. The tasks listed are the Two Unwaverings, a unified national market, better factor-market rules, and stronger basic institutions such as property rights, information disclosure and market access. Read the original if you want a brief, official-register summary of how the 2024 Third Plenum framed market-economy reform.
quoteEn: Accelerating the building of a high-standard socialist market economy requires giving fuller play to market mechanisms and creating a fairer, more dynamic market environment, so that resource allocation is maximally beneficial and efficient, with markets that are both "lively" and "well regulated".
quoteZh: 加快构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制，必须更好发挥市场机制作用，创造更加公平、更有活力的市场环境，实现资源配置效益最大化和效率最优化，既“放得活”又“管得住”

glossary.explanation: Official Party concept for China's own path to modernization, developed prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Official formula: unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector, and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
Xi-era framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
Official goal of shifting from speed-focused growth to growth emphasising quality, efficiency and sustainability.

t: The new form of human civilization sublates the paradox of capital's civilization
zh: 人类文明新形态扬弃资本文明悖论
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (23 May 2023), Zhao Ruize asks why the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) calls for regulating and guiding the healthy development of capital by law. The answer offered is that capital has a great civilizing role, but if left to grow wildly and expand without order it brings disastrous consequences. Zhao argues that the new form of human civilization distinguishes capital's dual character, as a relation of production and as a factor of production. It uses the positive side and avoids the negative, and in doing so sublates the paradox of capital's civilization.

The commentary has four sections. The first sets out how capitalist civilization arose through capital's civilizing role, and the second the paradox that role contains. The third places the new form of human civilization in Marx's account of historical stages, and the fourth lists three ways in which it can be enriched and developed.

Drawing on Marx, Zhao holds that capital's civilizing role lies in the rapid growth of productive forces and the universalization of social exchange, which opened the way to world history. Yet capital's aim is self-valorization, so its drive to expand keeps hitting the external limits of nature and society. In Zhao's account this triggers ecological and social crises and, at the level of the world system, domination of peripheral regions. Zhao reads Marx's three social forms in the Grundrisse as pointing to communism, which inherits capitalism's civilizational achievements while overcoming its alienation. On this view the new form is a transitional socialist civilization, "in progress" rather than complete, in which two kinds of production relations coexist.

Zhao draws three implications. First, capital can be "harnessed" by giving it "traffic lights": green for its productive-factor role, red for its valorizing role as a production relation. The ultimate aim is to "eliminate capital" within a higher set of production relations. Second, the new form coordinates five dimensions (material, political, spiritual, social and ecological), in contrast to what Zhao calls capitalism's one-dimensional civilization. Third, it respects civilizational diversity and promotes a community with a shared future for mankind, showing that capitalist modernization is not the only road. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese Marxist commentary links Marx's theory of capital to official claims about Chinese modernization and the regulation of capital.
quoteEn: The process of sublating the paradox of capital's civilization is the process of continually creating conditions for communism.
quoteZh: 扬弃资本文明悖论的过程，就是不断为共产主义创造条件的过程。

glossary.en: the new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A formulation in official discourse, prominent since Xi Jinping's 2021 speech on the Party's centenary. It presents Chinese modernization as creating a civilization distinct from the capitalist model.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's foreign policy and global governance discourse, stressing cooperation and common interests among states.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. It is presented as an alternative to Western models.

t: Upholding rule-based governance of the Party: the code behind "China's governance"
zh: 坚持依规治党:“中国之治”的密码
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2023, after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Wang Jianqin asks why governing the Party according to its rules has become what the author calls the distinctive governance code of "China's governance". The thesis is that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), rule-based Party governance, backed by intra-Party regulations and a system for the Party's self-reform, has become the political guarantee for the Party's governing capacity and for national governance.

The article has three parts. The first traces the Party's tradition of "building the Party through discipline" from the First Congress programme, the 1922 constitution and the Jinggangshan period to Mao Zedong's "four subordinations" and the Party constitutions of later congresses. The second examines the conceptual shift to "institutional governance of the Party" and rule-based Party governance in Xi Jinping's statements. The third links these to the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and to Chinese modernization.

Wang argues that Marxist parties are distinguished by strict discipline, which Lenin treated as a condition for overthrowing private ownership. Through democratic centralism, discipline takes on both a "Party" and a "legal" character, and over time discipline rules have turned into formal intra-Party regulations. The author presents rule-based governance as a change in the Party's ideas, thinking and methods, which combines the tradition of strict governance with the rule of law. It was written into the Party constitution in 2017, and Xi's "ten adherences" at the Second National Conference on Intra-Party Regulations are described as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Wang says the Party's governance moved from "lax, loose and soft" to "strict, tight and hard", and holds that the Party's leading role under the constitution makes its position in governance different from that of Western and other ruling parties.

Wang concludes that only by keeping strictness as the keynote, and by strengthening the authority and enforcement of intra-Party regulations, can the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party reach a stage of high-quality development. The author holds that the Party's self-reform is the "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and fall, and that Chinese modernization depends on this political guarantee. Wang claims this offers Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to party governance and legal civilisation worldwide. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party discipline, intra-Party regulations and the rule of law are linked in current Chinese Party-building discourse.
quoteEn: Only when rule-based Party governance takes root in the hearts of Party members can the rule of law take root in the hearts of the people.
quoteZh: 依规治党深入党心，依法治国才能深入民心。

glossary.literal: governing the Party according to regulations
glossary.explanation: The principle that the Party is governed through intra-Party regulations as well as state law. It was written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress (2017).
Formal rules issued by Party bodies to govern Party organisations and members, ranked below the Party constitution. They are treated as a system parallel to state law.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official slogan for the Party-building and anti-corruption drive launched after 2012, covering ideology, organisation, conduct, discipline and institutions.
Official term for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself. It is presented as the "second answer" to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, which the 20th Party Congress (2022) made the central task of the Party.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, which combines discussion with binding unity of action under higher bodies.
An official phrase, used here for the Party-building system, for development that stresses quality rather than speed.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The value implications of the "Three Musts"
zh: “三个务必”的价值意蕴
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in May 2023, asks what value the "Three Musts" carry. The report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) told all Party members they must keep to the original aspiration and founding mission, stay modest, prudent and hard-working, and dare and know how to fight. Yi Kaifa argues that these requirements do four things: guide Party building, support long-term rule, shape the Party's image and supply spiritual strength for national rejuvenation.

The article has four sections, one for each function. It takes the three requirements in turn within each section. It draws on Xi Jinping's remarks, on the Party's history and on a definition of party image as public perception.

On Party building, Yi links each "must" to a field of work. The first concerns ideological building, the second work style and discipline, and the third political building and governing capacity. On long-term rule, Yi attributes the Party's historical selection by the people to the three qualities. The Party still faces the "four tests" and "four dangers", so Yi calls for keeping the clarity and resolve of the "exam" in aims, work style and capability. On image, Yi describes party image as a public impression formed from everything people can see and feel of a party. In Yi's reading, the Three Musts embody a caring and responsible image, an advanced and striving one, and a capable and effective one.

Yi concludes that the Three Musts also supply the spiritual strength needed for national rejuvenation. They would do this by reinforcing belief, restraining complacency and strengthening the will to struggle, among Party members and the public alike. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party commentary presents the Three Musts as requirements for Party building and the Party's image.
quoteEn: The "Three Musts" requirements concern not only Party building and the Party's long-term rule, but also the shaping of the Party's image.
quoteZh: “三个务必”要求不仅关乎党的建设和党的长期执政，还关乎着党的形象塑造。

glossary.explanation: Three requirements set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). All Party members must keep to the original aspiration and founding mission, stay modest, prudent and hard-working, and dare and know how to fight.

glossary.literal: never forget the original heart, keep the mission firmly in mind
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan, prominent from 2017 onwards, calling on members to remember why the Party was founded: to seek the people's wellbeing and national rejuvenation.

The tests the Party says it faces in governing: those of governing, of reform and opening up, of the market economy and of the external environment. They are paired with the "four dangers" of lack of drive, inadequate ability, detachment from the people, and corruption.
The goal of restoring China's strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. It is the central aim of Party discourse under Xi Jinping.

t: The ideological content and practical paths of building a community with a shared future for mankind
zh: 构建人类命运共同体的思想内涵与实践路径
paras: Sun Xihui asks what ideas underpin the building of a community with a shared future for mankind and how it is to be pursued in practice. Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2023, Sun argues that the concept, together with the related global initiatives, rests on Marxist principles and a set of universal values, and that it can be advanced through specific diplomatic and cooperative channels. The article presents the concept as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization and a key part of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought.

The piece is organised in three parts: the moral and value foundations, the core content, and the basic paths. It draws on Xi Jinping's speeches at the United Nations and the Boao Forum, the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), and the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative and the Global Civilization Initiative. It also cites figures on the Belt and Road Initiative.

Sun first claims that the concept inherits and develops Marx's idea of the community, charting a route from an "abstract" or "illusory" community to a "true community". The author treats the common values of all humanity (peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom) as its moral basis, with peace and development the first prerequisites and fairness and justice the core pursuit. Second, Sun sets out its core content through the Global Development Initiative, which is people-centred, innovation-driven and attentive to developing countries, and the Global Security Initiative, which stresses respect for sovereignty, opposes bloc confrontation and unilateral sanctions, and links traditional and non-traditional security. Third, Sun identifies the paths: a new type of international relations, including relations among major powers, a correct approach to righteousness and interests, partnership without alliance and genuine multilateralism; communities of shared future with particular countries and regions as intermediate steps; and the Belt and Road Initiative. For the last, the author cites more than 200 cooperation documents signed by 151 countries and 32 international organisations.

Sun concludes that great practice produces great thought and that great thought guides practice. The author calls for deeper study and implementation of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought, so as to open new prospects for major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics and create a favourable external environment for the second centenary goal and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned overview of how Chinese scholars link the community with a shared future to Marxist theory, the global initiatives and the Belt and Road.
quoteEn: Building country-specific and regional communities of shared future is a necessary step on the ladder towards building a community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteZh: 打造国别区域命运共同体是构建人类命运共同体的必要阶梯。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humanity
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013. It envisages states bound by common interests and cooperating on peace, development and global governance.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The Party presents it as distinct from Western models.
Proposed by Xi Jinping at the UN General Assembly in 2021. It centres on development, people-centred policy and support for the UN 2030 Agenda.
Proposed by Xi Jinping at the Boao Forum in 2022. It advocates a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security concept, and a concept paper followed in February 2023.
A 2023 initiative by Xi Jinping promoting respect for the diversity of civilizations and dialogue and mutual learning among them.
An international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, tied to the centenary goals of 2021 and 2049.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Key focal points for steadily advancing common prosperity for all the people
zh: 扎实推进全体人民共同富裕的着力点
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in May 2023, asks where policy should concentrate in order to advance common prosperity. Ye Bing argues that, with a moderately prosperous society now built, the historical stage of steadily promoting common prosperity has arrived. The author treats it as an essential requirement of socialism and a defining feature of Chinese modernization, to be pursued under Party leadership by making the "cake" bigger through high-quality development and dividing it fairly through institutional arrangements.

The piece draws on two Xi Jinping articles in Qiushi (2021 and 2022) and on his phased targets for the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan, 2035 and the middle of the century. It then moves through Party leadership, high-quality development, employment, the regulation of capital, the distribution system, social security, and rural and urban-rural gaps.

Ye holds that Party leadership is the political guarantee and must run through every field, including drawing up an action outline for common prosperity. High-quality development, supported by technological self-reliance, a modern industrial system and a strong real economy, is called the fundamental route. On capital, Ye accepts its role in a socialist market economy but calls for "traffic lights" against disorderly expansion: strengthening state capital in strategic sectors, regulating the platform economy and enforcing anti-monopoly rules. Distribution is to combine primary distribution, redistribution through taxes and transfers, and philanthropy as a third distribution, with labour-based distribution as the mainstay.

Ye further urges wider social security coverage for migrant and flexible workers, and equalised basic public services in rural education and health care, since the heaviest tasks remain in the countryside. The author concludes that common prosperity shows the superiority of socialism with Chinese characteristics and will be achieved along the path of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented summary of the official agenda for common prosperity as framed in 2023.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is common prosperity for all the people, and in promoting it the most arduous and heaviest tasks still lie in the countryside.
quoteZh: 共同富裕是全体人民共同富裕，促进共同富裕，最艰巨最繁重的任务仍然在农村。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing goal of Chinese socialism, given new prominence under Xi Jinping from 2021. It refers to prosperity shared by all, with narrower gaps in income and public services.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out by Xi Jinping and the 20th Party Congress (2022), presented as distinct from Western models.
An official policy goal since 2017 that stresses innovation, efficiency and balance over growth in output alone.
Voluntary distribution of wealth through charity and philanthropy, alongside market-based primary distribution and state redistribution by taxes and transfers.

t: Mutual fit: the deep foundations for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture
zh: 彼此契合:马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合的深厚底蕴
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's remarks at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, this newspaper commentary asks why combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture was possible at all. Zhang Taiyuan's answer is that a combination presupposes mutual fit: although the two have different origins, the author argues that they are highly compatible in values and habits of thought, and this made an organic union possible.

The article is built around a brief introduction and four paired themes, each setting a traditional Chinese idea beside a Marxist one: 'the world belongs to all' and human emancipation; 'unity of heaven and humanity' and materialism; 'the people as the foundation of the state' and the people as makers of history; and the Great Harmony (datong) society and communism. Zhang draws on Mao Zedong, Li Dazhao, Liang Qichao, Qu Qiubai, Ai Siqi and the French sinologist Jacques Gernet, as well as on Xi Jinping and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

Zhang's central claim rests on Xi's phrase that Marxism took root in China because it connected with values the people lived by 'without being aware of it'. The author reads this as an unconscious convergence of thinking that formed the cultural basis for the combination. In the examples, Zhang finds in Chinese tradition a practical, worldly orientation, naturalistic and atheistic strands, a long-standing concern with the people, and an ideal of a society free of exploitation. Early Chinese Marxists such as Li Dazhao and Qu Qiubai are presented as understanding communism through the Great Harmony, and Ai Siqi as seeing 'seeds' of Marxism in Chinese thought.

Zhang concludes that this affinity helps explain why Chinese intellectuals chose Marxism among competing currents after the May Fourth Movement. Citing Xi, the author adds that the combination is mutually enriching: it makes Marxism Chinese and traditional culture modern, and yields a new cultural form for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholarship in 2023 presents the cultural compatibility of Marxism and Chinese tradition, with quotations from early Chinese Marxists.
quoteEn: This 'unconscious convergence' laid the cultural foundation for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture.
quoteZh: 这种“无意识融通”奠定了马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合的文化基础。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as distinct from Western models.
An ideal society described in the Confucian classic Liji, where the world is held in common and all are cared for. Early Chinese Marxists often used it to interpret communism.

glossary.literal: the world is for the public
glossary.explanation: A classical Chinese maxim, associated with the Great Harmony passage, expressing the ideal of a commonly shared world. The article links it to Marxist human emancipation.

glossary.en: the people as the foundation of the state
glossary.explanation: A traditional Chinese political idea, found in the Book of Documents, that the people are the root of the state. Official discourse often cites it as a precedent for people-centred governance.
A strand of Chinese thought holding that humans and nature form a harmonious whole. The article reads it as consistent with Marx's view of humans as part of nature.

t: The threefold logical meaning of abstract labour in Marx's "Paris Manuscripts"
zh: 马克思“巴黎手稿”中抽象劳动的三重逻辑意涵
paras: Most scholarship on Marx's concept of abstract labour concentrates on Capital and its manuscripts. Kou Dongliang asks what the term meant in its first appearance, in the 1844 "Paris Manuscripts". The article argues that Marx did not yet offer a scientific concept there. Instead, within the theory of alienated labour, he implicitly gave abstract labour three connected meanings: separation, inversion and non-objectivity. These opened the "revolution in terminology" that later led to the critique of political economy.

The article is organised around three pairs of logic, one for each meaning: "alienation–freedom", "making a living–human-centred" (谋生—人本) and "idea–sensuousness". It draws on Marx's critique of classical political economy (called "national economy" in the manuscripts) and of Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit and Philosophy of Right. It also uses Feuerbach's anthropology and the Comments on James Mill. Kou notes that Marx had not seen Hegel's Jena texts, where the term abstract labour first arises.

First, abstract labour means separation. Labour is cut off from the means and objects of labour, which become capital. Kou reads this through the "fourfold separation" of alienated labour: from the product, from the activity, from the human species-essence, and from other people. Marx's phrase about reducing "the greatest part of mankind" to abstract labour is read from the standpoint of workers, set against an ideal of free, species-defining labour. Second, abstract labour is inverted labour: a means of subsistence for the worker and of profit for the capitalist. It reduces the worker to a machine and distorts human needs into the need for money. Third, drawing on Feuerbach's sensuousness, Marx judges Hegel's labour to be "abstract spiritual labour", non-objective and merely logical. He counters with labour as sensuous, objective activity.

Kou concludes that the "Paris Manuscripts" follow Feuerbach's anthropological principles and reject the classical labour theory of value. Abstract labour there is therefore an ethical, metaphorical term, at most an idea, and not yet a defined theoretical concept. Yet it sketches an economic-philosophical outline and an \"embryo\" for later work. Only in Capital does Marx define abstract labour scientifically, as a material social function of capitalist production and as a conceptual movement. Kou calls for further study of how the concept was built. Read the original if you study the genesis of Marx's value theory or the relation of the young Marx to Hegel, Feuerbach and classical political economy.
quoteEn: Abstract labour in the "Paris Manuscripts" is better described as a metaphorical "term" in an ethical and moral sense, at most an idea, and not yet a theoretical concept with a clearly defined content and scope.
quoteZh: “巴黎手稿”中的抽象劳动更可谓一个伦理道德意义的隐喻性“术语”，至多是一种观念，尚不是一个具有明确内涵规定和外延指向的理论性概念。

t: Analysing rural land transfer through Marx's theory of ground rent
zh: 马克思地租理论视域下农地流转问题分析
paras: Chai Shu asks how Marx's theory of ground rent can explain the problems of rural land transfer in China, and whether it still applies under the socialist market economy. The article argues that it does. Land ownership and the separation of ownership from use exist in China as well as under capitalism, so ground rent exists too, and the theory can guide reform of land transfer.

The article has three parts. It first summarises Marx's ground rent thinking against the background of English enclosures and the rise of the three classes of landlord, capitalist and wage labourer. It then applies the theory to China's current land transfer, under the system in which collective ownership is kept while contracting and management rights are separated ("three rights separation"). Last, it draws policy conclusions.

On Marx, Chai stresses that ground rent is the economic form through which land ownership is realised and that it is a converted form of surplus value created by agricultural wage labour. The author distinguishes differential rent I and II from absolute rent. Applying this to China, Chai holds that absolute rent and differential rent I belong to the collective as owner, and differential rent II to the contracting households. In practice, the author argues, the "household contracting" system has stressed dispersed farming over unified collective management. This has weakened village collectives, and industrial and commercial capital entering the countryside has deepened the weakness. Chai says capital then dominates pricing, leaves farmers scattered and with little bargaining power, and captures rent that should go to collectives and farmers, which widens the rural wealth gap.

Chai concludes that collective land ownership must be upheld and the collective strengthened. The author proposes that the Party organise farmers through cooperatives led by village Party branches. These would pursue moderate-scale operation, give the collective a voice in setting transfer prices and in distributing rent, and advance common prosperity. Chai also suggests that government set up bodies to assess land transfer prices. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar applies Marx's Capital, Volume III, to current debates on rural land circulation and collective ownership.
quoteEn: Therefore, only by upholding collective land ownership, with the Party organising farmers along the path of Party-branch-led cooperatives and strengthening the collective's standing, can farmers' bargaining power be increased and the problems of unreasonable pricing and rent distribution in land transfer be solved.
quoteZh: 因此，只有坚持集体土地所有制，由党把农民组织起来走党支部领办合作社的道路，强化集体地位，才能增强农民的谈判能力和议价能力，使农村土地流转中的价格、地租分配不合理的问题得以解决。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese policy goal of shared prosperity for all, stressed in Party documents especially since the 2010s. It is used to frame efforts to narrow income and regional gaps.
A rural land reform that separates ownership (collective), contracting rights (households) and management rights (which may be transferred to third parties).
The system introduced from the late 1970s under which collectively owned farmland is contracted out to individual households to farm. It replaced the people's commune system.

t: Should Marx and Engels's critique of religion be divided into a narrow and a broad sense?
zh: 马克思恩格斯宗教批判是否应有狭义、广义之分？
source: Science and Atheism (科学与无神论), 2023 no. 2
paras: The article asks whether the concept of Marx and Engels's "critique of religion" should be understood in two senses. Zhu and Ma observe that Chinese scholarship mostly uses a narrow sense, treating the critique as the early views from the Rheinische Zeitung to the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher period. A second, looser usage simply equates it with Marx and Engels's religious theory as a whole. The authors argue that both senses are legitimate and that distinguishing them is worthwhile.

The piece first sets out the two usages through examples. For the narrow sense it cites Zhao Dunhua, who sees Marx's critique as a sublation of Bauer and Strauss, and Tang Xiaoyan, who extends it to Capital, Volume 1. For the broad sense it cites Tang Xiaofeng and Hu Jian. It then assesses the rationale and purpose of each sense, and ends by considering what the distinction means, including for building Marxist religious studies as a discipline after the 2021 national conference on religious work.

For the narrow sense, Zhu and Ma note that before historical materialism the early Marx and Engels criticised religion itself, exposing its falsity and artificiality, rather than the capitalist economic base behind it. Studying this phase helps separate their views from those of the Young Hegelians. For the broad sense, the authors ask why Marx and Engels criticised religion and why they did so in successive stages (political, economic, cultural, social). Their answer is that the aim was always to sublate human self-alienation and achieve human emancipation, and that criticism of religion alone could not do this. On this reading, later theories of the essence, origin and withering away of religion, and of the workers' party's attitude to religion, still belong to one critique of religion.

The authors conclude that the broad sense is a valid concept that shows continuity and wholeness in Marx and Engels's thinking on religion and illustrates the openness and developmental character of Marxism. Citing Xi Jinping's December 2021 call to strengthen Marxist religious studies, they claim that a continuous, comprehensive theory suits better as a theoretical basis for the discipline than a stage-bound one. Read the original if you work on Marxist theories of religion in China, or on how Chinese scholars frame the foundations of Marxist religious studies.
quoteEn: However many stages Marx and Engels's views on religion have, their ultimate aim is only one: to sublate the self-alienation of religion and to achieve human emancipation.
quoteZh: 马克思恩格斯宗教观不论有多少阶段，二人的最终目的只有一个，即实现对宗教自我异化的扬弃，实现对人的解放。

glossary.explanation: A discipline that Chinese authorities and scholars are seeking to build, studying religion on a Marxist basis. Interest rose after the 2021 national conference on religious work.
A high-level Party and state meeting that sets policy on religion. The 2021 session, in December, included Xi Jinping's call to strengthen the discipline of Marxist religious studies.
The usual Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: to negate something while preserving and surpassing it.

t: Engels's inheritance and development of Marx's thought on culture, and its contemporary value
zh: 恩格斯对马克思文化思想的继承、发展及当代价值
paras: Marx and Engels never gave a formal definition of culture, yet Wang Xiuhan and Hou Yanshe argue that human freedom and all-round development runs through their thought on it. The article asks what Engels inherited from Marx's thought on culture, what he added, and what this means for cultural construction in China today. Its thesis is that Engels fully inherited Marx's narrow sense of culture, extended the broad sense, completed the account through historical materialism, and supplied a theoretical basis for present-day socialist cultural work.

The article has four parts. The first examines the concept of culture, the second Engels's use of historical materialism to supplement Marx, and the third his treatment of culture and freedom and of the class character of culture. The fourth turns to contemporary value, drawing on the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and statements by Xi Jinping. The authors work mainly from Engels's late letters, Anti-Dühring, The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, and The Housing Question.

On the concept, the authors say Marx used culture narrowly for spiritual products such as ideas, art, morality and science, and broadly for stages of social development. Engels followed the narrow sense but separated culture from civilisation. In their reading, culture precedes civilisation, which is a higher stage of cultural development with a positive value orientation, while culture itself is value-neutral. Against charges of 'economic materialism', Engels held that the economic base is decisive only 'in the last instance'. Culture has relative independence and reacts back on the base, and people make their own history. The authors add that Engels treats freedom as both the driving force and the goal of culture, and that different classes have different cultures that also serve as tools in class struggle.

For the present, the authors draw four implications. Cultural construction should put the people first, since people are its subject and its beneficiaries. Party leadership is its fundamental guarantee, because of culture's class character. Material and spiritual civilisation must develop in coordination, which they present as a feature of Chinese modernization. Culture is both a driving force and a goal of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They call for continued Marxist guidance in building a socialist cultural power. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly account of how Engels's texts are used to ground current Party cultural policy.
quoteEn: Engels not only inherited Marx's thought on culture as a whole, but also put forward new views from different angles.
quoteZh: 恩格斯不仅从整体上继承了马克思的文化思想，还从不同的角度提出了新的观点

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, prominently elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as including coordination of material and spiritual civilisation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of restoring China's national strength and standing, central to Party discourse since the 2010s.
An official goal, stated in Party documents, of building China's cultural strength and soft power under socialism.
A principle in Party discourse under Xi Jinping that the people's interests are the highest standard of the Party's work.

t: Re-examining Marx's concept of "sociality"
zh: 重新审视马克思的“社会性”概念
source: Journal of Beijing Institute of Technology (Social Sciences Edition), online first 20 March 2023
paras: Wang Juan asks what Marx actually meant by "sociality" (shehuixing), a term the author says is widely used but rarely defined. Marx never gave it a dedicated treatment, and the article notes that the Chinese edition of the Marx-Engels Collected Works mentions it explicitly only 49 times. Wang argues that, since the surge of Chinese research on Marx's theory of the human being from the 1990s, the concept has habitually been read through "social relations", and that this reading is too shallow.

The article has three parts. The first sets out three common approaches: groupism (including Western communitarianism), a social-relations ontology, and sociological social structuralism (Durkheim, Weber, Simmel, Blau, Parsons). The second returns to Marx's original context, tracing his critique of social contract theory (Hobbes, Locke) and of Hegel's ethical state through the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, On the Jewish Question, the 1844 Manuscripts, The German Ideology and the Communist Manifesto. The third turns to the critique of political economy, taking the three equations of the value-form in Capital, Volume 1.

Wang argues that each common approach falls short. Groupism, in Wang's account, dissolves the individual into the collective and cannot separate humans from social animals. Reading sociality as social relations is "primary" sociality only, and structural sociology reduces it to a model of linkages. For Marx, the argument runs, sociality has two layers: relations between people, and the relation between particular and universal interests. It names real social relations grounded in the unity of the two. Wang reads the value-form analysis as showing how, through the money form and commodity, money and capital fetishism, social relations between people are masked as relations between things and sociality is split apart. Wang also contends that some Western Marxists shifted critique to culture, consumption and everyday life, offering only a "phenomenological" analysis without a critique of political economy.

Wang concludes that Marx's concept only becomes clear through the critique of political economy, which shows that conflicts between private and common interest cannot be resolved while private property exists. Re-examining it is presented as a response to the fragmentation and reification of contemporary society, and as a source of methodological guidance for analysing present social problems. Read the original if you want a systematic reading of Marx's "sociality" against communitarian, sociological and Western Marxist alternatives, with close attention to the value-form analysis in Capital.
quoteEn: Sociality is neither the simplified essence of human social relations nor an external social structure in the sociological sense, but a concept expressing the "organic connection" of the private and public spheres and of individual needs and social interests, that is, genuinely social ties between people.
quoteZh: 社会性不是简单化的人的社会关系本质，也不是社会学意义上外在的社会结构，而是表征私人领域和公共领域、个人需要和社会利益实现“有机联系”的概念，即人与人之间真实的社会性联系。

t: Making the study and implementation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era go deep and take root
zh: 在推动学习贯彻习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想走深走实上下功夫
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2023, no. 9), Liu Xiaoxin comments on the thematic education campaign on studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, launched across the Party in 2023. Liu presents the campaign as a major measure for implementing the 20th Party Congress (2022) and as a route for the Party's self-reform. The article argues that, following Xi Jinping's call to make study 'go deep and take root', Party organisations must ensure that learning is genuinely understood and applied rather than performed as a formality.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first sets out the methods of study: reading original works, grasping the worldview and methodology, and linking knowledge to practice. The second lists four aims of the campaign: forging conviction, increasing wisdom, correcting work styles and promoting practical work. The third turns to investigation and research as a way to solve concrete problems.

Liu's central claim is that study must unite learning, thinking and applying, and knowing, believing and acting. Party members and cadres are told to read prescribed texts, including the Selected Readings of Xi Jinping and the Outline for Studying the Thought, and to master the 'six musts' named in the 20th Congress report: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, a systems approach, and a global vision. Liu invokes the Marxist view that practice is the source and aim of knowledge, and requires that the campaign be judged by whether it solves problems and satisfies the people. On investigation, Liu calls for going to the grassroots with questions, listening also to unwelcome views, and giving equal weight to investigation and analysis.

Liu concludes that the campaign should strengthen ideals and loyalty to the Party, correct formalism and bureaucratism, and turn study into results in high-quality development, common prosperity and the management of risks. The Party's tasks, the article says, include full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, which is described as 'always on the road'. Read the original if you want a sample of how Party-school-style guidance on the 2023 education campaign was framed for cadres, including its reading list and its stated criteria of success.
quoteEn: Study is not rote memorisation, but must be used to solve practical problems.
quoteZh: 学习不是死记硬背，而是要用以解决实际问题。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
A Party-wide study and education drive organised around a set theme. The 2023 campaign focused on studying Xi Jinping Thought and applying it to work.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six principles summarising the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan since 2012 for stricter discipline, anti-corruption work and internal supervision.
A term used by Xi Jinping for the Party's continuous effort to correct its own problems and keep its governing capacity.
A stated goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, stressed in recent years, of broadly shared wealth for all the people.

t: Consciously using Xi Jinping Thought to transform the subjective and objective worlds
zh: 自觉用习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想改造主观世界和客观世界
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2023, Cao Wenze addresses Party members and cadres taking part in the thematic education campaign on studying and implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article's thesis is that cadres must use this body of thought to remould both their own inner world and the external world of practice. Cao describes the thought as contemporary Chinese Marxism, twenty-first-century Marxism, and the essence of Chinese culture and spirit for the present age.

The piece is a hortatory commentary in three parts. The first sets out how the thought should be studied; the second deals with transforming the subjective world; the third with transforming the objective world. Cao draws throughout on Xi Jinping's speeches, the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and a list of recommended texts, including the 2023 edition of the Study Outline.

In the first part, Cao argues that study must be comprehensive, systematic and in-depth, treating the thought as a single complete system. It should be based on reading original works and applying its worldview and methodology, including the Party's stress on people-centred development, systems thinking and a global outlook, and should link theory to practice. In the second part, the subjective world is reshaped by firming up ideals and convictions, strengthening Party spirit and upholding the principle of putting the people first. Cao treats the distinction between public and private interest as the basic measure of Party spirit. In the third part, the objective world is changed through four tasks: conducting investigation and research, improving the seven abilities required of cadres, implementing the 20th Party Congress decisions with a focus on high-quality development, and delivering practical benefits to the public. Cao adds a call for a willingness to struggle and take responsibility.

Cao concludes that cadres should turn learning into stronger conviction, better skills and tangible results in their own posts, so that thought and action are unified. The text is a statement of the official line on the campaign, and it frames the thought as a guide to both self-cultivation and to the tasks of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party publications presented the aims and method of the 2023 thematic education campaign to cadres.
quoteEn: Party members and cadres must consciously use Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to transform the objective world, promote a strong culture of investigation and research, steadily improve their working skills, and make new contributions in their own posts.
quoteZh: 党员、干部必须自觉以习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想改造客观世界，大兴调查研究之风，扎实提高工作本领，立足岗位建新功。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
A Party-wide study and rectification campaign on a set theme. The 2023 campaign focused on studying and implementing Xi Jinping Thought.

An official economic goal that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth. It is described in the 20th Party Congress report as the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
The Party's traditional practice of field investigation, associated with Mao Zedong and promoted in 2023 as a campaign across the Party.
The essential qualities of loyalty, discipline and commitment expected of a Party member, which the Party says must be developed through training.

t: The Chinese form of Marx's thought on labour justice: logic, historical evolution and contemporary orientation
zh: 马克思劳动正义思想的中国样态：逻辑理路、历史演进与现实指向
source: Study and Practice (学习与实践), 2023 no. 4
paras: Shao Xianping and Liu Lu ask how Marx's thought on labour justice (the evaluation of labour activity, labour relations and labour methods) has been taken up in China, and what form it takes today. They argue that Marx resolved the modern question of justice by tracing it back to labour, the human mode of production, and that the realisation of labour justice is the defining feature of socialism. In their account, the Communist Party of China has carried this thought forward through state reconstruction and institutional change, producing a distinctive Chinese form in the new era.

The article, published in Study and Practice in 2023, has three parts. The first reconstructs the logic of Marx's thought as a unity of critique and construction. The second traces its historical evolution in modern China, from the revolution to reform and opening up and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third examines its present orientation under institutional construction, value guidance and cultural incentive.

On Marx, the authors identify three shifts: from formal to substantive justice, from common labour to shared labour, and from labour in thrall to things to the liberation of labour. Drawing on the theory of surplus value, they say Marx exposed the justice of equal exchange in circulation as an illusion, because injustice lies in production and in the separation of labour from ownership. In China, they present three stages: the revolution and workers' movement, which addressed substantive justice; land reform, socialist transformation and the basic distribution system, which institutionalised sharing; and livelihood measures such as labour legislation and employment policy, which laid the basis for liberation. For the new era, they call for institutions that regulate public and private capital, including digital capital, and for putting the people first through employment, distribution and public services. They also call for a culture that respects labour dignity, decent work and the spirit of labour, model workers and craftsmanship.

The authors conclude that Marx's thought has become an endogenous intellectual force in the development of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and that its Sinicisation offers a Chinese form, wisdom and strength in answering contemporary ideas of justice. They urge that the value stance, policy arrangements and practical strategies of labour justice be upheld in building a modern socialist country, so as to promote people's free and all-round development. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how labour justice is linked to common prosperity, capital regulation and the Party's historical record.
quoteEn: Institution-building is the first guardrail for safeguarding labour justice and sublating the logic of capital.
quoteZh: 制度建设是维护劳动正义、扬弃资本逻辑的第一道护栏。

glossary.explanation: A concept the authors attribute to Marx: the evaluation of labour activity, labour relations and labour methods by the standard of justice, centred on who owns and enjoys the products of labour.
A long-standing socialist goal that has been given greater policy prominence under Xi Jinping. It refers to prosperity shared by all, with narrower gaps in income and region.

t: The theory of Chinese modernization as a major innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 中国式现代化理论是马克思主义中国化时代化的重大创新
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Yan Xiaofeng argues that the theory of Chinese modernization is a major theoretical innovation and a significant achievement in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The article, which opens by citing Xi Jinping's remarks at a study seminar on the Congress, presents the theory as an important component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Yan contends that building a modern socialist country and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation require developing this theory further.

The article has three parts. The first explains why opening new horizons for the adaptation of Marxism calls for developing the theory, tracing the Party's history through the New Democratic Revolution, the socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second sets out what the theory contributes. The third discusses its role in guiding the new journey of building a modern socialist country.

Yan's central claim is that Marxism advances by answering major questions of the era, and that modernization is one of them. In the author's account, Western capitalist modernization proved unworkable in China after the Opium War, and no ready-made answers exist for how to avoid its defects while using socialist institutions. The article lists the theory's contributions: modernization is not Westernization and has no single model; Party leadership is its most essential feature; it has distinctive Chinese characteristics (a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical balance, harmony between humanity and nature, peaceful development); and it has stated essential requirements and a strategic layout. Yan describes it as a product of the Two Integrations that rejects capital-centred, polarising, materialistic and expansionist paths.

Yan concludes that the theory must keep answering new questions: external risks, deep-seated domestic contradictions, problems of Party building, and the "questions of modernization" Xi has raised for humanity. The author calls for guidance from Xi Jinping Thought and for enriching the theory on the basis of practical innovation. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how Party theorists in 2023 linked Chinese modernization to the longer project of adapting Marxism to China.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that \"modernization equals Westernization\", widened the paths by which developing countries can modernize, and offered humanity a new option for achieving modernization, which gives it world significance.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，拓展了发展中国家走向现代化的途径，为人类实现现代化提供了新的选择，具有世界意义。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for China's own path of modernization, systematically set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is characterised as socialist, led by the Party and distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to combine Marxism's basic tenets with China's conditions, traditional culture and current era. The 'times' element was added to the older 'Sinification of Marxism' wording.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017 and presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The formula that Marxism's basic principles must be integrated with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It was formalised in Xi Jinping's 2021–2023 statements.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, presented in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal, usually tied to making China a strong modern socialist country by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Accelerating the new development pattern as the strategic fulcrum for promoting high-quality development
zh: 加快构建新发展格局是推动高质量发展的战略基点
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2023, He Zili takes up Xi Jinping's remark to the Jiangsu delegation at the first session of the 14th National People's Congress. Xi said that high-quality development is the first task of building a modern socialist country in all respects, and that accelerating the new development pattern is its strategic fulcrum. He argues that the new development pattern, with the domestic cycle as the mainstay, is both required by and a means of achieving high-quality development.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the new stage of development requires high-quality development. The second sets out how the new development philosophy should guide it, through innovation, coordination, green development, opening up and sharing. The third describes the features of the new development pattern and how each supports high-quality development.

In the first part, He gives three reasons. Extensive growth, driven by larger inputs of labour and other factors, is becoming unsustainable: the demographic dividend is fading, returns to capital are falling and resource constraints are hardening. Popular aspirations have moved from having goods to having good ones. The principal contradiction is now unbalanced and inadequate development, which He traces to extensive methods, low quality and efficiency, and weak momentum. In the third part, He holds that the new pattern supports high-quality development in five ways. It is oriented to self-reliant innovation, including a new whole-nation system for core technologies. It aims to expand domestic demand through investment and consumption. It rests on self-reliance and security of industrial and supply chains. It strengthens the real economy and manufacturing, and guards against finance circulating within itself. It also calls for a higher level of opening up, which He presents as consistent with economic globalisation.

He concludes that high-quality development, led by the new development philosophy and anchored in the new pattern, is the way to meet the people's aspirations and advance common prosperity. He also links higher-level opening to a community with a shared future for mankind. The piece is a policy exposition in the official register. Read the original if you want a compact account of how Chinese economists in 2023 tied the new development pattern to high-quality development.
quoteEn: The essence of unbalanced and inadequate development is extensive development methods, low quality and efficiency of development, and insufficient momentum; to solve it, high-quality development must be achieved.
quoteZh: 发展不平衡不充分问题的实质是发展方式粗放、发展质量和效率不高、发展动力不足，要解决发展不平衡不充分问题，必须实现高质量发展。

glossary.explanation: A strategy announced in 2020 that makes the domestic economic cycle the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. Official texts present it as a response to changes in China's development stage and the external environment.
The official goal of Chinese economic policy since around 2017. It stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed and scale.
The five concepts of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015 as the guiding principles of development policy.
A long-standing socialist goal that Party documents have given renewed emphasis since the early 2020s. It refers to prosperity shared by all, with a narrower income gap.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for international relations based on cooperation and shared interests. It is used in official foreign-policy discourse.
A model of mobilising state, market and institutional resources nationally to achieve breakthroughs in key technologies.

t: The development of Marxist social investigation methodology in the new era
zh: 马克思主义社会调查方法论的新时代发展
paras: Liu Jie and Gao Yang take up a gap they see in work on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times: the methodology of social investigation (diaoyan, survey and investigative research) is scattered through studies of Party history and has not been systematically distilled. Their thesis is that this methodology originates in Marx's turn to real individuals and their way of life. In their account the Chinese Communist Party then extended it to the lives of the masses, and in the new era it is developing along three lines.

The article has four parts. It first traces the origins of the methodology in Marx and Engels's critique of Hegel's philosophy of right and of Feuerbach. It then reviews the Chinese exploration of the method from Li Dazhao and Qu Qiubai through Mao Zedong's investigations to the socialist construction period. The third part, on the new era, draws on the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and Xi Jinping's call for a renewed culture of investigation. A short conclusion follows.

The authors argue that for Marx, knowing society requires starting from living individuals and their mode of life, which led him to take civil society as the empirical object of study. They cite Engels's The Condition of the Working Class in England and Marx's workers' questionnaire as examples. Marx and Engels, they say, divided the masses by class but did not fully explain the masses as practical subjects of investigation. The authors credit the Party with filling this gap: it refined classifications of the masses, treated them as subjects of investigation, and replaced civil society with the everyday life of the people as the object. They also credit it with producing principles such as seeking truth from facts.

For the new era, the authors identify three paths. The first is respecting the people's right to speak, with whole-process people's democracy as the institutional platform. The second is embedding investigation in grassroots democracy, which the authors contrast favourably with capitalist representative systems. The third is improving people's livelihood projects to stimulate the people's own initiative. They conclude that the methodology puts the people at the centre, supplies tools for building a socialist democratic system, and underpins Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese sociology and ethnology scholarly team links Marx's early philosophy to the Party's current investigation and research campaign.
quoteEn: Returning from the abstract world to the world of individual life is the theoretical starting point of the Marxist methodology of social investigation.
quoteZh: 从抽象世界回归个体生命世界，是马克思主义社会调查方法论的理论基点所在。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019, describing Chinese democracy as covering every stage of decision-making and not only elections. Official sources present it as the Party's characterisation of socialist democracy with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's development path, emphasised at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to each historical period.
A principle associated with Mao Zedong and later Deng Xiaoping, requiring that policy be based on investigation of actual conditions and not on dogma.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Letting Marxism show a stronger and more persuasive power of truth on Chinese soil
zh: 让马克思主义在中国大地上展现出更强大更有说服力的真理力量
paras: This commentary, published in 2023, is a study-and-reflection piece on volumes one and two of the Selected Readings from the Works of Xi Jinping. Li Yang argues that adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is a process of seeking, revealing and practising truth. In Li's account, the Selected Readings show the truth-power and practical strength of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and Marxism can show a stronger and more persuasive truth-power in China only if new horizons keep being opened.

The piece has three parts. The first treats the response of Xi and the Party Central Committee to great changes in the times and the situation: development, common prosperity, foreign relations and the banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The second covers the continuing adaptation of Marxism, the creation of Xi's Thought, and the Party's historical experience, including the Two Establishes. The third presents the principle of putting the people first as the distinguishing mark of a Marxist party.

Li argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party has met overlapping global upheaval, the pandemic and serious risks with strategic thinking, a fighting spirit and historical initiative. The new development stage, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern are described as mutually dependent and as the basis of high-quality development, through which common prosperity is to be advanced. Li presents Xi Thought as answering the major questions of the new era, as innovating in Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism, and as opening a new realm of Marxist party-building theory. The Two Establishes are described as the "golden key" to the new era and the core of the Party's historical experience. Putting the people first is presented as both the essence of Marxism and a creative transformation of the traditional Chinese idea that the people are the foundation of the state.

Li concludes that the Selected Readings unite upholding and developing Marxism, and that the Party should keep a spirit of historical initiative and creativity on the new journey. Only repeated, fresh study of the texts, the author says, will let readers absorb the truth-power of contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese academic and Party-affiliated writers present the Selected Readings and the official narrative of Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: Putting the people first is the essential embodiment of Marxism, and also the creative transformation and innovative development, in the new era, of philosophical ideas, humanistic spirit and moral concepts in fine traditional Chinese culture such as "the people are the foundation of the state".
quoteZh: 坚持人民至上是马克思主义的本质体现，也是中华优秀传统文化“民为邦本”等哲学思想、人文精神、道德理念在新时代的创造性转化和创新性发展。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: An official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary circumstances. It is presented as a continuing project of theoretical innovation by the Party.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A formula from the Party's third historical resolution (2021) affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of his Thought.
An official goal of shared wealth for all, promoted as a requirement of socialism and emphasised under Xi Jinping.
The official economic policy orientation since about 2017, stressing quality and efficiency over speed of growth.
The Party's five-part guiding concept for development: innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared.

t: Marx's "circle of friends"
zh: 马克思的“朋友圈”
paras: This short piece, from 2023 (the 205th anniversary of Marx's birth and 140th of his death), introduces a book published by People's Publishing House, Marx's Circle of Friends (《马克思的朋友圈》). Shu presents it as a popular, illustrated account of Marx's relationships, meant to help Party members, cadres and the public grasp the spirit of Marxism. The book's editor-in-chief is Gong Yun, deputy director of the Academy of Marxism at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

The piece describes the book as grounded in authoritative historical record and written in lively language. It sorts Marx's contacts into intellectual partners (Engels, Heine, Wolff, Westphalen, Feuerbach), comrades and students (Liebknecht, Bebel, Kugelmann, Weydemeyer, Dietzgen, Lafargue and others), and theoretical opponents (Proudhon, Bauer, Lassalle, Bakunin). The book contains over 100 images styled as social-media posts.

Most of the piece sketches two friendships. Engels, Marx's "top friend", is called his "second self"; Shu recounts their meeting in Paris in 1844 and their worried letters, and notes Engels's material help to Marx's family. Heine, a poet 21 years older, is said to have learned communism from Marx, whose influence Shu links to Heine's poem Germany. A Winter's Tale. Shu argues that Marx chose friends by shared theory, revolutionary stance and goals rather than personal gain, so that his friendships trace his intellectual development.

Shu concludes that Marx's approach to choosing friends is a lesson for today's Party members and cadres, who should combine warmth ("情") with integrity ("清"). The piece urges readers to hold to truth and ideals and not to judge friendship by utility. Read the original if you want a brief, officially oriented introduction to this popular book and to how Marx's friendships are used in Party education.
quoteEn: Marx's view of choosing friends, which upheld truth and held fast to ideals and did not judge friendship by utility, is worth learning from by every one of us.
quoteZh: 马克思坚持真理、坚守理想的择友观，不以功利论友谊，值得我们每一个人学习借鉴。

t: The evolving logic of Marx and Engels's critique of the city and its contemporary implications
zh: 马克思恩格斯城市批判思想的演进逻辑及其现实启示
paras: Li Xiaoguang and Niu Siqi ask how Marx and Engels's critique of the industrial capitalist city developed into a historical-materialist theory, and what it offers for urban work today. They argue that the critique has original significance for contemporary urban theory and that its method is best grasped by returning to the classic texts and tracing the logic of their evolution.

The article follows the texts in chronological order. It begins with Marx's journalism for the Rheinische Zeitung and the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher and with Engels's early empirical observations in the Wupper valley and England. It then turns to the works of the 1840s, from the 1844 Manuscripts to The German Ideology, The Poverty of Philosophy and the Communist Manifesto. Finally it covers the later period: Capital, 'On the Nationalisation of Land', The Housing Question, Anti-Dühring and The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State.

The authors identify three stages. The starting point is political critique of civil society and empirical observation. Marx's 1842 defence of equal rights for town and country is an early example, and Engels's accounts of industrial pollution and worker poverty are another. The second stage builds a social-historical and urban–rural framework. The German Ideology is called a watershed, introducing 'urban–rural opposition' and tracing it to the division of labour and private property. The Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy describes modern history as the 'urbanisation of the countryside', in contrast with the ancient 'ruralisation of the city'. In the third stage, Capital treats urban–rural separation as both a driver of accumulation and a source of the paradoxes of capitalist modernity. Marx's writing on land nationalisation and Engels's polemics on housing and the division of labour then present urban–rural integration as achievable only through abolishing private ownership, eliminating the old division of labour, balancing industry across the country and highly developed productive forces.

The authors draw three lessons for Chinese modernization in the new era. Urbanisation should be people-centred, meaning public participation, attention to livelihood problems and public satisfaction as the test of urban work. It should also rest on harmony between humans and nature, with ecological red lines and green, intensive development. Finally, it should aim at urban–rural integration and common prosperity, through supporting the countryside with industry and cities, rural revitalisation and new-type urbanisation. Read the original if you want a text-by-text account of how Marx and Engels's views on city and countryside developed, and of how a Chinese scholarly article links them to current urban policy.
quoteEn: Marx and Engels's critique of the capitalist industrial city has original (foundational) significance.
quoteZh: 马克思恩格斯的资本主义工业城市批判思想具有原生性意义

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path of modernization, given prominence at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A policy goal of shared wealth for all, stressed in Party documents especially since the 2010s. It is often linked to narrowing urban–rural and regional gaps.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to modernise agriculture and rural areas and to narrow the urban–rural gap.
An official policy approach to urbanisation, outlined in 2014, that stresses people-centred development, urban–rural coordination and environmental sustainability.
The Marxist idea of overcoming the opposition between town and country, also used in Chinese policy for coordinated urban and rural development.

t: Development and innovation of the fundamental institution of upholding Marxism's guiding role in the ideological field
zh: 坚持马克思主义在意识形态领域指导地位根本制度的发展与创新
source: Studies on the Marxist Theory Discipline (《马克思主义理论学科研究》), 2022 no. 12
paras: Wu Xueqin examines the institution of 'upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological field', which the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) formally named a fundamental institution (根本制度). The article argues that this institution, which Wu says bears on the Party's banner, direction and fate, took shape over a century of Party history and has been developed and given new content in the new era.

The article has three parts.
