The first traces four stages: germination in revolutionary struggle (night schools, peasant training institutes, Communist Youth League, periodicals, the Yan'an rectification), formation and a twisting course after 1949, improvement during reform and opening up, and maturity in the new era. The second sets out the new-era achievements, and the third discusses how the institution is to be put into effect.

In the core argument, Wu draws five lessons from the historical record: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times as the first task; propaganda and education as the core requirement; absorbing outstanding cultural achievements as a resource; a Party-led cultural and educational system as the key instrument; and seizing ideological leadership and discourse power as the guarantee. Wu says the new era has built on these in five respects: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the 'soul', constitutional and Party-charter provisions as the 'four beams and eight pillars', governance of cyberspace, a supporting enforcement system including responsibility for ideological work, and coordination with other fundamental institutions. For implementation Wu proposes five pairings: cultural confidence with institutional confidence, adherence to fundamentals with innovation, systematisation with workability, accountability built into institutions with institutionalised accountability, and outward conformity with inward conviction.

Wu concludes that the institution is a necessary result of China's historical, theoretical and practical logic, and that it works fully only if people internalise it as a way of life. Practical measures include better organisational leadership, management and early-warning mechanisms for ideological work, stronger Party leadership of media and online space, and distinguishing questions of political principle, of understanding and of academic opinion, with scholarly debate bound by propaganda discipline. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-official account of how ideological leadership is being institutionalised in China and which mechanisms are proposed for it.
quoteEn: Only when this fundamental institution is integrated into people's blood and becomes their way of life can it truly play its role and can the timely completion of the cause of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation be ensured.
quoteZh: 只有让这项根本制度融入人们的血脉，变成人们的生活方式，才能真正发挥这项制度的作用，才能确保中华民族伟大复兴事业的如期完成。

glossary.explanation: In Party documents since the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), the top tier of a three-level system of fundamental, basic and important institutions. It is said to have a top-level, all-encompassing and guiding role.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for combining Marxism with China's specific conditions and with contemporary developments. It is a central theme of Party theory.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party constitution.

t: Rallying minds and strength for the new journey
zh: 为奋进新征程凝心聚力
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 9 May 2023, explains why the Party is running a campaign of thematic education on studying and applying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Liu, Wang and Liu take their cue from Xi Jinping's speech at the work conference launching the campaign. They argue that the campaign, aimed chiefly at leading cadres at county and department level and above, is a major step in implementing the 20th Party Congress (2022).

The article is organised around three "necessary requirements" that, in the authors' account, make the campaign significant. The first is unifying the Party's thinking, will and action. The second is spurring Party members to take responsibility and open up new prospects for the cause. The third is advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform.

On the first point, the authors argue that each advance in Party theory must be followed by theoretical arming of the membership. They present Xi's thought as a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, reached through the Two Integrations. Leaders are called the "critical minority" who must set an example, grasp the Two Establishes and carry out the Two Upholds. On the second, they argue that the tasks set by the 20th Party Congress, pursued through Chinese modernization, face uncertain risks, so cadres must turn study into firmer ideals, stronger Party spirit and practical work, guided by the "six musts". On the third, they argue that the campaign addresses problems unique to a large party and the lasting "four tests", "four dangers" and "four impurities". It does so through political health checks, correcting deviations and strengthening the Party's capacity for self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-advancement.

The authors conclude that the campaign should be carried out thoroughly so that the Party stays united, remains the leading core of socialism with Chinese characteristics and never loses its character. The text is an official-style mobilisation piece rather than an analytical study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's press justified the 2023 thematic education campaign and linked it to ideology, governance and Party building.
quoteEn: Carrying out thematic education has strong strategic significance and practical relevance for advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and for leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform.
quoteZh: 开展主题教育，对于深入推进全面从严治党、以党的自我革命引领社会革命，具有很强的战略意义和现实针对性。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The formula of combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is used in official accounts of how Marxism is adapted in China.
A formula from the 2021 Party history resolution affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The official term for China's path to modernisation, set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022 as the means of achieving national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party-building drive since 2012, covering discipline, anti-corruption and ideological education within the Party.
An official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and renew itself. It is presented as the second "revolution" alongside social revolution.

t: Deeply understanding and grasping the "Two Establishes"
zh: 深刻理解和把握“两个确立”
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 April 2023
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in 2023, sets out how the authors think the Party should understand the Two Establishes. Zhang and Xiao point to the amended Party Constitution adopted at the 20th Party Congress (2022), which calls the Two Establishes a major political outcome of the new era. They argue that the formula is a sound historical conclusion and that its decisive significance should be grasped.

The piece has two parts. The first shows that the Two Establishes rest on the Party's century of history and on the practice of the new era. The second sets out three requirements for understanding them: the Two Upholds, theoretical armament, and the link between upholding the core and the guiding ideology.

On history, the authors contend that the Party has endured because it has stressed the Party's self-reform and, at each stage, formed a strong leadership core and openly set its guiding ideology. They trace a line from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which they describe as a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. On practice, they say that the achievements of the past decade show that the Party can lead the people to new victories only with a leader recognised by the people as its core and with this thought as its guide.

The authors call for loyalty to the core and for treating the Two Upholds as the highest political principle. They also call for deeper study and propagation of Xi Jinping Thought, including the Party's thematic education campaign, and for firm political discipline alongside theoretical confidence. They present these steps as ensuring that Chinese modernization advances steadily. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary justifies the Two Establishes through Party history and the achievements of the new era.
quoteEn: In the Party's history, the establishment of its leadership core and guiding ideology has been the product of responding to the needs of historical development and the call of the practice of the times.
quoteZh: 在党的历史上，党的领导核心和指导思想的确立，是回应历史发展的需要和时代实践呼唤的产物。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Party history resolution and the 2022 Party Constitution amendment. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought.

The requirement to uphold the authority of the Party Central Committee and its centralized, unified leadership, and to uphold Xi Jinping's core position. It is presented as the highest political principle for Party members.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party Constitution and presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of combining Marxist principles with Chinese conditions and contemporary developments.
An official concept for the Party's continuing efforts to discipline and renew itself. It is presented as a main reason for its longevity.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress as the way to national rejuvenation.

t: From alienated labour to alienated time: the contemporary transformation of Marx's social critical theory
zh: 从劳动异化到时间异化：马克思社会批判理论的当代转化
source: Gansu Theory Journal (Gansu Lilun Xuekan), 2023 no. 2
paras: The article asks how the concept of alienation, central to Marx's social critical theory, can be carried into a present that differs sharply from Marx's own. Xie and Chen argue that alienation has moved from the sphere of labour to that of time. They hold that Hartmut Rosa's theory of time alienation gives a useful diagnosis of late modern society, but that it needs to be corrected by Marx's critique of capital.

The text has three parts. The first traces Marx's own development from humanist to scientific alienation, through the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, The German Ideology, the 1857–58 manuscripts (the Grundrisse) and the 1861–63 manuscripts. The second turns to the Frankfurt School and to Rosa, a fourth-generation Frankfurt thinker, covering his definition of time alienation, his three dimensions of social acceleration and its driving mechanisms. The third compares the critical paths of Marx and Rosa and ends with remarks on Chinese modernization.

On Marx, the authors argue that the 1844 theory, with its four determinations of alienated labour, still rests on a humanist notion of species-essence and a Hegelian pattern of return. After The German Ideology, they say, alienation is grounded in the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production. Its resolution then lies in communism, not in a restored essence. On Rosa, they report his view that acceleration of technology, of social change and of the pace of life drives alienation from space, things, action, time, self and society. Competition, the cultural promise of a full life and a self-reinforcing acceleration cycle sustain this process. His critique has a normative side, since time norms undermine modernity's promise of reflexivity and autonomy. It also has a functional side, since desynchronization points to the system's eventual breakdown. His remedy is 'resonance' rather than slower living.

The authors judge that Rosa offers a phenomenological analysis that does not reach the deeper cause. In their account, he denies that acceleration follows from capital's drive to valorise itself and reduces it to psychological and cultural factors, and his resonance proposal remains abstract. They call for placing acceleration within the logic of capital, following Marx's critique. For Chinese modernization they draw two implications: expanding public ownership while regulating private capital, and building a sound legal and administrative system. Read the original if you want a Marxist assessment of Rosa's social acceleration theory set against the development of Marx's own concept of alienation.
quoteEn: Rosa does not go on to reveal the deeper pathology of capitalism; he denies that acceleration is an inherent requirement of the logic of capital valorisation, and reduces the problem of social acceleration to the psychological and cultural level.
quoteZh: 罗萨并没有进一步揭示资本主义的深层病因，否认加速是资本增殖逻辑的内在要求，将社会加速问题下降到心理学和文化学层面。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept of China's own path of modernization, prominent in official discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept from Hegel and Feuerbach that Marx used to describe how workers' own products and activity come to confront them as alien powers under capitalism.
Rosa's term for the increasing speed of technology, social change and the pace of life in late modernity. The article treats it as the root of time alienation.
Rosa's term for a responsive, two-way relationship between subject and world, offered as the counter-concept to alienation.

t: Marx's critique of Proudhon's economic philosophy
zh: 马克思对蒲鲁东经济哲学思想的批判
source: Journal of Hunan First Normal University, 2023 no. 1
paras: This article revisits The Poverty of Philosophy (1847), which Marx wrote in French as a reply to Proudhon's The Philosophy of Poverty (1846). Luo and Liu argue that in this polemic Marx used his new worldview, historical materialism, to criticise Proudhon's economic philosophy comprehensively. They hold that the work was not an immediate success against Proudhon's influence among workers, but that it retains lasting value as the first public, scientific statement of historical materialism's core ideas.

The article is organised in three parts followed by a conclusion. The parts take Marx's critique of the foundation of Proudhon's thought (an idealist view of history), of his method (the "serial" dialectic), and of his core theories of value and property, including ground rent. The conclusion places the book in the personal and political history of the two men and links it to the present-day guiding role of Marxism.

On the foundation, the authors report Marx's view that Proudhon treats economic categories as eternal and derives them from abstract thought, with the division of labour as the motor of history. Marx, by contrast, locates the motor in the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, so categories are only historical and transitory. On method, they argue that Proudhon borrowed only the terminology of Hegel's thesis–antithesis–synthesis, dividing each category into a "good" and a "bad" side and hoping to keep one and remove the other. In their account this ends the dialectical movement and produces a "system of economic contradictions" that exists only in thought. On theory, they set Ricardo, who started from real economic relations, against Proudhon's chain of assumptions about constituted value and the equal division of surplus labour. They also cover Marx's argument that property and rent are expressions of changing social relations, so that "rent comes from society, not from the soil".

The authors conclude that the critique of Proudhon's economics and philosophy shifted into a political critique of his petty-bourgeois class position. In their reading, Marx saw Proudhon as an opponent of feudalism but also an obstacle to the communist movement and a defender of small property owners. They add that the book put proletarian revolution at the centre and offered a path to human emancipation. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language account of how Marx's 1847 polemic is read today as a statement of historical materialism, including its treatment of value theory and ground rent.
quoteEn: The lack of a scientific basis in Proudhon's economics and philosophy inevitably led him away from the proletarian standpoint, and Marx's critique of him moved accordingly from the field of economic philosophy to the political field.
quoteZh: 蒲鲁东的经济学和哲学基础不具有科学性，导致他必然偏离无产阶级立场，马克思对蒲鲁东的批判也由经济哲学场域转到政治场域。

t: Understanding in depth why Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times works
zh: 深入理解中国化时代化的马克思主义为什么行
paras: Yang and Wang comment on the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which extended the "three whys" formula with a second "works" (xing) claim: that Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times works. The authors read this as marking both the spatial and the temporal dimension of Party theoretical innovation. They present it as an expression of theoretical confidence and historical consciousness.

The short piece, first printed in the China Social Sciences Today in March 2023, is organised in three parts. It sets out the theoretical character that makes Marxism "work", then the routes by which it does so, then the methodological principles involved. A brief closing section lists where the "works" lies.

On character, the authors attribute four qualities to Marxism: scientific rigour, a people-centred stance, practicality and openness. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is described as twenty-first-century Marxism. On routes, they stress the Two Integrations, of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. On method, they list putting the people first, self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, problem orientation, systematic dialectics and a global outlook tied to a community with a shared future for mankind.

The authors conclude that adapting Marxism has a starting point but no end point. In their account it works because it continues the Marxist tradition, realises the Two Integrations, rests on the worldview and methodology of Xi's thought, and is carried by a Party that believes in, practises and spreads Marxism. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how the official reading of the "works" formula was presented to Chinese readers in 2023.
quoteEn: The adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times has a starting point but no end point.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化时代化只有起点，没有终点。

glossary.explanation: Formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added prominently in Xi Jinping's 2021–2023 statements.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy and civilisational concept of common global interests and cooperation.

t: Accelerationism and its critique from the perspective of historical materialism
zh: 历史唯物主义视域中的加速主义及其批判
paras: Lei Yu takes up accelerationism, a radical Western theoretical current that proposes alternatives to capitalism. The article argues that in opposing the myths of neoliberalism, accelerationism has produced myths of its own and so become a new ideology. It also contends that accelerationism distorts Marx in order to present him as its forerunner. Lei calls for vigilance towards novel discourses and a methodological self-awareness grounded in historical materialism. The text first appeared as a newspaper article in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2023.

The piece has three parts. The first traces accelerationism's history in three stages. The first is the 1970s French thinkers Deleuze, Guattari, Lyotard and Baudrillard, writing after the failure of May 1968. The second is the right-wing accelerationism of Nick Land in the 1990s. The third is the left-wing accelerationism of Nick Srnicek and Alex Williams, whose 2013 manifesto brought the current to wide attention. The second part dissects five myths. The third turns accelerationism into a "model" that can be analysed and assessed.

Lei identifies five myths. In ideology, accelerationism is a product of the Enlightenment and capitalism, leading on the right towards fascism and on the left towards what Lei calls totalitarian socialism, such as Aaron Bastani's "fully automated luxury communism". In historical narrative, it is a "hyperstition" that reverses the order of history. In technology, it is a Promethean cult in which technology becomes destiny. In politics, it is a struggle for hegemonic discourse. In textual reading, it is a one-dimensional reading of Marx that cites the free-trade speech and the "fragment on machines". Lei argues that Marx always viewed capitalism through the contradiction between the forces and relations of production, whereas accelerationism affirms only the productive forces. As a model, its political hopes for an alternative remain unrealised. It grafts Marxism onto Nietzsche, post-structuralism and science fiction. Drawing on Althusser, Lei says its problematic stays inside capitalism and follows reality rather than critically transcending it.

Lei concedes that accelerationism offers some critical insight. It reflects the inherent contradiction of capital valorisation and the powerlessness of the Western left, and it draws attention to global capitalism's challenges to socialist theory and practice in China. Lei concludes that Marxists should stay alert to radical Western currents, strengthen their ability to answer them and deepen their own theoretical self-understanding. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese Marxist assessment of accelerationism, from Land to Srnicek and Williams, and of how Chinese scholars frame its relation to Marx.
quoteEn: In opposing capitalist ideology, accelerationism has itself become a new ideology and so cannot escape the cage of ideology.
quoteZh: 加速主义在反对资本主义意识形态的过程中却使自身成为新的意识形态，从而无法摆脱意识形态的牢笼。

t: Always holding on to the hearts of the people
zh: 始终守住守好人民的心
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2023, reads the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) through Xi Jinping's statement that in winning and defending the country the Party is defending "the hearts of the people". Wang and Fang argue that winning popular support is both the secret of the Party's first century of achievement and the key to future success.

The piece is organised in five steps. It begins with the improvement of living standards over the decade since 2012, then turns to the people-centred stance underlying the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context. It goes on to common prosperity as a mark of Chinese modernization, the Party's measures on livelihoods, and finally the creative power of the people.

The authors cite poverty alleviation and the building of a moderately prosperous society as evidence of improved lives, including nearly 100 million rural people lifted out of poverty and life expectancy rising to 78.2 years. They argue that Marxism took root in China because its defining attribute is its people-oriented character, whereas other currents failed to represent Chinese people's interests. They contrast Chinese modernization, which they describe as aiming at common prosperity of material and cultural life, with Western modernization, which in their account cannot solve widening wealth gaps.

Wang and Fang conclude that the Party should keep improving livelihoods through income distribution, employment, social security and health policies. It should also apply the mass line and combine whole-process people's democracy with full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, which they present as the two answers to the "historical cycle" question. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party commentary presents the 20th Congress report's people-centred themes.
quoteEn: History shows profoundly that any theory divorced from the people is pale and powerless, and any theory that does not benefit the people has no vitality.
quoteZh: 历史深刻表明，一切脱离人民的理论都是苍白无力的，一切不为人民造福的理论都是没有生命力的。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all rather than a few, covering material and cultural life.
Official term, promoted since 2019, for China's democratic model, said to involve people's participation across all stages of governance rather than only at elections.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline and fight corruption within its ranks.

t: Upholding the supremacy of the people as a defining trait of vivid practice in the new era
zh: 坚持人民至上是新时代生动实践的鲜明品格
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today on 3 January 2023, takes up the principle of putting the people first (人民至上) as it appears in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Ma Dekun notes that the word "people" occurs more than 170 times in the report and calls it a manifesto of the supremacy of the people for the new era. The author argues that this principle is a defining feature of the Party's practice since 2012 and an expression of the Marxist idea of the free and all-round development of the human being.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why the Party's new journey and mission require upholding the supremacy of the people. The second sets out four components of the principle as the author understands it. The third turns to practice and names three tasks: close ties with the masses, firm fairness and justice, and common prosperity. It draws throughout on speeches by Xi Jinping and on the Party Congress report.

On the first part, Ma argues that the Party's historical mission, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, points in value terms towards the people's happiness. Its realisation also depends on the joint effort of all the people under Party leadership, so the mission itself demands that the people come first. The four components are taking the people's stance, attending to the will of the people, respecting the people's principal position, and promoting the people's wellbeing. The author links the second to whole-process people's democracy and the people's congress system, and the fourth to the high-quality development the Party pursues in order to meet the people's needs.

In the practical section, Ma holds that the mass line, "from the masses, to the masses", must be maintained and that the Party grew through its ties with the people. The author lists measures for fairness and justice: improving the distribution system, prioritising employment, strengthening social security and building a healthy China. Ma treats common prosperity as the final aim of the principle, while acknowledging that, because China is in the primary stage of socialism, the road to it remains long. The author expresses confidence that the Party can meet the people's aspirations for a better life. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned account of how the people-first principle was presented after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: In the new era, upholding the supremacy of the people has a scientific theoretical system and rich practical content.
quoteZh: 新时代坚持人民至上，具有科学的理论体系和丰富的实践内涵。

glossary.explanation: A principle stressed in Xi Jinping's speeches and in the 20th Party Congress report. It holds that the Party's work should put the people's interests first.
A working method associated with Mao Zedong, summed up as "from the masses, to the masses". It asks officials to gather the views of ordinary people and turn them into policy.
A term put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019 for China's democratic system. Official accounts say it covers every stage of political participation, not only voting.
An official goal of shared wealth across society, given new prominence under Xi Jinping. It is presented as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official assessment that China is still in an early phase of socialism, with underdeveloped productive forces. It has been used since the 1980s to frame long-term policy.
An official economic goal that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability over raw growth rates. It has been prominent since about 2017.

t: Philosophical distillation of the great practice of the new era
st: Studying and applying the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
zh: 新时代伟大实践经验的哲学升华
zhSub: 深入学习和运用 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的世界观和方法论
paras: Zhao Jianying takes up the call in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to grasp the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article, first published in China Social Sciences Today in April 2023, argues that the "Six Musts" are the concentrated expression of that worldview and methodology. In Zhao's account they are a philosophical summation of the experience of the new era, the core of the Thought, and the latest result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece has three parts. It first places the Six Musts in the lineage of Marxist philosophy and of earlier Chinese Marxism. It then takes each of the six in turn: put the people first, be self-confident and self-reliant, uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground, stay problem-oriented, apply systems thinking, and keep the whole world in view. A final section sets out how Party members should use this worldview in the new journey of building a modern socialist country.

Zhao's central move is to tie each "Must" to a named Marxist principle. Putting the people first is linked to the materialist conception of history and to a value orientation of people-centred development. Self-reliance is linked to the unity of the universal and the particular and to the dialectic of internal and external causes, so that no single modernization model is universal. Problem orientation and systems thinking are tied to epistemology and to the principle of universal connection, and the "world in view" is tied to world-history theory and to traditional Chinese ideas such as "great harmony under heaven". Zhao also traces continuity from Mao Zedong's independence and self-reliance and Deng Xiaoping's "our own road" to Xi, presenting the Six Musts as consistent with earlier thought while moving with the times.

Zhao concludes that this worldview should serve as an ideological weapon for transforming both the subjective and the objective world. The proposed applications are to read the era and the strategic picture of national rejuvenation, to advance Chinese modernization and common prosperity, to guard against major risks, to handle international relations and work toward a community with a shared future for mankind, and to pursue full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned account of how the Six Musts are presented as Marxist philosophy and as a continuation of Mao and Deng.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles is not clinging to the old: one must not be rigid and closed like the man who marked his boat to find a lost sword, nor copy foreign models without digesting them.
quoteZh: 守正不是“守成”，不能刻舟求剑，封闭僵化；也不能照抄照搬，食洋不化。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage of Marxism adapted to China.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: A formulation in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) summarising the Thought's worldview and methodology: put the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, uphold fundamental principles and break new ground, problem orientation, systems thinking, and a global vision.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official phrase for the Party's ongoing project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary developments.
The Party's term for China's own path to modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report as a path distinct from Western models.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, which Xi Jinping has made a central objective of development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for global governance and international relations, promoted since 2012–13.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline and internal oversight.

t: Guiding China's high-quality economic development with Xi Jinping Thought on Economy
zh: 以习近平经济思想指引中国经济高质量发展
paras: Ren Baoping, in a commentary first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2023, argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Economy is a major theoretical innovation that answers the question of how China can achieve high-quality development. In Ren's account, the thought arose from the entry of socialism with Chinese characteristics into a new era and the shift of the economy from rapid growth to high-quality development. It is presented as both a scientific guide and a programme of action for the new stage of development.

The piece has two main parts, preceded by a short framing of the thought's place in the Party's theory. The first part sets out five theoretical contributions, tracing the concept from the 19th Party Congress report through the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee to the 20th Party Congress report (2022). The second part lists six practical requirements for high-quality development and ends with a call to study and implement the thought.

Ren contends that the thought adapts Marxist political economy to Chinese conditions and extends it. The five contributions are: starting from the change in the principal contradiction of society; a people-centred approach; the new development philosophy, whose innovation, coordination, green, open and shared dimensions are each described as a theoretical advance; reforms in quality, efficiency and drivers of growth, aimed at raising total factor productivity; and using high-quality development to advance Chinese modernization. The practical requirements are high-level self-reliance in science and technology, building a new development pattern, orienting growth towards people's well-being, supply-side structural reform focused on the real economy, the digital economy as a new engine, and high-level opening up.

Ren concludes that high-quality development is the first task of building a modern socialist country in all respects, and that Xi's expositions on it form an important part of the thought. The author calls on readers to study, interpret and follow the thought so that the economy moves steadily forward on the path of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned summary of how Chinese scholars frame the theory and policy priorities of high-quality development in 2023.
quoteEn: The logical starting point of Xi Jinping Thought on Economy is the entry of socialism with Chinese characteristics into a new era, and it scientifically answers the defining question of our time: how to achieve high-quality development in China.
quoteZh: 习近平经济思想的逻辑起点是中国特色社会主义进入新时代，科学回答了如何实现中国高质量发展的时代主题

glossary.explanation: An official goal, announced at the 19th Party Congress in 2017, of shifting the economy from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and innovation.
The body of Xi Jinping's economic ideas, which the Party presents as the latest result of Marxist political economy adapted to China.
The official principles of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
The official name for China's path to modernization, emphasised in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A policy line introduced around 2015 that aims to raise the quality and efficiency of supply, for example by cutting overcapacity and upgrading industry.
An official strategy making the domestic market the mainstay, with domestic and international circulation reinforcing each other.

t: Marx's thought on combating spiritual poverty and its implications for our times
zh: 马克思反精神贫困思想及其时代启示
paras: Yu Chunling and Zhou Hequn ask what Marx's critique of capitalist "spiritual poverty" (jingshen pinkun) contributes to understanding that phenomenon and to pursuing spiritual prosperity today. They define spiritual poverty as a cultural phenomenon of social-wide loss of spirit and impoverished mental life, and focus on its social form. They argue that capitalist spiritual poverty is a relative poverty, a serious imbalance between spiritual and material development driven by the logic of capital. Marx's anti-poverty thought, in their view, offers theoretical guidance for "common prosperity" in spiritual life.

The article has four parts. The first reconstructs Marx's diagnosis of five symptoms: withered creative capacity, lowered aesthetic level, declining morality, alienated spiritual intercourse and lack of self-conscious awareness. The second traces roots at three levels: material and technological, institutional, and ideological. The third sets out Marx's route to spiritual prosperity. The fourth draws lessons for contemporary China. The authors draw on the 1844 Manuscripts, Capital, the Communist Manifesto and The German Ideology.

The central argument is that spiritual poverty arises from capitalist use of technology, private ownership and bourgeois ideology rather than from technology as such. Machine industry reduces workers to fragments of persons and takes away their free time. Private property and the logic of capital make usefulness and money the sole measure of value. The ruling class, which controls material production, also controls the means of mental production, including education. The authors conclude that Marx's way out has three conditions: material abundance through developed productive forces and technological innovation, escape from the logic of capital by abolishing capitalist private ownership, and proletarian revolution.

In the final part the authors draw lessons for China in the new era. They call for using the advantages of the socialist system and holding to the Two Unwaverings, while recognising the dual role of capital. They want regulation to prevent its disorderly expansion and its corrosion of cultural life. They call for coordinating material and spiritual wealth in pursuit of common prosperity, with Marxism guiding ideology and core socialist values guiding cultural work. They also want better public cultural services to meet people's growing cultural needs. They say that reform-era commodity economy has brought moral anomie, hedonism and vulgar tastes. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language reading of Marx on alienation and culture, linked to current Party policy on spiritual common prosperity.
quoteEn: Escaping spiritual poverty and achieving spiritual prosperity requires replacing the capitalist system with the socialist system, and also, as people's material lives grow richer, replacing all decadent, backward, outmoded and hypocritical capitalist cultural consciousness with a new socialist cultural consciousness.
quoteZh: 摆脱精神贫困、实现精神富裕既要求以社会主义制度取代资本主义制度，也要求在人们物质生活日益富足的同时，以崭新的社会主义文化意识取代一切腐朽、落后、陈旧、虚伪的资本主义文化意识

glossary.explanation: The authors' term for a social-wide deficit in mental and cultural life, such as weakened creativity, morality and aesthetic sense. They treat capitalist spiritual poverty as relative poverty, an imbalance between material and spiritual development.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, which the Party has stressed in recent years. The article extends it from material to spiritual life.
The official principle of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A twelve-word official set of values (such as prosperity, democracy, patriotism and integrity), promoted in Party-led ideological and cultural work since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The rule of capital's self-expansion and profit maximisation, which the authors say subordinates both material and spiritual production.

t: The young Marx's critique of private property and his turn to civil society
st: Centred on the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right
zh: 青年马克思的私有财产批判和市民社会转向
zhSub: 以《黑格尔法哲学批判》为中心
source: Journal of Central South University (Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 2
paras: Wen and Tang take up the question of how the young Marx moved from criticising Hegel's theory of the state to focusing on civil society. The usual account credits Feuerbach's materialism with this turn. The authors argue that this idealist–materialist and state–civil society framework is too simple. They contend that around 1843 Marx used the contradiction between private property and the state, and his scrutiny of property's legal relations, to grasp the practical limits of Hegel's philosophy of right. In their reading, this gave him the premise of historical materialism.

The article has three parts. The first traces the modern link between private property and the state, from the ancient city-state through Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau to Hegel, in order to reposition Marx's concerns at the Rheinische Zeitung. The second follows Marx's Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right on estates, primogeniture and landed property. The third considers the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, the Introduction to the Critique, and The German Ideology, to assess what the turn means theoretically.

The authors argue that Hegel tried to reform the natural-law tradition by building property and personality into objective spirit and by making the ethical state mediate civil society's conflicts. Marx judged the estates a 'political illusion' of civil society. In his analysis, hereditary landed property makes private property the highest constituent of the political state and so pushes law back to a Germanic private-law level. Hegel's scheme therefore could not overcome the split in modern civil society. Wen and Tang add that Marx saw the Philosophy of Right as an extension of Hegel's Logic. He accordingly replaced its abstract personality with real social human beings and made civil society the real subject, historically situated.

The authors conclude that the turn to civil society deepened the same problem and did not swap one object of study for another. They say it was an essential event in the formation of historical materialism. They also argue that the critique of private property should not be used to divide Marx's work into a political-critique phase and a political-economy phase. In their view the critique of political economy is internal to historical materialism, and Marx's dialectic was not completed in 1844. They suggest that Feuerbach's relation to Marx be reassessed. Read the original if you study the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, Marx's relation to Hegel and natural-law theory, or the early roots of historical materialism.
quoteEn: Dialectics is not a formal framework external to social content, but a dynamic process that restores reality as it is from behind the veil of abstract philosophical categories.
quoteZh: 辩证法不是一种外在于社会内容的形式框架，而是将现实本然从抽象哲学范畴的遮蔽中还原出来的动态历程。

t: The logical starting point of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学的逻辑起点
paras: Xie Fusheng and Kang Meng take up a question they say has been unresolved since the founding of China's socialist economic system: what category should serve as the logical starting point of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Citing Xi Jinping's call to turn practical experience into a systematic economic doctrine, they argue that a correct starting point is the first task of building the theoretical system. Their answer is the commodity.

The article first sorts existing positions into three groups by the type of category chosen: complex categories (the state, the economic system), indirect categories (labour in its various forms, 'the people') and simple categories (product, surplus product, commodity, and variants such as 'planned commodity'). It then returns to Hegel's account of the 'beginning of science' in the Logic and to Marx's method in Capital. Finally it applies that method to the socialist market economy, ending with the specific features of the Chinese system.

The authors argue that, following Hegel and Marx, a starting category must be simple, abstract and mediating, and that complex categories can only be results of the ascent from the abstract to the concrete. In their reading, labour and 'the people' are mediated categories, and product or surplus product do not express social relations. Marx himself began Capital with the commodity as the 'cell form' containing the germs of all later contradictions. Because socialism with Chinese characteristics, in the primary stage of socialism, still rests on commodity production and market exchange, the commodity keeps the same character. The law of value, realised through the coercive law of competition, mediates the move to enterprises, labour relations, industrial chains, urban–rural and international relations.

The authors conclude that the socialist commodity, like the capitalist one, can anchor the system, which differs from the capitalist one through five general features of the economic base: centralised Party leadership of economic work, the people-centred new development philosophy, the three-part basic economic system, building a community with a shared future for mankind, and seeking progress while maintaining stability. They claim these combine an 'effective market' with a 'capable government' and capture the positive results of capitalist commodity production while curbing blind market development. Read the original if you want a detailed survey of Chinese debates on the starting category, and a Hegel–Marx methodological defence of the commodity as the starting point for socialist political economy.
quoteEn: Therefore, the commodity remains the basic category under the economic system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the basis of all other categories.
quoteZh: 因此，商品仍是中国特色社会主义经济制度下的基础范畴，是其他一切范畴的依据。

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学
glossary.en: the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: A theoretical project, promoted since the 2010s, to turn China's reform-era economic experience into a systematic Marxist economic theory. Xi Jinping has called for developing it.
The official characterisation of China's present historical stage, used to justify market mechanisms and mixed ownership alongside public ownership.
A set of five principles (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) put forward in 2015 as guiding China's development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance.
The first category from which a theoretical system is built up step by step, drawing on Hegel's idea of the 'beginning of science'.

t: Towards a reasonable Enlightenment: Engels and Nietzsche
zh: 走向合理启蒙：恩格斯与尼采
source: Journal of Shandong Normal University (Social Sciences Edition), 2022 no. 2
paras: Comparisons of Marx and Nietzsche are well established, but Liu Senlin observes that no comprehensive comparison of Engels and Nietzsche exists. The article treats both as Enlightenment thinkers who began from a radical critique of religion and later moved to a more 'reasonable' Enlightenment position. Liu argues that they overlap, often in the very years they wrote, on Christianity, eternal recurrence, a return to nature, traditional morality and the limited legitimacy of metaphysics, while differing in important ways.

The article has three main sections. The first compares the young Engels (his 1840s review of Carlyle's Past and Present) with Nietzsche on the critique of Christianity and the 'death of God'. The second takes up eternal recurrence and metaphysics, drawing on Engels's Dialectics of Nature and Anti-Dühring and on Nietzsche's Human, All Too Human and Beyond Good and Evil. The third addresses morality and 'natural right', setting Engels's 1886 critique of Feuerbach beside Nietzsche's On the Genealogy of Morals.

Liu argues that both men read religion as a symptom of real suffering and as a falsification of reality, but they diverge at the point of resolution. Engels moves to atheism and locates religion's secret in society and history; Nietzsche exposes its psychological secret and offers a new god, Dionysus. On recurrence, Engels's concept is cosmological and independent of human activity, so it does not exclude progress, whereas Nietzsche's is a critique of modern progress. Both grant metaphysics a historical and psychological justification, though Nietzsche extends it to far more people and rejects dialectics as itself metaphysical. On morality, both hold that moral judgement can obscure reality and that a 'natural right' persists that society cannot abolish. Liu says Engels treats it as historically bound and sorts social 'natural right' into three cases: ideological deception to be exposed, what suits the productive forces, and aspirations for the future.

Liu concludes that, as they matured, both adjusted their early radical Enlightenment stance into a more reasonable one, marked by a return to nature, qualified acceptance of natural right and a dialectical attitude to tradition. Engels's future philosophy lies in the critique of political economy, whereas Nietzsche turns to a new humanism and rejects modern economics and sociology. Liu says Engels would criticise Dionysus. Read the original if you want a detailed, text-based comparison of Engels and Nietzsche on religion, metaphysics and morality, written from within Chinese Marxist philosophy.
quoteEn: In sum, as their thought matured, both Engels and Nietzsche adjusted the radical Enlightenment stance they had held earlier into a more reasonable Enlightenment stance.
quoteZh: 总之，随着思想的不断成熟，恩格斯和尼采皆把先前所持的激进启蒙立场调适为更合理的启蒙立场。

t: Continuously fulfilling the people's aspiration for a better life
zh: 不断实现人民对美好生活的向往
paras: This commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today on 30 March 2023, interprets a passage of the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). The passage calls for safeguarding and improving people's livelihoods through development and for continuously fulfilling the people's aspiration for a better life. Peng argues that this formula shows the Party's firm stance of standing with the people. In the author's account it also gives the Party a fundamental guide for keeping to its founding mission on the new journey.

The piece has four sections. The first presents the aspiration for a better life as an expression of the Party's original aspiration and founding mission. The second traces the idea through the Party's century of struggle, from the revolution to the era after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third and longest section sets out how the Party should move forward actively, under four headings: grasping the general trend of the times, starting from actual national conditions, focusing on real problems, and applying bottom-line thinking.

Peng's central claim is that the Party has no interests of its own and represents the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority. In this reading, every stage of its history, including the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, and reform and opening up, was driven by the goal of people's happiness and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. For the present, the author stresses that China remains in the primary stage of socialism. The principal contradiction is described as the one between the people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development, so economic development must stay the central task. The author adds that this lays the material basis for common prosperity and for Chinese modernization. Peng also calls for attention to people's most immediate concerns, for historical patience, and for stronger risk awareness and fighting spirit.

Peng concludes that if the Party treats fulfilling the people's aspiration for a better life as the starting point and goal of modernization, and works for common prosperity, it will gather great strength and build a brighter future. The text is an official-style interpretive commentary on the congress report, not an independent analysis. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists present the link between the Party's mission, its history and the new journey after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: We have always taken the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority of the people as the basic starting point and goal of all our work.
quoteZh: 我们始终以最广大人民根本利益为自己一切工作的根本出发点和落脚点

glossary.explanation: A Party formula, prominent since 2017, describing the Party's founding goal as seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing.
The official judgement that China is still at an early stage of socialist development, which is expected to last a long time and shapes policy priorities.
A goal of shared affluence for all, which Xi Jinping has stressed as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
A method of reasoning about worst-case risks and preparing for them in advance, promoted in Party discourse under Xi Jinping.

t: Western left-wing scholars' critique of digital capitalism from the perspective of global governance
zh: 全球治理视域下西方左翼学者的数字资本主义批判
paras: Song Jianli asks what Western left-wing communication scholars reveal about the risks that digital capitalism poses to global governance. Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2023, Song argues that the critiques of Dan Schiller, Christian Fuchs and Dallas Smythe show how capital's logic widens the digital divide and installs invisible control. In Song's reading, this undermines both the equality and the democratisation of global governance.

The article has three parts. The first treats the digital divide and its effect on equality, drawing on Schiller and Fuchs. The second turns to Smythe's "consciousness industry" and to later theories of surveillance and transparency (Foucault, Deleuze, Byung-Chul Han, Shoshana Zuboff, Christoph Kucklick), and considers algorithmic power and Herbert Schiller's "information geopolitics". The third part sets out the governance deficit in the digital economy and the prospect of a new form of human digital civilisation.

Song reports that Fuchs shows how "productive consumers" supply unpaid labour to internet firms, which hides the unequal relation between capital and labour and supports global exploitation of digital labour. Schiller, in this account, denies that digitalisation relieves capitalist crisis or inequality, and argues that it strengthens transnational firms and marketisation. Song adds that US-led "digital imperialism" relies on data hegemony and knowledge monopoly. Smythe's work, together with Han's "transparency society", is used to argue that the democratic promise of networks is an illusion. Audiences labour unseen, voluntary self-exposure perfects surveillance, and transparency erodes trust. Kucklick's paradox of opaque machines producing transparency is presented as a governance dilemma. Song adds that "big-data positivism" depoliticises governance and threatens national political and cultural security.

Song concludes that digital technology can either deepen global inequality or help reverse it, depending on whether it escapes the domination of capital interests. Governments should build open, fair and non-discriminatory rules for cyberspace and close the digital divide, with cooperation as the only viable path. The author expects China to play a more constructive role by acting on a global governance outlook of dialogue, inclusiveness and expanding common interests. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese overview of how Western critical communication scholarship on digital capitalism is being used in debates on global digital governance.
quoteEn: The accelerating use of digital technology may either aggravate global inequality or become a catalyst for reversing its growth.
quoteZh: 数字技术的加速运用既可能加剧全球不平等，也可能成为扭转全球不平等加剧的催化剂

glossary.explanation: A term, associated here with Dan Schiller, for capitalism in which digital networks and technologies become tools of capital accumulation and pervade economic and cultural life.
Dallas Smythe's concept, as presented in the article, for the industry that produces audiences as commodities and manages consciousness through communication systems.
The gap between those with access to and control of digital technology and data and those without.
The international rules and institutions for managing shared problems. In Chinese official discourse it is often paired with calls for a fairer international order.

t: The cultural dimension of the "Two Integrations" and the development of sinicized Marxism
zh: “两个结合”的文化维度与中国化马克思主义的发展
source: Social Science Journal (Shehui kexue jikan), 2023 no. 3
paras: Hong Jun asks why the requirement that Marxism be integrated with China's fine traditional culture, set out in Xi Jinping's 2021 speech on the Party's centenary and restated at the 20th Party Congress (2022), matters for the development of Marxism in China. The article argues that the cultural dimension of the Two Integrations is a conclusion drawn from more than a century of debate and practice. In Hong's account, giving it prominence clears away long-standing confusion and moves sinicized Marxism to a higher stage.

The article is a historical-conceptual survey in four parts. It begins with Engels and Lenin on the "localisation" of Marxism, and with Stalin on national form and proletarian content, and notes the early Chinese Communists' attempts at adaptation. It then examines Mao Zedong's discussions of sinicization, followed by the mistaken views on the relation between Marxism and Chinese tradition, from both outside and inside the Marxist camp. The last part sets out the grounds on which the two are said to be compatible.

Hong argues that Mao's 1938 report already contained two dimensions, a practical one (applying Marxism to Chinese conditions) and a historical-cultural one (critically inheriting the heritage "from Confucius to Sun Yat-sen"). Mao's letters to Chen Boda on Mozi and Confucius are cited as evidence of his classical learning. Even so, Mao and later formulations stressed the practical dimension, so understanding stayed at "one integration" for a long time. Hong attributes this to historical conditions and to widespread mistaken views. Cultural conservatives, Guomindang right-wingers and some dogmatists inside the Party all treated Marxism and Chinese culture as incompatible. Many early Communist leaders, shaped by the New Culture Movement, were nihilistic about tradition.

Hong holds that the historical record refutes the claim that Marxism does not suit Chinese conditions, and points to an "affinity" between the two. Examples are the Confucian ideals of datong (great harmony) and xiaokang, the minben (people-as-basis) tradition, and ancient materialist and dialectical ideas, with support from Li Zehou. The influence ran both ways: tradition underwent modern transformation, and Marxism was enriched by it. Hong concludes that the 20th Congress formulation reflects cultural consciousness and confidence and provides theoretical support for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a detailed intellectual-historical account of how Party theorists and their critics treated Marxism and Chinese tradition from the 1920s to the present.
quoteEn: The question of the relation between Marxism and traditional Chinese culture is in fact bound up with the "China versus the West" and "substance versus function" controversy that has run for over a century.
quoteZh: 马克思主义与中国传统文化的关系问题，实际上与100多年来不断争论的“中西”“体用”问题是联系在一起的。

glossary.explanation: The formula that the basic tenets of Marxism must be combined both with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second element was added to the classic formula in Xi Jinping's 2021 speech.
A Confucian ideal of a world in which "all under heaven is shared". Some early Chinese Marxists and Mao Zedong linked it to communism.
In the classics, a stage of order below datong. Deng Xiaoping reused it in the reform era as a development goal.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of national revival that is central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: How is the integration of Marxist basic principles with fine traditional Chinese culture possible?
st: An examination centred on the social justice of the classical Marxist thinkers' attention to Chinese questions
zh: 马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合何以可能
zhSub: 以马克思主义经典思想家关注中国问题的社会正义性为中心的考察
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and Xi Jinping's speech of 1 July 2021, the article asks how the basic principles of Marxism can be combined with fine traditional Chinese culture, which it abbreviates as the "Two Combinations" in the narrow sense. Wang argues that the answer lies in a shared "social justice" dimension: Marxist theory and Chinese culture are compatible because both express justice, and Marx and Engels's writings on China show this. The combination is therefore described as both legitimate and necessary.

The article has three sections. The first sets out a "justice context" for the combination, addressing three doubts in the scholarly literature and reviewing five existing lines of interpretation. The second reads Marx and Engels's 1850s writings on China, including those on the Opium Wars and the opium trade, to show where the two traditions meet. The third draws practical implications for contemporary China under three headings, each beginning "着力于" (focusing on).

Wang first treats the doubts as constructive. The "change of nature" worry is that Marxism's revolutionary character is lost. The "change of flavour" worry is that Chinese culture's distinctiveness is diluted. The "change of score" worry is that the integration stays theoretical and detached from practice. Wang then reads Marx and Engels as holding that a just nation raises a just cry, a just people pursues a just cause, and just practice needs just theory. On this reading, they backed Chinese resistance to aggression while criticising fatalism and the idea that violence drives development. Wang finds affinities between their views and values such as "the world belongs to all", people-centredness and harmony between humanity and nature.

Wang concludes that the combination should aim to meet the people's need for a better life, advance the creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture, and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics. For the last of these, the article points to institutional improvement, distributive justice and Chinese modernization. It presents social justice as a lens that unites the scientific character of theory with its practical necessity. Read the original if you want a justice-centred reading of Marx and Engels's China texts within current Party discourse on the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: The inherent fit and mutual penetration between the basic principles of Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture, and their interaction, require us to understand more deeply and put into practice.
quoteZh: 马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化的内在契合融通及其相互作用，需要我们进一步深刻领会并付诸实践。

glossary.explanation: Party formula for integrating the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was added prominently in Xi Jinping's speech of 1 July 2021.
Official term for the parts of China's historical culture regarded as worth inheriting and developing in the present.
Official term for China's own path of modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: Official guideline for treating traditional culture: recasting it in forms suited to the present and developing its content.

t: From "categorical sophistry" to "critique of capital": how Engels surpassed the classical political economy of poverty
zh: 从“范畴诡辩”到“资本批判”：恩格斯对古典政治经济学贫困理论的超越
source: Studies on Socialism (Shehui zhuyi yanjiu), 2023 no. 1
paras: Wu Dajuan and Xue Junqiang ask how Friedrich Engels's theory of poverty broke with that of classical political economy. They argue that existing scholarship treats Engels mainly as a "bridge" to Marx's critique of political economy and as a subordinate of Marx's own poverty theory, and neglects his original contribution. In their account, Engels lifted the question of poverty from "categorical speculation" to a "critique of capital", opening a scientific path distinct from classical economics.

The article has three parts. The first characterises classical political economy (Adam Smith, Ricardo, Malthus) as ahistorical and uncritical. The second sets out Engels's critique in three steps: of the "economic man" premise, of the way classical economists explain the roots of poverty, and of their remedies. The third draws out the spirit and value of Engels's break, drawing on Althusser, Marcuse, Harvey, Foucault and Polanyi as supporting voices.

The authors claim that classical economists treated capitalist relations as eternal natural law and reduced poverty to individual failings or to distribution. Engels, they argue, showed that capital is not accumulated labour but a social means by which people rule people, and that poverty springs from capitalist private property and competition rather than from "small abuses". They read his phrase "social murder" as exposing a hidden form of capitalist exploitation, and compare it to Foucault's panopticon. Engels also treated political economy as a "historical science", embedding poverty in the history of industry, politics and the workers' movement.

The authors conclude that Engels offered a new "problematic" rather than a correction of the old one. On their reading, he held that small repairs are futile unless the ownership system built on the propertylessness of the majority is abolished, and that poverty is overcome only through the workers' liberation and communism. They present his fieldwork, journalism and later work on Capital and the Second International as combining scientific rigour with humanistic concern. Read the original if you study Engels's independent role in Marxist poverty theory or the Chinese reception of his early economic writings.
quoteEn: Engels pointed out that capital is in essence not accumulated labour but a social means by which people rule over people.
quoteZh: 恩格斯指出，资本本质上不是积累起来的劳动，而是人统治人的社会手段

t: Raising political capacity through stronger theoretical cultivation
zh: 在加强理论修养中提高政治能力
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily in April 2023, takes up Xi Jinping's remarks at the 90th anniversary of the Central Party School. Xi said that the firmer a leading cadre's grasp of Marxism, the higher their political standing and the stronger their political judgement, political comprehension and political execution. Li argues that theoretical cultivation is the core of a leading cadre's overall quality and largely determines their political capacity.

The piece first explains why openly emphasising politics is a mark of Marxist parties and a long-standing strength of the Party. It then takes the three capacities in turn: political judgement, political comprehension and political execution. For each it sets out what theoretical study should contribute.

On judgement, Li holds that systematic mastery of Marxist theory, especially the Party's innovative theory of the new era, sharpens the ability to read situations, tell right from wrong and resist risks. Cadres should use Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to "forge their souls" and spot political problems early. On comprehension, the author calls for deep study of that thought, an understanding of the Two Establishes, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, and close alignment with the Central Committee. On execution, Li says cadres must check their work against Party theory, line and Central Committee decisions, carry out what the Centre decides, and face problems directly.

Li concludes that theoretical maturity underpins political maturity, and that study should end in faithful implementation of Central Committee decisions. The aim is to keep advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party commentary links theoretical study to cadres' political capacities.
quoteEn: Theoretical maturity is the foundation of political maturity, and political firmness stems from theoretical clarity.
quoteZh: 理论上的成熟是政治上成熟的基础，政治上的坚定源于理论上的清醒。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), establishing Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: Demonstrating the power of scientific modes of thinking and working
st: Lessons from China's three-year COVID-19 response
zh: 展现科学思想方法和工作方法的强大力量
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in April 2023, after China moved to a new phase of COVID-19 management, Ding argues that the pandemic response shows the strength of the scientific ways of thinking and working that the Communist Party has long stressed. The commentary holds that the response, led by the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, reflects both the advantages of Party leadership and of the socialist system, and the practical power of these methods.

The piece is a short official commentary organised under five headings: strategic resolve and decisive decision-making; seeking truth from facts; a systems approach; bottom-line thinking; and respect for scientific spirit and technology. Each heading opens with a statement by Xi Jinping and then links it to episodes of the pandemic response, from the closing of outbound routes from Wuhan and Hubei in January 2020 to the downgrading of management of the infection on 8 January 2023.

Ding's central move is to read each stage of the response as an application of a named method. The shift from the "dynamic zero-COVID" policy to category B management is presented as flexible adjustment to the weakened pathogenicity of Omicron, wider vaccination and accumulated experience, and as evidence of seeking truth from facts. The principle of "containing the epidemic, stabilising the economy, ensuring development security" is described as a systems approach, supported by the "six stabilities" and "six guarantees" and by the author's figure of a 2022 GDP of 121 trillion yuan. Bottom-line thinking appears in preparing for worst cases, in support for small firms and the most vulnerable, and in strengthening the public health emergency system. The final section stresses science-led decisions, research on vaccines, tests and treatments, and public science education.

Ding concludes that these methods let the Party keep the strategic initiative, and that the outcome shows the power of scientific thinking and working methods. The article offers no critical appraisal of the response; it is an affirmative account that also serves as a guide to how Party theory frames the pandemic experience. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary in 2023 presented the pandemic response as a demonstration of Marxist methodology.
quoteEn: Insisting that the epidemic be contained, the economy stabilised and development kept secure is a scientific application of the systems approach.
quoteZh: 坚持疫情要防住、经济要稳住、发展要安全，就是对系统观念的科学运用。

glossary.explanation: China's general policy from 2020 to late 2022 of rapidly suppressing every outbreak through testing, tracing, lockdowns and quarantine.
A Party principle of basing policy on actual conditions rather than dogma. Mao Zedong gave it prominence, and the Party treats it as a core element of its ideological line.
A method stressed by Xi Jinping that calls for viewing problems comprehensively and as interconnected, not in isolation.
A way of thinking promoted by Xi Jinping that prepares for the worst outcomes while striving for the best, in order to prevent and defuse major risks.

Economic policy slogans introduced in 2018 and 2020. They call for stability in areas such as employment, finance, foreign trade and investment, and guarantees for areas such as jobs, basic living needs and supply chains.

t: Treating science with a scientific attitude and pursuing truth in the spirit of truth
zh: 以科学的态度对待科学 以真理的精神追求真理
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily in April 2023, takes up Xi Jinping's call to treat science with a scientific attitude and pursue truth in the spirit of truth. Zhong argues that Marxism is the Party's fundamental guiding ideology but is not a fixed dogma. In Zhong's account, it is an open theoretical system that develops with the times, practice and science, and its vitality lies in uniting adherence to Marxism with its development.

The piece moves from Marxism in general to the Chinese Communist Party's own record and then to present tasks. It first recalls what Marxism reveals about social development and capitalism, then reviews more than a century of Party practice, then sets out what is required now.

Zhong notes that Marx and Engels described their theory as a guide to action, applied according to historical conditions. Marxists have therefore kept their theory alive by adjusting it to national circumstances, history and the demands of the age. The Party, in this reading, has done the same through adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, combining its basic principles with China's realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Zhong says, this produced Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, described as a new leap and an original theoretical contribution.

Zhong concludes that practice and theoretical innovation have no end, and that Chinese communists today have a historic duty to keep writing new chapters. Citing Xi, Zhong rejects both dogmatism and pragmatism. Zhong calls for attention to major practical and strategic problems in building a modern socialist country, close links with the creative practice of the masses, and absorption of the achievements of other civilisations. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the official press justifies continuing theoretical innovation in Marxism.
quoteEn: Treating science with a scientific attitude and pursuing truth in the spirit of truth is the consistent position and distinct attitude of Chinese communists towards scientific truth.
quoteZh: 以科学的态度对待科学、以真理的精神追求真理，是中国共产党人对待科学真理的一贯立场和鲜明态度。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for each era. It is presented as the Party's ongoing task of theoretical innovation.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions after the 19th Party Congress (2017). It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
