t: Showcasing the distinctive character of "upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground" in the new era
zh: 彰显新时代守正创新的鲜明气象
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 12 April 2023, takes up one of the "six musts" set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): the requirement to uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground (shouzheng chuangxin). Qin Gang argues that this principle is a regular pattern the Party has drawn from a century of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. In the author's account it is also a distinctive mark of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and of the new era itself.

The piece is built in three parts, each opened and anchored by quotations from Xi Jinping. The first treats the principle as an experience of Party theory and practice. The second presents it as an objective requirement for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics. The third presents it as methodological guidance for advancing Chinese modernization. The article was written to support the study campaign on Xi Jinping Thought launched in 2023.

Qin's first move is to root the principle in both Marxism and Chinese tradition. The author reads Marx and Engels's statements that the application of the Manifesto's principles depends on historical conditions, and that theory is not a dogma to be repeated mechanically, as early expressions of the idea. The author then pairs these with classical Chinese sayings about renewal and adapting to the times, and presents the principle as the outcome of combining Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. Second, Qin defines the relationship between the two halves. Upholding principles means not wavering on Marxism, the Party's overall leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics, but it is not rigid adherence to old formulas. Innovation, in turn, must have roots and a source. Third, Qin credits this approach, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), with the new ideas and strategies of the new era, the elimination of absolute poverty and the building of a moderately prosperous society. The author also credits it with a theory of Chinese modernization that presents it as a new form of human civilisation, distinct from the Western model.

Qin concludes that the Party must keep to this method as the world undergoes what the article calls changes unseen in a century, and as it faces new risks and challenges. By keeping national development based on its own strength, the author says, the Party can win new victories in building a modern socialist country. Qin calls on readers to turn the worldview, methodology and standpoint of Xi Jinping Thought into their own intellectual tools. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2023 presented "upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground" as a methodology that links Marxism, Chinese tradition and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground complement each other, embodying the dialectical unity of change and constancy, inheritance and development, principle and creativity.
quoteZh: 守正与创新相辅相成，体现变与不变、继承与发展、原则性与创造性的辩证统一。

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground
glossary.literal: guard what is correct, create anew
glossary.explanation: A methodological formula in Party discourse. It combines firm adherence to Marxism, Party leadership and the socialist path with theoretical and practical innovation. It appears among the "six musts" in the 20th Party Congress report.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīnshídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to the present era.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist modernization led by the Party and distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six methodological principles named in the 20th Party Congress report for theoretical innovation. They include putting the people first, self-confidence, and upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground.
A long-standing Chinese goal of general, basic prosperity. The Party declared it "fully built" in 2021.

t: Embracing the world: demonstrating the responsibility of a major Party and a major country
zh: 胸怀天下彰显大党大国责任担当
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 17 April 2023, explains one of the "six musts" (liù ge bìxū jiānchí) in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era: the requirement to "embrace the world" (xiōnghuái tiānxià). Su Changhe presents this as a standpoint and method that the Communist Party of China uses to understand and handle its relations with the outside world. The author argues that it shows the global outlook and sense of responsibility of a major Party and a major country.

The piece is organised under three headings. The first concerns grasping global trends and the tide of the times. The second concerns placing China's own development within the framework of human development. The third concerns building a community with a shared future for mankind. It draws throughout on statements by Xi Jinping, and it opens by situating the topic at the point where the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation intersects with what it calls changes unseen in a century.

In Su's account, Xi applies dialectical and historical materialism to the international situation. Xi reaches several judgements: peace, development, cooperation and win-win outcomes remain the main line; economic globalization is a historical trend despite setbacks; and China is still in a period of strategic opportunity. Su then argues that the Party pursues its own development in step with the world's. The Belt and Road Initiative, trade expos and regional trade agreements are cited as ways of sharing opportunities, and Chinese modernization is described as rejecting colonial plunder and the path of a strong country seeking hegemony. The third section lists the principles, initiatives and values Xi has put forward to build a community with a shared future for mankind. These include the Global Development, Global Security and Global Civilization Initiatives and the "common values of all humanity". The article contends that hegemonic power, zero-sum games and ideological confrontation push the world towards division.

Su concludes that, whatever happens internationally, the Party will remain consistent in embracing the world. It will use Chinese modernization to advance national rejuvenation, add stability to the cause of peace and development, and uphold the common values of all humanity. The text reads as an authoritative exposition of official foreign-policy thinking in the early period after the 20th Party Congress. Read the original if you want a concise account of how Chinese official discourse in 2023 framed the link between domestic development, Chinese modernization and the idea of a shared-future community.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization does not follow the old path of colonial plunder, nor the crooked path of a strong country inevitably seeking hegemony; it takes the right path of peaceful development, benefiting the Chinese people while promoting the common development of the world.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化不走殖民掠夺的老路，不走国强必霸的歪路，走的是和平发展的人间正道，既造福中国人民、又促进世界共同发展。

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: A summary of the stance, viewpoint and method of Xi Jinping Thought: putting the people first, self-reliance, innovation, upholding principles and breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systems thinking, and embracing the world. It was set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

glossary.literal: to hold the whole world in one's heart
glossary.explanation: One of the six musts. It refers to a global outlook and a sense of responsibility towards humanity, and is used in official discourse to describe the Party's approach to external relations.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping from 2012–13 and now central to Chinese foreign-policy discourse. It stresses interdependence among states and joint responses to global challenges.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream. It denotes restoring China's strength and international standing.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The meaning and connotations of common prosperity in spiritual life
zh: 精神生活共同富裕的意义内涵
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 15 March 2023
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary in March 2023, Wan Ping asks what common prosperity in spiritual life means, taking as a starting point Xi Jinping's call at the tenth meeting of the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission to promote it under the guidance of core socialist values. Wan notes that scholars still debate the concept and mostly stress the functional, mutually supportive relation between the spiritual and the material. The author argues that this neglects the concept's "generative" dimension, and that common prosperity in spiritual life is an organic unity of three ideals.

The article is built around these three ideals: an ideal of inner richness in personal life, a social ideal of harmony between individual and society, and a national dream of promoting all-round human development. A closing section ties them to the core socialist values.

On the first ideal, Wan holds that material abundance does not automatically produce spiritual prosperity and that some groups may fall into a "spiritual poverty trap". The author calls for drawing on Zhuangzi and Kant, promoting a view of life based on contribution and goodness, curbing consumerism, and giving spiritual support to disadvantaged groups. On the second, Wan points to Confucian ethics and to digital technology's potential for "warm" social ties. On the third, Wan argues that earlier states, limited by class, could do little for all-round development, whereas the socialist state makes it a national aim, which Xi Jinping raised to the level of the Chinese Dream after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Wan concludes that the first two ideals are the starting point of the third, while the third guarantees their realisation. Core socialist values at the national, social and individual levels are said to guide all three, and spiritual and material civilization are to advance together. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese scholars link common prosperity to spiritual life, core socialist values and human development.
quoteEn: Considered from the generative dimension of its meaning, common prosperity in spiritual life is an organic unity of the life ideal of inner richness, the social ideal of harmony between individual and society, and the national dream of promoting all-round human development.
quoteZh: 基于内涵生成性维度考量，精神生活共同富裕是内心富足的人生理想、个人与社会和谐相处的社会理想与促进人的全面发展的国家梦想的有机统一。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping has made a central policy aim since the early 2020s, covering fairer distribution and, in this article, spiritual as well as material wealth.
A set of 24 characters in three tiers (national, social, individual) promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, referring to national rejuvenation and the well-being of the people.
The idea that common prosperity should include people's cultural and spiritual lives, not only their material wealth. It was stressed by Xi Jinping in 2021.

t: Grasping the meaning of the fighting spirit through materialist dialectics
zh: 基于唯物辩证法领悟斗争精神意涵
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2023, asks how the Party's call to be "bold and skilful in struggle" can be understood philosophically. Zhang argues that the fighting spirit is rooted in materialist dialectics, specifically the Marxist theory of contradiction. The piece follows the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, which told the whole Party to be "bold and skilful in struggle".

The article has four sections, each tying one aspect of contradiction theory to the practice of struggle. They cover the basic properties of contradiction, its universality and objectivity, the method of contradiction analysis, and the struggle aspect of contradiction. Zhang draws on Mao Zedong, Marx and Xi Jinping, and traces the wording of the 18th, 19th and 20th Party Congress reports on "great struggle".

Zhang holds that contradictions exist everywhere and independently of human will, so the willingness to acknowledge, expose and analyse them is the philosophical basis of daring to struggle. Skill in struggle comes from the method of contradiction analysis: distinguishing principal from secondary contradictions, concentrating on the former while coordinating the latter, and analysing each concrete problem on its own terms. This includes judging the timing, effect and degree of struggle. On the struggle aspect, Zhang says unity of opposites is conditional and relative while struggle is absolute, so the Party should unite all forces it can and work to shift the balance between the two sides.

Zhang concludes that this orientation shows the Party's resolve in dealing with the problems unique to a large Party in the world. The author states that, with unity around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, the Party can draw on Marxism to advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party commentary grounds the official language of struggle in the vocabulary of dialectical materialism.
quoteEn: Daring to struggle does not mean showing off or acting recklessly; it means grasping the direction of struggle, seizing its key points and attending to strategy, and understanding the method of contradiction analysis is the key to mastering the art of struggle.
quoteZh: 敢于斗争并不是逞强好胜、蛮干硬上，而是要把握斗争方向、抓住斗争重点，注重斗争策略，理解和掌握矛盾分析法则是把握斗争艺术的关键。

glossary.explanation: A Party term for a readiness to confront risks and difficulties. It has been stressed in Xi Jinping-era documents and is presented as a defining political trait of the Communist Party of China.
The official name for China's path of modernization. The 20th Party Congress (2022) presented it as the Party's central task.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream and tied to the second centenary goal for 2049.

t: Building a discourse system of institutions from the perspective of conceptual history
zh: 概念史视角下的制度话语体系建构
paras: This commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao) on 30 March 2023, asks how a discourse system for the institutions of socialism with Chinese characteristics can be built. Yang Binbin argues that conceptual history, a method that traces how concepts evolve in order to present historical logic as a whole, is a workable path. In Yang's view, it can support efforts to strengthen confidence in China's institutions and to tell the story of those institutions in a way suited to the times.

The article treats the institutional discourse of socialism with Chinese characteristics as a developing and open system of concepts, assertions and propositions with different historical, cultural and practical sources. It sorts these sources along three dimensions, each with three types: cultural origin, historical position and the form in which concepts are generated in practice. Yang acknowledges that conceptual history has several strands (social history, history of ideas, history of words) but holds that its methodology has distinctive value for this task.

On cultural origin, Yang distinguishes endogenous concepts, imported concepts and fusion concepts. The last are traditional Chinese terms that the Party has given new content, which Yang presents as an expression of combining Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. On historical position, Yang separates summarising or reflective concepts (oriented to the past), guiding or anticipatory concepts (oriented to the future) and responsive or judgemental concepts (oriented to present reality). Many political concepts, the author notes, combine factual and value judgements. On form, Yang lists inherited, borrowed and reworked concepts, with a further case of concepts re-imported. Concepts must be read in their specific historical context, Yang argues, or they will be misattributed or earlier thinkers wrongly criticised.

Yang concludes that introducing conceptual history into the study of the theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and into Party history, the history of reform and opening up, the history of the People's Republic and the history of socialism, has important value. In Yang's account, it would help build China's own knowledge system, make better use of discursive resources, make institutional explanation more self-aware and theoretical explanation more thorough, and show the values and wisdom in China's political path. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese scholars propose to use conceptual-history methods to systematise the vocabulary of institutional confidence and discourse building.
quoteEn: Concepts are historically fluid forms of expression; using the method of conceptual history to trace and examine the concepts in China's political theory, practice and institutions helps clarify the real-world positioning of efforts to build the institutional discourse system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the discourse system of philosophy and the social sciences.
quoteZh: 概念是一种历史性的流动表达，通过概念史的研究方法加强对中国特色政治理论、政治实践、政治制度中的概念追溯与辨析，有助于明确中国特色社会主义制度话语体系、哲学社会科学话语体系建构的现实定位

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, in use since the early 1980s and associated with reform and opening up.
One of the 'confidences' promoted in Party discourse, meaning conviction in the soundness of China's socialist system and its governance arrangements.
A structured set of concepts, terms and narratives through which a political or academic position is expressed; Party leaders call for building a distinctively Chinese one.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合
glossary.pinyin: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì jīběn yuánlǐ tóng Zhōnghuá yōuxiù chuántǒng wénhuà xiāng jiéhé
glossary.en: combining Marxism with China's fine traditional culture
glossary.explanation: The formula, part of the 'Two Integrations', that Marxism's basic tenets should be joined with elements of traditional Chinese culture that the Party regards as valuable.
A slogan, prominent in Xi Jinping-era discussions of the humanities and social sciences, for scholarship grounded in Chinese practice rather than Western frameworks.

t: Marx and Engels's critique of the paradoxes of capitalist society
zh: 马克思恩格斯对资本主义社会悖论的批判
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 23 February 2023
paras: This short commentary asks how to understand the claim in the Communist Manifesto that the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are equally inevitable. Liu Shuhui argues that the claim can be grasped through three paradoxes of capitalist society that Marx and Engels identified: those of wealth, freedom and civilisation. The author presents the Manifesto as the first comprehensive statement of the principles of scientific socialism, built on dialectical and historical materialism and on the law that society's basic contradictions drive its development.

The article takes each paradox in turn and traces it through the classical texts. For wealth, Liu draws on The Poverty of Philosophy, Wage Labour and Capital, the Manifesto and Capital. For freedom, the sources are Marx's speech on free trade, Capital and Engels's writing against Karl Heinzen. For civilisation, Liu turns to Engels's early outline of a critique of political economy and the Manifesto. A brief closing section ties the three paradoxes to the forms of working-class struggle.

On wealth, Liu argues that capitalist production relations generate wealth and poverty together. Accumulation at one pole, in Marx's words in Capital, goes with an accumulation of misery at the other. In Liu's reading, the bourgeoisie cannot guarantee even a bare subsistence to its wage-slaves, so it can no longer rule. On freedom, the freedom of buying, selling, trade and competition presupposes workers who own nothing but their labour-power. Liu says such workers are free only to sell themselves, and to choose by whom they are exploited. On civilisation, the bourgeoisie draws every nation into its mode of production and subordinates the East to the West through colonialism. The article calls the resulting world lopsided and deformed. Liu adds that the wealth paradox also covers ecological destruction, which the Manifesto does not address.

Liu concludes that the first two paradoxes lead workers to unite against their own national bourgeoisie, while the third leads proletarians worldwide to unite against the bourgeoisie as such. In this sense, the author says, the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are equally inevitable. Read the original if you want a compact, text-based outline of how the Manifesto and related classics ground the thesis of the bourgeoisie's inevitable downfall, as presented in the Chinese official press.
quoteEn: The civilised world that the bourgeoisie creates for itself in its own image is a seriously unbalanced, deformed world.
quoteZh: 资产阶级按自己的面貌为自己创造的文明世界，是一个严重失衡的畸形世界。

glossary.explanation: The term for the socialist theory founded by Marx and Engels, set against earlier utopian socialism. In Chinese texts it designates the core doctrine of Marxism on the laws of social development and the proletariat's historical mission.

A term in Chinese Marxist textbooks for the contradictions between the forces and relations of production and between the economic base and the superstructure. They are held to drive historical development.

t: Whole-process people's democracy: the unity of discourse construction and practical path
zh: 全过程人民民主：话语建构与实践路径的统一
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 15 February 2023
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary in February 2023, Chen Chengxin asks what distinguishes whole-process people's democracy among the world's democratic forms. The author's answer is that it unifies the construction of democratic discourse with the practical path of democracy, making it a form of democracy in which words and deeds agree. Chen traces this to three features: a people-centred starting point, democracy running through the entire process, and Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee.

The piece has three sections. The first deals with the people-centred logical starting point, discussed under two headings: the 'whole subject' (all the people) and the 'whole domain' (all fields of life). The second sets out the comparative advantages of whole-process people's democracy, especially relative to electoral democracy. The third explains why Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee that discourse and practice stay aligned.

Chen argues that 'the people' in this model includes respect for individual rights but unites them within a systemic 'whole subject'. The article presents the basic socialist economic system, with the means of production owned by all the people, as ensuring that democracy is not controlled by interest groups. It then claims that two kinds of 'completeness' give the model its advantage: a complete institutional procedure (the people's congress system, multiparty cooperation, regional ethnic autonomy, grassroots self-governance) and complete participatory practice, described as full-chain, all-round and full-coverage. Unlike 'one election decides everything' formal democracy, Chen contends, it is oriented to whether problems are effectively solved, with consultation and supervision running through the whole term of office and the whole decision cycle. Because the Party both constructs the discourse and leads the practice, the author argues, its leadership secures direction, orderly implementation and efficient governance, with the people's evaluation as the standard.

Chen concludes that Party leadership lets discourse and practice develop together, citing people's congress supervision and the People's Daily Online 'message board for leaders' as examples of democratic innovation in the new era. The author adds a caution that 'whole process' operates within a certain context and scope, so its discursive boundaries and operating limits should be kept in view. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how Chinese scholars present whole-process people's democracy as superior to electoral democracy and as inseparable from Party leadership.
quoteEn: Whole-process people's democracy does not take the "ballot" as its sole orientation, but takes "whether problems can be effectively solved" as its performance-based orientation.
quoteZh: 全过程人民民主不以“选票”为唯一导向，而以“是否能够有效解决问题”为实绩导向。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019 describing China's socialist democracy as operating through every stage of political life, not only elections. Official discourse presents it as an alternative to Western electoral democracy.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Party policy since the 18th Party Congress (2012), holding that governance should start from and serve the interests of the people.
China's fundamental political system, in which congresses at each level, up to the National People's Congress, exercise state power on behalf of the people.

t: The social-scientific methods of the dialectics of nature
zh: 自然辩证法的社会科学方法探赜
paras: Wang Yuexin asks how the dialectics of nature, usually read as Marx and Engels's thinking about nature and science, relates to the social sciences. The article, a short piece first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, argues that the dialectics of nature rests on a thorough use of social-scientific methods. This, Wang says, is why it avoids becoming a mere "dialectics of the natural world" and joins with the dialectics of history.

The piece opens with Bonifaty Kedrov's view that Engels's Dialectics of Nature is an important introduction to Capital and that it makes Marxist doctrine more complete. It then takes three methods in turn: the study of the social subject (the social body), the historical method, and class analysis. Wang draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin, and on commentators including Lukács, Alfred Schmidt, Sidney Hook and John Bellamy Foster.

Wang first argues that, seen from the social subject, "nature" in the dialectics of nature is not the bare natural world. It is mediated by labour and forms the basis of productive forces, and science and technology are likewise a social activity, driven by social need. Second, the historical method here is that of historical materialism, not natural-history explanation of the kind Marx criticised in Büchner's social Darwinism. Wang reads the unity of natural history and human history as implying a duty to future generations to treat the earth like "good heads of households". Third, class analysis exposes the ecological damage that capitalism does through its exploitation of workers and its seizure of resources worldwide. It also points to the liberation of the proletariat, which Wang links to the ecological liberation sketched in the 1844 Manuscripts as the unity of thoroughgoing naturalism and humanism.

Wang concludes that social-historical methodology runs through the dialectics of nature and completes Marx and Engels's thought on nature, science and technology. Ecology and technology then no longer appear as inert matter but are internally united with historical dialectics. The text relates the dialectics of nature to ecological concerns, including the harmonious coexistence of humanity and nature. Read the original if you want a compact account of how one Chinese author links Marxist ecology, historical materialism and class analysis within the dialectics of nature.
quoteEn: By applying the methodology of the social sciences, the dialectics of nature fundamentally avoids reducing itself to a mere "dialectics of the natural world".
quoteZh: 自然辩证法对社会科学方法论的运用，使自身从根本上避免了沦为“自然界的辩证法”

glossary.explanation: The title of Engels's unfinished work on natural science and dialectics. In Chinese Marxism it also names a field of study covering Marxist views of nature, science and technology.

The article renders Marx's Gesellschaftskörper / gesellschaftliches Subjekt as the social body or organism, the whole of society's productive sectors. It serves here as the starting point of social-scientific method.
The Marxist theory that material production and social relations shape historical development.
The Marxist method of analysing social phenomena through class relations and class struggle.

t: Strengthening the exposition of the Marxist stand, viewpoint and method
zh: 加强对马克思主义立场观点方法的阐释
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Yang Wenming asks how research on Party documents should respond to the Congress report's claim that the Party succeeds because Marxism, in its form adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, "works". Yang's thesis is that the historic achievements of the past decade are, at root, a victory for applying Marxist materialism and dialectics. The task for document researchers is therefore to strengthen exposition of the stand, viewpoint and method (lichang guandian fangfa) running through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

This short commentary has three parts. The first links the decade's results to the Party's use of dialectical and historical materialism, citing Politburo study sessions on these subjects and the handling of major relationships such as the whole and the part, or the long term and the present. The second sets out the worldview and methodology of the Party's innovative theory, summarised in the Congress report as the "six musts". The third turns to practical guidance for the China Society for CPC Documents Research.

In Yang's reading, the six musts are: put the people first; stay confident in our own path and self-reliant; uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground; be problem-oriented; adopt a systems approach; and keep the world in view. Each is tied to a Marxist root: people-centredness to historical materialism, self-confidence to concrete analysis of concrete conditions, and a systems approach to the core of materialist dialectics. Yang holds that the people's stand is the most fundamental, since without it even sound-looking views and methods slide into idealism and subjectivism. This stand is presented as what distinguishes a Marxist party from other parties.

Yang proposes that researchers explain which stands, viewpoints and methods the Party has used across its work, why, how, with what results, and with what consequences if they were abandoned. Exposition should treat the three as one whole, with stand determining viewpoint and both shaping method. It should rest on primary documents, be mainly positive but include comparison and rebuttal of erroneous positions, and speak to current public concerns in plain language. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-affiliated documents researcher sets out the political and methodological tasks of Party literature research after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Among these six aspects, upholding the materialist conception of history in which the people create history, putting the people at the centre, and doing everything for and relying on the people is the most fundamental. Without this foundation, even seemingly good views and methods will go wrong and slide into idealism and subjectivism.
quoteZh: 在以上六个方面中，坚持人民创造历史的唯物史观，坚持以人民为中心，坚持一切为了人民、一切依靠人民，这是最根本的东西，离开了这个根本，看似很好的观点和方法也会出问题，会滑向唯心主义和主观主义。

glossary.explanation: A standard Party formula for the Marxist stance, way of seeing and way of working that leaders are expected to apply. The 20th Party Congress report stressed it as running through Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six principles in the 20th Party Congress report (2022): put the people first, be self-confident and self-reliant, uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground, be problem-oriented, adopt a systems approach, and keep the world in view.

t: On Marcuse's defence of Hegel's thought
zh: 论马尔库塞为黑格尔思想的辩护
source: Foreign Social Sciences (Guowai shehui kexue), 2022 no. 2
paras: Herbert Marcuse's Reason and Revolution: Hegel and the Rise of Social Theory was written when Hegel's rationalism was under suspicion, since Nazism claimed his philosophy as a foundation. Gao and Zhu ask how Marcuse defended Hegel, and what that defence shows about the relation between Hegel and Marx. They argue that Marcuse recovers the critical and revolutionary side of Hegel's reason and thereby defends Marxist philosophy. They also argue that his reading stays at the level of Hegelian speculation and misses the philosophical revolution Marx carried out.

The authors say Chinese scholarship has paid the book too little attention, because Marcuse soon turned to comparing Marx and Freud. They examine the book through the dialectic between reason and history and between reason and reality. The article is organised into four themes in Marcuse's defence: the universality of reason, its historicity, its actuality, and its dialectic. A short conclusion follows.

Gao and Zhu report that Marcuse reads Hegel's reason as a universal principle that rebuilds unity after Kant's split between subject and object. It becomes a historical force, so that Hegel brings history into idealist philosophy. Marcuse also reads Hegel's actuality as the unity of essence and existence, so that "the real is rational" carries a hidden critical edge. Through the negativity of dialectic, Marcuse links Hegel to Marx, since both treat negation as the essence of reason.

The authors then criticise this reading. In their account, Marcuse and Hegel treat actuality as abstract reason, whereas Marx treats it as concrete human activity. Marcuse's dialectic begins and ends in reason, while Marx's begins and ends in real people and their practice. Marcuse stresses Hegel's continuity with Marx rather than the break between them. The authors conclude that Marx's ontological transformation of Hegel's dialectic turned the dialectic of reason into a dialectic of practice and made the "revolution of reason" real. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist assessment of Reason and Revolution and of how Marcuse relates Hegel to Marx.
quoteEn: The starting point and end point of Marcuse's dialectic are both reason, whereas the starting point and end point of Marx's dialectic are both real human beings and their activity.
quoteZh: 马尔库塞辩证法的起点和终点都是理性，而马克思辩证法的起点和终点都是现实的人及其活动。

t: Capital, world history and communism as a trinity
st: An examination of Capital and its manuscripts
zh: 资本、世界历史与共产主义的三位一体
zhSub: 《资本论》及其手稿的一个考察
paras: Liu Jingdong asks what historical structure underlies Marx's critique of capital and of political economy. The article argues that Capital and its manuscripts contain a three-part scheme, "capital, world history and communism", in which capital's mode of production and the world market, through their own crises and self-sublation, form the historical bridge to a communist association of free individuals. Liu presents this as the basic structure of Marx's capital theory and, more broadly, of his whole theory of society and history.

The article has four main sections plus a conclusion. It begins with Marx's plans for his economic work, in the 1857–58 Manuscripts, the 1858 letter to Engels and the Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy. It then turns to the world market and crisis, to the self-sublation of capitalist ownership and the re-establishment of individual property, and to credit, joint-stock companies and banking in Volume III. The last substantive section covers the transition from the realm of necessity to the realm of freedom. Liu supports each step with extended quotations from Marx.

Liu's central claim is that Marx's concept of capital has a double character, historical and class-based. Historically, capital's drive for surplus value creates the world market, develops needs and capacities, and lays the material basis for communism. In class terms, capital exploits labour, and the "freedom" of the wage-worker is only formal. Liu reads Marx's three social forms (personal dependence, dependence on things, free individuality) as the same scheme. Liu also argues that Marx saw joint-stock companies, credit, banking and workers' cooperative factories as transitional forms in which capitalism sublates itself within its own limits. In Liu's account Marx also warned against overstating this, and criticised Proudhon's hopes for reform through credit. Revolution by the proletariat is still required.

Liu concludes that, across the manuscripts, letters and volumes of Capital, Marx traced a consistent logic by which capital's self-sublation on the world market leads to communism. Liu also holds that Marx exposed the claim that capital or free competition is eternal as a bourgeois myth, an early critique of the "end of history" idea. Read the original if you want a close, text-based reconstruction of how Marx's writing plans and quotations from Capital are used to support a unified reading of capital, world history and communism.
quoteEn: The ultimate aim of Marx in creating his theory of capital was to envision a communist society, an association of free individuals founded on the principles of free individuality and human emancipation.
quoteZh: 马克思创制资本理论的最终目标，是展望以自由个性和人类解放为原则的自由人联合体的共产主义社会。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: the overcoming of something by negating it while retaining elements of it in a higher form.

glossary.en: realm of necessity to the realm of freedom
glossary.literal: kingdom of necessity and kingdom of freedom
glossary.explanation: Marx's distinction in Capital Volume III between labour imposed by material necessity and the free development of human capacities beyond it. The article treats it as the shape of the transition from capitalism to communism.
Marx's term in Capital Volume I for property re-established after capitalism on the basis of cooperation and common possession of the means of production. Chinese scholars debate its exact meaning.
Marx's image of communist society as a voluntary association in which free development of each is the condition for the free development of all.

t: The young Marx's inversion and transformation of Hegel's conception of philosophy
zh: 青年马克思对黑格尔哲学观问题的颠倒和转换
paras: How did Marx move beyond Hegel's abstract and inverted view of what philosophy is, and bring German philosophy "down from heaven to earth"? Lü Shirong takes up this question through the young Marx's treatment of Hegel's "problem of the conception of philosophy". The article argues that Marx first inverted that conception and then transformed it. Marx thereby left Hegel's framework of absolute spirit and turned philosophy towards real social problems, though the author stresses that the task was not yet complete in the early works.

The article has four sections. The first reconstructs Hegel's conception of philosophy as the culmination of traditional Platonic metaphysics and as a distinctively "German metaphysics" tied to Germany's backward transition from feudalism to capitalism. The second covers Marx's student-period legal-metaphysics experiment, his doctoral dissertation and his notes on Epicurus. The third turns to the Rheinische Zeitung articles of 1842–43. The fourth examines the Kreuznach notes, the critique of Hegel's philosophy of right and the introduction to that critique.

Lü holds that Hegel kept the Platonist opposition between a supersensible and a sensible world, and that Marx's dissertation began to invert it by affirming the reality of the sensible world and the activity of thought towards it. In the newspaper articles Marx then moved philosophy into political practice on behalf of "the people". He turned Hegel's "dialectic of concepts" into a "dialectic of practice", giving it a materialist content. In the Kreuznach notes Marx performs an "ontological reduction" of Hegel's philosophy of right: Hegel made the idea of the state the subject and real existence its predicate. Marx reverses this, so that family and civil society determine the state. Lü reads Marx's critique of political emancipation as exposing Hegel's metaphysics as a theoretical support for bourgeois rule, and as pointing to the proletariat's human emancipation.

Lü concludes that the young Marx turned Hegel's abstract speculation about the age into a new conception of philosophy that engages reality directly. He also began to show how rational metaphysics is bound up with German bourgeois domination, and so started building his own philosophy on the ground of real society. The author adds that Marx had not yet given a fully historical-materialist account of reason, the state and right. Read the original if you study the early Marx–Hegel relationship, the Kreuznach notes or the genesis of Marx's materialist turn, and want a systematic Chinese reading organised around "conception of philosophy".
quoteEn: If Hegel sought, in his head, to construct philosophy as the truth about a "supersensible world", Marx forged philosophy in the real world into a "wisdom of the human world".
quoteZh: 如果说黑格尔是在头脑中意图将哲学构造为关于“超感性世界”的真理，那么马克思则是在现实世界中将哲学锻造为“人世的智慧”。

t: Engels's conception of nature and his outstanding contribution to Marxism
zh: 恩格斯自然观对马克思主义的卓越贡献
paras: Zhou Ye and Zhu Yao ask what Engels's view of nature added to Marxism. They argue that Engels moved from "empirical natural science" to "theoretical natural science". By using materialist dialectics to explain, know and transform nature, they say, he revealed general laws common to nature, human society and thought, and brought about a major change in the history of natural science.

The article is organised in four parts. The first treats Engels's definitions of matter, motion, time and space. The second turns to the three basic laws of materialist dialectics as Engels set them out. The third examines his historical-materialist account of primitive society, and the fourth his dialectics of nature on the relation between humans, nature and society. Evidence comes mainly from Anti-Dühring, Dialectics of Nature, The German Ideology and The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State.

In the authors' reading, Engels refused to treat matter as a contemplated "pure object". He grounded it in human practice, and defined motion as matter's mode of existence and time and space as its forms of existence. The authors present the three laws as the transformation of quantity into quality, the interpenetration of opposites, and the negation of the negation. They stress that Engels drew examples from mechanics, physics, chemistry and biology, and understood negation as sublation, a unity of overcoming and preserving. On society, they discuss Engels's "two kinds of production", meaning the production of the means of life and the production of human beings themselves. These explain how kinship-based clan society gave way to private property, classes and the state.

The authors also highlight Engels's claim that "labour created man" and his warning that nature takes revenge for human victories over it. From this they draw a principle of "two elevations" of humanity. People must come to understand natural laws and the consequences of intervening in nature, and must also come to grasp and regulate the indirect social effects of production. Only then, the authors say, does human society pass from a spontaneous to a conscious stage, and humans become true subjects of natural history. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language overview of Engels's dialectics of nature, with extensive quotation from his texts.
quoteEn: In Engels's view, natural science is the science of human beings, and natural science and the human sciences stand in a relation of harmonious unity.
quoteZh: 自然科学就是人的科学，自然科学与人的科学是和谐统一的关系。

t: Marx forever: commemorating the 205th anniversary of Marx's birth
zh: 永远的马克思——纪念马克思诞辰205周年​
paras: Hao Guisheng, a professor at Tianjin Normal University, writes a commemorative essay on the anniversary of Marx's birth. It presents Marx as the greatest leader and teacher of the world's proletariat and working people. The author's thesis is that Marx's life had three defining features, learning, struggle and innovation, and that all three carry direct lessons for Chinese Communists today.

The essay is organised as three biographical sections followed by practical conclusions. The first follows Marx's learning from childhood and the Trier school, through Bonn and Berlin and his doctoral thesis on Democritus and Epicurus, to his work on the Rheinische Zeitung. It then covers political economy and the writing of Capital, and his late studies in mathematics, world history and early society. The second section surveys his struggles against feudal absolutism, the Young Hegelians, Proudhon, reactionary governments, poverty and various opportunists. The third presents his theoretical innovations.

In Hao's account, Marx's learning was driven by a sense of mission to serve humanity and by the principle that theory must engage with life. His struggle, in Engels's words, was his "element". Hao names as his two great discoveries the materialist conception of history and the theory of surplus value, which Hao says turned socialism from utopia into science. Hao attributes Marx's capacity for innovation to three causes: critical inheritance of earlier culture, revolutionary practice, and the vantage point that historical materialism provided.

Hao draws three lessons for Chinese Communists. First, the Party should launch another campaign to "reform our study", on the model of Mao Zedong's 1942 call, since the author sees the Party and society as impatient, utilitarian and poor at studying Marxism. Second, they should join the struggle between socialism and capitalism, which the author says persists. Hao argues that this means guarding against capitalist restoration, returning to the people power that has degenerated, and fighting opportunism and revisionism inside the Party. Third, innovation must rest on inheritance and on practice in class struggle. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-rich biographical survey of Marx that is also an example of a hard-left Chinese reading of Party tasks today.
quoteEn: Without learning and practical struggle in the true sense, there can absolutely be no innovation in the true sense.
quoteZh: 没有真正意义上的学习和实践斗争，就绝对没有真正意义上的创新。

t: Four dimensions for understanding the distinctive features of Chinese modernization and its world-historical significance
zh: 理解中国式现代化特质及其世界历史意义的四重维度
paras: Sun Leqiang takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the study session on the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022). The commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks how Chinese modernization and its world-historical significance should be understood. Sun argues that this requires a 'grand view of history', a world-historical perspective, China's own autonomy and a comparison with the Western path.

The piece is organised around four paired dialectical relations: understanding China from China, China from the world, the world from China, and the world from the world. Each pair is treated in a short section, and together they move from China's historical continuity to global debates about modernization.

In Sun's account, Chinese modernization cannot be understood within a single period. It is rooted in traditional Chinese culture and tied to Party leadership and the adaptation of Marxism to China, so it must be placed in the long sweep of Chinese history. Sun contends that the Western path is only one national path, characterised as capital-centred, polarising, materialist and expansionist. The 'modernization equals Westernization' narrative is therefore a myth, and Chinese modernization, with its five features set out in the 20th Party Congress report, shows that modernization takes plural forms. Sun adds that it sublates the defects of the Western model and offers a new form of human civilisation, citing a community with a shared future for mankind and whole-process people's democracy.

Sun concludes that historical materialism gives the unity of history, while concrete paths are diverse. Western modernization began world history but will not complete it, and Chinese modernization is said to represent the direction of human progress. Sun predicts that a new pattern breaking out of the capitalist world system will inevitably arrive. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese theorists frame Chinese modernization against Western modernization in 2023.
quoteEn: The path to modernization is by no means singular but plural.
quoteZh: 现代化道路绝不是单一的，而是多元的

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's path to modernization, developed under Xi Jinping and set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A term used in Xi Jinping's discourse for assessing events within long historical spans and a global frame, instead of short periods.
The official description of China's democratic system, put forward by Xi Jinping. It stresses people's participation at every stage of the political process.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's foreign-policy vision, centred on cooperation and shared interests.
The Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: to negate something while preserving and raising its valuable elements.

t: The historical logic of the exploration of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化探索的历史逻辑
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks how Chinese modernization came about historically. Chen argues that it is a great creation of the Communist Party of China, produced by successive generations of Party members who explored, opened up and extended it. Chen presents it as the only road to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The piece draws on Xi Jinping's speech at the study session on the 20th Party Congress (2022).

The article follows four periods in turn. These are the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. For each, Chen names the condition it supplied for modernization: social conditions, political prerequisites and material foundations, institutional vitality, and finally a more complete institutional, material and spiritual base.

Chen argues that each stage built on the one before. The revolution ended semi-colonial, semi-feudal society and won national independence. After 1949 the basic socialist system, the Two Integrations' precursor of a 'second integration' of Marxism with Chinese conditions, and an independent industrial system laid the foundations. Deng Xiaoping's idea of a moderately prosperous society and the 'three-step' strategy then combined socialism with the market economy. For the new era, Chen credits Xi with a theoretical system that surpasses neoliberalism and dependency theory and breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization. Chen also points to strategic plans and to practical results such as the elimination of absolute poverty.

Chen concludes that practice has proved Chinese modernization to be the Party's creation and the necessary road to national rejuvenation. Only by keeping to it, the author says, can that rejuvenation be achieved. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-aligned scholarship narrates Chinese modernization as a continuous, staged historical process.
quoteEn: Only by always adhering to the path of Chinese modernization can the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation be achieved.
quoteZh: 只有始终坚持中国式现代化道路,才能实现中华民族伟大复兴。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, given prominence at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, closely associated with Xi Jinping since 2012.
The official name for the Party's theory and system since reform and opening up, which combines socialism with a market economy and Chinese conditions.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the world launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
Deng Xiaoping's term for a modest level of material well-being, used as a staged development target.

t: New features of mass work and the growth of young cadres
zh: 群众工作新特点与年轻干部成长研究
paras: Sun Yingshuai takes up the question of how the Party's mass line and mass work must adapt to new conditions, and what this means for young cadres. Starting from the premise that the mass line is the Party's lifeline, Sun argues that the transformation of the principal contradiction and the spread of the internet have changed the environment of mass work. Young cadres, who are more attuned to the internet, are said to be well placed to build an online–offline "concentric circle" of mass work.

The article was published in People's Forum in 2022. It identifies four features of mass work in the new era: online mass work as a new model of public governance; truthfulness, speed, openness and transparency as new requirements; the coordination of group interests as the new normal; and the need to eradicate bureaucratism and formalism by putting the people first. Sun draws on internet-usage and education statistics, and on cases such as the Fengxian incident, the Zhengzhou "7·20" rainstorm, the Baiyin ultramarathon deaths and the MU5735 crash.

Sun's first move is to argue that, with 1.032 billion internet users by December 2021 according to the article's figures, gaps in information access between young, old and rural users are narrowing. Mass work therefore now spans physical and virtual society, and the pressure of analysing and guiding public opinion has grown. Officials, Sun says, must be willing to speak out, speak promptly and speak truthfully, or face a "crisis of trust". The second move turns to the principal contradiction: disputes over lift installation, neighbourhood clean-ups, epidemic controls and family matters show that mediating among diverse interests is now routine, and that small matters can become public incidents online.

Sun concludes that bureaucratism and formalism, although curbed, persist and must be tackled by keeping the people at the centre, feeling for the masses and judging achievements by popular experience. Cadres should also avoid arbitrary decisions and wait patiently until the majority are ready for reform. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of internet-era mass work, with domestic cases of public-opinion handling and community mediation.
quoteEn: Online mass work has become a new model of public governance in the new era.
quoteZh: 网络群众工作已成为新时代公共治理的新模式。

glossary.explanation: The Party's fundamental working method, developed under Mao Zedong, of drawing ideas from the masses and returning them as policy. Official texts call it the Party's lifeline.
The everyday work of Party members and cadres in communicating with, serving and mobilising ordinary people, including mediating disputes and responding to concerns.
In the official formulation since the 19th Party Congress (2017), the contradiction between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
Official terms for faults in Party work style: detachment from the people and empty, box-ticking performance of tasks. Campaigns against them have been a recurring theme of Party discipline.

t: Chinese-style democracy as inheritance and development of the Marxist view of democracy
zh: 中国式民主对马克思主义民主观的继承和发展
paras: Sun Yingshuai asks how democracy as practised under the Communist Party of China relates to the Marxist conception of democracy. The article argues that over more than a century the Party has held to the essential content of that conception while adapting it to China's revolution, construction and reform. In Sun's account, this produced Chinese-style democracy, which unites democracy with dictatorship, democracy with centralism, procedural with substantive democracy, and the people's democracy with the will of the state. The article opens with Xi Jinping's remark of October 2021 that democracy is a common value of all humanity.

The article is organised around three themes: the substance of democracy (from class democracy to people's democracy), its guiding principle (from "complete democracy" to democratic centralism) and its forms (from representative democracy to whole-process people's democracy). Sun draws on Marx and Engels, on Lenin's Soviet experience, and on Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. Historical illustrations include Athenian democracy, the bourgeois Enlightenment thinkers Locke, Montesquieu and Rousseau, the Paris Commune and the 1954 Chinese constitution.

On substance, Sun argues that Marx used historical materialism and class analysis to show earlier democracies, from slave-owning Athens to bourgeois states, to be democracies of a minority. Marx treated democracy as a question of the state and held that the proletariat must win rule to realise majority democracy. Sun presents Mao's analysis of China's classes and the doctrine of "people's democratic dictatorship" as widening the proletarian base to an alliance of workers, peasants and other classes. On principle, Sun traces Marx's elected and recallable organisation, Lenin's centralism, and the Chinese formula of "centralism on the basis of democracy, democracy under centralised guidance", noting that the Russian term stresses centralism. On form, Sun treats the people's congress system, the political consultative conference and consultative democracy as realising the Commune's principle of combining legislative and executive work.

Sun concludes that whole-process people's democracy, put forward since the 18th Party Congress (2012), completes this line of development. As evidence, the article cites direct election of over 90 per cent of county- and township-level deputies by more than one billion voters, and more than 3 million suggestions on over 200 draft laws. Sun holds that Chinese-style democracy goes beyond "minority democracy" and "one-off democracy" and ensures that the people are masters of the country. Read the original if you want a Party-theoretical account of how Chinese scholars link Marx, Lenin and Mao to the official concept of whole-process people's democracy.
quoteEn: Democratic centralism, as the fundamental organisational principle and leadership system of the Party and the state, is an important mark distinguishing Marxist parties from other parties.
quoteZh: 民主集中制作为党和国家的根本组织原则和领导制度，是马克思主义政党区别于其他政党的重要标志。

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2019 and written into Party documents from 2021. Official sources use it to describe democracy that spans elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight, not only voting.
The organisational principle of Leninist parties and of the Chinese state, combining internal discussion with binding unity of action. Sun notes the Russian original stresses centralism.

Mao Zedong's 1949 formula for the state form of the People's Republic, led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance. It is democratic for the people and applies dictatorship to hostile forces.
China's fundamental political institution, a system of congresses from the national to the local level. The constitution designates the National People's Congress the highest organ of state power.

The practice of consultation among the Party, other parties, social groups and citizens before decisions, centred on the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. Official texts present it as a distinctive form of socialist democracy.
A principle drawn from Marx's account of the Paris Commune, in which the representative body both makes and carries out laws. It is contrasted with the separation of powers.

t: Engels's view of nature and its outstanding contribution to Marxism
zh: 恩格斯自然观对马克思主义的卓越贡献
paras: This article asks what Engels's conception of nature added to Marxism. Zhou and Zhu argue that Engels moved from "empirical natural science" to "theoretical natural science", using materialist dialectics to explain, understand and transform nature. In their account, this revealed the general laws governing nature, human society and thought, and brought a major change in the history of natural science.

The article is organised in four parts, each based on Engels's texts, chiefly Anti-Dühring, Dialectics of Nature, The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, and The German Ideology. It covers his definition of matter and its forms of existence; the three basic laws of materialist dialectics in nature; his account of primitive society through the theory of the "two kinds of production"; and his dialectic of nature as a way to understand the harmony of humans, nature and society.

On matter, the authors argue that Engels rejected old materialism's intuitive treatment of nature as a pure object. Matter is for him an abstraction grounded in human practice, existing as motion in space and time. The authors then present the laws of the transformation of quantity into quality, the interpenetration of opposites, and the negation of the negation, illustrated with Engels's examples from mechanics, physics and chemistry. Negation is read as sublation, an inner self-movement of things. In the history section, Zhou and Zhu stress that social systems are conditioned by both the production of the means of life and the production of human beings themselves. They set out the shift from blood-kin groups to class society and the state.

The final part reads Engels's "labour created man" thesis and his warning that nature takes revenge for each human victory over it as the basis of the unity of natural history and human history. The authors extract from this the principle of the "two elevations" of humanity: learning nature's laws and their consequences, and learning to control the wider social effects of production. They conclude that only then does society move from a spontaneous to a conscious stage, with humans becoming subjects of natural history. Read the original if you want a systematic, text-based survey of Engels's natural dialectics and its links to historical materialism as presented in Chinese scholarship.
quoteEn: Engels held that dialectical negation is not an arbitrary negation imposed from outside, but "sublation", a unity of overcoming and preservation.
quoteZh: 恩格斯认为，辩证的否定不是外部强加的随意的否定，而是“扬弃”，是克服和保存的统一。

glossary.explanation: The standard Chinese rendering of Hegel's Aufhebung: a negation that both cancels and preserves what it supersedes. The article uses it to describe dialectical negation in Engels.

Engels's formulation in the preface to The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State: the production of the means of life and the production of human beings themselves (reproduction of the species). Chinese textbooks use it to explain early social structures.

A label the authors give to Engels's idea that people must first understand nature's laws and the effects of their interventions, then understand and regulate the social effects of production. It is not a standard term in Engels's own text.

t: The "five-dimensional scale" for judging Marxism's guiding role in the ideological sphere
zh: 判定马克思主义在意识形态领域指导地位的“五维尺度”
paras: The Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) established upholding Marxism's guiding role in the ideological sphere as a fundamental system. Liang Jianxin asks how one can tell whether that role is actually being upheld. The article answers that socialist ideology rests on five fundamentals: theoretical foundation, ideals and convictions, values, moral concepts and discourse. These five are proposed as the dimensions of assessment, and other ideological phenomena are treated as their reflection.

Drawing on the 19th Party Congress report (2017), Liang compares the five to a building: theory is the foundation stone, ideals, values and morality are the pillars, and discourse is the outer decoration. The article has five main sections, one for each dimension. Each combines quotations from Marx, Engels, Lenin, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping with practical recommendations. It ends by arguing that the five together form a "five-pointed star".

On theory, Liang says Marxism must be explained in four ways: the Marxist rationale behind Party lines and policies; the claim that the Communist Party has no special interests of its own; Marxism's superiority over rival theories; and its contemporary relevance, illustrated by the response to Covid-19. On ideals, communism is presented as a direction of social development that is pursued through accumulated stages, and the author calls for resolving three tensions: individual existence and transcendence, the personal dream and the Chinese Dream, and the long-term and the staged. On values, the core socialist values must be tied together as abstract and concrete, theory and practice, individual and society. On morality, Liang draws on Engels's critique of eternal moral dogma and asks for a detailed system of moral norms, rooted in everyday life, that combines breadth with vanguard standards. On discourse, Liang argues that it must be practical, critical and of its time. The author cites the "universal values" discourse as a "discourse trap".

Liang concludes that judging whether Marxism's guiding role is upheld depends on action as well as words, and that the five dimensions must work as an organic whole. The article is a Party-theoretical text on ideological work. It writes in the official register and treats the contrast between Marxism and liberalism or individualism as settled. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese Marxist scholars operationalise the ideological-leadership system, or if you study Party discourse on values, morality and communication.
quoteEn: Theoretical foundation, ideals and convictions, values, moral concepts and discourse become the "five fundamentals" of ideology, and also the five dimensions for judging whether Marxism's guiding role in the ideological sphere is upheld.
quoteZh: 理论基础、理想信念、价值理念、道德观念、话语体系就成为意识形态的“五大根本”，也是辨识意识形态领域是否坚持马克思主义指导地位的五大维度

glossary.explanation: A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values at the national, societal and individual levels. It was formally put forward at the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012. It refers to national rejuvenation and the well-being of the people.

The system of concepts and language through which an ideology is expressed and spread. Chinese theorists often link it to the idea of "discourse power" (huàyǔquán), meaning the ability to shape public narratives.
Values such as freedom, democracy and human rights, claimed to apply to all humanity. Official Chinese writing often criticises the idea as a vehicle for promoting Western values.

t: The "five-dimensional scale" for judging whether Marxism guides the ideological sphere
zh: 判定马克思主义在意识形态领域指导地位的“五维尺度”
paras: Since the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) made upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere a fundamental system, Liang Jianxin asks how one can tell whether that position is actually being upheld. The article proposes a "five-dimensional scale": theoretical foundation, ideals and convictions, values, moral concepts and discourse. Liang argues that every other ideological phenomenon is a reflection or echo of these five fundamentals.

Liang derives the five from the 19th Party Congress (2017) call for a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power, which unites people in ideals, values and morality. Ideals, values and morality rest on a theoretical base and are expressed through a distinctive discourse. The article uses an architectural image: theory is the cornerstone, ideals, values and morality are the pillars, and discourse is the outer decoration. Five sections take each dimension in turn, drawing on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

On theory, Liang says Marxism must be explained under "four clarifications": the Marxist rationale behind Party policy, the claim that the Communist Party has no special interests of its own, Marxism's superiority over rival theories, and its contemporary relevance, illustrated by the response to Covid-19. On ideals, Liang defines communism as a direction of development, a revolutionary movement and a gradual accumulation of qualitative change, and says three relationships must be clarified. On values, morality and discourse, Liang says core socialist values must link the abstract to the concrete, theory to practice, and the individual to society. Morality needs a detailed system of moral norms (a "guiding principle" plus specific items) that is both broad and advanced. Discourse must be practical, critical and of its time. Liang cites the "universal values" discourse as a "discourse trap".

Liang concludes that the five dimensions together form a "five-pointed star" supporting Marxism's guiding position, and that the test lies in action as well as in what is said. Ideals must show in reform, development and improving livelihoods. Liang also calls for stronger international communication so that China's story can be told in terms Western audiences can accept. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese academic turns the abstract principle of Marxism's ideological leadership into a checklist of criteria.
quoteEn: Theoretical foundation, ideals and convictions, values, moral concepts and discourse become the "five fundamentals" of ideology, and also the five dimensions for judging whether Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere is upheld.
quoteZh: 理论基础、理想信念、价值理念、道德观念、话语体系就成为意识形态的“五大根本”，也是辨识意识形态领域是否坚持马克思主义指导地位的五大维度

glossary.zh: 马克思主义在意识形态领域的指导地位
glossary.pinyin: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì zài yìshí xíngtài lǐngyù de zhǐdǎo dìwèi
glossary.en: Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere
glossary.explanation: A principle of Party rule, listed as a fundamental system at the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee in 2019. It requires Marxism to be the guiding thought across ideology, education and culture.

A twelve-word set of values promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at the national, social and individual levels. They include prosperity, democracy, freedom, equality, patriotism and integrity.

t: The dual logic of Marx's study of capital
st: Between economic philosophy and economic anthropology
zh: 马克思研究资本问题的双重逻辑
source: Journal of Wuhan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 2
paras: Yan Hui asks what the theoretical and practical value of Marx's critique of capital is for the present, and argues that Marx approached capital through a dual logic. The author distinguishes economics, economic philosophy and economic anthropology as three dimensions of his inquiry, though Marx never named them so. Economic anthropology comes first logically, because Marx had already fixed the anthropological meaning of labour and capital before analysing them. Economic philosophy comes first in time, because it concerns the historical emergence of capitalism.

The article has three parts. The first reads Marx's early manuscripts, notably the excerpts from James Mill and the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, on money, alienation, species-being and communism. The second turns to Capital and the Grundrisse, covering the movement from commodity and money to surplus value, and the historical standing of capitalism. The third takes up the passage from economic anthropology to philosophical anthropology and the real road back to a "human world". Yan draws on Hegel, Weber and Marxist classics throughout.

Yan holds that economics alone, treated as value-neutral natural science, would make exploitation look like a natural law. Marx therefore added a value logic of what people "ought to do" to the fact logic of what they "can do". Capital is abstract and also concrete: it is the starting point from which commodity, money, class and state relations unfold. Yan reads the mystery of surplus value through the gap between labour-power and labour, and through the fact that workers advance their labour to the capitalist on credit. Capitalism is analysed as a value outlook, a mode of production and a social formation. It is progressive because it dissolves relations of personal dependence and builds a system of universal exchange, but it is historically limited. The shift from dependence on things to social dependence is placed in public ownership, where sociality is the premise of production and not its alienated result. Yan also develops a threefold account of time (natural, social and meaningful) and argues that rising productivity should expand free time.

Yan concludes that Marx's study of capital was never an end in itself. It was a means of uncovering the secret of exploitation and finding a basis for moving beyond capitalism towards communism. The sequence economic philosophy, economic anthropology, philosophical anthropology gives Marx's mode of thought, while the movement from lower to complete private ownership to communist public ownership gives the objective historical logic. The author describes Marx as both an idealist and a realist, and sees continuing significance in his philosophical anthropology in an age of globalization. Read the original if you want a philosophical, early-Marx-centred reading of Capital that links alienation theory to the critique of political economy and to questions of public ownership and free time.
quoteEn: Returning labour to its original ethical-ontological status, and rebuilding the relations of objectification and mutual confirmation among the worker, the labour process and the product, so that labour goes beyond its economic meaning and acquires economic-anthropological and philosophical-anthropological significance, is the fundamental task of communism.
quoteZh: 将劳动回归到其初始的伦理本体地位，通过重建劳动者、劳动过程、劳动产品之间的对象性和印证关系，使劳动超越它的经济意义，而获得经济人类学和哲学人类学意义，乃是共产主义的根本任务。

glossary.explanation: The author's label for the value-laden dimension of Marx's analysis of capital. It concerns the human meaning of labour, property and exchange, and what people ought to do, beyond the factual laws of economics.
In this article, the philosophical study of how capital and capitalist society arise and develop historically. It mediates between economics and anthropology.
The author's term for the highest level of Marx's reasoning, where communism is conceived as the human being's return to its social essence.
The author's term for the world Marx envisages after alienation is overcome, in which people produce and enjoy as human beings and own their social essence.

t: Marx's idea of "species-being" and its contemporary value
st: Based on the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
zh: 马克思的“类存在”思想及其当代价值
zhSub: 基于《1844年经济学哲学手稿》
paras: Marx rarely uses the vocabulary of the "species" in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, yet Wu Ning and Li Xinglin argue that a developed idea of "species-being" runs through the text and survives the formation of Marx's new materialist worldview. The article claims that Marx took the terminology from Feuerbach but gave it a different foundation and content. It also holds that this idea has practical value today for building a community with a shared future for mankind.

The article has three parts. The first traces the idea from Feuerbach's concept of the species to Marx's transformation of it, and answers critics, above all Louis Althusser and his thesis of an "epistemological break". The second reconstructs the content of species-being through three categories: species-relations, species-characteristics and species-essence. The third draws out the idea's contemporary significance.

The authors' central contrast is that Feuerbach understands the species through consciousness, feeling and religion, and stays abstract, while Marx locates it in free, conscious labour and objectifying practice. On this reading, species-being is not given by nature but forms through human practice, in two relations: with nature and with society. The authors say Althusser mistook Marx's Feuerbachian vocabulary for Feuerbachian humanism and overlooked the role of labour, so his "two Marxes" is, in their view, a misreading. They argue that the early and later Marx are continuous, and that Marx's early exploration made his later thought more mature. They also hold that alienated labour reduces people to creatures of physical need and one-dimensional existence, which restricts their all-round development.

The authors conclude that species-being offers a way of thinking for the community with a shared future for mankind. In their account it stresses openness, inclusiveness and unity, and treats the individual and the species as a dialectical pair in which each enriches the other. They argue that it asks states to tolerate differences of system and culture while seeking deeper unity through mutual learning, and that it points to reconciliation between humanity and nature. They present the community with a shared future as a concrete application of Marx's idea in Chinese reality.
