Read the original if you want a Chinese reading of the 1844 Manuscripts that rejects Althusser's break thesis and links species-being to current Chinese foreign-policy language.
quoteEn: Marx regarded labour practice as the species-essence of human beings, and it was precisely labour practice that separated Marx from every abstract humanist theory and laid a solid foundation for historical materialism.
quoteZh: 马克思认为劳动实践是人的类本质，正是劳动实践活动使得马克思与一切抽象人道主义理论划清界限，为历史唯物主义奠定了坚实基础。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013. It calls for countries to pursue shared development and cooperation despite differences in systems and cultures.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Advancing the Party's self-reform with a great spirit of historical initiative
zh: 以伟大的历史主动精神推进党的自我革命
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, takes up the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to advance the Party's self-reform. Luo and Lin argue that, under new historical conditions, the Communist Party can complete its mission only if it pursues self-reform with a great spirit of historical initiative. They present willingness to reform itself as what marks the Party out from other parties.

The article builds its case around three requirements: historical consciousness, historical self-confidence and historical responsibility. Each is divided into two aspects and supported by quotations from Xi Jinping, the 2021 Party resolution on its century of struggle, and Marx.

On consciousness, the authors say the Party must grasp historical laws and put the people first, accepting supervision from the people and judging the results of self-reform by whether they approve. It must also hold to its founding mission and inherit its tradition of self-reform. On self-confidence, they hold that the Party's achievements and the historical experience set out in the resolution are the source of confidence, and that these must be fully summed up. On responsibility, they call for a clear reading of historical trends and of the Party's historical position, meaning the new era. They link this to the "great changes unseen in a century" and to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The authors conclude that the key to building a modern socialist country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation lies in the Party. They call on it to stay vigilant, rally around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, and so guide a "great social revolution". Read the original if you want a concise statement of how official Party discourse in 2023 framed self-reform in terms of historical initiative.
quoteEn: The Communist Party's hundred-year history is a history of self-reform carried out around seeking happiness for the people and rejuvenation for the nation.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的百年史就是一部围绕为人民谋幸福、为民族谋复兴而展开的自我革命史。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping: the Party's continuous effort to purify, improve and renew itself, presented as the second answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-building and anti-corruption drive launched after the 18th Party Congress (2012). It stresses strict discipline and supervision of Party members.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, tied to the Chinese Dream. It denotes restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Interpreting the classics and innovating discourse
zh: 经典诠释与话语创新
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 30 March 2023
paras: How should Chinese Marxists read the Marxist classics so that their language can renew itself? Writing in a newspaper commentary in March 2023, Shan argues that classical interpretation and discourse innovation form one process. Drawing on hermeneutics, Shan holds that interpretation must be historical, mediating and applied, and that it should aim at adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times rather than at repeating quotations.

The piece is built in three parts, each pairing a feature of interpretation with a feature of discourse innovation: historicity and the precondition of innovation; mediation and dialogue; application and practice. It engages Western hermeneutics (Schleiermacher's methodological hermeneutics, the idea of the text's autonomy, the limiting of interpretation to understanding and explanation). It also cites Xi Jinping, Engels, Lenin and Mao Zedong, and takes Chinese modernization as the main problem to which the classics are addressed.

Shan first rejects dogmatism and the ideal of returning wholly to an author's original meaning. Texts, authors and interpreters are all products of history, and interpreters carry the cultural tradition, including a Marxism that has by now become part of China's own pre-understanding. Second, interpretation is a dialogue organised around problems. Shan names the questions of modernization as today's problem field: whether it means Westernization, and whether it must bring polarisation, material supremacy and zero-sum competition. Marx's warning against turning his account of Western European capitalism into a universal philosophy of history is read as showing that modernization is not Westernization. Third, following Marx's emphasis on changing the world, Shan calls hermeneutics a practical philosophy in which understanding, explanation and application cannot be separated, and in which application is the core. Shan warns against pragmatism, which is said to use relative truth to deny absolute truth and so treat the classics as valid only for their own time.

Shan concludes that, in the new era, interpreters should return to the classics repeatedly, starting from the practice of Chinese modernization. In this way they can draw on the classics to generate innovation and use localised Marxist discourse to rally the people for building a modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese theorists use Western hermeneutics to justify reinterpreting Marxist texts in support of discourse innovation and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The source of discourse innovation is practice. Practice is the criterion for testing discourse innovation.
quoteZh: 话语创新的源头是实践。实践是检验话语创新的标准。

glossary.explanation: A Party formulation, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), for a modernization path led by the Communist Party and described as socialist, with a huge population, common prosperity, and harmony between humans and nature.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: An official formula for the Party's project of applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for the present era.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, usually tied to building a strong modern socialist country by the mid-twenty-first century.
The renewal of theoretical and political language so that Marxism can address new problems and persuade audiences in China.

t: Revisiting the claim that the logical starting-point category of Capital is the commodity "labour-power"
zh: 再论《资本论》逻辑起点范畴是“劳动力”商品
source: Journal of Hebei University of Economics and Business, 2023 no. 2
paras: Which category serves as the logical starting point of Marx's Capital? Cheng Hao and Cheng Yanjun argue that it is the commodity "labour-power", not the ordinary commodity as a "thing" analysed in the opening chapters. They call the first view the "thing-commodity theory" and their own the "labour-power commodity theory". In their account the choice decides whether Capital is read as a rigorous, scientific logical system of human emancipation, and it matters for building a political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics modelled on Capital.

The article surveys Hegel's Logic and Marx's remarks on method, and then recent Chinese scholarship on starting points. It sets out a broad meaning of "commodity" in Capital as a pair of categories, then criticises the thing-commodity theory for internal contradiction and vulgarity. It ends by outlining the content and significance of the labour-power theory. The authors also draw on the late statement of Wei Xinghua, a prominent Capital scholar, that the commodity cannot be the logical starting point of capitalist political economy.

The authors distinguish an "analytical starting point" from a "logical starting point". In their reading the opening analysis of the thing-commodity is only an "overture", while the labour-power commodity of the second part is the "main melody", to which the first part is subordinate. They hold that the two commodities form an opposed yet organically unified pair, and that the logical starting point must be unique. They argue that the thing-commodity existed long before capitalism and has no inherent emancipatory determination, so treating it as the starting point contradicts Capital's emancipatory and scientific character. They also say the thing-commodity theory ends up quietly substituting the capitalist mode of production, and so labour-power, for its own starting point. The authors tie this to Marx's path from "alienated labour" in the Paris Manuscripts to labour-power in Capital.

The authors summarise the labour-power theory as "one core, five key points" and link labour-power's emancipatory determination to the process of overcoming alienation, which they place in socialism and then communism. They connect this to the primary economic system of the Xi era, a public sector as the mainstay, and to common prosperity. They also sketch their own system built on "human-capital property rights" as a starting point. They call for more study of how Marx moved between 1844 and 1867 from "labour" and "alienated labour" to labour-power. Read the original if you work on the logic of Capital, on debates over its starting category, or on how Chinese economists draw on Marx's method to build a socialist political economy.
quoteEn: The inherent determination of the logical starting-point category is the "ground" on which a science's rigorous logical system is built.
quoteZh: 逻辑起点范畴的内在规定性是一门科学的严密逻辑体系建构“根据”

glossary.explanation: A goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics stressing shared wealth for all, given prominence in Party policy under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì zhèngzhì jīngjìxué
glossary.en: political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The effort to build a theoretical system of Marxist political economy that interprets China's reform-era economic practice.

t: Marx's critique of the "Holy Alliance" and the value concepts of a new world order
zh: 马克思对“神圣同盟”的批判与新型世界秩序的价值理念
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 10
paras: Lan Yang and Du Yue ask what Marx's analysis of the Holy Alliance, the conservative alliance of European monarchs formed after the French Revolution, can tell us about today's international order. They argue that the Alliance was a system of power, institutions and ideology, and that the US-led alliances and groupings of the present (NATO, the "Summit for Democracy", the Five Eyes, AUKUS) share its essence, whatever their outward differences. Against these they set a new type of international relations built on mutual respect, fairness and win-win cooperation.

The article has three parts. The first reads Marx's and Engels's remarks on the Holy Alliance through a historical-materialist "trinity" of power structure, institutional system and ideology. The second applies the same lens to contemporary hegemonic alliances. The third discusses the value concepts of a new world order, drawing on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and a community with a shared future for mankind. The authors rely on Marx's 1859 Preface, Engels's writings, Marx's articles on Poland and the Crimean War, and Gramsci's theory of hegemony.

On the Holy Alliance, the authors argue that its legitimist ideology was only the surface. Beneath it lay a balance-of-power arrangement meant to contain France, prop up Habsburg Austria and provide quasi-collective security. Its deepest basis was the combined dominance of British sea power and Russian land power, and the Crimean War marked its collapse. The authors treat this as a case of base and superstructure appearing "inverted", which historical materialism sets right. Applying this to the present, they say US-led alliances rest on capital's logic of accumulation and the core's domination of the periphery. They add that these alliances serve as institutional tools of a declining hegemon and rely on an exclusionary universalism. The authors list four features: conquest-based power politics, a disguised universalism, a confrontational centre–periphery structure and a hierarchical political order.

The authors contend that China's rejuvenation has world-historical significance because it replaces the principle of capital with that of labour, civilizational conflict with mutual learning, and zero-sum games with cooperation. They call for strengthening China's economic and technological base, deepening institutional innovation and global-governance participation, and building Chinese discourse. They also call for a community with a shared future for mankind, pursued through partnership without alliance. Power politics and zero-sum thinking, they conclude, have no future. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese Marxist scholars use Marx's nineteenth-century analysis of the Holy Alliance to interpret US alliance policy and justify China's vision of a new international order.
quoteEn: In short, China's peaceful rise opens a real path towards a higher form of civilization: it replaces the principle of capital with the principle of labour, supplants civilizational conflict with mutual learning among civilizations, and transcends zero-sum games through international cooperation.
quoteZh: 简言之，中国的和平崛起展开了一条通往更高文明形式的现实道路，它以劳动原则置换资本原则，以文明互鉴取代文明冲突，以国际合作超越零和博弈。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It calls for shared security, development and governance among states and is presented as an alternative to bloc politics.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream. It denotes China's restoration as a strong, prosperous and influential country.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Upholding the Two Integrations and continually opening up new horizons for Marxism
zh: 坚持“两个结合”，不断开辟马克思主义发展新境界
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in March 2023, Jin Nuo takes up a question that follows from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): how the Communist Party of China can keep Marxism vital while developing it. Jin's answer is the Two Integrations, which the article presents as the fundamental route for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times and as a key to the Party's success.

The commentary is built in three parts. The first explains why the Two Integrations are the basic path of adaptation, treating the link with China's concrete realities and the link with fine traditional Chinese culture in turn. The second reviews their significance across more than a century of Party history and for the present task of advancing Chinese modernization. The third sets out three requirements for further theoretical innovation.

Jin argues that Marxism is not a closed body of truth and cannot be treated as dogma, so it must be tied to national conditions in each period of revolution, construction and reform. It must also be tied to traditional culture, which Jin says shares a high degree of fit with the values of scientific socialism, so that Marxism takes root among the people and acquires distinct Chinese features. The article credits this method with Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It describes the last as a model of the Two Integrations, rooted in traditional culture and answering the major questions of the new era.

For the future, Jin calls for innovation that takes people's aspiration for a better life as its starting point and end point, keeps answering new questions, and gives theory distinctive Chinese features. The article names four sets of questions: those of China, the world, the people and the times. It links this work to common prosperity and to supporting Chinese modernization, which it calls a pioneering undertaking with unknown terrain and risks. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of how the Party presents the Two Integrations and the tasks of theoretical innovation after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The Two Integrations are the fundamental path by which we advance the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: “两个结合”是我们推进马克思主义中国化时代化的根本途径。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to the Party's official formulation by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of applying and developing Marxism in line with Chinese conditions and contemporary developments.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernisation, foregrounded in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A goal of prosperity shared by all, emphasised in official policy under Xi Jinping.

t: Bearing in mind the "five musts": steering the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics steadily into the future
zh: 牢记“五个必由之路”，引领新时代中国特色社会主义事业行稳致远
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in March 2023, takes up the "five musts" (wuge biyou zhi lu) that Xi Jinping put to the whole Party in his report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Jiang argues that they are the key to the historic achievements of the Party's first century and especially of the new era. In Jiang's reading, they express three qualities of Communists today: firm historical confidence, a high degree of theoretical consciousness and a strong sense of responsibility.

The article is organised in three parts that match these three qualities. The first reads the five principles as a summary of a hundred years of Party experience. The second treats them as a deepening of understanding of three laws: those governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and human social development. The third presents them as practical guidance for the future.

The first part takes each principle in turn. Jiang holds that the Party's overall leadership, socialism with Chinese characteristics, unity and struggle, the new development philosophy, and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party are each tied to the achievements of the Party's first century and the past decade. The second part assigns the principles to the three laws. Party leadership and self-governance are said to advance understanding of how Communist parties rule, including self-reform as the \"second answer\" to the historical cycle. Socialism with Chinese characteristics is said to enrich the laws of socialist construction. Unity and struggle and the new development philosophy are said to deepen understanding of the laws of social development, including the role of the people's state of mind.

In the third part Jiang calls on Communists to follow the five principles as a guide to action on the new journey towards the second centenary goal. Five tasks are set out. They are upholding Party leadership, the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds; innovating theory on the basis of practice; strengthening the patriotic united front and a sense of community among the Chinese nation; applying the new development philosophy to build a new development pattern and promote high-quality development; and continuing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 20th Congress formula was presented to a general Party readership in 2023.
quoteEn: The "five musts" deepen understanding of the laws of Communist Party rule, of socialist construction and of human social development, and reflect the high degree of theoretical consciousness of Communists in the new era.
quoteZh: “五个必由之路”深化了对共产党执政规律、社会主义建设规律、人类社会发展规律的认识，体现了新时代中国共产党人高度的理论自觉。

glossary.explanation: Five principles set out in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): Party leadership, socialism with Chinese characteristics, unity and struggle, the new development philosophy, and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The report calls them essential insights drawn from long practice.
A Party formula, adopted in 2021, that affirms Xi Jinping's status as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
A philosophy announced in 2015 that stresses innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development. It serves as a guiding framework for economic policy.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The label for Xi Jinping-era efforts to tighten Party discipline, including the anti-corruption campaign.
An official goal for the economy that puts quality, efficiency and innovation ahead of rapid growth alone.

t: Accurately grasping the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
zh: 准确把握习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的世界观和方法论
paras: This commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, takes up a line from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): that theoretical innovation must begin by grasping the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Shen Jiangping argues that this formulation lifts the Thought to the philosophical level and distils its theoretical essence. In Shen's reading, it is a concentrated expression of contemporary Chinese Marxism and opens a new realm for Marxist worldview and methodology.

The article has two parts. The first traces the sources of this worldview and methodology: inheritance from Marxist philosophy, development of earlier Sinicized Marxism, and nourishment from fine traditional Chinese culture. The second sets out its theoretical significance under three headings: innovating Marxist worldview and methodology, guiding the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and advancing world governance and human civilization.

Shen holds that the worldview is not self-generated but rests on dialectical and historical materialism, and that it continues the Party's long practice of summarising each period's theoretical innovation at the level of worldview and method, with seeking truth from facts as the constant stance. The "six must-haves" are presented as the essence and soul of the Thought and as its stance, viewpoint and method. Shen also says that concepts from traditional culture, such as harmony between humanity and nature, the people as the foundation of the state, and good-neighbourliness, are fused into this worldview through the Two Integrations, giving Marxism Chinese features.

Shen concludes that grasping this worldview is the precondition and applying it the key. The author calls on the whole Party to study the 20th Congress in this way, to arm minds and guide practice, and to keep advancing theoretical innovation so that the Party's cause stays on course. The article also presents the worldview as relevant beyond China, through the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary justifies the claim that the Thought is a philosophical advance in Marxism.
quoteEn: The 20th Party Congress put forward the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; grasping it is the precondition, and applying it is the key.
quoteZh: 党的二十大提出习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的世界观和方法论，把握是前提，运用是关键。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six principles set out in the 20th Congress report as the stance, viewpoint and method of the Thought: put the people first, have self-confidence and self-reliance, uphold fundamental principles and break new ground, maintain a problem-oriented approach, apply systematic thinking, and stand with humanity.

The formula that Marxism's basic principles must be combined with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in official discourse in 2021–2023.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept for a world of shared interests and cooperation. It is promoted in Party documents as China's contribution to global governance.
A classical phrase made a core principle of Mao Zedong's thought and of Party ideology. It stresses starting from actual conditions rather than from doctrine.

t: Communism as a "real movement" is by no means illusory
st: Viewed through Lenin's "A Great Beginning"
zh: 作为“现实运动”的共产主义绝非虚无缥缈
zhSub: 以列宁《伟大的创举》为观察视角
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 9
paras: Fan Xin takes up Lenin's 1919 pamphlet "A Great Beginning", written after Pravda reported that Moscow–Kazan railway workers had launched voluntary "communist subbotniks". The article asks what the text shows about communism and answers that communism is a "real movement" visible in actual labour, not a distant fantasy. Fan uses this to rebut the claim that communism is "illusory" (the "vague and remote" thesis).

The article has three parts. The first reads Lenin's three quoted Pravda reports as evidence of a concrete form of communist labour organisation and spirit. The second examines why Lenin saw labour productivity as the decisive ground of competition between social systems, and how the pamphlet treats the two stages of communist society. The third turns to the Chinese Communist Party's own statements on communism, from Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping, and to the setbacks and recovery of socialism since 1989–91.

Fan argues that earlier scholarship either treated the pamphlet as a description of subbotniks or simply stressed raising productivity. In Fan's reading, Lenin's real point is that the proletarian dictatorship must embody a higher type of social labour organisation than capitalism, and that this guarantees communism's victory. Fan reads Lenin's definition of communism as higher labour productivity created by voluntary, associated workers using advanced technology. Lenin also shows how voluntary initiative can break the "vicious circle" between hunger and productivity. Lenin's caution that subbotniks could not yet be universal, and that the work is long-term, is presented as proof that communists are not utopians.

Fan concludes that Lenin's lesson of nurturing the "shoots" of the new remains relevant. Citing Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping, Fan holds that building socialism with Chinese characteristics is already a practical step towards the highest ideal. Fan also contends that socialism's setbacks, including the Soviet collapse, are temporary twists in a historical trend. The article calls for firmer ideals, a proletarian character in state power and higher labour productivity. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar links Lenin's text to official Party discourse on communist ideals and the "illusory communism" argument.
quoteEn: This is Lenin's incisive interpretation of the historical-materialist principle that, under certain conditions, spirit can play a decisive role.
quoteZh: 这是列宁对历史唯物主义关于精神在一定条件下能起决定作用原理的精辟解读。

glossary.zh: 共产主义星期六义务劳动
glossary.explanation: Unpaid voluntary work on Saturdays that began among Moscow–Kazan railway workers in 1919 during the Russian Civil War. Lenin praised it as a seed of new communist labour discipline.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up. The Party presents it as adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions.

t: Upholding and developing Marxism requires integrating it with China's fine traditional culture
zh: 坚持和发展马克思主义，必须同中华优秀传统文化相结合
paras: This short commentary, published in People's Daily in April 2023, explains why the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) stated that upholding and developing Marxism must be combined with fine traditional Chinese culture. Zhang argues that this principle deepens the Party's understanding of how to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that it shows cultural confidence and cultural awareness.

The piece opens with quotations from Xi Jinping and the Congress report, then moves through the historical conditions for Marxism's reception in China, the influence of traditional culture on China's path, institutions and governance, and the task ahead. It is built largely around Xi's statements.

Zhang's central claim is that Marxism took root in China not by chance but because it resonated with values handed down over thousands of years. In this reading, the values of fine traditional culture closely match those of scientific socialism, which makes the combination possible. Zhang cites Xi's view that socialism with Chinese characteristics carries a cultural "gene", and argues that traditional ideas such as "the world belongs to all" and "the people are the foundation of the state" feed the country's institutions, governance system and the core socialist values. Marxism, Zhang says, gains Chinese style from this culture, while the culture gains new content from Marxism.

Zhang calls for stronger historical and cultural confidence and a deeper understanding of the Two Integrations. The commentary urges drawing out the philosophy, humanistic spirit, values and moral norms of traditional culture, so that the Party's innovative theory acquires distinctive Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how the cultural integration is justified in Party theory around the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Sinicized Marxism gains more Chinese characteristics, style and manner by fully drawing on the distinctive features and essence of fine traditional Chinese culture; fine traditional culture, in turn, acquires new features, spirit and content of the times through the truth-power of Marxism.
quoteZh: 中国化马克思主义因充分汲取中华优秀传统文化的特质和精华而更加具有中国特色、中国风格、中国气派；中华优秀传统文化因马克思主义的真理力量而具有新的时代特征、时代精神、时代内涵。

glossary.explanation: Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to Party theory by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023.
The Party's official name for its path, system and theory since the early reform era.
Official term for confidence in China's own cultural tradition and socialist culture, emphasised under Xi Jinping.

t: A scientific-atheist interpretation of Engels's contradiction between the "expected" and the "unexpected"
zh: 恩格斯“预期与非预期”矛盾的科学无神论诠释
source: Science and Atheism (科学与无神论), 2023 no. 1
paras: Engels observed late in life that the purposes of human actions are anticipated while the results they actually produce are not. Li Wen asks why a history that people make purposively so often yields outcomes contrary to their aims. Li argues that theistic answers, which place the cause in gods or providence, do not resolve the problem. Engels's practical-materialist account, which starts from real human beings and their practice, does resolve it, and in doing so it shows the spirit of Marxist scientific atheism.

The article has four parts. It first reviews theistic readings of the contradiction, moving from traditional theology to the "rational theology" of Vico, Kant and Hegel. It then explains why unexpected outcomes are not the work of divine will. A third section argues that anticipated outcomes have nothing to do with gods. A short conclusion draws out the practical implications, including for the Party's religious work in the new era.

Li contends that Vico's divine providence, Kant's "nature" and Hegel's "cunning of reason" all install a new deity above history and so amount to subtler forms of theism. In Li's reading, the "divine will" in these systems is a mystified expression of objective historical law, while human purposes lie hidden beneath it. Engels removes the mystification: historical necessity is set by real conditions of life, and people are the authors of their own history. Unexpected results arise because historical law and human purposes constrain and disturb each other. They also arise because individual wills conflict and merge into a resultant that no one intended. Li adds that Engels treats gods as human projections and reflections of human self-alienation, so that "God is man" and anticipation becomes a human affair.

Li concludes that the contradiction can be resolved only through human practice. Practice must move from conflict towards fit between conformity to law and conformity to purpose, with human aims approaching historical law and law incorporating human aims. Li adds that theism is sometimes used by states and interest groups for political and economic gain and can leave people passive in the face of the unexpected. Removing it, Li says, frees human agency and has value for the Party's religious work and for scientific-atheist education. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar of scientific atheism reads Engels's late theory of history against Vico, Kant and Hegel.
quoteEn: The deeper problem reflected in Engels's contradiction between the expected and the unexpected, namely the relation between historical law and human purpose, can find a reasonable solution only by removing every form of theistic interpretation.
quoteZh: 恩格斯“预期与非预期”矛盾折射的深层次问题——历史规律与人的目的之关系问题只有祛除任何形式的有神论解读，才能找到合理的解决径路。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist-Leninist form of atheism taught in China. It holds that gods do not exist and treats religion as a product of human social conditions. It is promoted in Party education and in journals such as Science and Atheism.

glossary.pinyin: hé guīlǜ xìng yǔ hé mùdì xìng
glossary.en: conformity to law and conformity to purpose
glossary.explanation: Two requirements that Chinese Marxist theory places on practice. Practice must follow objective laws, and it must also serve human goals.

t: Marx's transformation of Hegel's conception of the state and its theoretical effects
zh: 马克思对黑格尔国家观的变革及其理论效应
paras: Why did Marx criticise Hegel's theory of the state when Hegel clearly recognised modern subjective freedom? Wang Daiyue answers a long-running objection, raised by liberal-leaning Western readers, that Marx misread or treated Hegel unfairly. The article argues that the real dispute concerns where the state's universality comes from: Hegel treats it as prior to the people, while Marx traces it to the people's material activity. Overcoming Hegel's political metaphysics in this way, Wang contends, prepared the ground for historical materialism.

The article goes beyond the usual restriction of Marx's critique to the period before 1844 and draws on a wider body of early texts, combining philosophical and economic perspectives. It moves through five parts: a re-examination of the critique and its critics (Avineri, Fine, Ilting); the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, with Feuerbach's influence; Marx's 1844 economic studies, the 1844 Manuscripts and the dialectic of particularity; The German Ideology on the state and the proletariat; and a conclusion.

Wang's central reasoning has three steps. First, in the Critique, Marx makes the people the source of the constitution and proposes true democracy and universal suffrage to overcome the split between civil society and the political state. Marx's own analysis of landed property and of the labouring class, however, shows civil society to be divided, so that suffrage without structural change cannot work. Second, Marx's reading of Smith and Mill, then the 1844 Manuscripts and The German Illusion-free account in The German Ideology, shows universality arising in civil society itself through exchange, division of labour and objectified labour, not through a transcendental human essence. Third, The German Ideology distinguishes particular, common and "general" interests. It presents the state as having a double face: an abstraction of social interaction that the bourgeoisie has appropriated as an illusory community. Only the proletariat can reclaim that universality.

Wang concludes that the basic divide is the people-centred character of the state. By making universality emerge in material production, Marx removed the divine basis of Hegel's state and what Wang calls "superstition" in the philosophy of right. He also gave the proletariat's revolutionary role a scientific justification. The article presents the Paris Commune as confirming the German Ideology's vision, with universal suffrage as a transitional measure. Read the original if you work on the Marx–Hegel relationship, the early Marx's texts, or the genesis of historical materialism, and want a detailed rebuttal of the claim that Marx's critique of Hegel was unfair.
quoteEn: The people-centred character of the state constitutes the fundamental difference in standpoint between Marx's and Hegel's views of the state.
quoteZh: 国家具有人民性构成了马克思与黑格尔国家观的根本性立场分歧。

t: A manifesto for the age: "the point is to change the world"
st: A philosophical reflection on the path of Chinese modernization
zh: “问题在于改变世界”的时代宣言
zhSub: 中国式现代化道路的哲学反思
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Yuan Zushe asks what philosophical significance lies in the path of Chinese modernization as set out in Xi Jinping's report. The article, a commentary first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, argues that this path offers a new model of modernization suited to a new form of human civilisation. In Yuan's account it also opens a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

Yuan frames the discussion by combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and its fine traditional culture. The reflection is then organised under four headings: ontology (worldview), practice (the view of the subject), the conception of history, and values. Each section contrasts Chinese modernization with what the author calls Enlightenment modernity and the capital-centred modernization of the early-developing Western countries.

On ontology, Yuan contends that the Western worldview rests on free-market logic, the logic of capital, narrow instrumental rationality and relations of domination, and that it produces environmental, peace, development, trust and governance deficits. Chinese modernization, in this reading, stresses a community with a shared future for mankind and harmony between humans and nature. On practice and history, Yuan holds that Western modernization is marked by one-dimensional conquest of nature, hegemony and historical nihilism, while the Chinese path tests and develops Marxist truth through practice. Yuan also argues that it replaces a nation-state-centred view of history with one prioritising shared human values.

On values, Yuan argues that Western modernization maximises the interests and desires of the bourgeoisie. Chinese modernization, by contrast, is said to correct this by exposing the supposed universality of Western freedom, democracy, equality and human rights as illusory. It aims at common prosperity for over 1.4 billion people, adheres to the principle of putting the people first, and is presented as advancing the Marxist view of history centred on the masses, with the free and all-round development of the human being as its ultimate goal. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese Marxist philosophers frame Chinese modernization against Western modernity in ontological, practical, historical and axiological terms.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a process of discovering, creating, realising and confirming value, and it carries distinct and profound implications for values.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是发现价值、创造价值、实现并确证价值的过程，具有鲜明的、深刻的价值观意蕴。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, given a systematic statement in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as socialist, led by the Party and distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It calls for shared development, security and global governance among countries.
An official goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than by a few. It has received renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it for the present era. It is used to describe theoretical innovation by the Party.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilisation
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in official discourse, notably since Xi Jinping's 2021 speech on the Party's centenary, for the civilisational outcome claimed for Chinese modernization.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Understanding institutions from the perspective of the philosophy of social science
zh: 从社会科学哲学视角理解制度
paras: This short piece from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (10 January 2023) asks how institutions are established and sustained, and what philosophy of social science can add to sociological accounts. Li argues that the debate on collective intentionality, which spread in analytic philosophy from the 1980s, opened a new route. In this view the 'collective acceptance' account of John Searle and Raimo Tuomela explains the logical structure of institutions and underpins their social ontology.

The article has three parts. It first describes an 'ontological turn' in institutional research, setting sociological definitions (Jonathan H. Turner's) beside Searle's critique of social science. It then examines how institutions are created and maintained. Finally it considers two developmental trends of human institutions, which Li calls homogenisation and 'circle-isation'.

Li reports Searle's claim that social science has copied the natural sciences and treated money or government as objects like those of physics, while neglecting the ontological presuppositions of its own objects. Institutions are social constructions that exist only if collectively accepted. Humans assign 'status functions', such as a piece of paper serving as money, and these are observer-relative, so ontologically subjective but epistemically objective. This objectivity is what makes disciplines such as economics possible. Maintaining an institution requires continued acceptance and collective action. Tuomela adds 'collective commitment' as a guarantee of joint attitudes, giving acceptance the character of an action equilibrium in game theory. On this basis Li sees two trends. Under homogenisation, similar institutions (universities, governments, money, hospitals, science) converge in function across cultures as background culture loses influence. Under 'circle-isation', institutions divide people into groups, such as the 'DINK circle' or the 'e-sports circle', that communicate poorly with each other. Some circles, such as the 'science circle', hold authority across the whole social network.

Li concludes that human institutional action is caused by collective intentionality and that institutions are an important collective phenomenon. Explaining their creation and maintenance through collective acceptance may not strengthen the explanatory power of social-scientific theories of institutions, Li concedes. Even so, the author holds that this transcendental ontological account offers a new approach to institutional research. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-language introduction to Searle's and Tuomela's social ontology as applied to institutions, including the author's own account of institutional trends.
quoteEn: Institutional homogenisation is in essence a positive attitude of support, in which the development model of a given institution is collectively accepted.
quoteZh: 制度的同一化，本质上是一种积极的支持态度，即某种制度的发展模式被集体接受

t: The logical orientation of promoting a community with a shared future for mankind
zh: 推动构建人类命运共同体的逻辑指向
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, reads the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) on building a community with a shared future for mankind. Zheng argues that the report treats the idea systematically, grounding it in Chinese modernization and aiming it at creating a new form of human civilization.

The author organises the analysis around three parts of the report: the great changes of the new era, the essential requirements of Chinese modernization, and the promotion of world peace and development. Each part is used to bring out a different layer of the concept's logic.

Zheng first presents the community as the practical realisation of Marx's theory of community, which runs from the critique of capitalist society's "illusory community" to a "true community" or "association of free individuals". Xi Jinping's ideas from 2012 to 2017 are described as a creative development of that theory. Second, the author lists what the report's essential requirements imply for the community: Party leadership, socialism with Chinese characteristics and whole-process people's democracy as its political guarantee; high-quality development as its economic base; an enriched spiritual world as its cultural element; common prosperity as its social condition; and harmony between humanity and nature as its ecological condition. Zheng contends that Chinese modernization differs fundamentally from colonial, plundering capitalist modernization.

Zheng concludes that the community is one of the latest achievements of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that it answers the question of where the world is heading. The author sums up the report's stance as peaceful diplomacy, mutually beneficial opening up, reform of global governance and shared human values. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the 20th Party Congress report links Marx's community theory, Chinese modernization and foreign policy.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a modernization that genuinely puts the path of peaceful development into effect in theory and practice. It is a new choice for the modernization of human society, fundamentally different from capitalist colonial and plundering modernization, and it is guided by the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind as its inherent and essential requirement.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是从理论和实践上真正落实和平发展道路的现代化，是根本不同于资本主义殖民掠夺式现代化的人类社会现代化新选择，是以人类命运共同体理念指引为内在的、本质性要求的现代化。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping, developed from around 2012–2013. It calls for countries to pursue shared security, prosperity and openness.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, set out prominently in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). The Party presents it as distinct from Western models.
The official description of China's democratic system, put forward by Xi Jinping. It stresses popular participation at every stage of governance, not only at elections.
A socialist goal, stressed in Party policy since the early 2020s, of prosperity shared by all the people and a narrower wealth gap.
The official name for a growth model that prioritises innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed alone.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to apply and develop Marxism in light of Chinese conditions and contemporary problems.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: On the philosophical significance of the young Engels's "other path"
st: Centring on The Condition of the Working Class in England
zh: 论青年恩格斯“另一条道路”的哲学意义
zhSub: 以《英国工人阶级状况》为中心
paras: Was Friedrich Engels merely the "second violin" to Marx, or did he reach historical materialism by a path of his own? Liu Huaiyu takes up this long-running dispute between the "second violinist" and "other path" readings. The article argues for the "other path" view and gives it a new interpretation. In Liu's account, Engels's importance lies not only in his late systematisation of Marx's doctrine but also in the originality of his youthful, independent route to historical materialism, which also speaks to twenty-first-century urbanisation and globalisation.

The article first reconstructs Engels's intellectual development from the Bremen period to the 1842–1845 years in Manchester, Paris, Barmen and Brussels. It then surveys more than 170 years of readings of The Condition of the Working Class in England: Soviet and East European scholars, sociological and ecological readings, and Western accounts that treat the book as the founding text of \"urban Marxism\". Liu then sets out the classical significance of the \"other path\", before closing with its relevance today.

Liu makes three main moves. First, Engels reached communism through field investigation of advanced English capitalism, which served as an antidote to Young Hegelian abstraction and to the \"true socialists\". The book is also read as Hegelian historical dialectics: it traces how industrial revolution produced the proletariat as a new historical subject. Liu notes that the book is still immature, since its proletariat and communism concepts owe much to philosophical logic, and that Engels later gave the path up while Marx carried the critique of political economy forward. Second, Liu argues that Engels's treatment of Manchester anticipates later urban theory. This includes his critique of alienated urban interaction, of class segregation and of uneven development. It also includes his view that big cities foster working-class consciousness. Liu stresses that Engels held capitalist production, not the city, responsible for workers' conditions, so he was not a founder of \"urban Marxism\" as a substitute for the critique of capitalism.

Liu concludes that Engels's path was obscured because he abandoned it and because it was read dogmatically. Defending his originality, the author says, fights dogmatism and academic impoverishment. For the twenty-first century, Liu calls for a \"re-spatialised\" Marxism. It would study how capitalism turns cities into instruments of control, and how disadvantaged groups can gain the right to the city. It would also treat urban space as a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you are interested in the Engels–Marx relationship, the reception history of the 1845 book, or Chinese philosophical engagement with Marxist urban theory.
quoteEn: The Condition of the Working Class in England contains a Marxism that needs to be "re-spatialised".
quoteZh: 《英国工人阶级状况》蕴含着某种需要“重新空间化的”马克思主义

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013, stressing shared interests and common development among nations. Here Liu extends it to the idea of urban space.

keywords: The Condition of the Working Class in England

t: High-quality development of the Marxist theory discipline in the new era
zh: 新时代马克思主义理论学科高质量发展研究
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2023 no. 3
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhang Leisheng and Li Mengyun ask how the first-level discipline of Marxist theory, which studies the Party's guiding ideology and its theoretical innovation, can achieve high-quality development on the new journey. They argue that this requires three things: a firm awareness of high-quality development, a clear sense of the discipline's positioning, and stronger institutional and personnel construction.

The article first takes stock of the discipline's achievements and problems over the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then discusses positioning, with the academic system as its core, using the history of Marxism and the basic principles of Marxism as examples. It closes with three paths of construction: strengthening Schools of Marxism, raising the quality of teachers, and improving the training of specialist graduates.

On achievements, the authors cite incomplete statistics: by the end of 2022 there were 106 doctoral and 279 master's programmes, 125,000 ideological and political theory teachers, and over 1,440 Schools of Marxism. They name four problems: research fields that stray from the discipline's content, uneven teaching staff with few leading scholars, weak organised research with low-quality output, and homogenised or loosely regulated curricula. Their central claim is that the academic system underpins both the disciplinary system and the discourse system. It should be built on the unity of the "doctrine, theory and philosophy" of the Party's innovative theory and on the premise that Marxism, and Marxism adapted to China's conditions and the needs of our times, works. The authors also warn against "de-Marxification" of teachers and graduate training. They recommend that teachers read the classics, study history and grasp basic principles.

The authors propose concentrating resources on distinctive and leading sub-disciplines in key Schools of Marxism. They want the discipline kept distinct from Marxist studies in general, from ideological and political course teaching, and from the work of the Schools themselves. They also call for stricter control of graduate curricula, dissertation topics and research skills. They present these steps as the way to turn high-quality development from an aim into practice. Read the original if you want a Party-school-internal view of how Marxist theory is organised as an academic discipline in China, including its staffing, curricula and quality problems.
quoteEn: Building the academic system is the "lifeblood" of a discipline's development and the foundation of its high-quality development.
quoteZh: 学术体系建设是学科发展的“生命”，是学科高质量发展的根本。

glossary.explanation: An official slogan, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), that stresses quality and efficiency over scale of growth. Here it is applied to an academic discipline.
University units that host the Marxist theory discipline and teach ideological and political theory courses. Since 2015 a group of them has been designated as key Schools.

t: Marx and Engels on collective ownership of land
zh: 马克思恩格斯关于土地集体所有制的论述
paras: Chen Wenxue asks what Marx and Engels actually said about collective ownership of land, and what their statements imply for rural land reform in China today. The article argues that Marx and Engels treated collective ownership as a form of public ownership alongside nationalisation, and that cooperatives were the route to it. On this basis Chen concludes that China should neither privatise nor nationalise rural land.

The article has three parts. It first sets out why Marx and Engels wrote on land ownership: the aim of communist revolution, the need to win the peasantry as an ally, and concrete questions of land title in revolution. It then reads their texts from 1843 to the 1880s, including Engels's "The Peasant Question in France and Germany" and Marx's replies to Vera Zasulich on the Russian village commune. The final part turns to China's land history since 1949 and to current reform.

Chen's central move is to trace how "collective ownership" shifted from a general term for public ownership, opposed to private property, to the ownership of the working masses. In Chen's account, the cooperative ideas of Marx and Engels supplied that content. Large estates were to be expropriated and passed, first by lease, to agricultural workers' cooperatives under state ownership. Small peasants were not to be dispossessed by force: they were to be brought into cooperatives through example, social help and time, and Engels backed the Danish model of direct pooling. Chen adds that for Russia, Marx held that the commune could move straight to collective ownership, without passing through the stage of bourgeois smallholding, provided proletarian revolution succeeded.

Chen draws five conclusions about collective land ownership, covering its place in communism, its negation of capitalist property, its use in winning peasants, its basis in large-scale socialised production, and cooperatives as the route. For China, Chen defends the household contract responsibility system and the separation of ownership, contract and management rights, with homestead reform in progress. Privatisation is rejected as contrary to Marxism and the constitution. Nationalisation is rejected because of the urban–rural divide, fiscal burden and political risk, so reform must protect peasant interests and proceed by category and by stages. Read the original if you want a close, text-based survey of the classical sources on land and cooperatives, together with their use in current Chinese policy debate.
quoteEn: The land system is the core of the \"three rural issues\" (agriculture, rural areas and farmers).
quoteZh: 土地制度是“三农”问题的核心。

glossary.explanation: The arrangement, developed from the late 1970s, under which rural households contract collectively owned land and farm it, while ownership stays with the collective.

glossary.en: separation of ownership, contract and management rights
glossary.explanation: A reform policy, set out in 2016, that splits rural land rights into collective ownership, household contract rights and management rights. Its aim is to allow land-use rights to be transferred.
In China, a form of socialist public ownership in which resources, notably rural land, belong to a village collective. It is distinct from ownership by the whole people, i.e. the state.

t: Marx and Engels on social character
zh: 马克思和恩格斯关于社会性格的思想探析
source: Journal of Beijing Normal University (Social Sciences), 2022 no. 6
paras: Ouyang Kang and Zhao Beisite ask what Marx and Engels thought about "social character", a group-level psychological trait pattern and the behaviour it produces. They argue that, although the two never used the term in a strict sense, their writings on national character, class character and universal personality contain a coherent body of thought. The authors present it as a theoretical source of Erich Fromm's concept and as a resource for current concerns: building a sense of community among the Chinese nation, meeting the spiritual needs of the people in the new era, and responding to modern anxiety, depression and loneliness.

The article first defines social character and places it within Marx's and Engels's account of social consciousness. It then examines three dimensions: national character, class character, and a universal human personality form tied to Marx's three forms of human development. A final section draws out four underlying orientations of this thought: social, historical, practical and humanistic. The evidence comes mainly from Engels's The Condition of the Working Class in England, Marx's Eighteenth Brumaire and Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, and Marx's account of the three forms of human development in the Grundrisse.

The authors argue that social character is a stable system of low-level social consciousness, an intermediate link through which social psychology develops into systematic ideology. National character is shaped by modes of production and life, by the mode of social change, and by war and migration. Class character, they say, increasingly replaces national character as the real "nationality", with feudal lords, capitalists and workers each expressing their relation to a form of private property. The article reads the three forms of human development as a history of personality, from dependence on persons, through independence resting on dependence on things (with isolation and anxiety), to the free individuality of the third form. The authors also hold that, since all consciousness is social, no purely individual character exists.

The authors conclude that Marx and Engels linked healthy social character to the reform of social institutions and to proletarian revolution. In their reading, the subjects of social character are practising people who can change their own character, and its goal is the spiritual liberation and all-round development of each person. They also read Marx and Engels as rejecting both forced erasure of national character and the placing of narrow national particularity above human emancipation. Read the original if you want a detailed, text-based account of how Marx and Engels treated national and class psychology, and how a Chinese scholar links Fromm's concept to the Marxist theory of human development.
quoteEn: There is no absolute "individual character"; all character is social character.
quoteZh: 不存在绝对的“个体性格”,所有的性格都是社会性格。

glossary.explanation: A group-level psychological trait pattern and the behavioural pattern it produces. The term comes from Erich Fromm, and the authors trace its roots to Marx and Engels.
The psychological traits shared by members of a nation or state, also called national disposition (国民性). The authors treat it as shaped by historical and material conditions.
The psychological traits and behavioural pattern shared by members of a class, determined by the class's political and economic position.
A category of historical materialism covering the spiritual side of social life, from everyday social psychology to systematic forms such as morality, religion and philosophy.

t: Some reflections on combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture
st: Studying and implementing the spirit of the 20th Party Congress
zh: 关于马克思主义基本原理与中华优秀传统文化相结合的若干认识
zhSub: 学习贯彻党的二十大精神
source: Modern Chinese History Studies (Jindaishi yanjiu), 2023 no. 2
paras: Yang Yanqiu takes up a proposition that Xi Jinping first put forward in his 2021 speech marking the Party's centenary and that the 20th Party Congress (2022) elaborated: combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. Written as a study note on the Congress, the article asks why the two must be combined, why they can be, and how. Yang's answer is that the combination is the necessary route for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that it rests on a real inner compatibility between the two.

The article has four sections: the necessity of the combination, the inner affinity between Marxism and traditional culture, the grounds on which they can be joined, and methods and paths. Yang draws on Engels, on Mao Zedong's view of history, and above all on the historian Liu Danian and the Marxist historiography of Li Dazhao, Guo Moruo, Hou Wailu and Du Guoyong. Yang also cites Marx's writings on China and the Congress report's "six adherences".

On necessity, Yang argues that Marxism could take root in modern China only by explaining Chinese history and responding to the problems of the country's modern transformation, and that Chinese Marxist historiography was founded in the very act of interpreting traditional culture. Traditional culture in turn needs Marxism for its "creative transformation and innovative development". On feasibility, Yang points to Marx's and Engels's sustained attention to China and to the openness of Chinese culture, which Yang says absorbed Buddhism, Islam and Western learning in three major exchanges. Yang warns that compatibility must not be examined only as ideas set against ideas, but in relation to economic base and superstructure, citing the early Marxist historians' shift from a single economic-formation method to a more dialectical view.

On method, Yang lists several principles drawn from the six adherences: putting the people first and looking for inner spiritual affinity rather than surface resemblance; self-confidence and self-reliance; upholding fundamental principles while innovating, with a problem-oriented approach; a systematic outlook; and an open, world-embracing stance. Combination, Yang stresses, is not a blend or compromise but a process of both breaking and establishing under Marxist guidance, and research must serve practice rather than revive the past for its own sake. Read the original if you want an official-academic account of how Chinese historians frame the "Two Integrations", with extensive references to Marxist historiography.
quoteEn: Compromise can only stir the two together to form a so-called mixture.
quoteZh: 调和只能是把二者搅拌在一起，形成所谓的混合物

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in Xi Jinping's 2021 centenary speech.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's project of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. The 20th Party Congress report added "of our times" to the older formula of sinicizing Marxism.
The official term for those elements of Chinese tradition that the Party regards as worth inheriting and developing, as distinct from elements it treats as outdated.

Six methodological principles in the 20th Party Congress report: the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, a problem-oriented approach, a systematic outlook, and a world-embracing vision.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula for how the Party says traditional culture should be treated: reinterpreted and renewed to suit present needs rather than simply preserved.

t: The Kreuznach Notebooks and the young Marx's turn to materialism
zh: 《克罗伊茨纳赫笔记》与青年马克思的唯物主义转向
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 11 April 2023, p. 2
paras: How did the young Marx come to adopt materialism in 1843? Liu Bingjing notes that the usual account points to the material-interest problems of the Rheinische Zeitung period and to Feuerbach's philosophy. Drawing on the MEGA2 text of the Kreuznach Notebooks, Liu argues that Marx's own independent historical research was also indispensable to the turn.

The article draws on Marx's stay in Kreuznach from May to September 1843, when he studied the political history of England, France and other countries and wrote both the Notebooks and the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right. It follows the Notebooks in sequence: Notebook I's broad chronicle of French history, the narrowing focus from Notebook II onward, readings of Daru, Rousseau and Bailleul, and a long comment in Notebook IV on Ranke's journal. It then compares these with the Critique.

Liu contends that through excerpts on Venetian privilege, Rousseau's remarks on property and law, and feudal and bourgeois France, Marx came to see that property relations in civil society shape the state and politics. Land ownership underpinned feudal personal dependence, and property ownership underpinned bourgeois political status. On this basis Marx reversed Hegel's claim that the state determines civil society, as his Ranke comment on Hegel's state idea as 'subject' shows. The Critique then restates this argument, including its treatment of primogeniture and the claim that political estates become social estates.

Liu adds a qualification: Marx had not yet grasped the objective historical content of civil society. He still criticised the dominance of private property in ethical terms, citing Vergniaud and Robespierre, and called for restoring the human essence of social forms. In Liu's reading, Marx had inverted Hegelian speculation and turned to materialism, but his view of social history kept an implicit idealist tinge. Starting from concrete history nevertheless pointed him toward the political-economy study of civil society. Read the original if you want a short account of how the Kreuznach Notebooks bear on the origins of Marx's materialism and the limits of his 1843 position.
quoteEn: This shows that in 1843 Marx, although he had already inverted Hegel's speculative philosophy through historical research and thereby turned to materialism, still showed an implicit idealist colouring in his view of social history.
quoteZh: 这说明，在1843年间，马克思虽然已经通过历史研究颠倒了黑格尔思辨哲学，从而实现了向唯物主义思想转向，但在社会历史观上仍透露出隐性的唯心主义色彩。
keywords: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

t: Clarifying Marx's "philosophy of history" and its orientation for our times
zh: 马克思“历史哲学”的澄明及时代定向
paras: Against the backdrop of what Chinese discourse calls changes unseen in a century, Wu Hongzheng asks whether Marx's thought contains a philosophy of history capable of answering the question of where the world is heading. Wu argues that it does: Marx's theory of world history, set out in works such as the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, The German Ideology and the Communist Manifesto, is the core of an implicit philosophy of history. This has been neglected in scholarship, and Wu holds it should be recovered and given a contemporary orientation.

The article has three parts. The first explains why Marx's philosophy of history has receded from view. The second reconstructs its basic content by contrasting Marx with Kant and Hegel on the conception of history, its subject, its value and its laws. The third turns to the present and identifies three orientations: changes in contemporary capitalism, the new form of human civilization, and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Wu names three causes of the recession: Marx never built a separate system or used the term in his own materialist framework; his critique of Hegel gave the false impression that he rejected the field; and the emphasis on "historical science" overshadowed it. Wu replies that Marx attacked only the speculative "general philosophy of history", which offers abstract universality and treats history as a set of ideas. Marx's own version, in Wu's account, rests on concrete universality and on labour as the creator of history. It places the value of history in human freedom and emancipation, and finds historical necessity in the contradictory movement of productive forces and relations of production, a necessity that can be grasped in advance rather than only in retrospect. Wu also argues that Marx's view is not a linear one: the Renaissance and the October Revolution show necessity that includes contingency, so the author calls it a dialectical conception of progress.

Wu concludes that Capital is both Marx's economic philosophy and, at a higher level, part of his philosophy of history, so the surplus-value law belongs to the logic of social formations. In Wu's view, recent shifts such as unilateralism and de-globalisation do not change that orientation. Civilizations advance through sublation rather than clash or simple replacement, and the community with a shared future for mankind becomes the era's theme. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese philosophical argument that Marx has a philosophy of history, set against Kant and Hegel and linked to current Party-state concepts.
quoteEn: What Marx criticised was this "general philosophy of history" detached from concrete historical conditions, not a negation of the philosophy of history itself.
quoteZh: 马克思批判的是这种脱离具体历史条件的“一般历史哲学”，并不是对历史哲学本身的否定。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012, calling for joint global governance and shared development. The article treats it as the contemporary theme of Marxist philosophy of history.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.literal: great changes in the world unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping since 2018 to describe a period of shifting global power and rapid technological and geopolitical change.

glossary.en: the new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A Party formulation, prominent since 2021, describing Chinese modernization as creating a new type of civilization distinct from Western modernization.

t: Staying firmly confident in economic work
zh: 坚定做好经济工作的信心
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in March 2023, Gao Peiyong and Wang Hongju take up Xi Jinping's remarks to the Jiangsu delegation at the first session of the 14th National People's Congress, where Xi called high-quality development the first task of building a modern socialist country. The authors argue that 2023, the first year of implementing the 20th Party Congress (2022), calls for a correct reading of the economic situation, better social expectations and stronger confidence. Their thesis is that the economy is already improving and its long-term fundamentals are sound.

The commentary has three parts. The first reviews 2022 and early 2023 data and identifies positive changes in domestic demand, supply and market expectations. The second lists the strengths behind the claim that the long-term fundamentals have not changed. The third turns to the December 2022 Central Economic Work Conference and sets out four sets of tasks for guiding business entities and stabilising expectations.

On the first part, the authors cite GDP above 120 trillion yuan in 2022, growth of 3% and consumer price inflation of 2%. They also cite average growth of 4.5% over three years and an IMF upgrade of China's 2023 forecast from 4.4% to 5.2%. They say demand is recovering as pandemic controls are eased, supply is improving as commodity prices fall, and PMI readings have moved into expansion territory. On the second part, they name the leadership of the Party and the socialist system, a hardworking population, Chinese modernization, a solid industrial base, 170 million business entities, a huge domestic market and the dividends of reform and opening up. In their account these make up the "fundamentals".

The policy section calls for expanding consumption and investment, and for implementing the Two Unwaverings through state-enterprise reform and a better environment for private firms. It also calls for opening up at a high level to attract foreign investment, and for coordinated fiscal, monetary, industrial, technology and social policy. The authors present these steps as the way to turn the economy's potential into results and consolidate the overall recovery. Read the original if you want an example of how official economic commentary in early 2023 framed the post-pandemic recovery and the policy agenda behind it.
quoteEn: China's economy is resilient, has great potential and is full of vitality, and its fundamentals of long-term improvement remain unchanged.
quoteZh: 我国经济韧性强、潜力大、活力足，长期向好的基本面依然不变

glossary.explanation: A policy goal that has been central since the 19th Party Congress (2017). It stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability of growth rather than speed alone.
The official formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The Party's concept of its own path to modernization. The 20th Party Congress report (2022) summarised its distinctive features in five aspects.
An annual meeting held at the end of the year, in which the Party leadership sets the economic policy priorities for the next year.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: Coordinating the expansion of domestic demand with the deepening of supply-side structural reform
zh: 搞好统筹扩大内需和深化供给侧结构性改革
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2023, Liu Yuanchun takes up Xi Jinping's statements on coordinating the expansion of domestic demand with the deepening of supply-side structural reform. Liu argues that the two are unified rather than opposed. The author presents their integration as necessary for high-quality development, for building the new development pattern, and for coping with external shocks and current macroeconomic problems.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why both policies are needed and how they relate. The second sets out the principles that should guide their coordination, under Xi Jinping's economic thought. The third turns to concrete tasks, drawing on the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, the 2022 Central Economic Work Conference and the Outline of the Strategic Plan for Expanding Domestic Demand (2022–2035).

Liu holds that insufficient demand is one of the main obstacles to economic recovery. As evidence, Liu notes that final consumption has stayed above 50 per cent of GDP for twelve years but remains below the roughly 80 per cent of major developed economies and the roughly 70 per cent of India and Vietnam. Supply-side reform, by contrast, is described as the fundamental remedy for deeper structural problems, since the principal contradiction has shifted from weak aggregate demand to a mismatch between supply and demand structures.
