The first reconstructs the theory of alienated labour against Hegel's philosophy of right, classical political economy, the communist currents of the day (Weitling, Proudhon) and Feuerbach's anthropology. The second follows the turn to historical materialism in The German Ideology and related works. The third reads Capital, including Marx's letters on the dual character of labour, the contradictions of capital and the realm of freedom.

Yang's central claim is that Capital is not simply an application of the historical materialism of 1845–46. The logic of production defines production through material means of life, that is, use-value. In Capital, however, use-value only carries exchange-value, and production serves the valorization of capital, so the logic of production is subordinated to the logic of capital. Yang treats this as the deepest of the three shifts and as the key to the specificity of capitalist production. Moral critique of capitalists, on this reading, falls back into capital's own logic, and the contradictions of capital arise from its operation rather than from an a priori human essence. Yang also criticises scholars who say they start from the logic of capital but in fact derive it from the logic of production, a route Yang traces back to Lukács's ontology of social being.

Yang concludes that each shift deepened Marx's scientific understanding of history while rebuilding his critique of capitalism on a deeper footing. Only at the stage of the logic of capital could Marx show the historicity and distinctiveness of capitalist production, its internal contradictions and its possible futures. Marx also separates himself from Hegel, since capital's contradictions cannot be resolved by reconciling state and civil society and require overturning capital's logic, with the realm of freedom as the horizon. Read the original if you study the internal development of Marx's thought or the debate over capital-logic versus production-logic readings of Capital.
quoteEn: The shift from the logic of production to the logic of capital constitutes the most profound transformation in the development of Marx's philosophy.
quoteZh: 从生产逻辑到资本逻辑的转换，构成了马克思哲学发展中最为深刻的一次转变。

t: A glimpse of the transcendence of Marx's labour theory
st: A counter-critique of Arendt's critique of Marx's theory of labour
zh: 马克思劳动理论的超越性管窥
zhSub: 基于阿伦特对马克思劳动理论批判的再批判
source: Journal of Nanchang University (Humanities and Social Sciences), 2021 no. 6
paras: Hannah Arendt, in The Human Condition and her writings on Marx and the Western tradition of political thought, questioned and criticised Marx's theory of labour. Han and Yi argue that, because Marx and Arendt start from different points and aim at different ends, her criticisms rest on many misunderstandings. They contend that Marx's labour theory does not return to traditional Western philosophy but transcends its order and its traditional view of development.

The article first sorts existing scholarship on Arendt's critique into three views: complementarity, misreading and enrichment. It then takes up two charges in turn: the "dichotomy" charge, and the charge that Marx's theory contains an "unnatural growth of the natural". Each section sets out Arendt's position and then Marx's reply. A final section sets out four aspects of Marx's theory: labour and human essence, social practice, capitalist production, and free and all-round human development.

On the first charge, Arendt places Marx within the tradition running from Plato, so that he merely inverts the hierarchy of contemplative and active life. She also reads him as wanting to "abolish labour" and as treating violence as action. The authors reply that this misreads Marx's critique of alienated labour. In their account, Marx raises labour, the lowest activity of active life, to the highest place, and defines the human being as a labouring animal rather than a political one. They add that his aim is changing the world, so that philosophy ends in practice rather than in contemplation. On the second charge, Arendt holds that the theory carries totalitarian elements, dissolves the public and private realms into a labouring society, and leads through automation to a consumer society. The authors answer that it frees labouring subjects and gives them freedom of association and self-realisation. They argue that automation shortens necessary labour time and widens free time for all-round development, and that the theory overcomes the opposition between humans and nature.

The authors conclude that Arendt's objections amount to a utopian construction of classical political philosophy that seeks a spiritual refuge for capitalist elites. They call for returning to the authentic Marx and grasping the transcendent character of his labour theory. The aim is a socialist view of labour suited to China, one that respects labour, knowledge, talent and creation, in the context of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist rebuttal of Arendt's reading of Marx on labour, or an example of how labour theory is tied to the socialist view of labour in China.
quoteEn: The \"dichotomy\" and the \"unnatural growth of the natural\" in Marx's labour theory are not a return to traditional Western philosophy; on the contrary, they greatly transcend its order and its traditional view of development.
quoteZh: 马克思劳动理论的“二分性”和“自然的非自然增长”因素，不是西方传统哲学的复归，相反是对西方传统哲学秩序和传统发展观的极大超越。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party slogan, popularised under Xi Jinping, for restoring China's national strength and international standing. The article cites it as the strategic context for a socialist view of labour.

t: Marx's critique of the bourgeois view of interest
zh: 马克思对资产阶级利息观的批判
source: Journal of Donghua University (Social Science Edition), 2022 no. 4
paras: Why does capital bear interest, and should interest exist at all? Liu Huajun takes up this old question, which Böhm-Bawerk framed as one of what 'is' and what 'ought' to be, and examines how Marx answered bourgeois political economy on it. The article argues that Marx treats interest as a share of surplus value, that is, of unpaid labour. On this reading, bourgeois economists tried to make interest look rational by hiding that origin.

The article is organised in six parts. It begins with the denial of a 'natural rate of interest' (Locke against Massie). It then turns to the relation between interest and profit in Hume, Smith, Ricardo, Say and the Currency School. Next come Marx's dissolution of the 'qualitative division' of profit, his rejection of the claim that interest is the 'price of capital', and his view that interest belongs to labour, followed by a short conclusion. Liu draws on Capital Volume III and the 1861–63 manuscripts, comparing the two texts' wording.

Liu argues that bourgeois writers wanted both to keep interest and to lower it, and so invented a natural rate. Marx, citing Massie, counters that supply and demand for money cannot fix interest, whose determination is empirical and contingent. Liu holds that the economists blur the link between interest and industrial profit so that profit appears unconnected with labour. For Marx, by contrast, interest only divides surplus value between money-capitalist and functioning capitalist. Interest-bearing capital is mere form, and money lent circulates as M + ΔM, with ΔM drawn from surplus value. Liu then reads Marx's remark that interest as the 'price of capital' is irrational. In Liu's account, the absurdity lies in treating capital as a commodity, whose use-value is then presented as interest. This move hides the fact that capital extracts surplus labour.

Liu concludes that interest expresses capital's 'unlimited and endless' drive beyond its limits, and that interest-bearing capital hides this drive most completely. Equating interest with ground rent makes capital look like a thing that creates value in itself. Liu says that for interest to produce value it must return to the production process, where labour is the core of capital. The author also notes that the relation between labour and capital, on which realising interest depends, needs a separate treatment. Read the original if you want a close textual reading of Marx's critique of interest, including the comparison of Capital Volume III with the 1861–63 manuscripts.
quoteEn: The aim of bourgeois economists in blurring and inverting the relation between interest and profit is to make profit unrelated to labour, which in effect is to make interest unrelated to industrial profit.
quoteZh: 资产阶级经济学家模糊和颠倒利息与利润关系的目的是让利润与劳动无关，实际上是让利息和产业利润无关。

t: Four dimensions for understanding the distinctive features of Chinese modernization and its world-historical significance
zh: 理解中国式现代化特质及其世界历史意义的四重维度
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 21 February 2023
paras: Responding to Xi Jinping's speech at the study session on the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022), this newspaper commentary asks how Chinese modernization should be understood. Sun Leqiang argues that its distinctive features and world-historical significance can be grasped only through a "big view of history" and a comparison with the Western path.

The piece is organised into four dialectical pairs, each a way of reading Chinese modernization: understanding China from China (the stage and the whole), China from the world (the global and the national), the world from China (the particular and the universal), and the world from the world (diversity and unity).

In the first two dimensions, Sun holds that Chinese modernization is inseparable from Party leadership, the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and China's fine traditional culture, and must be placed within the continuity of Chinese history rather than a single period. Against the Western claim that modernization equals Westernization, the author describes the Western path as capital-centred, polarising, materialist and expansionist, and presents the five features named at the 20th Party Congress as a different model. In the last two dimensions, Sun argues that this particular path has universal meaning, because it sublates the defects of Western modernization and offers a new form of human civilisation. Historical materialism supplies unity, while concrete historical paths are diverse.

Sun concludes that Western modernization opened world history but cannot complete it, and that Chinese modernization represents the direction of human progress. As the "great changes unseen in a century" deepen, the author predicts that a new pattern breaking through the capitalist world system will inevitably arrive. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese theorists frame Chinese modernization against Western modernization in 2023.
quoteEn: The path to modernization is by no means singular but plural.
quoteZh: 现代化道路绝不是单一的，而是多元的

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, given a formal five-feature definition at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
A phrase used in Party discourse for viewing present developments within long historical continuity and a global perspective.

t: Chinese modernization and the exploration of a new form of intelligent civilization
zh: 中国式现代化探索智能文明新形态
paras: Gao Qiqi, in a short commentary first published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks how Chinese modernization can shape the coming age of artificial intelligence. Taking up Xi Jinping's statement that Chinese modernization offers a picture different from the Western model, Gao argues that it has distinct advantages for exploring a new form of intelligent civilization under the framework of common prosperity and high-quality development.

The article first reviews China's modernization during the third industrial revolution, which Gao divides into the computer, internet and mobile internet stages. It then turns to the fourth industrial revolution, the intelligence revolution, and to the rivalry between modernization models. A final section sets out China's institutional strengths for what Gao calls intelligent civilization.

Gao holds that China has moved from distant to close pursuit of the leading countries and that this reflects a learning from, and surpassing of, both the Soviet and American models. In artificial intelligence, Gao concedes that the United States leads in general large-model technology such as ChatGPT, while China has strengths in market scale, talent and institutional planning. Gao describes US entity lists, restricted cooperation and technology alliances as an attempt to wall off advanced productive forces. Because the intelligence revolution may bring creative destruction, unemployment and social polarisation, Gao argues that a new-type whole-nation system, shared computing and data platforms, intellectual property protection and common prosperity are needed.

Gao concludes that intelligent civilization requires innovation combined with responsibility: original innovation to bring China to the front in productive forces, and institutional design so that most people share the gains. Gao expects Chinese modernization to be refined further and to become a model for this new civilization. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Chinese scholar links the AI competition with the United States to the claims of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The key to the competition for leadership of the intelligence revolution is the competition between models of modernization.
quoteZh: 智能革命领导权竞争的关键是现代化模式的竞争。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), describing China's own path of modernization as distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal, stressed by the leadership in recent years, of prosperity shared by all rather than by a minority.
An official formulation since 2017 that prioritises quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth.
An approach that mobilises state, enterprises and research bodies nationwide to achieve major scientific and technological goals, adapted to a market economy.

t: The historical logic of the exploration of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化探索的历史逻辑
paras: This commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks how Chinese modernization came about and what historical logic runs through its exploration. Chen argues that it is a great creation of the Communist Party of China, the result of successive generations building on one another, and the only path to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The piece takes its framing from Xi Jinping's speech at the study session on the 20th Party Congress (2022).

The article moves through three periods. These are the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, and reform and opening up, followed by the new era that began with the 18th Party Congress (2012). For each stage Chen identifies what it supplied to modernization: social conditions, a political premise and a material base, an institutional and material framework, and then fuller institutional, material and spiritual support.

Chen holds that the revolution ended semi-colonial, semi-feudal China and created the basic social conditions. In Chen's account, the socialist system and an independent industrial system then laid the political and material foundations. After reform and opening up, Deng Xiaoping's xiaokang goal and the 'three-step' strategy, combined with a socialist market economy, produced rapid growth and what the article calls a new form of human civilisation. For the new era, Chen credits Xi Jinping with advances in theory, strategy and practice. Theory is said to have gone beyond neoliberalism and dependency theory and broken the equation of modernization with Westernisation. Strategy covers the 'two-step' plan, and practice covers poverty alleviation, the new development philosophy and cultural confidence.

Chen concludes that practice has proved Chinese modernization to be the Party's creation and the necessary road to national rejuvenation, which can be achieved only by adhering to it. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned periodisation of how Party writers present the continuity between the revolutionary, Maoist, reform-era and Xi-era stages of modernization.
quoteEn: Only by always adhering to the path of Chinese modernization can the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation be achieved.
quoteZh: 只有始终坚持中国式现代化道路,才能实现中华民族伟大复兴。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, elaborated especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the world economy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
Deng Xiaoping's term for a moderately prosperous society, used as a staged development target; the full goal was declared achieved in 2021.
The set of five principles (innovative, coordinated, green, open, shared development) put forward in 2015 to guide economic policy.

t: New features of mass work and the growth of young cadres
zh: 群众工作新特点与年轻干部成长研究
paras: Sun Yingshuai asks how the Party's mass work must change under the conditions of the new era, and what this means for younger cadres. Starting from Xi Jinping's call to study the characteristics and patterns of mass work in the new situation, Sun argues that the mass line remains the Party's basic working method but now has to be carried out both online and offline. Young cadres, in Sun's view, are better placed than older ones to notice difficulties and blind spots among the public on the internet and should build "concentric circles" linking the two spheres.

Published in People's Forum in 2022, the article is organised around four themes: online mass work as a new mode of public governance; the requirements of truthfulness, speed, openness and transparency in handling online opinion; the coordination of group interests as the normal state of mass work; and the need to keep a people-centred approach while eliminating bureaucratism and formalism. Sun draws on internet-usage and education statistics, and on cases such as the Fengxian incident, the Zhengzhou "7·20" floods, the Baiyin ultramarathon deaths and the MU5735 crash.

Sun's first argument is that mass work now spans physical and virtual society, because in the "self-media" era citizens have unprecedented rights to information and expression. If cadres respond more slowly than information spreads, the pressure of opinion guidance rises. Cadres should therefore speak up, speak promptly and speak truthfully, and must not delete posts or conceal facts. Sun also holds that, since the principal contradiction in society has shifted, conflicts of interest among groups are routine, and cites disputes over lift installation, clearing illegal structures and pandemic-related labour disputes. Handling such petty matters badly, Sun says, can turn them into public incidents.

Sun concludes that cadres must hold to a people-centred approach and feel real affection for the people. They should judge their achievements by how the people feel and avoid arbitrary decision-making, while Sun treats persistent bureaucratism and formalism, including during pandemic control, as the key point for improving work style. The title's reference to young cadres is developed mainly in the introduction rather than in a separate section. Read the original if you want a Chinese official-journal account of how internet governance, opinion management and interest coordination are framed as tasks of mass work.
quoteEn: Therefore, how to coordinate various social resources, reconcile the interests of different groups and build the broadest consensus among all parties has become the new normal of the Party's mass work in the new era.
quoteZh: 因此，如何统筹各种社会资源、协调群体利益需求、形成各方最大共识，就成为新时代党的群众工作的新常态。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese Communist Party's basic working method of going among the people, learning from them and serving them. It is traditionally associated with Mao Zedong and is presented as the Party's 'lifeline'.
The everyday work of Party organisations and cadres in communicating with, mobilising, serving and mediating among ordinary people.

The central tension that the Party says drives social development. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) it is defined as that between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development.
Party terms for work styles judged to be superficial, box-ticking or detached from the people, which the Party has repeatedly campaigned against.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Xi Jinping-era Party discourse that development and governance should be for, and rely on, the people.

t: How Chinese-style democracy inherits and develops the Marxist view of democracy
zh: 中国式民主对马克思主义民主观的继承和发展
paras: Sun Yingshuai asks how democracy as practised under the Communist Party of China relates to the Marxist conception of democracy. The article argues that the Party has kept the essential content of that conception while developing it to fit China's revolution, construction and reform. In Sun's account, this produced a set of unities: democracy and dictatorship, democracy and centralism, procedural and substantive democracy, direct and indirect democracy, and the people's democracy and the will of the state.

The article is organised around three themes: the substance, the principles and the forms of democracy. Each is traced from Marx and Engels through Lenin to the Party's own practice. It begins with Athenian and bourgeois democracy as Marxism criticised them, then covers the Party's organisational doctrine, and ends with institutions from the Paris Commune and the Soviets to the people's congress system and whole-process people's democracy.

On substance, Sun argues that Marx used historical materialism and class analysis to show earlier democracies, from Athens to bourgeois republics, to be democracies of a minority. Mao Zedong's class analysis of semi-colonial, semi-feudal China led the Party to widen proletarian class democracy into "people's democracy" and the people's democratic dictatorship. On principle, Sun traces the move from Marx's "complete democracy" to Lenin's centralism and then to democratic centralism. Sun notes that the Russian term stresses centralism, and that the Party's 1945 constitution used "democratic centralism" in that sense. On form, Sun presents the people's congress system as a Chinese realisation of the Marxist idea of unified legislative and executive power. It is supplemented by consultative democracy, regional ethnic autonomy and, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), whole-process people's democracy.

Sun concludes that Chinese-style democracy has gone beyond "minority democracy", "one-off democracy" and "pseudo-universal democracy". It aims to be broad, genuine and effective, and Sun describes it as a democracy of governance, efficiency, driving force and systematic verifiability. Sun cites figures, including that directly elected county and township deputies make up over 90 percent of deputies, and that over 200 draft laws were put out for public comment. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholarship links Marx, Lenin and Mao to the current doctrine of whole-process people's democracy.
quoteEn: Democratic centralism is "centralism on the basis of democracy, and democracy under centralised guidance".
quoteZh: 民主集中制就是“在民主基础上的集中，在集中指导下的民主”

glossary.explanation: A concept the Party leadership has promoted since 2019. It holds that democracy covers the whole cycle of elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight, not only voting.

The official definition of China's state system, set out by Mao Zedong in 1949. It combines democracy for "the people" with coercive power against those deemed their enemies, under the leadership of the working class.

The organisational principle of the Party and state, drawn from Lenin. Leaders are chosen and decisions discussed democratically, but the minority must obey the majority and lower levels must obey higher ones.
China's fundamental political system. Congresses at each level are the organs of state power, and the National People's Congress is the highest.
Consultation among the Party, other parties and social groups, mainly through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.

t: A review of research on whole-process people's democracy since 2019
zh: 2019年以来全过程人民民主研究述评
source: Journal of the Jinggangshan Cadre Academy of China, 2022 no. 5
paras: This literature review, published in the Journal of the Jinggangshan Cadre Academy of China in 2022, surveys scholarship on whole-process people's democracy since Xi Jinping first used the phrase in November 2019. Liang counts more than 1,400 related items on CNKI by June 2022, including over 850 journal articles. The review argues that the topic has quickly become a research hotspot with solid results, but that the work is limited in scope, comparison, empirical depth and method.

Liang organises the field into three clusters. The first covers meaning, features, status and significance: democracy centred on the people, completeness, institutional procedures, participatory practice, social effectiveness and innovation. The second covers the concept's historical, theoretical and realisation logics. The third covers practical paths: the people's congress system, consultative democracy and grassroots democratic practice, with examples from Guangzhou.

On the core debates, Liang reports that scholars define the concept by its comprehensiveness, in contrast to what they describe as the narrowed, election-centred "intermittent" democracy of the West. Scholars trace its roots to traditional Chinese ideas of people-based governance and to Marxist theories of democracy. Many hold that Party leadership is a necessary condition of its realisation and that the Party and the people's mastery of the country are not opposed. Several argue that consultative democracy followed by voting produces efficiency gains.

Liang identifies four weaknesses: homogeneous work that mostly interprets leaders' speeches, thin comparison with Western democracy, shallow practical research, and a narrow method that lacks surveys, statistics and case studies. The review proposes a wider temporal and international outlook, more attention to implementation problems, richer methods including cross-disciplinary and systematic research, and greater unity of understanding. Liang also notes some officials' bureaucratism and some citizens' passivity, and links research to building China's international discourse power on democracy. Read the original if you want a map of Chinese scholarly positions on whole-process people's democracy in 2019–2022, with names of the main authors and the field's self-criticism.
quoteEn: Existing scholarship mostly traces the historical evolution of people's democracy in China, or examines the institutional guarantees, mechanisms, practical forms and significance of whole-process people's democracy at home, and comparative research is somewhat lacking.
quoteZh: 学界现有成果多从历史维度梳理我国人民民主的历史演进过程，或者国内全过程人民民主的制度保障、体制机制、实践形式、重要意义等，横向比较研究稍显不足。

glossary.explanation: A concept first put forward by Xi Jinping in November 2019. Official discourse presents it as a form of socialist democracy covering election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight, in contrast with Western electoral democracy.
China's basic political system, in which people's congresses at each level are the organs of state power. The article calls it the main institutional vehicle of whole-process people's democracy.

A form of democracy based on consultation among Party, government, political parties and social groups, notably through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. The 19th Party Congress (2017) called it a distinctive form and strength of China's socialist democracy.

t: The basic guidelines for building a modern socialist country in all respects
zh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家的基本遵循
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 10 February 2023
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in February 2023, explains the five major principles set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the basic guidelines for building a modern socialist country in all respects. Xia argues that the task is great and arduous, carried out at a time when strategic opportunities coexist with growing risks and uncertainties. The principles are therefore presented as essential for meeting severe tests.

The piece takes the five principles in turn: upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership, keeping to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, the people-centred approach to development, deepening reform and opening up, and carrying forward the fighting spirit. Xia assigns each a role: fundamental guarantee, banner and direction, value stance, source of motivation, and spiritual outlook. Together they are described as a logically tight organic whole.

Xia argues that Party leadership is the defining feature and greatest strength of the system. In this account it lets Chinese modernization avoid the harms of capitalist modernization and ensures common prosperity and peaceful development. Western modernization is characterised as following the logic of capital and as bound up with plunder and exploitation, so Chinese modernization neither should nor can repeat it. Reform and opening up is called the key move that brought China abreast of the times, and the fighting spirit is framed as a feature of Marxism needed to face risks.

Xia concludes that the Party must uphold the authority of the Central Committee, follow the Four Cardinal Principles, rely on the people, deepen reform to turn institutional strengths into governance capacity, and stay vigilant while coordinating development and security. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style account of how the 20th Party Congress's five principles are explained to a Chinese readership.
quoteEn: The five major principles are the basic guidelines for building a modern socialist country in all respects. They cover its fundamental guarantee, banner and direction, value stance, source of motivation and spiritual outlook, and form a richly meaningful and logically tight organic whole.
quoteZh: 五个重大原则是全面建设社会主义现代化国家的基本遵循，分别涵盖了全面建设社会主义现代化国家的根本保证、旗帜方向、价值立场、动力源泉和精神面貌，是一个内涵丰富、逻辑严密的有机整体。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is contrasted with Western capitalist modernization.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all members of society, presented as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's system and path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and market-oriented reforms.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
Principles set out by Deng Xiaoping in 1979: the socialist path, the people's democratic dictatorship, Party leadership, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.

t: On the theoretical foundations of modern monetary policy
zh: 论现代货币政策的理论基础
source: Political Economy Review (Zhengzhi jingjixue pinglun), 2022 no. 5
paras: Modern monetary policy rests on Western monetary theory, which the authors trace back to the quantity theory of money. Li and Sun ask why a policy built on this theory has gained weight over decades of macroeconomic regulation, yet produces uncertain effects and cannot prevent periodic financial crises. Their answer, drawn from Marxist political economy, is that the quantity theory inverts cause and effect, so that policy based on it stays detached from the analysis of reproduction.

The article first describes the framework of narrow monetary policy, the shift from precious-metal to credit money, and two policy tendencies: single-target inflation targeting (the euro area, South Korea) and multi-target, New Keynesian-leaning frameworks (the US Federal Reserve, Japan), compared in a table of central banks. It then traces the quantity theory from Locke, Hume and Ricardo through Fisher, Marshall, Pigou, Wicksell, Keynes, Phillips, the new classical economists and Modern Monetary Theory. It ends with the limits of monetary policy and lessons for China.

The core claim is that prices are determined by value and that money supply is only an influencing factor. The authors list five defects of the quantity theory: it ignores money's function as a measure of value, ignores the social relations money represents, reverses causation, lacks a view of money as money capital, and misreads credit money, which is essentially a debt relation and is endogenous to production. Prices, interest rates and money stock are therefore functions of the reproduction process. In crises, the authors argue, monetary policy faces a dilemma: tightening cuts output and employment, while loosening worsens sectoral disproportions. They also say that indicators such as price levels do not register serious imbalances such as overcapacity, high leverage and property bubbles.

For China, the authors call for treating price changes as ultimately driven by value, respecting the conditions for the realisation of total social capital, and using monetary policy dialectically and in moderation. They also call for keeping a proper ratio between industrial and fictitious capital, with money directed mainly to material production. They regard supply-side structural reform as a return to a policy mix grounded in the labour theory of value, and reject treating real and value variables as separate policy targets. Read the original if you want a Marxist critique of the quantity theory and central-bank frameworks, together with policy implications drawn from the reproduction schemes.
quoteEn: Prices, interest rates and the like are themselves functions of the process of reproduction.
quoteZh: 价格、利率等本身就是再生产过程的函数。

glossary.explanation: A policy line announced by Xi Jinping in 2015. It aims to reduce overcapacity, excess inventory and leverage, and to improve the supply structure.
The Marxist doctrine that the value of commodities is determined by socially necessary labour time. The authors use it as the basis for an alternative monetary policy.
Marx's term for capital in financial form, such as stocks and bonds, that creates no value itself and claims a share of value produced in material production.

t: On common prosperity in spiritual life and the all-round development of the human being
zh: 论精神生活共同富裕与人的全面发展
paras: Liu Ying asks how common prosperity in spiritual life relates to the all-round development of the human being. Starting from Xi Jinping's 2021 statement that common prosperity covers both material and spiritual life and is highly unified with all-round human development, the article argues that the answer lies in the original context of Marx's theory. Marx formed the idea by criticising how private ownership under capitalism alienates spiritual life and so produces one-sided development. Liu concludes that in the new era, raising material living standards should go together with promoting common prosperity in spiritual life.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Marx's account of alienated spiritual life under capitalism and its consequences. The second discusses socialism and communism as the conditions that make spiritual common prosperity and all-round development possible, and the unity of the two. The third turns to practical measures for contemporary China.

Drawing on the 1844 Manuscripts, the Grundrisse, The German Ideology and Capital, Liu argues that labour alienation leads to alienation of spiritual needs, spiritual production and spiritual communication. These in turn make people's needs, social relations and individuality one-sided, turning them into "reified" beings. Liu holds that public ownership of the means of production and the abolition of forced division of labour remove the economic basis of this alienation. In the author's account, as material wealth grows, spiritual life carries more weight in human development, and eventually spiritual and material production converge. Liu treats present problems in China, such as money worship, hedonism and consumerism, as "growing pains" that socialist development will resolve.

Liu proposes four measures: strengthening the guiding role of core socialist values; raising the level of ideological and moral education; strengthening publicity on spiritual civilization, including through new media and internet governance; and improving the public cultural service system, including digital culture and greater investment in remote regions. The author presents these as ways to build people's spiritual home and advance all-round development. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar links the theory of alienation to current policy on cultural and ideological work under common prosperity.
quoteEn: In socialist and communist society, spiritual prosperity and the all-round development of the human being are internally unified.
quoteZh: 在社会主义社会和共产主义社会，精神富裕与人的全面发展是内在统一的。

glossary.explanation: A goal of socialism that the Party leadership has stressed, especially since 2021. It is presented as prosperity shared by all the people in both material and spiritual life.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at the national, social and individual levels. They are used in education and cultural work.
An official term for the cultural, ideological and moral side of social development, paired with material civilization. It is promoted through campaigns and propaganda work.

t: The contemporary value of the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists
zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系的时代价值
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks what the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists offers the Party today. Zhao argues that this body of spiritual wealth, running from the founding spirit to the spirit of poverty alleviation, is the "spiritual code" that has kept the century-old Party moving forward.

The piece is organised under three headings: the lineage supplies strength for the Party's self-reform, it shows why the Party's century of struggle succeeded, and it gathers the sources of strength for national rejuvenation. Zhao draws on the Zunyi Meeting, the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as examples.

Zhao treats the Party's courage in self-reform as the main thread running through the lineage. Marxism is called its soul, formed by combining Marxism's essence with fine traditional Chinese culture and the shared values of the people. The article also holds that the lineage developed around the theme of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, through the revolutionary, socialist construction, reform and new-era periods.

Zhao concludes that on the new journey the lineage should be turned into strength for taking on responsibility and into lasting motivation for strengthening the "four consciousnesses", the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds. Self-reform is meant to ensure the Party never changes in character. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary presents the Party's spiritual lineage after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: Courage in self-reform is a distinguishing mark separating the Communist Party of China from other parties, and also a clear main thread running through the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命是中国共产党区别于其他政党的显著标志，也是贯穿中国共产党人精神谱系的一条鲜明主线。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official term for the series of named "spirits" (e.g. the Jinggangshan spirit, the Yan'an spirit, the spirit of poverty alleviation) said to have emerged in the Party's history. It was formalised in Party discourse in the early 2020s.
An official concept for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself, stressed since the 18th Party Congress. Official English usually renders it as the Party's self-reform.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The Party slogan calling on members to uphold the core position of Xi Jinping on the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and standing after the humiliations of the modern period.

t: The Marxist classics' methodological critique of positivism
zh: 马克思主义经典作家对实证主义思潮的方法论批判
paras: How did Marx, Engels and Lenin criticise positivism, and where exactly did the two currents part ways? Guo and Fu argue that the nineteenth-century clash between positivism and Marxism began as a dispute over what philosophy is, carried over into methodology, and ended in opposed views of society and history. The critique varied in emphasis from Marx to Engels to Lenin, but the authors say it never altered the underlying epistemological position.

The article re-reads the classic texts of both camps and draws on existing scholarship. It treats positivism through Comte, Spencer and Mach, and argues that Chinese scholarship has compared the two currents without tracing the move from worldview to method or the internal changes within each. Its sections cover the philosophical basis of the critique, its main methodological dimensions, and its expression in conceptions of society and history, followed by a conclusion.

On philosophy, the authors argue that positivism rejects metaphysics but also discards philosophy's worldview function, confining knowledge to phenomena in a way they call neo-Humean. Marxism, by contrast, is said to sublate traditional philosophy, keeping Hegel's dialectic and the rational core of Feuerbach's materialism, and joining them in historical materialism. On method, Marx is presented as rejecting Comte's search for eternal social laws, since laws are historically specific. Engels is said to hold that positive science needs dialectical thinking and to find Comte's method mechanical and his classification of sciences unoriginal. Lenin is shown attacking Mach's reduction of matter to sensations as idealism. On history, positivism is said to ground progress in intellectual and moral change, to stress order, and to defend capitalism and class conciliation. Marxism is said to locate the basis of change in the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, and to look to revolutionary practice.

The authors conclude that the conflict concerns social goals and the means of achieving them as well as worldview and method. They hold that Marxism enriches itself by engaging rival theories, and that Marxist methodology should be applied consciously in both natural and social science. Read the original if you want a close, text-based account of how Marx, Engels and Lenin each criticised Comte, Spencer and Mach, as presented in Chinese Marxist scholarship.
quoteEn: Positivism overemphasises facts, places reason beneath objective fact, refuses to go beyond existing relations and denies history's own negativity, so that it can only compromise with reality and adapt to it passively.
quoteZh: 实证主义过分强调事实，把理性置于客观事实之下，拒绝超越现实关系，并否定历史本身的否定性，这样就只能与现实妥协，并消极地适应现实

t: Marx's critique of the productive presupposition of capitalist distribution relations
st: An inquiry into Notebook I of the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
zh: 马克思对资本主义分配关系的生产前提批判
zhSub: 关于《1844年经济学哲学手稿》笔记本Ⅰ的探讨
paras: Li Shumei asks how the young Marx, in Notebook I of the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, criticised bourgeois political economy's account of wages, profit and rent. The article argues that the economists described the income forms of different classes but never examined their presupposition, the separation of capital, landed property and labour. Marx, in Li's reading, traced distribution back to this separation and showed that it is necessary, essential and harmful only for the worker.

The article has four parts. The first treats wages and the separation itself, set against Adam Smith and Proudhon. The second examines capital's command over labour and the profit and accumulation that follow. The third follows landed property and rent from feudal holdings to capitalised property, including the debate over dividing estates. The fourth sets out the significance of Marx's critique, links it to Capital, and closes with remarks on China's current practice.

Li contends that Marx read wages as the result of the separation, not a free contract, since workers must sell their labour to live. In every state of society, whether declining, growing or at its peak, the worker stays in poverty. Capital is accumulated labour and the power to command others' labour, and competition concentrates it in few hands. Landed property follows the same path, and Marx concluded that both Proudhon's wage equalisation and the division of estates leave private ownership untouched. Li adds that Marx also exposed classical economics for valuing labour while despising the labourer, and that this critique prepared his later rejection of the 'trinity formula' in Capital. Marx's picture of free labour and free enjoyment, with land as 'true individual property', is read as anticipating the Communist Manifesto and Capital.

Li concludes that Notebook I is Marx's earliest text on production and distribution and has lasting theoretical value. Marx did not yet distinguish labour from labour-power, nor state the problem as the separation of producers from the means of production. The article then ties Marx's ideas to China, citing the primary stage of socialism, a basic economic system with public ownership as the mainstay, regulation of capital, distribution according to work, common prosperity and Chinese modernization. Read the original if you study the early Marx's economic thought, or how Chinese scholars link the 1844 Manuscripts to contemporary Chinese policy.
quoteEn: Looking past the outward appearance of income forms such as wages, profit and rent, Marx traced the capitalist productive presupposition, the separation of capital, landed property and labour, and showed how fatally this separation harms the workers' interests.
quoteZh: 马克思透过工资、利润和地租等收入形式的外观，追溯了资本、地产和劳动分离的资本主义生产前提，指明了这种分离对于工人利益的致命侵害。

glossary.explanation: An official thesis that China is still at an early, underdeveloped stage of socialism. It is used to justify a mixed economy with several forms of ownership.
A policy goal, stressed in Party discourse especially since the 2010s, of prosperity shared by all. It is pursued by narrowing regional, urban–rural and income gaps.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It is a central slogan of the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The socialist principle that individuals receive income in proportion to the labour they contribute. In China it is the mainstay of distribution alongside other forms.

t: The internal logic of the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists
zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系的内在逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 3 February 2023
paras: This short commentary asks how the "spiritual genealogy" of Chinese Communists came to be formed and developed. Zhao argues that it rests on three interlocking logics: theoretical, historical and practical. Understanding them, the author says, matters for carrying forward the Party's spiritual lineage and for achieving new successes in the new era.

The piece opens with the resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), which traces the genealogy to the great founding spirit of the Party. It then takes the three logics in turn, moving through the periods of the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era.

On the theoretical side, Zhao holds that the genealogy derives from Marxism and its revolutionary spirit, and that each stage of Marxism's adaptation to Chinese conditions, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, nurtured it. On the historical side, the author lists the spirits formed in each period: the Red Boat, Jinggangshan and Long March spirits before 1949; the Korean War resistance, Daqing and \"Two Bombs, One Satellite\" spirits afterwards; the reform and opening up, flood-fighting and women's volleyball spirits; and, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the poverty-alleviation, craftsmanship and anti-epidemic spirits. On the practical side, Zhao argues that these spirits were distilled from experience in leading revolution, construction and reform.

Zhao concludes that spirits formed in different periods together make up a complete genealogy expressing the Party's character. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style outline of how Party commentary periodises and classifies the named \"spirits\" of the Communist Party.
quoteEn: The spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists is a great collection of spirits that was conceived, formed and continually developed in the Party's great practice of leading revolution, construction and reform.
quoteZh: 中国共产党人精神谱系是在中国共产党领导革命、建设和改革的伟大实践 中，孕育形成和不断发展的伟大精神集合体。

glossary.explanation: A Party-theoretical term for the series of named "spirits" (such as the Long March spirit) said to have arisen in the Party's history and to be handed down. The 2021 history resolution traces it to the great founding spirit.
The policy course launched in 1978 that introduced market-oriented reforms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: The great founding spirit of the Party as the wellspring of the Communist Party of China's spirit
zh: 伟大建党精神是中国共产党的精神之源
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, Xu Jinghui takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the Party's centenary celebration (2021) that the great founding spirit is "the wellspring of the Communist Party of China's spirit". Xu argues that this founding spirit is the source, the nourishing spring and the common thread of the Party's whole genealogy of spirit.

The short commentary has three parts, one for each of these roles. It runs through the Party's historical periods: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. It names the spirits associated with each, including the Red Boat spirit, the Jinggangshan spirit, the Resisting US Aggression and Aiding Korea spirit and the "two bombs, one satellite" spirit.

Xu contends that the later spirits grew out of the founding spirit's convictions, fundamental purpose and good work style. In the author's account, each emerged from a concrete achievement: the Korean War victory, the nuclear and space breakthroughs, reform and opening up, the fight against Covid-19 and the Beijing Winter Olympics. The author then reads the four parts of the founding spirit as a "red bloodline": upholding truth and ideals, practising the original mission, fearless struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people.

Xu concludes that the founding spirit is the root and soul of the Party's spirit, giving direction and spiritual support against domestic and international risks in every period. The piece is a brief, affirmative statement of the official reading of this theme. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party commentary links the founding spirit to later named spirits.
quoteEn: The great founding spirit is the source of the genealogy of spirit of Chinese Communists.
quoteZh: 伟大建党精神是中国共产党人精神谱系的源头。

glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping set out on 1 July 2021: upholding truth and ideals, practising the original mission, fearless struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people. It is presented as the source of the Party's later spirits.
The official term for the series of named spirits (such as the Jinggangshan spirit) said to have formed in the Party's history and to share a common source.
Named after the boat on Nanhu Lake in Jiaxing, where the First Party Congress's final session was held in 1921. It stands for the Party's founding period.
A Party phrase for its stated aims of seeking the people's happiness and the nation's rejuvenation.

t: Distinctive features of the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists
zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系的鲜明特质
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks what characterises the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists. Ma describes it as a valuable legacy of the Party's century of struggle that expresses its fundamental purpose and fine traditions. The author argues that the spirit forged in different historical periods has distinct features yet forms an organic whole.

The piece identifies four features: fearlessness in sacrifice together with love of country and people; self-reliance and hard struggle; bold exploration and daring to be first; and upholding fundamental principles while innovating, joined with moral responsibility. It draws on the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and on examples such as the Nanniwan spirit and the Red Flag Canal spirit.

Ma presents patriotism as the core of the national spirit and links it to the Party's aim of serving the people wholeheartedly. Self-reliance is tied to the claim that China's problems must be answered by Chinese people on the basis of national conditions. In the new era, the author cites comprehensive deepening of reform and the anti-corruption campaign as expressions of daring to be first. Moral responsibility is said to be rooted in both traditional Chinese culture and Marxism, which Ma says transcends narrow nationalism, unilateralism and protectionism.

Ma concludes that this genealogy should be passed on to give Communists a continuing spiritual source for firm ideals and convictions. The author also presents China's conduct abroad as an example of the moral responsibility involved in building a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary summarises the character of the Party's spiritual tradition.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles while innovating is a basic principle contained in the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists.
quoteZh: 守正创新是中国共产党人精神谱系蕴含的基本原则。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: A set of named 'spirits' (e.g. the Great Founding Spirit, the Nanniwan spirit) that the Party presents as formed in successive periods of its history. It was formalised in official discourse around the Party's centenary in 2021.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012, calling for shared development and global governance.
The Communist Party of China's national congress held in October 2022, whose report is widely cited in official commentary.

t: Leadership of the Communist Party of China gives modernization its "Chinese" meaning
zh: 中国共产党领导赋予现代化“中国式”意涵
paras: This commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks what makes modernization "Chinese" in the phrase Chinese modernization. Xie Lixia and Li Bin answer that the leadership of the Communist Party of China is the decisive factor. In their account, the Party's leadership gives Chinese modernization four defining features and is what allows China to move closer to the centre of the world stage.

The authors trace the pursuit of modernization from the Party's founding through the early socialist exploration, the period of reform and opening up, and the new era under Xi Jinping. Each period is linked to a Party leader's formulation: the Four Modernizations, Deng Xiaoping's call to take a "Chinese-style" path, and Xi's statement that the modernization being pursued is socialist modernization led by the Party. The text is organised in four sections: socialism as the political meaning, Chinese characteristics as the paradigm, coordinated development as the philosophical trait, and common prosperity as the goal.

Xie and Li argue that Western powers presented Western, capitalist modernization as the universal model, and that the rise of socialism put a socialist banner on modernization. In their reading, the Party's insistence on independence and self-reliance produced a new paradigm, since no single model or universal standard of modernization exists. They present coordinated development as the Party's way of handling the principal contradiction of Chinese society, citing Mao Zedong's \"On the Ten Major Relationships\" (1956), the mid-1990s guidance on major relationships, and the \"Five-Sphere Integrated Plan\" since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Common prosperity is traced from early revolutionary aims through Deng's moderately prosperous society to the 2021 declaration that poverty alleviation had been won and a moderately prosperous society built, and the 2035 and mid-century targets.

The authors conclude that Party leadership is the key to Chinese modernization. They contrast its socialist character with capitalist modernization, its Chinese characteristics with the Western paradigm, its coordination with one-sided and distorted development, and its common prosperity with wealth for a minority. They claim this path offers developing countries a reference and contributes a Chinese approach to human civilisation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style account of how Party writers tie the four features of Chinese modernization to Party leadership across historical periods.
quoteEn: The key to Chinese modernization is the leadership of the Communist Party of China.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化的关键是中国共产党领导。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's development path, which the Party presents as distinct from Western modernization. Deng Xiaoping used a similar phrase in 1979, and it became central to Party theory after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official goal of shared wealth for all people, associated with socialism. It was stressed anew under Xi Jinping and is tied to the 2035 and mid-century targets.
A development goal introduced by Deng Xiaoping in the early 1980s, drawing on a classical Chinese notion. The Party declared it fully built in July 2021.
The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented economic reforms and opening China to foreign trade and investment.
The official framework, adopted at the 18th Party Congress (2012), for advancing economic, political, cultural, social and ecological progress together.

t: The solemn historical responsibility of contemporary Chinese Communists
zh: 当代中国共产党人的庄严历史责任
paras: Published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, this short commentary takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's statement that continually writing new chapters of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is the solemn historical responsibility of contemporary Chinese Communists. Guo Jianning argues that this is also the mission of philosophy and social science scholars, and that the report gives direction for theoretical innovation grounded in practice.

The piece is organised under three headings: the "two capabilities" (that Marxism works, and that Marxism adapted to China and the times works), the Two Integrations as the fundamental path, and the "six commitments" as the core of the ideas.

Guo contends that the Party's success rests ultimately on Marxism's scientific, practical, people-centred and open character and on the Party's own sustained adaptation of it, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Integrating Marxism with China's realities is said to have produced Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilisation, which the author describes as rejecting capital-centred, polarising Western modernization. Integrating it with fine traditional culture is presented as a matter of mutual connection, with examples such as "the people as the foundation of the state" and people-centred development. The "six commitments" (putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systems thinking, and a global vision) are described as the worldview and methodology running through the Thought.

Guo concludes that the six commitments should be studied as the key to the spirit of Xi Jinping Thought, so that Chinese Communists can keep advancing the adaptation of Marxism and write new chapters. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 20th Party Congress formulations were presented to scholars in early 2023.
quoteEn: Without five thousand years of Chinese civilisation, where would Chinese characteristics come from?
quoteZh: 如果没有中华五千年文明，哪里有什么中国特色？

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to apply and develop Marxism in line with Chinese conditions and contemporary developments. The 'times' element was added to the older 'Sinification of Marxism' wording.

Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is presented in Party documents as the fundamental path of adapting Marxism.

Six methodological principles identified in the 20th Party Congress report as the worldview and methods of Xi Jinping Thought: people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, problem orientation, systems thinking and a global vision.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
The official term for China's path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress and contrasted by officials with Western models.

t: Three dimensions of ecological thought in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
zh: 《1844年经济学哲学手稿》生态思想的三个维度
paras: Luo Junli asks what ecological thought can be found in the young Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, and what it offers in a period of worsening global ecological crisis. The article argues that the text contains an ecological outlook that can be read along three dimensions: nature, society and institutions. Together they run from the human–nature relation, through the capitalist roots of ecological crisis, to its resolution in communism.

The article is organised in three main sections followed by a short conclusion. The first deals with the dialectical relation between humans and nature. The second treats labour, alienated labour and private property as the social origins of ecological crisis. The third takes up communism as the way out. Luo draws mainly on Marx's own formulations in the Manuscripts, such as nature as the human being's "inorganic body" and the species-specific character of human production.

In the nature dimension, Luo argues that humans depend on nature for both material and spiritual needs, yet differ from animals in being self-conscious and active, producing "in accordance with the laws of beauty". In the social dimension, labour is the mediating link through which humans and nature produce and confirm each other, a relation Luo describes as objective activity. Under capitalism this link is alienated. Luo holds that alienated labour is the fundamental cause of ecological crisis and private property its direct cause, because nature becomes a mere profit-making instrument and science and human needs are alienated as well.

In the institutional dimension, Luo reads Marx's communism as the positive sublation of private property and human self-alienation, distinct from earlier crude communism. It brings two reconciliations: between humans and nature, and between people. Luo concludes that communism means both the full liberation of humanity and the full revival of nature, and that the Manuscripts remain a useful reference for easing present environmental problems. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language reading of the 1844 Manuscripts as a source for Marxist ecological thought, organised around alienated labour and communism.
quoteEn: Therefore, under conditions of alienated labour, humanity's unrestrained appropriation and use of nature is the root of ecological crisis.
quoteZh: 所以，异化劳动条件下，人类对自然无节制地占有与利用，是引发生态危机的根源。

glossary.explanation: Marx's term in the 1844 Manuscripts for labour under capitalism in which workers are estranged from their product, their activity, their species-being and other people. Luo extends it to the estrangement between humans and nature.
The Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: to abolish something while preserving and carrying forward its valuable content. Here it describes how communism supersedes private property.
Marx's notion that beings exist and confirm their essence only through objects they act upon. Luo uses it to describe humans and nature as mutual objects.
Marx's image in the 1844 Manuscripts for nature as the extension of the human body, on which human life depends.

t: The dialectics of technological innovation in Capital
zh: 《资本论》中技术创新思想的辩证法
paras: Wang Cheng asks how technological innovation should be understood in Capital and its manuscripts, where it forms an implicit line of thought. The article argues that Western economics, lacking dialectics, explains only the surface effects of innovation. Marx, in Wang's reading, treats innovation dialectically, as an expression of capital's essential character in the interaction of productive forces and relations of production.

The article has four parts. It first criticises Western readings of Marx as a technological determinist or evolutionist, covering Schumpeter's methodological individualism, paradigm-based models such as the Rae–Marx–Schumpeter growth idea, and David Harvey's structuralist reading. It then follows Hegel's logic of essence through Marx's work: the inner driving force (essence), the phenomenon, and actuality. A final part considers how capitalist innovation is transcended.

Wang's core claim is that the inner driving force of capitalist innovation is the reproduction of capitalist social relations, mediated by social labour as traced through Marx's three major manuscripts. Innovation is therefore not the same as productive-force progress. At the level of phenomenon, it appears as a contradiction between producing and realising surplus value. Wang reads this as a three-stage cycle of individual innovation, generalisation through competition, and a new round of innovation driven by the average rate of profit. Volume II is read as showing how innovation intensifies discontinuities in circulation, hides value transfer and deepens crises, while Volume III's falling profit rate completes the account. Wang concludes that Marx's dialectic differs from Hegel's closed circle by adding human agency.

Wang concludes that innovation has a dual character. It strengthens capital's control over workers, yet it creates the material basis of a future society and the conditions for overturning capitalist relations. Human beings, as the actors in innovation, move from enslavement by things toward real liberation and all-round free development, in what Wang calls an objective reversal of the logic of subjugation. Read the original if you want a Hegelian-dialectical reading of Marx's theory of technology, set against Schumpeterian and Harvey-style interpretations, with close reference to the Capital manuscripts.
quoteEn: In short, the inner driving force of capitalist technological innovation is the reproduction of capitalist relations.
quoteZh: 质言之，资本主义技术创新的内部动力是资本主义关系的再生产。

t: The basic demands and fundamental flaws of Proudhon's conception of justice
st: An analysis based on the materialist conception of history
zh: 蒲鲁东正义观的基本诉求和根本缺陷
zhSub: 以唯物史观为方法论基础的分析
paras: Research on Proudhon has concentrated on his theory of value and his reform schemes, and has paid less attention to his theory of justice. Wang and Wang argue that without understanding that theory one cannot understand the other two, and that it carries a petty-bourgeois appeal which still shapes ideas of justice today. Using the materialist conception of history as method, they contend that Proudhon's conception of justice is abstract, idealist and in the end a petty-bourgeois fantasy of turning back history.

The article follows three questions in Proudhon's work. First, why justice is 'necessary': for Proudhon it underlies law, institutions, order, cooperation and exchange. Second, what justice is: an eternal principle, human sociality, equality, and finally absolute equality of property. Third, how justice is to be realised: through a 'constituted value' theory and through a social form that keeps individual private ownership. Each section sets out Proudhon's position and then criticises it, mainly with Marx's texts, including Capital, the Grundrisse and The German Ideology.

On the first question, the authors argue that Proudhon inverts the relation between social life and ideas. In their account, ideas of justice reflect existing economic relations, and law and institutions are tools by which the ruling class consolidates a given economic order. On the second, they hold that Proudhon's demand to abolish property targets only bourgeois ownership based on exploiting others' labour. It leaves intact the property of small producers in simple commodity production, so his ideal of 'eternal justice' is drawn from the legal relations of commodity production.

On the third question, the authors raise three objections. Proudhon's theory ignores socially necessary labour time and treats the value of labour as a measure of value, which they say undermines the labour theory of value. Individual private ownership, they argue, inevitably develops into capitalist private ownership and polarisation. Equivalent exchange also holds only as a tendency and on average, so 'full' exchange of equal labour is utopian. The authors conclude that real equality would require abolishing commodity exchange and private ownership and building a society on public ownership of the means of production. Read the original if you want a Marxist critique of Proudhon's ethics and a view of how Chinese scholars use the materialist conception of history to assess petty-bourgeois theories of justice.
quoteEn: As a form of social consciousness, every conception of justice contains concrete content determined by the social relations in which the particular evaluating subject stands.
quoteZh: 作为一种社会意识形式，任何正义观念都包含着由特定的评价主体所处的社会关系所决定的具体内容。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist theory that the mode of production of material life conditions social, political and intellectual life. Chinese texts use it interchangeably with historical materialism.
Proudhon's term for a value whose proportions are fixed by labour time, intended to resolve the contradiction between use-value and exchange-value. He presented it as the basis of equal exchange.
Marx's concept of the labour time needed to produce a use-value under average social conditions. It determines the magnitude of a commodity's value.
In Marxist usage, the class of small independent producers and owners, such as artisans and small farmers. The article applies the label to Proudhon's outlook.

t: On the dissemination and Sinicization of the concept of revolution in the Communist Manifesto
zh: 论《共产党宣言》革命概念传播与中国化
paras: Taking up Wolfgang Fritz Haug's remark that the question of revolution is the "source code" of Marxism, the article asks how the Manifesto's concept of revolution was established, translated and adapted to the Chinese context. Dai and Pan argue that the classic passage on the tasks of proletarian revolution, which Lenin expounded in The State and Revolution, became the "revolution code" of the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that Chinese Communists gradually decoded it through practice.

The study has three parts. It first traces the European word revolution from Greek and Latin terms through the English, American and French Revolutions to Marx, Engels and Lenin. It then follows the Chinese word geming, its Japanese re-coining as a translation of revolution, and its return to China, tracked through early English–Chinese dictionaries from Morrison (1822) to 1916. The third part examines Chinese renderings of the Manifesto's key passage, from Zhu Zhixin and Cheng Shewo through Chen Wangdao and Li Da to the two Chinese translations of The State and Revolution.

The authors make three main moves. First, they hold that Marx treated revolution as the highest expression of class struggle, centred on state power and aimed at remaking the socio-economic structure, a sense that sets it apart from rebellion or dynastic change. Second, they argue that the Chinese term moved from its classical meaning of dynastic mandate-change to a positive modern concept through Japanese mediation, with reformers, democrats and liberals stressing different aspects. Third, they read successive translations as steadily deepening understanding: Chen's literal rendering left room for the new state form, Li Da cited Lenin to defend the dictatorship of labour against anarchist readings, and Ke Bonian's vernacular translation of The State and Revolution, which Mao Zedong carried with him, stressed the violent first step. The 1929 Manifesto of the Fourth Red Army is presented as the passage's practical application to Chinese land revolution.

The authors conclude that Chinese Communists clarified the defining features of proletarian revolution: smashing the old state machine, establishing a new state form, and reshaping ownership relations. They say the contemporary Chinese dictionary definition preserves this content, whereas Western scholars still dispute the term and a Webster's definition, in their account, describes only pre-proletarian political revolution. Read the original if you are interested in conceptual history, translation studies of the Manifesto, or how Chinese scholars narrate the Sinicization of Marxist revolutionary theory.
quoteEn: The essence of revolution is the highest expression of class struggle, its fundamental question is that of state power, and its ultimate goal is to transform the socio-economic structure.
quoteZh: 革命的实质是阶级斗争的最高表现，革命的根本问题是国家政权问题，最终目标是改造社会经济结构。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary circumstances. The article uses the shorter 'Sinicization' for the earlier historical process.

glossary.en: Manifesto of the Fourth Red Army
glossary.explanation: A proclamation issued in early 1929 by the Party organisation of the Red Fourth Army in the Soviet areas. The article reads it as applying the Manifesto's revolutionary tasks to China.

t: Visual imagery in Marx's narrative of historical materialism and its implications
st: The case of The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte
zh: 马克思唯物史观叙事的视觉形象呈现及其启示
zhSub: 以《路易·波拿巴的雾月十八日》一文为例
paras: Zhang Guoqi asks how Marx's historical-materialist narrative in The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte produces vivid visual images, and what that offers present-day China. The article argues that the images of bayonets, the Phrygian cap, the calendar, Napoleon's statue on the Vendôme column and the 'cackling of geese' are not literary decoration. In Zhang's reading they are the concrete form of a scientific analysis of French class struggle, and they show Louis Bonaparte as a 'mediocre and ridiculous' figure who staged a coup on his uncle's model.

The article has four parts. The first sets out three rules governing visual imagery in historical-materialist narrative: its scientific character, its value-orienting character and its practical character. The second reads the Brumaire through four devices: the buffoon figure, the decoding of the 'Napoleonic ideas', scenes suited to the characters, and symbolic props. The third examines the self-consistent logic behind these images, partly in contrast to Italo Calvino's account of how visual images arise. The fourth draws lessons for contemporary China.

Zhang's central claim is that visual images arise from real life, not from spontaneous fantasy. On this view the coup and its imagery reflect a specific economic base and the class struggle in France, which let a mediocre figure play the hero. Marx's images are tied to four principles: acting 'in the real world and with real means'; discovering the new world through criticism of the old; the aim of revolutionising the existing world; and the unity of interpreting and changing the world. Zhang adds that French workers lacked revolutionary theory and a strong leading class, and that Marx urged the peasantry to ally with the urban proletariat. Zhang also holds that such narrative must remain non-fictional, though artistic treatment is allowed.

Zhang concludes that this method offers guidance for telling China's story well, in line with Xi Jinping's call to highlight Chinese cultural features and the 'visual image of the Chinese nation'. The article also draws on the 20th Party Congress (2022) goal of presenting a credible, lovable and respectable China. Zhang calls on theorists to use concrete imagery to portray the Party's vanguard role and China as a responsible major country, and to cultivate young people as 'new people of the era' fit to carry out the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you study Marx's historical writings as narrative, or want to see how Chinese scholars link them to current ideological and cultural-communication work.
quoteEn: The generation of visual images cannot do without thought and imagination, but thought and imagination are products of the process of real life; the self-consistent logic of how visual images arise must therefore be understood from that process.
