quoteZh: 视觉形象的生成离不开思维和想象，但思维和想象是现实生活过程的产物，因此，要从现实生活过程去理解视觉形象生成的自洽逻辑。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely tied to Xi Jinping's 'Chinese Dream', of restoring China to national strength and international standing by the mid-21st century.
A slogan of Xi Jinping-era propaganda and external communication, calling for China's achievements and values to be conveyed effectively at home and abroad.

glossary.literal: narrative of the materialist conception of history
glossary.explanation: The author's term for historical narration grounded in historical materialism and in non-fictional facts, which seeks to reveal the underlying laws of social change.
A phrase from Xi Jinping-era Party documents for young people who are expected to be loyal to the Party and capable of carrying out national rejuvenation.

t: Engels's method of criticising Bakunin's "anti-authority theory" and its lessons
st: A textual study based on "On Authority"
zh: 恩格斯对巴枯宁“反权威论”的批判方法与启示
zhSub: 基于《论权威》的文本考察
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2022 no. 11
paras: How did Engels dismantle Bakunin's rejection of all authority, and what does his method offer today? Li Zijuan argues that in "On Authority", written in the 1870s after the defeat of the Paris Commune, Engels used dialectical and historical materialism to expose the idealist basis of Bakunin's anarchism. In Li's account, this also set out a Marxist theory of authority and a model for criticising erroneous currents of thought.

The article has three parts. It first reconstructs Bakunin's four core positions: an abstract, absolute notion of freedom; the equation of authority with the state and with evil; the absolute opposition of authority and autonomy; and the abolition of the state in place of proletarian revolution. It then examines how Engels answered each position through philosophy, history, dialectics and class standpoint. Finally it draws four methodological lessons, with a short survey of Western and Chinese thinkers on authority, including Weber and Follett.

Li's central claim is that Engels grounded authority in material production. Using examples such as the cotton mill and the railway, Engels showed that large-scale production requires a unified will, so that authority is an objective necessity. Subordination tends to shift from compulsion to voluntary acceptance. Li reads Engels as treating authority and autonomy as a dialectical unity of opposites whose scope changes with the stage of social development. Engels is also said to have argued that revolution is "the most authoritarian thing there is", that the Paris Commune fell for lack of centralisation and authority, and that Bakunin mistook the state rather than capital for the main evil. Li adds that Bakunin contradicted himself by running a secret organisation with strict discipline.

Li concludes that authority must be studied on a materialist basis, from a historical and class standpoint that rests on the people, and with a dialectical view of authority and autonomy. Theories of authority should be inherited critically and developed creatively. Li links this to the Party's maintenance of the authority of the Party Central Committee, arguing that it is compatible with grassroots self-government and regional ethnic autonomy, and sees authority and autonomy as a form of the relation between democracy and centralism. Read the original if you want a close, Party-theoretical reading of Engels's "On Authority" and of how it is used to defend the authority of the Central Committee.
quoteEn: Authority and autonomy stand in a relative relationship.
quoteZh: 权威和自治是相对的关系

glossary.en: the authority of the Party Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse stressing that the Central Committee holds unified leadership. The Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) listed institutions to uphold it.
China's system of residents' and villagers' committees, which the author cites as compatible with central authority.
The Chinese constitutional system granting autonomy to areas where ethnic minorities live in concentrated communities, within the unitary state.

t: Improving the distribution system to consolidate the foundational institution for promoting common prosperity
zh: 完善分配制度 夯实促进共同富裕的基础性制度
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 8 February 2023, this short commentary by Wei Zhimin and Yang Xiubo takes up how the distribution system can serve common prosperity. Starting from the 20th Party Congress report (2022), which calls the distribution system the foundational institution for promoting common prosperity, the authors argue that improving it is of great importance for the new journey ahead.

The article first gives three reasons why distribution matters, then sets out measures for each of the three levels of distribution. It closes its framing by stressing that common prosperity is a long historical process that cannot be achieved at one stroke.

Wei and Yang argue that the distribution system is the key to combining effective incentives with reasonable distribution: it must make the 'cake' bigger and also divide it well. They treat a distribution system with distribution according to labour as the mainstay and several modes coexisting as part of the basic socialist economic system, suited to the primary stage of socialism. They describe primary distribution as the foundation, redistribution as the safeguard and the third distribution as a supplement, and claim that together these form a 'three-wheel drive' of an efficient market, a capable government and a caring society.

For primary distribution, the authors call for raising the share of household income and of labour remuneration and for building an olive-shaped income structure. For redistribution, they propose improving taxation, equalising basic public services, strengthening transfer payments and regulating the order of income distribution. For the third distribution, based on voluntary charity, they call for supportive rules, charity law and oversight, and better public mobilisation. Read the original if you want a concise official-style outline of the policy measures linked to the three levels of distribution.
quoteEn: Primary distribution is the foundation and an important route to common prosperity; redistribution is the safeguard and an important means; the third distribution is a supplement and an auxiliary way.
quoteZh: 初次分配是基础，是促进共同富裕的重要途径；再分配是保障，是促进共同富裕的重要手段；第三次分配是补充，是促进共同富裕的辅助方式。

glossary.explanation: A goal of shared affluence for all, described in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism. It has been given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The official characterisation of China's present development stage, in which relatively underdeveloped productive forces are said to justify multiple ownership and distribution forms.
Distribution of resources through voluntary charity and philanthropy by enterprises, social organisations and individuals, in addition to market-based primary distribution and state redistribution.
An income pattern with a large middle-income group and small low- and high-income groups, presented as a policy goal.

t: Persisting in deepening reform and opening up to build a high-standard socialist market economy system
zh: 坚持深化改革开放 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), this commentary asks what a "high-standard socialist market economy system" means and how it is to be built. Zhou Shaopeng defines it as a socialist market economy in which a modern enterprise system with Chinese characteristics is combined organically with an effective market and a capable government. The piece first appeared in Guangming Daily on 7 February 2023.

The article opens by defining the economic system, the market economy system and the socialist market economy system, with resource allocation as the core criterion. It then takes up three requirements in turn: improving the modern enterprise system with Chinese characteristics, building a high-standard market system, and letting the government play its role better. It refers throughout to Xi Jinping's statements, the 20th Party Congress report and the 2022 Central Committee and State Council opinions on a unified national market.

Zhou treats the enterprise system as the micro-foundation of the economic system. In Zhou's account, a modern enterprise system rests on corporate legal personhood, limited liability and a governance structure of shareholders, board, supervisors and managers. The Chinese version adds Party leadership of state-owned enterprises, to be combined with the modern enterprise system, and Zhou lists five reform areas: shareholding reform, governance, cadre management, pay and personnel systems. A high-standard market system is described as unified, open, orderly and efficient. Zhou argues that it can help the economy withstand shocks and, in special circumstances, circulate internally. On government, Zhou assigns macroeconomic stability to the central government and public services and market supervision to local governments. The article stresses coordinating fiscal and monetary policy under the principle of seeking progress while maintaining stability, along with antitrust enforcement, removal of local protectionism and planning that guides investment and consumption.

Zhou concludes that a high-standard socialist market economy system will only be truly established if government is made capable ("有为政府") alongside effective markets and modern enterprises. The text is mostly a policy exposition, restating the Congress's directions with definitions and a list of measures. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese economists framed the post-2022 market-economy reform agenda, including state enterprise reform and the unified national market.
quoteEn: A high-standard socialist market economy system is a socialist market economy system that organically combines the modern enterprise system with Chinese characteristics, an effective market and a capable government.
quoteZh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制，就是中国特色现代企业制度与有效市场和有为政府有机结合的社会主义市场经济体制。

glossary.zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.pinyin: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
glossary.explanation: A formulation from the 20th Party Congress report (2022) for the next stage of improving China's market-based economic system under Party leadership.

glossary.zh: 中国特色现代企业制度
glossary.en: modern enterprise system with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The modern corporate system as adapted to China's basic economic system. It combines Party leadership of state-owned enterprises with corporate governance structures.
A term used with "effective market" (有效市场) to describe a government that actively performs its economic functions while the market plays the decisive role in resource allocation.
A policy goal set out in the 2022 Central Committee and State Council opinions. It aims to remove local barriers and unify market rules across China.
The general keynote of Chinese economic work since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It prioritises stability while pursuing progress.

t: Advancing economic theoretical innovation grounded in practice and making original contributions to developing Marxist political economy
zh: 不断推进实践基础上的经济理论创新为发展马克思主义政治经济学作出原创性贡献
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 31 January 2023, asks how Xi Jinping's economic thought contributes to Marxist political economy. Zhou Wen argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi has drawn on China's experience to put forward new ideas and strategies, which together form Xi Jinping Thought on economics. In Zhou's account, this body of thought upholds the basic principles and methods of Marxist political economy and makes important original contributions that open a new realm for it.

The article is organised under three headings: deepening understanding of the laws of socialist economic construction; answering major questions of China's economic development in the new era; and resolving the relationship between government and market.

Zhou argues that the stress on the Party's overall leadership of economic work enriches Marxist theory on the relation between economics and politics. The people-centred approach and the commitment to common prosperity are said to clarify the purpose of socialist production and the nature of the socialist economy. Treating public ownership as the mainstay, with multiple forms of ownership, distribution according to work as the mainstay, and the socialist market economy as the basic economic system is presented as an enrichment of Marxist market theory. The new development philosophy of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing is described as a systematic answer to questions of the purpose, driving forces and paths of development. Zhou claims that combining the market's "invisible hand" with the government's "visible hand" resolves a worldwide problem in economics and goes beyond both Western development models and mainstream Western economics.

Zhou concludes that this provides a basis for a Chinese economics with its own disciplinary, academic and discourse systems. The author calls for further research and practice on combining socialism with the market economy, so that an efficient market and a capable government work together better. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register statement of how Chinese commentators present Xi's economic thought as an original contribution to Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: How to handle the relationship between government and market is the core question of a market economy, and also a worldwide problem in economics.
quoteZh: 如何处理好政府和市场的关系，是市场经济的核心问题，也是一个经济学世界性难题。

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, formally put forward after the 18th Party Congress and presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought. It covers Party leadership of the economy, people-centred development and the new development philosophy.
A guiding framework announced in 2015 comprising innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. It is meant to steer China's economic policy.
An official goal of shared wealth for all members of society, presented as an essential feature of socialism and emphasised in Party policy under Xi Jinping.

The official term for China's core economic arrangements: public ownership as the mainstay alongside other ownership forms, distribution according to work as the mainstay, and the socialist market economy.

glossary.en: an efficient market and a capable government
glossary.literal: effective market and government that accomplishes things
glossary.explanation: A formula in Chinese policy discourse for the proper pairing of market mechanisms with active state guidance.

t: Deeply grasping the decisive significance of the "Two Establishes"
zh: 深刻领悟“两个确立”的决定性意义
paras: Li Junru takes up the Party's call, issued at the 20th Party Congress (2022), to understand the "Two Establishes" in depth. The commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 7 February 2023, argues that establishing Xi Jinping as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and establishing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the guiding ideology, is of decisive significance for the Party and country in the new era and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece is built in three parts under separate headings. The first presents the Two Establishes as the decisive factor behind the changes of the past decade. The second argues that they reflect the shared wish of the whole Party, the military and the people of all ethnic groups. The third names grasping them as the most pressing task of the new journey and sets out what Party members should do.

Li's central claim is that the achievements of the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012) came under the leadership of the Central Committee with Xi as its core and under the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought. The author lists economic gains, poverty reduction, the anti-corruption struggle, ideological work, disaster relief and epidemic control, and attributes each to Xi's personal leadership. Li then grounds the Two Establishes in history and popular will. Citing the Zunyi Conference and Deng Xiaoping's remark that a leadership collective needs a core, Li holds that a Party without a core drifts into weak leadership. Li also reports that at the Sixth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2016), localities, departments and the military all wanted Xi's core status made explicit. The Thought is said to answer the major questions of the era and to give practice its direction.

Li concludes that, amid what the text calls great changes unseen in a century and possible \"black swan\" and \"grey rhino\" events, the Party needs a helmsman and a compass. Li calls on Party members to defend Xi's core status \"emotionally, ideologically, politically, organisationally and in action\" and to strengthen centralised, unified leadership. Li also urges them to apply the Thought's worldview and methodology and to turn it into practical work. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of how the Two Establishes were explained to Party cadres after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The "Two Establishes" are a major political achievement of the Party in the new era and the decisive factor behind the historic achievements and historic changes in the cause of the Party and the country.
quoteZh: “两个确立”是党在新时代取得的重大政治成果，是推动党和国家事业取得历史性成就、发生历史性变革的决定性因素。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted in the Party's 2021 historical resolution and stressed at the 20th Party Congress. It refers to establishing Xi Jinping's status as core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party constitution in 2017 as a guide to action.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-standing official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.

t: Firmly grasping the requirements of our times for unity and struggle
zh: 牢牢把握团结奋斗的时代要求
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 11 January 2023, interprets "unity and struggle" as a key phrase of the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Li notes that Xi Jinping, in discussion with the Guangxi delegation, listed "five firm grasps", one of which is firmly grasping the requirements of the times for unity and struggle. Li argues that the Party and people must understand its strategic significance, political meaning and practical demands in order to advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first presents unity and struggle as the most distinctive spiritual hallmark of the Party and the Chinese people. The second sets out what unity and struggle mean in the new era, namely acting under the Party's banner. The third explains how the "Three Musts" from the Congress report apply to the task.

In the first part, Li traces the roots of unity and struggle to some 5,000 years of civilisation and to the resistance to aggression in modern times. Li also grounds it in the Party's character: its lofty ideal, its guiding theory, its purpose of serving the people, and its strict organisation and discipline. The second part calls for uniting will and action through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It also calls for closer unity around the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core, supported by the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. Li adds four further kinds of unity: within the Party, between Party and people, between the military and government and between the military and civilians, and among Chinese at home and abroad. The third part reads the Three Musts as, respectively, the source of strength, the proper spirit and the essential feature of unity and struggle. These are staying true to the founding mission, remaining modest and plain-living, and daring and being skilled at struggle.

Li concludes that the Party's central task is to lead the people in building a modern socialist country and advancing national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. In Li's account, a complex international and domestic environment, including the Russia–Ukraine conflict, rising anti-globalisation and unresolved domestic problems, makes unity and struggle indispensable. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-theory commentary in early 2023 presented the 20th Congress's unity-and-struggle theme and its links to the Two Establishes and the Three Musts.
quoteEn: Unity and struggle is the most distinctive spiritual hallmark of the Communist Party of China and the Chinese people.
quoteZh: 团结奋斗是中国共产党和中国人民最显著的精神标识

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2022 Party resolution and 20th Congress documents. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as core of the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of his thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The official term for China's path to modernisation, highlighted at the 20th Party Congress as the means to national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term national goal in Party discourse, associated with restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
A formula in the 20th Congress report: remain true to the founding aspiration, be modest and plain-living, and dare to struggle. It extends Mao Zedong's 1949 "Two Musts" on modesty and hard struggle.

t: Continuing to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 不断谱写马克思主义中国化时代化新篇章
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2023, Yang Genqiao takes up the task of continuing to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, which the author calls the solemn historical responsibility of today's Communist Party members. Yang argues that the 20th Party Congress (2022) supplied the fundamental guidance for this task through the Two Integrations and its account of the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The short commentary first explains why Marxism matters to the Party and the country, citing the Congress report's claim that it is Marxism adapted to China and to the times that "works". It then reviews the Party's century-long record of theoretical innovation, from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory to Xi Jinping Thought. A final section sets out what must be done on the new journey.

Yang's central claim is that the Party's achievements rest on continually updating Marxism. Quoting Xi Jinping, Yang reads Marxism's "localization" and "timeliness" as its spatial and temporal dimensions of development. Xi Jinping Thought is presented as the latest result of this process, credited with helping the Party meet risks and produce historic changes since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Yang rejects both dogmatism and pragmatism: the classics' words should not be mechanically applied to today's China, since present conditions exceed what Marx, Engels and Lenin could imagine.

Yang calls for adherence to Marxism's guiding position together with theoretical innovation grounded in practice. This means applying the six "musts" of the Thought's worldview and methodology: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, problem orientation, systems thinking, and a global outlook. It also means pursuing the Two Integrations, linking Marxism to China's concrete realities and to its fine traditional culture. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of how the Party presents its theoretical lineage and the 20th Congress's guidance on Marxist innovation.
quoteEn: Today, the breadth and depth of change in the times and of China's development far exceed what the Marxist classic authors could have imagined, and we cannot simply take what Marx, Engels and Lenin said back then and force it onto China's reality today.
quoteZh: 今天，时代变化和我国发展的广度深度远远超出了马克思主义经典作家当时的想象，我们不能简单拿马克思、恩格斯、列宁当年所说的话来套今天的中国实际

glossary.explanation: The principle that Marxism must be combined with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It was prominent in Xi Jinping's speeches and in the 20th Party Congress report.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

t: Fully, accurately and comprehensively applying the new development philosophy to drive high-quality development
zh: 完整、准确、全面贯彻新发展理念 着力推动高质量发展
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 20 January 2023, this short commentary by Lu Mingchuan and Zhang Yixiu takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report and the 2022 Central Economic Work Conference. Both stressed applying the new development philosophy and promoting high-quality development. The authors argue that this is a necessary task for the Party's central mission in the new era and on the new journey.

The article is organised around the five elements of the new development philosophy: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. Each receives a section that links the principle to a set of policy priorities.

On innovation, the authors call for new mechanisms, focused national science and technology projects, and a stronger role for enterprises, together with self-reliance in science and technology and home-grown talent. On coordination, they tie the task to the principal contradiction in Chinese society and urge a modern industrial system, rural revitalisation and regionally coordinated development. They also propose green and low-carbon transition, with carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, and high-standard opening up that relies on the domestic market while drawing in global resources.

On sharing, which the authors call an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics, they list priorities. These are employment, basic public services, social security and a distribution system that supports common prosperity. They also propose raising low incomes, expanding the middle-income group and regulating excessive and illegal income. The text works as a policy outline built on official documents. Read the original if you want a compact summary of how the five concepts were translated into policy priorities in early 2023.
quoteEn: Further strengthening innovation capacity is both a precondition for safeguarding development security and the key to achieving high-quality development.
quoteZh: 进一步增强创新能力，既是保障发展安全的前提，也是实现高质量发展的关键。

glossary.explanation: A framework introduced by Xi Jinping in 2015 that names five principles for development: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
The official goal, set out in 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to development stressing quality, efficiency and sustainability.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, which the Party has stressed in recent years, including through distribution reform.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop the rural economy, society and environment and narrow the urban–rural gap.
China's declared goals of reaching peak carbon emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060.

t: Taking the Chinese modernization path of common prosperity
zh: 走共同富裕的中国式现代化道路
paras: Following the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which describes Chinese modernization as modernization for the common prosperity of all the people, Li Heliang argues that China must unwaveringly follow a path of Chinese modernization built on common prosperity. The piece, a short commentary first published in Guangming Daily on 3 January 2023, holds that this path comprehensively transcends the modernization model dominated by the logic of capital.
The article has three parts: why common prosperity goes beyond Western capital logic, why it is a defining feature of Chinese modernization, and how it is to be advanced in practice.

In Li's account, Western modernization, resting on capitalist production, is built on exploitation and deprives proletarians of the right to modernize. China, by contrast, keeps public ownership as the mainstay, distribution according to labour as the main form, and the central place of labour, and since the 18th Party Congress (2012) has eliminated absolute poverty and built a moderately prosperous society. Li then analyses common prosperity by its subject, content, process and goal. It is not egalitarian sameness. It covers material and spiritual life and all five forms of civilization. It requires both creating and fairly distributing wealth, and it provides the basis for the free and comprehensive development of the human being.

Li proposes three tasks: upholding the Party's overall leadership without wavering, improving the top-level design across the five-sphere integrated plan (including the Two Unwaverings, ecological civilization and social governance), and advancing with historical initiative and creativity, guided by dialectical and historical materialism. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated theorists link Chinese modernization, common prosperity and a critique of capital logic.
quoteEn: Achieving common prosperity is an essential requirement of Chinese modernization and an inevitable choice for fully building a modern socialist great country.
quoteZh: 实现共同富裕是中国式现代化的本质要求，是全面建成社会主义现代化强国的必然选择。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, foregrounded in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal of shared wealth for all people, described as an essential requirement of socialism. Official usage stresses that it does not mean uniform equality.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A long-standing Chinese development goal of general, moderate well-being. The Party declared it fully achieved in 2021, the first centenary goal.
The official overall layout of socialism with Chinese characteristics, covering the economic, political, cultural, social and ecological spheres.

t: A comparative study of Critique of Hegelian Philosophy and Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right
st: With remarks on the origin, birth and development of historical materialism
zh: 《黑格尔哲学批判》与《黑格尔法哲学批判》比较研究
zhSub: 兼论历史唯物主义的源起、诞生和发展
source: Journal of Chongqing Second Normal University, 2019 no. 2
paras: Chai Peng and Ding Sanqing compare Ludwig Feuerbach's Critique of Hegelian Philosophy with Marx's Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, the first systematic critiques of Hegel written by each thinker. They ask what the two texts reveal about the link between Feuerbach's materialism and historical materialism. Their thesis is that Feuerbach laid a philosophical foundation but stopped at materialism in general, whereas Marx's unfinished text is a transitional work that already contains the germ of historical materialism.

The article has four parts. It first examines Feuerbach's breakthrough, omissions and misplaced emphasis, then Marx's text: its transitional character, its layout and its limits. The third part compares the two works on six points: aim, standpoint, method, subject matter, significance and limitations. A short conclusion draws out the consequences for the origins of historical materialism. The authors draw on Engels, Althusser, and Chinese scholars such as Han Lixin and Zhu Xueping.

On Feuerbach, the authors argue that he traced Hegel's roots in Fichte, Schelling and Kant. By inverting subject and predicate and taking a genetic approach, he made sensuous, real being the starting point of philosophy. But he discarded Hegelian dialectics along with idealism. His 'natural man' therefore stayed an isolated, unhistorical figure, and he relapsed into dependence on religious morality when he addressed social change. On Marx, they stress the context of writing: material-interest disputes at the Rheinische Zeitung, a growing sense of the Prussian state's class character, and Engels's Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy. Marx criticised Hegel's monarchy, bureaucracy and estates assembly and argued for democracy. Yet he still hoped to overcome political alienation through the state, and his claim that civil society is the state's presupposition was, in the authors' view, only a logical inference from the inversion.

The authors conclude that Feuerbach's limits come from his inability to escape modern idealism and metaphysics. Marx's limits come from a mind in transition, where Hegelian, Feuerbachian and historical-materialist tendencies collided. Marx later developed 'civil society determines the state' in the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher and The Holy Family. He then turned to material production and economic relations as the real starting point. For the authors, the 1843 manuscript shows the beginnings of historical materialism. Read the original if you study the young Marx's break with Hegel and Feuerbach, or want a structured six-point comparison from a Chinese perspective.
quoteEn: The profound significance of Marx's Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right lies mainly in the field of historical materialism.
quoteZh: 马克思《黑格尔法哲学批判》的深刻意义则主要在于历史唯物主义领域。
keywords: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

t: The historical and theoretical foundations of "Marxism works"
zh: “马克思主义行”的历史和理论基础
paras: The report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) states that the ultimate reason the Party succeeds and socialism with Chinese characteristics is good is that Marxism works, specifically Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Hu Changshuan takes up how this claim should be understood. The author argues that "Marxism works" and "sinicized, contemporary Marxism works" are essentially unified, and that grasping this is a theoretical precondition for further advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has three parts. The first treats the historical and theoretical grounds for confidence in Marxism as such. The second treats the grounds for confidence in sinicized, contemporary Marxism. The third explains how the two relate, drawing on Marx's remarks on theory and practice.

In the first part, Hu locates the strength of Marxism in its scientific and elevated character, and in its practical value. Scientific character means that Marxism emerged from the best natural and social science of its day and revealed general laws of social development. Its elevated character lies in its proletarian standpoint and its commitment to human emancipation. In practice, Hu says, it moved socialism from utopia to science and from theory to reality. The second part holds that the 20th Party Congress conclusion expresses the achievements of practice and the theoretical results of Marxism's adaptation, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Hu reads the Soviet collapse as confirming the conclusion, because it resulted from departing from Marxism. The third part presents a two-way relation. Sinicized Marxism shares with Marxism the logic of historical materialism, the aim of communism, the people's standpoint and the dialectical-materialist method. Hu also argues that most other Marxisms remain at the level of theory and have not realised its practical essence.

Hu concludes that studying the classics and the conditions in which Marxism arose will deepen conviction in sinicized Marxism. Conversely, sinicized Marxism must be understood on a larger world-historical scale, where it embodies the unity of theory and practice. The author describes Xi Jinping Thought as the most influential, creative and practically significant Marxism in the world today. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party theorists justify the claim that Marxism works and the standing of sinicized Marxism within global Marxism.
quoteEn: Sinicized, contemporary Marxism working is, in essence, Marxism working.
quoteZh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义行，在本质上就是马克思主义行

glossary.explanation: A phrase from the 20th Party Congress report (2022), which says that the Party's success and the merits of socialism with Chinese characteristics ultimately rest on the efficacy of Marxism. The article treats it as a historical conclusion.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Official texts describe it as the Marxism of contemporary China and of the twenty-first century.
The official name for China's path, system and theory of socialism since reform and opening up. It was introduced by Deng Xiaoping in the early 1980s.

t: Marx's view of world history and its contemporary value
zh: 马克思的世界历史观及其当代价值
paras: Wu Hongzheng asks what Marx's view of world history is and what it offers today. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's speech at the centenary of the Communist Party (2021), the article argues that the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics must be understood within the process of world history. It frames the problem through three basic questions: whether world history is created by human practice or by a supernatural power, whether its laws can be known, and whether it should lead to peace or destruction.

The article has three parts. The first sets Marx's critique of German classical philosophy, mainly Kant and Hegel, against these three questions. The second defines the core of Marx's view of world history, drawing on the Theses on Feuerbach, Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, The German Ideology and the Communist Manifesto. The third draws out its present-day value for building a community with a shared future for mankind.

Wu argues that Kant locates world history in a hidden plan of nature and Hegel in the Absolute Spirit, so that both stand outside history and regard its laws as unknowable or fatalistic, and neither commits to lasting peace. Marx, in Wu's account, reverses this: humans create world history through practice, its laws are knowable as historical materialism, and the world is to be changed, not merely interpreted. World history begins with the "universal intercourse" produced by capital's expansion, and the proletariat, as a "universal class" without particular interests, is its creating subject. Private ownership is identified as the root of conflict, so peace requires its abolition.

Wu concludes that three lessons follow today. Peace and development remain the theme of the age, while the Hegelian priority of national interest survives in Western "cold war thinking" and zero-sum logic. Historical nihilism, which Wu calls an expression of the capital-led view of history, must still be fought. A community with a shared future for mankind needs the "common values of all humanity" as its spiritual basis, and Wu presents it as inheriting Marx's call to change the world. Read the original if you want a Chinese reading of Marx's critique of Kant and Hegel that is tied directly to current Chinese foreign-policy language.
quoteEn: A view of world history is fundamentally a set of values.
quoteZh: 世界历史观根本上是一种价值观。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2013, calling for countries to cooperate on shared security, development and governance. Chinese official texts present it as an ideal of international relations.

glossary.literal: shared values of the whole of humanity
glossary.explanation: A formula Xi Jinping put forward in 2015 and restated in 2021: peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. Official sources present it as an alternative to Western "universal values".

In Chinese Party discourse, a label for views that question or reject the official account of history, especially of the Communist revolution and socialism. Here Wu gives it a broader philosophical meaning, as denial that history has meaning for humanity.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of socialist development since the reform era.

t: Scientifically understanding and guarding against ideological risks in the new era
zh: 科学认识和防范新时代意识形态风险
source: China Party and Government Cadres Forum (Zhongguo dangzheng ganbu luntan), 2023 no. 1
paras: Taking up the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to safeguard ideological security and strengthen the capacity to prevent ideological risks, Zhang asks what such risks actually are and how they should be handled. The article argues that ideological risk is above all an endogenous problem: a gap between a ruling ideology and social practice, not mainly the effect of outside influence. Zhang holds that mishandled ideological risk could delay or even interrupt the building of a modern socialist country.

The article has three parts. The first defines the essence of ideological risk, drawing on Marx, Sartre and the notion of ideology as the ruling class's systematised thought. The second sets out basic principles for guarding against such risk in the new era. The third proposes four practical paths, quoting Xi Jinping's remarks on risk prevention throughout.

Zhang's central move is to define ideological risk as the ruling ideology's inability to answer major problems in practice, which leaves it "floating" and powerless. In this reading, an "internal tension" between theory and practice is a source of renewal if turned into productive "internal tension" (tension as creative force), but it makes a crisis logically inevitable if ignored. The principles that follow are: uphold Marxism's guiding position through four kinds of research (textual, practical, absorptive and anticipatory); use institutional confidence and the mutual shaping of ideology and institutions; and strengthen communication power to win discourse power at home and abroad, with zero tolerance for erroneous trends. The practical paths are responsibility and a sense of duty among those in charge, monitoring and early warning (using a "social combustion theory" and the stages of public-opinion development), scientific and refined governance moving towards intelligent governance, and attention to timing, degree and effect so that small risks do not grow into systemic ones.

Zhang concludes that guarding against ideological risk is systematic work. It requires continuous innovation in mainstream ideology, institutional safeguards, effective propaganda and education, and accountable officials. The author presents the Party's ideological innovation since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as a successful precedent. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account, written for cadres, of how ideological risk is conceptualised and managed under Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: Ideological risk, in the final analysis, is mainly not an external risk but an endogenous one, arising from a significant deviation between the ideology's own practical adjustment and its innovation to keep pace with the times.
quoteZh: 意识形态风险，说到底主要不是外在的风险，而是意识形态自身的现实调试和时代创变之间出现了重要偏差而导致的内源性风险。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Party discourse for protecting the dominant position of Marxism and the Party's ideology against threats at home and abroad. It is treated as part of national security.
The capacity to shape public narratives and set the terms of debate, domestically and internationally. Chinese writers often link it to a country's political and economic strength.
Zhang's term for the strain that arises when an ideology lags behind practice. He treats it as a driver of innovation if addressed and a source of risk if neglected.
Confidence in China's socialist institutions, one of the Party's four 'confidences' (path, theory, system, culture).

t: The civilizational implications of Marx's theory of Eastern society and its contemporary significance
zh: 马克思东方社会理论的文明论内涵及其当代启示
paras: Duan Feifei and Che Yuling ask what Marx's late writings on Russia and the East contribute to thinking about civilization today. They argue that Marx's idea of 'skipping the Caudine Forks' was a civilizational proposal grounded in the particular form of Eastern society, not a universal law of development. In their account, this idea is being continued in practice by Chinese modernization, which they present as a new type of civilization.

The article has three sections. The first asks how an Eastern civilization is possible, examining Russia's geography, culture and communal landownership. The second revisits Marx's 1850s–1880s engagement with India and Russia, including his correspondence with Vera Zasulich and the 1877 letter to the editors of Otechestvennye Zapiski. The third turns to the present, discussing Western capitalist civilization, Fukuyama and Derrida, and the community with a shared future for mankind.

The authors argue that Marx moved from an early Eurocentric view, in which the bourgeoisie subordinates East to West, to treating the East as a coexisting civilization. They locate the key difference in ownership: in their reading, the absence of private landownership is the 'key' to the East, as Engels put it. Marx's view of the Russian village commune shifted from scepticism to conditional affirmation. He saw its dual character, combining communal and private elements, as a source of both vitality and dissolution, and held that it could become a point of social renewal only with a Russian revolution and by absorbing Western material achievements. The authors say Marx explicitly limited the 'historical inevitability' of capitalism's rise to Western Europe.

The authors conclude that the Russian attempt was difficult but did not disprove the proposal, and that China is realizing it by developing socialism without repeating capitalism's evils. They describe the community with a shared future for mankind as sublating capitalist civilization through plural civilizations, open cooperation, ecological balance and 'mutual learning' in place of civilizational conflict. They claim the Chinese approach has world-historical significance comparable to English industry, French politics and German philosophy. Read the original if you want a Chinese philosophical reading of Marx's late Russian texts and of how they are used to ground claims about a new form of human civilization.
quoteEn: The Chinese approach, like English industry, French politics and German philosophy, has world-historical significance.
quoteZh: 中国方案如同英国的工业、法国的政治和德国的哲学一样具有世界历史意义。

glossary.en: the community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013. It calls for shared global governance, cooperation and respect for different political systems and civilizations.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models and as a new form of human civilization.
Marx's phrase in his late writings on Russia, referring to the possibility that a society might bypass the capitalist stage and its sufferings. It alludes to the Roman defeat at the Caudine Forks.
The Hegelian and Marxist concept (Aufhebung) of simultaneously negating, preserving and transcending an earlier form.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: A critique of the fragmentation syndrome of historical nihilism
zh: 历史虚无主义的碎片化症候批判
paras: Li Jinrong takes up a feature that scholars have noticed in historical nihilism: its fragmentation. The article argues that historical nihilists break up holistic historical thinking into disconnected pieces, in their minute focus, cut-and-paste narration, fragmented communication and splintered value judgements. Li holds that merely describing this negatively is not enough, and that it must be analysed through historical materialism in order to clear away its ideological space and secure ideological security in the new era.

The article is organised around four dimensions in which fragmentation operates: historical facts, historical laws, historical narrative and historical action. Each of the first four sections names what is dissolved (certainty of facts, necessity of laws, wholeness of narrative, consciousness of action) and the resulting effect on the public (cognitive confusion, wavering conviction, flippant speech, practical retreat). It draws on Ranke, Collingwood, Becker, Hayden White, Karl Popper, Lyotard and Derrida as Western sources, and on Marx, Engels, Lenin and Lukács as counterweights. A final section sets out four countermeasures.

Li's central move is to argue that nihilists exploit relativism and positivism: they treat texts as free interpretation, mistake selected fragments of evidence for facts, and use contingency and individual experience to deny regularity in history. Against this, Li defends the unity of objective and subjective in historical knowledge and the interplay of necessity and chance in historical events. Li also holds that micro-narrative and individual narrative, set against grand and collective narrative, leave history as 'free-flowing grains of sand' with no theme or mainstream. The article treats abstract human-nature theory as a vehicle for this, citing literary works that dwell on desire and portray revolution as mere violence, and online short-video platforms where history is commercialised. Li says these erode shared memory and the Party's sense of historical initiative, while distinguishing them from legitimate micro-history.

Li proposes four measures. These are to end fragmented Party-history study in favour of systematic study, to keep historical research holistic under a grand historical outlook, to improve governance of online dissemination, and to build a multi-actor system for resisting historical nihilism. The article closes by calling for the historical initiative of the Party to be exercised in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how current Chinese Marxist scholarship frames historical nihilism as a problem of method, narrative and media, and how it ties that critique to ideological security.
quoteEn: Historical laws are precisely the cognition of historical universality contained within particular, individual appearances.
quoteZh: 历史规律恰恰是包含在特殊个别表象中的历史普遍性认知。

glossary.explanation: In Chinese official and scholarly usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's history, revolution and socialist achievements. It is widely criticised in Party ideology work.
The Marxist theory of history, which explains social change through material production and relations of production. The article uses it as the standard for analysing nihilist fragmentation.
A concept associated with Xi Jinping that stresses viewing history across wide time and space and in its overall mainstream. Li presents it as the tool for criticising fragmented history.
A concept in Chinese Party discourse about protecting the dominant Marxist ideology from perceived erosion by hostile or erroneous ideas.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: From digital inequality back to Marx
st: Contemporary foreign Marxist critiques of digital capitalism
zh: 从数字不平等到重新回到马克思
zhSub: 当代国外马克思主义学者对数字资本主义的批判
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 29 December 2022
paras: This newspaper commentary by Lan Jiang asks how contemporary Marxist thinkers outside China understand digital capitalism and what remedy they propose. Lan argues that these scholars find digital technology and biopolitics deepening inequality and hollowing out human existence, and that they converge on a return to Marx, above all to the critique of private ownership.

The piece opens with Etienne Balibar's 2021 remark that capitalist productive forces have reached a 'totalising stage' touching every individual life, and with Nancy Fraser's 2022 image, in Cannibal Capitalism, of capitalism as a snake devouring its own tail. It then moves through three steps: the widening inequalities of digital capitalism, the 'scorched earth' of life under it, and the call to return to Marx. Thinkers discussed include Habermas, Giddens, Yuval Noah Harari, Guy Standing, Jonathan Crary, Alain Badiou, Fraser and Christian Fuchs.

On inequality, Lan contrasts the neoliberal-era faith in dialogue and deliberative democracy (Habermas, Giddens) with the 'digital divide' and with monopoly platforms that control data and algorithms. After the Covid-19 pandemic, Lan says, biological and medical data become objects of capital, so that the wealthy can buy enhanced bodies while a 'useless class' of precarious workers (Standing's precariat) falls behind. Lan reads this as a shift from spatial to biological inequality. Drawing on Crary's Scorched Earth and 24/7: Late Capitalism and the Ends of Sleep, Lan then describes capital's round-the-clock control of bodies and the abstraction of life into screens, user identities and data, which leaves people rootless.

As the remedy, Lan presents Badiou's September 2022 argument that the problem lies not in digital technology but in the capitalist, especially financial, monopolisation of data and algorithms, so that the struggle must target ownership. Fraser, in Lan's account, abandons a purely identity-based feminism for Marx's critique of political economy, and Fuchs's book on rereading Marx in the age of digital capitalism calls for ending private property so that all share the benefits of digital and AI technology. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-language overview of how Balibar, Badiou, Fraser, Crary and Fuchs are being presented to Chinese readers as critics of digital capitalism.
quoteEn: In other words, in Badiou's view the real problem is not digital technology: digital and artificial intelligence technologies merely fully expose the greedy nature of contemporary capitalism and the secret of its inequality.
quoteZh: 换言之，在巴迪欧看来，真正出问题的不是数字技术，无论是数字技术还是人工智能技术，无非将当代资本主义贪婪的本质和不平等的秘密充分暴露了出来

t: The Marxist outlook of Communists in the new era
zh: 新时代共产党人的马克思主义观
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today in November 2022, Han Meng takes up a formulation in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): that the Party succeeds and socialism with Chinese characteristics is good ultimately because Marxism works, specifically Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Han argues that this sentence condenses the Marxist outlook of Communists in the new era.

The short commentary has two parts. The first asks which Marxism is said to "work", drawing on Marx, Engels, Lenin and the history of the Chinese revolution. The second asks how this Marxism should be grasped philosophically, and compares two wordings found in Party documents.

Han contends that Marxism is easily mistaken for fixed dogma, a danger that Marx, Engels and Lenin themselves noted. In Han's account, Chinese revolutionary history shows the cost of applying Russian experience as an abstract formula, as in the strategy of armed uprisings in central cities. Success came with the strategy of encircling the cities from the countryside, which joined principles to Chinese conditions. Han then distinguishes "adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times" (a verb, a process of theoretical integration) from "Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times" (an adjective, an intrinsic attribute and the result of that process). Han locates this attribute in Marxism's worldview and methodology, and lists six aspects, including the creative practice of the people, independent exploration, unity of theoretical and historical logic, problem-solving, systematic thinking and a world-historical character.

Han concludes that the adaptation of Marxism is a development from theory to practice, from the spontaneous to the conscious, and from the national to the world. Han presents the practical task for Marxists, especially theorists, as laying foundations for the independent development of Chinese modernization and for building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the 20th Congress wording on Marxism is interpreted philosophically in Chinese official theory.
quoteEn: The former \"adapting to the Chinese context and the needs of our times\" is used as a verb, stressing the process of seeking truth and integrating theory; the latter is used as an adjective, highlighting the result of that process and the essential attribute it contains.
quoteZh: 前者的“中国化时代化”是作为动词来使用的，强调的是探索真理、理论结合的过程；后者的“中国化时代化”是作为形容词来使用的，凸显的是理论结合过程的成果，以及这种成果蕴含的本质属性。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism's basic principles to China's concrete conditions and to present-day circumstances. The 20th Congress report added the "needs of our times" element.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, given prominence in the report to the 20th Party Congress.

t: Seizing the historical initiative and answering the questions of history
st: Continuously opening up new horizons for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 把握历史主动 回答历史之问
zhSub: 不断开辟马克思主义中国化时代化新境界
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today on 29 December 2022, asks how the Party can seize the historical initiative and answer the questions of history. Zhang and Sun answer that it can do so only under the guidance of Marxism that has been adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They present upholding Marxism's guiding position and opening new horizons for that adaptation as the historic mission of Chinese communists.

The piece surveys more than a century of revolution, construction and national rejuvenation. It then turns to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the latest theoretical result of this process, and to the Two Integrations as the method for developing it further.

The authors argue that adapting Marxism means combining its basic principles with China's actual conditions, the world's conditions and historical conditions, rather than reciting conclusions or applying them dogmatically. In their account, Xi Jinping Thought gives original answers to the questions of the new era. They name the new historical position of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the redefined principal contradiction in society. That contradiction is between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development, and the authors say it enriches Marxist contradiction theory. They describe the second of the Two Integrations, with fine traditional Chinese culture, as a major theoretical innovation. It requires historical and cultural confidence, and it gives Marxism distinctive Chinese features, style and character.

The authors conclude that practice and theoretical innovation have no end. They call on every thinker to take up the theoretical and historical task of opening new horizons for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official line frames the Two Integrations and Xi Jinping Thought at the end of 2022.
quoteEn: The Two Integrations have deepened the Party's understanding of the laws governing the upholding and development of Marxism, and are also the key to understanding and grasping Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
quoteZh: “两个结合”深化了我们党对坚持和发展马克思主义的规律性认识，也是我们理解和把握习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的关键。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it to the present era. The 'times' element was added in Party documents around 2021–22.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–18. It is officially described as 21st-century Marxism.
Combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was stressed by Xi Jinping in 2021–22.
The official name for China's path, system and theory of socialism since reform and opening up.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: The theoretical foundations of why the sinicised and contemporary Marxism "works"
zh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义行的理论根基
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in December 2022, Zhang Tao takes up a line from Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): that the Party's success and the merits of socialism with Chinese characteristics come down to the fact that Marxism "works", specifically Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The commentary argues that this efficacy rests on two foundations: the Two Integrations and the answers the theory gives to four sets of questions.

The piece is short and has two main sections. The first examines the Two Integrations, the combination of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second shows how Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era answers what the author calls the questions of China, of the world, of the people and of the times. It opens with a lineage running from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development.

On the first foundation, Zhang argues that Marxism is to be used as a worldview and method for solving China's problems, not as dogma or a set of phrases to recite. The author cites Marx and Engels as models, since they refused to apply their theory mechanically and kept revising it. On culture, Zhang holds that ideas such as "the world belongs to all" and "the people are the foundation of the state" are highly compatible with scientific socialism's values. On the second foundation, the author says the Thought answers the question of China through Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It answers the question of the world through a community with a shared future for mankind. It answers the question of the people through a people-centred standpoint, and the question of the times by addressing the tasks of the new era.

Zhang concludes that upholding Xi Jinping Thought amounts to truly upholding and developing Marxism, and that practice in guiding China and the world will further show that sinicised, contemporary Marxism works. The text is an official-line explanatory commentary rather than a scholarly study. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the 20th Party Congress formula that Marxism "works" is explained and justified in Chinese theoretical writing.
quoteEn: We uphold Marxism as our guide in order to use its scientific worldview and methodology to solve China's problems, not to recite and repeat its specific conclusions and phrases, still less to treat Marxism as an unchanging dogma.
quoteZh: 我们坚持以马克思主义为指导，是要运用其科学的世界观和方法论解决中国的问题，而不是要背诵和重复其具体结论和词句，更不能把马克思主义当成一成不变的教条。

glossary.explanation: The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to the Party's official account of Marxism's adaptation in China around 2021–2022.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, stressing shared interests and common development among states.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.

t: Making an original contribution to developing Marxist political economy
zh: 为发展马克思主义政治经济学作出原创性贡献
paras: In this short commentary, published in the People's Daily on 31 January 2023, Zhou Wen asks what Xi Jinping's economic thinking adds to Marxist political economy. Zhou argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi has drawn on China's economic experience to form Xi Jinping's economic thought, which upholds the basic principles and methods of Marxist political economy. In Zhou's account, it makes important original contributions and opens a new horizon for the discipline.

The piece is organised under three headings: deepening understanding of the laws of socialist economic construction, answering major questions of China's economic development in the new era, and resolving the relationship between government and market.

Under the first heading, Zhou lists three contributions. The first is strengthening the Party's overall leadership of economic work, which Zhou says enriches Marxist theory on the relationship between economics and politics. The second is the people-centred approach and the pursuit of common prosperity, which Zhou says clarifies the purpose of socialist production. The third is a basic economic system combining public ownership as the mainstay, distribution according to work and the socialist market economy. Zhou then presents the new development philosophy as a systematic theory that answers questions about the aims, drivers, methods and paths of development. On government and market, Zhou describes Xi's formula of letting the market play the decisive role while the government plays its role better. In Zhou's reading, this goes beyond both Western development models and mainstream Western economics.

Zhou concludes that this approach supplies a fundamental guide for building a Chinese system of economic disciplines, scholarship and discourse. Zhou calls for continued research and practice on combining socialism with the market economy, and for better integration of an efficient market with a capable government. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style summary of how Chinese commentary frames Xi's economic thought as a contribution to Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: How to handle the relationship between government and market is the core question of a market economy, and also a worldwide puzzle in economics.
quoteZh: 如何处理好政府和市场的关系，是市场经济的核心问题，也是一个经济学世界性难题。

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping since 2012, presented officially as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It was formally named in the late 2010s.
A framework introduced in 2015 that names five principles of development: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis in Xi-era policy.

The official term for China's core economic arrangements: public ownership as the mainstay alongside other ownership forms, distribution according to work as the mainstay alongside other methods, and the socialist market economy.

t: Understanding and grasping the historical responsibility of opening up new realms of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 深刻认识和把握开辟马克思主义中国化时代化新境界的历史责任
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 16 November 2022, shortly after the 20th Party Congress, Huang Yibing argues that writing new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is the solemn historical responsibility of today's Chinese communists. The commentary reads the Congress as a summing-up of the Party's experience with Marxism, an elaboration of the Two Integrations, and a call for theoretical innovation grounded in practice. Huang's thesis is that this work depends on a scientific attitude toward Marxism, on the Two Integrations, and on the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The piece has four numbered sections. The first treats the Party's attitude to Marxism. The second presents the Two Integrations as a major original contribution of Xi Jinping Thought. The third explains the "six commitments" that the Congress report used to summarise that Thought's worldview and methodology. The fourth turns these into requirements for future theoretical work.

On attitude, Huang holds that the Party's century of achievement rests on upholding Marxist fundamentals and seeking truth from facts. In this account Marxism is an open system, so the Party opposes both dogmatism and pragmatism. Huang notes that Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping each stressed development, and that today's China has outrun what the classical authors could imagine. On the Two Integrations, Huang says Marxism must be combined with China's concrete realities, to solve Chinese problems rather than recite conclusions, and with fine traditional Chinese culture, which is said to be highly compatible with scientific socialism. This second integration is credited with turning "Marxism in China" into "Chinese Marxism". The six commitments are: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systemic thinking, and a global vision.

Huang concludes that the six commitments are a "golden key" and a "bridge and boat" for further theoretical innovation, and sets out what each requires. These include firm adherence to Marxist fundamentals, the Party's overall leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics, attention to new problems, and learning from other civilisations. Practice has no end, Huang says, so adapting Marxism has none either, and continuing the Two Integrations will open new realms. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of how the 20th Party Congress framed theoretical innovation and the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: Only by unwaveringly advancing the integration of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture can Marxism truly be transformed from "Marxism in China" into "Chinese Marxism".
quoteZh: 只有坚定不移推进马克思主义与中华优秀传统文化结合，才能使马克思主义从“在中国的马克思主义”真正转化为“中国的马克思主义”

glossary.explanation: The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Xi Jinping stated it explicitly in his July 2021 speech for the Party's centenary, and the 20th Party Congress elaborated it.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formulation for the Party's continuing effort to adapt Marxism to Chinese conditions and to the present era. "Shidaihua" was added to the older "Sinification of Marxism" around the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Official texts present it as the latest stage of the Sinification of Marxism.

The 20th Party Congress report's summary of the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought. They are: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systemic thinking, and a global vision.

t: Three dimensions for a scientific grasp of the "Two Integrations"
zh: 科学把握“两个结合”的三个维度
paras: Following the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), this Guangming Daily commentary asks how the "Two Integrations" should be understood. Sun Laibin argues that the report presents them as the inner mechanism by which Marxism keeps developing. In Sun's reading, they can be grasped along three dimensions: why they are necessary, why they are possible, and how they are to be advanced.

The article first reviews the historical record of combining Marxism with Chinese realities, from early Party mistakes to the Sinicization of Marxism under Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. It then turns to the relationship between Marxism and traditional culture, drawing on Engels and on Lenin's critique of Bogdanov. It ends with practical routes for carrying the Integrations forward.

On necessity, Sun contends that Marxism can guide practice only if it is joined to China's specific conditions. Sun cites the early Party's mechanical borrowing of Soviet experience as a costly lesson. Marxism can flourish only if rooted in the nation's own historical culture. On possibility, Sun argues that Marxist principles are universal, having grown from the sum of world revolutionary experience. Sun also claims that excellent traditional culture closely matches scientific socialism's values, and lists four areas of fit: cosmology (the unity of heaven and humanity), the vision of "all under heaven" and a world of great harmony, social harmony amid difference, and ethics. The Party's "historical initiative" is the third ground. Sun holds that the Party has repeatedly taken the initiative in advancing the Integrations.

On the path forward, Sun calls for two things. The first is to integrate Marxism with present-day realities by identifying the basic national conditions and by being problem-oriented. The second is to let Marxism and traditional culture interact. Marxism should guide and revitalise the culture, for instance by reading "unity of heaven and humanity" as harmony between people and nature. In turn, the culture should enrich Marxism with ideas and terms such as "seeking truth from facts" and "a moderately prosperous society". Sun stresses that the Integrations do not happen automatically. They require centralised Party leadership and a sense of responsibility among scholars and the public. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the Two Integrations were explained after the 20th Party Congress, including its examples of cultural parallels with Marxism.
quoteEn: The "Two Integrations" are not achieved automatically.
quoteZh: “两个结合”不是自动实现的。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second element was added prominently in Xi Jinping's formulations, including his 2021 and 2022 speeches and reports.
A term in Party discourse for the Party's conscious, proactive grasp of historical trends, stressed in recent Party documents.

t: Upholding the fundamental requirement of putting the people first
zh: 坚持人民至上的根本要求
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 14 November 2022, takes up the principle of "putting the people first" (renmin zhishang), which the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) lists as part of the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Han argues that it is a fundamental requirement of the Marxist materialist conception of history and a key lesson of the Party's century of struggle.

The piece is short and organised as a sequence of six requirements, each introduced by a classical Chinese maxim and supported by quotations from Xi Jinping, and in one case Mao Zedong. It opens by defining "the people" as a historical and political category whose core is the working masses who produce material goods.

Han's six requirements are: take a firm people's standpoint; give priority to the people's interests; improve the people's wellbeing; respect the people's creativity; draw on the people's wisdom; and ensure that the people share in development. The author links these to the mass line, to the principal contradiction in Chinese society, defined as that between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development, and to the claim that the people are the creators of history. Reform and development are said to be judged finally by whether the people share in their results.

Han concludes that, on the new journey towards the second centenary goal, Party members and cadres should treat the fundamental interests of the great majority as the starting and end point of all work. Whether the people support, approve, are happy with and agree to a policy is presented as the basic test of success. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-line commentary links people-centred development to Marxist historical materialism.
quoteEn: Putting the people first is a fundamental requirement of the Marxist materialist conception of history, an important lesson from the Communist Party of China's century of struggle, and the basic guideline for doing all our work well.
quoteZh: 坚持人民至上，是马克思主义唯物史观的根本要求，是中国共产党百年奋斗的一条重要经验，也是我们做好一切工作的基本遵循。
