glossary.explanation: A principle stressed in Xi Jinping's discourse and listed in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) as part of the worldview and methodology of Party theory. It holds that the people's interests rank above all other considerations.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

A working method developed by Mao Zedong that requires the Party to gather the views of ordinary people, turn them into policy and return to the people to implement it. The Party still describes it as its fundamental line of work.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.literal: development thinking with the people at the centre
glossary.explanation: A formulation promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012) holding that development should be for the people, rely on the people and have its results shared by the people.
The official goal of building a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic. The first centenary goal was a moderately prosperous society by 2021.

t: Building a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power
zh: 建设具有强大凝聚力和引领力的社会主义意识形态
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), this commentary in Guangming Daily asks how to build a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power. Lin argues that ideological work is the work of giving the country and the nation their "heart" and "soul", and that it decides their survival, prospects and fate. The author's answer is that Marxism's guiding position must be upheld and the Party's leadership over ideological work firmly held.

The piece is organised in four numbered sections. It first explains why ideological work matters, then turns to the Party's leadership over it. It next sets out how to consolidate mainstream thought and public opinion, and ends with governance of the internet. Almost all of its authority comes from extended quotations of Xi Jinping.

Lin's core argument runs as follows. Ideological work is paired with economic work as mutually supporting, and the author presents a world of sharper ideological struggle, in which hostile forces are said to seek "colour revolutions" and to subvert Party leadership. Control of positions (zhendi) is therefore the key: Lin says the Party must hold the leadership, management and discourse power over ideology and defend its positions actively. Mainstream opinion is to be strengthened in four ways: arming the Party and people with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, practising core socialist values, developing a Marxist-guided philosophy and social science "with Chinese characteristics", and building an integrated all-media communication system under the principle that the Party manages the media. The internet is described as the main battlefield of ideological struggle. Lin calls for a comprehensive online governance system and rule-of-law management of cyberspace.

Lin concludes that a strong socialist ideology will unite the whole people in ideals, values and morality. In the author's account, that unity will generate the force needed to advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Cadres at all levels are urged to strengthen their ability to manage and use the internet. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the official Party line on ideological work after the 20th Party Congress, including how it frames ideological security, media and the internet.
quoteEn: The internet is now the very front line of ideological struggle, and controlling the leading role in online ideology means safeguarding the country's sovereignty and state power.
quoteZh: 网络已是当前意识形态斗争的最前沿，掌控网络意识形态主导权，就是守护国家的主权和政权。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out at length in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term national goal emphasised by Xi Jinping, linked to the Chinese Dream and to the aim of building a modern socialist country.
A twelve-word official set of values (prosperity, democracy, patriotism, integrity and others) promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A military-derived term for ideological and media outlets (press, schools, online platforms) which the Party says it must occupy and hold.

t: Advancing the adaptation of Marxism to China and the times through great practice
zh: 以伟大实践推进马克思主义时代化中国化
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in November 2022, takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's claim that Marxism, adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, explains the Party's success. Zhou Jiaxin argues that further theoretical innovation rests on grasping the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The piece first treats the standpoint of practice as the basic viewpoint of Marxist philosophy. It then sets out six principles that Zhou presents as the method for advancing adaptation, each tied to the Party's "historical initiative".

Zhou argues that practice unites historical, truth and value perspectives: it is concrete and historical, carries social relations, and is the test of truth. Citing Fang Jun of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhou holds that a scientific view of history is in essence a scientific view of values. Chinese modernization is described as a world-historical practice that is highly distinctive, profound and complex. Zhou then lists six commitments: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, adhering to fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systems thinking, and a global vision. Each is said to strengthen historical initiative.

Zhou concludes that these six commitments form an interrelated whole. In this account they make up the method for understanding Xi Jinping Thought and for the Two Integrations, and they express the unity of historical, truth and value perspectives in the new journey of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Party-affiliated philosophers link practice, the 20th Party Congress's six commitments and the adaptation of Marxism.
quoteEn: Theory is the flower that blooms and the fruit that grows on the tree of problems.
quoteZh: 理论是问题之树盛开的花朵、结出的果实。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official term for China's development path, set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022 as a distinct model of modernization.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
A term in Party discourse for consciously seizing the initiative in shaping historical development, stressed in the 20th Party Congress report.

t: A Marxist philosophical reflection on Chinese modernization
zh: 对中国式现代化的马克思主义哲学思考
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in November 2022, Gao Chao takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's statement that Chinese modernization shares common features with other countries' modernization while having distinctive Chinese characteristics. Gao argues that this is both a political and a theoretical judgement, and that Marxist philosophy in the new era must explain what is common, what is specific, and how the two relate.

This short commentary first challenges the popular view that modernization has a single model, the Western one. It then draws on Marx and Engels, turns to the practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and ends with research agendas that Gao, citing the researcher Fang Jun, assigns to Marxist philosophy.

Gao reasons from historical materialism that modernization is, at root, the modernization of productive forces, and that the scientific and industrial revolutions first occurred in the West. Quoting Engels on the interaction between economic base and superstructure, Gao holds that Marx's remark that advanced countries show backward ones their future does not imply one road only. In Gao's account, problems such as polarisation, imbalance between material and cultural-ethical progress, ecological damage and conflict between states are common to all modernizing countries, but China addresses them differently: through common prosperity, ecological harmony and peaceful development, not through aggression, expansion or the sacrifice of the majority.

Gao concludes that Marxist philosophy should "illuminate reality with theory", and endorses Fang Jun's two priority questions: why socialism was first established in less developed capitalist countries, and why it was not consolidated in some of them. Answering these would, Gao says, explain why socialism can be built well in China, and show that Chinese modernization is a new path, not one valid for China alone. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how the official line on Chinese modernization is framed in philosophical terms.
quoteEn: Modernization has both commonality and individuality.
quoteZh: 现代化既有共性，也有个性。

glossary.explanation: A Party concept elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022), describing China's modernization as led by the Party and distinct from the Western path.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, presented in official discourse as a defining feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's theory and system of socialism since the reform era.

t: Chinese modernization and the modernization of the human being
zh: 中国式现代化与人的现代化
paras: This short review, first published in Chinese Social Sciences Today on 24 November 2022, uses Fang Jun's book Scattered Leaves of Thought (思想的散叶) to discuss how Chinese modernization should be understood. Zhou Ke argues that approaching it through the modernization of the human being requires attention to the unity of the historical outlook and value theory in Marxist philosophy. In Zhou's reading, Fang's book upholds and develops that unity.

The piece has three parts. The first reads Chinese modernization, as set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), in terms of human modernization. The second reviews value-theory research in Chinese Marxist philosophy since the 1980s. The third discusses the book's pairing of practical concern with theoretical reflection.

Zhou holds that modernization includes changes in people's psychology, values and conduct, not only in technology, economy and politics. Chinese modernization, the author says, affirms human needs and development through common prosperity, balanced material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony with nature and peaceful development. Zhou therefore rejects simply copying Western personality-and-psychology approaches. The review credits Chinese scholars with moving value theory beyond a purely epistemological frame and defining value through the contradictions of practice. It also credits them with treating ethical questions, such as institutional ethics, as questions of historical outlook.

Zhou concludes that the book exemplifies turning real problems into scholarly ones, following Liu Ben's principle that research on real problems should drive foundational theory and foundational theory should deepen research on real problems. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese account of how value theory and human development are linked to Chinese modernization, and of how one strand of Chinese Marxist philosophy has developed since the 1980s.
quoteEn: To understand Chinese modernization from the dimension of the modernization of the human being, one cannot overlook the theoretical character of Marxist philosophy in which the historical outlook and value theory are unified.
quoteZh: 从人的现代化的维度理解中国式现代化，不能忽视马克思主义哲学的历史观与价值论相统一的理论特质。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. It was set out in five defining features in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

A long-standing socialist goal, given prominence under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all people rather than a part of the population. The article extends it to cover both material and spiritual wealth.

t: Chinese modernization and the adaptation of Marxist philosophy to the times
zh: 中国式现代化与马克思主义哲学的时代化
paras: Following the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which set out the features and requirements of Chinese modernization, Lin Qing asks how Chinese modernization relates to the adaptation of Marxist philosophy to the needs of our times. The short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in November 2022, argues that the relationship can be grasped through two dimensions: the original historical setting of Chinese modernization, and the move from a formal to a substantive crossing of the "Caudine Forks".

The first part addresses why modernization in China is socialist. Lin notes that for Marx, socialism was not itself a project of modernization, since it was built on surpassing capitalist industrial modernity. The second part turns to Marx's late reflections on the Caudine Forks, prompted by Vera Zasulich's question, and to the concept of appropriation in The German Ideology.

Lin reads Mao Zedong's On New Democracy as concluding, from a historical-materialist analysis of China's situation, that national independence required a path from new-democratic to socialist revolution. Lin then argues that China crossed the Caudine Forks only formally through revolution, and must now cross them substantively: appropriating the means and achievements of Western-style modernization without its suffering. Drawing on Marx and Engels, Lin says appropriation is conditioned by its object, by the individuals who appropriate (hence the stress on modernization of the human being) and by the manner of appropriation, which means joint appropriation by united people. Lin reads the features listed in the Congress report as building social commonality.

Lin concludes that Marxist philosophy should offer a general interpretation of Chinese modernization as a world-historical effect, first imposed and later actively pursued, while refusing a "philosophy of history" reading. Lin adds that understanding socialism remains the essential question as the process unfolds. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese philosopher links the Caudine Forks debate to current Party theory on modernization.
quoteEn: Substantively crossing the "Caudine Forks" ultimately comes down to how to appropriate the means and civilisational achievements of modernization without going through the suffering that Western-style capitalist modernization brought.
quoteZh: 实质跨越“卡夫丁峡谷”，说到底还是如何不经过西式资本主义现代化带来的苦难过程而占有其现代化的手段和文明成果。

glossary.explanation: Marx's image, in his late letters to Zasulich, for whether a society such as Russia could reach socialism without undergoing the full capitalist stage and its sufferings. Chinese theorists use it in discussing China's path.

The Party's official formulation of China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022 with five stated features, including common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义哲学时代化
glossary.en: adaptation of Marxist philosophy to the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Derived from the official formula of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, applied here to Marxist philosophy.

t: Advancing the adaptation of Marxism to China and our times through great practice
zh: 以伟大实践推进马克思主义时代化中国化
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in November 2022, takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's claim that it is Marxism, adapted to China and the times, that explains the Party's success. Zhou argues that theoretical innovation grounded in practice depends first on grasping the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and on applying its stance, viewpoint and method.

The piece begins with the standpoint of practice in Marxist philosophy, then turns to the Chinese practice of the new era, which Zhou characterises as extremely distinctive, profound and complex. It closes with six principles that the author presents as the methodological requirements of the Thought.

Zhou argues that practice opens Marxist philosophy to social and historical depth, supplies a test of truth, and sketches a better future. Drawing on Fang Jun, the piece holds that a scientific view of history is in essence a scientific view of values, so that taking historical initiative means unifying views of history, truth and value. Adaptation of Marxism is then tied to six commitments: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systemic thinking, and a global vision. Each is said to be the ground on which historical initiative grows.

Zhou concludes that these six commitments form an interrelated whole. In the author's account, they embody the scientific unity of views of history, truth and value achieved on the basis of practice, and they keep advancing adaptation of Marxism on the new journey of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-affiliated philosophers link the standpoint of practice to the six methodological principles drawn from the 20th Party Congress report.
quoteEn: Problems are the slogan of the age, the most practical call through which it expresses its state of mind.
quoteZh: 问题是时代的口号，是它表现自己精神状态的最实际的呼声。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for China's path to modernity, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A term in recent Party discourse for consciously grasping and shaping the course of history. It stresses acting from an understanding of historical laws.

t: Chinese modernization: our road to rejuvenation
zh: 中国式现代化：我们的复兴路
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in November 2022, reads the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) as setting out Chinese modernization as the means of advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Qi argues that the Party must grasp the strategic plan and world-historical significance of Chinese modernization and draw on a spirit of historical initiative as the country begins a new journey.

The piece has three parts. It first summarises the great changes since the 18th Party Congress (2012), then sets out the features, requirements and guiding principles of Chinese modernization, and finally places it in three historical frames: the history of the Chinese nation, of socialism, and of human society.

Qi's core claim is that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party, with Party leadership as its fundamental political guarantee and socialism as its fundamental political direction. The author lists its Chinese characteristics as a huge population, common prosperity, coordination of material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development. Historically, Qi presents it as marking the nation's leap from standing up to becoming prosperous and then strong. It is also said to reject the old path of capital-centred, polarising, materialist and expansionist modernization, creating a new form of human civilization and offering other countries a new option.

Qi concludes that following its own path is the Party's historical conclusion from a century of struggle, and that this path serves the Chinese people and nation as well as human progress. The author calls for stronger awareness of risks, deeper reform and opening up, and a fighting spirit among Party members and cadres. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line summary of how the 20th Congress report framed Chinese modernization and its global significance.
quoteEn: Taking our own path is the foothold of all the Party's theory and practice, and even more the historical conclusion drawn from the Party's century of struggle.
quoteZh: 走自己的路，是党的全部理论和实践立足点，更是党百年奋斗得出的历史结论。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path to modernity under Communist Party leadership, elaborated in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and international standing, associated especially with Xi Jinping's leadership.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, described as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: A profound transformation in the form of human civilisation
zh: 人类文明形态的深刻变革
paras: Feng Ziyi, in a short commentary first published in the China Social Sciences Today (2022), argues that China's development has produced not only a path of Chinese modernization but also a new form of human civilisation. Feng presents the step from a "new path" to a "new form" as a major rise from development to civilisation, and as China's highest achievement and greatest contribution to world civilisation.

The article first clarifies what "new form" means, then sets out six ways in which the new form of human civilisation advances and leads human civilisation: expanding it, changing its configuration, widening its paths, guiding its direction, adding momentum, and reshaping its mode of development.

On the meaning of the term, Feng holds that it is a comprehensive view of civilisation rather than a set of indicators, that it forms a new paradigm of ideals, values and norms, and that it is still unfolding. Feng argues that it enriches existing civilisation with values such as mutual respect, fairness and win-win cooperation, and that it reinterprets categories such as the core socialist values. In Feng's account, China's rise rests on moral and value-based influence rather than capital or hegemony, and shows that there is more than one Western-style route to modernity. A community with a shared future for mankind points a way forward amid the "great changes unseen in a century". Poverty alleviation and the Belt and Road Initiative are cited as sources of momentum. Mutual respect and exchange, Feng says, replace hostility and isolation.

Feng concludes that the new form is an "upgraded version" of civilisation that is still a work in progress. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese scholars frame Chinese modernization as a civilisational contribution.
quoteEn: Differences in paths to modernization are differences in forms of civilisation.
quoteZh: 现代化道路的差异就是文明形态的差异。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A formulation, used in Party documents from 2021, that presents Chinese modernization as creating a new type of civilisation, not only a new development path.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept advanced by Xi Jinping since 2013, calling for cooperation and shared interests among states.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched in 2013.
A twelve-term official set of values (such as prosperity, democracy, freedom, equality and justice) promoted by the Party since 2012.

t: Chinese modernization and a new form of civilization
zh: 中国式现代化与文明的新形态
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 30 August 2022
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2022, asks in what sense Chinese modernization generates a new form of civilization. Yang argues that the novelty lies in three features: how China handles tradition and Western civilization, its socialist character, and the fusion of several social transformations in one period.

The piece is organised around the repeated phrase that each point is where the "newness" of the civilization lies. Yang approaches modernization through a typology (endogenous versus exogenous), through social formation (capitalist versus socialist modernization), and through the historical sequence of marketization, industrialization and reform.

Yang classes China's modernization as exogenous, set off by the challenge of Western capitalism and bound up from the start with national rejuvenation. Its central tension is therefore between native tradition and Western modernity. Yang holds that the measure for what to borrow and what to inherit is neither Western civilization nor tradition itself but contemporary Chinese practice. Yang adds that capitalist modernization produced capitalist civilization, whereas Chinese modernization is socialist, aims at common prosperity and removes class and capital–labour antagonism, while still absorbing rational elements of capitalist civilization. In the West marketization preceded industrialization, but in China modernization, marketization and socialist reform proceeded together.

Yang concludes that this "triple transformation" and "trinity" will constitute a new form of human civilization. The text is a compact statement of one scholar's framing of the topic. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese Marxist philosopher links modernization theory to the idea of a new civilizational form.
quoteEn: The important feature and significance of contemporary Chinese practice lies in the fact that it has condensed three major social transformations, modernization, marketization and socialist reform, into the same time and space.
quoteZh: 当代中国实践的重要特征和重要意义就在于，它把现代化、市场化和社会主义改革这三重重大的社会变革浓缩在同一时空中进行了

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization, led by the Communist Party and described as socialist. It was given prominence in Party documents around the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A goal of shared wealth for all, associated with socialism in Party discourse. It is often cited from Deng Xiaoping's definition of the essence of socialism.

glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan for restoring China's strength and status after the 19th-century decline. It is closely tied to the Chinese Dream.

t: A major enrichment and development of the theory of world modernization
zh: 对世界现代化理论的重大丰富和发展
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 19 December 2022, takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's account of Chinese modernization. Yu argues that the theory of Chinese modernization, formed through long practice, raises the Party's understanding to a new level and is a major enrichment and development of the theory of world modernization.

The piece first recounts the Party's exploration of its own path: the goal of a modern socialist country in the period of revolution and construction, the phrase "Chinese-style modernization" and the "three-step" strategy after reform and opening up, and the advances since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then summarises Xi Jinping's exposition of the theory and ends with a contrast with Western modernization.

Yu stresses that modernizing a developing country whose population exceeds that of all existing developed countries combined has no precedent and no ready-made road. In Yu's account, Xi's statements form a rigorous theoretical system covering the distinctive features, essential requirements and major principles of Chinese modernization. The author claims there is neither a single modernization model nor a universal standard. Chinese modernization is said to go beyond the older Western paths, described as capital-centred, polarised, materialist and expansionist, and to widen the routes open to developing countries.

Yu concludes that the theory fits China's reality and reflects both the laws of socialist construction and those of human social development. The author calls on readers to focus on problems arising in the process, to propose new ideas and methods, and to produce further innovations in modernization theory and practice. Read the original if you want a brief, official-register statement of how Chinese modernization was presented as a contribution to world modernization theory after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: There is neither a single, supreme model of modernization in the world, nor a standard of modernization that holds true everywhere.
quoteZh: 世界上既不存在定于一尊的现代化模式，也不存在放之四海而皆准的现代化标准。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from 1978.

t: Grasping the essential features of Chinese modernization accurately
zh: 精准把握中国式现代化本质特征
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), this commentary in the Chinese Social Sciences Today asks what the distinctive, essential features of Chinese modernization are and how it differs from Western modernization. Liu and Yang argue that only by answering this can Chinese modernization be grasped in thought and advanced in practice.

The article goes through six features in turn: modernization led by the Communist Party and socialist in character; modernization of a huge population; modernization toward common prosperity; coordinated development of material and cultural-ethical advancement; harmony between humanity and nature; and the path of peaceful development. Each is set against a contrasting account of Western capitalist modernization.

For the authors, Party leadership and the socialist system are the most essential feature and the basic dividing line. Western modernization, they write, is driven by the bourgeoisie's pursuit of surplus value and so produces polarisation, crises, consumerism, ecological damage and external plunder. Chinese modernization is described as people-centred rather than capital-centred, citing the eradication of absolute poverty (98.99 million rural people lifted out of poverty under current standards) and the principle that clear waters and green mountains are invaluable assets. Marx's Capital is invoked on polarisation and on workers' need for time for spiritual needs.

The authors conclude that the idea that 'modernization equals Westernisation' is a myth, and that Western 'modernization traps' should be recognised as deceptive and unsustainable. They call for practice grounded in China's realities and experience, offering other countries a reliable alternative. Read the original if you want a compact, official-line outline of how Chinese commentators contrast Chinese modernization with Western modernization.
quoteEn: Socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China is the most essential feature of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 中国共产党领导的社会主义现代化,是中国式现代化的最本质特征。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization, elaborated in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist, Party-led and distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis in Party policy in recent years as a counter to inequality.

t: Deepening philosophical reflection at a major historical juncture
zh: 在重大历史关键节点深化哲学思考
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in November 2022, Zhang Wu argues that the 20th Party Congress (2022) marks a historical turning point. The commentary contends that this moment obliges Marxist philosophy to leave its "comfort zone" and ask a new overarching question: how is Chinese modernization possible?

Zhang first reads the Congress's central task, advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization, against several histories: the Chinese nation, socialism, the Communist Party, the People's Republic, and reform and opening up. The text then turns to the history of Marxism itself and to the idea of "living history" producing "living Marxism".

In Zhang's account, nineteenth-century Marxism had developed Western Europe as its stage, and twentieth-century Marxism backward Eastern countries. The twenty-first century's stage will be a developed Eastern country, a situation Marx never faced. Zhang holds that Chinese modernization is possible theoretically because of the Two Integrations, since Marxism's critique of modernity and China's fine traditional culture both rule out the capitalist road. Its difficulty, notably its huge population, should be turned into momentum by developing people into talent, which calls for a theory of human development grounded in historical materialism rather than copied from the West. Philosophically, Zhang says, Chinese modernization is building a "post-capital-logic" form of philosophy, one that sublates capital logic instead of rejecting it, so that capital serves human development.

Zhang concludes that this juncture is an opportunity for Marxist philosophy to innovate, likened to Rhodes, the place to dance. Read the original if you want a short example of how a Chinese Marxist philosopher frames the 20th Party Congress as a task for philosophical theory.
quoteEn: Concretely, this means reversing the relationship between capital logic and human development: human development is no longer an internal moment of capital logic, but rather capital logic serves human development.
quoteZh: 具体而言，就是要颠倒资本逻辑与人的发展的关系：人的发展不再是资本逻辑的内在环节，而是反过来，资本逻辑服务于人的发展。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western capitalist modernization.
The Party's formula for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-standing official goal of restoring China's national strength and standing, tied to the two centenary goals.

glossary.zh: 后资本逻辑的哲学形态
glossary.pinyin: hòu zīběn luójí de zhéxué xíngtài
glossary.explanation: The author's term for a philosophy that sublates capital logic by using and governing capital under socialism so that it serves human development.

t: Development and innovation of the fundamental system of upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere
zh: 坚持马克思主义在意识形态领域指导地位根本制度的发展与创新
source: Research on the Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2022 no. 12
paras: Writing after the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), Wu Xueqin asks how the Chinese Communist Party came to make "upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere" a fundamental system, and how that system can be effectively implemented. The article argues that the system is one of the Party's basic institutions and an important component of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics. In Wu's account, it has been built up over a century and matured in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first traces four historical stages: its emergence in revolutionary struggle, its formation and uneven development after 1949, its improvement during reform and opening up, and its maturation in the new era. The second sets out what the new era has achieved since the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) formally designated the system as fundamental. The third discusses five pairings through which the system should be implemented.

Wu draws five lessons from the century of experience: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, propaganda and education, absorbing other cultural achievements, a Party-led cultural and educational structure, and winning discourse power. For the new era, Wu describes five achievements: a first task of implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; "four beams and eight pillars" that write the principle into the Party Constitution, the state Constitution and other laws; cyberspace governance; a responsibility system for ideological work; and coordination with other fundamental systems. On implementation, Wu pairs cultural confidence with institutional confidence, and preserving fundamentals with innovation. The author also pairs a coherent system with practical operability, accountability with the institutionalisation of accountability, and external rules with internalised conviction. Wu insists that academic debate be distinguished from questions of political principle.

Wu concludes that the system must be made part of people's way of life if it is to work and to secure the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Wu calls for better organisational leadership, management and environmental mechanisms for ideological work, including online ideological security and stronger accountability. Read the original if you want a Party-theoretical account of how ideological leadership is institutionalised in China, with its periodisation, policy documents and prescriptions for ideological work.
quoteEn: Only when this fundamental system is integrated into people's blood and becomes their way of life can it truly play its role and can the cause of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation be completed on schedule.
quoteZh: 只有让这项根本制度融入人们的血脉，变成人们的生活方式，才能真正发挥这项制度的作用，才能确保中华民族伟大复兴事业的如期完成。

glossary.explanation: In Party discourse, the top tier of the institutional hierarchy, above basic and important systems. It is meant to have top-level decisive, all-round and guiding effect on the socialist system.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for fitting Marxism to Chinese conditions and to the current era. It is presented as a continuing task of the Party's theoretical work.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Party, written into the Party Constitution in 2017.
A Party mechanism that assigns Party committees and officials responsibility for ideological work and holds them accountable for failures.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central official national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream and the aim of building a strong modern socialist country.

t: An assessment of Bidet and Duménil's view of "another Marxism"
zh: 比岱与杜梅尼尔“另一种马克思主义”观评析
paras: Wang Yicheng examines the claim by the European left theorists Jacques Bidet and Gérard Duménil, in Altermarxisme: Un autre marxisme pour un autre monde, that a new "other Marxism" is needed for a different world. The article asks what changes in contemporary capitalism led the two authors to say that the era of classical Marxism must be surpassed. It also asks what theoretical qualities "other Marxism" inherits and whether it really goes beyond Marxism in standpoint and method. Wang concludes that it contributes a sharp reading of capitalism's structural changes but departs from historical materialism.

The article has three parts. The first traces how Bidet and Duménil place "other Marxism" in the history of Marxism, in relation to classical Marxism and what they call neo-Marxism. The second sets out their analysis of present-day struggle: a three-step strategy, the "world-state" and the age of "ultimate modernity". The third assesses contributions and limits. Wang links these ideas to Bidet's earlier "meta-structure" theory, developed in his work on Capital, Theory of Modernity and General Theory.

Wang reports that Bidet and Duménil see modern society as ruled by two poles, market/capital and organisation. Class struggle is therefore a "three-way game" among capitalists, holders of organisational power and a "fundamental class" of wage-earners and other dominated groups. Their strategy runs from unification of this class, to an alliance with the organisational power-holders against capital, to continuing self-reform of new organisations so that new class structures do not form. They also argue that a "world-state" is emerging, which brings a "world people" into being and requires the struggle to be joined with Third World national liberation.

Wang's critique has four points. The "meta-structure" dialectic is formal-logical deduction on a single plane, not materialist dialectic, so it cannot reach capitalism's essential contradictions. Class conflict is read as a purely political matter, resting on a critique of unrealised freedom, equality and reason. The authors dismiss the Leninist role of the Communist Party as vanguard and rely on spontaneity and plural social movements. Treating market and organisation as trans-historical leaves the organisation of the fundamental class absent. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist critique of Bidet's meta-structure theory and of Western left strategies of alliance and the world-state.
quoteEn: The "meta-structure" dialectic is less a materialist dialectic than a deduction in formal logic dressed in the garb of dialectics.
quoteZh: “元结构”辩证法与其说是唯物辩证法，倒不如说是披着辩证法外衣的形式逻辑推演。

t: The new-era logic of the period of strategic opportunity
st: A strategic-philosophy analysis based on Marx's thought on world history
zh: 战略机遇期的新时代逻辑
zhSub: 基于马克思主义世界历史思想的战略哲学分析
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2022 no. 5/6
paras: Xin Ming asks how China's "period of strategic opportunity" should be understood in the new era. The article reads it through Marx's thought on world history and the methods of what the author calls strategic philosophy. Xin argues that the period is not a gift of circumstance. It is a objective strategic situation that the strategic actors, China included, jointly bring about through correct strategy. Its content has changed substantially since the 1980s, and the Party's continued use of the term signals what Xin calls a high degree of strategic self-awareness.

The article has four parts. The first traces how the concept was formed. It was formally put forward at the 16th Party Congress (2002), but it builds on Deng Xiaoping's judgments from the 1980s about peace and development. The second analyses changes in the strategic environment: the world pattern, the era and history. The third examines how China's strategic goals have moved from the "three-step" plan to the present two-step plan for a modern socialist country. The fourth sets out strategic responses suited to the new era.

Xin's core argument is that environment and goals together reshape the period's meaning. On the environment, the author describes the rise of emerging economies, the weakening of Western dominance and the drive of new technology towards a more interconnected world. Xin draws on Lenin's account of a revolutionary situation and on Marx's statements about world history to read these shifts as part of a historical logic. On goals, Xin cites the shift from solving subsistence needs to building a modern socialist power that is "leading" in comprehensive national strength. Because the West now treats China as its main strategic competitor, the author contends that earlier restraint (taoguang yanghui) no longer fits. Xin proposes three responses. The first is active struggle backed by strength. The second is turning two-sided rivalry into multi-actor games, as in Mao Zedong's "three worlds" idea. The third is reshaping strategic perceptions through shared human values and cooperation.

Xin concludes that, although risks have multiplied, time and momentum remain on the side of China and the emerging countries. China can therefore still treat its present stage as an important period of strategic opportunity if it acts in line with historical trends. The author presents the Party's persistence with the concept as proof of a historical initiative that goes beyond opportunism. Read the original if you want to see how a Party School scholar combines Marxist world-history theory with strategic analysis to justify the continued use of the "strategic opportunity" judgment.
quoteEn: It is not that the period of strategic opportunity existed because we kept a low profile; rather, the strategic environment of the time made it possible for us to keep a low profile.
quoteZh: 不是因为我们韬光养晦才有战略机遇期，而是其时的战略环境让我们有可能韬光养晦。

glossary.explanation: A Party assessment, first formally stated at the 16th Party Congress (2002), that the first two decades of the 21st century offered China favourable conditions for development. Later documents have kept the term while adjusting its content.

glossary.literal: hide one's light and nurture obscurity
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy maxim associated with Deng Xiaoping, usually rendered as keeping a low profile. It advised avoiding leadership claims and confrontation while China built up its strength.

The development strategy set out in the 1980s, with steps of doubling output, reaching a moderately prosperous standard (xiaokang) by 2000, and reaching a mid-level developed country by the mid-21st century.

keywords: great changes unseen in a century

t: The idea of ideological leadership in Lenin's What Is to Be Done? and its contemporary implications
zh: 列宁《怎么办？》中的意识形态领导权思想及其当代启示
paras: Lan Botao asks what Lenin's What Is to Be Done? contributes to the question of how a proletarian party secures ideological leadership, and what that offers the Communist Party of China today. The article argues that the book is a theoretical guide for Russian Social Democracy and that its ideas remain relevant. Lan frames ideological leadership as a strategic question that decides the Party's future, not a slogan, and cites Xi Jinping's demand that leadership, management and discourse power in ideological work never be allowed to slip away.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the content of Lenin's idea of ideological leadership, drawing on his critique of 'freedom of criticism' and of the 'Economists'. It covers the role of scientific theory, the emphasis on conscious workers' movements, the organisation of revolutionaries, and the founding of an all-Russia political newspaper. The second part discusses the guiding significance of these ideas. The third draws lessons for the Party in the new era.

Lan's central reasoning follows Lenin against the Economists, who exalted spontaneous workers' movements. Lan reports Lenin's view that a purely workers' movement cannot create an independent ideology and so stays under bourgeois ideological domination, remaining at the level of trade-unionism. Socialist consciousness therefore has to be instilled 'from outside' by the party, which Lan presents as a necessity because the working class under capitalism cannot produce its own ideology. Lan adds that Lenin saw a centralised all-Russia newspaper as the means to propaganda, agitation and the unification of local organisations. The struggle is described as irreconcilable, with a strengthened bourgeois ideology meaning a weakened socialist one.

Lan draws three lessons for today. The Party should arm minds with its latest theory, upholding Marxism's guiding position and the principle that the Party manages ideology. It should also keep using the 'theory of inculcation', which Lan says should rely mainly on positive propaganda rather than rote teaching. Lan adds that this includes online and offline work, using media convergence to win hearts in a 'competition for identification' and to establish socialist core values against erroneous trends of thought. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar reads Lenin's early party-building text to support the Party's current ideological work.
quoteEn: Ideological work is construction carried out inside people's minds, and an important way of forging souls and educating people.
quoteZh: 意识形态工作是在人的头脑里搞建设，是铸魂育人的重要方式

glossary.explanation: The Party's authority to direct what ideas and values prevail in society. In Chinese Party discourse it is closely tied to Xi Jinping's formula of leadership, management and discourse power in ideological work.
A principle in Chinese Party discourse that the Party directly controls ideological and propaganda work, including media and education.
Lenin's thesis in What Is to Be Done? that socialist consciousness must be brought to workers from outside by the party. Chinese official discourse uses it as a basic method of ideological education.
A tendency in Russian Social Democracy around 1900 that stressed economic struggles over wages and conditions over political struggle. Lenin attacked it in What Is to Be Done?.
A set of values promoted officially in China since the 18th Party Congress (2012), formulated at national, social and individual levels.

t: Lenin's important thought on being good at "looking at problems politically" and its contemporary value
zh: 列宁关于要善于“从政治上看问题”的重要思想及其当代价值
paras: Li Dongming asks what Lenin meant by the injunction that a proletarian party must be good at "looking at problems politically", and what the idea offers Party-building today. Li argues that Lenin treated this as a defining trait of the Bolshevik party. In Li's reading it helped the party seize the political initiative and defuse political risks, and it gives a model for strengthening a party's political construction and political leadership.

The article, published in Marxism Studies in 2022, opens with Xi Jinping's December 2020 call to be good at looking at problems politically. It then draws almost entirely on Lenin's writings and speeches from the period of the transition from War Communism to the New Economic Policy (NEP), including the trade-union debate and the 10th Congress of the Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks). Three sections reconstruct Lenin's thought: grasping political factors when assessing a situation, avoiding political dangers and errors, and putting political requirements into practice. A fourth section draws out its present-day value.

Li stresses that Lenin's remark that politics must take precedence over economics does not mean politics determines or replaces economics. It means that economic questions such as the food tax must first be judged by the relation between the working class and the peasantry, on which the survival of Soviet power depended. Li presents the Trotsky–Bukharin trade-union dispute as a failure of this approach. In Li's account Lenin saw danger in factional activity, in a debate that hostile forces could exploit, and in a split that could open the way to capitalist restoration. Li adds that Lenin demanded real ideological unity, not just an end to argument. On implementation, Li reports Lenin's calls to learn to trade, to master economic management, to avoid empty talk, and to "grasp the main link in the chain".

Li concludes that Lenin's approach still bears on Party-building in China. Li links it to three capacities set out by Xi: political judgement, political comprehension and political execution. Li calls on cadres to read situations through their political factors, to avoid political errors that endanger the Party's governing position, and to turn the Central Committee's decisions into concrete, creative work. Li holds that political initiative is the most advantageous initiative and political passivity the most dangerous. Read the original if you want a close account of how Lenin's NEP-era writings are used to support current Chinese Party discourse on political awareness and political risk.
quoteEn: This fully proves a principle: political initiative is the most advantageous initiative, and political passivity is the most dangerous passivity.
quoteZh: 这充分证明了一个道理：政治上的主动是最有利的主动，政治上的被动是最危险的被动。

glossary.explanation: The policy Soviet Russia adopted in 1921 in place of War Communism. It replaced grain requisitioning with a tax in kind and allowed limited private trade and state capitalism.
The Bolshevik economic policy of 1918–1921 during the Civil War. It featured grain requisitioning, nationalisation and labour mobilisation.

glossary.zh: 政治判断力、政治领悟力、政治执行力
glossary.pinyin: zhèngzhì pànduànlì, zhèngzhì lǐngwùlì, zhèngzhì zhíxínglì
glossary.en: political judgement, political comprehension and political execution
glossary.literal: political judging power, political understanding power, political executing power
glossary.explanation: Three capacities that Xi Jinping has called on Party members and cadres to develop. They are part of current Chinese Party discourse on political construction.
A strand of Party-building in China that stresses political orientation, discipline and loyalty to the Central Committee. It has been prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: The idea of self-reform in the Communist Manifesto and its contemporary value
zh: 《共产党宣言》的自我革命思想及其当代价值
paras: Miao Ruidan asks what the Communist Manifesto contributes to the Chinese Communist Party's current effort at self-reform. The article argues that the Manifesto holds a rich body of thought on how a proletarian party purifies, perfects, renews and improves itself, and that this thought forms the theoretical source of the Party's present self-reform. Miao sets this against the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), which named perseverance in self-reform as a historical lesson of the Party's first century.

The article has three parts. The first draws out four strands of thought from the Manifesto: purity (the basis of self-purification), vanguard character (the inner driving force of self-perfection), thoroughgoing revolutionary spirit (self-renewal) and party tactics (self-improvement). The second sets out the internal logic that links them. The third turns each strand into a requirement for the Party in the new era, presented under the Party's four capacities: self-purification, self-perfection, self-renewal and self-improvement.

In Miao's account, the logic runs from motive to aim to purpose. The motive comes from the proletarian party's essential nature: it has no special interests of its own, so it must keep its purity and advanced character in order to represent the future of the movement. The aim is to temper revolutionary spirit and capacity through renewal and improvement, a process that includes turning the blade inward. The ultimate purpose is to honour the original aspiration and mission of liberating the proletariat and all humankind. Miao then maps the Manifesto's themes onto current Party practice. Ideological, political and organisational purity correspond to ideals-and-convictions education, political building and disciplinary rules. The Manifesto's account of vanguard character is tied to a problem-oriented approach to institution-building and the mass line. Its continuous revolution is tied to upholding fundamental principles while innovating, to criticism and self-criticism, and to using self-reform to lead social revolution. Its tactics are tied to coordinating the 'two overall situations' at home and abroad.

Miao concludes that grasping the Manifesto's self-reform ideas as a theoretical source and 'political gene' has both theoretical value and practical relevance. It matters for advancing the Party's self-reform and for the great project of Party building in the new era. Throughout, the Manifesto is read as a source for contemporary Party-building doctrine. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese Party theorists derive the Party's four-part self-reform formula from a classic Marxist text.
quoteEn: The driving force of the proletarian party's self-reform derives from the essential nature of the proletarian party.
quoteZh: 无产阶级政党自我革命的动力，源自无产阶级政党的本质属性。

glossary.explanation: A key term in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for the Party's capacity to correct itself from within. The article breaks it into four components: self-purification, self-perfection, self-renewal and self-improvement.

A Party slogan stressing that members should keep to the founding goal of serving the people and pursuing national rejuvenation and communism. It was the theme of a 2019 Party-wide education campaign.

An official formulation referring to the overall strategy for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the profound changes in the world unseen in a century. The Party is asked to coordinate the two.
A long-standing Party working method that calls for drawing ideas from the people and returning them as policy. It is treated as one of the Party's fundamental working principles.

glossary.literal: keeping to what is right and innovating
glossary.explanation: A formulation in recent Party discourse that couples fidelity to core principles with innovation in theory and practice.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Keep advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era
zh: 把新时代中国特色社会主义不断推向前进
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 19 October 2022, this commentary responds to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and its theme of holding high the banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The authors argue that the Party will keep advancing this cause and winning new victories on the new journey of building a modern socialist country.

The piece is organised under three headings. It first treats socialism with Chinese characteristics as the renewal of scientific socialism in twenty-first-century China. It then presents it as the only correct path to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Finally it calls for consistent adherence to and development of the cause.

The authors contend that socialism with Chinese characteristics upholds the basic principles of scientific socialism while giving them Chinese features. They list Party leadership, the people's democratic dictatorship, public ownership as the mainstay, the guiding role of Marxism and a people-centred stance. They also claim that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party has enriched theories of development stages, social contradictions and modernization. In their account, this shows the path is correct and will be walked steadily and well.

The authors call for full implementation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and for pursuing high-quality development, common prosperity and whole-process people's democracy amid what they call great changes unseen in a century. They stress the "five musts" set out in the Congress report, including Party leadership and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official People's Daily framing of the 20th Party Congress theme.
quoteEn: Socialism with Chinese characteristics is both a great cause that we must keep advancing and the fundamental guarantee for opening up our future.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义既是我们必须不断推进的伟大事业，又是我们开辟未来的根本保证。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official name for China's path, theory and system since the reform era, presented as scientific socialism adapted to Chinese conditions.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central national goal of the Party, associated with the Chinese Dream and framed as restoring China's strength and standing.
Official term, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, for China's democratic model, said to cover every stage of political and policy processes.
Official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, stressed in Party policy under Xi Jinping.
Official economic goal, emphasised since 2017, favouring quality, innovation and efficiency over growth rates alone.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's discipline and anti-corruption drive under Xi Jinping.

t: Persistently and deeply advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 持之以恒深入推进全面从严治党
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 15 September 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, Li Lifeng argues that the Party must keep advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party as the way to consolidate its long-term governing position. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's speech to a seminar of provincial and ministerial leading cadres, the commentary treats this governance as the Party's self-reform, which Li presents as leading social revolution.

The piece has three sections. The first presents full and rigorous self-governance as a great practice of self-reform in the new era. The second calls for a political awareness that this work is "always on the road". The third sets out measures for opening "new realms" of self-reform.

In the first section Li ties the policy to five tasks: the great struggle, the great cause, the great project of Party building, the great dream, and the Party's founding mission. Li holds that courage in self-reform is the Party's most distinctive trait and has let it solve its own problems repeatedly. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Li says, the Party has reversed laxity in Party governance and found a path to escape the "historical cycle" through self-reform. The second section argues the work must continue because of the "four tests" and "four dangers", a turbulent international environment, and unresolved impurities in the Party's politics, thinking, organisation and conduct. Li quotes Xi on the continuing struggle against corruption.

The third section gives six measures: political building as the guiding principle, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds; ideological building through theoretical study; strict discipline and a campaign against formalism, bureaucratism and extravagance under the eight-point rules; a sustained anti-corruption drive with "zero tolerance", hitting "tigers" and "flies"; stronger Party organisations and a cadre corps willing to struggle; and a system of Party regulations and supervision. Li concludes that only persistence will keep the Party from degenerating and keep the "red country" from changing colour. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Party theory framed self-reform and anti-corruption on the eve of the 20th Party Congress."
quoteEn: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the great practice of the Party's self-reform in the new era, and it has opened a new realm of self-reform for a century-old Party.
quoteZh: 全面从严治党是新时代党的自我革命的伟大实践，开辟了百年大党自我革命的新境界。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), to tighten discipline, fight corruption and strengthen Party organisation. It is one of the "Four Comprehensives" strategic layout.
A formulation stressing that the Party corrects its own problems by itself. Xi Jinping presents it as the Party's answer to the "historical cycle" of rise and decline.
A 2021 Party formulation affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb formalism, bureaucratism, extravagance and other undesirable work styles among officials.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The world significance of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的世界意义
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in October 2022, asks what Chinese modernization means beyond China. Guo argues that it breaks the myth that "modernization means Westernization", develops modernization theory, and offers the world a new form of human civilisation, a different path for developing countries and a fresh vitality for scientific socialism.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's five defining features of Chinese modernization. It then proceeds in three numbered sections: the creation of a new form of human civilisation, the reshaping of the international order, and the strengths of the socialist system.

In the first section, Guo contends that Chinese modernization abandons four features of the traditional model: capital-centred development and polarisation, material growth as the sole aim, disregard for ecology, and expansionist plunder. In their place it puts common prosperity, balance between material and cultural-ethical advance, harmony between humanity and nature, and a community with a shared future for mankind. The second section describes an irreversible trend of "the East rising and the West declining" and cites 2021 trade and foreign-exchange-reserve figures, as well as a population of over 1.4 billion entering modernity. The third section argues that people-centredness shields modernization from the logic of capital and so expands scientific socialism.

Guo concludes that the socialist character under Communist Party leadership and the people-centred orientation are the essential features of Chinese modernization and the root of its success. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 framed the international meaning of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The essence of modernization is the modernization of people, and modernization must not depart from the path of putting people first.
quoteZh: 现代化的本质是人的现代化，现代化建设不能偏离以人为本的轨道

glossary.explanation: A Party concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), describing China's own path to modernization as distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, which Xi Jinping's leadership has made a central objective of development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations based on cooperation and respect for each country's chosen path.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilisation
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping to describe the civilisational outcome of Chinese modernization, presented as an alternative to the Western model.

t: Reading the great changes unseen in a century through principle, theory and philosophy
st: A review of Great-Power Games and the Future World: International Relations in the Perspective of the Philosophy of History
zh: 从道理学理哲理解读世界百年未有之大变局
zhSub: 《大国博弈与未来世界：历史哲学视域中的国际关系》评介
paras: This book review, first published in Guangming Daily in September 2022, introduces Han Zhen's Great-Power Games and the Future World: International Relations in the Perspective of the Philosophy of History (Central Party School Press, June 2022). Han is a professor at Beijing Normal University. Reviewer Lin Jianhua presents the book as an original work that uses the philosophy of history to interpret what Xi Jinping has called the great changes unseen in a century, and sums up its three main features.

According to Lin, the book examines how international relations and the international order ought to be built and how they actually are, the basic pattern of interaction between China and the future world, and the general laws of social development. The review is organised around the three features, each ending with one dimension of explanation: the philosophical (zhéli), the theoretical (xuéli) and the practical (daoli).

The first feature is that the book takes historical materialism and materialist dialectics as its basic guide. In Lin's account, Han holds that world history is driven by contradictions between productive forces and relations of production, not by good intentions, and that dialectics joins idealist "ought" with realist "is". The second is looking beneath appearances through unity of opposites. Three chapters treat North–South, East–West and capitalism–socialism, and Han reads the changing balance in each as favouring the South, the East and socialism. The third is strategic clarity and confidence and historical consciousness. Lin reports Han's view that the United States regards China as its chief strategic rival, so hopes of an American change of heart contradict historical materialism.

Lin concludes, following Han, that China should combine resolute and skilful struggle with promotion of shared human values and a community with a shared future for mankind. The review treats this as both the fundamental theme of the philosophy of history and a rational demand for the future. Read the original if you want a short Chinese-language introduction to how a Party-affiliated scholarly book frames great-power rivalry through Marxist philosophy of history.
quoteEn: The author points out that world history has never developed according to people's good wishes, but is the product of the movement of social contradictions, especially those between productive forces and relations of production and between economic base and superstructure.
quoteZh: 作者指出,世界历史从来不是按照人们的善良愿望发展的,而是社会矛盾运动特别是生产力与生产关系之间、经济基础与上层建筑之间矛盾运动的产物。

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.literal: great changes in the world not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping since around 2017–2018, describing a period of rapid shifts in the global balance of power, technology and international order.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–2013, calling for shared interests and joint responses to global challenges.
The Marxist theory that material production and the contradictions between productive forces and relations of production drive historical development.
The philosophical study of the overall direction, laws and meaning of historical development, the perspective the reviewed book adopts.

keywords: great changes unseen in a century

t: Why confidence in our institutions has grown firmer
zh: 制度自信何以更加坚定
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 28 September 2022, asks why confidence in China's institutions (zhidu zixin) has become firmer in the new era. Ren Lixuan answers that the institutional system has become more mature and settled, and that it has shown strong governance effectiveness in practice. In the article's account, these two grounds are the basis for stronger confidence in the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews institution-building since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee and the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee, which dealt with modernizing the system and capacity of national governance. The second sets out the governance results of the "Chinese system" in tackling long-standing problems and in meeting risks. The third turns to what must be done on the new journey.

Ren describes the institutional system as complete, scientific and standardised, and effective in operation. The article lists 13 areas of institutional innovation, with the Party's leadership system holding the commanding position. Ren treats governance effectiveness as the test of any system and cites poverty alleviation, major technological projects and ecological protection as results. The article adds the response to Covid-19, external pressure from the United States and the West, and the Party's self-reform as further evidence. It contrasts "Chinese governance" with "Western disorder". It attributes this effectiveness to the Party's leadership as the greatest advantage and to the coordination of institutions across levels, which it says yields a whole greater than the sum of its parts.

For the new journey, Ren calls for three things. These are to keep drawing on the Party's leadership as the greatest advantage, including through the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, to hold to fundamental principles while innovating, and to turn institutional advantages into governance effectiveness. The last requires strict implementation, with leading cadres as the "key minority" setting an example, and comprehensive supervision of enforcement. Ren concludes that the aim is to modernize national governance by the time a modern socialist country is built.

Read the original if you want a representative example of the official People's Daily case for institutional confidence in the Xi Jinping era, including its list of the 13 institutional areas.
quoteEn: One important measure of whether a country's institutions are successful and superior is whether, in the face of major risks and challenges, they can command all quarters and organise every side to respond together.
quoteZh: 衡量一个国家的制度是否成功、是否优越，一个重要方面就是看其在重大风险挑战面前，能不能号令四面、组织八方共同应对。

glossary.explanation: Confidence in the socialist system with Chinese characteristics. It is part of the 'Four-sphere Confidence' formula in official discourse.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernizing the system and capacity of national governance
glossary.explanation: The overall goal of comprehensively deepening reform, set at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013. It refers to improving institutions and their implementation.
A formula adopted in 2021 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline itself and remove harmful elements, linked to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
A phrase in official discourse for China's institutional system. It is paired with 'Chinese governance' (中国之治), the order and results the system is said to produce.

t: How cultural confidence has become more firm
zh: 文化自信何以更加坚定
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in September 2022, Ren Lixuan asks why cultural confidence among the Party and the Chinese people has grown firmer over the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Ren's answer is that cultural work under Xi Jinping has produced "historic achievements" and that this confidence is a basic, deep and lasting force on which national rejuvenation depends. The piece is an authoritative commentary on Party cultural policy rather than a scholarly study.

The article has three parts. The first sets out six areas in which cultural confidence is said to have strengthened: Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, the treatment of fine traditional Chinese culture, the meeting of people's spiritual and cultural needs, responses to risks and challenges, and exchange and mutual learning among civilisations. The second part explains how the Party's "cultural consciousness" and Xi Jinping's leadership and thought guide this process. The third turns to the future and sets out three tasks.

Ren argues that cultural confidence is built on Marxism as the guiding ideology, since abandoning it would mean losing one's soul and direction. It also rests on a "scientific" attitude to tradition, meaning creative transformation and innovative development. The author cites the Party's elevation of cultural confidence into the Four-sphere Confidence, the Party's control over propaganda, ideology and media, and Xi's speeches and cultural diplomacy. Examples include popular television dramas, free public cultural venues, the "great anti-epidemic spirit" and the poverty-alleviation spirit, and the 2019 Dialogue of Asian Civilizations. Ren presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the theoretical guide that gave the Party's understanding of culture a new level.

Looking ahead, Ren calls for adherence to the cultural development path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, which the article calls the only correct path. This means learning from other cultures without treating foreign things as superior. Ren also urges cultural creation grounded in practice, with reform of cultural management systems and use of advanced technology, and the full release of the spiritual force in cultural confidence for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an example of the official People's Daily framing of cultural confidence and Party leadership over culture after 2012.
quoteEn: Unwaveringly upholding Marxism as the guide in the ideological sphere is the most fundamental requirement and the most concentrated expression of firm cultural confidence.
quoteZh: 在意识形态领域坚定不移坚持以马克思主义为指导，是坚定文化自信最根本的要求、最集中的体现。

glossary.explanation: A concept prominent in Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012), referring to confidence in China's own culture, including traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. Xi Jinping has called it the most basic, deepest and most lasting force in a nation's development.
The official formula of confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Culture was added as the fourth after the 18th Party Congress.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central goal of Party discourse since the 2010s, meaning China's return to national strength and prosperity, with a target of building a modern socialist country by mid-century.
The official name of the Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining Marxism with China's national conditions.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
