glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018, that bears the name of Xi Jinping.
A term meaning a reflective awareness of the role and development of one's culture. In this article it describes the Party's deliberate positioning of culture in its strategy.

t: How theoretical confidence becomes firmer
zh: 理论自信何以更加坚定
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in September 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, Ren Lixuan asks why the Party and the whole country should hold firmer confidence in theory. The answer is that Marxism, repeatedly adapted to Chinese conditions, has proved itself in practice. The commentary presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the latest result of that process, and as the basis for stronger theoretical confidence.

The piece has four parts. It first reviews modern Chinese history to explain why "Marxism works". It then sets out how the Thought opens up "new realms" of Marxism. A third part treats the Thought as a theory that arises from practice and guides it, citing the achievements of the decade since 2012. A final part gives practical requirements for the new journey.

Ren's central claim is that the Party's successes come from adapting Marxism to China's realities and to traditional Chinese culture. The author traces this through Mao Zedong Thought and Deng Xiaoping Theory to the new Thought, which is called twenty-first-century Marxism. The Thought is said to answer major questions in four areas: national rejuvenation, Chinese modernization, building a Marxist party in long-term power, and the world's future. Under the last heading the author lists the community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative. In Ren's account the Thought has guided the response to external pressure and to the pandemic, the Party's anti-corruption and self-reform drive, and economic and social progress. The author cites GDP of 114 trillion yuan and per capita GDP above 12,000 US dollars.

Ren calls for three things: studying and absorbing the Thought thoroughly, applying it to solve concrete problems, and continuing to innovate while upholding fundamental principles, so that Marxism is further adapted to China. The author argues that theoretical innovation never ends and that confidence rests on understanding. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official Party commentary justified theoretical confidence on the eve of the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: Firm theoretical confidence is built on a profound theoretical understanding.
quoteZh: 坚定的理论自信，建立在深刻的理论认知基础上。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, which the Party contrasts with Western models. It is characterised by features such as a huge population and common prosperity.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, advanced since 2012–13, which stresses interdependence among states and calls for a new type of international relations.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013.

t: How confidence in the path has become firmer
zh: 道路自信何以更加坚定
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 26 September 2022, during the press-conference series "China's Decade" and shortly before the 20th Party Congress, Ren Lixuan asks why confidence in the path (daolu zixin) of socialism with Chinese characteristics has grown firmer. The commentary answers that the achievements of the past decade and a deepened understanding of that path justify firmer confidence. Ren concludes that China will neither return to a "closed and rigid old path" nor take the "evil path" of changing the Party's banner.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews what the path has achieved since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second sets out four "unities" that the author says capture the new understanding of the path. The third lists four requirements for going forward. Throughout, Ren draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements.

In the first part, Ren credits the path with three results. It has produced Chinese modernization, which Ren says rejects the Western model of modernization centred on capital, polarisation, materialism and external plunder, and breaks the notion that modernization means Westernization. It has created a "new form of human civilization". And it has brought the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation into an irreversible process, with the building of a moderately prosperous society in all respects, GDP of 114 trillion yuan in 2021, and the leap from "standing up" to "becoming rich" to "becoming strong". The second part presents the four unities: Party leadership with the people's主体 role, scientific socialism's theoretical logic with China's historical logic, conformity to laws of development with conformity to purpose, and promoting Chinese civilization with promoting common human values.

For the future, Ren calls for upholding and improving Party leadership, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. Ren also urges independence and self-reliance, coordinated advancement of the "five-sphere integrated plan" and the "four-pronged comprehensive strategy", and development as the first priority with solid steps toward common prosperity. The author holds that doing so will secure the second centenary goal and the Chinese Dream. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official Party commentary in 2022 framed the "path" as a justification for continuity ahead of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The path of socialism with Chinese characteristics is a path that has grown from within, inheriting China's historical and cultural traditions, rooted in China's distinctive national conditions, and aimed at solving China's problems.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义道路是传承中国历史文化传统、立足中国独特国情、着眼解决中国问题而内生出来的道路。

glossary.explanation: One of the 'Four-sphere Confidence' formulations: confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is used in Party discourse to affirm the chosen course of development.
The official term for China's own path to modernization under Communist Party leadership. Party texts describe it as distinct from Western models.
A Party formulation, adopted in 2021, that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole. It also affirms the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party requirement to uphold the authority of the Central Committee and the core status of the General Secretary. The Party presents it as a political obligation for all members.
The official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, with narrowed regional, urban–rural and income gaps. It is presented as an essential requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The overarching goal of Party policy since 2012, tied to the Chinese Dream. It is linked to two centenary goals, in 2021 and 2049.

t: Building China's spiritual strength in the new era
zh: 构筑新时代的中国精神力量
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 28 September 2022, reviews what the author presents as the achievements of socialist cultural-ethical progress (spiritual civilization building) since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Tian argues that the key to new breakthroughs has been adherence to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and a people-centred approach to development.

The article first surveys three strands of work: creating civilized cities, villages and families; expanding civilized practice through volunteer service; and cultivating civilized conduct through moral role models, festival activities and youth education. It then draws out the principles said to underlie these results.

In Tian's account, the work has produced wider and more credible national civilized-city programmes, rural customs reform linked to poverty alleviation and rural revitalization, and new practice centres in county-level districts across the country. The author sets out four requirements: keep the people's interests first, uphold fundamental principles while innovating in forms and carriers, seek truth and practical results, and persevere over the long term with broad participation. Each is tied to raising people's sense of gain, happiness and security and to strengthening cultural confidence.

Tian concludes that, under Xi Jinping's personal guidance, this work should keep deepening civilized creation, practice and cultivation so as to raise society's level of civility. The stated aim is to build Chinese spirit, values and strength for achieving the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style summary of how Party-aligned writers framed spiritual civilization building in autumn 2022.
quoteEn: Spiritual civilization building must be people-centred: it must always put the interests of the masses first, take improving people's wellbeing as its starting and end point, listen and respond to their concerns, and, while serving them, publicise to, educate and guide them, so as to rally hearts, warm hearts and build common purpose.
quoteZh: 精神文明建设要做到以人民为中心，始终把群众利益放在第一位，把提升民生福祉作为出发点和落脚点，倾听回应群众关切，在服务群众过程中宣传群众、教育群众、引导群众，做到聚民心、暖人心、筑同心。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official term for efforts to raise ethical standards, culture and ideology alongside material development, through campaigns, education and public activities.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to develop rural economy, governance and culture.

t: Relying on tenacious struggle to open up new horizons for the cause
zh: 依靠顽强斗争打开事业发展新天地
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 22 September 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, Liu Zhiming argues that struggle is the decisive means by which the Communist Party of China has achieved its results and the means it must keep using. The short commentary contends that the future, like the past, has to be won through struggle rather than received as a gift.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews the Party's history since 1921 and claims that all the achievements of the Party and people came through continuous struggle. The second explains why struggle is needed now, citing the current international situation and complacency inside the Party. The third sets out how a spirit of responsibility and struggle should be cultivated.

Liu's reasoning starts from a Marxist premise: society advances through contradictions, and struggle is the form in which development and practical innovation are realised. The author describes a world of accelerating great changes unseen in a century, with unilateralism, protectionism and hegemonism, and says China faces more complex risks than before. Liu also points to cadres who seek a comfortable post, avoid difficulties or pass problems upward, and warns that a party or country that loses its will to struggle is close to collapse. Struggle in this sense is not for its own sake or for private gain. It serves the people's aspiration for a better life and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Liu calls for selflessness and courage, a spirit of historical initiative, and a focus on what the commentary calls "matters of national importance", with local interests subordinate to the whole. Struggle capacity is not innate, the author says, and must be tempered through theoretical study, including understanding the Two Establishes, strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence and achieving the Two Upholds, and through practice in hard places. Liu concludes that cadres should take the initiative in struggles, never yielding on matters of principle, as the country advances towards the goal of a modern socialist country and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary in 2022 framed struggle as a duty for cadres in the new era.
quoteEn: Our Party has made history through struggle, and it must all the more rely on struggle to win the future.
quoteZh: 我们党依靠斗争创造历史，更要依靠斗争赢得未来。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted in the Party's 2021 historical resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and standing, with the target of a modern socialist country by mid-century.

t: Continuously advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context through the "Two Integrations"
zh: 在“两个结合”中不断推进马克思主义中国化
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 29 September 2022, He Bingbing asks what is required to keep advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context through the Two Integrations: combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The short commentary argues that this work rests on four supports: theoretical, practical, cultural and political.

The piece is organised into four numbered sections. Each takes one support in turn: upholding the basic principles of Marxism, grasping China's concrete realities, transforming and developing fine traditional Chinese culture, and deepening the Party's self-reform.

On theory, He insists that Marxism's guiding position must never waver. The author calls both for rejecting a rigid, stagnant attitude towards Marxism and for opposing attempts to distort its principles in the name of "reality" or to deny their universal validity in the name of "particularity". On practice, He treats the interplay of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the great changes unseen in a century as the starting point. Questions such as common prosperity, high-level scientific self-reliance and social fairness are named as problems that theory must answer. On culture, He rejects both cultural nihilism and cultural conservatism, and urges drawing the essence from traditional culture and giving it contemporary form.

In the fourth section, He argues that the Party's leadership and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, driven by a people-centred orientation and the mass line, guarantee that adapting Marxism stays on the right course. The author presents the Party's self-reform as leading broader social transformation. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a 2022 official-press commentary frames the Two Integrations in terms of theory, practice, culture and Party leadership.
quoteEn: If Marxism's guidance is abandoned or departed from, the "Two Integrations" will lose their soul and lose their direction.
quoteZh: 背离或放弃马克思主义的指导，“两个结合”就会失去灵魂、迷失方向。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressing that Marxism must be combined with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to Party theory around 2021–2022.

glossary.en: adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-standing term for applying Marxism to China's conditions and developing it there. It is usually presented as a process of theoretical innovation.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Slogan for the Party-building and anti-corruption drive pursued since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing discipline and strict internal oversight.
Official term for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself from within, presented as its means of avoiding decline.
Official goal of broadly shared prosperity, given renewed emphasis in Party policy from 2021.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: Official description of the current shifts in the international order, used in Chinese foreign-policy and theoretical discourse.

t: Drawing nourishment for the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics from fine traditional Chinese culture
zh: 从中华优秀传统文化汲取中国特色社会主义政治经济学的养分
paras: Chen Xudong, in a short newspaper commentary first published in Guangming Daily in September 2022, asks how the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics can draw on traditional Chinese economic thought. The author argues that it should systematically extract, summarise and elevate the ideas of fine traditional Chinese culture, because economics is essentially a historical science.

The piece has three parts. It first notes that Marx's Theories of Surplus Value and Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations both built on earlier doctrines, and it describes the history of Chinese economic thought as a weak discipline in Chinese universities, lacking an authoritative textbook spanning ancient and modern times. It then discusses the historical influence of Chinese thought abroad. Finally it maps traditional ideas onto the new development philosophy.

Chen observes that ancient China had no professional economists, so economic ideas lie scattered through political and philosophical writings and must be "refined" by researchers. The author cites claims of Chinese influence on the French Physiocrats and on American agricultural legislation during the Great Depression, via the "ever-normal granary". Chen then pairs each element of the new development philosophy with a tradition: innovation with the Book of Changes, coordination with the Doctrine of the Mean, green development with "unity of heaven and humanity" and ancient environmental offices, openness with Silk Road and Song-Yuan maritime trade, and sharing with Laozi, Confucius and Guanzi on common prosperity.

Chen concludes that these resources offer useful intellectual and practical reference for the Belt and Road Initiative, institutional opening up and the pursuit of common prosperity, even though many ancient ideas were never put into practice. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese scholars link classical Chinese texts to current policy concepts.
quoteEn: The development of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics cannot do without excavating and organising traditional Chinese economic thought.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学的发展离不开对中国传统经济思想的挖掘整理。

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì zhèngzhì jīngjìxué
glossary.en: political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: A body of economic theory promoted in official discourse since the 2010s, presented as a Marxist political economy adapted to China's reform-era practice.
Xi Jinping's formula, introduced in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development as the guide to economic policy.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, promoted prominently under Xi Jinping as a defining feature of socialism.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

t: "People first" and the logic of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: “人民至上”与中国特色社会主义政治经济学的逻辑理路
paras: Hu Leming asks how the principle of putting the people first (人民至上) can serve as the organising thread of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article, published in Guangming Daily in October 2022, argues that this principle gives the discipline a coherent logic. In Hu's account, the logic runs from people's everyday needs, through micro-level and macro-level analysis, to common prosperity and the all-round development of the person.

The piece is built in four sections: the logical starting point, the micro logic, the macro logic and the logical destination. Hu draws on Marx's treatment of needs and of labour, capital and relative surplus population. Hu also draws on a Party resolution on the Party's century of struggle, a Report to the 19th Party Congress (2017) and remarks by Xi Jinping.

Hu first proposes "living needs" as the starting category. Marx never defined it clearly, Hu says, yet it played a hidden role in his theories of value, surplus value and crisis, and it links life activity to production. Starting from the sequence of life process, needs and production process, Hu argues, the discipline can unfold the tensions between production and consumption, government and market, and public and private goods. At the micro level, Hu holds that the central issue is a harmonious and stable cooperation between labour and capital. Hu calls for worker participation in management through staff and workers' congresses, shared enterprise surplus with pay rising in step with productivity, and government and social organisations that curb monopoly and "disorderly expansion of capital". Hu also calls for extending labour protection to platform and flexible workers. At the macro level, Hu argues that employment should come first, and that the discipline should abandon the Western mainstream's one-sided stress on GDP growth. Hu cites Marx to warn that if capital and market logic alone steer technological change, a large relative surplus population results. Hu therefore urges labour-biased innovation, employment-oriented policy and social security for flexible workers and migrant workers.

Hu concludes that common prosperity and the all-round development of the person are the destination of this political economy. Meeting needs is its precondition, labour–capital cooperation its micro foundation and employment-first its macro safeguard. Hu stresses that common prosperity in the primary stage of socialism falls short of Marx's vision of distribution according to need. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Chinese economist links "people first" to the structure of a Marxist political economy, covering labour–capital relations, digital-era employment and common prosperity.
quoteEn: The micro-level analysis of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics must both put into practice the idea of "centring on the worker" and take account of the rights of other factor owners, promoting a harmonious and stable cooperation between labour and capital on the basis of reasonable protection of workers' rights.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学的微观分析既要落实“以劳动者为中心”的理念，又要兼顾其他要素所有者的权益，促进实现劳动者权益合理保护基础之上的劳动与资本之间和谐稳定的合作关系。

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学
glossary.en: the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The officially promoted body of economic theory that seeks to systematise China's reform-era experience within a Marxist framework. It is often linked to Xi Jinping's call to develop it.
A Party principle, stressed in recent official documents, that the interests of the people are placed above all else in governance.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all members of society, which Xi Jinping has stressed since 2021.
The official characterisation of China's current historical stage, which is said to last a long time and to justify market mechanisms and mixed ownership.
A strategy named in the Report to the 19th Party Congress that makes employment the top priority of macroeconomic policy.

t: Did Lenin not know of the "Caudine Forks" hypothesis?
st: A perspective based on textual verification
zh: 列宁不知道跨越“卡夫丁峡谷”设想吗
zhSub: ？——基于文本学考证的视角
paras: Most Chinese scholars hold that Lenin did not know Marx's hypothesis that Russia might skip the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism, because the term never appears in his works and key Marx and Engels texts were unpublished in his lifetime. Zhu and Yang ask whether this is true and answer that, on textual evidence, Lenin did know the hypothesis. They argue that it served him as a weapon against the Russian Narodniks (populists) and as a theoretical basis for the October Revolution.

The article first reconstructs the publication history of the relevant texts by Marx, by Engels and by the two jointly. It separates items published in Lenin's lifetime from those that were not: Marx's draft replies to Vera Zasulich (1924), his ethnological notebooks (after 1958) and Engels's 1893 letters to Nikolai Danielson. It then checks Lenin's writings and marginal notes for traces of the published texts. A final section considers how the hypothesis, the "theory of victory in one country" and the October Revolution relate.

The authors' evidence is that Lenin quoted Marx's letter to the editors of Otechestvennye Zapiski at length against Mikhailovsky and marked the key passage "Note". He also asked for and praised Engels's 1894 Afterword to "On Social Relations in Russia", annotated it in 1906, and showed close familiarity with the 1882 Russian preface to the Communist Manifesto. The authors argue that Lenin used this knowledge against the Narodniks on three points: capitalism and the dissolution of the commune were already facts, peasants were backward small producers rather than "born communists", and Russia could leap forward only through proletarian-led social revolution.

On this basis Zhu and Yang reject the view that Lenin's "theory of victory in one country" merely coincides with Marx's hypothesis. In their account the hypothesis is its theoretical cornerstone, Lenin's theory of imperialism supports it, and it in turn guides the October Revolution. They conclude that establishing Lenin's knowledge of the hypothesis explains this logical chain and gives Russia, China and other backward countries a theoretical basis of legitimacy for taking the socialist road first. Read the original if you want a source-by-source account of the publication history and of Lenin's references to Marx and Engels on the Russian commune.
quoteEn: The hypothesis of skipping the "Caudine Forks" is the theoretical cornerstone of the "theory of victory in one country", the theory of imperialism is its theoretical support, and the "theory of victory in one country" is in turn the theoretical forerunner of the October Revolution.
quoteZh: 跨越“卡夫丁峡谷”设想是“一国胜利论”的理论基石，帝国主义论是“一国胜利论”的理论支撑，“一国胜利论”又是十月革命的理论先导。

glossary.explanation: Marx's image, from the Roman defeat at the Caudine Forks, for the humiliations of capitalism. Chinese scholarship uses it for his late idea that Russia might reach socialism without passing through capitalist development.

glossary.en: theory of victory in one country
glossary.explanation: Lenin's view that socialist revolution can win first in one or a few countries, not everywhere at once. Chinese scholars contrast it with Marx and Engels's expectation of a joint, simultaneous victory.
Russian populist revolutionaries of the 19th century who saw the peasant commune as the basis of a socialist path that would avoid capitalism.

t: Did Marx really think the circulation process creates value?
st: Upholding the monism of "productive labour creates value" and its lessons for the new era
zh: 马克思真的认为流通过程能创造价值吗？
zhSub: 坚持“生产劳动创造价值”一元论及其在新时代的启示
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 5
paras: Wang Xianpeng takes up a long-running dispute in Chinese economics: whether labour in circulation (trade, transport, services) creates value. The question has returned with the rise of the tertiary sector, after earlier debates in the 1960s and the early reform years. Through a close reading of Marx's texts, Wang argues that Marx did not hold that circulation creates value, and that only productive labour does.

The article has four parts. It first establishes productive labour creating value as the cornerstone of Marx's critique of political economy. It then examines the main passages in Volume II of Capital that are cited to show circulation creates value, namely those on transport costs, storage costs and the transport industry's "useful effect". Next it draws four conclusions about how to read Marx's monism. It ends with the significance of this stance for contemporary socialist practice.

Wang's central move is textual. Citing the 1861–63 manuscripts, Wang says Marx's "labour" means labour directly exchanged with capital in material production, and that services and "total labour" fall outside it. Wang then reads the Volume II passages closely. Marx speaks of value "added" (zhuijia), not "created". His remarks that costs act as value-creating are limited to the "single capitalist" and concern price mark-ups, not value. And what transport sells is a "useful effect", not a commodity. Wang adds a logical test: if circulation created value, the value of the same good would differ by transport distance, which contradicts the determination of value by socially necessary labour time. Wang says the proponents cannot explain where the extra value would come from.

Wang concludes that abandoning the monism would dissolve the coherence of Marx's system and, in socialist practice, split theory from practice and open the way to claims that Marxism is outdated. Circulation and non-productive labour are still said to be necessary for realising value and use-value. Wang adds that separating them from value creation helps clarify the nature of trade, finance and intermediary services, strengthen the real economy, guard against the disorderly expansion of capital and advance common prosperity. Read the original if you want a text-by-text defence of the view that Marx confined value creation to production, or want to see how this debate is tied to current economic policy.
quoteEn: It can be seen that it is \"productive labour\", not \"total labour\", that creates value.
quoteZh: 可见，是“生产劳动”而非“总体劳动”创造了价值。

glossary.explanation: A goal of the Chinese Party-state to achieve prosperity for all, emphasised in official discourse especially since 2021. It is linked to narrowing income and regional gaps.
Production of goods and services, such as manufacturing, as opposed to finance and speculative activity. Official discourse treats it as the foundation of national economic strength.
In Marx's usage, labour that produces surplus value for capital. Chinese economists debated in the 1960s and 1980s whether commercial and service labour counts as such.

t: Engels's threefold contribution to defending Marxist ideological discourse power in his later years
zh: 恩格斯晚年维护马克思主义意识形态话语权的三重贡献
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2022 no. 9
paras: Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the article notes, strengthening the Party's capacity for ideological discourse and holding firmly to ideological discourse power has been a central task. Tang argues that Chinese scholarship on the Marxist lineage of this theme remains fragmentary because Marx and Engels never used the term itself. Tang's thesis is that Engels, after Marx's death in 1883, was the first to defend Marxist ideological discourse power systematically, through three linked contributions: polemic combined with defence, refinement combined with development, and transformation combined with popularisation.

The article first argues that Engels's role has been obscured by Western interpretations, notably the 'Marx–Engels opposition' thesis of Western Marx scholarship, and by Chinese research that follows Western Marxism or Marx studies. It then takes the three contributions in turn, drawing on The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy, Anti-Dühring and Engels's late letters on historical materialism. It closes with lessons for contemporary China.

On polemic, Tang argues that Engels countered the bourgeois claim that the state is eternal, the revival of neo-Kantian and neo-Hegelian thought, Paul Barth's charge of 'economic materialism', and the dogmatic reading of the 'Young Ones' such as Paul Ernst. Against the last two, Engels held that the economic factor is decisive only 'in the last instance', and Tang reads this phrase as meaning necessity, mediation and non-exclusivity. On development, Tang credits Engels with defining ideology as 'false consciousness', mapping its layers by distance from the economic base, introducing the relative independence of ideology and stressing its reaction on the base. On popularisation, Tang presents Anti-Dühring as the first complete systematic presentation of Marxism, and Socialism: Utopian and Scientific as the model for turning a theoretical system into a discourse workers could grasp.

Tang concludes that grasping Engels is necessary for understanding Marxism, and that his account of the interaction of economic base and superstructure still guides practice. Tang links this to Xi Jinping's 2013 statement that ideological work is an extremely important task of the Party. Tang calls on Chinese scholars to adopt a 'fighter, not gentleman' attitude toward anti-Marxist currents, combine critique with construction, and join theoretical development with popularisation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a Chinese reading of Engels's late letters and polemics as a source for current ideological discourse power.
quoteEn: In his later years Engels, responding to the situation of the international workers' movement, combined polemic with defence, refinement with development, and transformation with popularisation, making an outstanding intellectual contribution to defending Marxist ideological discourse power and accumulating valuable practical experience.
quoteZh: 恩格斯晚年顺应国际工人运动形势，坚持论战与捍卫相结合、完善与发展相结合、转化与普及相结合，为维护马克思主义意识形态话语权作出了杰出思想贡献，积累了宝贵实践经验。

glossary.explanation: A concept prominent in Chinese Party discourse since the 2010s. It refers to the capacity to shape public narratives and have one's ideological account accepted, domestically and internationally.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary developments. It describes the Party's ongoing theoretical innovation.
Engels's idea, developed in his 1890s letters, that ideology and the state develop by their own logic and react on the economic base while still being determined by it ultimately.
Engels's qualification of the economic factor as determining history only 'in the last instance'. Tang reads it as implying necessity, mediation and non-exclusivity.
Western academic study of Marx's texts, often treated by Chinese writers as separating Marx from Engels and from later Marxism.

t: A contemporary decoding of Marx's philosophical revolution
st: Analysis of major theoretical questions in the Theses on Feuerbach
zh: 马克思哲学变革的当代解码
zhSub: 《关于费尔巴哈的提纲》重大理论问题辨析
paras: Hou Huiqin takes up a long-running dispute over Marx's Theses on Feuerbach (1845). One influential reading, which Hou says is often presented as consensus in Chinese scholarship, holds that the Theses mark a 'practical turn' founding 'practical materialism' and a 'practice ontology'. Hou rejects this reading. The article argues that the Theses perfect a worldview Marx had already reached in 1843–44, and that practice belongs to the epistemology of dialectical materialism, not to ontology.

The article has four parts. It first places the Theses in intellectual history through a critique of Louis Althusser's 'epistemological break'. It then examines the 'two transformations' that Marx completed in the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher period, and asks why the Theses target Feuerbach. It ends by locating the scientific view of practice within Marxist philosophy and by reading the eleventh thesis. Hou draws on Marx's Rheinische Zeitung articles, the 1844 Manuscripts, The German Ideology, and statements by Engels and Lenin.

Hou makes three main moves. First, against Althusser, Hou separates two kinds of Feuerbachian influence: the materialist standpoint, which Marx never abandoned, and abstract humanism, which Marx held at a distance from the start. Marx's materialist turn, Hou argues, came with the discovery of the proletariat and the communist standpoint, and so preceded the Theses. The Theses supplied a scientific way of stating that worldview. Second, Hou distinguishes materialist from idealist activity: Marx's innovation lies in the objective conditioning of the subject, not in subjective initiative. Feuerbach grasped the 'sensuous object' but not 'sensuous activity'. Third, Hou holds that 'the priority of external nature' is the premise of historical materialism. Practice, citing Lenin and Mao Zedong, mediates the transformation of the 'thing-in-itself' into a 'thing-for-us' and cannot be an ontological foundation.

Hou concludes that materialism, not practice, is the primary core of Marxist philosophy. Hou reads the eleventh thesis as saying not that earlier philosophers only interpreted the world, but that they lacked a scientific knowledge of it and a real social force to change it. Hou warns that stressing practice apart from this premise leads to a 'value socialism' and to the rejection of scientific socialism. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-philosophy defence of dialectical materialism against 'practical materialism' readings, built on close citation of Marx, Engels and Lenin.
quoteEn: It is not the view of practice that determines materialism; rather, materialism determines the division between two views of practice, the materialist and the idealist.
quoteZh: 不是实践观决定了唯物论，而是唯物论决定了两种实践观的分野，即唯物论实践观和唯心论实践观。

glossary.explanation: A reading of Marx, influential in Chinese philosophy since the 1980s, that treats practice as the core of his philosophy and the basis of his 'new materialism'. Hou criticises this reading.
The view that practice is the ground of being, so that the world is understood as the product of human practical activity. Hou argues that it denies the priority of external nature.
Louis Althusser's thesis that Marx's thought divides around 1845 into an 'ideological' and a 'scientific' phase.
Lenin's summary of Marx's shift in 1843–44 from idealism to materialism and from revolutionary democracy to communism.

The philosophical system of the Marxist tradition, developed by Engels, Lenin and Soviet and Chinese theorists, combining materialism with dialectics. Hou defends it against those who call it 'official philosophy'.

t: Innovative development of Marxist philosophy
zh: 对马克思主义哲学的创新性发展
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 24 October 2022, during the 20th Party Congress, Liu Jun argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, while inheriting the basic standpoint, viewpoints and methods of Marxist philosophy, has produced a series of innovative developments of it. The piece is a short commentary that treats Marxist philosophy as the "core skill" the whole Party is urged to study and apply.

The article is organised in three parts: the continuation and development of Marxism's basic standpoint; the enrichment of its viewpoints; and the upholding and innovation of its methods. The second part takes four areas in turn: the view of practice, the view of nature, the view of contradiction and the view of development. Liu supports each point with passages from Marx, Engels and Xi.

On standpoint, Liu holds that putting the people first expresses historical materialism and runs through Xi's thought like a "red thread". The article says it answers the questions of for whom, on whom to rely and who we are, by describing the people as the "examiner" of the era. It also says the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind develops Marx's "real community" and the aim of human emancipation. On viewpoints, Liu credits the thought with an advance from a "dialectical unity" of humanity and nature to a "community of life", and with the judgement that the principal contradiction in Chinese society has changed. It also credits the new development philosophy and Chinese modernization, said to break the equation of modernization with Westernization. On method, Liu stresses seeking truth from facts, keeping to fundamentals while innovating, a problem-oriented approach and systems thinking, together with strategic, historical, dialectical, innovative, rule-of-law and bottom-line thinking.

Liu concludes that these elements enrich the Marxist philosophical "treasury" of methodology and constitute original contributions to the theory of social contradictions, the laws of civilisational development and the world-historical theory. The text is a concise, officially framed overview rather than a detailed philosophical analysis. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Chinese Party theorists in October 2022 presented Xi Jinping Thought as a development of dialectical and historical materialism.
quoteEn: Upholding the supremacy of the people is the fundamental expression of adherence to historical materialism, and a red thread running through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
quoteZh: 坚持人民至上，是坚持历史唯物主义的根本体现，是贯穿习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的一根红线。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the Marxism of contemporary China.
The official name for China's path of modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models. It was prominently elaborated at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013. It calls for common responses to global challenges.
A 2015 official framework consisting of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development. It guides economic and social policy.
A slogan stating that the Party's work should place the people's interests first. It is presented as the standpoint of Xi Jinping Thought.

t: The historical logic of the early spread of Marxism in the East
zh: 马克思主义在东方早期传播的历史逻辑
source: Journal of Peking University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2022 no. 4
paras: Sun Laibin asks why Marxism, which first spread in advanced capitalist Western Europe, found its next centre of gravity in the East, and what historical logic governed that shift. Taking Russia (loosely counted as Eastern) and China as examples, Sun argues that early diffusion combined features common to all scientific theories with differences arising from social setting, cultural tradition and revolutionary conditions. This combination, the author contends, produced a distinctive dialectic that helps explain how Marxism rose in the East.

The article is organised around four "laws" of theoretical diffusion: the law of theoretical need, the law of diffusion through struggle, the law of practical orientation, and the law of advanced sacrifice. Each is illustrated with parallel cases from Russia, from the 1860s to the October Revolution, and from China, from the 1900s to the founding of the Communist Party. Sun draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin, and on figures such as Plekhanov, Zasulich, Chen Duxiu, Cai Hesen and Qu Qiubai.

Sun's central claims are as follows. First, Marxism spread in economically backward Russia and China because it answered a pressing need. The author presents the "strange" pairing of backwardness and revolutionary leadership as an instance of the dialectic of the general and the particular, avoiding both Narodnik theories of backwardness as advantage and Second International economic determinism. Second, Marxism advanced by contending with other Western currents, among them Narodism, "legal Marxism", anarchism, and in China the debates over "problems" and "isms" and over socialism. Sun describes these currents as at once fellow-travellers, competitors and opponents, owing to disputes over national paths, varied responses to capitalism, and the "Easternisation" of imported ideas. Third, translators were also revolutionaries, and many early propagators came from propertied families, so their move to the proletarian standpoint demanded sacrifice. Sun cites Qu Qiubai's self-criticism of his "dualistic personality".

Sun concludes that Russian and Chinese intellectuals treated Marxism as a weapon for changing the world, not as pure doctrine. The author holds that without these class-standpoint shifts, the adaptation of Marxism to Russia and China would have been very different. Revisiting this history, Sun suggests, helps in understanding how Marxism rose in the East and in advancing its contemporary spread. Read the original if you want a conceptual account of early Marxist diffusion in Russia and China, framed through four named laws and illustrated with biographical and documentary detail.
quoteEn: It can be said that, from the outset, advanced intellectuals in Russia and China did not explore Marxism as mere doctrine but treated it as an ideological weapon for transforming the world and society.
quoteZh: 可以说，俄国和中国的先进知识分子从一开始就不是把马克思主义当作单纯的学理来探究，而是把它当作改造世界、改造社会的思想武器。

t: A new form of human civilization and developing twenty-first-century Marxism
zh: 人类文明新形态与发展21世纪马克思主义
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 29 September 2022
paras: Writing in a newspaper piece of September 2022, Han Qingxiang argues that "path" and "civilization" are the fundamental questions for developing Marxism, and that twenty-first-century Marxism should be built on the path of Chinese modernization and the new form of human civilization it creates. Han treats these two "creations" as the foundation of a Marxism suited to the present century.

The article begins from the claim that the essence of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is the question of the path: of revolution, construction, reform and national rejuvenation. It then lists six things the "two creations" are said to contain: the growth point and centre of Marxism, the features of the age, the theme, the fundamental questions, the capacity for development, and the core elements. It closes by turning these elements into a theoretical structure and linking it to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Han first proposes that the Chinese path has "originary" significance: Chinese theory, institutions, culture and discourse all rest on it, so that disputes between Chinese and Western theory are, in the end, disputes over the path. On this basis Han argues that the centre of the world socialist movement has moved to contemporary China, and that the growth point of Marxism has moved with it. Han also identifies the age's defining feature as "transformation and reconstruction", produced by the interaction of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the world's "great changes unseen in a century". Han sets the theme of twenty-first-century Marxism beside those of Marx and Engels, Lenin and Mao Zedong, each tied to a path. It is to show the superiority of the socialist system and to choose the right path and civilization for China and the world.

Han names five fundamental questions: people's wellbeing, national strength, world peace, the Party's strength and the vitality of Marxism. From the "two creations" Han extracts seven elements of strength: Party leadership, the people's principal role, market allocation, social mobilization, cultural cohesion, ecological nourishment and global harmony. Han calls their combination, under Party leadership, the "Party-led theory of a systemic structure of forces" and presents it as an expression of Xi Jinping's emphasis on systematic strategic planning and strategic thinking. Han calls for this structure to be further theorised. Read the original if you want to see how a prominent Chinese theorist ties the Chinese path, the new form of human civilization and the future of Marxism together in one framework.
quoteEn: Chinese theory can be properly explained only by grounding it in the Chinese path; where the path differs, the theory must differ.
quoteZh: 中国的理论只有立足于中国道路才能得到合理解释，道路不同，理论必然不同。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official phrase, used from 2021, for the civilization said to be created by Chinese modernization. It is presented as an alternative to the Western modernization model.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to each new era.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping since 2017–18 for a shifting global balance of power and order.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream. It denotes restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: Understanding the valuable experience of "persisting in pioneering and innovation"
zh: 深刻理解“坚持开拓创新”的宝贵经验
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022, takes up one of the ten lessons of historical experience set out in the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). That lesson is "persisting in pioneering and innovation". Shi argues that this has been a defining source of the Party's successes and remains a requirement for the current period.

The piece first traces the historical roots of the principle, then reviews the Party's achievements by period, and finally draws out what the principle demands today. The historical roots are found in Marxism itself and in Chinese civilisation. The periods covered are the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era.

Shi's central move is to present innovation as built into both Marxism and Chinese civilisation. Marxism is described as an open theory that is "not a dogma but a guide to action", and the Chinese nation's five-thousand-year history is said to show a continual search for change. Each period of Party history is then read as a case of innovation: the strategy of surrounding the cities from the countryside, the establishment of the basic socialist system, the socialist market economy, and the formation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author links these to the first and later leaps in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. For the present, Shi names three requirements: a problem orientation, since problems are the starting point of innovation; a spirit of initiative, meaning grasping historical laws, strengthening historical awareness and acting on it; and reliance on the people's strength, through a people-centred approach and the cultivation of talent, especially young people.

Shi concludes that the Party's century of struggle shows that only persistent innovation can win great struggles and realise great dreams. Because practice never stops developing, theoretical and practical innovation must continue, and the lesson must be inherited and carried forward in advancing Chinese modernization and socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party commentary presents innovation as a historical lesson in the official narrative of the Party's first century.
quoteEn: Persisting in pioneering and innovation is a distinctive character of Marxism.
quoteZh: 坚持开拓创新是马克思主义的鲜明品格。

glossary.zh: 党的百年奋斗重大成就和历史经验的决议
glossary.pinyin: dǎng de bǎinián fèndòu zhòngdà chéngjiù hé lìshǐ jīngyàn de juéyì
glossary.en: Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century
glossary.explanation: The third historical resolution of the Communist Party of China, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee in November 2021. It sums up the Party's first century and lists ten lessons of historical experience.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and developing it further. Party history speaks of successive "leaps" in this process, associated with Mao Zedong Thought and later theories.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, stressed in Party documents after the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

t: The value and significance of the great founding spirit of the Party for national rejuvenation
zh: 伟大建党精神对民族复兴的价值意蕴
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022, Wei Qiang takes up the "great founding spirit of the Party", the concept Xi Jinping put forward in his 1 July 2021 speech. Wei argues that this spirit, formed when the Party was founded, has guided the whole historical course of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In the article's account it is the spiritual source of the Party's struggles, sacrifices and creations.

The short commentary is organised in four parts, each tied to one element of the founding spirit. They deal with faith and ideals, a sense of responsibility, strength of will, and political guarantees. Wei draws on episodes from the Party's history, from the Second Congress to reform and opening up and the new era.

Wei's central claim is that the spirit supplies the rejuvenation project with beliefs, a mission, character and discipline. Marxist truth, in its Sinified forms from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and the communist ideal give faith its content. The original aspiration to seek happiness for the people and rejuvenation for the nation is said to have stayed constant through revolution, industrialisation, reform and opening up, and poverty alleviation. Fearlessness in struggle and loyalty to the Party, together with a commitment never to fail the people, are presented as the inner and political guarantees of rejuvenation.

Wei concludes that the spirit is not abstract but carries practical concern. The author calls for its value to be turned from inner spirit into outward practice, giving strong spiritual force to national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholarship in 2022 tied the founding spirit to the narrative of national rejuvenation.
quoteEn: The great founding spirit is not an abstract spirit suspended in an illusory pavilion, but a real concern with practical rationality, and its inner values continually enrich the theory and practice of national rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 伟大建党精神不是悬浮于虚幻楼阁的抽象精神，而是具有实践理性的现实关怀，蕴含的内在价值不断丰富民族复兴的理论和实践。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping presented on 1 July 2021, the Party's centenary. It sums up the founding spirit as upholding truth and ideals, fulfilling the original aspiration and mission, fearless struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. It is a central slogan of Party discourse, especially since 2012.

keywords: great founding spirit of the Party

t: Seen from the standpoint of civilization or culture: plural philosophies and the mutual transformation of the lifeworld
zh: 从文明或文化的观点看：多元哲学与生活世界的互变
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2022, asks what philosophy means if it is viewed through culture and civilization rather than only through science and cognition. Sun Litian argues that, from the scientific standpoint, a single philosophy is nearest to truth and others are error, whereas from the cultural standpoint many differing philosophies may have value. Marxist philosophy, in Sun's account, is both the scientific truth of our era and the high ground of its civilizational and moral values.

Sun traces a cultural conception of philosophy from Hegel's turn to the spirit of the age and Marx's description of philosophy as the living soul of civilization, to Cassirer, Rorty and Chen Lai. The text then turns to Gao Qinghai's idea of a practical standpoint as the mode of thinking of Marxist philosophy, and to the concept of the lifeworld.

Sun treats the natural, existence, consciousness, logic and language standpoints as different worldviews, or horizons for understanding the world. Borrowing Deleuze, Sun calls them distinct planes of thought that shape the lifeworld directly. The lifeworld, the pre-reflective world given before philosophy and science, carries stable beliefs that set limits on philosophical imagination: naive realist intuition, the Chinese intuition that people are good at the outset, and Rawls's intuitions about distributive justice. Philosophy must listen to the lifeworld yet also enter it with estranging, negating ideas that bring new norms and ways of living.

Sun concludes that in an age of world history and globalization, plural philosophies will meet in a long dialogue of mutual interpretation, which is a dialogue of civilizational souls. A world with only one philosophy would mean the end of philosophy and of civilization. Sun adds that such dialogue must be tested against lifeworld intuition, as in Rawls's "reflective equilibrium", and that its calm voice is welcome as nationalism and populism rise against globalization. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Chinese philosopher links Marxist philosophy, cultural pluralism and the lifeworld.
quoteEn: Philosophy originates in the lifeworld, yet guides the transformation of the lifeworld through negating ideas and modes of thinking.
quoteZh: 哲学源于生活世界，而又以否定性的观念和思维方式引导生活世界的变革。

t: Theory and history: the twofold requirement of contemporary Marxist philosophy research
zh: 理论与历史：当代马克思主义哲学研究的双重要求
paras: This short report, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022, surveys the lecture series "Theory and History: Lectures by Young Scholars of Marxist Philosophy", hosted by the School of Philosophy at Fudan University. Zhang and Lai argue that the lectures show young Chinese scholars working on real problems of the era, which they present as the aim of contemporary Marxist philosophy. In their reading, such work grasps the contemporary relevance of Marxist philosophy through both theory and practice, and contributes to building a distinctive discourse system of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics.

The report groups the lectures under three headings: the social-critical dimension of Marx's critique of political economy, new work on classic texts, and the history of ideas linking Marx to the Western tradition. It names speakers from Renmin University of China, Capital Normal University, Nanjing University, Shandong University, Jilin University, Sun Yat-sen University, Fudan University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, and summarises each contribution in a sentence or two.

On political economy, Xi Ge is reported as holding that capitalism has developed only at the level of natural necessity and alien necessity, while generating the material basis for sublating both. Huang Zhijun is cited on Marx's two senses of "averaging", which he reads as pointing to Marx's communist orientation. Adorno's concept of "exchange abstraction" is presented as showing that the critique of political economy remains tied to social reality. On texts, Yang Hongyuan treats the Introduction to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right as the start of Marx's discussion of human emancipation, and Zhou Jiaxin traces the private-property question back into the critique of Hegel's philosophy of right. On intellectual history, Feng Bo, Zhang Yin, Tian Guanhao and Huang Xuesheng are cited on Marx's relations with Spinoza, Rousseau and the Enlightenment. Huang describes Marx as a "new" Enlightenment thinker.

The authors conclude that contemporary Marxist philosophy combines close textual work with new methods and a wider disciplinary horizon. They also call for scholars to engage the essential dimensions of social being, meet national needs and answer the questions of the age. Read the original if you want a quick map of current topics and names among younger Marxist philosophers in China, from Marx's critique of political economy to Marx and Spinoza.
quoteEn: Contemporary Marxist philosophy research not only attaches importance to excavating traditional textual studies, but has also been effective in keeping pace with the times by absorbing new research methods and establishing a broad disciplinary vision.
quoteZh: 当代马克思主义哲学研究不仅重视挖掘传统文本研究，还在与时俱进地吸收新研究方法、建立开阔的学科视野等方面卓有成效。

t: Marx's concept of cooperation and its contemporary significance
zh: 马克思的协作概念及其当代意义
paras: This short newspaper article, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2022, asks what role the concept of cooperation plays in Marx's thought. Pan argues that cooperation is the standpoint from which Marx criticises capitalism, and also the basis of his idea of a socialist and communist economy.

The piece first sets out Marx's definition of cooperation in Capital and its manuscripts and lists four features: internal interconnection, planning, the joining of labourers with their products, and the generation of new productive power. It then covers two themes: cooperation in the critique of capitalism, and cooperative production in Marx's view of socialism, including his engagement with the cooperatives of his day.

Pan reads Marx as holding that under capitalism the social productive power created by cooperation is appropriated without payment and appears as the productive power of capital. Capitalist management, the author says, hides exploitation behind the neutral need for coordination, and workers become mere parts in the labour process. In the second half, Pan traces Marx's interest in cooperative production in the 1860s to the struggle against Lassalleanism, the First International and the influence of Owen and Ernest Jones. Marx and Jones criticised cooperatives that were isolated and competed with one another, but valued those that shared profits with members and society. Marx called such cooperatives "possible" communism.

Pan concludes that Marx gave the cooperative only two principles, not a detailed blueprint: the dictatorship of the proletariat as a political precondition, and the use of new social elements that capitalism itself produces. According to Pan, this stresses both individual self-emancipation and objective conditions, so that Marx's idea avoids both utopianism and blind action. Read the original if you want a brief account of how Marx's theory of cooperation links his critique of capitalism to his view of the path towards communism.
quoteEn: Cooperative production is one of the principled stipulations that Marx and Engels made for socialism.
quoteZh: 协作生产是马克思恩格斯对社会主义的原则规定之一。

glossary.explanation: A Marxist term for working-class political rule during the transition from capitalism to communism. Pan presents it as the political precondition for workers' self-management.

t: The internal paradox of the aesthetic dimension in Marxism outside China
zh: 国外马克思主义审美之维的内在悖论
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2022, asks why foreign Marxism has invested so much hope in the aesthetic dimension as a way of critiquing modernity. Wang Qi argues that this dimension hides paradoxes it cannot resolve, so it cannot deliver the revolutionary, world-changing significance it promises.

The article first lists the thinkers who drew on aesthetics: Lukács, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School, Benjamin, Eagleton, Plekhanov and Jameson. It then examines two paradoxes, one at the starting point of the aesthetic critique and one in its practical aim. It ends with remarks on what this means for Chinese Marxist aesthetics and for cultural work in China.

On the first paradox, Wang says foreign Marxism begins from social critique, such as Marcuse's "one-dimensional society", and concludes that domination now works through ideology and mass culture. Struggle therefore shifts from seizing power to contesting consciousness. In Wang's reading, this turn makes critique focus on thought and ideas rather than reality, and it ends in a utopia of reforming consciousness. On the second, Wang identifies three practical paths: aesthetic politics (Marcuse, Eagleton), aesthetic production (Benjamin, Lifshitz) and aesthetic existence (Adorno, Foucault). Wang argues that all three shrink revolution into individual self-formation, so they either stay in the study or sink into self-technique, an existentialist self-salvation.

Wang concludes that these paradoxes confirm the scientific character of Marx's answer on the relation of thought and being. Chinese Marxist aesthetics should return to Marx and Engels, on the wholeness of sensibility, all-round human development and a harmonious ideal society. It should not copy this critical framework onto China's cultural problems. Wang calls for joint efforts in ideological and cultural development and aesthetic education, to raise a new generation developing morally, intellectually, physically, aesthetically and in labour. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist critique of the Frankfurt School and related aesthetic theory, and its link to current cultural policy.
quoteEn: Aesthetic practice aims at practice, yet it is not carried through into activity that transforms the objective world, and becomes instead a mental activity of transforming the subjective world.
quoteZh: 审美实践旨在实践，却没有落实到改造客观世界的实践活动，而成为改造主观世界的思维活动

glossary.explanation: The broad field of Marxist thought developed outside China, including Western Marxism and other traditions. Chinese scholars study it, often critically, as a counterpart to Chinese Marxism.

glossary.pinyin: dé zhì tǐ měi láo quánmiàn fāzhǎn
glossary.en: developing morally, intellectually, physically, aesthetically and in labour
glossary.literal: all-round development of morality, intelligence, physique, aesthetics and labour
glossary.explanation: A formula for the aims of education in China, stressing all-round development in five areas, with aesthetic education as one.
Education in aesthetic appreciation and ability, treated in Chinese policy as part of moral and cultural cultivation.

t: How the Chinese miracle happened
st: Based on a political-economy interpretive framework
zh: 中国奇迹何以发生
zhSub: 基于政治经济学阐释框架
paras: Zhou Wen asks how China's economic miracle came about and argues that it needs a new political-economy explanation. In this short commentary, Zhou holds that the answer lies in persistently modernizing the state's governance system and capacity, and in a dialectical, organic combination of market and government. Zhou presents this as a critical reconstruction of neoliberal theory and the seed of a distinctive Chinese economics.

The piece begins with the Western-centric view that modern China fell behind because of despotism and an underdeveloped market economy. It then turns to the historical role of government in the rise of capitalism and the early industrial revolution. Finally it sets out the analytical framework Zhou attributes to contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy.

Zhou contends that China's modern backwardness stemmed from the government's absence from the economy and weak governance, not from a lack of markets. Claims that a free market and limited government suffice for development are, in Zhou's words, theoretically baseless and poorly supported in practice. In place of the Western binary of government versus market, Zhou describes a three-dimensional framework of the Party, government and market. Under it, the Party exercises centralized, unified leadership over economic work, and the market plays the decisive role in allocating resources while government makes up for market failure.

Zhou concludes that economic development has always been driven by the state, and that the rise and fall of governance capacity is its main thread. Zhou calls for a new political-economy discourse centred on development and the state. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Chinese economist frames the Party–government–market relationship as an alternative to neoliberal theory.
quoteEn: Neither a pure market economy nor government planning alone can put a country's economic development on the right track.
quoteZh: 单纯的市场经济或政府计划都无法将一国经济发展引入正轨。

t: The national character and global significance of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学的民族性与世界性
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 29 August 2022
paras: This short newspaper commentary asks how the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics can be both specifically Chinese and universal. Liu Wei argues that political economy, as a social science, is a dialectical unity of national particularity and worldwide significance, and that the Chinese version shows this unity in a particular way.

The piece begins with a general point about learning across national traditions. It then develops two themes: the historical staging that gives the Chinese theory its national specificity, and the movement of socialism from a single country to the international sphere.

Liu holds that comparative critique of different schools requires a fixed standard, namely the class standpoint and historical value orientation of political economy. It also requires scientific method and a thorough understanding of the object being criticised. The national specificity of the theory depends on the historical stage of the Chinese socialist mode of production. Liu locates this in the primary stage of socialism, whose basic programme is socialist modernization, to be achieved by 2050 under the "two-step" plan set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017). Liu then argues that socialism has been international since its origins and is now at a stage where it exists in individual countries. As Chinese socialism develops, the author says, it moves from the national to the global, and its political economy expands from a narrow to a broad sense.

Liu concludes that the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics should explain the laws of motion of the Chinese socialist mode of production, and that it develops from national to international scope. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Chinese economist links the stages of socialism to the claim that Chinese political economy is universal.
quoteEn: An important feature of political economy as a social science is that it is a dialectical unity of national particularity and worldwide significance.
quoteZh: 政治经济学作为社会科学的重要特征，就在于其是民族性与世界性的辩证统一。

glossary.explanation: An official thesis, formalised in the 1980s, that China is in a long initial phase of socialism. The article ties this stage to the basic programme of socialist modernization.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's theory and system of socialism, in use since the 1980s.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and innovating: the path of economic development in the new stage of development
zh: 新发展阶段经济发展道路的守正创新
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary of August 2022, Hong Yinxing argues that China's economic development path combines fidelity to the right direction of reform and opening up ("upholding fundamental principles") with continuous innovation. As China enters the new era and the stage of an upper-middle-income country, Hong says, this path is moving towards development that is higher in quality, more efficient, fairer, more sustainable and safer.

The piece is organised around four paths: changing the mode of economic development, synchronised development of the "four modernizations", common prosperity for all the people, and open development under the new development pattern. Each is tied to statements by Xi Jinping and to what Hong calls Xi Jinping's economic thinking.

On the first path, Hong holds that crossing the "middle-income trap" requires a shift from factor- and investment-driven growth to innovation-driven growth, with supply-side structural reform and green development as means. On the second, Hong describes China's "parallel" development of industrialisation, informatisation, urbanisation and agricultural modernisation as shortening the process and lowering its costs compared with the West's "serial" path. On common prosperity, Hong stresses that it does not mean egalitarianism or levelling incomes. Instead, it implies a "reasonable range" of income gaps, a larger middle-income group and a distribution system balancing efficiency and fairness across primary distribution, redistribution and the third distribution.

Finally, Hong presents the new development pattern, with the domestic circulation as the mainstay and domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other, as the route to economic modernization, while coordinating security and development. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line overview of how an economist close to Party theory links Xi's economic ideas to China's development path.
quoteEn: Common prosperity cannot eliminate absolute differences in levels of affluence, is not simply a levelling of incomes, and still less can it be an egalitarian distribution system.
quoteZh: 共同富裕不可能消除富裕程度的绝对差距，也并非简单地拉平收入，更不可能是平均主义分配制度

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping has made a central objective of Chinese modernization, stressing prosperity shared by all rather than by a minority.
A strategy announced in 2020 that takes the domestic market's "great circulation" as the mainstay while linking it with international circulation.
A policy line introduced in 2015 aimed at improving the structure, quality and efficiency of supply, for example by cutting overcapacity.
A term from development economics for economies that stall after reaching middle-income status; it is used in Chinese policy discourse to motivate a change in growth mode.

t: Engels's dialectics in the perspective of the critique of political economy
zh: 政治经济学批判视域中的恩格斯辩证法
source: Journal of the Party School of the CPC Central Committee (Chinese Academy of Governance), 2021 no. 2
paras: Zhou Dan takes up a long-running claim in Western and Second International scholarship (Bernstein, Schmidt, Lukács's History and Class Consciousness, and 'Marxologists' such as Lichtheim and Levine) that Engels's dialectics is confined to nature and diverges from Marx's social-historical dialectics. Zhou argues that this misreads Engels. Seen through the critique of political economy, Engels's dialectics has a clear social-historical line and is fundamentally consistent with Marx's, to which it made distinct contributions.

The article proceeds in three stages. It first examines Engels's early philosophical, social and economic writings, from the Schelling essays to the Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy, The Holy Family and The German Ideology. It then turns to his reviews of Marx's A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy and Capital, Volume 1, and his letters on Capital. Finally it considers the political-economy sections of Anti-Dühring.

Zhou makes three main moves. First, Engels moved from the Young Hegelian primacy of reason to grounding dialectics in 'real experience', through his studies of English society. Zhou holds that this approach preceded Marx's and helped fix the methodological basis of historical materialism. Second, in his reviews Engels presented Marx's dialectic as the 'only correct form of intellectual development', resting on a new materialism and on the unity of logic and history. Zhou says Engels saw it as a tool for penetrating the reification of social relations under capitalism. Third, in Anti-Dühring Engels unified method and object: he derived general laws from historically specific ones and traced the interaction of production, exchange and distribution. He also defended the 'negation of the negation' behind Marx's re-establishment of individual property against Dühring's charge of incoherence.

Zhou concludes that Engels's dialectics extends well beyond nature. His stress on real experience, his reading of Marx's dialectic and his grasp of its modern, critical character show a basic agreement with Marx on foundation, form and practical aim. They also show a clear understanding of how Marx's dialectic differs from Hegel's. In Zhou's view this answers attempts to diminish Engels or to set him against Marx. Read the original if you want a close, text-based Chinese defence of Engels's place in Marxist dialectics, built on his political-economy writings rather than the Dialectics of Nature.
quoteEn: Engels's dialectics is materialist and grounded in reality, rooted in society and history.
quoteZh: 恩格斯的辩证法是唯物的、现实的，根植于社会—历史当中。

glossary.explanation: The subtitle and project of Marx's major economic works, including Capital. It examines the categories of classical political economy and the capitalist social relations they express.
The process by which relations between people appear as relations between things. Chinese scholars use this term for Marx's analysis of commodity and capital fetishism.

glossary.zh: 唯一正确的思想发展形式
glossary.pinyin: wéiyī zhèngquè de sīxiǎng fāzhǎn xíngshì
glossary.en: only correct form of intellectual development
glossary.explanation: Engels's phrase, in his review of Marx's 1859 Contribution, for Marx's dialectical method stripped of Hegel's idealism.
