The author calls for attention to livelihood issues, economic growth, better governance and stronger cultural soft power. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese commentators trace the lineage of Xi Jinping's \"people-centred\" formula and relate it to Marxism and Chinese tradition.
quoteEn: Relying on the people to create great historical undertakings has achieved a leap from traditional minben thought to "putting the people at the centre".
quoteZh: 依靠人民创造历史伟业，实现了从传统的民本思想向“以人民为中心”的飞跃。

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A development philosophy associated with Xi Jinping, formally stressed from the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2015). It holds that development should be for the people, rely on the people and have its fruits shared by them.
A strand of traditional Chinese political thought, found in Confucian and earlier writings, that treats the welfare and will of the people as the foundation of legitimate rule.
A goal of shared affluence for all the people, described in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism and a feature of Chinese modernization.
A guiding concept of the Hu Jintao era, adopted by the Party in 2007. It stresses people-oriented, comprehensive and sustainable development.

t: The contemporary significance of Marx's labour theory of value
zh: 马克思劳动价值论的时代意义
paras: This short commentary, published in People's Daily in August 2022, asks what Marx's labour theory of value still offers China today. Huang argues that, although Marx built the theory on an analysis of private-ownership commodity economies, its account of general laws of commodity production, exchange and market development guides the building and improvement of the socialist market economy.

The piece first summarises the theory's content, then draws out its implications for production and distribution in what it calls the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It ends with the changing scope of productive labour in the modern economy.

Huang identifies the dual character of labour as Marx's main advance over bourgeois classical economics. Labour is divided into concrete and abstract, necessary and surplus, private and social (private labour becoming social only through exchange), and productive and unproductive. From this Huang derives three values: labour creates wealth, productive labour strengthens the country, and income distribution should reflect labour's contribution. Policy follows: raise labour's share in primary distribution, strengthen the real economy and avoid economic 'hollowing out', and deepen market-based allocation of production factors so that rewards follow contribution.

Huang adds that productive labour now includes producing knowledge, technology, information and data. Creative and complex labour by scientists, technicians and managers therefore deserves pay matching its contribution, which would also raise China's position in global industrial and value chains. The article presents the theory as a guide to common prosperity and to balancing production and distribution. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese economist links Marx's value theory to current policy on distribution and the real economy.
quoteEn: In modern society the scope of productive labour has expanded greatly, and includes not only labour that produces material goods but also labour that produces knowledge, technology, information or data products.
quoteZh: 在现代社会，生产性劳动的外延大大扩展了，不仅包括生产物质产品的劳动，而且包括生产知识、技术、信息或数据产品的劳动。

glossary.explanation: A goal of shared affluence for all, long associated with socialism in Party discourse and given fresh emphasis under Xi Jinping, especially from 2021.
The Party's official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership with a market economy.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system, adopted as a goal in 1992, which combines public ownership's leading role with market allocation of resources.

t: The people are the Party's greatest source of confidence in governing and rejuvenating the country
zh: 人民是党执政兴国的最大底气
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily in July 2022, takes up the formula that "the people are the Party's greatest source of confidence in governing and rejuvenating the country". Yang draws it from the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), which lists "putting the people first" among ten historical experiences. The author's thesis is that the Party's roots, lifeblood and strength lie in the people.

The piece has three parts. The first treats the people's standpoint as the fundamental political position of the Communist Party of China. The second reviews the Party's history as one of close ties with the masses. The third turns to the people as the creators of history and to the tasks of the new journey ahead.

Yang argues that the people's standpoint distinguishes a Marxist party from other parties, citing the Communist Manifesto on the proletarian movement as one of the great majority in the interest of the great majority. In this account the Party, unlike earlier political forces, has no particular interest of its own and was founded to seek the happiness of the people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Yang names its greatest political advantage as close ties with the masses and its greatest danger after taking power as separation from them. The author cites the mass line, whole-process people's democracy and the achievement of a moderately prosperous society across a population of over 1.4 billion as evidence, and invokes Xi Jinping on the people as the driving force of history.

Yang concludes that the Party must keep its flesh-and-blood ties with the people, uphold the people's principal position and respect their initiative. On this basis the Party is to lead them towards the second centenary goal of a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary presents the people-centred rationale for the Party's long-term rule.
quoteEn: The Party's greatest political advantage is close ties with the masses, and its greatest danger after taking power is becoming divorced from them.
quoteZh: 党的最大政治优势是密切联系群众,党执政后的最大危险是脱离群众。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019, describing China's political system as involving popular participation at every stage of governance, not only in elections.
A working method associated with Mao Zedong in which Party cadres gather the views of the masses, turn them into policy and take the policy back to the masses.
A long-standing official goal of well-off living for all, which the Party declared achieved in 2021.

t: Promoting the better conversion of institutional advantages into governance effectiveness
zh: 推动制度优势更好转化为治理效能
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in July 2022, Shuang Chuanxue takes up a judgement Xi Jinping made during the 2022 "two sessions": that China enjoys "five strategic favourable conditions", one of which is the distinctive advantages of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics. The commentary argues that these advantages have been repeatedly proven in practice, and that the task on the new journey is to convert them better into effective national governance.

The article has three parts. It first sets out the advantages of the system, which the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) summarised under 13 headings, and which Shuang groups as advantages of value, organisation and operation. It then explains how the institutional system and governance mechanisms should be integrated, and finally lists three requirements for upholding and improving the national system and the system of governance. Xi Jinping's statements are quoted at almost every step.

Shuang's core argument is that institutions and governance are dialectically unified. The national system is the basis of governance, while the governance system and governance capacity are where institutional strength is concentrated and realised. A system is superior, the author holds, not only because its design is sound but because it operates effectively and brings tangible benefits. The article cites the response to Covid-19 and the campaign against poverty as proof. In the author's account, these showed the capacity to "concentrate resources on major undertakings" and to coordinate the country "as one chess game", and the author contrasts "China's governance" with "Western disorder".

Shuang proposes three requirements: upholding the Party's overall leadership, described as the system's greatest advantage; keeping the people's principal position, which includes finding institutional flaws behind problems the public raises repeatedly; and adhering to fundamental principles while innovating, so that institutions are refined in the course of solving real problems. The author links this to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 framed the link between institutional advantages and governance capacity.
quoteEn: The system of national governance and governance capacity complement and reinforce each other, and through their interaction they advance the continual improvement and maturation of the national system.
quoteZh: 国家治理体系和治理能力相辅相成、相得益彰，在互动共进中推进国家制度不断完善和成熟定型。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

glossary.literal: concentrate strength to do big things
glossary.explanation: A phrase used officially to describe the capacity of the Party-led system to mobilise resources nationwide for major goals.

t: The rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has entered an irreversible historical process
zh: 中华民族伟大复兴进入不可逆转的历史进程
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in July 2022, Ma Jiantang assesses the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012). He argues that, under the leadership of the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, a moderately prosperous society has been fully built and that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has entered an irreversible historical process.

The short commentary is organised as five "over the decade" claims. These cover Marxism in China, the maturing of the socialist system, economic and social breakthroughs, the building of a community with a shared future for mankind, and Chinese modernization.

Ma first presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the product of combining Marxism with China's realities and its fine traditional culture. He calls it a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. He then reports results: comprehensive deepening of reform, GDP above 110 trillion yuan, per capita GDP above US$12,000, victory in the poverty-alleviation campaign and high-quality development. Ma also states that China's contribution to world economic growth has stayed around 30 per cent for several years. On the international side, he credits the Belt and Road Initiative and the global development and security initiatives with addressing deficits in governance, trust, development and peace.

Ma concludes that Chinese modernization has created a new form of human civilization. In his account it is a modernization of huge population size, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical balance, harmony with nature and peaceful development. He contrasts it with a Western path he describes as capital-centred, polarising and expansionist, and says it offers developing countries a new route and a Chinese approach. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official People's Daily summary of the Party's achievements over the decade from 2012 to 2022.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has resolved many problems of human social development and has abandoned the old Western paths of capital-centred modernization, polarising modernization, modernization of expanding materialism, and modernization through external expansion and plunder.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化破解了人类社会发展的诸多难题，摒弃了西方以资本为中心的现代化、两极分化的现代化、物质主义膨胀的现代化、对外扩张掠夺的现代化老路

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the current era.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–2013. It calls for cooperative global governance and shared development.
The Party's term for China's own path to modernization, described by its five features. It is presented as an alternative to the Western model.
A Chinese-led infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream. It means restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Promoting steady results in common prosperity
zh: 推动共同富裕不断取得成效
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 27 July 2022, asks how common prosperity can be advanced step by step. Han Keqing argues that common prosperity is an essential requirement of socialism and a key feature of Chinese modernization. In Han's account it means prosperity for all the people, neither wealth for a few nor egalitarian "eating from the same big pot".

The article sets out the staged targets attributed to Xi Jinping: solid progress by the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan, more marked substantive progress and equalised basic public services by 2035, and basic realisation by the middle of the century. It then moves through development, livelihood protection, spiritual life and distribution policy.

Han's central reasoning is that China remains in the primary stage of socialism and is the largest developing country. It must therefore first "make the cake bigger" through economic development, then divide it well through institutional arrangements that handle growth and distribution. Han also stresses that common prosperity covers both material and spiritual life and is closely tied to the all-round development of the person. Livelihood measures focus on education, healthcare, elderly care and housing, together with human capital and upward mobility. Cultural measures include core socialist values, patriotic and collectivist education, and public cultural services.

Han concludes that common prosperity for over 1.4 billion people is a dynamic process that cannot be achieved at one stroke. Han calls for coordinated primary, secondary and tertiary distribution, stronger tax, social security and transfer-payment adjustment, a larger middle-income group, the abolition of illegal income, and an olive-shaped distribution structure. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line summary of how common prosperity was framed in mid-2022.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is prosperity for all the people; it is not the prosperity of a small minority, nor is it egalitarian "eating from the same big pot".
quoteZh: 共同富裕是全体人民共同富裕，不是少数人的富裕，也不是平均主义“大锅饭”。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal in Chinese Party discourse, given new prominence under Xi Jinping from 2021. It refers to prosperity shared by all, with narrower income and consumption gaps.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, formally presented at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. Common prosperity is listed as one of its features.
An official assessment that China is at an early, long-lasting stage of socialist development. It is used to justify prioritising economic growth and a mixed economic structure.

glossary.en: eating from the same big pot
glossary.explanation: A colloquial term for egalitarian distribution regardless of effort or contribution, associated with the pre-reform economy and criticised in reform-era discourse.
A policy image of an income distribution with a large middle-income group and small low- and high-income groups.

t: The threefold meaning of the essence of Marx and Engels's "science of history" and its contemporary significance
zh: 马克思恩格斯“历史科学”实质的三重蕴涵及其现实意义
source: Marxist Theory Discipline Studies (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2022 no. 8
paras: Hu Haibo takes up the concept of the "science of history" (历史科学), which Marx and Engels used from The German Ideology to Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy. Chinese scholars read it in conflicting ways: as the "one science" uniting natural science and the science of man, as historical materialism, or as a "genuine positive science" (the last disputed by those who treat historical materialism as philosophy). Hu argues that the concept means a science of human practical activity and its real development, and that this essence has three connected layers.

The article has three parts. The first re-reads the concept across the whole corpus rather than through Marx's early texts alone, giving weight to Engels's later definitions in Anti-Dühring, the Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy review, Dialectics of Nature and the Marx graveside speech. The second sets out the three layers and the logic by which they unfold. The third draws lessons for building China's "independent knowledge system", a topic that became prominent after Xi Jinping's visit to Renmin University of China on 25 April 2022.

Hu's central move is to show that Engels defined "science of history" as every science that is not natural science, covering human living conditions, social relations, legal and state forms and the ideological superstructure. Since Marx knew and approved this work, Hu holds that neither the "one science" reading nor the pure "historical materialism" reading is adequate. The three layers, set against German ideology, are: first, the basic principles and method of historical materialism (real individuals, life determining consciousness, the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production as a "natural historical process"); second, the "genuine knowledge" gained by applying that method to economics, politics, law, anthropology and other fields, with Capital as the main example; and third, the aim of human emancipation, so that scientific socialism is the proletariat's "science of history". Hu describes the three as mutually conditioning and forming a logical whole, with historical materialism as the foundation.

Hu concludes that building China's independent knowledge system continues the Marx–Engels construction of the "science of history" in the new era. He proposes three requirements: adhering to the historical-materialist worldview and method; answering the major theoretical and practical questions facing the Party and country across all disciplines; and holding to a people-centred stance as the value orientation. Read the original if you want a text-based account of how Engels's later writings shape the interpretation of "science of history" and how that reading is tied to current Chinese debates on knowledge-system construction.
quoteEn: The "science of history" also contains the value implication of proletarian emancipation; it is a unity of scientific character and value.
quoteZh: “历史科学”也包含着无产阶级解放的价值蕴涵，是科学性与价值性的统一。

glossary.zh: 建构中国自主的知识体系
glossary.pinyin: jiàngòu Zhōngguó zìzhǔ de zhīshi tǐxì
glossary.explanation: A slogan prominent after Xi Jinping's 25 April 2022 speech at Renmin University of China. It calls for philosophy and social sciences grounded in Chinese experience rather than borrowed from the West.
A term used by Marx and Engels in The German Ideology and later works. Its exact meaning is disputed in the scholarship the article discusses.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse. It says that work, including scholarship, should serve the fundamental interests of the people.

t: The threefold implication of the essence of Marx and Engels's "science of history" and its contemporary significance
zh: 马克思恩格斯“历史科学”实质的三重蕴涵及其现实意义
source: Research on the Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2022 no. 8
paras: Marx and Engels used the term "science of history" repeatedly, from The German Ideology to Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy, yet Chinese scholars disagree about what it means. Some read it as the single unified science of nature and man found in the 1844 Manuscripts; most read it as historical materialism, and within that camp argue over whether historical materialism is a philosophy of history or a "genuine positive science". Hu argues that the concept's essence has three interlocking implications: the basic principles and method of historical materialism, the "genuine knowledge" obtained by applying them to social life, and the value aim of human emancipation.

The article has three parts. The first re-reads the concept across the whole body of Marx's and Engels's texts, giving weight to Engels's later writings. The second sets out the three implications and the logic by which they unfold. The third draws lessons for building a Chinese independent knowledge system, a topic that became prominent after Xi Jinping's visit to Renmin University of China on 25 April 2022.

Hu's first move is textual. Earlier readings concentrated on Marx and the early works and neglected Engels, who defined the history sciences as "all sciences that are not natural sciences" and, in Anti-Dühring, as the third class of science covering human living conditions, social relations and the ideological superstructure. Since Engels describes the two men's work as a joint effort, Hu holds that neither the "one science" reading nor the pure historical-materialism reading is adequate. In Hu's account, the term narrows from nature-plus-human history to "human history", the science of real people's practical activity, set against ideology. The second move is to show how the three implications are ordered. Historical materialism supplies the foundation. Its application yields genuine knowledge in political economy (Capital), politics, law and anthropology. Proletarian emancipation gives both the value aim and the practical test, so that science and value are united.

Hu concludes that the construction of a Chinese independent knowledge system is the logical development of the "science of history" in China today. The author draws three implications. The system must rest on the worldview and method of historical materialism. It must answer major theoretical and practical problems facing the Party and the country, which calls for a comprehensive, cross-disciplinary system. Its value orientation must be a people-centred stance. Read the original if you want a text-based argument about the meaning of "science of history" in Marx and Engels, or an example of how the concept is linked to current Chinese debates on self-reliant knowledge production.
quoteEn: Scientific socialism is the "science of history" by which the proletariat achieves its own emancipation.
quoteZh: 科学社会主义就是无产阶级实现自身解放的“历史科学”。

glossary.explanation: A slogan promoted after Xi Jinping's speech at Renmin University of China on 25 April 2022. It calls for philosophy and the social sciences in China to be built on Marxism and Chinese realities rather than on Western frameworks.
A concept used by Marx and Engels from The German Ideology onwards for the scientific study of human history. Its exact meaning is disputed among scholars.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Xi Jinping-era Party discourse, applied to policy and also to scholarly research orientation. The article uses it to define the value aim of social science.

t: Building the national ideological security system in the new era
zh: 新时代国家意识形态安全体系建构研究
paras: Writing in 2022, Wang Yonggui asks how China should build a systematic national ideological security system in the new era. Wang treats ideological security as a cornerstone of overall national security and argues that it needs institutionalised safeguards and systemic support. The article's answer is a framework of four sub-systems, supported by deliberate capacity-building.

The article follows a path from strategic assessment to strategic layout to strategic capability. It first sets out the theoretical and contemporary grounds for the system, citing Xi Jinping's remarks and the National Security Strategy (2021–2025). It then describes the system's elements: supporting factors, driving forces and a layered structure. The longest section examines the four sub-systems in turn, and a final section turns to capabilities.

Wang's central claim is that the system rests on four sub-systems, each with four subordinate parts. The leadership and organisation system has the commanding position and covers leadership, organisation, personnel and responsibility. The risk prevention and control system is the core and covers monitoring, early warning, feedback and assessment. The legal safeguard system is the leading one and works through legislation, enforcement, adjudication, compliance and legal education. The resource system is the foundation and covers personnel, social forces and material and financial support. Wang adds that legislation must balance freedom of thought and speech against national security. The system must then be turned into capacity in four areas: political ability, thinking ability (strategic, bottom-line and historical thinking), coordination and innovation.

Wang concludes that ideological security work has become heavier in the new journey. Strong leadership, risk prevention, legal safeguards and resources are needed, together with improved capabilities, so that Marxist ideology can act as a stabilising anchor for socialism with Chinese characteristics amid great changes unseen in a century. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars conceptualise the institutional design of ideological security, including its monitoring, early-warning and legal mechanisms.
quoteEn: Ideological security is an important cornerstone of overall national security in the new era.
quoteZh: 意识形态安全是新时代总体国家安全的重要基石。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014. It treats security as spanning politics, economy, culture, society, technology and other fields, not only the military.

The idea that the dominant, Marxist-led ideology of the state must be protected from perceived internal and external challenges. Chinese official discourse treats it as part of political and national security.

t: Marx's theory of "capital in general" and "many capitals" and the study of capital in China
zh: 马克思“资本一般”和“许多资本”理论与中国资本问题研究
source: Studies on the Theoretical Discipline of Marxism, 2022 no. 8
paras: Gu Hailiang asks how Marx's theory of capital can guide the study of regulating and guiding the healthy development of capital under China's socialist market economy. Writing in 2022, he argues that Marx never discussed capital in socialist countries, but that his categories \"capital in general\" and \"many capitals\" supply the basic ideas and method. Gu presents these as the root of the current Party formulation about understanding \"the characteristics and law of behaviour of capital\".

The article first traces how the two categories emerged in the 1857–58 manuscripts (the Grundrisse): from the \"five-part plan\" through the six-part and three-part structures of the capital theory to a two-part structure, and then to the six-book plan and a four-part structure for the book on capital. It then shows how Marx used the categories in Capital, volumes 1 to 3. The final section applies them to the Party's current discussion of capital, drawing on Xi Jinping's remarks of December 2021 and April 2022 and on the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021).

Gu reads \"capital in general\" as capital's common determinations: the total form from which individual capitals abstract. \"Many capitals\" is its unfolding in competition among capitals, with accumulation, concentration, credit and joint-stock capital as its forms. He links this to Hegel's Logic, where the \"many\" arises from the \"one\" through repulsion. He holds that in Capital the categories no longer structure the work but act as a method: volumes 1 and 2 treat industrial capital in general, while volume 3 moves towards concrete forms such as commercial, bank and agricultural capital.

Gu maps the pair onto Xi's two-sided framing. Capital's \"characteristics\" correspond to capital in general, and its \"behaviour\" to many capitals. He argues that the five coexisting forms of capital in China (state, collective, private, foreign and mixed) are \"many capitals\" under a dominant public sector, whose \"universal light\" alters the colour and weight of private capital without removing its profit-seeking nature. He draws on Marx's remarks on competition and personification to support \"orderly\" governance of capital, \"traffic lights\" and guiding private entrepreneurs away from capital personified, and he adds that Marx's unfinished treatment of the world market opens a research agenda. Read the original if you want a textual account of how the Grundrisse and Capital are being used to ground current Chinese policy on capital.")
quoteEn: Capital's "characteristics" are an understanding of the determinations of "capital in general", highlighting the understanding of capital's attributes and essential determinations.
quoteZh: 资本“特性”是对 “资本一般”规定性的认识，突出对资本属性和本质规定的认识

glossary.explanation: Marx's category in the 1857–58 manuscripts for the common determinations of capital, abstracted from individual capitals and their competition.
Marx's category for capital as it exists in the plural and in competition. In the author's reading, it is the concrete unfolding of capital in general.
The official name for China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining a market allocation of resources with a dominant public sector.

t: Advancing Marxist research in depth and on solid foundations
zh: 深入扎实推进马克思主义研究
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, Xin Xiangyang argues that studying Xi Jinping's 17 May speech on Marxism and his remarks at Renmin University of China should drive further research on twenty-first-century Marxism and contemporary Chinese Marxism. The piece is a short commentary tied to the 14th Five-Year Plan for philosophy and social sciences.

The article has three parts. It first discusses why Marxism keeps its vitality, then sets out the original contributions it attributes to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and finally reports on the work of the Academy of Marxism at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Xin contends that Marxism stays vital when upholding it is combined with developing it, which the author links to the Two Integrations. Marxist guidance, in this account, is what distinguishes contemporary Chinese philosophy and social sciences. Xin says Xi Jinping Thought spans Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. Its philosophical contributions include the theory of the principal contradiction in the new era; its economic ones include the new development philosophy and common prosperity theory; its contributions to scientific socialism include theories of the Party's long-term governance and the Party's self-reform.

Xin reports that the Academy of Marxism has published chronologies of Marx's and Engels's thought and is issuing an eight-volume history of Marxism's development. It has also launched book series on Xi Jinping Thought and completed over 300 policy reports. The author calls for taking this research to a higher level. Read the original if you want a brief official-institutional view of how the Academy of Marxism framed its research agenda in 2022.
quoteEn: Taking Marxism as guidance is the fundamental mark that distinguishes contemporary Chinese philosophy and social sciences from other philosophy and social sciences.
quoteZh: 坚持以马克思主义为指导，是当代中国哲学社会科学区别于其他哲学社会科学的根本标志。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
Formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
Official framework introduced in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
Official goal of prosperity shared by all, increasingly emphasised in Party policy since the 2010s.
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, associated with Xi Jinping's anti-corruption and Party-building drive.

t: Accelerating the building of the "three systems" of economics with Chinese characteristics
zh: 加快推进中国特色经济学“三大体系”建设
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2022, Huang Qunhui asks how economists should carry out Xi Jinping's 2016 call to build philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics, applied here to economics. Huang's answer is that the work must be led by Marxism and, concretely, by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. This Thought is to guide the building of the discipline system, the academic system and the discourse system of Chinese economics.

The short commentary first states the guiding principle. It presents the Party Central Committee's economic thinking since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as a further theoretical leap in combining Marxist political economy with China's concrete realities. It then sets out three tasks for the 14th Five-Year Plan period, one for each system. Each task is illustrated with projects of the Institute of Economics at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

For the discipline system, Huang stresses foundational work: textbooks, handbooks and yearbooks. Examples are the Handbook of Chinese Economics, the Yearbook of Chinese Economics and the textbook Contemporary Chinese Economics. For the academic system, Huang calls for research on major theoretical and practical questions, such as high-quality development, the new development philosophy, common prosperity and the nature and behaviour of capital. The Institute's annual China Economic Report is cited as a collective effort on these themes. For the discourse system, Huang proposes turning political discourse into scholarly concepts, making academic discourse accessible to the public, and taking Chinese discourse abroad, so that distinctive concepts with world influence emerge.

Huang concludes that studying and explaining Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is both a basic need of building a modern socialist country and a necessary condition for Marxism to lead economics. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line statement of how Chinese economists are told to organise textbooks, research programmes and public discourse around Xi's economic thought.
quoteEn: Innovation in the academic and theoretical system of economics must closely follow the practice of China's economic development, using Chinese theories of economic development to explain that practice and using that practice to deepen Chinese economic theory.
quoteZh: 经济学学术理论体系创新，需要紧紧围绕中国经济发展实践，用中国经济发展理论解释中国经济发展实践，用中国经济实践深化中国经济理论。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义经济思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì jīngjì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official Party doctrine associated with Xi Jinping since 2017. The commentary uses its economic component, called Xi Jinping's economic thought, as the guiding framework for Chinese economics.
An official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation. It has been prominent in Party economic policy since around 2017.
The official framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015 as a guide to economic policy.
A Party goal of prosperity shared across society, with reduced inequality. It was given renewed emphasis in policy from 2021.

t: The theoretical power of a system comes from practical requirements of building that system
zh: 体系的理论力量来自服务于体系建设的实践要求
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2022, Mo Jihong takes up the task, set by Xi Jinping in his May 2016 speech on philosophy and social sciences, of building a philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics. Mo argues that legal scholarship should construct a theoretical system of socialist jurisprudence with Chinese characteristics by integrating its discipline system, academic system and discourse system. Two tasks are described as key.

The short commentary is organised around those two tasks. The first concerns teaching: the discipline, curriculum and instruction systems of legal studies. The second concerns linking the "three systems" to the practical requirements of building a socialist system of rule of law with Chinese characteristics.

On the first task, Mo notes that the revised national teaching quality standard for law (2021) changed the "10+X" core curriculum into "1+10+X", making the Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law the foundational "1". Mo holds that this one course cannot by itself carry the Thought's spirit into the other legal disciplines, so its theoretical system must be unified with the discipline and curriculum systems. Mo describes the response of the CASS law school, which formed a teaching group of senior researchers. On the second task, Mo traces the path from the 15th Party Congress's goal of a legal system to the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2014) and its overall goal of a socialist system of rule of law with Chinese characteristics. Mo argues that scholarship must be problem-oriented and organised around the seven legal branches, so that it keeps lasting academic vitality.

Mo concludes that legal scholars should keep to the Chinese path of rule of law and resist what the article calls blind worship of Western constitutionalism and rule-of-law theory. They should also tell China's rule-of-law story in terms the world can understand and hold discourse power. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a CASS legal scholar ties the "three systems" agenda to law teaching and legal-system building.
quoteEn: The building of the \"three systems\" of legal studies must be closely tied to the practical requirements of building a socialist system of rule of law with Chinese characteristics; only then can it have lasting academic vitality.
quoteZh: 法学“三大体系”的建设必须与建设中国特色社会主义法治体系的实践要求紧密结合起来，这样才能具有久久为功的学术生命力。

glossary.explanation: A formula from Xi Jinping's 2016 speech on philosophy and social sciences: the discipline system, academic system and discourse system, through which Chinese characteristics are to be expressed.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's ideas on law and governance, formally set out at the Central Conference on Law-based Governance in 2020. Its theory is summarised in the "eleven upholds", and it has become a core course in Chinese legal education.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义法治体系
glossary.en: socialist system of rule of law with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The overall goal of advancing law-based governance, set by the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2014. It comprises legal norms, implementation, supervision, support, and Party-internal regulations.
The capacity to shape how issues are framed and understood internationally. Chinese official and academic writing uses it to argue for China's own voice in global debate.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law

t: Implementing the speech's spirit, staying problem-oriented, and promoting the integrated development of basic and applied research
zh: 落实讲话精神 坚持问题导向 推动基础研究和应用研究融合发展
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2022, Sun Zhuangzhi takes up how international studies in China should respond to Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on philosophy and social sciences and to the national 14th Five-Year Plan for the development of philosophy and social sciences. Sun's answer is that research must stay problem-oriented, because theoretical innovation, in Xi's words, begins from problems. Doing so, Sun argues, would join basic theoretical research with applied, policy-oriented research.

The short commentary sets out four tasks. These are strengthening the guiding role of theoretical innovation, the supporting role of disciplinary expertise, the policy-advisory role of think tanks, and the building of international communication capacity. It draws examples from the work of institutes in the international studies division of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS). It closes with a brief assessment of strengths and shortcomings.

Sun contends that international studies should be guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, especially his thought on diplomacy, and should answer questions such as "what is happening to the world" and "where is humanity heading". Area studies, in Sun's view, need interdisciplinary methods from a Marxist standpoint and should avoid fragmented, low-level repetition. Think-tank output should be judged by whether it solves real problems and serves central decision-making, not by description alone. Sun cites the China–Russia strategic cooperation think tank and joint opinion polls with partner countries as cases of effective practice.

Sun concludes that CASS has balanced its disciplines and improved its management, but still lacks enough high-quality outputs, wider international cooperation and sufficient talent. Sun calls for closing these gaps so that CASS can show "national team" standards. Read the original if you want a brief insider view of how a CASS institute links the Party's research guidelines to think-tank and international-communication work.
quoteEn: The basic standard for evaluating think-tank output should be whether it genuinely solves complex real-world problems and offers targeted, workable policy proposals that serve the Central Committee's decision-making.
quoteZh: 评价智库成果的基本标准，应该是能否切实解决复杂的现实问题，提出有针对性、操作性的对策建议，为中央决策服务。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
An interdisciplinary field studying particular regions and countries, promoted in China as a priority discipline.

t: The deepening of Marx's view of the internal contradictions of capitalism
st: From the Economic Manuscripts of 1857–1858 to the Economic Manuscripts of 1861–1863
zh: 马克思资本主义内在矛盾观的深化
source: Ideological and Theoretical Front (思想理论战线), 2022 no. 2
paras: Huang Lu asks how Marx's understanding of the internal contradictions of capitalism changed between two of his economic manuscripts. The article argues that in the 1857–1858 manuscripts Marx was still held within a framework of exchange between capital and labour, which limited his grasp of those contradictions. In the 1861–1863 manuscripts, Huang contends, he moved to the capitalist mode of production itself and reached the view that capital is its own real barrier, producing a fuller, systematic account.

The article has three parts. It first traces the move from monetary relations to capital's process of valorisation, then the shift from the direct production process to the production process of large-scale machine industry, and finally the move from the collapse of the capitalist system of exchange value to a deepened account of crisis. Huang also links the study to the Chinese context, saying that as socialism with Chinese characteristics enters a new era and the socialist market economy is refined, the basic logic of capital must be understood more deeply.

Huang argues that the 1857–1858 manuscripts locate the contradiction in the ratio of necessary to surplus labour: capital needs necessary labour and at the same time seeks to reduce it. Machinery, in the 'fragment on machines', pushes this ratio to its limit and is presented as undermining exchange value and the basis of capital. This still treats production as the realisation of unequal exchange. In the 1861–1863 manuscripts, Huang says, Marx analyses machinery as constant capital within production, covering the factory's simplified labour, intensified labour, the pull between absolute and relative surplus value, and the antinomy in the labour relation, which leads to the legal limiting of the working day and to class struggle. Science and general social productive forces are absorbed by capital, so machines replacing labour do not lead directly to collapse.

Huang concludes that Marx came to see the contradictions of capitalism as arising in capital's production and reproduction as both a thing and a social relation. On this reading they reflect the logic of capital and the capitalist system, not merely unjust distribution or wasted productive forces, and this prepares Marx's treatment of crisis in Capital. Tracing the shift is said to show how Marx's critique of political economy extended and deepened. Read the original if you study the genesis of Capital, the 'fragment on machines' or Marx's theory of capitalist crisis, and want to see how a Chinese scholar reads the change between the two manuscripts.
quoteEn: In this sense, Marx argues that since the production of wealth is no longer the direct labour of an individual but directly a general social activity, exchange value no longer needs to exist as the social medium necessary for realising use value, and capitalist production aimed at value collapses with it.
quoteZh: 在这个意义上，马克思提出，由于财富生产的性质已经不再是某个个人的直接劳动，而直接就是一般社会性活动，那么交换价值也不必再作为实现使用价值所必需的社会中介而存在，以价值为目的的资本生产也随之崩溃。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's current system and path, associated with reform and opening up from the late 1970s. It is the standard formula in Party documents.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system, adopted as a goal in 1992. It combines market mechanisms with public ownership and state guidance.

t: The basic orientations and institutional failures of economic governance in capitalist states
zh: 资本主义国家经济治理的基本取向及制度性失灵
paras: Western economists remain divided over how far the state should govern the economy. After the 2008 financial crisis, neoliberals restated the case for a minimal state, while most left-wing scholars demanded stronger action on equality. Wang Shengsheng argues that the dispute can be resolved only by starting from the dialectical unity of economic base and superstructure. On this basis the article analyses the nature of the capitalist state and its "elastic structure", identifies the basic orientations of its economic governance, and explains why that governance fails at the level of institutions.

The article first criticises Western theories of the "modern state" as public and autonomous, citing Skocpol, Mann, Evans and others, and sets against them Marx, Engels, Miliband and Poulantzas. It then derives a four-layered elastic structure of the capitalist state from four determinations of capitalist relations of production, and draws from each a basic orientation of governance. A fourth part sets out the institutional failures corresponding to each orientation, and a short closing section draws lessons for China.

Wang's central claim is that the public and autonomous features of the capitalist state do not contradict its class character but are the concrete form in which bourgeois rule operates. Because capitalist economy and politics are relatively separated, the state can absorb part of the proletariat's economic claims while preserving the relations of production. The four layers are institutional (private property and freedom of contract), organisational (elections and party competition), operational (supporting accumulation and technical progress) and discursive (bourgeois ideology). The corresponding orientations are partial "de-commodification" of labour-power, balancing different fractions of capital under industrial capital, macroeconomic balance through demand management, and presenting governance as value-free economics. Each fails because the root cause of disruption, the antagonism between capital and labour, cannot be removed without negating capitalism itself. Wang cites the post-war shift from Keynesianism to neoliberalism, the rise of financial monopoly capital (with US profit-share figures), overproduction, and the dependence of mainstream economics on bourgeois ideology.

Wang concludes that capitalist economic governance marks historical progress over earlier social forms but has insurmountable limits. The author argues that China should draw on its reasonable elements, coordinating the rule of law, political, educational and Party-building work, while going beyond its limits by consolidating socialist relations of production, putting the people at the centre, and relying on the Party's overall leadership. Read the original if you want a Marxist state-theory critique of Western debates on economic governance, with extensive engagement with Poulantzas, Polanyi, Arrighi and the autonomy-of-the-state literature.
quoteEn: The class nature of the capitalist state determines the limits of its elastic structure and at the same time marks out the institutional boundary of its economic governance.
quoteZh: 资本主义国家的阶级性本质规定了其弹性结构的限度，也同时划定了其经济治理的制度边界。

glossary.explanation: Wang's term for the capacity of the capitalist state, owing to the relative separation of economy and politics, to absorb part of the working class's economic demands without threatening capitalist relations of production. It builds on Poulantzas's remark on the "flexibility" of the capitalist state.

Measures such as labour law, welfare provision and union bargaining that shield labour-power from pure market determination. The usage follows Polanyi's account of the protective counter-movement against the labour market.

t: The political-philosophical meaning of Marx's "illusory community"
zh: 马克思“虚幻的共同体”的政治哲学意涵
paras: Wang Tian takes up a long-standing reading of Marx and Engels's phrase "illusory community" (illusory communality) in The German Ideology. On that reading, the state is simply the counterpart of the "real community" and is therefore a purely negative notion. The article argues that this equation of the state with the "illusory community" is too simple. It holds that the state does take a community form with real public functions, and that the charge of illusoriness has a specific target and a specific value standard.

The article, published in Theory Journal in 2022, has three sections and a short conclusion. The first examines the state's community form (rule by a class, law, bureaucracy, ideological packaging) and its public functions. The second reconstructs the polemical context of the phrase, namely Marx and Engels's critique of Max Stirner in the "Saint Max" chapter. The third explains the phrase as an evaluation tied to individual freedom, drawing on the Grundrisse, Capital and other texts.

Wang makes three main moves. First, the state arises from the division of labour and the clash between particular and common interests. It therefore takes a community form that mediates class conflict, keeps public order, builds public institutions and works, and takes part in world-market competition. The article describes this as the premise of the state's illusoriness. Second, Wang contends that the formulation was aimed first at Stirner's petty-bourgeois, idealist treatment of the "universal" as an abstraction opposed to the individual ego. It was not a general definition of the modern state. For the modern state Wang points to the "bourgeois manipulation" account, in which civil society determines the state and the bourgeoisie uses taxation and credit to make its interests universal. Third, "illusory" carries a value judgement. The state is separated from the individuals in it, who take part only as class members. The freedom it proclaims differs by class and rests on the contingency of living conditions and on the "limits of things", so it restricts individual freedom.

Wang concludes that equating the state with the "illusory community" fits neither Marx and Engels's theory nor actual state relations. The bourgeois state, in Wang's account, does not stand apart from civil society. It pushes the opposition between bourgeoisie and proletariat deeper into the defence of private property. Wang says this is a dimension to remember when re-examining Marx's theory of the state and when considering how that theory bears on present-day state governance. Read the original if you work on Marx's theory of the state, the Marx–Stirner dispute in The German Ideology, or Chinese scholarly debates on Marxist political philosophy.
quoteEn: The "illusory community" was put forward in the course of criticising Stirner's ideological conception of the state, and was meant to show that petty-bourgeois ideologists mistook the particularity of the German state for the illusoriness of the modern state in general.
quoteZh: “虚幻的共同体”是在批判施蒂纳意识形态性国家观的脉络中提出的，意在指明小资产阶级意识形态家把德意志国家的特殊性当作现代国家一般规定的虚幻性。

glossary.explanation: Marx and Engels's term in The German Ideology (illusory communality) for the form that common interest takes as the state, standing apart from real individual and collective interests. The article disputes the habit of reading it as a wholly negative theory of the state.

t: The historical coordinates and world significance of Chinese modernization from the perspective of historical materialism
zh: 唯物史观视野下中国式现代化的历史坐标与世界意义
paras: Huang Jianjun asks where Chinese modernization sits within the overall course of human modernization, and what significance it has for the world. Writing in 2022, Huang argues that, read through historical materialism, Chinese modernization is a non-capitalist path that goes beyond the logic of capital and puts people's value at its centre. In this reading it has far-reaching world-historical significance.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs how Marx and Engels understood the origin of modernization, and the problems of Western modernization. The second sets out the historical coordinates of Chinese modernization: its historical starting point, a vertical axis (the Communist Party's independent exploration) and a horizontal axis (comparison with the West). The third turns to the world significance of the Chinese path. It cites Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping throughout.

Huang first argues that for Marx modernization is driven by changes in the mode of production, especially machine industry and the expansion of capital. Western modernization therefore brings a chain of problems: the expansionary logic of capital, polarisation between rich and poor, and the alienation of human beings. Against this, Huang presents Chinese modernization as the practical application of Marx's idea of bypassing the 'Caudine Forks' of capitalism. Its vertical coordinate is the Party-led path from passive to active exploration, ending in modernization that is socialist and has Chinese characteristics. Its horizontal coordinate is a 'parallel' (bingliánshì) model, centred on the people, which Huang contrasts with the West's capital-centred 'serial' model.

Huang concludes that Chinese modernization points towards a future form of civilization beyond industrial civilization. It offers developing countries a way to avoid 'dependency', 'convergence' or 'decoupling' models, and it widens the field of practice for scientific socialism. The article cites an economy of more than 100 trillion yuan, and long-term social stability, as evidence that theories of socialism's failure and of the 'end of history' have been refuted. Huang calls for continued theoretical and practical exploration. Read the original if you want a systematic example of how Chinese scholars use classical Marxist texts to place Chinese modernization within world history.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a new pioneering undertaking in the course of human modernization. It is a path of development that goes beyond the logic of capital and brings out human value, and it carries universal and far-reaching world-historical significance and significance for the direction of civilizational development.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是人类现代化进程中的崭新创举，是超越资本逻辑、彰显人的价值的发展道路，具有普遍而深远的世界历史意义和文明发展指向意义。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization under Communist Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models, and became prominent in Party discourse after the 20th Party Congress (2022).

Marx's metaphor, used in his late writings on Russia, for the humiliating ordeal of capitalist development. The question is whether a backward country could skip it and still gain capitalism's positive achievements.
